doi:10.1007/s41252-026-00492-2.title: Learning From People With Disability in University Courses
doi:10.1007/s41252-026-00492-2.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>What this paper is about</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This Easy Read paper talks about two disability courses at Curtin University that were co-designed and co-developed with people with disability. The paper explains how lived experience of disability was prioritised in the design and teaching of the courses to reduce tokenism. Tokenism means including people in a small or non-meaningful way that does not give them real power or influence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>What we did</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>People with disability helped plan, write, and teach the learning content. Many lived experience educators were people with high communication and learning support needs. People with disability shared their lived experience and knowledge in authentic ways. The courses focus on what people with disability say matters to them in real life and on the practical skills they need from supporters.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>What we are doing now</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>People with disability are leading a study on the impact of the courses. The study will explore the long-term effects of lived experience teaching on: Student knowledge and attitudes, and How students work in partnership with people with disability in meaningful and person-led ways. This study will help improve co-designed content creation and further identify examples of tokenism.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Take-away messages</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Universities, and other forms of teaching, still have a long way to go to create learning and resources that are truly co-designed and led by people with disability. The authors, both with and without disability, suggest what needs to change.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1038/s44298-026-00193-6.title: Application of plant viruses in biotechnology with relation to artificial intelligence, machine learning, and nanotechnology
doi:10.1038/s44298-026-00193-6.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Plant viruses, once viewed as harmful agricultural pathogens, are now powerful tools in biotechnology. Their nanoscale structure, self-assembly, and biocompatibility enable applications in agriculture, medicine, and environmental sustainability. They serve in gene delivery, genome editing, diagnostics, and nanomaterials for vaccines and drug delivery. Integration with AI, ML, and bioinformatics enhances virus discovery and prediction. Despite challenges, plant viruses are emerging as versatile, sustainable resources for global biotechnological innovations.</jats:p>

doi:10.66857/f7c5.title: SMARTPHONE LABS AND VIRTUAL SIMULATIONS IN STEM EDUCATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF LEARNING OUTCOMES AND COGNITIVE LOAD EFFECTS
doi:10.66857/f7c5.abstract: <jats:p>Technology enhanced learning environments, such as the use of a smart phone as a Science laboratory or virtual simulations, have been mushrooming in the field of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM). These digital tools have the promise of overcoming traditional limitations of the physical lab, and may also help to reduce cognitive burden and promote better learning outcomes. But the relative effectiveness of these interventions in different STEM disciplines, at different levels of education, and in different implementation contexts are not well summarized in the literature. This systematic review was conducted using the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, the databases searched were SemanticScholar, PubMed, OpenAlex, arXiv, and ClinicalTrials. Studies were included if they used experimental, quasi-experimental, or comparative design to assess the use of a smartphone lab or virtual simulation in formal STEM education courses and reported learning outcomes or cognitive load measures. Adapted Cochrane tools were used to assess risk of bias and GRADE methodology was used to assess the certainty of evidence. In total 1,106 records were identified and 18 studies included following screening. These articles fulfill the study requirements. The studies included ranged from physics, chemistry, biology, engineering, and mathematics education from primary, secondary, and tertiary levels. Overall, the effect size of virtual laboratories on engineering education outcomes was found to be 0.686 (95% CI: 0.414-0.959), which is considered a significant positive effect. The largest effect size (ES = 3.571) was observed for learning motivation, followed by effect size for learning engagement (ES = 2.888). The medium effect size on conceptual understanding (Cohen's d = ~0.9) was found for the experimental tasks consist of smartphone-based tasks. Cognitive load results were mixed with some of the immersive environments reducing intrinsic load and increasing extraneous load. There was moderate positive evidence for technology enhanced learning environments and learning outcomes in STEM and moderate certain evidence of positive effects on motivation and engagement. Instructional design, sufficient scaffolding, and cognitive load principles are crucial for the success of the implementation. Future investigations should focus on more rigorous randomized designs, the use of uniform outcome measures, and the use of longitudinal measures.</jats:p>

doi:10.55041/ijsmt.v2i7.024.title: FPGA-DLAF: An FPGA-Based Deep Learning Acceleration Framework for High-Performance and Energy-Efficient Intelligent Computing
authors: Prof A K Rahtod Prof A K Rahtod
doi:10.55041/ijsmt.v2i7.024.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid advancement of deep learning has revolutionized numerous application domains including computer vision, natural language processing, healthcare analytics, autonomous systems, and intelligent edge computing. Despite their remarkable performance, deep learning models require extensive computational resources and memory bandwidth, making their deployment challenging in power-constrained and real-time environments. Traditional processing platforms such as Central Processing Units (CPUs) often fail to meet the performance requirements of modern neural networks, while Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) may consume substantial amounts of power and incur high operational costs. Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) have emerged as a promising alternative due to their reconfigurability, parallel processing capabilities, and superior energy efficiency. This paper presents an FPGA-based acceleration framework for deep learning models that integrates parallel computation engines, optimized memory architectures, dynamic resource allocation mechanisms, and low-latency inference pipelines. The proposed architecture is designed to accelerate convolutional neural networks and other deep learning models while minimizing hardware resource utilization and power consumption. Experimental analysis demonstrates significant improvements in inference speed, throughput, and energy efficiency compared to conventional computing platforms. The proposed FPGA acceleration framework offers a scalable and flexible solution for deploying deep learning applications in cloud environments, edge devices, and embedded intelligent systems.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch009.title: AI-Driven Digital Twin Maintenance Automation in AR/VR
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch009.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI), when integrated with Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR), is transforming industrial maintenance through immersive, data-driven Digital Twin environments. This chapter presents a comprehensive framework that demonstrates how AI-enhanced VR systems can optimize the monitoring and repair of industrial equipment. Using a centrifugal pump as a case study, the system uses AI-based anomaly detection, programmable logic control, real-time sensor inputs, and immersive virtual reality interfaces for remote issue resolution. IoT and MQTT protocols are used to synchronize a Unity 3D-created digital twin with real machinery. Operators can see, identify, and fix issues remotely with an Oculus Go headset. A Cartesian robotic arm that has been trained using AI procedures to mimic human repair movements makes physical adjustments. Scalable predictive maintenance, less downtime, and less human intervention are the results of this AI-AR/VR synergy.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch007.title: Adaptive Image Encryption Using Artificial Intelligence and Crypto-GANs
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch007.abstract: <jats:p>Crypto-Generative Adversarial Networks (Crypto-GANs) as an intelligent and adaptive framework for secure image encryption. By combining adversarial deep learning with cryptographic principles, the proposed system learns complex non-linear transformations to convert plain images into noise-like cipher images while enabling accurate reconstruction using the correct secret key. Unlike traditional encryption methods based on fixed mathematical rules, Crypto-GANs dynamically adapt to emerging attack strategies. Experimental results demonstrate strong security performance. Encrypted images achieved entropy values close to the theoretical maximum (up to 7.9978), indicating high randomness. Adjacent pixel correlations were reduced to near zero, confirming the removal of inherent statistical patterns. High NPCR and UACI values reflected effective diffusion, ensuring resistance against differential and chosen-plaintext attacks. Decryption quality remained excellent, with high PSNR and SSIM values supporting accurate image recovery.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2716-5.ch009.title: Gamification and Game-Based Learning With Accessibility Considerations
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2716-5.ch009.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the integration of gamification and game-based learning with accessibility principles as a foundation for advancing inclusive learning in the digital era. It outlines key theoretical frameworks, including motivational theory and Universal Design for Learning, and discusses the roles of assistive technologies and artificial intelligence in supporting adaptive instruction. Empirical findings on inclusive game-based practices across educational levels are reviewed to highlight their impact on engagement and learning outcomes. The chapter also addresses pedagogical, ethical, and policy challenges, emphasizing the need for interdisciplinary collaboration and equitable technology design to support diverse learners.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/s11295-026-01746-9.title: Integrating machine learning with single-step GBLUP for enhanced genomic prediction in white spruce
doi:10.1007/s11295-026-01746-9.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    We evaluated the predictive performance of machine learning-augmented single- and multi-trait single-step genomic best linear prediction (ssGBLUP) models for 30 complex traits spanning productivity, chemical defense, and climate adaptability in white spruce (
                    <jats:italic>Picea glauca</jats:italic>
                    ) from Alberta, Canada, genotyped at 211,061 SNPs. We extend a novel integration of the ssGBLUP with non-linear kernels for forest tree improvement. Using the conventional ssGBLUP model with VanRaden’s linear genomic relationship matrix as baseline, we compared two non-linear extensions: an averaged Gaussian kernel (GK) with trait-specific bandwidths and an arc-cosine kernel (AK) with 1–20 layers (depth). To relate prediction gains to genetic architecture, we also fitted an extended GBLUP model explicitly including additive, dominance, and epistatic (additive × additive and additive × dominance) effects. Additive effects predominated in 21 traits, dominance contributed > 50% of variance in several chemical-defense traits, and epistasis explained ~ 25% in key physiological traits. Predictive performance varied by kernel type and trait architecture. AK achieved the highest accuracy in 29 traits, improving prediction by up to 27% (predictive differences up to ~ 0.10), particularly for traits with more complex genetic architectures. GK yielded modest gains (< 7%; predictive differences < 0.03), while linear G kernel remained competitive for core productivity traits. In multi-trait models, non-linear kernels performed similar to the linear alternatives. Notably, low-heritability traits such as drought resistance improved from 0.446-0.517 to 0.461-0.547 accuracy with multi-trait integration. These findings suggest that matching kernel complexity to genetic architecture may enhance genomic prediction and highlight the potential of non-linear kernels, particularly AK, in forest tree breeding.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.1515/jccall-2026-0006.title: Defining AI-literacy and AI-illiteracy: how teachers and their students are using and misusing AI in English language and literature classes
doi:10.1515/jccall-2026-0006.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper reviews some of the challenges to academic integrity posed by AI, and identifies three specific areas of AI illiteracy that require recalibration of student behaviour and higher education pedagogy: technical understanding deficits, critical evaluation deficits, and societal impact deficits. We review the emerging evidence of the impact of AI on cognitive and neurological processing, in particular the danger posed by the threat of long-term degradation of learning and memory due to excessive “cognitive offloading”. We emphasise the need for CALL teachers to not only provide guidelines for students on how to use AI tools wisely, but to also provide training sessions, and develop student-centred curricula and pedagogy that encourage higher-order thinking, creativity, and teamwork. We follow Cope and Kalantzis in arguing for a reconceptualisation of assessment, at the same time as incorporating AI within a multimodal curriculum, with a focus on peer review, collaboration, and student voice, and incorporating tools such as ChatGPT within a “Brain-first” model of learning, and to view AI a just one of many potential sources of feedback for students.</jats:p>

doi:10.1088/2057-1976/ae6d02.title: Deep learning-based intraluminal gas modeling for anatomically accurate synthetic CT in MRI-based radiation therapy
doi:10.1088/2057-1976/ae6d02.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:italic>Purpose.</jats:italic>
                    Accurate modeling of intraluminal gas in synthetic computed tomography (sCT) is often compromised by the stochastic nature of bowel and rectal gas, which complicates magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)/CT deformable image registration (DIR) and necessitates time-consuming manual corrections. Here, we propose a novel, DIR-free, two-stage deep learning framework designed to improve the definition of intraluminal gas in sCT. By circumventing registration-based errors, this method aims to streamline MRI-only simulation and enhance the dosimetric reliability of sCT images in MRI-based radiotherapy.
                    <jats:italic>Methods.</jats:italic>
                    sCT generation was implemented using a two-stage generative adversarial network (GAN) framework. In the first stage, a CycleGAN or pix2pix model converted MRI inputs into segmented map images (SMI); in the second stage, a conditional GAN (pix2pix) transformed the SMI into the final sCT. Ground-truth intraluminal gas cavities were defined in the following order: gastrointestinal contours were generated via CNN-based autosegmentation, manually verified, and subjected to a 20% intensity threshold. The framework was trained and validated using a publicly available 60-patient dataset. Performance was evaluated using the Dice-Sørensen coefficient for gas definition and mean absolute error (MAE) for global and tissue-specific Hounsfield unit (HU) accuracy, comparing the two-stage framework against a direct single-stage MRI-to-sCT model. To evaluate dosimetric accuracy, prostate volumetric modulated arc therapy plans (36.25 Gy in 5 fractions) were optimized on five reference bulk-density sCT datasets and recalculated on both one-stage and two-stage sCT using a clinical treatment planning system.
                    <jats:italic>Results.</jats:italic>
                    The gas cavity Dice-Sørensen coefficient for the two-stage method and the single-stage method were 0.63 ± 0.11 and 0.04 ± 0.03 for pix2pix, while for CycleGAN, they were 0.67 ± 0.07 and 0.57 ± 0.11, respectively. The global MAE for the standard single-stage method and the two-stage method for pix2pix were 86 ± 20 HU and 94 ± 20 HU, while for CycleGAN, they were 105 ± 21 HU and 103 ± 22 HU, respectively. Dosimetric analysis demonstrated excellent agreement for the planning target volume (PTV D95%), with mean differences of 0.04 ± 0.08 cGy and −0.89 ± 1.98 cGy for the one-stage and two-stage models, respectively. Both models exhibited negligible deviations across all assessed organ-at-risk volumetric metrics, including D0.1cc, D1cc, and D15cc.
                    <jats:italic>Conclusions.</jats:italic>
                    The proposed two-stage framework significantly enhances the anatomical accuracy of intraluminal gas in sCT images, achieving a nearly threefold improvement in gas cavity definition over standard direct-conversion models. This method maintains high fidelity for bone and soft tissue while addressing a critical bottleneck in MRI-only simulation. Future studies will focus on the prospective evaluation of this framework to quantify its impact on dosimetric accuracy and treatment efficiency in online adaptive radiotherapy workflows.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1875393.title: Translating viral genetic data to PRRSV-2 cross-neutralization using machine learning
doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1875393.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Swine herd immunization through modified live vaccination or live virus inoculation is a core strategy for controlling porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome (PRRS), one of the most economically important endemic diseases in the United States that is caused by PRRSV-2. While antigenically homologous PRRSV-2 viruses are expected to elicit better immunological cross-protection, questions remain as to how genetic similarity translates to the degree of cross-protection elicited between the immunizing strain and subsequent challenge virus. For PRRSV-2, virus neutralization (VN) assays are commonly used to approximate humoral immune responses and to assess cross-variant vaccine efficacy; however, these assays are labor-intensive and difficult to scale for rapid immunization planning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Here, we developed a machine learning–based predictive model for PRRSV-2 cross-neutralization using viral genetic sequence data to address this gap. Virus neutralization assays were performed across a panel of viral isolates and anti-sera, representing a variety of contemporary and vaccine-like PRRSV-2 variants. Our internal dataset comprised 219 cross-neutralization pairs involving nine viral isolates and 25 antisera generated from animals inoculated with six isolates (immunizing viruses). Neutralization titers were classified as above versus below average using mean standardized log
                      <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                      titers as the cutoff. Candidate predictors included residue-wise amino acid property differences, overall viral genetic distances, and protein structural comparison metrics. Eleven machine learning algorithms were trained and evaluated using internal and external test sets.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The best models, which utilized predictors from protein ectodomain features, effectively estimated whether a virus-antisera pair would exhibit above versus below average neutralization, achieving balanced accuracies of 87–92% on internal data, and 71–89% across three external VN datasets. Key predictors included amino acid properties in GP5 decoy epitope and hypervariable regions, residues within GP2–GP3 epitopes, and overall genetic distance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      These models are publicly available through a web-based tool (
                      <jats:ext-link>https://stemma.shinyapps.io/PRRSLoom-NeutralizationPredictor/</jats:ext-link>
                      ) for end-users to estimate the neutralization potential between genetically distinct PRRSV-2 viruses. Our integration of machine learning,
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      experimental data, and webtool bridges experimental research with real-world application in veterinary decision-making.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1201/9781003611110-2.title: Unraveling the Impact of Social Networks
doi:10.1201/9781003611110-2.abstract: Social media networks have changed the paradigm of communication. It includes both individual and marketing communications. It has spurred the sharing of information and knowledge gathering. It has changed the way people engage with each other on a wider network. Social networks have positive impacts like sharing thoughts and experiences, gaining knowledge, and working through social sites and harmful impacts, like information stealing, fact manipulation, etc. Both impacts have been discussed in the chapter in detail. The work focuses on both their advantages and limitations of our society at large. It also discusses the key advantages of social networks by applying the framework of deep learning models. It also takes into account the various models like sentiment analysis, fake news detection, and recommendation systems. For the better understanding, models like anomaly detection and structural analysis are also explored. Some recent research studies have shown that deep learning models like Long Short-Term Memory and transformer-based architectures significantly improve tasks such as sentiment classification and fake news detection. This chapter highlights the algorithms in terms of social recommendations. It proves that the algorithms are very effective in enhancing the accuracy and giving clarity to the context. In addition to the mentioned models, emerging models like graph neural networks and blockchain are also very effective in addressing the practical issues. It helps in addressing the limitations by enhancing real-time analysis and focusing on decentralization. It also addressed the challenges driven by misinformation and data privacy. Pressing issues and concerns like mental health linked with social media can also be addressed with these models. Thus, these models can also be applied for the betterment of the society. It can help in addressing crisis management and other important social concerns. This chapter has critically examined all the mentioned aspects comprehensively. The conclusions are backed and supported by some real-world case studies. The present work also gives a direction for the future research regarding data privacy and solutions driven by artificial intelligence (AI).

doi:10.70609/g-tech.v10i3.10060.title: Integrating Boolean Logic-Based Feature Representation and Artificial Neural Networks for Digital Divide Level Classification in Online Learning
doi:10.70609/g-tech.v10i3.10060.abstract: <jats:p>Digital divide remains a major challenge in online learning, affecting students’ ability to access and benefit from digital education. While previous studies have primarily focused on first-level digital divide factors or employed machine learning models using raw input variables, limited research has explored the integration of logical feature engineering and artificial intelligence to model the multidimensional nature of digital divide. This study proposes a hybrid classification framework that combines Boolean Logic-based feature engineering and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) for digital divide classification in online learning. The proposed framework utilizes four variables, namely Primary Device, Internet Stability, Equity Score, and Accessibility Score. Boolean Logic operations (AND, OR, and XOR) were applied to generate additional logical representations of digital access conditions before the ANN classification process. Data were collected from 324 student respondents participating in online learning. The model was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized ANN model achieved 93% accuracy, 93% weighted precision, 93% weighted recall, and 93% weighted F1-score. Comparative analysis revealed that Boolean Logic features contributed additional logical representations of digital access patterns, although their impact on predictive performance was not consistently significant. The findings highlight that digital divide should be viewed as a multidimensional phenomenon and demonstrate the potential of ANN based predictive modeling to support data-driven digital inclusion strategies in education.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-9502299/v1.title: Supervised Machine Learning for Predicting Power Conversion Efficiency in Perovskite Solar Cells: A Systematic Review and Quantitative Meta-Analysis
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-9502299/v1.abstract: In recent years, perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have attracted considerable research interest due to rapid efficiency improvements and cost-effective fabrication processes. Despite these advancements, achieving optimal power conversion efficiency (PCE) remains difficult due to complex interactions among material composition, device structure, and fabrication parameters. To address this complexity, supervised machine learning (ML) techniques are increasingly applied for predictive modeling and optimization of PSC performance. This work provides a systematic review combined with a quantitative meta-analysis of supervised ML approaches for PCE prediction in PSCs, covering 36 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2025. A comparative evaluation framework is developed to assess model performance across different dataset types, sizes, and validation strategies. The meta-analysis of 27 studies indicates that tree-based ensemble methods, such as Random Forest and XGBoost, consistently outperform other models for tabular PSC datasets, achieving average R² values in the range of 0.80–0.90, while neural networks become increasingly competitive with larger datasets. Furthermore, the study examines how feature engineering, dataset quality, and validation strategies influence predictive performance, identifying key challenges such as the lack of standardized datasets, inconsistent benchmarking practices, and limited use of uncertainty quantification. A key contribution of this work is establishing a quantitative relationship between dataset size and optimal model selection strategies. Finally, a structured machine learning roadmap is proposed, integrating dataset curation, feature engineering, model benchmarking, explainable AI, and physics-informed learning to accelerate PSC development. The findings provide actionable insights to improve the reproducibility, reliability, and scalability of ML-driven PCE prediction, supporting next-generation sustainable photovoltaic technologies.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-9502299/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch011.title: Enhancing Community Resilience and Disaster Preparedness Through AI-Assisted Open Mapping
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch011.abstract: <jats:p>Africa confronts a dual crisis: escalating natural hazards like floods and droughts, compounded by a severe lack of foundational geospatial data needed for disaster response. This “data gap” traps communities in reactive cycles instead of proactive resilience. This chapter proposes an AI-Assisted Open Mapping Ecosystem (AIA-OME) to address this. The framework integrates artificial intelligence with community platforms like OpenStreetMap in a four-stage cycle: remote data acquisition, AI-powered feature extraction, community validation using local knowledge, and data integration for disaster risk reduction. This human-centered approach balances AI scalability with contextual accuracy. It incorporates ethical oversight, data sovereignty, and community feedback for continuous model improvement. Conceptual findings suggest gains in efficiency, data quality, and community empowerment. The chapter calls for empirical validation through pilot projects, emphasizing interdisciplinary collaboration and sustainable governance to ensure equitable outcomes in vulnerable African regions.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch011.venue: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

doi:10.1126/sciadv.aee2319.title: A chemistry-informed deep learning network for mitigating the stratospheric OH data gap
doi:10.1126/sciadv.aee2319.abstract: <jats:p>The hydroxyl (OH) radical is a key species in stratospheric chemistry, driving ozone loss and the coupling of other chemical families. However, global OH observations are very sparse, with a critical gap in satellite-based observations since 2009. Although alternative chemical methods attempt to mitigate such gaps, they have limitations. Here, we present DRCAT, a chemistry-informed deep learning network to predict stratospheric OH profiles using coincident satellite observations of chemically related species. Trained on only 2 years of data, DRCAT provides reconstruction of a continuous and reliable global stratospheric OH dataset from late 2004 to the present. Results show that DRCAT outperforms both a chemical transport model and an observation-constrained steady-state approximation. Moreover, DRCAT successfully predicts anomalous OH enhancements after the 2022 Hunga volcanic eruption, showing generalizability to extreme conditions outside of the training regime. DRCAT thus provides a robust pathway to fill OH observational voids. Beyond OH, this work offers a scalable framework for similar reconstruction of other key short-lived species.</jats:p>

doi:10.55862/gg8jrp96.title: Making Technical & Vocational Education Accessible to the Grassroots Students through Digital Learning
doi:10.55862/gg8jrp96.abstract: <jats:p>This paper explores the integration of digital learning platforms into technical and vocational education to enhance accessibility for grassroots students. Addressing the limitations of the traditional vocational system, this system struggles to meet the growing demand for skilled workers. To address these challenges, the proposed model leverages digital platforms, such as YouTube, to deliver theoretical knowledge in essential vocational areas, including welding, General Electrical, Electronics, Dressmaking, Civil Construction, and IT. This approach delivers free, accessible content enhanced with interactive 3D models and live sessions, increasing the flexibility of vocational education. Classes are designed in clear, easily understandable language and uploaded to YouTube to reach a broad audience. Upon completing the courses, students undertake an open-book examination. This online assessment will serve to measure their credibility and ensure they have grasped the material. The methodology combines online and offline learning to deliver comprehensive, industry-aligned education, incorporating partnerships with technical institutions for advanced training and certifications. Additionally, the paper highlights how the model itself operates as a social business, integrating financial sustainability with social impact. This model bridges the vocational education gap in remote areas, offering accessible learning opportunities to all students. By offering these courses, it aims to reduce unemployment and contribute to national economic growth.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-9971493/v1.title: Multi-site Radiomics and Machine Learning for Bone Status Classification in Panoramic Radiographs: A STARD-Compliant Diagnostic Accuracy Study
authors: Kelly Wivian de Souza Leitão Viana
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-9971493/v1.abstract: Objective To evaluate texture analysis (TA) in panoramic radiographs for bone status classification (normal, osteopenia, osteoporosis) in women and its correlation with clinical variables. Materials and methods Panoramic radiographs of 47 women (Control, n = 11; Osteopenia, n = 25; Osteoporosis, n = 11) were retrospectively analyzed. ROIs were defined in the maxillary tuberosity and posterior mandible. Thirty-six features selected via Fisher and POE + ACC were extracted using MaZda software. Random Forest (RF), Logistic Regression (LR), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models were developed with SMOTE for class balancing. Results The 10th Percentile showed significant intergroup differences in both ROIs (p < 0.05). RF achieved acceptable discriminative power (AUC > 0.70), whereas LR performed poorly (AUC < 0.60). Although SVM showed high sensitivity for osteopenia (0.875), it failed for the control group (Sens: 0.0) and showed low accuracy for osteoporosis (Sens: 0.333). Strong correlations were confirmed between GLRLM features and age at menopause onset (p < 0.05, FDR-adjusted); no associations were found with BMD or fracture risk (p > 0.05). Conclusions Panoramic radiograph TA shows potential for bone screening, particularly in detecting early postmenopausal changes. However, reliability is highly model-dependent; RF provided the most stable global classification, whereas SVM was limited to osteopenia detection. Small sample size warrants further large-scale validation. Clinical relevance : Conventional panoramic radiographs serve as a powerful opportunistic screening tool for early systemic bone loss. By integrating multi-site radiomics and machine learning, clinicians can detect sub-visual trabecular microarchitectural degradation, particularly early-stage osteopenia, during routine dental evaluations, bridging the diagnostic gap left by densitometric examinations (DEXA) that fail to capture structural bone quality.

doi:10.1201/9781003611110-4.title: Understanding Deep Learning and LLMs for Detecting Depression in Social Media Posts
doi:10.1201/9781003611110-4.abstract: Social media shapes today’s society through two distinct mental health effects, including benefits from remaining connected and expressing oneself, alongside potential drawbacks. Digital footprints now exhibit signs of depression while serving as an underdiagnosed mental health condition throughout these digital traces. Through analyzing these digital footprints, researchers can detect depression. Various complex tools for detecting depression can be developed through deep learning algorithms and large language models (LLMs). Deep learning tools with LLMs assist in identifying people with depression within virtual environments, according to this chapter. The detection of social media text-based depression signs starts with examining psychological depression indicators, which appear as emotional sentiment along with linguistic indications and user participation indicators. Most importantly, this chapter demonstrates the use of convolutional neural networks alongside recurrent neural networks and transformers to achieve accurate depression pattern identification. The chapter presents real-world deep learning applications with LLMs for depression detection in current systems. The chapter outlines future research goals to enhance model transparency, create real-time surveillance mechanisms, and establish partnerships with therapy practitioners.

doi:10.61351/mf.v4i3.606.title: Machine learning stock selection: Evidence from the South African factor zoo
doi:10.61351/mf.v4i3.606.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines whether machine learning can predict Johannesburg Stock Exchange stock returns using South African factor zoo features. Six models are tested in an expanding-window, walk-forward design, with portfolio performance evaluated across alternative weighting schemes and factor-spanning regressions. Ensemble tree-based models, particularly Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM, deliver the strongest out-of-sample performance, especially under more intensive training and linear rank weighting. Market-capitalisation weighting weakens alpha. Although machine-learning portfolios generate meaningful alphas under Fama–French models, the inclusion of momentum materially reduces alpha, highlighting momentum’s dominance in South African equity returns.</jats:p>

doi:10.1201/9781003611110-11.title: Sarcasm Detection in Code-Mixed Social Media Posts
doi:10.1201/9781003611110-11.abstract: Sarcasm detection in social media is challenging due to the implicit and context-dependent nature of sarcastic expressions. This challenge is amplified when dealing with code-mixed data, where users blend two or more languages within a single utterance. Such linguistic complexity often results from multilingual environments, making conventional natural language processing techniques less effective. This chapter presents a deep learning approach for sarcasm detection in code-mixed social media posts. We explore preprocessing strategies tailored for code-mixing, embedding representations, and neural architectures that effectively capture semantic and contextual cues. Experiments demonstrate that the transformer-based hybrid model (mBERT-XLM-R) outperformed with an F 1-score of 0.94 compared to traditional baselines, highlighting the importance of contextual embeddings in detecting sarcasm in multilingual digital discourse.

doi:10.1201/9781003611110-9.title: Explainable Transfer Learning Model for Disaster Damage Assessment from Social Media Images
doi:10.1201/9781003611110-9.abstract: The rapid expansion of social media platforms has revolutionized how information is shared during disaster events, providing real-time, ground-level perspectives that support emergency response and damage evaluation. This chapter investigates the incorporation of social media imagery into disaster impact assessment frameworks, highlighting their ability to enhance traditional satellite and aerial data sources. We begin by discussing the importance of social media in disaster management and outlining methodologies for data acquisition and annotation. The chapter then reviews a spectrum of computational strategies—from Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to advanced transfer learning—that enable precise evaluation of disaster severity from visual content. Critical challenges such as noisy data, annotation limitations, ethical considerations, and model generalizability are analyzed in detail. Finally, the chapter identifies emerging trends and future directions, including explainable AI, cross-modal integration, and real-time deployment for decision support. This synthesis provides researchers and practitioners with a structured roadmap for harnessing social media imagery in disaster damage assessment.

doi:10.1201/9781003611110-3.title: Understanding Factors Leading to Local and Global Spatial Spread in Social Media
doi:10.1201/9781003611110-3.abstract: Social media has emerged as a valuable data-driven approach for analysing information dissemination in various domains, including news, memes, and hashtags, across online platforms. Understanding the mechanisms and pathways of information spread is critical for effective information management in industries like advertising, marketing, and new media, where real-time insights play a crucial role. Previous research has largely overlooked geographical factors in information spread. In this study, we focus on the propagation of online hashtags in India, investigating the differences between local and global spread. Our research delves into the pathways of information spread, user engagement, and demographic factors influencing hashtag localization or globalization. By exploring these aspects, we contribute significantly to the expanding domain of spatial spread analysis within edge computing. Moreover, our findings highlight the importance of further refining edge computing strategies to optimize information dissemination and management, offering valuable insights for industrial applications.

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9725-2.ch014.title: Machine Learning Approaches for Real-Time Industrial Quality Monitoring
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9725-2.ch014.abstract: <jats:p>Maintaining consistent product quality in modern manufacturing environments is increasingly challenging due to dynamic process variations and complex production conditions. Traditional quality assurance approaches, which primarily depend on post-production inspection, often result in delayed defect identification and inefficient resource utilization. These limitations highlight the need for intelligent, real-time quality monitoring solutions. This chapter proposes an adaptive machine learning–based framework for continuous quality assessment in industrial systems. Multiple ML models, including SVM, RF, and ANN, are implemented and comparatively evaluated to identify their effectiveness in detecting early-stage defects. Model performance is assessed using standard evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The results demonstrate that the proposed data-driven framework significantly improves early defect detection, enhances process visibility, and supports timely decision-making.</jats:p>

doi:10.4271/2026-99-0538.title: Research on Urban Bus Timetable Optimization Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
doi:10.4271/2026-99-0538.abstract:
<jats:p><div class="section abstract">
<div class="htmlview paragraph">Public transportation serves as a crucial component of urban mobility, contributing to the alleviation of urban congestion, reduction of travel expenses, and mitigation of air pollution. Nonetheless, the dynamic passenger demand and the complex traffic conditions render traditional bus timetables inadequate, leading to ineffective allocation of public transportation resources. Consequently, it is essential to create bus timetables that are responsive to actual traffic scenarios and fluctuating passenger demand. This study regards the bus timetable planning problem as a Markov decision-making process within a discrete time framework, proposing a deep reinforcement learning-based optimization model for bus timetables. In particular, the model is designed to account for both bus companies and passengers, incorporating a state space and reward calculation method that emphasizes passenger comfort. Then Deep Q-Network (DQN) methodology is employed to issue instructions on whether a bus departure at each time, and bus timetable is generated gradually over time. Experimental results indicate that the proposed approach significantly reduces bus travel costs and enhances the overall travel experience for passengers in comparison to traditional methods.</div>
</div></jats:p>

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i1.280.title: <b>IMPROVING STUDENTS' READING COMPREHENSION ABILITY THROUGH THE SQ3R METHOD (SURVEY, QUESTION, READ, RECITE, AND REVIEW) IN INDONESIAN LANGUAGE LESSONS FOR FOURTH GRADE AT SDN 1 LIMBOTO, GORONTALO REGENCY</b>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i1.280.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to improve students' reading comprehension skills through the application of Survey, Question, Read, Recite, and Review (SQ3R) method in the Indonesian language class for fourth-grade students at SDN 1 LIMBOTO, GORONTALO REGENCY. This study was motivated by students’ low reading comprehension skills, as evidenced by their difficulty in understanding the content of the text, identifying the main idea, answering questions based on the text, and summarizing the reading. The research design used was Classroom Action Research (CAR) based on the Kemmis and McTagart model, conducted over two cycles. The research subjects consisted of 29 fourth-grade students at SDN 1 LIMBOTO. Data collection techniques included observation, testing, and documentation. The results showed that the application of the SQ3R method was able to improve students' reading comprehension skills. This was evident from the improvement in student learning outcomes in each cycle as well as the increased activity of both teachers and students in the learning process. The SQ3R method helps students become more active in understanding reading materials through activities such az analyzing, formulating questions, active reading, restating the content of the text, and reviewing the material. Thus, the SQ3R method is effective for improving students' reading comprehension skills in Indonesian Language classes at elementary school level.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch001.title: Groundwater Salinity Prediction in the African Continent Using Machine Learning Techniques and Methods
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch001.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter details a study using Machine Learning (ML) to predict rising groundwater salinity across Africa, a critical threat to water security. Traditional models face challenges with data scarcity and computational demands. By analyzing continent-wide data on climate, soil, and hydrogeology, the research tested multiple ML algorithms. Ensemble methods, particularly Random Forest and XGBoost, proved most accurate in predicting key salinity indicators (EC and TDS), significantly outperforming traditional linear models. Analysis identified nitrogen content (often from agriculture), sand fraction, and aridity as primary drivers of salinity, highlighting a mix of human and natural causes. The study establishes a robust ML framework for salinity prediction in data-scarce regions and bridges the gap between advanced modeling and practical water management policy, offering a vital tool for informed decision-making.</jats:p>

doi:10.1126/sciadv.aea3611.title: Discovery of flat-band 2D materials via physics-informed scoring and structure-based learning
doi:10.1126/sciadv.aea3611.abstract: <jats:p>Flat electronic bands are a fertile ground for exotic quantum phenomena, from unconventional superconductivity to fractional topology. However, their rarity and the reliance on density functional theory (DFT) calculations for identification have limited systematic exploration across large material spaces. Here, we report the discovery of multiple previously unrecognized flat-band two-dimensional materials through a structure-informed, data-driven framework. We introduce a physically motivated flatness score that combines band dispersion and density-of-states features, enabling algorithmic labeling of known materials without requiring manual inspection. This score is then used to train a multimodal deep learning model that predicts flat-band propensity directly from atomic structure. Applied to more than 10,000 unlabeled materials, our framework identifies numerous flat-band candidates. Among the top-scoring structures (flatness score higher than 0.9), DFT calculations on materials with kagome-like lattices confirm a flat-band prediction accuracy of 98%, demonstrating the ability to discover topologically nontrivial systems. By bypassing the need for precomputed band structures, our approach enables large-scale, interpretable screening and expands the design space for correlated quantum phases in low-dimensional systems.</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/ajim-08-2025-0620.title: Predicting movie success with machine learning and explainable AI: a large-scale analysis using IMDb and TMDB data
doi:10.1108/ajim-08-2025-0620.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The commercial success of a movie remains difficult to anticipate during early production stages, despite the availability of digital information on audience engagement and film attributes. While prior studies have explored box office or rating prediction, few have combined early-stage feature sets with transparent, interpretable models. This study addresses this gap by developing a large-scale prediction framework using machine learning and explainable AI techniques.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The analysis draws on a dataset of 433,350 films from IMDb and TMDB. Multiple predictive models were employed alongside SHAP and LIME to identify the factors most strongly associated with success, defined through a dual rating–vote threshold.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results show that popularity metrics, director and thematic attributes are the strongest predictors of success, while genre effects such as comedy and drama play a more modest but still meaningful contextual role.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study contributes a scalable, interpretable, early-stage prediction approach that supports producers, investors and distributors by highlighting both the drivers of success and the reasoning behind model outputs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.67315/gentabangsa.v1i04.88.title: Pengembangan Desain Materi Ajar Berorientasi Student-Centered Learning dalam Meningkatkan Kualitas Pembelajaran
doi:10.67315/gentabangsa.v1i04.88.abstract: <jats:p>Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengembangan desain materi ajar berorientasi Student-Centered Learning (SCL) dalam meningkatkan kualitas pembelajaran pada era transformasi pendidikan digital. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode studi kepustakaan (library research) melalui analisis berbagai buku, artikel ilmiah, dokumen kebijakan, dan hasil penelitian terkini yang dipublikasikan pada periode 2020–2025. Data dianalisis menggunakan teknik thematic content analysis untuk mengidentifikasi konsep, karakteristik, strategi pengembangan, serta implementasi desain materi ajar berbasis SCL. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa desain materi ajar yang berorientasi pada peserta didik mampu menciptakan pengalaman belajar yang lebih aktif, kolaboratif, kontekstual, dan bermakna. Pengembangan materi ajar yang mengintegrasikan pembelajaran berdiferensiasi, asesmen autentik, teknologi digital, serta prinsip Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) berkontribusi terhadap peningkatan keterlibatan peserta didik, kemampuan berpikir kritis, kreativitas, komunikasi, kolaborasi, dan kemandirian belajar. Kajian ini menegaskan bahwa desain materi ajar tidak hanya berfungsi sebagai sumber belajar, tetapi juga sebagai instrumen strategis dalam membangun ekosistem pembelajaran yang inovatif, adaptif, dan berpusat pada peserta didik. Temuan penelitian diharapkan menjadi landasan konseptual bagi pendidik dalam mengembangkan materi ajar yang relevan dengan tuntutan pendidikan abad ke-21.</jats:p>

doi:10.1201/9781003611110-1.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Social Network Analysis
doi:10.1201/9781003611110-1.abstract: With the advancement in the digital world, Social Network Analysis (SNA) has developed as one of the most feasible methods to study human interaction. The traditional methods of analyzing social data have succumbed to their volume, velocity, diversity, or heterogeneity, requiring the aid of Artificial Intelligence (AI), as well as improving the interpretability, scalability, and insight generation in networked systems. This chapter covers the developmental steps of AI infusion into SNA, starting with deep learning methods that provide feature extraction at scale, and then moving to graph neural networks (GNNs) that analyze relationships and topology across nodes and edges. This area is further advanced with the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs), enabling semantic reasoning, context awareness, and the inclusion of unstructured text to the network models. Most recently, the development of AI agents in this domain has been revolutionary, providing SNA pipelines with autonomy, adaptivity, and continuous self-learning. Shifts from these breakthroughs are routinely found in practices within e-commerce, real-time systems, misinformation detection, and diverse areas within the frame of computer and web security. Major unethical factors concerning AI-powered SNA are also highlighted, with a focus on responsible and trustworthy policies to ensure transparency and dependability. The integration of these AI-driven techniques results in measurable improvements in prediction accuracy, network understanding, and decision-making effectiveness across social platforms.

doi:10.55041/ijsmt.v2i7.023.title: Deep Learning-Based EEG Signal Classification for Intelligent Brain-Computer Interface Applications
authors: Musapuri Shiva Kumar Musapuri Shiva Kumar
Prof A K Rahtod Prof A K Rahtod
doi:10.55041/ijsmt.v2i7.023.abstract: <jats:p>Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) technology represents one of the most transformative developments in biomedical engineering, enabling direct communication between the human brain and external devices. Electroencephalography (EEG) is the most widely used non-invasive technique for acquiring brain activity signals due to its safety, portability, and cost-effectiveness. EEG signals contain valuable information regarding cognitive processes, motor intentions, emotional states, and neurological conditions. However, EEG signal classification remains a significant challenge because of the non-stationary nature of brain signals, low signal-to-noise ratio, inter-subject variability, and high-dimensional feature spaces. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Deep Learning have emerged as powerful solutions for improving EEG classification accuracy and enabling robust Brain-Computer Interface systems. This paper presents a comprehensive study of EEG Signal Classification for Brain-Computer Interfaces and proposes an Artificial Intelligence-Based EEG Classification Framework (AI-ECF) designed to enhance neural signal interpretation and BCI performance. The proposed framework integrates signal preprocessing, feature extraction, deep learning-based classification, and intelligent decision-making mechanisms. Experimental evaluations demonstrate significant improvements in classification accuracy, response time, and computational efficiency compared with traditional EEG analysis methods. The findings indicate that AI-driven EEG classification technologies will play a critical role in future neuroengineering, assistive technologies, healthcare systems, and intelligent human-machine interaction platforms.</jats:p>
doi:10.55041/ijsmt.v2i7.023.venue: International Journal of Science, Strategic Management and Technology

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2606-9.ch006.title: Investigations of AI-Driven Personalization and Learning Analytics for Enhanced Education
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2606-9.ch006.abstract: <jats:p>The exploration of the disruptive possibilities and far-reaching implications of the “Algorithmic Classroom” is undertaken here. Such an innovative form, the Algorithmic Classroom, is inherently attended by widespread applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled individualized learning within educational environments. Various learning technologies allow instructors to use AI to fit knowledge involvements into the requirements of individual students, provide pedagogical innovations, and supply data-driven insights to teachers and institutions. This research will comprehensively examine the plan, execution, and impact of AI-enabled systems within different educational settings and across levels. Learning pathways, adaptive assessments, and intelligent tutoring systems are facilitated by the algorithms and architectures that this project will explore. New research data will assess how these AI interventions can effectively boost student engagement, learning achievements, and critical skills for the 21st century.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2606-9.ch006.venue: Data-Driven Innovation, Curriculum Transformation, and Learner Success in Higher Education

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch006.title: Extracting Personality Traits From Digital Identity on Social Media
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch006.abstract: <jats:p>This research investigates the potential of extracting personality traits from social media linguistic productions, focusing on Moroccan users' digital identity. Using an experimental exploratory methodology, the study applies IBM Watson's Personality Insights—grounded in the Big Five model—to fourteen Facebook and Twitter profiles. Data was gathered via netnography between 2020 and 2021 from accounts selected for rich expression and accessibility. Results confirm the feasibility of detecting traits like openness and conscientiousness, though accuracy varies; Arabic texts showed weaker correlations (mean absolute error – 0.09–0.12) than English. The study reveals that specific linguistic choices significantly influence algorithmic outputs, raising questions regarding potential manipulation. Ultimately, this novel application of AI to Moroccan bilingual data underscores the promise of digital psychology while emphasizing the critical need for enhanced algorithmic precision and contextualized interpretation in future research.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch006.venue: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

doi:10.58421/misro.v5i3.869.title: The Influence of Social Media on Students' Mathematical Communication Skills in Mathematics Learning
doi:10.58421/misro.v5i3.869.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to analyze the effect of social media use on students' mathematical communication skills. It employs a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design (non-equivalent control group design). The sample consisted of 60 eighth-grade students, divided into an experimental group and a control group. The experimental group received social media-assisted mathematics learning, while the control group received traditional instruction. The research instruments included a questionnaire on social media use and a mathematical communication skills test. The questionnaire used a 1-to-5 Likert scale, while the mathematical communication skills test was assessed using a rating scale with scores categorized into three levels: high, medium, and low, defined by intervals of values. Data analysis was performed using simple linear regression and a comparison of means between the two groups. This analysis was conducted using SPSS software. The results showed a significant difference in average mathematical communication skills between the experimental and control groups . Inferential analysis revealed that social media use had a significant effect on students' mathematical communication skills.  Furthermore, regression analysis showed that social media use contributed 27.4% to the development of students' mathematical communication skills, with the remainder influenced by other factors external to the study. These results indicate that social media can be a promising pedagogical tool for improving mathematical communication skills through interaction, collaboration, and the interactive exchange of information. Therefore, integrating social media into mathematics learning could create a more communicative and participatory learning environment.</jats:p>
doi:10.58421/misro.v5i3.869.venue: Journal of Mathematics Instruction, Social Research and Opinion

doi:10.3389/fpubh.2026.1871339.title: Machine learning analysis of the association between psychosocial risks and burnout syndrome in mining workers
doi:10.3389/fpubh.2026.1871339.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Burnout syndrome represents a critical issue in occupational health, particularly in high-demand contexts such as mining, where physical, environmental, and psychosocial risks converge and affect workers' wellbeing and job performance. In this context, the study objective is to analyze the association between psychosocial risk factors and burnout syndrome among mining workers in Moquegua, Peru.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A quantitative, analytical cross-sectional study with a non-experimental design was conducted. The study population consisted of 65 workers from a mining unit in Moquegua, Peru. Given the complete accessibility of the target population, a census approach was adopted, and all eligible workers were included in the study (
                      <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                      = 65). Validated instruments were used, including the SUSESO/ISTAS21 questionnaire for psychosocial risks and the Maslach Burnout Inventory. Data analysis involved descriptive and correlational statistics, multiple linear regression, and machine learning techniques.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings revealed significant associations between psychosocial factors particularly social support, leadership, and work–family conflict (double presence) and burnout. All analyzed factors demonstrated significant associations capacity, with double presence emerging as the most influential predictor. Furthermore, machine learning analyses identified relevant burnout-related patterns within the analyzed dataset, highlighting their effectiveness in identifying burnout-related patterns.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Burnout in mining is a multifactorial phenomenon influenced by organizational and psychosocial conditions. The results support the use of machine learning as an useful tool for identifying psychosocial risk patterns that may support prevention strategies, contributing to improved occupational health strategies in high-risk industrial settings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.70125/v93ga685.title: Academic Dropout Prediction Using Institutional Data: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Methods
doi:10.70125/v93ga685.abstract: <jats:p>The rise in academic dropout rates at universities across Brazil is notable, especially in the post-COVID-19 pandemic period. At the Federal University of Paraná (UFPR), the problem escalated after 2019, reaching peaks in 2021 and 2022, underscoring the urgency for targeted intervention. This study aims to compare different Machine Learning methods - Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Trees (DT), Random Forest (RF), Stochastic Gradient Boosting (GBM), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Neural Networks (NN) - using institutional data in undergraduate courses from UFPR (2009-2024). The fitted models are based on academic performance and course-related variables, specifically the Academic Performance Index (IRA), the Proportion of Failed Courses (PropRep), the course's academic type (Degree), and its area of knowledge (THE Area). Results showed that while all models achieved similar predictive performance (MCC ~ 0.70 | Precision > 0.90), in general, the Logistic Regression model offers high interpretability and easiness to implementation. The LR model is proposed as the most robust and transparent predictive tool for the university's management.</jats:p>
doi:10.70125/v93ga685.venue: Journal of Educational Technology Studies and Applied Research

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2721-9.ch010.title: Re-Imaging Military Education Pathways for Military-Connected Students
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2721-9.ch010.abstract: <jats:p>Military-connected students face a credential portability crisis where service mobility clashes with rigid academic structures. This creates a $15B annual economic drag on military family stability. This analysis establishes a framework integrating location-independent digital architecture with policy reform. Key mechanisms include AI for advising, VR for skill validation, and blockchain for identities. A five-year roadmap details the transition to a mastery-based, verifiable competency ecosystem.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2721-9.ch010.venue: Military-Connected Student Success in Higher Education

doi:10.65956/ltlt.2026.112.title: The dialogical teacher-self: A narrative inquiry into an EFL teacher’s professional identity
doi:10.65956/ltlt.2026.112.abstract: <jats:p>This study explores how a Vietnamese EFL lecturer constructs and negotiates his professional identity through the lens of Dialogical Self Theory (DST). Framed as a qualitative single-case narrative inquiry, the study draws on a written narrative frame and a semi-structured interview. The data were analysed using DST-informed narrative analysis, focusing on I-positions, internal and external voices, dialogical tensions, repositioning, and the maintenance of unity and continuity across the participant’s professional journey. The findings reveal that the participant’s teacher identity was constructed through a changing repertoire of I-positions, including tutor, lecturer-researcher, friend of students, mentor, responsible professional, pedagogical guide, researcher, and lifelong learner. These positions were shaped by early tutoring experience, postgraduate study, university teaching, influential others, institutional expectations, emotional tensions, artificial intelligence, and future aspirations. The participant negotiated tensions between care and academic accountability, among teaching, research, administration, and student support, and between the traditional role of knowledge provider and the emerging role of pedagogical guide in response to AI. Despite these tensions, he maintained a coherent sense of professional self through salient orientations as a supportive educator, developing professional, and opportunity-opening teacher. The study contributes to EFL teacher identity research by showing how narrative inquiry and DST can illuminate teacher identity as a multivoiced, relational, and evolving process of becoming situated within Vietnamese higher education.</jats:p>
doi:10.65956/ltlt.2026.112.venue: Journal of Language Teaching and Learning Today

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1755916.title: Effectiveness of Camtasia-supported flipped learning on improving self-learning achievement among female students at the college of basic education
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1755916.abstract: <jats:p>The main concern of this research is to investigate the effect of implementing Camtasia Studio in activating flipped learning method on improving self-learn achievement among female students at the College of Basic Education in the State of Kuwait. This research adopted the descriptive approach to analyze the literature and the quasi-descriptive approach based the two groups (experimental and control), with the two measurements (the pre-test and post-test), in addition to the Follow-up measurement. The tool of the research involved a questionnaire consisted of (30) statements distributed to six axes. It was applied to a sample that comprised (66) students enrolled in the Department of Educational Technology. The experimental group adopted the flipped learning model which provided instructional videos produced by Camtasia Studio, while the control group adopted the traditional method of learning. The Post-test results indicated that there are statistically significant differences in favor of the experimental group. These results prove the effectiveness of the program in improving the level of self-achievement. Furthermore, the Follow-up measurement reveals sustainable positive effects after two weeks of its implementation, thus reflecting the effectiveness of this strategy. In light of these results, this research highly recommends the implementation of flipped learning supported by Camtasia Studio in the educational fields, when teaching the courses of educational technology, and in other fields.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch004.title: An Attention-Augmented U-Net Model for Lung Region Segmentation From Chest X-Ray Images
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch004.abstract: <jats:p>Lung segmentation from chest X-ray images plays an important role in the early diagnosis of pulmonary diseases such as pneumonia, lung cancer, and COVID-19. Manual segmentation is time-consuming and susceptible to observer variability, creating the need for automated and reliable approaches. This study proposes an Attention-Augmented U-Net model for accurate lung region segmentation. The proposed framework enhances the conventional U-Net architecture by integrating Attention Gates (AGs) into skip connections between encoder and decoder layers, enabling the network to focus on relevant lung regions while suppressing background structures. Publicly available chest X-ray datasets were used for training and evaluation with preprocessing techniques including normalization and data augmentation. Experimental results achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.93 and improved segmentation performance compared with conventional U-Net models. The proposed system may support radiologists in computer-aided diagnosis and collaborative clinical workflows.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9725-2.ch001.title: AI-Driven Personalization in Education
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9725-2.ch001.abstract: <jats:p>The swift development in areas like machine learning, natural language processing, and data-driven computation has made artificial intelligence a revolutionary concept in contemporary learning. In this chapter, three critical pedagogical aspects facilitated by the application of AI in modern education are analyzed. They are adaptive learning systems, which personalize the content and its delivery pace; automated assessment systems, which provide a detailed evaluation of students' achievements; and intelligent tutoring systems, which simulate individual assistance of teachers. Evidence based on the empirical research conducted from 2014 to 2024 is collected in order to discuss learning results achieved through AI use, as well as its design and implementation issues. Key aspects of the discussed learning systems and studies focused on them are presented in comparative tables. Special attention is paid to the ethical and social implications associated with this phenomenon.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10300349/v1.title: A Physics-Informed Hypoplasticity–Machine Learning Framework for Offshore Foundation Design: Comparative Insights from the German North Sea and the Peruvian Pacific Coast
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10300349/v1.abstract: Background Offshore foundation design increasingly requires constitutive models capable of reproducing the strongly non-linear, rate-dependent, and cyclic response of marine soils, while remaining computationally tractable for iterative design. Hypoplasticity offers a mathematically consistent alternative to classical elastoplastic formulations, and Machine Learning (ML) offers efficient pattern recognition, yet the literature rarely couples the two within an explicit, physically constrained pipeline, and almost never discusses how such a coupling could be transferred from mature offshore markets to emerging ones. Methods We develop a physics-informed hypoplasticity-ML framework grounded in established hypoplastic formulations for sand and clay, define an explicit coupling and validation protocol (k-fold cross-validation, R², RMSE, MAE, confidence intervals), and build a structured comparative matrix contrasting geotechnical, regulatory, and technological conditions in Germany, Peru, and the United States, synthesising quantitative findings already reported in the peer-reviewed literature rather than presenting unverified primary data. Results The comparative matrix identifies which elements of the German hypoplasticity-ML pipeline are directly transferable to Peru (constitutive formulation, ML validation protocol, p-y curve generation methodology) and which require substantial local recalibration (soil database, seismic coupling, liquefaction screening). Free-body equilibrium diagrams for monopile, jacket, and gravity-based foundations are used to make explicit the physical principles that any constitutive-ML coupling must respect. Conclusions A technology-transfer pathway is proposed in which the mathematical core of hypoplasticity-ML coupling developed for German offshore wind conditions can be adapted to Peru through regional recalibration, seismic-liquefaction extensions, and a phased data-acquisition programme, without requiring reproduction of the full German site-investigation infrastructure. The conclusions drawn are explicitly limited to what the synthesised evidence supports; site-specific validation for Peruvian conditions remains an open research need.

doi:10.3389/feart.2026.1748893.title: A framework for earthquake seismic signal classification with the aid of hybrid feature selection schemes and robust machine learning models
doi:10.3389/feart.2026.1748893.abstract: <jats:p>One of the most catastrophic natural events is an earthquake, which causes huge destruction to humanity, thus necessitating the use of seismic signals to detect and classify them. Many machine learning models have been proposed that act as automated earthquake detection and classification methods by using seismic signals. However, the proposed method in this study utilizes the concept of learning-based feature extraction from seismic signals such as graph-embedding learning (GEL), through low-rank representation (LRR) and robust neighborhood embedding (RNE). In a parallel approach, statistical feature extraction approaches such as cross-correlation function (CCF) and partial CCF (PCCF) are implemented with multivariate variational mode decomposition (MVMD). Kriging model-based feature selection and K-best features selection techniques are then utilized, and the features are finally classified with the standard machine learning classifiers. This combined approach is considered a novel technique. The second technique proposed in this study utilizes the concept of reinforcement learning (RL) Bayesian networks (BNs) with the AdaBoost-based Elman neural network (ENN) model known altogether as the “RL–BN–AENN model” with extracted and selected features. Third, a differential evolution (DE)-based Bayesian classifier is proposed, the DE-BC model, with extracted and selected features. Finally, the concept of linear discriminant analysis (LDA) is utilized with a fuzzy weighted relevance vector machine, the LDA–FW–relevance vector machine (RVM) model, and the same LDA is utilized with a fruit fly optimization algorithm (FFOA) and support vector machine (SVM) concept, the LDA–FFOA–SVM model, which is utilized with extracted and selected features. The results show that a high classification accuracy of 98.89% is obtained for the two-class classification problem when LLR with Kriging model feature selection and the AdaBoost–ENN classifier are implemented. A high classification accuracy of 92.95% is obtained for the three-class classification problem when PCCF with MVMD and Kriging model feature selection classified with the LDA–FFOA–SVM classifier is implemented.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch003.title: Identification of Pneumonia in Chest X-Ray Images Using Generative and Explainable AI Methods
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch003.abstract: <jats:p>Pneumonia remains a significant global health concern, particularly in regions with limited access to specialized medical expertise. Chest X-ray imaging is widely used for diagnosis; however, interpretation is subjective and dependent on experienced radiologists. This chapter presents a deep learning-based framework for automated pneumonia detection from chest X-ray images, focusing on accuracy and interpretability. To address class imbalance and improve performance, traditional data augmentation is integrated with synthetic image generation using an Auxiliary Classifier Generative Adversarial Network (ACGAN), enhancing dataset diversity. Thirty-two convolutional neural network models from Keras Applications, including EfficientNet, ResNet, DenseNet, and MobileNet, are evaluated under three experimental scenarios. Leading models such as EfficientNetB1 and MobileNet achieve accuracies above 93%. Explainable AI techniques, including Grad-CAM, SHAP, and LIME, highlight diagnostic regions, strengthening transparency, generalization, and clinical trust in AI-driven healthcare systems.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch010.title: Fieldwire Business Tier and Construction 4.0
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-2701-1.ch010.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter evaluates Fieldwire's Business Tier as a Project Management Information System (PMIS) for construction in the context of Industry 4.0 and PMBOK principles. It synthesises empirical evidence and peer-reviewed literature to map Fieldwire features to PMBOK performance domains, quantify likely operational impacts, and benchmark the Business Tier against competitors (Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud/PlanGrid). The chapter identifies organisational, technical, and governance challenges in adoption and offers an implementation roadmap, metrics for impact assessment, and research avenues. The analysis draws on systematic literature synthesis, product documentation, and proxy empirical studies to provide practitioners and researchers with evidence-based guidance on leveraging mobile-first PMIS to reduce delays, control costs, and improve stakeholder engagement.</jats:p>
