doi:10.3389/fenvs.2026.1876737.title: Can computing power infrastructure enhance mineral resource security resilience? Evidence from China using a hybrid econometric and machine learning approach
doi:10.3389/fenvs.2026.1876737.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In the era of artificial intelligence (AI), computing power infrastructure (CPI) has become a foundational pillar of the digital economy. At the same time, the security and resilience of mineral resource supply chains particularly for critical minerals such as gallium, germanium and rare earth elements face unprecedented challenges from geopolitical tensions and surging demand. Prior research has examined these two domains separately, leaving the potential of CPI to enhance mineral resource security resilience (MRSR) unexplored.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We construct a provincial CPI development index and an MRSR composite index based on a resistanceadaptationtransformation framework, using panel data from 30 Chinese provinces over 20122023. We employ a hybrid methodological approach integrating two-way fixed effects (TWFE), mediation analysis, moderation analysis, spatial Durbin models (SDM), panel threshold models, instrumental variable (IV) estimation and double machine learning (DML) for causal inference, supplemented by LASSO, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, support vector regression (SVR) and SHAP-based interpretability analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We document five key findings: (1) CPI significantly enhances MRSR (β = 0.218, p &lt; 0.01), a result robust to IV (0.276) and DML (0.243) corrections for endogeneity; (2) the effect operates through dual mediating pathways of technological innovation (24.8% mediation share) and information empowerment (18.4%); (3) digital governance capacity and regional openness positively moderate the CPIMRSR relationship; (4) the SDM reveals significant positive spatial spillover effects of CPI on neighbouring provinces MRSR; (5) panel threshold regression identifies a non-linear, marginally increasing pattern across two threshold values (γ
                      <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                      = 0.215, γ
                      <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                      = 0.478). Machine learning ensemble analysis and SHAP interpretation provide methodological triangulation that corroborates and extends the econometric findings.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results establish a novel “digital infrastructureresource security” analytical framework, showing that computing power is not only a consumer of critical minerals but also an enabler of their security. Because the returns are threshold-dependent and conditional on complementary institutions, concentrated and scaled-up computing power development should be integrated explicitly into national mineral security strategies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1921354.title: Psychometric evidence for the universal design for learning 3.0 teacher implementation questionnaire (CID-DUA3): development and preliminary validation
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1921354.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Universal Design for Learning (UDL 3.0) provides a framework for designing educational environments that anticipate barriers, broaden participation, and promote student progress. Despite its increasing incorporation into educational policy and practice, there remains a need for robust instruments capable of assessing its implementation through the self-reported frequency of specific and potentially observable teaching practices. The aim of this study was to develop the Universal Design for Learning 3.0 Teacher Implementation Questionnaire (CID-DUA3) and obtain preliminary evidence of its validity and reliability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An instrumental, non-experimental, cross-sectional study was conducted in two phases. In the first phase, an initial 20-item version was reviewed by a panel of 10 experts. Following the content validation process, a refined 12-item version was obtained. This version was subsequently administered to 91 practicing teachers. Descriptive and internal consistency analyses were conducted, together with an exploratory factor analysis based on polychoric correlations and a confirmatory factor analysis in R using the lavaan package and the mean- and variance-adjusted weighted least squares estimator.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The CID-DUA3 showed high internal consistency (
                      <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                       = 0.876; standardized
                      <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                       = 0.879). The ordinal EFA supported the retention of a single factor, and the preliminary CFA evaluation showed fit indices consistent with this structure (CFI = 0.975; TLI = 0.969; RMSEA = 0.068). In addition, teachers who reported greater knowledge of UDL obtained significantly higher questionnaire scores than those with lower levels of knowledge (

                       &lt; 0.001).
                    </jats:p>

doi:10.58230/edutech.v4i1.107.title: Needs Analysis for Gamified Learning Media Development: A Focus on Civilisation Française Course
doi:10.58230/edutech.v4i1.107.abstract: <jats:p>The Civilisation Française course presents challenges due to its complex socio-cultural, historical, and geographical content. This study conducted a needs analysis to identify requirements for developing ZepQuiz, a gamification-based learning medium. Using a descriptive quantitative approach, data were collected from 27 undergraduate students through a structured questionnaire. The findings showed that 85.2% experienced moderate-to-high learning difficulties, while 77.8% preferred interactive gamified quizzes and 55.6% preferred short videos. Students also emphasized introductory summaries, instant feedback, interactive activities, and motivational features. These findings provide an empirical basis for developing an accessible, visually supported, and interactive ZepQuiz platform.</jats:p>

doi:10.51878/science.v6i4.13726.title: EFEKTIVITAS MODEL PROBLEM-BASED LEARNING TERHADAP KEMAMPUAN KOMUNIKASI MATEMATIS SISWA DI SD NEGERI 92 PALEMBANG
doi:10.51878/science.v6i4.13726.abstract:
<jats:p>The low level of elementary school students' mathematical communication skills represents a fundamental barrier in mathematics learning, requiring innovative models that train students to articulate mathematical ideas systematically. This study aimed to determine the effectiveness of the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model on the mathematical communication skills of fifth-grade students at SD Negeri 92 Palembang in learning two-dimensional geometry. This research employed a quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design. The research population and sample consisted of all 18 students from class V.B at SD Negeri 92 Palembang during the 2025/2026 academic year selected through total sampling. The research instrument consisted of an essay test measuring mathematical communication skills that had been tested for validity and reliability. Data were analyzed using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality test and paired sample t-test via SPSS 25. The results showed that both pretest and posttest data were normally distributed (p > 0.05). The mean score of students' mathematical communication skills improved significantly from 52.78 in the pretest to 94.17 in the posttest, with an average increase of 41.39 points. The paired sample t-test yielded a t-count of -8.919 with a significance value of p = 0.000 (p < 0.05), confirming a statistically significant difference between pretest and posttest scores. Thus, the Problem-Based Learning model is proven effective in enhancing the mathematical communication skills of fifth-grade elementary school students.
ABSTRAK
Rendahnya kemampuan komunikasi matematis siswa sekolah dasar menjadi kendala mendasar dalam pembelajaran matematika, sehingga diperlukan model pembelajaran inovatif yang mampu melatih siswa mengartikulasikan ide secara terstruktur. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui efektivitas model Problem-Based Learning (PBL) terhadap kemampuan komunikasi matematis siswa kelas V SD Negeri 92 Palembang pada materi bangun datar. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode pra-eksperimen berdesain one-group pretest-posttest design. Populasi penelitian adalah seluruh siswa kelas V.B SD Negeri 92 Palembang Tahun Ajaran 2025/2026 yang berjumlah 18 siswa, dengan penentuan sampel menggunakan teknik sampling jenuh. Instrumen penelitian berupa tes esai kemampuan komunikasi matematis yang telah divalidasi dan diuji reliabilitasnya. Data dianalisis menggunakan uji normalitas Kolmogorov-Smirnov dan uji hipotesis paired sample t-test berbantuan SPSS versi 25. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa data pretest dan posttest berdistribusi normal (p>0,05). Rata-rata nilai kemampuan komunikasi matematis siswa meningkat secara signifikan dari 52,78 pada pretest menjadi 94,17 pada posttest dengan selisih rata-rata sebesar 41,39 poin. Hasil uji paired sample t-test memperoleh nilai t_"hitung" =-8,919 dengan signifikansi p=0,000<0,05, yang membuktikan adanya perbedaan yang signifikan antara hasil pretest dan posttest. Dengan demikian, model Problem-Based Learning terbukti efektif dalam meningkatkan kemampuan komunikasi matematis siswa kelas V sekolah dasar.
 
 </jats:p>
doi:10.51878/science.v6i4.13726.venue: SCIENCE : Jurnal Inovasi Pendidikan Matematika dan IPA

doi:10.9734/jesbs/2026/v39i51522.title: Personalized Learning in Virtual Learning Environments: A Systematic and Thematic Review of Technological, Pedagogical, and Learner-Centric Innovations
doi:10.9734/jesbs/2026/v39i51522.abstract:
<jats:p>Purpose: Personalised learning has emerged as an important approach for addressing learner diversity within increasingly digital and technology-mediated educational environments. This systematic and thematic review examines how personalised learning is conceptualised, implemented, and experienced within Virtual Learning Environments (VLEs), with particular attention to pedagogical design, technological integration and adaptivity, and learner agency and perception.
Methodology: A systematic literature search was conducted across Scopus, ERIC, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect for literature published between 2007 and 2024. Following screening and eligibility assessment, 35 studies were included in the final review corpus. Data were analysed using manual content analysis with a combination of deductive and inductive coding. The thematic synthesis identified eight recurrent thematic strands and three interconnected dimensions of personalised learning: pedagogical design, technological integration and adaptivity, and learner agency and experience.
Findings: The findings indicate that personalised learning is not solely a technological process but emerges through the interaction of pedagogical intentionality, technological affordances, teacher facilitation, and learner participation. Artificial intelligence, learning analytics, adaptive systems, learning management systems, and interactive technologies expand the possibilities for scalable personalisation, while concerns relating to digital inequality, algorithmic bias, data privacy, teacher readiness, and learner support remain significant. The review further highlights the importance of balancing learner autonomy with structured guidance and situating personalisation within broader principles of equity, accessibility, ethical governance, and Sustainable Development Goal 4.
Conclusion: The review concludes that effective personalised learning in VLEs requires a human-centred integration of pedagogy, technology, and learner agency, supported by inclusive infrastructure, appropriate teacher capacity, and stronger empirical evidence from diverse and longitudinal contexts.</jats:p>
doi:10.9734/jesbs/2026/v39i51522.venue: Journal of Education, Society and Behavioural Science

doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i8p102.title: Explainable Deep Tabular Learning with SHAP-Guided Feature Optimization and Squeeze-Excitation Enhanced TabNet for Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Classification
doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i8p102.abstract: <jats:p>Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most prevalent reproductive endocrinopathies in women of reproductive age. This requires diagnostic systems that reliable and interpretable. This paper presents a deep tabular framework that like to maintain efficiency in the classification of Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome (PCOS) through effective data pre-processing, synthetic balancing of data, and optimizing for significant features. Initially, the clinical dataset is preprocessed by iterative imputation, outlier handling, feature normalization and synthetic balancing for statistical consistency and robust model learning. The study uses Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) to augment the sample diversity and address class imbalance by generating additional minority samples. Moreover, a Transformer-based feature extractor captures associations between features to encode better reference feature embeddings. Then, performing Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)-guided feature selection using an XGBoost explainer to determine what predictors are most important in the model performance, hence improving both interpretability and computational efficiency. The TabNet-SE ahead of running the baseline model, i.e.Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost, in addition both conducting of these steps with the complete feature set and also SHAP-selected features. The experimental results show that TabNet-SE consistently outperforms all baseline models in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score when trained on the set of features optimized with SHAP. Model performance was further corroborated with confusion matrix, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve, and other evaluation metrics. This framework not only facilitates accurate diagnosis of PCOS but also enhances interpretability, thus bridging the gap between clinical requirements and model transparency.</jats:p>
doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i8p102.venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10727616/v1.title: Metacognitive Instruction for Metaphor Learning: Effects on Metacognitive Awareness, Self-Efficacy, and Learning Performance among Chinese EFL Learners
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10727616/v1.abstract: This study examines the effects of metacognitive instruction (MI) on Chinese EFL learners’ metacognitive awareness of metaphor learning (MAML), self-efficacy in metaphor learning (SEML), and metaphor learning performance (MLP) among Chinese EFL undergraduates. It aims to extend current understanding of metaphor pedagogy by investigating how metacognitive support facilitates learners’ regulation of cognitive awareness, self-efficacy, and metaphor learning outcomes. A quasi-experimental design was adopted with 70 Chinese EFL undergraduates assigned to an experimental group (EG) receiving metacognitive instruction and a control group (CG) following conventional Presentation–Practice–Production (PPP) instruction. Pretest and post-test data were collected through MAIML, QMSEML, and MLPT. Independent-samples t-tests and one-way ANCOVA were conducted to examine post-intervention differences between the two groups. The results reveal that the EG significantly outperformed the CG in MAML, SEML, and MLP after the intervention. The metacognitive intervention was particularly effective in promoting learners’ metacognitive knowledge and regulation, with notable gains in conditional knowledge and debugging skills. Learners in the EG also demonstrated stronger SEML, especially academic self-efficacy. Regarding MLP, the EG showed significant improvement in complex metaphor construction. These findings suggest that effective metaphor learning involves not only acquiring figurative expressions but also developing the ability to understand and regulate the cognitive processes involved in interpreting and using metaphorical language. This study contributes to metaphor pedagogy by demonstrating the value of metacognitive instruction for supporting learners’ metacognitive awareness, self-efficacy, and metaphor learning performance. It extends research on metacognitive instruction beyond conventional EFL skills by highlighting the roles of metacognitive awareness and self-efficacy in metaphor learning. The findings provide theoretical and pedagogical implications for designing more effective EFL metaphor instruction.

doi:10.3998/mjcsl.8184.title: Using Virtual Reality to Advance Psychology, Social Justice, and Service-Learning Goals
doi:10.3998/mjcsl.8184.abstract: <jats:p>Psychology and service-learning both aim to cultivate empathy, ethical responsibility, and engagement with diverse communities. As educators seek innovative approaches to support these learning outcomes, immersive virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising experiential tool for exposing students to perspectives and social issues that may be outside their lived experience. This paper examines the use of VR within a psychology service-learning course grounded in social justice and critical reflection. Students (N = 81) participated in the immersive VR simulation “Becoming Homeless: A Human Experience” (Ogle et al., 2018) and provided qualitative feedback regarding their experience. Using thematic analysis, we explored students’ perceptions of the activity’s educational value, impact, and limitations. Students overwhelmingly reported that the experience enhanced empathy, perspective-taking, and awareness of housing instability while also highlighting the engaging nature of the immersive technology. Some students described increased motivation to help others and challenge stereotypes, whereas a small number reported physical discomfort associated with VR use. Beyond presenting student feedback, this paper considers the broader role of VR in psychology and service-learning education, including its potential to support social justice learning outcomes, foster critical reflection, and complement community-engaged pedagogies. We also discuss the limitations and ethical considerations associated with using immersive simulations to represent marginalized experiences. Findings suggest that VR can serve as a valuable experiential learning tool when embedded within reflective, justice-oriented educational frameworks.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10894069/v1.title: Monte Carlo Positive-Unlabeled Two-Step Learning for Landslide Susceptibility Mapping under Inventory Uncertainty: Comparison with Hard-Threshold PU Two-Step and EIV in Northern Morocco
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10894069/v1.abstract: Landslide susceptibility mapping depends critically on the definition of the non-landslide class. In many study areas, including the Rif of northern Morocco, the completeness of landslide inventories cannot be guaranteed, making conventional random absence sampling unreliable. This study proposes MC-PU-2S (Monte Carlo Positive-Unlabeled Two-Step), a probabilistic extension of classical PU Two-Step learning, and compares it with Enhanced Information Value ( EIV ) and deterministic PU Two-Step on a database of 5,877 observations (2,320 mapped landslides, 3,557 unlabeled) described by 21 conditioning factors. All three methods share the same Random Forest classifier and are evaluated under a five-fold spatial block cross-validation to prevent spatial leakage. EIV selects reliable negatives deterministically from the lowest-susceptibility quantile of a preliminary model. PU Two-Step applies a hard threshold (30th percentile) to an out-of-bag PU Bagging score. MC-PU-2S converts those scores into Bernoulli membership probabilities \(\:{\pi\:}_{i}=1-\:g\left({u}_{i}\right)\) ,resamples M plausible reliable-negative sets, and aggregates M Random Forest predictions into a mean susceptibility surface \(\:\widehat{u}\left(x\right)\:\)and an uncertainty surface \(\:\widehat{\sigma\:}\) (x). The five-fold cross-validation yielded mean ROC-AUC values of 0.641 (EIV), 0.637 (PU Two-Step), and 0.673 (MC-PU-2S); mean Brier scores of 0.434, 0.389, and 0.236, respectively. Calibration analysis confirms that EIV and PU Two-Step produce poorly calibrated probabilities (slope beta approx. 0.45), whereas MC-PU-2S approaches the ideal. Beyond predictive metrics, MC-PU-2S produces three additional cartographic products — an uncertainty map, a confidence index CoI, and a mask of indeterminate areas— that support risk-differentiated decision-making. The main contribution is methodological: MC-PU-2S extends deterministic PU Two-Step into an uncertainty-aware framework by propagating variability in pseudo-negative selection all the way to the final susceptibility products.

doi:10.3389/fcell.2026.1896989.title: Machine learning models for predicting liver cancer: a real-world cohort study in China
doi:10.3389/fcell.2026.1896989.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Liver cancer has high incidence and mortality worldwide, and timely identification is important for improving prognosis. However, prediction models based on routinely available clinical data remain insufficiently evaluated in hospitalized real-world populations. This study aimed to develop and interpret a machine-learning model for liver cancer prediction using multidimensional clinical and laboratory features.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This retrospective real-world cohort included 9,284 hospitalized patients from Hainan General Hospital between January 2020 and December 2023. Patients were divided into a training set (n = 6,426) and an internal validation set (n = 2,858). Seventy-four demographic, clinical, and laboratory variables were collected. Feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression in the training set. Six models were developed: logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbors, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and Elastic Net. Discrimination was assessed primarily using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Decision curve analysis evaluated clinical net benefit, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Liver cancer accounted for 48.7% of the training cohort and 48.8% of the validation cohort. LASSO retained 57 nonzero model terms at the minimum-error penalty. XGBoost achieved the highest AUC among all models, with an AUC of 0.909 (95% CI, 0.903–0.915) in the training set and 0.802 (95% CI, 0.788–0.817) in the validation set. At a threshold of 0.5, validation accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score were 0.730, 0.758, 0.698, and 0.753, respectively. Decision curve analysis showed that XGBoost provided the greatest net clinical benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis identified serum sialic acid, the aspartate aminotransferase-to-alanine aminotransferase ratio, alkaline phosphatase, basophil percentage, and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio as the leading predictors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>XGBoost showed good discrimination and interpretability for liver cancer prediction in a hospitalized real-world cohort using routinely available clinical and laboratory data. The findings support the feasibility of leveraging large-scale inpatient laboratory data for risk-stratification model development. Serum sialic acid, the aspartate aminotransferase-to-alanine aminotransferase ratio, and alkaline phosphatase were important predictors. Prospective validation in outpatient, first-visit, high-risk, and external populations is required before broader clinical or screening application.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.3389/fcell.2026.1896989.venue: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology

doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i8p104.title: Hybrid Resampling and Ensemble Learning for Predicting Radiation-Induced Pneumonitis in Head and Neck Cancer
doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i8p104.abstract: <jats:p>Radiation-Induced Pneumonitis (RP) is a clinically important but difficult-to-predict toxicity in Head and Neck Cancer (HNC), particularly when only routinely collected hospital variables are available. This study developed a recall-oriented machine learning framework for RP prediction using clinical and treatment-related data from 2,482 HNC patients treated with radiotherapy between 2018 and 2024. Twenty-five baseline variables and four engineered interaction terms were analysed using a stratified 70/30 train–test split. Three phase-wise experiments were performed: Phase I on the original imbalanced training data, Phase II with SMOTETomek-based class balancing, and Phase III as an extension of Phase II with Gaussian-noise data augmentation. XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and SVM were evaluated as individual classifiers, while the proposed stacking classifier combined XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost with Logistic Regression as the meta-learner. Hyperparameters were optimized by Bayesian search with stratified cross-validation, and thresholds were selected from training-only out-of-fold probabilities using F2-score as the primary criterion. In Phase I, the stacking classifier achieved the highest F2-score 0.57 and recall 0.86. In Phase II, the stacking classifier achieved the highest F2-score 0.58 and ROC-AUC 0.67. In Phase III, it again performed best overall, with a precision 0.24, recall 0.92, F2-score 0.59, and ROC-AUC 0.65. These findings support stacking-based prediction as a screening-oriented aid for identifying high-risk RP cases from routinely available hospital records.</jats:p>

doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i8p113.title: Leakage-Proof Reliability-Aware Deep Learning Framework for Rice Leaf Disease Diagnosis
doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i8p113.abstract: <jats:p>Timely and accurate diagnosis of rice leaf diseases is significant in order to achieve reduced loss and precision agriculture management. In this paper, a leakage-aware and reliability-oriented deep learning framework is proposed to classify rice leaf diseases based on the Mendeley rice leaf disease dataset. In order to avoid the problem of similar and duplicate images in the training and validation set, the framework incorporates perceptual hashing and stratified group K-fold cross-validation. The evaluation measures the accuracy of the in-domain classification, robustness to controlled image corruption, evaluation of the Expected Calibration Error and temperature scaling methods, selective prediction using risk-coverage analysis, external-dataset validation, and computational efficiency profiling. The in-domain evaluation resulted in an almost perfect score. The accuracy achieved by the cross-validation method applied to the folds evaluated showed high values, while the external UCI rice leaf dataset presented significantly lower values, with an accuracy of 54.17% and macro-F1 of 48.98%. This contrast suggests that high in-domain accuracy should be considered with caution if there is a domain shift. In addition, efficiency and reliability analysis indicated that mid-scale convolutional models, especially ResNet-based models, achieved a better trade-off between predictive performance and computational cost compared to larger high-capacity models. The suggested assessment scheme in the proposed framework then focuses not only on accuracy but also on deployment-oriented evaluation in the context of rice leaf disease diagnosis with the help of AI.</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s40359-026-05491-5.title: Development of the online course learning adjustment scale for undergraduate
doi:10.1186/s40359-026-05491-5.abstract: Online learning differs substantially from traditional classroom learning in terms of instructional supervision, interaction, environmental distraction, and demands for self-regulation. However, instruments specifically designed to assess undergraduates’ adjustment to online course learning remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate the Online Course Learning Adjustment Scale for Undergraduates. An initial pool of 29 items was generated through a literature review, semi-structured interviews with 20 undergraduates, and evaluations by experts and graduate students in psychology and education. The initial questionnaire was administered to 217 undergraduates for item analysis and exploratory factor analysis. An independent sample of 532 undergraduates was then used for confirmatory factor analysis, criterion-related validity analysis, and reliability testing. Item analysis indicated that all initial items had adequate discriminatory power. Exploratory factor analysis resulted in a 22-item scale comprising four factors: online learning ability, online learning behavior, online learning attention, and online learning attitude. The four factors explained 57.83% of the total variance. Confirmatory factor analysis showed that the four-factor model provided a good fit to the data and performed better than the alternative three-factor model (χ²/df = 2.288, RMSEA = 0.049, CFI = 0.948, TLI = 0.941, and SRMR = 0.047). The total scale demonstrated good internal consistency reliability (Cronbach’s α = 0.894) and split-half reliability (0.763). The total score and four subscale scores were positively correlated with academic performance (r = 0.157–0.378, all p < 0.01), supporting criterion-related validity. The Online Course Learning Adjustment Scale for Undergraduates demonstrates satisfactory factorial validity, criterion-related validity, and reliability. It may serve as a useful instrument for assessing undergraduates’ adjustment to online course learning and identifying areas in which students require additional educational support.

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1938135.title: A machine learning-based adaptive platform is associated with cognitive improvements in Peruvian secondary school students: a quasi-experimental study
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1938135.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    This study determined the impact of a personalized educational platform based on machine learning (ML) on the cognitive learning of secondary education students at a public institution in Piura, Peru. The research followed an applied, quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental design. A sample of 56 fourth-grade students was distributed into a control group (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 26, traditional teaching) and an experimental group (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 30, platform-assisted teaching), using two pre-existing classrooms randomly assigned to each condition. Cognitive learning was assessed across four dimensions (attention, memory, reasoning, and comprehension) with pretest and posttest exams administered at the start and end of the same two-hour session per topic, over three consecutive weeks. The platform combined an unsupervised clustering model for cognitive profiling with a supervised classifier that predicted, in real time, the optimal content level for each student. Analyses were based on improvement scores (posttest - pretest); intergroup comparisons used the Mann–Whitney U test with rank-biserial effect sizes, and the relationship between platform metrics and the posttest score was examined through Spearman correlations. Results showed significant differences favoring the experimental group across the three topics (
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     &lt; .001), with increasing effect sizes (r = 0.527, 0.610, 0.738), confirmed through a sensitivity analysis that controlled for the pretest. The experimental group achieved an average improvement of 8.29 points out of 20, versus 4.90 for the control group. Requested adaptations showed a moderate association on average with the posttest score (
                    <jats:italic>ρ</jats:italic>
                     = 0.485,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     &lt; .001), strengthening over the course of the intervention (up to
                    <jats:italic>ρ</jats:italic>
                     = 0.588), while the predictive weight of the initial micro-diagnostic declined progressively. The platform was associated with a significant, progressive, and dimension-differentiated improvement, although the single-classroom-per-condition design and the within-session measurement warrant interpretive caution. This work contributes to inclusive education in resource-limited contexts and aligns with Sustainable Development Goals 4 and 10.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.18494/sam6437.title: Microclimate Air Temperature Prediction Method Based on Difference Prediction and Transfer Learning
doi:10.18494/sam6437.abstract: Microclimate air temperature varies substantially over short distances because of local factors such as buildings, vegetation, solar radiation, and shading.Dense observations can capture this variability, but long-term deployment at many target sites is costly.This study evaluates an long short-term memory (LSTM)-based framework for air-temperature prediction at data-scarce microclimate sites using a nearby public meteorological station as a reference.The model predicts the temperature difference between the target site and the reference station instead of directly predicting the target-site temperature.Transfer learning is also introduced by pretraining the model on other nearby microclimate sites and fine-tuning it using limited targetsite data.The framework was evaluated using observations from Wakayama University and the automated meteorological data acquisition system (AMeDAS) Wakayama station.Difference prediction reduced root mean square error (RMSE) compared with direct prediction at all evaluated sites.Transfer learning did not always improve the best accuracy when sufficient target-site data were available, but it improved robustness when fine-tuning data were limited or seasonally different from the evaluation period.These results suggest that difference prediction and transfer learning can support practical air-temperature prediction at data-scarce microclimate sites under conditions similar to those examined in this study.

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10967756/v1.title: How Reliable and Explainable Are Machine Learning Models for Dementia Detection? A Leakage-Aware Evaluation
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10967756/v1.abstract: Reported dementia-classification performance depends on how the label is defined, which clinical information the model sees, and whether participants are separated between training and test data. We examine these choices on OASIS-2 (373 visits, 150 participants) using demographics, education, the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), and three global magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) measures. The outcome is a Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) above zero at the visit, not diagnosis or conversion. Nine modeling procedures are tuned within five outer and three inner participant-grouped folds, and the procedure is selected inside each training partition. Conditional on this partitioning, the selected procedure reaches a pooled area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.867 (95% participant-bootstrap interval 0.817 to 0.915), accuracy 0.786, sensitivity 0.689, and specificity 0.864. MMSE alone gives mean fold ROC-AUC of 0.85 to 0.86. Against a matched clinical-only comparator, MRI raises logistic-regression ROC-AUC by 0.035 (exploratory interval 0.007 to 0.061), while the four tree-based contrasts have intervals spanning zero. Supplying CDR itself yields perfect accuracy in all five positive controls, and row-level cross-validation raises CatBoost from 0.865 to 0.913; the protocols also differ in stratification and tuning. Held-out XGBoost attributions are dominated by MMSE in every fold and describe model behavior, not validated clinical explanations. The MRI contribution is learner-dependent, and independent-cohort and prospective validation remain necessary.

doi:10.1108/978-1-80686-777-620261003.title: Access to Quality Education: A Study on How the Tertiary Education System of Mauritius and South Africa Reflects This Goal
doi:10.1108/978-1-80686-777-620261003.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>For emphasis to be laid on the question, “for whom higher education is about,” it shows that there is a disparity in terms of the availability or accessibility of higher education to people around the globe. The right to education, in itself, is a fundamental basic human right which should be, if not, within the reach of every human being on the planet, regardless of any factors which might discriminate against them in any way, such as race, gender, religion, political affiliation, sexual orientation, etc. The purpose of this study is to analyze how, by making tertiary education accessible to all (including students with disabilities), the core missions of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) can be achieved. In Mauritius, free access to public universities contributed positively to the inclusion of diversity and equity. Similarly, as for South Africa, despite its challenges and differences in terms of its geography, history, and journey of economic and political stability, it has also been able to show a good record of more females pursuing tertiary education. Hence, the authors note that the goal is similar for both countries but the method of achieving the same result could be different. This study aims at looking into the inputs of each country to address the gap between access to quality education and equity, diversity, and inclusion and how does this help in creating a better future for human societies with education as a main focus.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10424779/v1.title: Participation Before Proficiency: A Three-Year Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study of Motivation and Engagement in Bilingual STEAM Learning Through a Triple-On Learning Ecology
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10424779/v1.abstract: Background The convergence of competency-based STEAM reforms and Taiwan’s Bilingual 2030 Policy has stimulated growing interest in Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) as an approach to bilingual STEAM education. Within such contexts, sustaining learners’ motivation and engagement remains a central challenge, particularly when students are expected to participate in cognitively demanding disciplinary practices through an emerging second language. Young learners frequently encounter a cognitive–linguistic bottleneck when engaging in inquiry, engineering design, and problem-solving through an emerging second language. Although previous studies have documented the benefits of CLIL, little is known about how learners’ motivation and engagement are sustained, how bilingual STEAM participation develops longitudinally, or how pedagogical mediation supports learners when linguistic resources lag behind disciplinary demands. This three-year mixed-methods case study examined a vertically articulated CLIL-STEAM curriculum to investigate students’ English achievement, learning experiences, and the ecological processes that shaped bilingual participation across Grades 4 to 6 in a Taiwanese public primary school (N = 89). Results Semester-level analyses indicated significantly higher English achievement during CLIL-STEAM intervention semesters than during adjacent non-intervention semesters in Grades 4 and 5, with moderate effect sizes, whereas the Grade 6 comparison was not statistically significant. Across the three-year period, intervention-semester composites exceeded non-intervention composites by 2.68 points, t (88) = 6.35, p < .001, Cohen’s d z = 0.67, a pattern further supported by linear mixed-effects modeling. Qualitative analyses of annual focus group interviews, classroom observations, and student artifacts revealed that bilingual participation and learner engagement were sustained despite persistent language anxiety. Three interrelated patterns emerged: (1) hands-on design and peer collaboration provided equitable entry points for participation regardless of English proficiency; (2) purposeful communication and multimodal resources enabled students to negotiate linguistic challenges while engaging in disciplinary inquiry; and (3) repeated engagement with civic-oriented STEAM projects repositioned English from a test-oriented subject to a functional resource for problem-solving and public communication, thereby strengthening learners’ motivation for meaningful language use. These developmental processes were mediated through material prototyping, multimodal representation, and trans-semiotizing practices that expanded students’ opportunities for meaningful participation and communication. Conclusion The findings suggest that bilingual STEAM development is better understood as a mediated, non-linear process than as language acceleration alone. The proposed Triple-On Learning Ecology explains this process through the interaction of Head-On disciplinary challenge, Hands-On material and multimodal mediation, and Minds-On collaborative meaning-making. The study argues that participation can precede proficiency, competence can be distributed across learners and semiotic resources, and communicative agency can emerge through authentic disciplinary practice. By demonstrating how authentic participation sustains learners’ motivation and engagement while language proficiency is still developing, the study contributes to current discussions on learner engagement, CLIL, and second language learning in interdisciplinary educational contexts.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10424779/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.15294/ujmer.v1i1.12328.title: Kemampuan Komunikasi Matematis Siswa Ditinjau dari Linguistik Matematika pada Problem Based Learning Bernuansa Etnomatematika Budaya Bima
doi:10.15294/ujmer.v1i1.12328.abstract: <jats:p>Kemampuan komunikasi matematis  merupakan salah satu kompetensi  yang di anggap penting dan harus dikuasai oleh seluruh siswa. Indikator kemampuan komunikasi matematis yang dibahas pada penelitian ini adalah (1) menyajikan masalah matematematika dalam bentuk objek (gambar, diagram dan tabel); (2) menyusun argumen dalam penyelesaian masalah matematika; (3) menerapkan rumus matematika dalam menyelesaikan masalah. Linguistik matematika adalah salah satu pendekatan yang dapat menghubungakan kemampuan matematis terutama dalam kemampuan komunikasi matematis. Linguistik matematika dapat mempengaruhi  tingkat kemampuan  komunikasi matematis siswa berdasarkan linguistik matematika rendah, sedang dan tinggi. Model pembelajaran yang mendukung  dalam peningkatan kemampuan komunikasi matematis siswa salah satunya adalah model pembelajaran Problem Based Learning bernuansa etnomatematika budaya Bima. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk (1) menganalisis  kualitas pembelajaran  dengan model Problem Based Learning  bernuansa etnomatematika budaya Bima dalam meningkatkan kemapuan komunikasi matematis siswa, dan (2) menganalisis kemampuan komunikasi matematis siswa ditinjau dari linguistik matematika siswa pada pembelajaran Problem Based Learning bernuansa etnomatematika budaya Bima. Metode penelitian ini adalah  metode mixed method dengan model sequantial eksplanatory. Penelitian ini dilaksanakan di MTs Negeri 3 Bima dengan sampel  penelitian kelas VIII A sebagai kelas eksperimen  dan kelas VIII B sebagai kelas kontrol. Subjek penelitian kualitatif ditentukan berdasarkan linguistik matematika siswa. Teknik analisis data menggunakan uji t dan uji z, sedangkan untuk analisis data kualitatif menggunakana uji keabsahan data, reduksi data, penyajian data dan penarikan kesimpulan. Berdasarkan hasil penelitian  diperoleh informasi  bahwa pembelajaran berkualitas  dengan perangkat pembelajaran  dan instrumen penelitian  dengan kategori baik dan keterlaksanaan pembelajaran   dengan kategori sangatt baik.  Penilaian hasil pembelajaran  dengan model  Problem Based Learning bernuansa etnomatematika budaya Bima lebih dari KKM 75, tuntas klasikal > 75%, rata-rata kemampuan komunikasi matematis siswa  dan proporsi ketuntasan  siswa kelas eksperimen  lebih tinggi dari kelas kontrol, dan terjadi peningkatan kemampuan komunikasi matematis pada kelas eksperimen. Siswa dengan linguistik matematika rendah dan sedang hanya mampu menguasai 2 indikator kemampuan komunikasi matematis. Sedangkan siswa dengan linguistik matematika tinggi mampu menguasai semua inikator kemampuan komunikasi matematis siswa.</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/lthe-09-2025-0068.title: The impact of service quality on student satisfaction and retention in higher education
doi:10.1108/lthe-09-2025-0068.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Ensuring student retention is crucial for higher education institutions' (HEIs) survival and success. Central to this is the level of service quality that students receive during their educational journey at HEIs. However, the literature provides limited guidance on the service quality criteria that affect student retention in HEIs in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Therefore, this study aims to examine the impact of service quality dimensions on student retention and the mediating role of student satisfaction using a modified SERVQUAL model.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study employed an online survey to collect responses from students at different study levels in public and private universities in the UAE. In total, 196 responses were received and analysed using structural equation modelling.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The analysis reveals that none of the five service quality dimensions had a direct impact on student retention. However, tangibility, empathy and responsiveness of HEI services positively influence student satisfaction, whereas reliability and assurance of HEI services do not. Moreover, student satisfaction fully mediates the relationships between tangibility and student retention, and between responsiveness and student retention.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study was limited to the perspectives of service recipients (students), five dimensions of service quality and the country of the UAE. Therefore, future research can extend this study by considering the perspective of other stakeholders (e.g. staff), other service quality dimensions (e.g. accessibility) and other countries.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study emphasises the critical role of service quality in higher education and offers guidelines for improving student satisfaction and retention in the developing world context.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-4435771/v1.title: Quasi-Optic, Radio Frequency Joint Wireless Power Transfer and Machine Learning-Enabled Sensing
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-4435771/v1.abstract: Wireless power transfer could energise remote devices such as Internet of Things sensors, but is yet to be implemented as a means for direct sensing in edge receivers. While radio frequency (RF) sensing is prevalent, they typically require dedicated active receivers and special modulated waveforms. Here we improve the power transfer efficiency and introduce combined power delivery and sensing, using quasi-optically focused, multi-receiver RF power transfer system with a long indoor safe wireless powering and sensing range. The receiver simultaneously senses the operating environment through wave-matter interaction, demonstrating Joint Sensing and Powering (JSAP) from the power output fluctuations. Using a 3D-printed lens, the microwave power incident on the receiver is focused, providing multi-directional multi-beam coverage. Experimental and numerical statistical analysis shows how the indoor path-loss exponent could be reduced, improving the sensing accuracy and channel determinism through the multi-antenna lens feed. Bluetooth Low Energy nodes are demonstrated being safely powered continuously at up to 32 m distances, without additional intermediate power electronics. The focused rectennas array is used for Fresnel region and far-field sensing, showing the feasibility of breathing sensing, exploiting passive antenna-enabled accuracy improvement. Using a trained machine learning model and edge-collected data, accurate contactless people detection and localization are demonstrated, without any additional RF transceiver chains.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-4435771/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10394488/v1.title: Construction of a machine learning-based prediction model for intraoperative acquired pressure injury in children undergoing neurosurgery
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10394488/v1.abstract: Background : Intraoperative acquired pressure injury (IAPI) is a common complication in children undergoing neurosurgery, and early identification of its risk factors is essential. However, the risk factors for IAPI in this population are not well understood, and no study has reported a machine learning-based prediction model. This study aimed to construct and validate a prediction model for IAPI in children undergoing neurosurgery and to provide a reference for IAPI prevention. Methods : The clinical data of 776 children who underwent neurosurgery in a tertiary children's hospital in Chongqing from January to June 2023 were retrospectively collected. Variables were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Nine machine learning algorithms were selected, and the models were constructed and validated using tenfold cross-validation and a validation set. The predictive effects of each model were compared using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, cross-validation results, and efficiency metrics, to construct the optimal model for predicting IAPI in children undergoing neurosurgery. Finally, the SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) toolkit was used to explain and analyze the model and to identify the most important factors causing IAPI. Results : The incidence of IAPI in children undergoing neurosurgery was 7.9%. The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model had the best predictive performance, with sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1 score, and area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.8889, 0.4813, 0.126, 0.2207, and 0.7325, respectively. The decision curve showed that the predicted probability of IAPI occurrence by this model was consistent with the actual probability. Through visualization analysis of the SHAP swarm plot, clinical indicators such as intraoperative blood loss, surgical position, patient age, operation duration, anesthesia duration, and use of external force were identified as key risk factors. Conclusions : The prediction model for neurosurgical children constructed in this study has certain predictive efficacy and can provide a scientific basis for clinical nurses to identify high-risk children with IAPI early and to take personalized preventive measures.

doi:10.58723/vbbmz163.title: Interactive Scratch-Based Learning to Enhance Engagement and Digital Literacy in Early Childhood Education
doi:10.58723/vbbmz163.abstract: <jats:p>Purpose of the Study: The purpose of this study is to explore how interactive Scratch-based learning influences children's engagement and digital literacy within the context of early childhood education (PAUD). Specifically, the study examines whether integrating Scratch into the learning process improves children's attention, motivation, active participation, and fundamental digital interaction skills compared with conventional instructional methods.Methodology: The study adopted a quasi-experimental design using a non-equivalent control group approach. The participants comprised 30 children aged 4–5 years enrolled in a single early childhood education (PAUD) institution. They were assigned to two groups: an experimental group (n = 15), which participated in Scratch-based interactive learning activities, and a control group (n = 15), which received conventional storytelling-based instruction. Data were collected using observation sheets with a 4-point scale measuring focus, enthusiasm, participation, and digital literacy through pre-test and post-test observations and subsequently analyzed using paired-samples and independent-samples t-test.Main Findings: The findings revealed that children in the experimental group demonstrated significantly greater improvements across all measured variables than those in the control group. Interactive Scratch-based learning effectively increased attention, active participation, and enthusiasm during learning activities. Additionally, children demonstrated improved ability to interact with digital media and follow simple digital instructions. The effect size analysis also indicated large practical effects in the experimental group.Novelty/Originality of This Study: This study offers an empirical contribution by examining the effectiveness of Scratch-based interactive learning in early childhood education through a quasi-experimental research design. It integrates digital game-based learning with measurable engagement and digital literacy outcomes, which remains limited in research on PAUD, particularly in real classroom contexts.</jats:p>
doi:10.58723/vbbmz163.venue: JENTIK : Jurnal Pendidikan Teknologi Informasi dan Komunikasi

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10959649/v1.title: Integrated photonic Ising machine with full connectivity for ultra-large-scale combinatorial optimization
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10959649/v1.abstract: Ising machines can efficiently solve real-world combinatorial optimization problems. Among them, photonic Ising machines (PIMs) exploit the parallelism and broadband bandwidth of optical systems to outperform digital computers in certain metrics. However, the bulky footprint of conventional discrete components imposes significant limitations on the miniaturization of current PIMs. Meanwhile, the scalability of problem size and spin connectivity density is constrained by limited computational resources. To address these challenges, we proposed and demonstrated an integrated PIM (IPIM) based on a hybrid architecture on a silicon-based photonic platform with an optical component footprint of 0.065 mm², achieved success rates exceeding 90% in finding global optimal solutions across all three benchmark tests. To tackle the common challenge in PIMs, where large-scale and high-connectivity-density problems naturally incur high computational complexity, we developed a joint algorithm with sparsity, inverse sparsity, and decomposition operations (JA-SID). Using this approach, we successfully solved Ising problems with sparse and dense spin connectivity, involving 102,400 spins. In addition, we introduced an optimized parameter configuration scheme (OPCS), which reduced the iteration count by over 50% for slowly converging problems, thereby lowering time complexity and power consumption. In practice, we used the IPIM to successfully partition a Facebook social network with over 60,000 users, demonstrating its capability to handle ultra-large-scale real-world problems. Our research substantially extended the applicability of IPIM, offering a promising solution to the increasing global demand for computational resources.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10959649/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1859149.title: Service-learning using the BOPPPS model in TCM nursing education: a mixed-methods study
doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1859149.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Service-learning is increasingly used in nursing education to connect classroom learning with authentic practice and community engagement. However, evidence on how instructional models can optimize service-learning in nursing education remains limited. This study aimed to examine the educational effects of service-learning using the BOPPPS model in an undergraduate traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) nursing course.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This mixed-methods study included a quasi-experimental quantitative component and a qualitative component using thematic analysis. Ninety-six undergraduate nursing students participated, including 49 in the experimental group and 47 in the control group. The experimental group received service-learning using the BOPPPS model, whereas the control group received conventional teaching. Quantitative outcomes included course scores, service-learning abilities, and course evaluation scores. Qualitative data were collected through final reflective reports and analyzed to explore students' learning experiences.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Compared with the control group, the experimental group achieved better academic performance (87.69 ± 5.69 vs. 84.15 ± 8.35,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.018), stronger service-learning abilities (288.76 ± 47.28 vs. 259.66 ± 46.51,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.003), and more positive course evaluation scores (37.84 ± 3.85 vs. 34.81 ± 4.88,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.001). Qualitative findings further showed that the intervention supported knowledge application in practice, strengthened communication and caring, and deepened students' understanding of the value of TCM nursing. Students also reported increased workload and time demands.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Service-learning using the BOPPPS model may be a valuable teaching approach in TCM nursing education. It may help students connect classroom learning with authentic care needs while fostering practical competence and humanistic awareness.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10959072/v1.title: BioForm-LM: Generative Design of Biologics Formulations via In-Context Learning and Physics-Informed Decoding
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10959072/v1.abstract: Motivation: Formulation design for biologics (proteins, antibodies) is a critical bottleneck in drug development, yet remains largely manual and data-poor. Existing computational tools score or rank a fixed candidate set; no prior work generates formulation recipes de novo . Results We present BioForm-LM, a generative system for biologics formulation design combining mechanistic simulation, in-context few-shot learning, and physics-informed decoding. A mechanistic simulator encoding DLVO colloidal theory and Lumry–Eyring aggregation kinetics generates \(\:{10}^{5}\) synthetic training recipes; a small decoder-only transformer pretrained on this corpus adapts to novel proteins from 3–10 real stability measurements without gradient updates; and a distilled physics critic reranks candidates by best-of-\(\:N\) decoding. On BioFormBench — a curated benchmark of real literature-mined formulations — the model attains perfect calibration on the held-out scFv (Spearman \(\:r=1.0\), \(\:p=0.0\)) from only three in-context examples, and covers 35.3% of formulation space versus 7.5% for random sampling (\(\:4.7\times\:\)). Aggregate leave-one-protein-out recall@10 is 0.167 against 0.080 (random forest) and 0.050 (SVM). Ablations show both in-context adaptation (\(\:-67\text{\%}\) recall) and the physics critic (\(\:-33\text{\%}\)) are necessary. Availability: Code, model weights and the BioFormBench dataset are openly released (see Data and code availability). Contact: sravansaijohn@gmail.com
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10959072/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.1007/s11696-026-05468-z.title: Modeling equilibrium adsorption isotherms of human immunoglobulin G onto fibroin microparticles using machine learning and physics-informed neural networks
doi:10.1007/s11696-026-05468-z.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Accurate modeling of adsorption equilibrium is essential for designing and optimizing bioseparation processes. This study investigates the modeling of immunoglobulin G (IgG) adsorption equilibrium isotherms onto fibroin microparticles under different physicochemical conditions using five distinct modeling strategies. Fifteen experimental isotherms with different conditions, including buffer type, pH, temperature, and agitation, were modeled using classical approaches, machine learning (ML), physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), symbolic regression (PySR), and a hybrid PINN–PySR framework. Classical models showed moderate performance, with Langmuir providing the best fit (root mean square error, RMSE = 7.03–29.66 mg g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ). The ML model achieved the highest predictive accuracy (RMSE = 0.81–21.71 mg g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ) but often produced physically inconsistent curves. In contrast, PINNs incorporated physical constraints such as monotonicity, concavity, and saturation, yielding slightly higher errors (RMSE = 9.51–37.16 mg g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ) but preserving physically realistic isotherm shapes. Results highlight a trade-off between predictive accuracy and physical consistency. PINNs significantly improved curve smoothness and adherence to expected adsorption behavior, particularly under interpolated conditions not included in training. Additionally, the PINN framework provides a unified parameterization across varying conditions, avoiding separate fits for each experiment. Overall, PINNs represent a robust and reliable approach for adsorption modeling, combining predictive capability with fundamental physical consistency.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i8p138.title: Unified Multi-Disease Prediction and Risk Assessment Framework: Hybrid Deep Learning with Secure Multi-Party Computation for Comorbidity Analysis
doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i8p138.abstract: <jats:p>Modern healthcare systems are experiencing severe problems in both forecasting comorbid conditions and patient privacy amid decentralized healthcare facilities. This paper introduces a single framework in which multi-task deep learning and secure multi-party computation are combined to result in privacy-preserving disease prediction and risk assessment. The suggested Multi-Task Modified Deep Neural Network (MT-MDLNN) system with five conditions proposed simultaneously to determine cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, respiratory disorders and bi- or inter-disease associations. A new Correlation Aware Hybrid Whale-Coati Optimization (CA-HWCO) algorithm explicitly captures comorbidity patterns and it attains better convergence and clinically significant disease relationship learning. To achieve collaborative training between healthcare institutions without sharing sensitive patient information, the framework uses secure multi-party computation protocols that are based on Modified Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (M-ECDH) cryptography as well as secret sharing schemes. It is experimentally validated on six publicly available healthcare datasets with extraordinarily high mean classification accuracy (92.4) and can recognize pattern of clinically validated comorbidity such as diabetes-kidney disease correlation (0.76), as well as cardiovascular-hypertension patterns (0.79). Secure aggregation protocols add as little as 6-9% overhead to communication but information theorems not only in order distance but also in image value fidelity. Risk stratification analysis depicts that 89.4% are in accord with expert clinical examination with real-time inference ability of 38ms per patient. This study provides an overall remedy towards privacy-sensitive collaborative healthcare intelligence by allowing medical institutions to come up with precise multi-disease prediction models without failure to the privacy of patients.</jats:p>
doi:10.14445/22315381/ijett-v74i8p138.venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10966878/v1.title: Auditable machine learning for high-stakes decisions
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10966878/v1.abstract: Machine-learning predictions increasingly inform high-stakes decisions that must be auditable, yet post-hoc surrogates never certify the decision itself. Bipolar logic networks (BLN) make predictions that are verifiable symbolic logic: sufficient and necessary rule paths, combined by a learnable gate, certify what is enough and what is required. Across a pre-registered 30-dataset benchmark, BLN attains macro ROC-AUC 0.841 on 17 audit-decision tasks—first among rule-based models, second among interpretable models behind EBM (0.856), tied with XGBoost (0.840, p = 0.75). It answers policy-audit queries with under 0.5% false vetoes, recovers necessary conditions at F1 = 0.92 versus NCA (0.88) and QCA (0.72), and aligns with 83% of known causal edges on interventional proteomics (p = 0.019). The dual-rule structure is indispensable across all 30 datasets (p < 10⁻⁸), and degradation outside its pre-registered envelope is predictable. BLN does not surpass EBM—the 1.5-point deficit is the price of binarization—but uniquely provides interrogatable Boolean structure and calibrated probabilities.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10966878/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.1117/1.jmi.13.5.054501.title: Selective segmentation with rejection option: a machine reasoning approach and evaluation metrics in CT kidney segmentation
doi:10.1117/1.jmi.13.5.054501.abstract: <jats:p>PurposeDeep learning models for medical image segmentation achieve high average performance but can produce anatomically implausible errors that undermine trust and necessitate manual review. This work addresses this limitation through selective segmentation with a rejection option, enabling systems to accept plausible results while rejecting questionable ones.ApproachA nnUNet model trained for kidney segmentation on the KiTS23 dataset was integrated into the SimpleMind (SM) reasoning framework. Kidney segmentation candidates were evaluated and selected using SM reasoning methods fuzzy membership reasoning (FMR), adaptive reasoning (AR), and largest connected component analysis per side (LCCAPS), and performance was compared with the commonly used largest connected component analysis (LCCA). Performance was assessed via false positive rate and false negative rate across five validation folds. Candidate-level acceptance and rejection metrics were also introduced to evaluate selective performance. Robustness was further examined under added noise.ResultsReasoning-based approaches (FMR, AR, and LCCAPS) reduced false positives and anatomically invalid outputs more effectively than LCCA, while preserving acceptance of valid segmentation candidates. Results persisted under noise, avoiding acceptance of implausible results.ConclusionsIncorporating reasoning into DL segmentation supports selective acceptance of anatomically valid outputs and rejection of invalid ones, increasing reliability and autonomy in medical imaging workflows. This selective segmentation framework provides a practical path toward trusted, semi-autonomous clinical deployment.</jats:p>

doi:10.3998/mjcsl.8273.title: Evolving from Collaborrators to Co-Creators in a Film-Making Partnership
doi:10.3998/mjcsl.8273.abstract: <jats:p>Faculty reflect upon a 13-year documentary project that began as a traditional service-learning project and evolved into a more collaborative, integrative model of community engagement with a social justice goal. They offer guidelines for equitable collaboration on projects grounded in reciprocal outcomes and guided by a responsibility to historically marginalized groups</jats:p>
