doi:10.59944/jipsi.v5i4.1748.title: Penggunaan Individual Learning Plan dan Arah Belajar Siswa Pendidikan Kesetaraan: Studi Eksploratif
doi:10.59944/jipsi.v5i4.1748.abstract: <jats:p>Individual Learning Plans (ILPs) are intended to connect students’ interests, strengths, goals, and learning actions, yet evidence on how students actually use such plans remains limited, particularly in equivalency education. This exploratory cross-sectional study examined self-reported learning direction and active ILP use among 31 junior- and senior-secondary-equivalent students at PKBM Flexi School Bintaro, Indonesia. The 12-item, five-point Likert questionnaire was developed from the ILP, personalized learning, goal-setting, and self-regulated learning literature, reviewed internally by two senior facilitators for content relevance, and organized a priori into four conceptual groups—self-understanding, direction and goal clarity, planning and ILP use, and monitoring and reflection—that separate students' self-reported conditions from items explicitly referring to ILP use. Because internal consistency of the four groups was modest (α = .50–.58), reflecting the instrument's status as an initial, not-yet-validated version, item-level analysis rather than group-score comparison was treated as the primary and more trustworthy level of evidence. Self-understanding indicators received relatively higher responses, whereas indicators explicitly referring to active ILP use were weaker. The lowest item was revisiting the ILP to decide the next learning step (M = 2.84; 25.8% selected agree/strongly agree). Open-ended responses converged with this pattern: self-understanding was most frequently identified as helpful (38.7%), while progress-tracking features were one of the most frequent improvement requests (16.1%). Exploratory comparisons by school level and enrolment duration did not show statistically meaningful differences, but small subgroups limited inference. The findings do not establish ILP effectiveness; instead, they identify a practical gap between setting a learning direction and repeatedly using a personal plan to guide subsequent action. Future studies should test scheduled review points and progress-tracking mechanisms using independently reviewed instruments and stronger multi-site designs.</jats:p>

doi:10.59944/postaxial.v4i3.1819.title: Free Nutritious Meal Program at SMPN 10 Bekasi: A Phenomenological Study of Teacher and Parent Perceptions
doi:10.59944/postaxial.v4i3.1819.abstract: <jats:p>The Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) Program is a strategic national policy aimed at improving students’ health, nutritional status, and learning readiness. This study aims to analyze in depth the concrete lived experiences and subjective meanings of teachers and students’ parents regarding the implementation of the MBG Program at SMPN 10 Bekasi City. Using a qualitative phenomenological approach, with George Edward III’s Policy Implementation Theory, Joyce Epstein’s School-Family Partnership Theory, and Husserlian and Heideggerian phenomenological frameworks as analytical lenses, data were collected through in-depth interviews, participant observation, and document study involving five teachers and eight parents. The study revealed two main phenomenological findings. First, among teachers, there was ambivalence between improved student learning readiness and academic energy and an increase in non-academic workload, or the domestication of teachers’ duties, such as food distribution management and classroom cleanliness. Second, among parents, there was a dual perception between gratitude for household economic savings and existential concern regarding hygiene control, menu variety, and picky-eater behavior. A major structural obstacle was the compression of break time, which distorted effective instructional time. The study recommends establishing a dedicated logistics team, restructuring the daily schedule, and digitizing nutritional transparency to strengthen school-parent synergy.</jats:p>
doi:10.59944/postaxial.v4i3.1819.venue: International Journal of Post Axial: Futuristic Teaching and Learning

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10704594/v1.title: Intersection of Personal Values and Professional Responsibilities in Preclinical Medical Training: Implications for Reflection, Learning, and Professional Identity Formation
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10704594/v1.abstract: Professional identity formation (PIF), the integration of personal values with professional responsibilities, is critical during preclinical medical training. Yet preclinical curricula persistently prioritize biomedical knowledge over values-based, reflective learning, leaving students inadequately supported when personal and professional values conflict. This study explored how personal values and professional responsibilities intersect during preclinical training and the implications of these intersections for reflection, learning, and PIF. A qualitative, reflective narrative design was employed. Reflective writing assignments from second-year medical students (Essay 1: N = 86; Essay 2: N = 88) were analyzed using thematic analysis to characterize the types, sources, and consequences of personal-professional conflicts. Response frequencies were also calculated. Two thematic domains emerged. In the ethical and clinical domains, students described conflicts related to reproductive health, patient hesitancy, cultural sensitivity, end-of-life care, and inclusivity, shaped by religious beliefs, personal experiences, and upbringing. In the structural and relational domain, students struggled to balance family obligations, relationships, academic demands, and well-being, with consequences including burnout, emotional depletion, and academic decline. Structured reflective practice served as a catalyst for ethical reasoning and identity consolidation. PIF is a morally formative process. Medical schools should explicitly scaffold personal-professional conflicts, develop reflective and ethical reasoning skills, and foster supportive learning communities.

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-1533-9.ch002.title: Advanced Machine Learning Techniques for Crime Prediction in Smart Heterogeneous Policing Networks
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-1533-9.ch002.abstract: <jats:p>The proposed chapter suggest a highly complex machine learning crime prediction model on an intelligent heterogeneous policing network, which will have to consider dynamic environment, multimodal, and real-time decision-making. A deep learning (CNN LSTM) hybrid architecture that is founded on graph neural networks and reinforcement learning is created. With the assistance of multimodal fusion strategy and the security and privacy preservation measures that are inherent in the framework, the spatial, temporal, behavioral and environmental data are calculated. The proposed model is more predictive since it has an accuracy of 96.8, and AUC-ROC of 0.98, which is better than the traditional and standalone deep learning models. The adaptive learning and multimodal data can be much more useful regarding context awareness, power and responsiveness in the intricate police situations. The framework will also help in the real-time crime prediction and the best distribution of resources and as such can be applied in smart city policing systems.</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/ijqrm-03-2026-0137.title: A machine learning–driven framework for Quality 4.0 maturity assessment in service organizations: a socio-technical systems approach to digital quality transformation
doi:10.1108/ijqrm-03-2026-0137.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This research aims to develop and validate a comprehensive machine learning (ML)-driven Quality 4.0 maturity assessment framework for service organizations grounded in Socio-Technical Systems (STS) theory.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An STS-integrated framework comprising 18 Quality 4.0 dimensions across People, Process, and Technology subsystems was developed through systematic literature synthesis and expert validation. Survey data were collected from 285 service organizations and analysed using Latent Class Analysis to empirically derive five maturity levels. Six supervised machine learning algorithms were evaluated, with the Random Forest classifier achieving the highest predictive performance (accuracy = 0.963). Model interpretability was ensured using SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) to quantify the relative importance of individual maturity dimensions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The ML-based model reliably classifies organisations into five empirically derived maturity levels. The SHAP analysis highlights Big Data Analytics, Digital Quality Management, and Technology Integration as the strongest predictive signals for Quality 4.0 maturity classification. The empirical results show that 41% of service organizations operate at a Basic Quality level, whereas only 7% demonstrate maturity aligned with Quality 4.0 excellence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Managers can use an ML-driven model to assess their current Quality 4.0 maturity, identify critical improvement areas, and prioritize investments in AI, digital quality management, cultural readiness, and capability development. The model's explainable ML outputs also support evidence-based decision-making and clearer alignment between technological adoption and organizational development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study introduces an empirically grounded, socio-technical, and explainable ML based Quality 4.0 maturity assessment framework tailored to service organizations in a developing economy context. By combining Latent Class Analysis with interpretable machine learning, the framework advances both methodological rigor and practical transparency in maturity assessment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.62476/bio.ph.12162.abstract: The post-conflict reconstruction of Karabakh presents an urgent public health challenge: more than 10,000 displaced individuals had returned to liberated territories as of January 2025, with official targets of 140,000 returnees by end of 2026, substantially outpacing healthcare infrastructure development.This paper presents a conceptual framework for deploying a machine learning-enhanced, fingernail-mounted photoplethysmography (PPG) device as a low-cost, non-invasive vital sign monitoring tool in these underserved communities.Building on a previously developed and TÜBİTAK-funded prototype, we propose an upgraded architecture integrating Random Forest-based artifact detection, LSTMbased adaptive noise cancellation and autoencoder-based anomaly detection.As a limited preliminary computational feasibility test, the proposed Stage 1 artifact detection workflow was evaluated on the openaccess Pulse Transit Time PPG Dataset (n=3 subjects, 108 windows) under Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation.PPG-only features achieved 36.1% classification accuracy (F1=0.23),while adding accelerometer features improved performance to 78.7% accuracy (F1=0.74)-a 42.6 percentage point gain -confirming that accelerometer-assisted artifact labeling is essential for reliable signal quality assessment.These results do not validate the nail-mounted device directly; rather, they demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed artifact-detection pipeline on publicly available PPG data.This framework provides an early structured, technologygrounded proposal for wearable vital-sign monitoring in the Azerbaijani post-conflict resettlement context.

doi:10.63688/t721c183.title: Failure based learning methodologies and their impact on students’ self efficacy and frustration tolerance
doi:10.63688/t721c183.abstract:
<jats:p>Introducción: Las metodologías de aprendizaje basado en el fracaso permiten comprender los errores y los intentos fallidos como oportunidades para fortalecer el aprendizaje, la autoeficacia y la tolerancia a la frustración. El objetivo del estudio fue analizar el impacto de estas metodologías en estudiantes mediante literatura científica publicada entre 2020 y 2026.
Metodología: Se realizó una revisión sistemática cualitativa siguiendo el modelo PRISMA 2020. Se consultaron Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, SciELO y Google Scholar. De 72 registros identificados, 16 estudios cumplieron los criterios de inclusión y fueron analizados mediante una matriz documental.Resultados: El 37,5 % de los estudios se relacionó con aprendizaje basado en el fracaso y fracaso productivo; el 31,25 % abordó la autoeficacia y el 31,25 % la tolerancia a la frustración y al fracaso. Los hallazgos evidenciaron que los errores pueden convertirse en experiencias productivas cuando se acompañan de retroalimentación, reflexión, apoyo docente y oportunidades de mejora.Conclusiones: Las metodologías de aprendizaje basado en el fracaso pueden favorecer el aprendizaje, la autoeficacia y la tolerancia a la frustración cuando se desarrollan en ambientes estructurados, seguros y no punitivos.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1945376.title: Explainable deep learning reveals a stagewise temporal deterioration from skin tone to contour to texture in Chinese women’s skin aging
doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1945376.abstract: <jats:p>Skin aging is a continuous and progressive physiological process characterized by gradual structural and functional changes. Early identification and accurate assessment of aging-related facial features are essential for developing targeted skincare strategies. This study aimed to establish a deep learning-based framework combined with Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis to classify facial aging stages in Chinese women and provide interpretable evidence for personalized skincare. A total of 300 Chinese women aged 18–60 years were included. Standardized facial images were acquired using the VISIA imaging system. Four dimensions, including tone, contour, texture, and porphyrin, were evaluated, and 23 facial indicators were extracted. A hybrid multimodal deep learning classification model was developed by integrating facial image data with quantitative facial aging indicators. Five-fold stratified cross-validation was performed to evaluate model performance, with Top-2 accuracy used as the primary evaluation metric. SHAP analysis was further applied to assess the contribution weights of different facial aging indicators to model predictions. Based on the fitted quantitative facial aging indicators, a six-class facial aging classification model was established. The model demonstrated stable convergence and achieved a highest validation Top-2 accuracy of 85.0%. The confusion matrix showed that classification errors occurred primarily between adjacent aging stages. SHAP analysis revealed a progressive aging pattern characterized by early changes in skin color, middle-stage changes in facial contour, and later deterioration in skin texture. This study demonstrates that integrating deep learning with SHAP analysis can effectively classify facial aging stages in Chinese women while providing interpretable insights into the key features driving aging-related predictions.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10583148/v1.title: Least-squares-based deep learning for short-term ionospheric TEC prediction with uncertainty quantification and DIA quality control
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10583148/v1.abstract: High-precision Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) applications require ionospheric total electron content (TEC) predictions together with statistically interpretable uncertainty and quality control. This study applies least-squares-based deep learning (LSBDL) to one-hour-ahead TEC prediction and integrates RMS-driven stochastic weighting, joint first-order uncertainty propagation, and detection–identification–adaptation (DIA) within one framework. Hourly TEC and RMS data from 36 CODE GIM grid points along 115°E (0°–87.5°N) in 2015 were used with a 24-h sliding window. Under clean conditions, the mean RMSE across all grid points was 1.137 TECU, and the pooled empirical coverages of the nominal 95% and 99% prediction intervals were 96.26% and 98.80%, respectively. The propagated model-parameter uncertainty was small relative to the RMS-derived observation term, indicating that the current prediction uncertainty is dominated by the TEC-product stochastic information. Under 2% and 5% controlled contamination with gross errors of five times the RMS, DIA achieved mean F1-scores of 0.988 and 0.992, and both Remove and Downweight adaptation restored prediction accuracy and interval calibration. At 15°, 45°, and 75°N, LSBDL achieved accuracy comparable to or better than ARIMA, LSTM, and GRU, with a mean training time of 0.749 s. These results show that LSBDL can provide competitive short-term TEC prediction while integrating stochastic weighting, uncertainty quantification, and statistically traceable quality control.

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1874928.title: Higher-dimensional embedding of time-series data for machine learning
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1874928.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Deep learning has revolutionized image analysis, yet most clinical biosignals, especially multi-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs), remain one-dimensional and awkward for modern vision models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We introduce an orthogonal-polynomial imaging (OPI) framework that encodes 12-lead ECGs into a single two-dimensional image through an invertible transformation prior to coarse-graining, producing compact image representations that retain sufficient information for accurate classification. We benchmark the proposed representation against established architectures including ResNet, Transformers, and 1D temporal convolutional models on large-scale PhysioNet ECG datasets.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our results demonstrate that OPI-based image representations achieve highly competitive classification performance while preserving diagnostically relevant temporal and cross-lead information.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The framework bridges raw multi-channel biosignals and standard image-based learning architectures without representation loss prior to coarse-graining, offering an effective, scalable, and physics-inspired representation for automated cardiac diagnostics.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.62274/qev16f77.title: <b>Penerapan Pembelajaran Deep Learning Melalui Model PBL untuk Meningkatkan Hasil Belajar IPAS Kelas V SD</b>
doi:10.62274/qev16f77.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to improve the learning outcomes of fifth-grade elementary school students in Science and Social Studies (IPAS) through the implementation of Deep Learning-based Problem Based Learning (PBL). Low learning outcomes evidenced by a pre-cycle average of 69.79 with only 41.67% mastery rate prompted this classroom action research. The study was conducted in three cycles with 26 students as research subjects. Data were collected through learning outcome tests, observations, and documentation. Results showed significant improvement each cycle: Cycle I average 70.28 (38.46% mastery), Cycle II 79.17 (57.69%), and Cycle III 85.33 (88.46%). The Deep Learning approach within PBL encouraged students to think critically, solve contextual problems, and build deep understanding of IPAS material. The conclusion is that the implementation of Deep Learning through PBL is proven effective in improving IPAS learning outcomes of fifth-grade elementary school students.</jats:p>

doi:10.57260/csdj.2026.286245.title: An Analysis of Social, Cultural, and Community Management Factors Contributing to the Success of the Tai Phuan Community Learning Center in Ban Klang, Loei Province, Thailand
doi:10.57260/csdj.2026.286245.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the social, cultural, and community management factors contributing to the success of the Tai Phuan community learning center in Ban Klang, Pak Tom Subdistrict, Chiang Khan District, Loei Province, Thailand. Adopting a qualitative research design, the study employed purposive sampling to recruit twelve key informants comprising community leaders, representatives of educational institutions, and community members with relevant knowledge and experience. Data were collected through documentary research, in-depth interviews, field surveys, and observation. SWOT analysis, supported by schematic mapping, was used to examine internal conditions and external influences on the center’s development. The findings were subsequently discussed with community members and local leaders in small groups to support contextual interpretation and identify development priorities.The findings identified six internal dimensions: organizational structure and administration, community leadership, human resources, financial resources, physical facilities and learning spaces, and community participation. Community members’ cultural knowledge and active involvement emerged as central strengths, while limited financial resources constituted the principal internal constraint. Social relationships, trust, and collective decision-making supported coordination and shared ownership, whereas Tai Phuan language, traditions, beliefs, and local wisdom provided the cultural foundation for learning and intergenerational knowledge transmission. External support from educational institutions and expert practitioners complemented these capacities through academic guidance, knowledge management, and access to collaborative networks. Although no significant external threats were identified within the scope of the study, the findings underscored the importance of adaptive planning and continued resource support. Taken together, these findings suggest that the center’s development depends on the interaction of social capital, cultural capital, and participatory management, with external partnerships strengthening the community’s capacity to organize and transmit local knowledge. The study therefore recommends reinforcing participatory governance, developing local leadership, and sustaining community–academic partnerships to support the continuity of culturally grounded learning.</jats:p>

doi:10.61710/tasp1g44.title: Enhancing Telecom Customer Churn Prediction Using Voting Ensemble Learning with SMOTE and ADASYN
doi:10.61710/tasp1g44.abstract: <jats:p>Customer churn prediction is an important task in the telecommunications sector, particularly when class imbalance affects the ability of machine learning models to identify churned customers. The results showed that ensemble-based models generally outperformed individual classifiers. doi:10.1108/et-01-2026-0005.title: Integrating user behaviour into sustainable urban transformation: machine learning model from university campus
doi:10.1108/et-01-2026-0005.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This research proposes a data-driven model situated at the intersection of occupancy, sustainable design and building utilisation. The model is designed to assess the sustainability performance of the existing campus building stock while offering predictive insights for future developments. A university campus was selected as a controlled “micro-city” environment to address the difficulties of collecting consistent city-scale data. The main objective is to demonstrate how occupancy, operational and spatial information can be integrated through machine learning (ML) to support a gradual and human-centred urban transformation process.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An open-access Green Campus Dataset comprising 2,138 data points representing environmental, spatial and socioeconomic variables was analysed. Following exploratory correlation analysis and feature engineering, seven ML algorithms – linear regression, random forest, gradient boosting, multilayer perceptron (MLP), K-nearest neighbours (KNN), support vector regression (SVR) and XGBoost – were comparatively evaluated for predicting energy savings. Model performance was assessed using R2, RMSE, MAE and MAPE, and XGBoost was selected as the best-performing model. Explainable AI techniques, and sensitivity analysis, were subsequently applied to interpret the relationships between key variables and sustainability performance. The resulting framework was used to generate building-level sustainability scores and support a cloud-based decision-support prototype.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>XGBoost achieved the highest predictive performance among the evaluated ML models. Feature importance analysis identified Beam Irradiance as the most influential predictor of energy savings, with an importance score of 74.45%, while explainability analyses further demonstrated the influence of energy efficiency, solar utilisation and occupancy-related variables on sustainability performance. The findings indicate that campus sustainability emerges from the interaction of environmental, operational and occupancy-related factors rather than from technical characteristics alone. The proposed framework demonstrates the potential of campus-scale ML to support human-centred, data-driven sustainability assessment and decision-making.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study introduces a human-centred ML framework for campus-scale sustainability assessment, beginning with the comparative evaluation of seven supervised ML models to identify the most effective predictive approach. By integrating environmental, operational and occupancy-related variables with explainable AI techniques, the framework extends conventional performance-based assessment towards a more interpretable socio-technical approach. Treating the university campus as a bounded urban laboratory, the study demonstrates how machine learning and sustainability scoring can support data-driven decision-making and provide a scalable foundation for future smart and sustainable urban applications.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1097/cej.0000000000001037.title: Predicting prostate cancer mortality using UK Biobank data: a multimodal machine learning approach
doi:10.1097/cej.0000000000001037.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title/>
                    <jats:p>Prostate cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality among men worldwide; however, it remains challenging to predict disease progression in individuals. While numerous tools attempt to forecast the likelihood of developing the cancer, fewer studies focus specifically on mortality prediction using population-scale clinical datasets. UK Biobank data were used to develop population-scale predictive models of prostate cancer mortality. The study assessed medical records, blood work, physical measurements, and genetic information of approximately 167 000 males aged 50 and above. A feedforward neural network was compared with logistic regression to determine their effectiveness. The neural network demonstrated substantially stronger predictive performance than logistic regression, achieving a receiver operating characteristic–area under the curve of 0.767 compared with 0.633 and a precision–recall–area under the curve of 0.271 compared with 0.153, respectively. The analysis revealed that age and genetics were the primary influencing factors. Decision curve analysis demonstrated minimal net benefit across clinically relevant thresholds. These findings support the utility of multimodal risk modeling while highlighting challenges in clinical translation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

                    <jats:title>Background.</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Normothermic regional perfusion (NRP) and normothermic machine perfusion (NMP) have rapidly expanded donation after circulatory death (DCD) liver transplant, but comparative real-world data are lacking.</jats:p>

                    <jats:p>Adult liver transplants performed in the advanced perfusion era (December 2021–June 2025) were analyzed via the Organ Procurement and Transplant Network/Standard Transplant Analysis and Research database. DCD grafts were stratified by advanced perfusion modality (DCD+NMP, DCD+NRP, or DCD+NRP+NMP) or static cold storage (DCD+SCS), and compared with donation after brain death (DBD) transplants. “Back-to-base” machine perfusion cases were excluded. Primary outcome was 2-y graft survival.</jats:p>

                    <jats:p>

                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>

                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001). Propensity score matching to DBD cohorts revealed no difference in 2-y graft survival after DCD+NMP (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.11), DCD+NRP (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.12), or DCD+NRP+NMP (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.6), with inferior graft survival after DCD+SCS (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001). Comparison of DCD+NMP and DCD+NRP by propensity score matching showed no difference in 2-y graft survival (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.3). Hazard of ischemic cholangiopathy was increased over DBD liver transplants for DCD+SCS (HR, 5.51; 95% CI, 2.94-10.3;
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001) and DCD+NMP (HR, 2.11; 95% CI, 1.02-4.23;
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">P</jats:italic>

                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.29303/darmadiksani.v6i3.11956.title: Pendampingan Penerapan <i>Deep Learning</i> dalam Pengembangan Media Pembelajaran Berbasis Teknologi
doi:10.29303/darmadiksani.v6i3.11956.abstract: <jats:p>Transformasi digital dalam pendidikan menuntut guru memiliki kemampuan dalam memanfaatkan teknologi untuk menciptakan pembelajaran yang inovatif, bermakna, dan sesuai dengan kebutuhan peserta didik. Namun, hasil observasi awal menunjukkan bahwa pemanfaatan media pembelajaran digital oleh guru SMK Negeri 18 Samarinda masih terbatas, pemahaman mengenai pembelajaran mendalam belum komprehensif, serta keterampilan dalam mengembangkan media berbasis teknologi masih perlu ditingkatkan. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan meningkatkan pemahaman dan keterampilan guru dalam menerapkan pembelajaran mendalam melalui pengembangan media pembelajaran berbasis teknologi. Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada 09 Juli 2026 di SMK Negeri 18 Samarinda dengan melibatkan 40 guru melalui tahapan penyampaian materi, diskusi, praktik langsung, dan pendampingan. Materi mencakup konsep pembelajaran mendalam, prinsip pembelajaran yang berkesadaran, bermakna, dan menyenangkan, serta peran guru sebagai aktivator, kolaborator, dan pengembang budaya belajar. Pada tahap praktik, peserta mengembangkan media pembelajaran dengan memanfaatkan berbagai platform teknologi, seperti Gamma dan Canva, sesuai tujuan dan karakteristik pembelajaran. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan adanya peningkatan pemahaman peserta mengenai penerapan pembelajaran mendalam dan kemampuan dalam merancang media pembelajaran berbasis teknologi. Peserta juga mampu menghasilkan rancangan awal media pembelajaran yang lebih interaktif dan kontekstual. Kegiatan ini memberikan pengalaman praktis bagi guru untuk mengintegrasikan teknologi dalam pembelajaran serta menjadi dasar pengembangan media secara mandiri dan berkelanjutan. Kegiatan ini diharapkan dapat ditindaklanjuti melalui pendampingan berkelanjutan agar guru mampu mengembangkan dan menerapkan media pembelajaran berbasis teknologi secara mandiri.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10879607/v1.title: Reliability-Calibrated Phenology-Guided Dual-Cycle Learning for Mapping Single- and Double-Season Rice from Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 Time Series
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10879607/v1.abstract: Reliable discrimination of single- and double-season rice is required for mapping agricultural cropping intensity, but it remains difficult in cloud-affected and fragmented landscapes. Regular optical sequences commonly contain interpolated observations whose reliability varies with gap length and position, while generic temporal models do not explicitly organize annual evidence by crop-cycle number. We developed the Phenology-Guided Dual-Cycle Rice Network (PGD-RiceNet) to classify non-rice, single-season rice, and double-season rice from a 2025 Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 time series. PGD-RiceNet combines Bi-directional Gap-Topology Reliability Calibration, Phenology-Conditioned Adaptive Cycle Routing, and Cycle-Consistent Hierarchical Learning. On the spatially independent test set, the model achieved 97.60% overall accuracy, 96.85% macro-F1, 93.92% mean intersection over union, and 96.30% double-season-rice F1. These values exceeded the strongest CTH-Net-style baseline by 1.08, 1.46, 2.66, and 1.92 percentage points, respectively. In the cumulative ablation, the full model increased combined-rice F1 from 90.42% to 96.66%, with the largest class-specific gain for double-season rice. Mechanistic analyses showed that learned reliability decreased with missing-span severity and that latent-cycle attention centres were more widely separated for double-season rice. Leave-one-county-out evaluation retained useful transfer performance but revealed the largest penalty in Yudu. These results show that observation reliability and annual cycle structure are useful inductive biases for rice-cropping-intensity mapping within the tested one-year, three-county, 30-m optical setting.

doi:10.4995/raet.2027.25630.title: Spatial modeling of soil salinity in hyperarid agroecosystems of northern Peru using a hybrid machine learning ensemble
doi:10.4995/raet.2027.25630.abstract: <jats:p>Soil salinization poses a critical threat to agricultural sustainability in arid agroecosystems, limiting food security and economic stability. On the northern coast of Peru, the synergy between inefficient water management and extreme climate variability has accelerated soil degradation, demanding precise spatial monitoring tools. This study proposes a Hybrid Smart Ensemble model to map soil electrical conductivity (EC), integrating optical data (Sentinel-2), dual-polarization SAR texture (Sentinel-1), and thermal imagery (Landsat-9 LST). Three modeling scenarios were evaluated: (1) Random Forest (RF), (2) Deep Neural Network (DNN), and (3) a Hybrid Ensemble. To overcome the typical scarcity of field data in developing regions, a Spatial Data Augmentation strategy based on Tobler's First Law was implemented. The results demonstrated that the hybrid architecture (Scenario 3) achieved superior performance (R² = 0.86; RMSE = 1.70 dS/m), exceeding the baselines of individual classifiers. While the Random Forest provided stability in moderate ranges, the inclusion of Deep Learning proved essential for capturing the nonlinear spectral response of extreme salt crusts (>12 dS/m). Variable importance analysis identified Ground Surface Temperature (LST) and Elevation as dominant predictors, validating the hypothesis that thermal inertia and topographic depressions are the main physical drivers of salinity in hyperarid environments. The resulting map, with a 10 m resolution, reveals "hot spots" in the Chulucanas and Lower Piura sectors, providing valuable information for implementing targeted detection and analysis zones to optimize drainage rehabilitation and soil recovery strategies.While themodel effectively delineates non-saline baselines and severe salt crusts, boundary zones (moderate salinity)remain challenging due to historical sampling limitations. Therefore, the applicability of the model is currentlylimited to hyperarid agroecosystems with edaphic and topographic characteristics similar to those of the LowerPiura Valley; results should be validated with additional field campaigns before implementation in other contexts.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10810357/v1.title: Computational Investigation and Defect-Related Optimization of Lead-Free Cs₂AgBiBr₆ Double-Perovskite Solar Cells Using DFT, SCAPS-1D, and Machine Learning
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10810357/v1.abstract: The lead-free double perovskite materials have become attractive alternatives to the traditional lead-based photovoltaic (PV) absorbers in view of their relatively low toxicity to the environment. The electronic complexities and simulated PV performances of the lead-free double perovskite Cs₂AgBiBr₆ were investigated using complementary computational tools such as Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, device simulation through the SCAPS-1D code, and Machine Learning (ML). In the electronic structure calculations, we have used the quantum ESPRESSO package, with the generalized gradient approximation (GGA-PBE) functional. The electronic properties of Cs₂AgBiBr₆ were studied using DFT calculations at the self-consistent field (SCF) convergence, total density of states (TDOS), and projected density of states (PDOS) analysis methods. A PV simulation was then carried out for the FTO/SnO₂/Cs₂AgBiBr₆/NiOₓ/Au device for investigation of the PV performance of the device. The PV performance of the FTO/SnO₂/Cs₂AgBiBr₆/NiOₓ/Au device was then studied by photovoltaic simulation in SCAPS-1D simulation. The simulation results of various photovoltaic parameters were systematically studied for variations in the absorber thickness and the bulk defect density.The variation of the bulk defect density was systematically studied while changing the thickness of the absorber, for the simulated photovoltaic parameters. In the parameter range investigated, a maximum simulated power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 11.46% was obtained for an absorber thickness of 1200 nm with a bulk defect density of 1×10 12 cm⁻³. The same dataset generated by the SCAPS-1D simulation was used as the input for a second Random Forest regression model, with the model inputs being the thickness of the absorber layer and bulk defect density, while the output data are its PCE. This model, as expected, was good with the simulation data, and a value of about 0.96, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.12, and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.18 were achieved. The relative influence of the parameters of robustness – absorber thickness and bulk defect density – on the simulation result of PCE was analyzed by using feature-importance analysis. Overall, the study offers a complementary electronic-structure and device-simulation approach, as well as a data-driven evaluation of the simulated photovoltaic performance and optimization of defect-related parameters of Cs₂AgBiBr₆-based lead-free double perovskite solar cells.

doi:10.60087/jklst.vol5.n3.003.title: <b>Changes in First-Year English-Majored Students’ Paragraph Writing Performance During a Blended Course at a Public University in Hanoi</b>
doi:10.60087/jklst.vol5.n3.003.abstract: <jats:p>This research examined changes in the paragraph-writing performance of 32 first-year English-majored students during a blended course at a public university in Hanoi. A single-class pre-test/post-test design was used. Following baseline assessment and orientation in Weeks 1–2, students completed blended activities from Weeks 3-10, combining asynchronous preparation on Google Classroom with face-to-face instruction, guided practice, peer interaction, drafting, and feedback. The post-test was administered in Week 11, followed by an 11-item questionnaire and semi-structured interviews with three purposively selected students in Week 12. Paired-samples t-tests indicated a significant increase in overall writing scores, with significant changes in content, organization, and grammar but not vocabulary. The questionnaire scales showed high internal consistency, and students reported favourable perceptions of engagement, motivation, confidence, and autonomy. Interview accounts illustrated perceived improvements in organization while also identifying distraction, unclear instructions, comprehension difficulties, and access constraints. Overall, higher post-test scores were observed after eight weeks of substantive blended instruction. However, the single-group design cannot isolate the contribution of blended learning from regular instruction, practice, feedback, task familiarity, or maturation.</jats:p>

doi:10.60087/ijls.vol3.n3.013.title: Investigating the Effects of the STEAM Approach on English Test Scores and Learning Experiences of Grade 5 Students at BVT School
doi:10.60087/ijls.vol3.n3.013.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates the impact of the Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM) approach on Grade 5 Vietnamese students' English achievement and learning experiences compared to the traditional Present-Practice-Produce (PPP) method. Employing a convergent mixed-methods quasi-experimental design, the research involved 91 students divided into an experimental group (STEAM) and a control group (PPP). Quantitative data were collected through pre-tests and post-tests measuring overall English proficiency, while qualitative insights were gathered via semi-structured interviews with the experimental cohort. Quantitative results indicated that both groups achieved statistically significant longitudinal score improvements; however, there was no significant difference in the growth trajectories between the two instructional methods, meaning the STEAM approach did not outperform the PPP method in immediate academic gains. Conversely, qualitative findings demonstrated that STEAM instruction significantly enhanced student engagement, motivation, peer collaboration, and perceived authentic language use through hands-on, real-world projects. In conclusion, while the STEAM approach may not yield superior immediate cognitive test outcomes compared to traditional instruction, it effectively cultivates essential non-cognitive competencies and positive affective attitudes that support long-term language development. </jats:p>

doi:10.1108/mip-08-2025-0668.title: Enhanced retail customer equity prediction using a hybrid machine learning and Markov chain model
doi:10.1108/mip-08-2025-0668.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to improve the accuracy of customer equity (CE) estimation in complex retail environments by introducing a hybrid framework that integrates machine learning (ML) with Markov Chain modeling, enabling dynamic prediction of CE in settings characterized by frequent transactions and diverse product offerings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study develops a hybrid framework that integrates ML and Markov Chain modeling for dynamic CE prediction. ML models extract customer behavioral features, which are combined with a probabilistic model to enhance retention prediction. A newly introduced “stability” dimension extends the traditional Recency–Frequency–Monetary (RFM) framework, enabling dynamic clustering. These clusters form the basis for Markov states, allowing the modeling of customer transitions and more accurate CE estimation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings demonstrate that integrating ML with Markov Chain modeling improves the accuracy of CE estimation. The approach enables managers to monitor both current and future customer states with precision. Dynamic clustering, enhanced by the stability dimension, identifies behavioral shifts early, supporting proactive churn detection and more targeted retention strategies for high-value customers.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes originality by introducing a hybrid ML–Markov Chain framework that extends the traditional RFM model with a stability dimension. This integration enables dynamic analysis of customer transitions and provides more accurate assessments of CE. Compared to traditional static models, the approach delivers deeper insights into customer behavior and supports more informed managerial decision-making.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1910483.title: Enhancing ZTMAF through federated trust learning, post quantum cryptography integration and seamless cross domain authentication handover
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1910483.abstract: <jats:p>Vehicular Fog Computing (VFC) has a major role to play in facilitating low-latency and real-time communication in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). Nevertheless, there exist major issues in trust management, security, and cross-domain authentication, considering the dynamic nature of vehicular networks. The Zero-Trust Mobility-Aware Authentication Framework (ZTMAF) has been proposed to overcome issues in trust management, security, and cross-domain authentication. Nevertheless, there exist major issues in distributed intelligence, trust transmission, and handover, which have been addressed in this proposed framework. The proposed framework extends ZTMAF with three major advancements: Federated Trust Learning, PQC-inspired Secure Transmission, and Cross-Domain Authentication Handover. The proposed framework uses fog nodes to train a trust model in a distributed setting, allowing for scalability and privacy preservation. Additionally, Post-Quantum Cryptography inspired encryption would be utilized for secure trust transmission, as well as to remain compliant with future post-quantum encryption standards. A token-based handover mechanism will allow vehicles to make use of previously verified trust, thus lowering latency in cross-domain authentication. The proposed framework has been validated via multiple simulation scenarios, and its performance has been evaluated against different types of attacks (e.g., stealth, on/off, Sybil). The results of the evaluations show that trust stability has improved, that detection of behavior-based attacks has improved, and that the use of the token-based handover mechanism has reduced the authentication delay by 45%. The proposed framework represents a secure and scalable solution for next-generation vehicular networks, and it sheds light on the issues associated with detecting Sybil attacks as part of the process.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1926040.title: Explaining English learning motivation in digital EFL environments through emotional intelligence, academic well-being, and perceived digital learning support
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1926040.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The rapid expansion of digital learning environments has transformed English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education and increased the importance of understanding the psychological and contextual factors associated with EFL learners' motivation. This study examined the relationships among Emotional Intelligence (EI), Academic Well-Being (AWB), English Learning Motivation (ELM), and Perceived Digital Learning Support (PDLS) in digitally supported English as a Foreign Language environment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed using 435 valid responses, and the proposed relationships were evaluated through partial least squares structural equation modelling using WarpPLS.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity. EI was positively associated with AWB (β = 0.354,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      &lt; 0.001) and ELM (β = 0.331,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      &lt; 0.001). AWB was also positively associated with ELM (β = 0.229,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      &lt; 0.001). The Stable3 output indicated a positive indirect association between EI and ELM through AWB (β = 0.081,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      = 0.008). It also indicated a positive interaction between PDLS and AWB in relation to ELM (β = 0.180,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      &lt; 0.001). The model explained 12.5% of the variance in AWB and 24.3% of the variance in ELM.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings indicate that EI, AWB, and PDLS are positively associated with ELM. However, because the analysis used 100 Stable3 resamples and did not generate conventional bootstrapped confidence intervals, the indirect and interaction results are provisional associations that require confirmation through conventional bootstrapping. Given the cross-sectional design, the findings represent statistical associations rather than causal relationships.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fphar.2026.1876559.title: Interpretable machine learning classifies β-lactamase subclasses and prioritizes boundary variants for antimicrobial resistance surveillance
doi:10.3389/fphar.2026.1876559.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Antimicrobial resistance is a major global health threat, and β-lactamase-mediated inactivation of β-lactam antibiotics remains a leading cause of treatment failure. Rapid identification of emerging β-lactamase variants and improved understanding of their functional diversity are therefore essential for resistance surveillance and therapeutic development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Here, we developed an interpretable machine learning framework to classify major Class A β-lactamase subclasses (TEM, SHV, and CTX-M) and distinguish them from non-β-lactamase hydrolases using multidimensional protein descriptors. Descriptors based on sequence composition, physicochemical properties, residue accessibility, and structural topology were evaluated to identify a minimal panel of 30 descriptors while preserving biological interpretability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The selected descriptors provided strong discriminatory power and were linked to steric environment, hydrophobicity, flexibility, solvent exposure, and residue interaction patterns, consistent with roles in substrate recognition and catalysis. Projection into reduced descriptor space identified transitional variants near subclass boundaries, including CTX-M/SHV convergence zones and non-β-lactamase hydrolases with partial β-lactamase-like signatures. Representative case studies indicated that some apparent misclassifications may reflect annotation inconsistencies, scaffold convergence, or early adaptive trajectories, highlighting candidates for experimental follow-up. External validation using 271 independent proteins annotated as non-β-lactamase hydrolases demonstrated 96.95% specificity, with only limited false-positive assignments. Most incorrect classifications showed weak statistical support, indicating that confidence filtering could further improve screening performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Overall, this study demonstrates that compact descriptor-based models can provide accurate and interpretable classification of β-lactamase-related proteins while identifying emerging boundary variants relevant to antimicrobial resistance surveillance. The framework offers a scalable approach for protein annotation, monitoring resistance evolution, and supporting future inhibitor development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.60087/jklst.vol5.n3.002.title: Measuring Hydrogen Sulphide (H₂S) Gas in The Air of The Refinery And around the Refinery in Erbil – Iraq
doi:10.60087/jklst.vol5.n3.002.abstract: <jats:p>The aim of this study is to publish the measurement results of hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) gases both inside and around petroleum refinery complex, and study the environmental and social impacts of the results, in the town of Erbil (Kurdistan Region of Iraq). These measurements were made at twelve monitoring stations at an equal distance (0–5 km) from the refinery and analyzed for a period of twelve months, with analysis also examining the output of AERMOD dispersion modelling and a hazard quotient framework. The results demonstrated that the on-site mean concentrations are above international occupational exposure and community exposure guidelines and that concentrations are a function of the distance from the source source, varying exponentially but concentrations remain significantly higher than the odour detect levels in the residences of the community ring. Winter and night time are periods of time when atmospheric stability will make for much greater exposure. The study highlights that the emissions generated in the refinery activities represent an externality which is not internalized and provides policy suggestions with regard to the need for buffer-zone regulation, monitoring infrastructure over the years and the prioritization of investment for the abatement.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-1533-9.ch009.title: Emerging Cybersecurity Challenges in Machine Learning-Enabled Smart Heterogeneous Networks
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-1533-9.ch009.abstract: <jats:p>The chapter tries to resolve this emerging problem of machine learning-based smart heterogeneous networks, and cybersecurity by creating a multi-layered security infrastructure which is scalable to detect and react to security attacks in real-time. It proposes a multi-modal deep learning (CNNLSTM), adaptive control by reinforcement learning, and privacy-sensitive controls, such as federated learning. Heterogeneous datasets, including the IoT traffic, intrusion detection benchmarks, and multi-step attack scenarios, which are synthetic, are trained and tested with the model. The accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC, and the computational efficiency metrics are used to measure the performance in dynamic and noisy settings. The suggested framework is also a better performer than the baseline models, where accuracy is 98.37 and has a better ability to resist multi-step and evolving cyber threats. Integration of reinforcement learning increases adaptability and multi-modal features fusion increases detection accuracy.</jats:p>

doi:10.56040/emgb2314.title: Rethinking translation through an interlingual focus on form: Students' experiences and pedagogical insights for grammar learning
doi:10.56040/emgb2314.abstract: <jats:p>This study explores how translation as a communicative activity may support learners’ experiences of grammar learning through an interlingual focus on form. While recent research has re-evaluated translation through a translanguaging lens, its role in facilitating focus on form remains under-explored. Drawing on a functionalist (Skopos-oriented) view of translation, the study examines how students experienced interlingual focus on form in an introductory tertiary translation unit. Survey data from 73 EFL students suggest that purpose-oriented translation tasks were widely experienced as meaningful opportunities to engage with grammar in context across learners with differing levels of course performance. Students particularly associated translation with contextualized grammar use, heightened awareness of grammar’s communicative role, and opportunities to apply grammatical forms in contexts where the L1 supported access to meaning. Rather than positioning translation as a technique for isolated form practice, the study conceptualizes translation as a mediational space in which learners evaluate grammatical choices in relation to communicative purpose, audience, and contextual appropriateness. The findings highlight the pedagogical value of designing translation tasks that strategically engage learners’ plurilingual repertoires to support meaningful engagement with grammar in communicative contexts.</jats:p>

doi:10.1093/g3journal/jkag264.title: Evolutionary and Deep Learning Models Highlight Deleterious Mutations Behind the History of Sugar Beet Breeding
doi:10.1093/g3journal/jkag264.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Sugar beet (Beta vulgaris ssp. vulgaris) is a major global source of sucrose. Domestication and a history of breeding have shaped the distribution of deleterious mutations across the genome. Accurately resolving these variants offers a compelling avenue to accelerate crop improvement through breeding or genetic engineering. We combine three evolutionary methods to identify putatively deleterious derived mutations: angiosperm-wide DNA language deep learning model (PlantCaduceus), fine-scale evolutionary rates from Amaranthaceae plant family sequence alignments using PAML and PhyloP. We defined a high-confidence set of ∼5k deleterious variants enriched for alleles under negative selection. We then evaluate these deleterious mutations across a multi-study panel of more than 1,900 whole-genome sequenced wild and cultivated beet accessions. We found that domesticated beet accessions exhibit higher deleterious load relative to wild maritima, yet sugar beet carries significantly fewer deleterious variants than other cultivated beet crops. Historical trends show a decline in genetic load across more than a century of sugar beet entries in the U.S. NPGS, likely reflecting sustained purging during modern breeding. This combinatorial method of leveraging evolutionary conservation reveals how deleterious mutations have shaped sugar beet breeding history and provides potential targets for future selection, causal-variant discovery, and precision genome engineering.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fmech.2026.1926649.title: A unified unsupervised deep learning and stride threat modeling framework for multi-domain cyber-physical security in nuclear digital twins
doi:10.3389/fmech.2026.1926649.abstract: <jats:p>The increasing adoption of Digital Twin (DT) architectures in nuclear power systems has accelerated the convergence of Operational Technology (OT) and Information Technology (IT), exposing critical cyber-physical infrastructure to sophisticated signature-independent attacks that cannot be reliably detected using conventional signature-based Intrusion Detection Systems. Addressing the heterogeneous characteristics of physical process telemetry and industrial network traffic remains a major challenge for developing practical anomaly detection frameworks. This research proposes a unified unsupervised deep learning and threat modeling framework that integrates domain-aware preprocessing, temporal anomaly detection, adaptive thresholding, and STRIDE-based threat attribution into a single cyber-physical security architecture for nuclear DT. The framework combines a Long Short-Term Memory Autoencoder (LSTM-AE) with domain-specific normalization strategies, applying Min-Max scaling to bounded physical telemetry and Robust scaling to highly variable network traffic while preserving the statistical characteristics of each operational domain. A dynamic 99.5th-percentile anomaly threshold is employed to reduce false-positive alarms that could lead to unnecessary operational interventions in safety-critical environments. To improve the interpretability of unsupervised anomaly detection, the framework incorporates a deterministic feature-level attribution mechanism that maps localized reconstruction errors to the STRIDE threat taxonomy, providing human-readable cyber-physical threat intelligence for system operators. The proposed framework is validated across three publicly available industrial control system datasets acting as nuclear-relevant industrial proxies for complementary operational domains: HAI (primary power generation), SWaT (secondary cooling processes), and WUSTL-IIoT (edge network monitoring). Experimental evaluation demonstrates high discriminative capacity, achieving ROC-AUC scores of 0.944, 0.948, and 0.985, respectively. The results demonstrate that integrating domain-aware preprocessing, unsupervised anomaly detection, adaptive thresholding, and STRIDE-based threat attribution provides an effective and interpretable framework for enhancing cyber-physical security in DT -enabled nuclear environments.</jats:p>

doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.6c02307.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning Overcomes Particle-Size Nonlinearities That Confound the Raman Spectrometry of Granular Carbonaceous Materials
doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.6c02307.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Raman spectroscopy supports multivariate regression models that can offer a rapid and nondestructive approach to quantifying the composition of granular materials. Soils constitute a class of such materials for which chemical analysis provides vital information for agriculture and environmental stewardship. However, soil samples typically present highly heterogeneous mixtures of varying particle size and diverse optical properties owing to light-absorbing constituents. Although particle-size effects on Raman spectrometry in scattering media have long been considered in the context of pharmaceutical analytical technology, the quantitative influence of particle size in opaque, absorbing materials remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the effect of particle size and light absorption in controlled mixture systems that mimic soils. These mixtures, containing particles of varying sizes and optical properties, isolate the ways in which fluorescence, granularity and light absorption affect the accuracy of machine learning regression models. Using a dual-laser Raman system, we collected both conventional Raman and Shifted-Excitation Raman Difference Spectroscopy (SERDS) spectra, showing that light-absorbing compounds attenuate Raman intensities nonlinearly to an extent that varies with particle size. Multivariate regression models link this behavior to optical extinction governed by the surface area of the absorbing grains. We account for this behavior in terms of a simple physical model that incorporates the physics of light scattering and absorption in heterogeneous systems of varying particle size. This hybrid, physics-informed machine learning framework outperforms purely data-driven approaches in predicting sample composition from Raman spectra, highlighting the importance of physical characteristics in the analysis of light-absorbing granular materials.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fnagi.2026.1922577.title: Application of unsupervised and supervised machine learning approaches to blood-based biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease in a memory clinic cohort
doi:10.3389/fnagi.2026.1922577.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Blood-based biomarkers (BBMs) are promising tools to facilitate biological diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). Establishing reliable cutoffs for BBMs represents a major issue for real-world implementation and the investigation of combined BBM approaches is limited. Our aim is to test different machine learning (ML) models for BBMs interpretation with respect to established gold-standard
                      <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic>
                      biomarkers, i.e., cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers, to enhance their standalone and combined diagnostic value for AD.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We selected 434 patients who referred to Perugia University Hospital for perceived cognitive decline with available CSF A β 42/40, pTau181 and tTau and plasma Aβ42, Aβ40, pTau217, pTau181 and NfL. Multiple unsupervised clustering algorithms for cutoff determination and supervised classification models were compared for the prediction of AD defined by a CSF A
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      /T
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      profile.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Different unsupervised clustering models obtained cutoffs with high performances in predicting an AD CSF profile (accuracy &gt; 0.85). Each combination of cutoffs was tested, the best ones achieving A
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      /T
                      <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                      CSF profile prevalences &gt; 0.9 in BBM-positive subgroups. The best supervised ML models achieved accuracies up to 0.88 in 10-fold cross-validation.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our results prove that clustering approaches can help in identifying reliable BBMs cutoffs for AD diagnosis even in the absence of CSF gold standard reference and that ML approaches combining multiple BBMs can strongly enhance their diagnostic accuracy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.60087/ijls.vol3.n3.004.title: University students’ intentions to use AI applications for learning an additional foreign language:
doi:10.60087/ijls.vol3.n3.004.abstract: <jats:p>During the ongoing digital transformation, a growing range of artificial intelligence (AI) applications has become available to support foreign-language learning. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), this study examines how perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) shape university students' attitudes (ATT) toward AI applications and, in turn, their intention to use these applications for learning an additional foreign language (INT). Data were collected through a cross-sectional, convenience-sample survey of 300 undergraduate students at the University of Finance – Marketing (UFM), Vietnam, who reported prior experience using AI applications for language learning; responses were analyzed using PLS-SEM. The results show that both PEOU (β = 0.756, p < 0.001) and PU (β = 0.227, p = 0.004) positively predict ATT (adjusted R² = 0.659), and that ATT in turn positively predicts INT (β = 0.594, p < 0.001; adjusted R² = 0.350), with PEOU exerting a substantially stronger influence than PU. Because the design is cross-sectional and self-reported, and because the sample was restricted to students who had already adopted AI applications, the findings describe behavioral intention rather than actual use or learning effectiveness. The study extends TAM to the context of AI-assisted additional-language learning and offers universities practical guidance on promoting the usability of AI tools in language teaching.</jats:p>

doi:10.1097/jnr.0000000000000772.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Effect of Gamified Clinical Skill Learning on Learning Outcomes in Undergraduate Nursing Education
doi:10.1097/jnr.0000000000000772.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Nursing education requires innovative approaches to develop core competencies in knowledge, skills, and attitudes. Gamified learning interventions offer promising alternatives to traditional teaching methods for enhancing outcomes in undergraduate nursing education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of gamified learning interventions on knowledge acquisition, skill performance, and attitude enhancement among undergraduate nursing students and to investigate the differences in effects achieved across different gamification categories.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Following PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses) guidelines, a comprehensive search was conducted across six databases (A+ Education, CINAHL, Embase, ERIC, PubMed, and Web of Science) on March 18, 2025. This search targeted randomized controlled trials designed to compare gamified learning with traditional teaching methods in undergraduate nursing education. Study quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool, and evidence certainty was evaluated using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) methodology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The findings of randomized controlled trials involving a total of 1,698 participants demonstrated significantly positive effects favoring gamified learning across all key domains, including knowledge acquisition (standardized mean difference [SMD]=0.81, 95% CI [0.55, 1.07]), skill performance (SMD=1.64, 95% CI [0.96, 2.32]), and attitude enhancement (SMD=0.54, 95% CI [0.07, 1.00]). The subgroup analysis revealed differential effectiveness across gamification categories, with serious games demonstrating large and consistent effects on knowledge acquisition (SMD=0.84, 95% CI [0.43, 1.25],
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">I</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      =61%), while gamified web and mobile learning interventions showed moderate effects with greater variability (SMD=0.55, 95% CI [0.23, 0.87],
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">I</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      =70%). Skill performance exhibited the largest overall effect sizes, although substantial heterogeneity was observed across all outcome domains (
                      <jats:italic toggle="yes">I</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      =82–95%). The results of the GRADE assessment support moderate-certainty evidence for all learning outcomes.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results of this systematic review and meta-analysis provide robust evidence that gamified learning interventions significantly enhance undergraduate nursing education across the knowledge, skills, and attitudes domains. Serious games demonstrated superior consistency for knowledge acquisition, while the strongest overall effects were identified for skill performance. The substantial heterogeneity observed underscores the critical importance of selecting appropriate gamification approaches based on specific educational objectives, institutional technological capabilities, and implementation contexts. These findings support the strategic integration of evidence-based gamified learning into nursing curricula as an effective supplement to traditional teaching methods. Future research should focus on assessing long-term competency retention and developing standardized implementation frameworks to guide the widespread adoption of effective gamified learning approaches in nursing education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.24112/ijccpm.243560.title: 儒家倫理視域下人機如何可信？
doi:10.24112/ijccpm.243560.abstract:
<jats:p>LANGUAGE NOTE | Document text in Chinese; abstract also in English.
人工智能深度介入社會生活，在帶來效率與便利的同時，也引發了前所未有的信任危機。這種危機不僅表現為算法黑箱導致的知情不透明，更觸及人類交往的深層結構——信任本是一種植根於主體間性的心理與德性現象，而人工智能作為非人行動者，既不具備真正的意向性，也缺乏情感與責任能力。儒家倫理以“信”為核心德目之一，將信任置於人倫秩序的存在論基礎之中。本文從儒家“信”的意涵出發，分析人工智能對人際關係信任結構的挑戰：單主體性消解了可信賴性的相互性，人機依賴侵蝕了人際心理基礎，禮的規範性難以有效調節人機互動。這些挑戰的根源在於機器缺乏主體性、心理機制與情感賦予意義的能力。儒家倫理的回應不是簡單地拒絕技術，而是在“以人為本”的價值前提下，嚴格區分人機關係與人際關係，並嘗試創構一種異於傳統人際禮儀的“人機禮儀”。這種建構的理論意義在於：從文化價值觀出發，為可信人機關係提供一種非西方中心主義的倫理方案。
The deep integration of artificial intelligence into social life, while bringing efficiency and convenience, has triggered an unprecedented crisis of trust. This crisis is not only manifested in the opacity of information associated with algorithmic black boxes; it reaches deeper into the fundamental structure of human interaction. Trust is a psychological and moral phenomenon rooted in intersubjectivity, whereas artificial intelligence, as a non-human actor, possesses neither genuine intentionality nor the capacity for emotion or responsibility. Trustworthiness (xin) is one of the core virtues of Confucianism, which situates trust within the existential foundation of the human ethical order. This paper begins with the Confucian meaning of xin and analyses the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to the trust structure of human relationships: the dissolution of dual subjectivity eliminates the mutuality of trustworthiness, human–machine dependency erodes the interpersonal psychological foundation, and the normative power of ritual (li) proves inadequate in regulating human–machine interactions. At the root of these challenges is the machine’s lack of subjectivity, of psychological mechanisms, and of the capacity to endow meaning through emotion. The Confucian ethical response is not to simply reject technology but rather, under the value premise of ‘human-centredness’, to strictly distinguish human–machine relations from human–human relations, and to attempt to construct a ‘human–machine ritual’ that differs from traditional interpersonal ritual propriety. The theoretical significance of this construction lies in offering, from the perspective of cultural values, a non-Western-centric ethical framework for trustworthy human–machine relationships.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11025381/v1.title: Identification of Lactylation-Related Diagnostic Biomarkers for Atherosclerosis via Integrative Transcriptomic and Machine Learning Analysis
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11025381/v1.abstract: Introduction: Atherosclerosis (AS) is the primary pathological driver of cardiovascular disease mortality. Lactylation modification plays a critical role in cardiovascular diseases, the potential of lactylation-related genes (LRGs) as novel diagnostic biomarkers for AS remains to be fully elucidated. Objectives This study aims to identify key LRGs for the diagnosis of AS. Methods We analyzed the transcriptome dataset of AS patients from the GEO database, identified key genes and co-expression modules through differential expression analysis and Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), and selected key LRGs related to AS by integrating the MSigDB database. Establish a foam cell model to verify these key LRGs. Machine learning diagnostic models (random forest, support vector machine, and generalized linear model) were constructed to evaluate the importance of key LRGs in AS. CIBERSORT and xCell were used to assess the cell composition of AS patients, with a focus on LRGs related to macrophage function. Results Our integrated analysis identified four key LRGs (KCNN4, PIK3CG, SLC25A4, and TPP1) that were significantly dysregulated in AS, and their expression was successfully validated in the macrophage model. The machine learning models further confirmed the importance of these four LRGs. Immune infiltration analysis revealed that TPP1 may be a key gene involved in macrophage function within the AS context. Conclusion This study identified and verified that KCNN4, PIK3CG, SLC25A4, and TPP1 are key LRGs related to AS, highlighting the potential of these LRGs as diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets for AS.

doi:10.60087/ijls.vol3.n3.012.title: Blended Learning and AI in Higher Education: A Literature Review of Their Effectiveness and Barriers for Teachers to Apply Blended Learning in Teaching English Skills to Tourism Students
doi:10.60087/ijls.vol3.n3.012.abstract: <jats:p>There are dramtic transformations undergone in learning and teaching activities as a positive shift from the appearance of the Internet and the network techonology (Cheng & Chau, 2016). Educational activities, especially in higher education, have been witnessing many changes and adjustments to suit the new situation based on scientific, technical development, and infrastructure availability post COVID-19. As a result, the application of blended learning, a form of education that combines both learning via electronic devices as well as online media and face-to-face traditional classroom, in higher education, especially in foreign language courses, is increasingly popular. Moreover, with the dramatic development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) nowadays, blended learning together with AI can be seen as a powerful combination. Tourism students, along with this trend, may improve their learning and practical experience through this adaptive and realistic approach, which helps them in the globalization and sustainable development of this industry. Drawing on recent studies published in reliable academic sources, this literature review aims to synthesize existing evidence on the reported effectiveness as well as barriers of applying blended learning and AI in teaching English skills to tourism learners. Based on the findings, recommendations will be provided on teaching methods and curriculum program to enhance the effectiveness of this application.</jats:p>
