doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1943564.title: Leakage-aware machine learning for data-driven performance prediction of metal–organic framework systems
doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1943564.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are highly tunable porous materials whose performance is governed by complex interactions among structural, chemical, material, and operating variables. This study develops a leakage-aware, data-driven framework for predicting two distinct MOF performance endpoints: loading capacity and cell viability. The curated datasets comprised 161 loading-capacity observations described by 110 metal, ligand, functionality, and molecular-fingerprint variables, and 444 cell-viability observations described by 25 MOF, cell-category, and exposure variables. Histogram-based gradient boosting regression (HGBR) and partial least squares regression (PLSR) were optimized using differential evolution within five-fold grouped cross-validation. Exact duplicate records were constrained to the same data partition to prevent information leakage, while an additional source-held-out test was employed to assess transferability to publications not represented during model training. On the duplicate-safe 20% holdout, HGBR achieved the strongest predictive performance for cell viability (
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                     = 0.774, RMSE = 11.655 percentage points, MAE = 8.153, and AARD = 16.69%), whereas PLSR performed best for loading capacity (
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                     = 0.557, RMSE = 0.345 g/g, and MAE = 0.210 g/g). Permutation analysis identified concentration, Zn and Fe indicators, zeta potential, cell category, and particle size as the most influential variables for viability prediction, while PLSR loading predictions were most sensitive to 2,5-dioxidoterephthalate and Mg-related descriptors. However, negative R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    values obtained when entire source publications were held out revealed substantial distribution shift and limited cross-study generalization. Overall, the results demonstrate the value of leakage-aware machine learning for rigorous, data-driven performance prediction and screening of MOF systems, while showing that broader standardized datasets and independent-study validation are essential before reliable predictive deployment.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.37237/170307.title: Navigating the Shift to Self-Access Learning: Students’ Experiences in a Flipped EFL Writing Course
doi:10.37237/170307.abstract: <jats:p>Developing learner autonomy remains a central goal of self-access language learning, yet many English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners experience difficulties regulating independent learning. This study investigated students’ experiences with a semi-structured pre-class self-access learning approach implemented in a flipped EFL writing course. During a six-week intervention, 58 undergraduate students in a Thai university independently selected learning resources and strategies, and synthesized information through reflective notebook writing. A mixed-methods descriptive design was employed, combining questionnaire data with focus group discussions to examine students’ perceptions, challenges, and learning strategies. Overall, students reported positive perceptions of learning preparation, information management, learning responsibility, and writing readiness. However, they also experienced challenges related to limited linguistic knowledge, evaluating multiple resources, and regulating independent learning. Students addressed these challenges through planning, reflective notetaking, strategic help-seeking, and critical use of multiple learning resources, including GenAI. The findings suggest that semi-structured self-access learning, supported by pedagogical scaffolding, can provide a structured context for exercising learner autonomy while promoting self-regulated learning and emerging GenAI literacy.</jats:p>

doi:10.53941/sce.2026.100011.title: Screening High-Efficiency Deep Eutectic Solvents for Oxidative-Extractive Desulfurization via a Machine Learning Framework to Analyze Intermolecular Interactions
doi:10.53941/sce.2026.100011.abstract: <jats:p>Oxidative-extractive desulfurization (OEDS) represents a highly efficient pathway for removing recalcitrant thiophenic sulfides from liquid fuels. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as promising green extractants due to their tunable multi-site non-covalent interactions and favorable environmental profile. However, exploring the vast chemical space of potential DES formulations demands rational, data-driven methodologies to identify molecular affinities while bypassing costly experimental trial-and-error. Herein, we report a novel hybrid algorithm termed PDI-DMPNN+SME. By coupling solvation free energy predictions with substructural masking, this framework quantitatively decodes the affinity and repulsion aimed at target molecules. The algorithm systematically evaluates both the extraction affinity of candidate DESs toward oxidized thiophenic species and the internal eutectic feasibility between solvent components. Through high-throughput screening of 19,291 binary candidates, an environmentally benign citric acid-glycerol DES system was identified as a promising extractant candidate. Under optimized process conditions, this system achieved a single-stage dibenzothiophene (DBT) removal efficiency of 99.95% in model oil and 93.72% in real diesel, maintaining satisfactory performance (98.50% and 90.80%, respectively) after the tested three consecutive regeneration cycles. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the total interaction energy between the citric acid-glycerol system and dibenzothiophene sulfone (DBTO2) reaches −31.24 kcal/mol. Energy decomposition analysis indicates that electrostatic and dispersion interactions contribute comparably to this stabilization, jointly overcoming Pauli repulsion to form a thermodynamically favorable extractant-solute complex. This work establishes an intelligent, green paradigm for the rational design of functional solvents in advanced separation processes.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10610585/v1.title: Development and Performance Evaluation of a Vacuum-Assisted Stirred Dehumidification Machine for Stingless Bee Honey
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10610585/v1.abstract: Stingless bee honey is a premium natural product with high nutritional and medicinal value; however, its naturally high moisture content (30–35%) promotes microbial fermentation, shortens shelf life, and restricts commercial production. This study presents the development of a compact vacuum-assisted dehumidification machine integrated with a drying-time prediction model for community-scale stingless bee honey processing. The system combines indirect hot-water heating, vacuum evaporation, and mechanical agitation to accelerate moisture removal while maintaining stable operating conditions. Drying experiments were conducted using 10 L of a honey-like sugar solution with an initial moisture content of 35%, targeting a final moisture content of 20%. The effects of heating temperature (50 and 70°C), operating pressure (0 and − 80 kPa), and agitation speed (0 and 60 rpm) on drying performance were investigated. Moisture content, soluble solids (°Brix), thermal efficiency, electrical energy consumption, and drying time were determined. Drying kinetics were analyzed using Newton's drying equation, and an empirical regression model was established to predict drying time under different operating conditions. Vacuum pressure was identified as the dominant factor governing moisture removal, followed by heating temperature and agitation speed. The optimum condition (70°C, -80 kPa, and 60 rpm) reduced the moisture content from 35% to 20% within 9 h, whereas 168 h was required under atmospheric pressure at 50°C without agitation. Soluble solids increased from 64 to 79 °Brix during dehydration. Vacuum operation improved thermal efficiency by 4.21–7.76 times and reduced electrical energy consumption to 0.12–0.14 USD kg -1 . The proposed machine and predictive model provide an energy-efficient and practical solution for producing high-quality stingless bee honey and support process design, optimization, and scale-up for community enterprises.

doi:10.31980/caxra.v6i3.4061.title: Pengaruh Penggunaan Model Pembelajaran Discovery Learning terhadap Minat Belajar Siswa pada Mata Pelajaran IPAS Kelas IV Sekolah Dasar Islam Ar-Raafi Makassar
doi:10.31980/caxra.v6i3.4061.abstract: <jats:p>Penelitian ini bertujuan utnuk mengetahui gambaran penerapan model pembelajaran, minat belajar siswa serta terdapat pengaruh penerapan model discovery learning untuk meningkatkan minat belajar siswa pada mata pelajaran IPAS kelas IV SD Islam Ar-Raafi Makassar. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan jenis Quasi Experiment dan Desain Nonequivalent Control Group Desaign. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 43 siswa yang terdiri atas kelas eksperimen dan kelas kontrol. Teknik pengumpulan data menggunakan observasi dan angket minat belajar dengan skala Likert. Data analisis menggunakan statistik deskripstif dan statistik inferensial melalui uji normalitas, uji homogenitas, serta Independent Sample T-test. Hasil penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa adanya pengaruh kegiatan pembelajaran pada aktivitas guru kategori sangat baik, sedangkan pada aktivitas siswa kategori baik</jats:p>

doi:10.28948/ngumuh.1893199.title: Torque estimation using industrial sensor data: A comparative analysis of deep learning, machine learning, and hyperparameter optimization approaches
doi:10.28948/ngumuh.1893199.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Predictive maintenance is an important approach for reducing unexpected failures and improving operational reliability in industrial systems. In this study, deep learning and machine learning models were comparatively evaluated for torque estimation using the AI4I 2020 predictive maintenance dataset. Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) architectures were analyzed together with conventional regression models, including Random Forest, Extra Trees, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Regression, Ridge Regression, K-Nearest Neighbor, Linear Regression, and Decision Tree. Random Search, Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and model-specific optimization strategies were applied to examine the effect of hyperparameter optimization. Experimental results showed that recurrent deep learning models generally achieved the highest prediction performance under the applied experimental setting. The Random Search-optimized LSTM model obtained the best numerical result with R² = 0.8363, RMSE = 4.0170, and MAE = 3.0004. However, the effect of optimization was model-dependent. While optimization provided limited improvement in recurrent deep learning models, it produced more visible gains in some machine learning models, particularly Support Vector Regression and Gradient Boosting. The findings indicate that model selection and optimization strategy should be evaluated together in sensor-based torque estimation problems.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67147-z.title: A forecast-guided reinforcement learning approach for trajectory planning of unmanned aerial base stations
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-67147-z.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The rapid growth of wireless devices and the emergence of dynamic traffic hotspots have increased the need for intelligent trajectory planning in unmanned aerial vehicle base stations (UAV-BSs) operating in complex urban environments, where conventional reactive methods relying only on current system states cannot anticipate near-future changes in demand, obstacle risk, and communication conditions, often resulting in inefficient coverage, higher energy consumption, and unsafe flight behavior. To address this limitation, this paper proposes Forecast-SAC, a forecasting-enhanced deep reinforcement learning framework for proactive 3D UAV-BS trajectory planning that integrates a CNN-LSTM forecasting module with a Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) controller, where the forecasting module learns spatiotemporal demand and obstacle-risk patterns from historical map sequences and the SAC agent uses both predicted and current states to generate continuous control actions under joint service, safety, and energy constraints. The framework is evaluated in a grid-based urban simulation environment with mobile Gaussian hotspot demand, spatial obstacle-risk fields, queue-based service accumulation, and an air-to-ground channel model dependent on elevation angle, while training is performed using sequence-based forecasting and environment interaction under collision-avoidance and energy constraints. Experimental results show stable convergence and demonstrate that Forecast-SAC achieves an average served traffic of 4439.26 ± 532.96 Mbit, energy efficiency of 0.0623 Mbit/J under a revised rotary-wing energy model, average risk of 2.85, a baseline fairness index of 0.229 (a limitation addressed by the proposed fairness-enhancement term, which raises the index to 0.318–0.401; Sect. 4.7), and battery retention of 96.23%, while maintaining low-latency inference (3.07 ± 0.21 ms) compatible with real-time control loops; deployment readiness beyond simulation would additionally require hardware-in-the-loop validation. Comparative results indicate that Forecast-SAC produces smoother and safer trajectories than reactive baselines while maintaining competitive throughput. Ablation studies further show that replacing SAC with heuristic forecast-driven rules increases risk by 57–157%, confirming the necessity of learned continuous control, while PPO and DDPG baselines without forecasting are outperformed by 25.7–41.3% in episodic return, validating the contribution of spatiotemporal prediction. Sensitivity analysis over the violation penalty (λv ∈ {100–1000}) identifies 700 as a near-optimal tradeoff point, achieving 85.7% fewer violations than the least-penalized setting with only a small throughput loss. Multi-step forecasting analysis shows that single-step (t + 1) prediction is adopted as the primary operating point for its favourable accuracy–latency tradeoff, while the two-step (t + 1 + t + 3) variant yields a marginal return improvement at increased inference cost, and longer horizons (t + 5) degrade performance due to error accumulation, and a fairness-oriented variant increases the fairness index to 0.318–0.401. The proposed framework demonstrates that unified predictive-control learning enables safe and efficient UAV-BS navigation under dynamic uncertainty, achieving a strong safety–throughput balance that reactive methods cannot match in high-risk environments.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1889499.title: Problem solving and responsible GenAI use in assessment: students’ reported experiences in open and distance learning
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1889499.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used by students to obtain explanations, generate ideas, improve written responses and prepare assessment tasks. However, limited evidence exists on how students in open-distance alternative-access programmes experience GenAI in mathematics assessment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This qualitative study examined how 27 Higher Certificate students at a South African open and distance learning institution described the role, benefits and limitations of GenAI while preparing fraction-related portfolio activities. Data were collected via a single open-ended questionnaire item, completed voluntarily after all assessment activities had been submitted. The responses were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Four overlapping themes were identified: support for understanding and approaching tasks, support for constructing written responses, conditional trust and evaluative engagement, and non-use, resistance and ambiguous engagement. Students reported that GenAI assisted with clarification, examples, organisation, and language, but they also described outputs they perceived as inaccurate, overly general, or insufficiently explained. Ten participants expressed concerns about reliability or described checking, adapting, limiting or rejecting GenAI use, although the study did not verify the quality of these practices.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings suggest that the educational value of GenAI is shaped by students' capacity to exercise judgement and retain responsibility for the reasoning represented in their work. Verification is therefore positioned as a potentially important epistemic practice in GenAI-supported mathematics assessment. The study recommends explicit discipline-specific guidance and assessment designs that make students' mathematical reasoning visible.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1108/ijilt-12-2025-0390.title: AI-enhanced learning tools: impact of information quality characteristics on perceived ease of use analyzed with PLS-SEM and NCA
doi:10.1108/ijilt-12-2025-0390.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The purpose of this paper is to explore how the four dimensions of informational quality characteristics – accuracy, comprehensiveness, relevance, and timeliness – shape learners' perceptions of the ease of use of information in AI-enhanced learning environments. The study seeks to deepen understanding of how the quality of AI-generated instructional content influences students' ability to engage with, interpret, and apply information effectively. By extending the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to comprise informational attributes, the paper aims to clarify which informational quality characteristics make AI-supported learning more intuitive, cognitively efficient, and pedagogically meaningful.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 197 responses were collected among undergraduate and graduate business students at a mid-sized Canadian university during the winter of 2024. The respondents were at least 18 years old. The researchers developed a survey instrument whose questions originated from prior research. SPSS and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with the Importance-Performance (IPMA) and Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) were utilized as statistical techniques.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results indicate that comprehensiveness is the only significant determinant of perceived ease of use of information in AI-enhanced learning environments. IPMA identifies comprehensiveness as a high-importance but underperforming factor, suggesting that improvements in this area would most enhance usability. NCA further reveals that both comprehensiveness and relevance are essential, must-have conditions for ease of use. In contrast, accuracy and timeliness exert limited influence on perceived ease of use.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study extends the explanatory scope of TAM by incorporating informational quality characteristics as antecedents of perceived ease of use in AI-enhanced learning contexts. It is among the first to combine PLS-SEM, IPMA, and NCA to distinguish between determinant and must-have predictors of usability. The findings highlight that the comprehensiveness and relevance of AI-generated information – rather than its accuracy or timeliness – are the key factors shaping learners' perceptions of ease of use.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.1108/ijilt-12-2025-0390.venue: The International Journal of Information and Learning Technology

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10952282/v1.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Climate-Sensitive Agricultural Pesticide Exposure Modeling and Water-Quality Validation
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10952282/v1.abstract: Water-quality monitoring networks are too sparse to track how climate extremes are shifting agricultural pesticide pollution, and screening-level exposure models proposed to fill this gap are rarely tested against independent real-world monitoring data. We built such a model for California and tested it directly. A physics-based fate index – first-order decay from each chemical’s soil half-life – is driven by a LightGBM model that predicts weekly pesticide application by county and chemical from eight years (2016–2023) of public agricultural, weather, and chemical-property data. We validated the resulting exposure index against 3,924 real U.S. Geological Survey stream measurements at 554 California stations, never used in training. For the two most-monitored chemicals, agreement was strong and statistically significant (Malathion, ρ = 0.51, p < 10−6; Metolachlor, ρ = 0.28, p < 10−8); across all fourteen monitored chemicals pooled together, the correlation was weak, which we attribute to genuinely different fate behavior across chemical classes rather than a failure of the method. The underlying application model generalized well across space (R2 = 0.64) and time (R2 = 0.89), but far less well to entirely unseen chemicals (R2 = 0.32) – and we found, unexpectedly, that adding hand-curated chemical descriptors made this harder task worse, not better. A bounded climate-stress sensitivity analysis using warming scenarios drawn from California’s own state climate assessment indicates population-weighted exposure could roughly double by mid-to-late century, concentrated in desert and Central Valley counties that also have large farmworker populations. We report every result here, including the ones that did not work as hoped, because that is what makes a screening model trustworthy.

doi:10.37237/170304.title: Analysing Student Staff Member Community Networks Through Basic Psychological Needs Theory
doi:10.37237/170304.abstract: <jats:p>Student staff members (SSMs) are a central component of self-access language learning (SALL) communities. Previous research has predominantly explored SSM psychology and practical issues from an individualistic perspective, rather than adopting holistic approaches that examine SSMs as a single yet complex group of interacting individuals. This article explores the internal dynamics of a community of 16 SSMs at a university self-access centre in Kansai, Japan, by drawing on research methods used in Social Network Analysis (SNA). Based on data collected from the SSMs via surveys, network graphs of SSM relations are produced and interpreted using both SNA and the lens of Basic Psychological Needs Theory. This approach results in visual snapshots of the internal structure of the SSM group’s dynamics and insights into how its organisation and structure may impact the motivation and well-being of the group as a whole. Analysis of the graphs reveals a generally cohesive community with both features suggestive of basic psychological need satisfaction and frustration. Practical recommendations are offered based on these results, and the theoretical and methodological implications of applying SNA to SSM communities are also discussed. Finally, limitations of the study and future research directions are considered.</jats:p>

doi:10.58230/josse.v3i2.767.title: Teachers’ Perceptions of Deep Learning in History Education
doi:10.58230/josse.v3i2.767.abstract: <jats:p>This study is motivated by the tendency for history instruction in schools to be dominated by conventional, rote-memorization-based methods, which can limit students’ active engagement, motivation, and critical thinking skills. The study aims to describe teachers’ perceptions of the deep learning approach in history instruction and to identify the obstacles they face in implementing this approach at SMA Negeri 2 Sipora. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed. The research informants consisted of three history teachers. Data were collected through checklist-based observation, interviews, and document analysis, and were analyzed through the stages of data collection, reduction, presentation, and conclusion drawing. The results indicate that teachers hold a highly positive perception of deep learning as a student-centered approach that emphasizes in-depth conceptual understanding, specifically learning that is mindful, meaningful, and joyful. This approach has proven effective in enhancing students’ active engagement, motivation, and critical thinking skills by connecting past historical events with real-life contexts. However, implementation in the field faces several obstacles, including: (1) the need for students to adapt, as they are accustomed to passive learning methods; (2) the diversity of students’ socioeconomic backgrounds and family geographical locations; (3) limited technological facilities, such as an insufficient number of projectors; and (4) limited internet access and students’ ability to afford data packages. In conclusion, the deep learning approach has proven capable of increasing students’ active engagement in learning; however, optimizing its implementation requires improvements in school facilities and infrastructure, stronger parental support, and the ongoing development of teacher creativity.</jats:p>
doi:10.58230/josse.v3i2.767.venue: Journal of Social and Scientific Education

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11160449/v1.title: Subjective Task Value and Activating Affect in English Learning: Construct Differentiation and Associations with Proficiency
authors: Jesús A. G. Ochoa de Alda
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11160449/v1.abstract: Subjective task-value appraisals and affective experiences are theoretically distinguishable components of learning and motivation, but their empirical differentiation when assessed concurrently remains unclear. This study examined the distinctiveness and interrelations of interest, utility, perceived cost, positive activating emotions (PAE), and negative activating emotions (NAE), and evaluated how these dimensions related to English proficiency in a consequential learning context. Participants were 178 Spanish preservice teachers enrolled in a bilingual-track program who completed a brief value–affect questionnaire and a 15-item English proficiency measure. Confirmatory factor analyses compared a theoretically specified five-factor model with alternative models collapsing closely related dimensions. The five-factor model provided better comparative fit than models combining interest with utility, perceived cost with NAE, or both pairs. However, interest and utility showed very limited discriminant differentiation, while perceived cost and NAE also overlapped substantially. Despite this overlap, collapsing these dimensions resulted in poorer model fit, supporting their retention as separate dimensions while qualifying claims about their empirical independence. Proficiency was positively associated with interest, utility, and PAE and negatively associated with perceived cost and NAE, with the largest associations observed for perceived cost and NAE. These findings highlight an important distinction between theoretical separability and empirical differentiation and identify perceived cost as a potentially informative negative component of task value when motivation and affect are examined jointly.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11160449/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.1108/jsit-07-2025-0313.title: Unravelling risk-trust interplay in artificial intelligence-based systems for e-learning platforms: evidence from CB-SEM and fsQCA
doi:10.1108/jsit-07-2025-0313.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to investigate the interplay between perceived risk and initial trust in shaping learners’ satisfaction and intention to use Artificial Intelligence-based Systems (AIS) in e-learning platforms. It addresses a key gap by theorising multidimensional risk factors and early-stage trust antecedents in AI-enabled personalised learning environments characterised by algorithmic opacity, continuous data-driven personalisation, and heightened privacy concerns, particularly in emerging economies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Grounded in perceived risk theory and the initial trust model, the study analyses data from 371 higher-education students from an emerging economy. A complementary multi-method quantitative design combines covariance-based structural equation modelling (CB-SEM) to test hypothesised net effects with fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) to identify configurational pathways leading to intention to use AIS.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>CB-SEM shows that time, performance, psychological and privacy risks significantly influence satisfaction and intention to use AIS, while trust propensity and structural assurance shape initial trust. Although initial trust exhibits no direct linear effect on intention, fsQCA reveals eight equifinal configurations through which satisfaction and structural assurance compensate for elevated risk perceptions demonstrating that AIS adoption is shaped by a risk–trust–satisfaction interplay rather than a single causal pathway.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>While the cross-sectional design limits causal inference, the study advances IS theory by demonstrating how risk, trust and satisfaction jointly shape AIS adoption and by showing how configurational mechanisms complement net-effect explanations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes by integrating CB-SEM and fsQCA within a complementary multi-method quantitative design and by revealing how satisfaction and structural assurance jointly compensate for risk perceptions in shaping AIS adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1186/s12912-026-05254-y.title: Enhancing critical thinking skills and self-directed learning among critical care nursing students: a quasi-experimental study on the impact of the modified KWHLAQ strategy
doi:10.1186/s12912-026-05254-y.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To evaluate the effect of the modified Know–Want–Learn–How–Apply–Questions (KWHLAQ) strategy on critical thinking and self-directed learning among third-semester undergraduate nursing students enrolled in a critical care nursing course.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A quasi-experimental, nonequivalent control group pretest–posttest design was employed. One hundred undergraduate nursing students (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 50 per group) enrolled in the Critical and Emergency Nursing Department, Faculty of Nursing, Alexandria University, participated during the 2025 academic session. The study group received a 12-week structured intervention based on the KWHLAQ framework; the control group received standard lecture-based instruction. Both groups completed the Critical Thinking Questionnaire (CThQ; α = 0.80) and the Self-Directed Learning Instrument (SDLI; α = 0.80) before and after the intervention.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      After covariate adjustment, the study group demonstrated significantly higher post-intervention critical thinking scores than the control group (
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       < 0.05; Cohen’s d = 0.67, moderate-to-large effect). The study group improved significantly in overall critical thinking (mean difference = 5.66;
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       < 0.01) and in the evaluating subscale (mean difference = 4.50;
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001; Cohen’s d = 2.10, whereas the control group’s scores declined. Self-directed learning improved substantially in the study group (mean difference = 23.06;
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001; Cohen’s d = 2.45), with significant gains across all four SDLI subscales.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Integration of this structured, low-cost, and replicable pedagogical framework into nursing curricula may promote active learning, reflective reasoning, and clinical decision-making competencies essential for high-acuity practice.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.59261/bustechno.v7i4.820.title: Machine Learning Pipeline for Educational Prediction and Student Segmentation
doi:10.59261/bustechno.v7i4.820.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: Educational data mining has become increasingly important for understanding student performance and learning patterns; however, challenges in data preprocessing, feature selection, interpretability, and the limited integration of predictive modeling with clustering remain unresolved.
Objective: This study develops an integrated machine-learning workflow that combines feature engineering, predictive modeling, and student segmentation for educational data analysis.
Methods: The analytical dataset contains 343 student records and 87 numeric features after data-type conversion, with Adaptability as the prediction target. The workflow combines data-quality control, feature engineering, ANOVA, mutual information, and recursive feature elimination (RFE) for feature selection; comparative classification; stratified cross-validation; and K-means clustering with principal component analysis (PCA) for student segmentation.
Results: Logistic Regression produced the strongest reported discrimination (Accuracy = 0.9855; Precision = 1.0000; Recall = 0.9697; F1 = 0.9846; MCC = 0.9713; Kappa = 0.9709; AUC = 0.997). AUC values for the remaining models ranged from 0.958 (KNN) to 0.996 (Gradient Boosting). Feature rankings are interpreted as predictive associations rather than causal effects, and clustering provides descriptive student subgroups.
Conclusion: The study provides a traceable, dataset-specific workflow linking preprocessing, feature construction and selection, predictive benchmarking, and descriptive student segmentation. Generalization beyond the supplied dataset requires external validation, and the clustering results should not be interpreted as evidence of intervention effects.</jats:p>

doi:10.31980/caxra.v6i3.3851.title: Pengaruh Model Project-Based Learning terhadap Keterampilan Kolaborasi dan Literasi Ekonomi Siswa Sekolah Dasar
doi:10.31980/caxra.v6i3.3851.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to determine the differences in collaborative skills and economic literacy of fifth-grade students at SDN 1 Karyasari when using the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) method compared to a traditional teacher-centered approach. This study also examines the influence of the PjBL method on students' ability to collaborate. This study employed a mixed methods approach, a combination of quantitative and qualitative research methods, to obtain more comprehensive, valid, reliable, and objective data. The results indicate that the project-based learning model significantly improved collaboration skills and economic literacy in the science subject of grades 6 (Experimental) and 7 (Control) of SDN 1 Karyasari. Therefore, it can be concluded that the project-based learning model significantly influenced the improvement of collaboration skills and economic literacy in students in the science subject.</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/lthe-06-2025-0039.title: Stakeholder prioritization in higher education accreditation in the UAE context: a multi-criteria analysis using Analytic Hierarchy Process
doi:10.1108/lthe-06-2025-0039.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study compares how students, faculty, administrators and employers in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) prioritize key higher education accreditation criteria to inform more stakeholder-responsive quality assurance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) pairwise comparisons, data from 240 participants across four accredited UAE Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) were analyzed across five criteria; only consistent judgments (Consistency Ratio = 0.10) were retained to compute priority weights.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Faculty prioritized teaching quality (0.418), students prioritized student support services (0.381), administrators assigned their highest weight to teaching quality (0.310), followed by employability outcomes (0.247) and employers assigned equal highest weights to teaching quality and continuous improvement (0.248 each).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study is limited by its use of purposive sampling across four UAE institutions and a restricted set of accreditation criteria, which may constrain generalizability. Despite this, the findings offer clear practical implications by demonstrating how stakeholder-weighted priorities can guide more targeted, transparent and outcome-oriented accreditation policies and resource allocation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings help institutions and accreditation bodies align evaluation criteria and resources with stakeholder priorities, strengthening teaching quality, student support, employability outcomes and continuous improvement within outcome-based accreditation frameworks.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Social implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Embedding stakeholder priorities in accreditation supports more inclusive and transparent quality assurance, improving graduate readiness, public trust and the societal value of higher education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes to the limited literature applying AHP to stakeholder prioritization of higher education accreditation criteria in the UAE. It provides a data-driven basis for aligning accreditation criteria with stakeholder expectations and supports the shift from compliance-based evaluation to stakeholder-informed, outcome-oriented quality assurance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1108/tlo-03-2025-0074.title: Women entrepreneurial orientation, organisational learning capability and business performance in a hostile environment
doi:10.1108/tlo-03-2025-0074.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to explore how organisational learning capability (OLC) mediates the link between entrepreneurial orientation (EO) and small enterprise performance of women-owned and/or managed tourism and hospitality firms in a hostile environment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study adopts a quantitative approach, using a two-wave time-lagged survey to collect data from a sample of 405 women entrepreneurs in the tourism and hospitality small enterprises in Nigeria. A random sampling technique was used to select participants for the survey. Partial least square-structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) via PLS4 was used to analyse the data collected.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings indicate that the EO dimensions (i.e. innovativeness, proactiveness, risk-taking, competitive aggressiveness and autonomy) significantly predict the performance of women-owned and/or managed tourism and hospitality small enterprises. Moreover, the study demonstrates that OLC significantly mediates the impact of all EO dimensions on their performance, except for risk-taking.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study addresses the limited understanding of how OLC is central to the performance of entrepreneurial-oriented organisations owned and/or managed by women within the tourism and hospitality industry operating in a hostile environment. Specifically, it clarifies the EO–OLC–performance links through the theoretical frameworks of the resource-based view and organisational learning theory, thereby advancing knowledge at the intersection of gendered entrepreneurship and organisational learning in underexplored contexts.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.59188/eduvest.v6i9.53414.title: Innovations in Design and Islamic-Value-Based Learning Models in the Digital Age: A Qualitative Study at MTS MAI Purwakarta
doi:10.59188/eduvest.v6i9.53414.abstract: <jats:p>s study examined the development of design innovations and Islamic-value-based learning models in addressing the challenges of the digital era at MTs MAI Purwakarta. The madrasah has distinctive characteristics due to its location within an Arab community that has developed since the colonial period, contributing to the formation of a strong Islamic educational tradition, particularly in Arabic language instruction, adab (Islamic manners), and the internalization of religious values. This study employed a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through field observations, in-depth interviews, and document reviews. The data were analyzed interactively through the processes of data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that learning innovations at MTs MAI Purwakarta focus not only on the integration of digital technology but also on strengthening historically rooted Islamic values. The learning design integrates cognitive, affective, and spiritual dimensions through value internalization in learning planning, the utilization of Islamic-content-based digital media, and religious habituation within the learning environment. The implemented learning models are adaptive, including blended learning and digital-based collaborative learning, while remaining guided by Islamic values of adab and ethics. The findings reveal a synthesis between the Islamic educational traditions of the Arab community and the demands of contemporary digital learning. This study contributes to the development of an integrative Islamic-value-based learning model that is contextual and relevant to education in the digital era.</jats:p>

doi:10.1515/cppm-2025-0318.title: Hybrid modeling and energy optimization of NGL demethanizers using deep reinforcement learning
doi:10.1515/cppm-2025-0318.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Cryogenic NGL demethanizers suffer from energy inefficiencies due to non-convex thermodynamic constraints. This study aims to implement a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework to optimize energy consumption while respecting complex operational boundaries. A Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) agent was employed, trained on 2,000 rigorous Aspen HYSYS digital twin scenarios via a Deep Neural Network (DNN) surrogate. Unlike simplified proxy models, this supervisory strategy directly interacts with the high-fidelity simulation to navigate nonlinear process dynamics. The results demonstrate a 12 % reduction in reboiler duty compared to baseline operations, yielding potential annual savings of $4.0 million and a reduction of approximately 15,000 tonnes of CO₂. Sensitivity analysis confirms economic robustness under conservative market conditions. The proposed framework demonstrates the potential of DRL as a computationally efficient alternative for steady-state supervisory optimization in complex cryogenic processes. By utilizing a high-fidelity steady-state process surrogate, it provides a promising framework for industrial energy optimization, setting the stage for future real-time industrial applications.</jats:p>

doi:10.2166/wpt.2026.470.title: Machine learning-based hydrological trend analysis for water scarcity assessment in Erbil, Kurdistan Region of Iraq
doi:10.2166/wpt.2026.470.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study explores how long-term changes in temperature and precipitation have shaped river discharge in Erbil, a city in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, using historical climate data from the World Bank Group Climate Knowledge Portal and discharge data from the Eski Kalak gauge station. A machine learning approach, extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), was applied to extrapolate future discharge trends for 2024–2050 based on historical climate observations. The future results represent trend-based extrapolations rather than physically based climate model projections. The findings show a clear decline in precipitation and river flow over the past century, while temperatures continue to rise. The precipitation–discharge statistical relationship was weak (r = 0.038), suggesting that rising temperature and associated evapotranspiration processes may contribute to discharge variability alongside other climatic and anthropogenic influences, supported by a moderate negative discharge–temperature correlation (r = −0.255). The effect of upstream activities, including water diversions and dam construction, also cannot be disregarded and likely contributes to disruption of natural flow regimes. The XGBoost model achieved strong predictive performance (testing: R2 = 0.89, NSE = 0.88, RMSE = 17.3 m3/s), and the future-risk assessment indicates a rising likelihood of below-average discharge.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/978-3-032-38618-2_15.title: Designing a Universal Student Passport for Responsible AI-Driven Personalised Learning in Engineering Higher Education
doi:10.1007/978-3-032-38618-2_15.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence (AI), and particularly Generative AI, is increasingly being adopted in higher education to support content adaptation, feedback generation, concept explanation, and more personalised learning experiences. While these developments offer substantial promise, current approaches to AI-supported personalisation often remain fragmented, tool-driven, and insufficiently grounded in structured representations of learner needs and preferences. This creates a gap between the technical capabilities of AI and the pedagogical, organisational, and governance requirements necessary for its responsible integration in higher education.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper proposes a conceptual architecture for a Universal Student Passport to support responsible AI-driven personalised learning in engineering higher education. The work is developed within the context of the Erasmus+ funded MultAI-PASS project, and is grounded in early project design activities, including a review of learning preferences and learner variability, as well as an analytical synthesis of learner-related dimensions relevant to personalised support. The paper focuses on the design rationale of the passport, its core architectural layers, its intended information flow, and the governance principles required to ensure transparency, student agency, and educator oversight. In doing so, it offers a structured conceptual bridge between learner-related preferences and AI-supported educational adaptation in engineering higher education.</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s13000-026-01831-6.title: TedMIL: Text-Driven Multiple Instance Learning for Fine-Grained Pathological Classification with Melanoma-FISH Status Prediction
doi:10.1186/s13000-026-01831-6.abstract: Fine-grained classification of melanoma with fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) status prediction using whole slide images (WSIs) provides critical insights into progression and prognosis. Multiple instance learning (MIL) has been effectively applied. However, existing MIL methods rely on visual features, which makes MIL lack macroscopic prior-driven guidance, resulting in the inability of visual modeling to better capture the intrinsic representations of melanoma. To fully model the macroscopic priors provided by category-agnostic texts, this study proposes TedMIL, a novel Text-driven MIL, which consists of the Text Injected Re-embedding (TIR) and the Text-Image Matching (TIM). Based on pathological priors, LLMs, and gated feature fusion, TIR re-embeds the feature representations of MIL by injecting macroscopic sementic into morphological features. TIM refines the final class output probabilities through the cross-modal affinity quantification mechanism based on normalized feature space distance. Data were accessed for research purposes between 25/10/2025 and 24/10/2026 in accordance with the approved study protocol. For the melanoma identification task, TedMIL achieved an AUC of 97.9% and an accuracy (ACC) of 93.4% on the test set, demonstrating impressive discriminative capability. For the more challenging fine-grained three-class classification task, TedMIL improves accuracy (ACC) by 2.8%, AUC by 2.2%, and F1-score by 3.0% compared with state-of-the-art MIL baselines. Qualitative visualizations further show that text guidance leads to more spatially coherent attention patterns that better align with diagnostically relevant morphological regions. This paper demonstrates that the proposed text-driven MIL could realize more intrinsic pathological representations and achieve efficient fine-grained classification of melanoma.

doi:10.37237/170302.title: Bridging Classroom and Self-Access Learning: Teacher–Advisor Collaboration for Learner Autonomy
doi:10.37237/170302.abstract: <jats:p>Ecological perspectives on language learning emphasize that learning develops through learners’ interactions with environments across multiple settings. This view is especially relevant to first-year university students, whose learning environments change as they enter higher education and who are expected to take greater responsibility for their learning. Drawing on spatial and ecological perspectives, this study examines how classroom-based practices helped students connect a compulsory English for Academic Purposes (EAP) course with a Self-Access Learning Center (SALC) and other out-of-class learning opportunities. SALC learning advisors collaborated with the classroom teacher through a team-teaching approach involving class visits, goal setting, action planning, e-Portfolio tasks, learning activity records, and reflection. Reflective questionnaire data from 37 students in the 2024 and 2025 cohorts and retrospective interviews with two focal learners were analyzed. The findings suggest that teacher–advisor collaboration helped make out-of-class learning more visible, approachable, and personally meaningful, while allowing students to decide whether and how to engage with the opportunities introduced. They also suggest that engagement beyond the classroom was shaped by emotional and relational support, routines, and changing learner identities. The study argues that teachers can support learner autonomy by positioning the classroom as a point of departure into wider learning spaces.</jats:p>

doi:10.59188/eduvest.v6i9.53340.title: Implementation of Deep Learning Based on Islamic Educational Strategies in Student Character Development at MTs Daruur Rahmah Sukatani
doi:10.59188/eduvest.v6i9.53340.abstract: <jats:p>Character education is one of the primary objectives of Indonesia’s national education system and a fundamental goal of Islamic education. Along with the development of educational paradigms, the deep learning approach introduced by the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education emphasizes meaningful, reflective, and applicable learning experiences rather than mere knowledge acquisition. In Islamic schools, this approach needs to be integrated with Islamic educational strategies to strengthen students’ character development. This study aimed to analyze the implementation of deep learning based on Islamic educational strategies in developing students’ character at MTs Daruur Rahmah Sukatani. A qualitative case study approach was employed. Data were collected through observations, in-depth interviews, and document analysis, and were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. The findings showed that deep learning was implemented by integrating the principles of mindful, meaningful, and joyful learning with Islamic educational strategies, including role modeling, habituation, advice, reflection, and the cultivation of a religious school culture. These strategies contributed to strengthening students’ religious character, discipline, responsibility, honesty, social awareness, and independence. The main challenges identified were teachers’ limited understanding of the deep learning concept and insufficient parental involvement in character education. This study contributes to the development of an integrated model combining deep learning and Islamic educational strategies for character education in Islamic junior secondary schools.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fnins.2026.1939985.title: Enhancing structural to functional brain network prediction using topological graph learning
doi:10.3389/fnins.2026.1939985.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Understanding the relationship between structural and functional brain connectivity remains a fundamental challenge in network neuroscience. While structural connectivity constrains neural interactions, functional connectivity emerges from complex, nonlinear dynamics that are not fully explained by anatomical wiring alone. Existing graph-based and deep learning approaches often focus on pairwise relationships, thereby overlooking higher-order topological organization in brain networks.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We propose TopoGCN, a topology-informed graph convolutional network that integrates topological data analysis (TDA) into structure—function prediction. Persistent homology is used to extract multiscale topological features from structural connectomes, which are incorporated as node-level inputs. Additionally, a topology-aware loss function is incorporated to enforce preservation of higher-order structures in predicted functional networks. The model is evaluated on Human Connectome Project data (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                      = 998) using both edge-wise metrics and topological measures, including motif distributions, Betti curves, and Wasserstein distances between persistence diagrams.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>TopoGCN achieves competitive accuracy in reconstructing functional connectivity while significantly improving the preservation of higher-order network organization. Compared to state-of-the-art models, it yields lower KL divergence for node strength and motif distributions, and smaller Wasserstein distances between persistence diagrams, indicating better recovery of multiscale topological structures. Furthermore, hypothesis tests on Betti curves show no significant differences between observed and predicted networks, demonstrating strong agreement in both connected-component and cycle-based topology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our findings show that incorporating persistent-homology information into graph learning improves the modeling of structure-function relationships in the human brain. By preserving multiscale topological features beyond pairwise connections, TopoGCN provides an improved framework for topology-aware connectome prediction and offers new opportunities for studying brain organization and individual variability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.64828/conf-155-2026-1.title: DEVELOPING REFLECTIVE COMPETENCE OF ECONOMICS STUDENTS IN AI-MEDIATED ENGLISH FOR SPECIFIC PURPOSES LEARNING
doi:10.64828/conf-155-2026-1.abstract: <jats:p>The article examines the development of reflective competence among economics students in professionally oriented English language learning supported by generative artificial intelligence technologies. It is argued that the pedagogical value of artificial intelligence lies not only in its capacity to generate language materials, provide feedback, and support individualised learning, but also in its potential to facilitate students’ critical engagement with AI-generated content. The reflective sequence analyse – compare – verify – justify – reflect is proposed for use in professionally oriented English for Specific Purposes (ESP) tasks. The potential of this sequence to foster critical evaluation, self-regulation, professional judgement, and the responsible use of artificial intelligence by future economics professionals is highlighted.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/s44163-026-02213-z.title: Optimized hybrid BEiT and EfficientNetB0 deep learning model with whale and particle swarm algorithms for colorectal cancer histopathological image classification
doi:10.1007/s44163-026-02213-z.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>One of the deadly cancers, known as colorectal cancer, affects millions of people globally and therefore the need for an effective way of diagnosing it at early stages. While histopathology is the current method of diagnosis of colorectal cancer, it is time-consuming and subject to human interpretation whose results will vary according to the individual carrying out the diagnosis. Although deep learning has been successful in automating the process, traditional CNNs cannot extract global context information, and Vision Transformers must be optimized in order to obtain consistent results. To overcome such limitations, this study will develop a deep learning hybrid model using the strengths of both the Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Image Transformers and EfficientNetB0 in classifying colorectal cancer. This process will be optimized by Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). For this reason, the experiment will use 5000 hematoxylin and eosin-stained images of eight different types of tissues to train the models. From the results obtained, the optimized hybrid model performed better compared to the baseline hybrid model with 96.00% and 96.27% accuracy for WOA and PSO, respectively, against 92.13% for the baseline hybrid model. Among the two optimization methods, PSO outperformed WOA. In this connection, the integration of the Transformer model’s feature learning, convolution feature extraction, and bio-inspired algorithms proves to be a successful approach for automated diagnosis of colorectal cancer. The methodology can be helpful in aiding the pathologists with uniform diagnosis and decision-making process.</jats:p>

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Online learning has become an integral part of medical education, and understanding the factors associated with medical students’ knowledge sharing is important for designing effective learning environments.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examined the associations among web-based learning environment, media literacy, flow, and knowledge sharing, and tested whether media literacy and flow moderate the association between web-based learning environment and knowledge sharing.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from July to September 2021 in China. Of 1,200 undergraduate medical students invited, 987 valid responses were retained (response rate 82.25%; 70.7% women). Hierarchical linear regression with mean-centered variables was used to examine factors associated with knowledge sharing and to test the moderating effects of flow and media literacy.</jats:p>

                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = 0.732,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.001; Δ
                      <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1951569.title: Curriculum satisfaction and pre-service teachers’ social–emotional competencies: the serial mediation role of artificial intelligence anxiety and learning engagement
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1951569.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    This study examined the serial mediation role of artificial intelligence anxiety and learning engagement in the relationship between pre-service teachers’ curriculum satisfaction and social–emotional competencies. This study included 550 pre-service teachers from a public university in Türkiye. This correlational study used the IBM SPSS PROCESS macro (Model 6-Two-Mediator Serial Mediation Analysis/Model). In this study, the scales of student satisfaction, artificial intelligence anxiety, student engagement, and social–emotional expertise were used as data collection tools. To provide a coherent and integrated understanding of the structural relationships, this study was grounded in the input-process-output framework. In this model, curriculum satisfaction was regarded as an input. Artificial intelligence anxiety and learning engagement were regarded as processes. Social–emotional competencies were regarded as an output within the framework. As a result, curriculum satisfaction was negatively associated with artificial intelligence anxiety. Artificial intelligence anxiety was negatively associated with learning engagement. Learning engagement was positively associated with social–emotional competencies. Curriculum satisfaction was also positively associated with social–emotional competencies. When the model included artificial intelligence anxiety and learning engagement simultaneously, the relationship between curriculum satisfaction and social–emotional competencies was reduced but remained statistically significant. In line with these results, artificial intelligence anxiety and learning engagement played a partial serial mediation role in the relationship between curriculum satisfaction and social–emotional competencies (β = 0.051, SE = 0.010, 95% CI = [0.028, 0.074],
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     &lt; 0.01). The findings may help clarify the importance of curriculum satisfaction, artificial intelligence anxiety, learning engagement, and social–emotional competencies together when designing teacher training curriculum.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10371340/v1.title: Machine Learning Model for Predicting Operative Duration in Transsphenoidal Neuroendoscopic Pituitary Adenomectomy
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10371340/v1.abstract: Aim To develop and validate a machine learning model predicting surgical duration for transsphenoidal endoscopic pituitary tumor resection, and assess its utility for nursing management. Background Accurate surgical duration prediction is vital for nursing resource allocation and OR scheduling, yet traditional methods often lack precision, leading to workflow inefficiencies and increased nursing burden. Methods Retrospective data from 100 patients (2016–2025) yielded 22 preoperative variables. Artificial neural network (ANN) and random forest models were developed and evaluated using R², MAE, RMSE, and clinical accuracy (± 30/±45 min). Results The ANN model outperformed random forest, achieving a test set MAE of 0.636 hours (~ 38 min). Clinically, 63.3% of predictions were within ± 30 min, and 76.7% within ± 45 min. Key predictors included tumor recurrence, distance from the third ventricle floor, and the cinch sign. Conclusion ANN enables accurate surgical duration prediction, providing objective evidence to optimize nursing schedules, reduce uncertainty, and alleviate perioperative nursing burden.

doi:10.1088/2632-2153/aea3a0.title: Gradient-based versus gradient-free optimization in hybrid quantum machine learning: a systematic benchmark
doi:10.1088/2632-2153/aea3a0.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Hybrid quantum machine learning (QML) relies on quantum variational circuits (QVCs) trained together with classical components. While gradient-based training is standard, it is costly on near-term hardware and vulnerable to barren plateaus, motivating gradient-free alternatives. However, there is limited systematic evidence comparing gradient-free methods to strong gradient baselines under matched quantum-evaluation budgets. A benchmark of 15 gradient-based, gradient-free, and hybrid optimizers is conducted on four binary classification datasets and two three-qubit QVC architectures using a unified experimental protocol under a fixed per-step quantum-evaluation budget. Across tasks,
                    <jats:sc>Adam</jats:sc>
                    is the strongest gradient-based method. Among the purely gradient-free schemes, Asexual Reproduction Optimization is the strongest optimizer; tournament-selection and elite-pool genetic algorithms (GA-Tourn, GA-Elite) also frequently match the best gradient-based configurations. Among the hybrid schemes, Gradient Lexicase Selection with
                    <jats:sc>Adam</jats:sc>
                    (GLS-
                    <jats:sc>Adam</jats:sc>
                    ) performs comparably. In contrast, the two gradient-free methods big bang–big crunch and a cross-entropy method variant often fail to improve beyond chance. Additional sensitivity analyses show that circuit depth can change the preferred optimizer, whereas finite-shot sampling budget and post-training backend-specific noise do not materially change the main conclusions. Overall, gradient-based methods remain robust defaults for hybrid QML, while a small subset of gradient-free and hybrid approaches provides viable alternatives under realistic quantum-evaluation constraints.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10647910/v1.title: A novel EMG artifact removal algorithm based on complete local convolutional sparse dictionary learning in ECG signals
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10647910/v1.abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals are essential for health monitoring and disease detection. They are often contaminated by electromyogram (EMG) artifacts, which distort the signal and complicate clinical interpretation. Unlike periodic ECG signals, EMG artifacts are random yet overlap with ECG signals in the frequency domain. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel algorithm based on Complete Local Convolutional Sparse Dictionary Learning (CLCSDL). This algorithm utilizes the transient and periodic features of ECG signals to construct a convolutional dictionary with local short supports. Then, it employs a Local Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (LocOMP) algorithm to obtain the convolutional sparse representation (SR) of ECG features. Finally, it utilizes the Local Dictionary Update (LocDU) technique to learn the convolutional dictionary, thereby achieving self-learning of periodic transient features (dictionary atoms). This novel dictionary learning algorithm utilizes the local short support characteristics of transient QRS complexes in both the SR and dictionary update (DU) stages. Computation and updates are performed only in local regions near non-sparse locations. Compared to traditional convolutional dictionary learning techniques, this method does not require truncating the input data, thus avoiding the generation of spurious QRS complexes. The dictionary learning is performed entirely within the local support intervals of the ECG. Therefore, it has the advantages of high computational speed and low memory consumption, making it ideal for processing long-term, large-scale clinical data.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10647910/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.15788/1790098860.title: FROM SCOTTISH SNOW PATCHES TO GLOBAL SNOW COVER: A DEEP LEARNING APPROACH TO SNOW COVER FRACTION RETRIEVAL
doi:10.15788/1790098860.abstract: Optical snow mapping products are often developed and validated on regions with deep, clean, continuous snowpacks under clear skies.Maritime mountain ranges with marginal snowpacks suffer from particularly harsh conditions for optical snow observations: fragmented cover, spectrally degraded snow, and near-permanent heavy cloud influence.In the case of cloud, quality is usually assured with a conservative cloud mask, but this discards useful observations.We quantify the cost of that trade-off and offer an alternative.Using 25 cm aerial surveys of the Scottish Highlands, we built an open snow cover fraction (SCF) reference dataset for Sentinel-2 comprising 2455 labelled 1 km chips from 37 scenes, deliberately retaining imagery through cloud gaps and heavy atmospheric interference rather than masking it away.On this dataset we trained SPUN, a U-Net with a ResNet50 encoder and a regression head that predicts continuous SCF per 10 m pixel.Evaluated on a spatially independent test set at the 20 m operational grid, SPUN and the operational Let-It-Snow (LIS) product are separated modestly under clear-sky conditions (snow-only MAE 19.10 % versus 23.26 %; F1 0.606 versus 0.493).Under all-sky conditions the gap becomes distinct: SPUN improves slightly (MAE 18.81 %, F1 0.747), while LIS recall falls to 0.013 and it recovers 1.6 % of the reference snow-covered area.Aggregated to the 1 km chip scale, SPUN tracks snow-covered area with R 2 = 0.934 against -0.238 for LIS.SPUN is trained only on late-season Scottish snow patches but, nonetheless, transferred to an independent 40-scene global dataset, reaching a macro-averaged F1 of 0.931 and a snow-only F1 of 0.892.We present this as a proof-of-concept rather than a finished operational tool, and argue that the limiting factor in optical snow retrieval is training data rather than model architecture.
