doi:10.4038/cjs.v55i4.8929.title: A fisher kernel vector learning framework with Bahdanau-Adapted rectified deep neural networks for predicting student academic performance
doi:10.4038/cjs.v55i4.8929.abstract: <jats:p>Educational Data Mining (EDM) utilizes data mining, machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) techniques to extract valuable insights from educational environments. Although predicting student performance is crucial for enhancing academic achievements, existing prediction models often suffer from class imbalance issues and fail to select optimal features, leading to high computational complexity and reduced accuracy. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel framework termed Fisher Kernel Vector Machine Learning and Bahdanau Attention Rectified Deep Learning (FKVML-BARDL). The proposed model operates in two primary phases: (1) preprocessing using a Fisher Kernel Globality–Locality Vector Machine Learning model to balance classes while preserving local and global feature properties via Kirchhoff matrices, and (2) classification using Rectified Deep Neural Networks combined with a Bahdanau Attention Adaptable function to select relevant features. The performance of the FKVML-BARDL model was evaluated using a comprehensive student academic performance dataset. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing baseline models across all evaluation metrics, achieving a 17% improvement in precision and recall, an 11% increase in accuracy, and a 31% reduction in computational time.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fphys.2026.1920214.title: Deployability of machine-learning prediction models in elite and high-level team sports: a task-specific systematic review
doi:10.3389/fphys.2026.1920214.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Machine-learning models are increasingly used for match forecasting and athlete monitoring in elite and high-level team sports, but high reported performance does not necessarily indicate readiness for real-world use. This systematic review evaluated whether models were developed and tested under conditions compatible with their intended decision time. Eight databases were searched, with searches completed by 12 July 2026. Eighty reports representing 77 studies contributed 87 analysis units: 55 Core, 23 post-event or high-leakage Comparators, and nine Boundary units. All 87 units were assessed for deployable prediction validity (DPV) across six domains, and 78 Core or Comparator units were also assessed with PROBAST. Amongst Core units, 26/55 (47.3%) were rated at least Moderate, including five Moderate-to-strong and 21 Moderate units. Pre-adjudication agreement for the overall DPV classification was 85/87 (97.7%; κ = 0.968; linearly weighted κ = 0.978), whilst domain-level exact agreement ranged from 75/87 to 87/87. In
                    <jats:italic>post hoc</jats:italic>
                    sensitivity analyses, 19/55 Core units met the primary DPV threshold and had Sufficient validation; 14/55 met the primary threshold and had at least partial evidence of predictive reliability or probability-quality; and 9/55 met the primary threshold and both additional conditions. PROBAST risk of bias was High for 56/78 units, Unclear for 21/78, and Low for one. The main limitations were evaluation designs that did not adequately reflect intended future use and limited assessment of predictive reliability. Overall, the evidence supports selective methodological readiness rather than general deployability, with different requirements for pre-game, in-game, and athlete-monitoring applications.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.18458/kb.2026.3.91.title: A mese mint az élményalapú szóelsajátítás eszköze
doi:10.18458/kb.2026.3.91.abstract: <jats:p>The present study examines how word learning embedded in stories can be related to experiential learning, with particular attention to tales. Drawing on research findings in narrative processing and word learning, it suggests that stories may provide an imaginatively constructed context that differs from direct sensory experience and is shaped in part by the learner’s prior experiences. The paper then reviews factors that may influence story-embedded word learning, including characteristics of the tale, repetition, language abilities, and information from different modalities that may support the development of word meaning. The study argues that, under certain learning conditions, stories can serve as tools for experiential word learning.</jats:p>

doi:10.64358/9dnym189.title: <b>PRIVATE SCHOOL TEACHERS’ RETENTION RATE: A BASIS FOR DEVELOPING A PROFESSIONAL LEARNING COMMUNITY PLAN</b>
doi:10.64358/9dnym189.abstract: <jats:p>This study analyzed the retention level of teacher stayers among selected private schools in Santiago City, Philippines in order to determine its implications to existing educational policies. A quantitative descriptive design was employed by collecting data from 31 teacher stayers through a structured questionnaire that includes PERMA Profiler and Teacher Retention Survey. Results revealed that teacher stayers are generally in a “normal functioning” level of well-being (M=3.88). This indicates that they are adequately functioning but not flourishing. Relationship domain (4.13) ranked highest among PERMA domains while Engagement (M=3.59) was ranked the lowest. Negative Emotions (M=3.01) were rated at a sub-optimal level because of the presence of anxiety. The study shows interpersonal support as the strongest non-financial factor for teacher retention. However, gaps in engagement, achievement, and emotional well-being need to be addressed. Also, key areas in non-financial factors remain limited in terms of encouragement to pursue graduate studies, confidence to communicate to administrators, work-life balance practices, and stress management programs. Teacher stayers receive constructive feedback (M=3.29) and support from the school community (M=3.10) but need immediate recognition and enough opportunities to showcase best practices.</jats:p>

doi:10.24114/tj.v15i3.74927.title: The Impact of Using AI Technology to Support Learning For Students
doi:10.24114/tj.v15i3.74927.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education has reshaped learning processes by influencing how students acquire knowledge, engage with materials, and develop academic skills. This article examines studies published between 2022 and 2026 to explore the impact of AI technologies on student learning outcomes. The findings indicate that AI tools, including intelligent tutoring systems, automated writing assistants, and adaptive learning platforms, significantly improve academic performance, motivation, engagement, and language proficiency. In addition, AI supports personalized, interactive, and independent learning while also reducing teachers’ administrative workload through automation. However, the literature also identifies key challenges, such as over-reliance on AI, ethical concerns related to academic integrity and data privacy, and unequal access to digital resources. Guided by Constructivist Learning Theory, Personalized Learning Theory, and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), this article emphasizes that AI effectiveness depends on pedagogical strategies, learner readiness, and institutional support. Overall, it provides insights for optimizing AI integration in education.</jats:p>

doi:10.65224/jopate.v2i3.300.title: AI Use and Learning Outcomes Among Undergraduate Students: The Mediating Role of Learning Motivation, Locus of Control, and Learning Preferences
doi:10.65224/jopate.v2i3.300.abstract:
<jats:p>Background. The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has created new opportunities for personalized learning, although its contribution to student achievement remains theoretically and empirically contested.
Purpose. This study examined the direct and indirect effects of AI use on conceptual understanding and problem-solving ability through learning motivation, locus of control, and learning preferences.
Method. A quantitative explanatory design was employed with 88 pre-service teachers enrolled in an Instructional Media course at a teacher education institution in Central Java, Indonesia. Data were collected using validated questionnaires and cognitive assessments. Preliminary analyses were conducted using SPSS, while the measurement and structural models were evaluated through PLS-SEM with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples.
Novelty. This study simultaneously tested three psychological and learning-related mediators within a single structural model, thereby extending previous research that primarily examined the direct relationship between AI use and academic performance.
Results. AI use significantly predicted learning motivation and locus of control but did not significantly influence learning preferences. Learning motivation significantly predicted learning outcomes and mediated the relationship between AI use and learning outcomes. In contrast, locus of control and learning preferences showed no significant mediating effects. The direct effect of AI use on learning outcomes was also nonsignificant.
Conclusion. AI contributes to student learning primarily by strengthening learning motivation rather than through direct technological exposure. Effective AI integration should therefore emphasize reflective, autonomous, and cognitively engaging learning activities.</jats:p>

doi:10.69974/glsuj.2026.06.01.02.title: Over-Reliance on Generative AI and Its Impact on Critical Thinking and Learning Outcomes among Management Students: Evidence from Jodhpur
doi:10.69974/glsuj.2026.06.01.02.abstract:
<jats:p>The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT, Bard,  and Copilot has fundamentally transformed learning practices in higher education. These tools enable students to generate text, solve problems, summarise complex material, and complete academic tasks with unprecedented speed and convenience. While generative AI offers significant benefits in terms of efficiency, accessibility, and personalised learning support, growing concerns have emerged regarding students’ over-reliance on AI and its potential impact on higher-order cognitive skills. In particular, educators and researchers have raised alarms about whether habitual dependence on AI may weaken students’ capacity for independent thinking, analytical reasoning,  and deep learning. 
In this scenario, the current research investigates how generative AI use depends on critical thinking ability and its subsequent effect on learning outcomes among management students in the  Jodhpur region of India. Following the cross-sectional design, a quantitative web survey was conducted among 390 management students in various courses such as BBA, MBA, PGDM, and  Executive MBA. Two hypotheses were tested using simple linear regression analysis. The findings indicate that AI reliance has a strong, statistically significant negative impact on learners’ critical thinking skills (β = –0.869, p < .001), with an adjusted R2 of 74.2%. Additionally, there is a strong and statistically significant positive impact of critical thinking on learning performance (β  = 0.729, p < 0.001, 55.1% of the variance). 
Collectively, the results show a direct causal link between reliance on generative AI and reduced critical thinking, which, in turn, reduces learning. The paper empirically contributes to the emergent literature on AI in education and provides a timely warning about the importance of an academically informed, ethical, and balanced deployment of generative AI within management education that prioritises cognitive development over technological efficiency.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1891713.title: Artificial intelligence adoption and organizational efficiency: the mediating role of organizational learning capability and moderating role of digital literacy
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1891713.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Strategic and organizational solutions are becoming essential due to the global demand for digital transformation, sustained operational efficiency, and the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. This study examines the influence of artificial intelligence adoption on organizational efficiency, with digital literacy as a boundary condition and organizational learning capability serving as a mediator.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study utilized a quantitative cross-sectional survey-based design. A multistage sampling technique was used to collect data from employees working in the Ghanaian banking sector. Data collected from 388 employees from the banks were utilized in an empirical study employing structural equation modeling. Both direct and indirect relationships were assessed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings revealed that the level of artificial intelligence adoption has a significant and positive influence on both organizational efficiency and organizational learning capability. The results further showed that organizational learning capability has a significant and positive influence on organizational efficiency and partially mediates the relationship between artificial intelligence adoption and organizational efficiency. Additionally, the results revealed that digital literacy moderates the relationships between artificial intelligence adoption and organizational efficiency, as well as the relationships between organizational learning capability and organizational efficiency.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study introduces a novel theoretical framework that connects the hitherto overlooked linkages between artificial intelligence adoption, organizational learning capability, digital literacy, and organizational efficiency within the banking sector of an emerging economy. By integrating these constructs into a unified model, the study clarifies the mechanisms and boundary conditions through which AI adoption translates into organizational efficiency, thereby extending the Resource-Based View in an emerging-market context.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.63954/wajss.v5i3.506.title: The Geography of Becoming: Thirdspace, Family Systems, and Transformative Learning in Tara Westover's Educated
doi:10.63954/wajss.v5i3.506.abstract: <jats:p>This study offers a close reading of Tara Westover's memoir Educated (2018) through an interdisciplinary framework that joins Edward Soja's spatial theory of Thirdspace with family systems theory, transformative learning theory, and contemporary trauma and posttraumatic growth scholarship. Rather than treating the protagonist's upbringing as a case study in any particular belief system, the paper approaches her isolated rural childhood, her labor in a family scrapyard, and her eventual departure for formal schooling as a problem of space, family structure, and psychological development. Drawing on Soja's distinction between Firstspace, Secondspace, and Thirdspace, the study traces how Buck's Peak is produced, conceived, and ultimately reimagined as the narrator moves from an undifferentiated family unit toward what Murray Bowen calls differentiation of self. Jack Mezirow's transformative learning theory illuminates how formal education functions less as the acquisition of facts than as a disorienting dilemma that restructures the narrator's frame of reference, while Judith Herman's stages of trauma recovery, Rachel Pain's concept of geotrauma, and Richard Tedeschi and Lawrence Calhoun's model of posttraumatic growth account for the psychological costs and gains of that transformation. The paper argues that Educated dramatizes a sustained act of self-authorship in which space, family, and learning are inseparably entangled, and proposes this combined framework as a model for reading contemporary memoir that foregrounds psychological and spatial explanation over biographical description.</jats:p>

doi:10.54963/dtra.v5i3.3081.title: Evaluating Deep Learning Architectures for Effective Detection of Manipulated Media across Multiple Datasets
doi:10.54963/dtra.v5i3.3081.abstract: <jats:p>The advancement of artificial intelligence has enabled the creation of highly realistic synthetic media raising serious concerns about misinformation, identity manipulation, and digital security. As these technologies continue to evolve and become more accessible the potential misuse of manipulated media increases significantly making it easier to spread deceptive content across digital platforms. This growing threat highlights the urgent need for reliable and efficient deepfake detection techniques capable of identifying manipulated content and limiting its potential societal and technological impact. Deep Learning (DL) has emerged as a promising solution for automatically identifying manipulated multimedia content. In this study, we harnessed Transfer Learning (TL) techniques to fine-tune and evaluate the performance of seven different DL models including EfficientNetB5, XceptionNet, EfficientNet3D, Vision Transformer (ViT), CrossViT, ViViT, and CoAtNet. These models were trained and evaluated on three widely used deepfake detection datasets: FaceForensics++, the DeepFake Detection Challenge (DFDC), and CelebDF. Our experimental results demonstrate that hybrid approaches combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Vision Transformer-based architectures outperform individual models in detecting manipulated media. Furthermore, the findings indicate that models trained on the FaceForensics++ and DFDC datasets exhibit stronger generalization capabilities when applied to previously unseen deepfake samples.</jats:p>

doi:10.15631/ubmrj.v15i1.263.title: Self-Efficacy and Language Learning Strategies in Relation to English Language Proficiency of Senior High School Students, University of Bohol
authors: Karen G. Estareja Karen G. Estareja
doi:10.15631/ubmrj.v15i1.263.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates the interplay between academic self-efficacy, language learning strategies, and English proficiency among senior high school students in the Philippines, framed by the findings of the 2022 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA). Despite various educational reforms, Filipino students continue to perform below global averages in key academic areas, underlining persistent educational challenges. The research focuses on the University of Bohol's senior high school students, examining how their self-efficacy and language learning strategies correlate with their English language skills. The study employs a descriptive quantitative-correlational design, utilizing both self-made and modified questionnaires to assess these attributes among 252 participants. Results suggest a significant relationship between students' confidence in their academic abilities and their English proficiency, which is vital for their future academic and professional endeavors. The findings are expected to inform targeted educational interventions aimed at enhancing language skills and overall student outcomes in a global educational context.</jats:p>

doi:10.5302/j.icros.2026.26.0158.title: Development of an Educational Platform for Reinforcement Learning Control of a Rotary Inverted Pendulum Based on LW-RCP
doi:10.5302/j.icros.2026.26.0158.abstract: This study proposes a compact rotary inverted pendulum experimental platform designed for implementing reinforcement learning (RL) based controllers on physical systems. While RL demonstrates superior performance in simulated environments, applying it to real-world systems often leads to performance degradation and instability due to the sim-to-real gap and physical actuator constraints. In particular, when a stepper motor is employed as the actuator, its drive characteristics need to be considered when applying control commands generated by the learned policy to the physical system. This study treats the stepper motor as a high-pole-count synchronous motor and implements a closed-loop drive system using a field-oriented control (FOC)-based current control structure. Furthermore, a real-time control platform is established by integrating a lightweight rapid control prototyping(LW- RCP) environment with the rotary inverted pendulum system, enabling RL policies trained in simulations to be deployed directly onto the hardware. The proposed platform is designed with a desktop-sized, low-cost architecture to enhance accessibility in educational settings. The feasibility of applying RL-based controllers to actual systems is experimentally validated. Consequently, this research bridges the gap between theory and practice, providing an effective integrated environment for experiment-oriented control education and RL research.

doi:10.31185/wjcms.542.title: <b>Optimized Deep Learning for Feature Extraction and Detection of Oral Cancer from Histopathological Images</b>
doi:10.31185/wjcms.542.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to develop an efficient, powerful deep learning model that accurately classifies oral cancer from high-resolution histopathology images, especially in cases with high intra-class variability and extreme class imbalance. We propose a novel Ensemble Deep Learning framework combined with two streams: CNN1(EfficientNet-B5), CNN2 (DenseNet-201), and a new Hybrid -Spatial-Channel Attention module to extract and fuse the cytological and structural features. We addressed class imbalance using a cost-sensitive learning approach and data augmentation techniques. The Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) was used for optimizing hyperparameters. The model is based on late-fusion of CNN1 (fine-grained features) and CNN2 (architectural features). The procedure that was followed was to utilize seven classes of 12425 high-resolution images from (ORCHID and UFES-NDB) and diagnose the seven specific histopathological classes into three primary diagnostic groups: normal, pre-cancer, and cancer. The dataset was divided into Training (80%), Validation (10%), and Testing (10%) to prevent data leakage. It is found that the overall accuracy of the proposed architecture is very robust at 90.35% on the test set. Using five-fold cross-validation. The model achieved the highest Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), particularly in highly imbalanced classes. The proposed method can effectively improve the representation of features and the precision of classification for complex medical image analysis by achieving high metrics in Accuracy, Precision, Recall, Specificity, and F1-Score, which will be a powerful computational tool for automated histopathology analysis. Optimized ensemble learning enhances the detection and classification of Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma (OSCC) and precancerous lesions by merging fine-grained features and architectural features. Future models should be validated in independent patient populations on external datasets to make it ready for full clinical use and investigated regarding the incorporation of multimodal patient information.</jats:p>

doi:10.46810/tdfd.1927529.title: SE-ResNet18: Attention-Enhanced Deep Learning for Multi-Class Classification of Tuberculosis and Pneumonia from Chest X-ray Images
doi:10.46810/tdfd.1927529.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Tuberculosis and pneumonia are major causes of respiratory mortality worldwide, requiring accurate and timely diagnosis. This study proposes SE-ResNet18, an attention-enhanced deep learning model for multi-class classification of chest X-ray images into Normal, Pneumonia, Tuberculosis, and Unknown categories. The model integrates Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) blocks into the ResNet18 architecture to improve channel-wise feature representation. A dataset of 15,316 chest radiographs was used, split into training (13,028), validation (761), and testing (1,527) sets. Transfer learning was applied using ImageNet-pretrained weights, followed by fine-tuning for 10 epochs with the Adam optimizer (learning rate: 1×10⁻⁵). To enhance generalization, limited data augmentation (horizontal flipping and ±5° rotation) was applied only to the training set. Dropout (p = 0.4) was used in the classification head to reduce overfitting. The proposed model achieved 98.03% accuracy and a macro F1-score of 0.97 on the test set, indicating balanced performance across classes. Class-wise results were: Unknown (1.00 precision, recall, F1-score), Tuberculosis (0.95 precision, 0.99 recall, 0.97 F1-score), Pneumonia (0.98 precision, 0.96 recall, 0.97 F1-score), and Normal (0.96 precision, 0.95 recall, 0.95 F1-score). No misclassification occurred between Pneumonia and Tuberculosis. Confidence analysis showed well-calibrated predictions, with higher confidence for correct predictions (0.947) than errors (0.823), enabling identification of uncertain cases for expert review.</jats:p>

doi:10.1142/s0218001426500497.title: Emotion Classification in Music: Leveraging Machine Learning for Music Therapy and Emotional Response Analysis
doi:10.1142/s0218001426500497.abstract: <jats:p>Emotion classification in music is a central problem in affective computing with critical applications in music therapy, personalized media, and emotionally adaptive systems. This study proposes a novel multi-modal stacking ensemble framework for multi-label music emotion recognition using the Emotify dataset. The proposed architecture integrates acoustic features, listener metadata (age, gender, mood), and genre information to capture both perceptual and contextual determinants of emotional response. Six modeling phases were evaluated using Random Forest, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), XGBoost, and ensemble learning strategies. The final Stacking Ensemble, combining Random Forest, MLP, and XGBoost through a logistic regression meta-classifier, achieved a subset accuracy of 0.41, Hamming loss of 0.25, and macro-averaged F1 score of 0.67, outperforming all individual models as well as recent state-of-the-art approaches evaluated on the same Emotify dataset. Compared with existing CNN-LSTM and LLM-based methods, which report macro-F1 values below 0.51 or rely on shortsegment evaluation, the proposed framework delivers substantially higher performance on full-length music clips with strict multi-label evaluation. The results demonstrate that stacked ensemble learning combined with multi-modal feature fusion provides a robust and generalizable solution for modeling complex emotional landscapes in music, enabling accurate emotionaware music therapy systems, adaptive media platforms, and personalized music recommendation engines.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1957447.title: How AI sycophancy shapes learner autonomy in digitalized learning: the mediating roles of metacognitive laziness and AI dependence
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1957447.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tutors rarely disagree. Drawing on cognitive offloading theory, this study examines how perceived AI sycophancy (PAS) and perceived AI intellectual stimulation (PAIS) relate to learner autonomy through the serial mediators of metacognitive laziness (MCL) and AI dependence (AIDEP).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Responses from 542 university students using generative AI for coursework were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), necessary condition analysis (NCA), and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Perceived sycophancy was associated with greater MCL (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                      = 0.38), whereas intellectual stimulation was associated with lower levels of MCL (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                      = −0.29); laziness predicted AIDEP (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                      = 0.45), and dependence predicted lower autonomy (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                      = −0.30). Both serial paths were significant and opposite in sign, explaining 46% of autonomy variance. NCA identified intellectual stimulation as the tightest necessary condition, and fsQCA showed that no high-autonomy configuration tolerated sycophancy
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Because data are cross-sectional and self-reported, findings indicate associations rather than causation. Perceived interaction style, not usage intensity, correlated most with autonomous learning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1895612.title: Integrated machine learning and multi-dataset analysis identify SDS as a diagnostic and immune-related hub gene in hepatoblastoma
doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1895612.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Current clinical diagnostic models lack sufficient sensitivity and specificity for Hepatoblastoma (HB) individualized prediction. This study aimed to identify robust hub genes for HB diagnosis and molecular subtyping by integrating multiple transcriptomic datasets and machine learning algorithms.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Four merged GEO hepatoblastoma datasets (GSE131329, GSE132037, GSE104766, GSE133039) were analyzed by differential expression and WGCNA to identify HB-related genes. Further use three algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, Random Forest) to identify central genes. In addition, consensus clustering was used for molecular typing, and four deconvolution algorithms (TIMER, MCPcounter, xCell, quanTIseq) were used to characterize the tumor microenvironment. The biological function of SDS in hepatoblastoma was elucidated through
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      experiments (CCK-8 detection, colony formation assay, Transwell assay), as well as
                      <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic>
                      using a xenograft mouse model.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A total of 268 differentially expressed genes (77 up, 191 down) were identified. WGCNA revealed the blue module as most correlated with HB (correlation coefficient 0.66). Three machine learning algorithms jointly selected four hub genes (CLEC1B, ITGA6, SDS, TTC36). Consensus clustering based on these four genes stratified HB into two subtypes (Clust1, Clust2). Clust1 exhibited enhanced immune infiltration and activation of complement, IFN-α, and IL6-JAK-STAT3 pathways. Low SDS expression associated with cell cycle pathways, whereas high SDS expression associated with immune-related pathways. Functionally, SDS overexpression significantly suppressed HB cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and colony formation, while promoting apoptosis
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      , and markedly reduced tumor growth
                      <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic>
                      .
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Integrated machine learning identified CLEC1B, ITGA6, SDS, and TTC36 as robust diagnostic genes for hepatoblastoma. SDS, in particular, exerts a tumor-suppressive role and is closely linked to the immune microenvironment, making it a promising diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target in HB.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.26389/ajsrp.g040126.title: فاعلية استراتيجية التدرج المرحلي في تحسين نواتج التعلم والجاهزية الأكاديمية لدى طلبة التعليم ما بعد الأساسي بولاية بوشر بمحافظة مسقط - سلطنة عمان
doi:10.26389/ajsrp.g040126.abstract: <jats:p>هدفت الدراسة إلى الكشف عن فاعلية استراتيجية التدرج المرحلي في الصفين العاشر والحادي عشر وأثرها في تحسين نواتج التعلم والجاهزية الأكاديمية لدى طلبة الصف الثاني عشر بمدارس التعليم ما بعد الأساسي بولاية بوشر بمحافظة مسقط خلال الفترة من سبتمبر إلى ديسمبر 2025، انطلاقًا من ملاحظة وجود فجوات معرفية وتفاوت في جاهزية الطلبة نتيجة ضعف التدرج المنهجي في بناء المفاهيم والمهارات. واعتمدت الدراسة المنهج شبه التجريبي بتصميم القياس القبلي والبعدي لمجموعة واحدة، وشملت عينة طبقية عشوائية قوامها (360) طالبًا وطالبة من مدرستي الإمام المهنا بن سلطان ودوحة الأدب، إضافة إلى (15) معلمًا وإداريًا لدعم تفسير النتائج الكمية. وجُمعت البيانات باستخدام استبانة تضمنت خمسة محاور رئيسة ومقابلات شبه مقننة، مع التحقق من صدق الأدوات وثباتها باستخدام معامل ألفا كرونباخ. وأظهرت النتائج فروقًا دالة إحصائيًا لصالح القياس البعدي في جميع المحاور؛ إذ ارتفع متوسط الجاهزية الأكاديمية من (2.73) إلى (4.26)، ومتوسط الفهم والاستيعاب من (2.76) إلى (4.19)، وبلغت قيمة اختبار (T) للجاهزية الأكاديمية (14.02) عند مستوى دلالة p<0.001. كما أسهمت الاستراتيجية في تحسين نواتج التعلم، وتقليل الضغط المعرفي، وتعزيز ثقة الطلبة بأنفسهم، دون فروق دالة تعزى للجنس أو المدرسة، بما يؤكد استقرار أثرها في البيئات التعليمية المتقاربة. وأوصت الدراسة بدمج استراتيجية التدرج المرحلي في الممارسات التدريسية، وتدريب المعلمين على تطبيقها، وإعداد أدلة إجرائية وبرامج داعمة لتعزيز الجاهزية الأكاديمية.</jats:p>

doi:10.14391/ajhs.e3005.1.003.title: Strengthening Cross-Cultural Religious Literacy for Peace Education:
doi:10.14391/ajhs.e3005.1.003.abstract: Cross-cultural religious literacy (CCRL) is a practical peace-education competence in plural higher-education settings, yet evidence remains limited on whether a Design Alchemy layer adds value beyond ordinary project-based collaborative learning (PBCL).This quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test study compared PBCL + Design Alchemy (n = 46) with PBCL only (n = 45) in four intact first-semester Islamic Education classes at an Islamic university in Palu, Indonesia.CCRL was measured before and after one semester through total scores and four indicators, while social skill was examined as a moderator.Descriptive statistics, Welch tests, indicator-level analyses, and ANCOVA were used after assumption testing.The two groups began with equivalent CCRL baselines (55.57vs. 55.44,p = .941)and comparable social-skill levels (122.00 vs. 119.38,p = .619).By semester end, the PBCL + Alchemy group showed higher overall CCRL than the PBCL group (81.98 vs. 68.93,p < .001)and a larger gain score (26.41 vs. 13.49).The instructionalmodel × social-skill interaction remained significant after controlling for pre-test CCRL (F = 18.09, p < .001,partial η² = .174).The largest differences appeared in collaborative and integrative CCRL, and collaboration skill showed the strongest correlations with CCRL outcomes (r = .40-.44).Within the limits of an intact-class quasi-experimental design, the findings suggest that Design Alchemy may strengthen PBCL by structuring inclusive, contextual, and reflective collaboration rather than merely adding more project tasks.

doi:10.68337/cpsm.v1.i1.2026-004.title: Automated Tuberculosis Detection from Chest X-Ray Images Using CNN and Transformer-Based Deep Learning Models
doi:10.68337/cpsm.v1.i1.2026-004.abstract: <jats:p>Tuberculosis (TB) is a contagious infectious disease that mainly affects the lungs and is associated with persistent cough, chest pain, fever, night sweats, and weight loss. Late diagnosis and a shortage of qualified radiologists contribute greatly to the spread of the disease and to deaths from it, especially in low- and middle-income regions. Effective and accurate diagnosis of TB is therefore necessary to improve treatment outcomes and to reduce transmission in the community. Recent advances in deep learning have substantially improved diagnostic accuracy, particularly in clinical evaluation and noninvasive methods, by introducing new techniques for the early detection of TB. This study compares convolutional neural network (CNN) and transformer models for early TB diagnosis from chest X-ray (CXR) images in the TB Chest X-ray dataset, framed as a binary classification of TB-positive and normal cases. Seven architectures were trained with a hold-out 80:20 validation split: four CNNs (VGG16, ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B0, and MobileNet-V2) and three transformers fitted with an Adaptive Patch Reduction Block (PRB), namely the Vision Transformer (ViT-PRB), the Data-efficient image Transformer (DeiT-PRB), and the Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT-PRB). The results indicate that the transformer-based models performed better than the conventional CNNs, and PVT-PRB, which combines the PRB with global attention, achieved the highest classification accuracy of 96%.</jats:p>
doi:10.68337/cpsm.v1.i1.2026-004.venue: Conference Proceedings in Science and Management

doi:10.68337/cpsm.v1.i1.2026-009.title: Early Detection of Diabetes Using Machine Learning Algorithms and Performance Analysis
doi:10.68337/cpsm.v1.i1.2026-009.abstract: <jats:p>Diabetes is a widespread metabolic disease and a major public health problem that affects millions of people worldwide. Early screening and risk prediction allow timely intervention for high-risk groups and significantly reduce the risk of severe complications. In recent years, machine learning (ML) has shown clear value in the analysis of large-scale medical data. This study reviews and compares mainstream models for diabetes prediction and proposes a new prediction framework. On the Pima Indians Diabetes Dataset, the proposed hybrid model reached an accuracy of 0.92, a precision of 0.91, a recall of 0.90, and an F1 score of 0.91, higher than the decision tree, support vector machine, random forest, and logistic regression models tested. Such a system may help medical staff with screening and clinical decision-making.</jats:p>

doi:10.68337/cpsm.v1.i1.2026-008.title: MERGE-Med: Multi-Expert Retrieval-Grounded Engine for Medical Report Summarization Using Hierarchical RAG and Contrastive Learning
doi:10.68337/cpsm.v1.i1.2026-008.abstract: <jats:p>Electronic health records (EHRs) have created large volumes of clinical data that require automated and accurate summarization that patients can understand. Current large language models (LLMs) are prone to hallucination and show limited task specialization and inadequate clinical grounding. MERGE-Med is a hybrid multi-expert architecture that consists of (i) a mixture-of-experts (MoE) layer with three domain-specialized LLaMA-3 8B models for diagnostic reasoning, treatment protocol generation, and patient-friendly communication; (ii) a hierarchical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline that combines FAISS dense retrieval, BM25 sparse retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, and Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) knowledge-graph traversal over 35 million PubMed abstracts, 50,000 clinical guidelines, and 15,000 pharmaceutical records; and (iii) a contrastive fine-tuning framework validated by an ensembled DeBERTa-v3-large fact-checking layer that achieves more than 95% consistency. MERGE-Med achieved accuracies of 92.45%, 82.34%, and 98.76% on MedQA, MedMCQA, and Clinical Knowledge, respectively, improvements of 5.18, 6.44, and 1.78 percentage points (pp) over the baseline LLaMA-3 8B. The hallucination rate decreased by 67% (from 18.3% to 6.1%), ROUGE-L improved by 22.3%, and in an evaluation by board-certified physicians of 100 de-identified reports, 92% of summaries were judged appropriate for patients, with an inference latency of 2.3 s.</jats:p>

doi:10.33497/2026.latesummer.2.title: Learning to See with Night Vision
doi:10.33497/2026.latesummer.2.abstract: <jats:p>Alessandri’s  Night  Vision  argues  that  the  negative  moods  and  emotions,  including anger,  grief,  depression,  and  anxiety,  have  moral  and  epistemic  value  and  contribute  meaning  to  our  lives.  The  book  aims  to  destigmatize  and  change  our  social  responses to   the  negative  emotions,  both  interpersonally  and  intrapersonally.  I  raise three  sets   of  questions  for  this  project.  First,  I  point  to a complication  related   to  “uptake”  of  the  negative  moods  and emotions,   namely  the  basic  economic fact   that  emotional  work  is work,  which   can  be  exploited  and  unjustly  distributed,  especially  when disappeared.  Second,   I  argue  that a  clear-eyed   picture  of  our  darker  emotions  should also  factor   in  their  aptness or   inaptness.  New  scripts  around  the  dark  emotions  should  be  alive  to  the possibility  that  they   sometimes  stem  from  gross, even   dangerous,  moral  confusions.  Third,  I  point  to  further  questions  around the   medicalization  of  the  dark  moods,  including  the  background question of ableism.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1917777.title: Educommunication and artificial intelligence for learning, creating, and communicating: professional competency development in university prosumers
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1917777.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines the pedagogical integration of educommunication and artificial intelligence (AI) and its association with self-reported professional competencies among university prosumers-students who simultaneously consume, produce, and share academic content through digital platforms.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A non-experimental, cross-sectional quantitative design with descriptive-correlational and structural purposes was employed. Data were collected using a psychometrically validated 26-item Likert-scale questionnaire (plus six open-response items) administered to a convenience sample of 547 university students enrolled at Universidad Politécnica Salesiana, Ecuador. The instrument assessed five dimensions: (1) AI-mediated learning processes, (2) educommunication and expression, (3) knowledge prosumption, (4) perceived professional competencies, and (5) ethics and critical AI use. Psychometric validation confirmed excellent reliability (Cronbach's
                      <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                       = 0.91; McDonald's
                      <jats:italic>ω</jats:italic>
                       = 0.93). Exploratory factor analysis supported the five-factor structure (Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin [KMO] = 0.91; Bartlett's test
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.001; variance explained = 61.4%). Confirmatory factor analysis indicated a satisfactory model fit (comparative fit index [CFI] = 0.96; Tucker-Lewis index [TLI] = 0.95; root mean square error of approximation [RMSEA] = 0.052; standardized root mean square residual [SRMR] = 0.061). A single-factor test yielded a first unrotated factor accounting for 28.3% of the variance, below the 50% threshold, offering a preliminary indication against a single dominant method factor, although this test alone does not rule out common method bias (see Section 3.3).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Structural equation modeling revealed significant direct paths from AI-mediated learning to perceived professional competencies (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = 0.58,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.001) and from educommunication to knowledge prosumption (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = 0.51,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.001), with knowledge prosumption partially mediating the educommunication-competency association (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                      _indirect = 0.21; R² = 0.74 for D3; R² = 0.78 for D4), and ethics and critical AI use functioning as a significant moderator of the AI learning-competency path (interaction
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = 0.34,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.001). Given the cross-sectional, self-report design, these results are interpreted as structural associations rather than causal effects.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Findings indicate that AI integration within educommunicative frameworks is positively associated with autonomous learning, creativity, and digital communication skills. However, risks associated with technological over-reliance and epistemic dependency were also identified in the qualitative data. These findings constitute structurally validated evidence that pedagogical AI integration, framed within educommunicative approaches, is associated with the perceived development of critical, collaborative, and innovative professional competencies in higher education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.21832/9781800413917-006.title: Orienting: Learning and Teaching IS
doi:10.21832/9781800413917-006.abstract: <jats:p>Rather than approaching IS learning as similar to ‘L2 sign language learning’, I focus on what is specific to IS learning. Here I introduce the concept of orienting as central to this chapter. Orienting means tuning in to the practice of signing with deaf people from different countries. Each international encounter becomes a moment of re-orientation, and over time these moments accumulate. Orienting runs through the entire chapter: it underpins my analysis of learning IS through mingling, but also how I interpret what happens in classrooms and in online spaces.</jats:p>

doi:10.24002/jai.v6i5.15067.title: Service Learning dalam Pemanfaatan Limbah Compact Disc pada Galeri Kerukunan Desa Jarak
doi:10.24002/jai.v6i5.15067.abstract: <jats:p>Galeri Kerukunan Umat Beragama in Jarak Village, Wonosalam Sub-district, Jombang Regency, is a tourism support facility built to represent the values of tolerance and diversity within the local community. During the initial construction phase, the building faced limitations in terms of its appearance and visual identity due to constraints on available resources. This community service initiative aimed to enhance the building’s visual quality by utilising waste Compact Discs (CDs) as adaptive façade elements. The program was implemented using the service-learning method through the ‘Sustainable Built Environment Service Learning’ course, involving two lecturers, sixteen students from the architecture program at Petra Christian University, the Makmur Bersinar Jarak Village-Owned Enterprise (BUMDes), and the community of Jarak Village. The implementation methods included identifying the partners’ needs, designing façade modules, collecting materials, assembling panels, installing the façade, and evaluating the activity. The program results showed that 52 façade panels made from waste compact discs were successfully installed at the Interfaith Harmony Gallery. An evaluation of 96 respondents revealed positive feedback, particularly regarding aesthetic aspects (79.00%), economic benefits (77.04%), and environmental impact (72.32%). This initiative not only produced a physical outcome in the form of an adaptive façade but also enhanced community participation and strengthened students’ contextual learning experiences through the application of sustainability principles and collaboration with the local community.</jats:p>

doi:10.35234/fumbd.1881368.title: Integrating Local and Global Feature Learning for Retinal Disease Detection: An EfficientNetB3-ViT Hybrid Model
doi:10.35234/fumbd.1881368.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Undiagnosed ocular conditions in initial phases can progressively impair vision, potentially leading to critical visual dysfunctions. Fundus imaging has enabled the identification of several retinal disorders, notably diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and age-related macular degeneration. However, manual evaluation of these images is both time-consuming and dependent on expert judgment. In this context, artificial intelligence-based automatic diagnosis systems have become an important need in the field of medical image analysis. In this study, deep learning-based models were compared for multi-class eye disease detection from fundus images, and a unique hybrid model was proposed. In this study, current deep learning architectures, including EfficientNetB3, DenseNet-121, ResNet-50, MobileNetV2, and ViT, were employed. All models were independently trained and tested, and their effectiveness was evaluated using commonly employed classification metrics. Additionally, a hybrid model based on EfficientNetB3 and ViT was designed, combining the strengths of Transformer and CNN architectures. All models were subjected to hyperparameter optimization using the GridSearch method, allowing for a fair comparison. The results obtained showed that the hybrid model successfully learned both local and global features in fundus images and exhibited higher performance compared to other models. In this context, the developed system has the potential to be integrated into future clinical decision-support systems.</jats:p>

doi:10.65224/jopate.v2i3.290.title: Constructivist Flipped Learning as a Recursive Knowledge Transformation Cycle
doi:10.65224/jopate.v2i3.290.abstract:
<jats:p>Background. Flipped learning has been widely implemented to reorganize learning activities across pre class, in class, and post class environments. However, existing models often emphasize instructional inversion and activity sequencing without adequately explaining how learners transform prior understanding into reconstructed knowledge.
Purpose. This conceptual study develops the Constructivist Flipped Learning Cycle (CFLC), an integrative theoretical model explaining knowledge transformation through cognitive and social constructivist mechanisms.
Method. The study employed a conceptual theory-building design comprising targeted literature identification, theoretical comparison, conceptual synthesis, framework development, and proposition formulation. Relevant perspectives on flipped learning, constructivism, cognitive conflict, social negotiation, knowledge reconstruction, and metacognitive reflection were integrated into a coherent explanatory model.
Results. The CFLC comprises seven interconnected stages: prior knowledge activation, exploratory pre-class engagement, cognitive conflict, social negotiation, knowledge reconstruction, authentic application, and metacognitive reflection. These stages form a recursive cycle in which reconstructed knowledge becomes prior knowledge for subsequent learning.
Novelty. The CFLC reframes flipped learning from a temporal-spatial inversion of instruction into a knowledge-transformation architecture and introduces a mechanism-based explanation linking cognitive conflict, social negotiation, and knowledge reconstruction across interconnected learning environments.
Conclusion. The CFLC provides a theoretically grounded framework for explaining how meaningful conceptual transformation may occur in flipped learning and offers testable propositions for future empirical validation across diverse educational contexts.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fenvs.2026.1928610.title: UAV-based RGB imagery and supervised–unsupervised machine learning for estimating sorghum biomass and grain yield under water and nitrogen stress
doi:10.3389/fenvs.2026.1928610.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Precision agriculture emerged as a key strategy for rational management of water and nutrients amid growing food demand driven by global population expansion. Therefore, timely monitoring of field crops is crucial in maintaining adequate nutrient and water levels in the crop fields. Vegetation indices are increasingly being studied for their use in plant nutrient management and in guiding fertilizer recommendations. However, these indices were not adequately evaluated for nutrient management of crops grown with different water and nitrogen application levels. This study investigated the potential application of RGB imagery from low-cost Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), combined with machine learning techniques, for quantifying water and nutrient stress in sorghum [
                    <jats:italic>Sorghum bicolor</jats:italic>
                    (L.) Moench] crop performance. The field experimental setup at Prairie View A&amp;M University, located in Southeast Texas, applied four irrigation levels (0, 75, 100, and 125% of irrigation; the 100% irrigation level is a fully irrigated treatment with no water stress) and four nitrogen application rates (0, 90, 180, and 360 kg N ha
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ). The RGB images were captured before harvesting the grain sorghum. Image segmentation for filtering sorghum crops from soil and weeds was performed using K-means clustering and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The vegetation indices, including the Green-Red Vegetation Index (GRVI), Green Leaf Index (GLI), and Excess Green Index (ExG), derived from the segmented images were used to predict sorghum grain and biomass yields using multiple linear regression, Partial least squares regression, Ridge regression, and XGBoost. The results indicated that no single model consistently outperformed the others across both segmentation approaches and response variables, suggesting that the predictive information in the RGB indices is meaningful with selected ML approaches. For example, biomass prediction using ridge regression yielded a Pearson correlation coefficient (r) of 0.65 and an RMSE of 0.72 for K-means clustering-derived indices. The models exhibited moderate, stage-specific predictive performance, with no single regression method consistently outperforming the others across both segmentation approaches and response variables. Because imagery was acquired only once during the late reproductive period, the RGB indices primarily reflected canopy condition, maturity, and senescence at that time. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of a low-cost, single-date UAV RGB workflow for late-season sorghum assessment, while emphasizing the need for multi-temporal imagery and independent validation before application to season-long stress diagnosis or operational yield forecasting.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.31110/2616-650x-vol14i7-018.title: ОСОБЛИВОСТІ ВИКОРИСТАННЯ ВЕЛИКИХ МОВНИХ МОДЕЛЕЙ СТУДЕНТАМИ НЕФІЛОЛОГІЧНИХ СПЕЦІАЛЬНОСТЕЙ У ПРОЦЕСІ ВИВЧЕННЯ ІНОЗЕМНОЇ МОВИ
doi:10.31110/2616-650x-vol14i7-018.abstract: <jats:p>The article presents the results of an empirical study examining the use of large language models by first-year non-philology students during foreign language learning. The aim of the study is to investigate the frequency, patterns, purposes, and motivations behind students' use of large language models who are not majoring in a foreign language. The empirical basis of the study consists of survey results from 51 respondents in March 2026. The collected data were analyzed using both quantitative and qualitative research methods. The survey revealed that ChatGPT and Gemini are the most widely used large language models among students. The paper found that more than one-quarter of respondents use large language models daily for educational purposes. The primary motivation for using these tools is time efficiency and the desire to complete academic tasks more quickly, regardless of subject complexity. Large language models are most frequently employed for vocabulary and text translation, grammar explanation, and the completion of lexical-grammar exercises and tests. However, their potential for developing productive language skills, particularly speaking and listening, remains underutilized. The study also revealed that most students are aware that using large language models may lead to violations of academic integrity principles. At the same time, the findings suggest that students do not always have a clear understanding of the boundaries between acceptable and unacceptable uses of artificial intelligence tools in academic contexts. Based on the results obtained, methodological recommendations are proposed for integrating large language models into foreign language instruction, including the use of Text-to-Speech technologies, elements of the flipped classroom approach, and creative communicative tasks in which large language models serve as supportive learning tools.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/rs18193344.title: Spectral Trajectory-Based Change Detection and Support Vector Machine Algorithm for Assessing Forest Landscape Disturbance Dynamics in Canada’s Athabasca Oil Sands Region
doi:10.3390/rs18193344.abstract: <jats:p>Monitoring the long-term cumulative impacts of industrial mining and environmental changes in sensitive ecosystems remains a critical challenge for sustainable resource management. This study investigates 41 years (1984–2025) of land use and land cover (LULC) dynamics in the Athabasca oil sands region (Alberta, Canada) using the historical Landsat archive (TM, ETM+, and OLI). The methodology integrated temporal and spectral features through two complementary phases: automated spectral trajectory-based change detection and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification combining original bands with multiple spectral indices, including normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), soil adjusted vegetation index (SAVI), enhanced vegetation index (EVI), transformed difference vegetation index (TDVI), bare soil index (BSI), and Modified Normalized Difference Water Index (MNDWI). This framework quantified baseline LULC, mining expansion, tailings pond footprints, and reclamation operations across a 12,146-km2 study area. The spectral trajectory analysis effectively tracked multiple temporal disturbances, revealing accelerating mining activities alongside forest harvesting, wildfire stress, and insect damage. Additionally, it captured progressive and significant spectral variations in the Athabasca River’s surface water, reflecting cumulative industrial runoff and long-term environmental pressure. Concurrently, the SVM classifications (Overall accuracy ≥ 96.8% and Kappa coefficient ≥ 94%) measured major LULC shifts. Dense coniferous forests declined by 1200 km2, while mixed forests decreased from 4500 km2 in 1984 to a minimum of 1200 km2 in 2010, before recovering to 3040 km2 by 2025 due to reclamation efforts. Conversely, active mining infrastructure and tailings ponds expanded from 95 km2 (1984) to 900 km2 (2025), occupying 7.41% of the landscape. Ultimately, this integrated remote sensing approach captured the complex interactions between accelerating industrial development, climate stressors, and the localized progress of land reclamation, providing a scalable framework for ecosystem monitoring in heavily disturbed landscapes.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1880789.title: Ready to learn: goal orientation and academic performance in a service-learning course for health professions students
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1880789.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Goal orientation and academic self-efficacy are central constructs in educational psychology; however, their roles in applied, interpersonal learning environments remain underexplored. This study examined relationships among mastery, performance, and avoidant goal orientations, academic self-efficacy, and academic performance in a service-learning course for health professions students. The mediating role of academic self-efficacy was also evaluated.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Seventy-four undergraduate and graduate public health students enrolled in a semester-long wellness coaching service-learning course completed baseline measures of goal orientation and academic self-efficacy. Academic performance was assessed using final course grades. Pearson correlations and mediation analyses were conducted while controlling for age and gender. Indirect effects were estimated using bootstrapped confidence intervals with 5,000 resamples.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Performance and avoidant goal orientations were positively associated with academic performance, whereas mastery goal orientation was not significantly associated with academic outcomes. Mastery and performance goal orientations were positively associated with academic self-efficacy; however, academic self-efficacy was not significantly associated with academic performance and did not mediate the relationship between goal orientation and academic performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings differ from patterns commonly observed in traditional academic settings, where mastery orientation and academic self-efficacy are typically stronger predictors of achievement. Results suggest that the influence of motivational orientations may depend on learning context, particularly in environments emphasizing interpersonal performance and applied skill use. These findings highlight the importance of considering contextual factors when applying motivational theory to experiential learning settings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.51878/strategi.v6i4.15371.title: ANALISIS PENERAPAN STRATEGI COLLABORATIVE LEARNING DENGAN TEKNIK JIGSAW TERHADAP HASIL BELAJAR IPAS KONTEN IPS SISWA KELAS IV SD
doi:10.51878/strategi.v6i4.15371.abstract:
<jats:p>ABSTRACT
Elementary social studies learning frequently struggles with passive classroom interactions. This qualitative case study aims to contextually analyze the implementation of a collaborative learning strategy using the Jigsaw technique in IPAS social studies content among fourth-grade students at SD Negeri 280811 Lawira. The empirical exploration involved five informants, namely the school principal, the fourth-grade teacher, and three students representing diverse participation levels, via non-participant observations, in-depth interviews, and documentation. Data were analyzed interactively employing the Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña framework. Field findings reveal that organizing the classroom into home and expert groups provides exploratory space for students to engage in discussions, execute peer-teaching roles, and foster shared responsibility. However, the collaborative dynamic remains constrained by psychological barriers such as nervousness, uneven individual participation, and limited discussion time. This study concludes that the Jigsaw technique fosters a more dynamic learning atmosphere, wherein its contribution to learning outcomes is understood qualitatively through perceived comprehension and classroom responsiveness, rather than as statistical evidence of quantitative improvement.
ABSTRAK
Interaksi instruksional yang searah masih menjadi tantangan mendasar dalam pembelajaran muatan sosial di tingkat sekolah dasar. Penelitian kualitatif studi kasus ini bertujuan menganalisis secara kontekstual penerapan strategi collaborative learning dengan teknik Jigsaw pada pembelajaran IPAS konten IPS siswa kelas IV SD Negeri 280811 Lawira. Pengungkapan fenomena kelas ini melibatkan lima informan, yaitu kepala sekolah, guru kelas IV, dan tiga orang siswa dengan representasi keaktifan yang berbeda, melalui observasi nonpartisipan, wawancara mendalam, serta dokumentasi. Olahan data dianalisis secara interaktif menggunakan kerangka Miles, Huberman, dan Saldaña. Temuan lapangan menunjukkan bahwa pengorganisasian kelas melalui skema kelompok asal dan kelompok ahli memberikan ruang eksplorasi bagi siswa untuk berdiskusi, mengeksekusi peran peer-teaching, dan membangun tanggung jawab bersama. Kendati demikian, efektivitas alur kolaborasi masih dibayangi oleh hambatan psikologis berupa rasa gugup, ketimpangan partisipasi individu, serta keterbatasan alokasi waktu diskusi. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa teknik Jigsaw mampu menstimulasi atmosfer belajar yang lebih dinamis, di mana kontribusinya terhadap hasil belajar dipahami secara kualitatif berdasarkan persepsi pemahaman dan responsif siswa di kelas, bukan sebagai bukti statistik atas peningkatan kuantitatif.</jats:p>
doi:10.51878/strategi.v6i4.15371.venue: STRATEGY : Jurnal Inovasi Strategi dan Model Pembelajaran

doi:10.24114/tj.v15i3.75114.title: Speaking Anxiety in EFL Students and Its Impact on Language Performance
doi:10.24114/tj.v15i3.75114.abstract: <jats:p>Speaking is one of the most important skills in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learning because it enables students to communicate ideas, opinions, and information effectively. Despite its importance, many EFL students experience difficulties when speaking English due to feelings of anxiety. Speaking anxiety has become a common issue in language classrooms and is often considered a major obstacle to successful communication. This paper aims to discuss students’ speaking experiences in EFL contexts, examine the factors that contribute to speaking anxiety, and analyze its impact on language performance. The discussion highlights several causes of speaking anxiety, including psychological factors such as fear of negative evaluation, communication apprehension, and low self-confidence, as well as linguistic limitations and classroom-related factors. Furthermore, the paper explores how anxiety affects students’ fluency, confidence, participation, motivation, and overall speaking performance. Previous studies indicate that students who experience high levels of anxiety are more likely to avoid speaking activities and face difficulties in expressing their ideas effectively. The discussion also emphasizes the importance of supportive classroom environments and appropriate teaching strategies in reducing anxiety and promoting communication. In conclusion, speaking anxiety significantly influences language performance and should be addressed through continuous practice, positive learning experiences, and effective instructional approaches to help students become more confident and successful English speakers.</jats:p>
doi:10.24114/tj.v15i3.75114.venue: TRANSFORM: Journal of English Language Teaching and Learning

doi:10.47116/apjcri.2026.09.54.title: Development of a Pediatric Asthma Nursing Scenario for Generative AI-Based Question-Centered Learning (QcL): Focusing on the Seamless Transition of ER, PICU, and General Ward (3-Steps)
doi:10.47116/apjcri.2026.09.54.abstract: The purpose of this study was to develop a pediatric asthma nursing scenario incorporating generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) based Question-Centered Learning (QcL) and to verify its content validity through an expert panel.This methodological study developed the scenario based on a literature review and analysis of clinical guidelines, integrating Gen AI with QcL strategies.The developed scenario reflected a continuum of nursing care across the emergency room (ER), pediatric intensive care unit (PICU), and general ward.To verify content validity, five experts in pediatric nursing and pediatrician evaluated the scenario, and content validity index (CVI) were calculated.Items with an item-level content validity index (I-CVI) of 0.80 were revised based on qualitative feedback from the experts, followed by a second review and reevaluation.The final scenario demonstrated a scale-level content validity index based on the average method (S-CVI/Ave) of 0.93, indicating a high level of content validity.In addition, the scenario incorporated a Gen AI-based feedback structure and QcL strategies to support learners' clinical reasoning and self-directed learning.In conclusion, the Gen AIbased QcL pediatric asthma nursing simulation scenario developed in this study can serve as a valid educational tool with clinical validity and educational applicability.In particular, the integration of a continuum of nursing care with a question-centered learning strategy suggests the potential to support learners' clinical judgment.Future studies should apply this scenario in actual educational settings with nursing students and newly graduated nurses to empirically evaluate its educational effectiveness.Further research is also needed to examine the practical applicability of Gen AI-based learning environments, as well as related ethical and technical considerations.

doi:10.68337/cpsm.v1.i1.2026-003.title: Early Detection and Severity Assessment of Parkinson's Disease Using Speech-Based Machine Learning
doi:10.68337/cpsm.v1.i1.2026-003.abstract: <jats:p>Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by progressive motor disability and early speech disorders. Early diagnosis and regular follow-up allow timely clinical intervention and a better quality of life. This paper introduces a machine learning framework that identifies PD and estimates its severity from acoustic features derived from speech. The data analyzed are from the Parkinson's Telemonitoring dataset of the UCI Machine Learning Repository, which consists of 5,875 voice recordings. Acoustic characteristics such as jitter, shimmer, harmonicity, and nonlinear vocal parameters capture the speech changes associated with PD. Supervised linear regression, support vector regression (SVR), random forest (RF) regression, and gradient boosting (GB) models, together with an RF and GB ensemble, were trained to predict the motor and total Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS) scores, and the predicted scores were then grouped into discrete severity levels. Model performance was analyzed with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The RF model achieved the best accuracy, 95.49%, which indicates strong predictive ability.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69924-2.title: Anomaly detection of internet of medical things cyberattacks using federated learning
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69924-2.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Devices connected to the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) handle sensitive patient data under strict privacy and resource constraints. Centralized intrusion detection introduces privacy risks and communication bottlenecks, while existing Federated Learning (FL) solutions struggle with class imbalance and data heterogeneity. This paper proposes One-Shot Federated Anomaly Detection (OneShot-FedAD), which completes feature selection and model training in a single communication round, eliminating iterative weight exchange. It integrates Federated Differential Privacy Mutual Information (DP-MI) for feature selection, local Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to reduce false alarms without sharing raw data, and Adaptive Weighted Aggregation (AWA) based on each client’s local validation F1-score. Across seven experiments on CICIoMT2024 and WUSTL-EHMS-2020, LightGBM achieves 99.75% accuracy and 99.87% F1-score on CICIoMT2024, stable across five random seeds (99.88% ± 0.01%, 95% CI), and 93.77% accuracy with 55.70% attack recall on WUSTL-EHMS-2020, reflecting severe class imbalance on this smaller dataset. DP-MI reduces the feature space by 28.57–44.44%. With per-client uploads under 350 KB, a 1.7 MB aggregated model, and 9.01–24.14 µs inference latency (72–193 µs under an 8
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$\times $$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    hardware slowdown), OneShot-FedAD is feasible on 512 MB edge devices.
                  </jats:p>
