doi:10.58344/jmi.v5i10.2974.title: Implementasi Pembelajaran Blended Learning Untuk Meningkatkan Motivasi dan Hasil Belajar Makanan Kontinental Pada Siswa Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan
doi:10.58344/jmi.v5i10.2974.abstract: <jats:p>Perkembangan teknologi informasi mendorong perubahan dalam proses pembelajaran, termasuk pada pendidikan kejuruan yang membutuhkan strategi pembelajaran inovatif untuk meningkatkan motivasi dan hasil belajar siswa. Permasalahan dalam pembelajaran Pengolahan Makanan Kontinental di Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan (SMK) menunjukkan rendahnya motivasi belajar dan pencapaian hasil belajar siswa akibat penggunaan metode pembelajaran yang masih berpusat pada guru. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui implementasi pembelajaran Blended Learning dalam meningkatkan motivasi dan hasil belajar siswa pada mata pelajaran Makanan Kontinental. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) dengan model spiral McTaggart yang terdiri atas tahapan perencanaan, tindakan, observasi, dan refleksi. Subjek penelitian adalah 40 siswa kelas XI Tata Boga. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi, dokumentasi, tes, dan angket, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kuantitatif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penerapan Blended Learning berbasis Web Learning mampu meningkatkan aktivitas dan motivasi belajar siswa. Pada Siklus II, sebanyak 90% siswa berada pada kategori motivasi tinggi dan 92,5% siswa mencapai nilai ketuntasan minimal. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa Blended Learning dapat menjadi alternatif strategi pembelajaran yang efektif dalam meningkatkan keterlibatan siswa dan pemahaman materi praktik. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa penerapan Blended Learning memberikan dampak positif terhadap peningkatan motivasi dan hasil belajar siswa SMK.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11239563/v1.title: AI Literacy and Academic Performance among Non-STEM Students in KNUST: The Roles of LMS Quality and Blended-Learning Satisfaction
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11239563/v1.abstract: With the growing integration of AI in higher education, it remains unclear how AI literacy relates to academic performance among non-STEM students. This study examined the sequential mediating roles of learning management system (LMS) quality and blended-learning satisfaction (BLS) in the relationship between AI literacy and academic performance. 432 students from the non-STEM at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology in Ghana participated in a quantitative cross-sectional survey. Partial least squares structural modelling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4 was used for the data analyses. AI literacy strongly predicted LMS quality (β = .814, p < .001) and showed a notably significant effect on academic performance (β = .222, p = .001). The LMS quality significantly predicted BLS (β = .604, p < .001), which then predicted academic performance (β = .535, p < .001). LMS quality did not significantly influence academic performance (β = .074, p = .233). It did not independently mediate the correlation between AI literacy and academic performance (β = .061, p = .236). In contrast, in a direct sequential pathway, LMS quality proved significant (β = .263, p < .001). University policymakers should support students with blended learning support and organise AI literacy training in addition to funding digital infrastructure. AI literacy strongly correlates with academic performance when digital systems are built to support rewarding blended learning experiences.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11239563/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.4324/9781003608271-10.title: Issues-Centered Learning and Decision-Making
doi:10.4324/9781003608271-10.abstract: Social studies helps develop students into effective citizens and helps students better understand the world and the various people in it. With this in mind, a focus of social studies has to be on understanding and discussing issues that cause conflicts in society, decision-making, values, and character development. This chapter focuses on the social studies teacher’s role in issues-centered learning, the decision-making process, the development of values, and the cultivation of positive character development for the purposes of helping students become good citizens. While many of these topics, such as issues-centered learning, values education, and character education, will always be controversial, the necessity of effective democratic values and character education elements in the social studies program cannot be denied.

doi:10.1108/ijius-05-2026-0176.title: Enhancing the manufacturing processes and productivity in Industry 5.0 with the integration of machine learning and cyber-physical systems
doi:10.1108/ijius-05-2026-0176.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper aims to examine the synergistic integration of Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and Machine Learning (ML) as a foundational enabler for Industry 5.0, focusing on creating human-centric, sustainable and resilient manufacturing ecosystems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study utilizes a synthesis and review approach, analyzing recent advances in ML-driven CPS applications such as workflow optimization and predictive maintenance, alongside enabling technologies like 5G and digital twins.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings show that the integration of ML in multi-tier Edge-Fog-Cloud CPS brings significant operational advantages for the shop floor, such as sub-millisecond real-time control, more efficient human–robot interaction and a 10–20% reduction in energy used by the shop floor. But, the benefits of such physical manufacturing solutions rely on the need to work through a number of operational challenges. These include formally verifying non-deterministic ML policies, reducing IT/OT cybersecurity threats, including data poisoning and signal spoofing, reducing data heterogeneity in Federated Learning (FL) and lowering high deployment costs for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Future implementation requires addressing the need for Explainable AI (XAI) for transparency, FL for privacy and reinforcement learning for human-in-the-loop control.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The proposed paradigm is applicable in smart factories, autonomous production lines and supply chain optimization, helping manufacturers maximize asset output and reduce environmental impact.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper highlights the essential shift from “technology-driven” (Industry 4.0) to “value-driven” (Industry 5.0) manufacturing, identifying the CPS-ML convergence as the critical engine for this transition.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.1108/ijius-05-2026-0176.venue: International Journal of Intelligent Unmanned Systems

doi:10.32529/glasser.v10i2.5098.title: THE INFLUENCE OF WAYGROUND GAME-BASED LEARNING AND SELF-EFFICACY ON STUDENTS LEARNING OUTCOMES IN SAVINGS MATERIAL
doi:10.32529/glasser.v10i2.5098.abstract: <jats:p>Uninteractive teaching methods often lead to suboptimal learning outcomes in banking and accounting. To address this, innovative strategies like Wayground Game-Based Learning (GBL) are essential for boosting student engagement. Furthermore, psychological factors such as self-efficacy play a crucial role in determining students' academic confidence. This study aims to analyze The Influence of Wayground Game-Based Learning (GBL) and Self-Efficacy on Students’ Learning Outcomes in Savings Material. This research employed a quantitative approach using an associative research design. The sample was determined using a saturated sampling technique, in which all twelfth-grade students of the Accounting and Financial Institution program at SMK Negeri 1 Sooko Mojokerto were selected as the research respondents. Data were collected through questionnaires and learning outcome tests and subsequently analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results revealed that the Wayground Game-Based Learning and Self-Efficacy simultaneously had a positive and significant effect on students' learning outcomes (Sig. = 0.000 < 0.05). Partially, both variables were also found to have a positive and significant effect on learning outcomes. The coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.853, indicating that 85.3% of the variance in students' learning outcomes was explained by the Wayground Game-Based Learning and Self-Efficacy, while the remaining 14.7% was attributed to other factors beyond the scope of this research model. Based on these empirical findings, it can be concluded that the implementation of the Wayground Game-Based Learning, supported by a high level of Self-Efficacy, can effectively enhance students' learning outcomes in the Savings material. Therefore, this learning model may be considered an innovative instructional strategy to optimize the quality of learning outcomes in the savings material.</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s12911-026-03664-1.title: Using interpretable machine learning models to predict the occurrence of severe influenza in hospitalized children: a retrospective cohort study
doi:10.1186/s12911-026-03664-1.abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza, a prevalent disease, significantly threatens public health. Accurately predicting severe influenza occurrences is crucial for developing personalized prevention strategies and treatment plans. AIMS: This study aimed to construct a highly interpretable model to assess the risk of severe influenza in hospitalized children, using the SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) method to interpret the Random Forest (RF) model and identify risk factors for severe influenza. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted, collecting hospitalization records of influenza patients from the Electronic Medical Records (EMR) system for model development and performance evaluation. Data were collected within the first 24 h after patient admission and the dataset was randomly divided into two parts: 70% for model training and 30% for model accuracy verification. RESULTS: A total of 436 eligible influenza patients were included in the study analysis. The RF model demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy among the six models compared, with an area under the receiver-operating-characteristiccurve(AUROC) of 0.88. The decision curve analysis (DCA) indicated that the net benefit of the RF model surpassed that of other machine learning models. According to the importance ranking by the SHAP method, blood glucose was identified as the most significant predictive variable. CONCLUSION: The study established a RF model capable of predicting severe influenza occurrence in hospitalized children. The model, interpreted through the SHAP method, assists physicians in providing better treatment plans.
doi:10.1186/s12911-026-03664-1.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10852588/v1.title: Early prediction of refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia in children: development and internal validation of a combined CT radiomics–clinical machine learning model
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10852588/v1.abstract: Background Refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (RMPP) has a protracted course and frequent complications, and its diagnosis is often delayed; early identification of children at high risk is therefore crucial. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a combined machine-learning model integrating CT radiomics features and early clinical indicators to predict progression from Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) to RMPP in children. Methods This single-center retrospective study enrolled 527 children with MPP (204 RMPP, 323 non-refractory MPP [NRMPP]) between January 2022 and December 2024, randomly split into training (n = 368) and internal test (n = 159) cohorts at a ratio of approximately 7:3. From 1834 CT radiomics features, 25 selected by stability (intraclass correlation coefficient ≥ 0.85), Mann–Whitney U screening, correlation-based redundancy removal and LASSO dimensionality reduction formed a radiomics score (Rad-score); seven machine-learning classifiers were compared. A clinical model was built by multivariate logistic regression with backward stepwise selection of variables with P < 0.1 on univariate analysis, and a combined model integrating the clinical prediction and Rad-score was visualized as a nomogram. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, the Hosmer–Lemeshow test and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results The combined model achieved AUCs of 0.876 (95% CI: 0.839–0.913) and 0.869 (95% CI: 0.815–0.923) in the training and test cohorts, respectively, significantly outperforming the clinical model (0.704 and 0.638; P = 1.42 × 10⁻⁸ and P = 1.59 × 10⁻⁶); in the test cohort, its AUC was also higher than that of the radiomics model (0.851), although not significantly (P = 0.060). The final clinical model included LDH, peak body temperature and ALT. DCA demonstrated a higher net benefit of the combined model across a wide range of threshold probabilities. The Hosmer–Lemeshow test indicated some degree of miscalibration of the combined model in the test cohort (P = 0.032). Conclusions The combined machine-learning model showed good discrimination for predicting progression from MPP to RMPP (internal test AUC 0.869) and significantly outperformed the clinical model; however, its calibration was suboptimal in the test cohort (Hosmer–Lemeshow P = 0.032), and external validation and recalibration are required before clinical deployment.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10852588/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11212418/v1.title: From Prediction to Recommendation: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Fine-Tuned Language Model Approach for Soil-Based Crop Recommendation
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11212418/v1.abstract: Crop recommendation is an important decision-support task in agriculture, where multiple crops may be suitable under similar soil and environmental conditions. In this paper, we propose a hybrid framework that combines classical machine learning with a fine-tuned lightweight language model for soil-based crop recommendation. We first evaluate several classical machine learning models and a neural network baseline on tabular agricultural data. Our results show that XGBoost achieves the best predictive performance (0.487 Top-1 and 0.770 Top-3 accuracy across 48 crop classes), while a Multi-Layer Perceptron does not provide meaningful improvement over tree-based methods. Because strict single-label prediction is often inadequate in agricultural settings, we reformulate the task as a Top-K recommendation problem and show that Top-3 accuracy provides a more realistic measure of practical utility. To improve interpretability and usability, we further fine-tune a lightweight language model using LoRA to generate structured, farmer-friendly recommendations conditioned on machine learning predictions. Qualitative evaluation on held-out examples demonstrates that the fine-tuned model produces more coherent, grounded, and useful outputs than the base model. Overall, our results highlight the effectiveness of combining tabular machine learning for prediction with language models for explanation in agricultural decision-support systems.

doi:10.3390/w18192464.title: Hybrid Deep Learning with Multi-Source Data Fusion for Deep Groundwater-Level Prediction and Anomaly Detection
doi:10.3390/w18192464.abstract: <jats:p>Deep groundwater dynamics, influenced by multiple factors, exhibit multi-scale periodicity, nonlinearity, and non-stationarity, posing significant challenges for reliable groundwater level prediction and anomaly detection. To address this issue, this study develops a hybrid deep learning model for simulating and predicting normal groundwater dynamics, which integrates multi-source observations—including barometric pressure, solid tide, and historical groundwater levels—with convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Attention mechanisms. An Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) control chart is then applied to the prediction residuals for statistical anomaly detection. The results show that CNN kernels capture multi-period local features induced by barometric and tidal effects; LSTM gating mechanisms learn long-term temporal dependencies; and the Attention mechanism dynamically assigns weights to both temporal steps and input features. Compared with single-source inputs or standalone LSTM/CNN models, the hybrid model enhances prediction accuracy (MAE < 0.02, RMSE < 0.03, R2 > 0.99), while integration with the EWMA control chart helps to identify the possible anomalies. Collectively, these results provide a reliable means for predicting deep groundwater levels and detecting hydrological anomalies under complex multi-scale periodic forcings, holding significant practical value in groundwater resource management and disaster warning.</jats:p>

doi:10.58764/j.im.2026.7.209.title: Optimalisasi Investasi Wakaf Uang melalui Diversifikasi Aset dan Peningkatan Kapasitas Nazhir: Studi Kasus Badan Wakaf Uang Muhammadiyah Sumatera Barat
doi:10.58764/j.im.2026.7.209.abstract: <jats:p>Aims: This study aims to analyze the optimization of waqf investment at Badan Wakaf Uang Muhammadiyah (BWUM) West Sumatra by focusing on waqf asset diversification, investment management, risk control, and the utilization of investment returns for community welfare. Method: This research employs a qualitative approach using an ex-post facto method. Data were collected through interviews and documentation related to waqf investment management at BWUM West Sumatra. The data were analyzed descriptively to examine the practices of investment development, supervision, reporting, risk management, and distribution of waqf benefits. Results: The findings indicate that BWUM West Sumatra has developed waqf funds through Islamic financial institutions and productive business activities, including UD Berkah. However, several investments have been discontinued due to considerations of efficiency and sustainability. Waqf investment management is supported by supervision, financial reporting, reserve fund establishment, and the distribution of investment benefits to social, educational, and healthcare sectors. These findings demonstrate that waqf investment optimization requires a balance between asset development, risk control, professional nazhir management, transparency, and the orientation toward public welfare. Conclusion/Novelty/Implications: The novelty of this study lies in its integrated analysis of waqf investment optimization by linking asset diversification, investment management, risk control, and the utilization of investment returns within the context of BWUM West Sumatra. The findings imply that strengthening nazhir professionalism, investment governance, transparency, and risk management is essential to ensure the sustainability and productivity of waqf assets. Future efforts should emphasize broader asset diversification, more strategic investment planning, and the development of productive waqf models that generate sustainable socio-economic benefits for the community.</jats:p>

doi:10.54536/ajelps.v2i2.8239.title: Exploring the Role of Hands-On Learning Activities in Supporting Preschoolers’ Cognitive and Social Development: Evidence from Two Early Childhood Centres in Malawi
doi:10.54536/ajelps.v2i2.8239.abstract: <jats:p>Early childhood education plays a critical role in promoting children’s cognitive, social, and emotional development, laying the foundation for lifelong learning and well-being. Among the pedagogical approaches widely advocated in contemporary early childhood education, hands-on learning has gained increasing recognition for its potential to foster active engagement, problem-solving, communication, and collaborative learning. Despite growing international evidence supporting activity-based and experiential learning approaches, limited research has examined how hands-on learning activities support child development within preschool settings in Malawi. Furthermore, the study sort to fill the gap on the role of promoting children’s cognitive, social and emotional development by exploring how hands-on learning activities influence preschoolers’ cognitive and social development and identify factors that affect their effective implementation as specific gaps identified. Drawing from Vygotsky’s sociocultural theory, this study explored the role of hands-on learning activities in supporting preschoolers’ cognitive and social development in two early childhood centers in Lilongwe, Malawi. A qualitative-dominant comparative case study design was employed involving classroom observations, semi-structured teacher interviews, and document analysis. Data were collected from two preschool centers serving children aged three to six years and analyzed by using themes. Interview transcripts, observation notes, and documentary evidence were reviewed repeatedly to ensure familiarity with the data. The findings indicate that hands-on learning activities supported children’s cognitive development through enhanced problem-solving, creativity, language development, concentration, and numeracy skills. The activities also promoted social development by encouraging cooperation, communication, sharing, empathy, and collaborative participat ion. However, the developmental benefits of hands-on learning appeared to depend heavily on teacher scaffolding, peer interaction, and institutional support. Centers characterized by stronger teacher guidance, planning practices, and resource availability demonstrated more consistent developmental outcomes. This study contributes to sociocultural and early childhood education literature by demonstrating that the value of hands-on learning extends beyond children’s interaction with materials. Rather, developmental gains emerge through scaffolded social participation, collaborative learning, and supportive educational environments. </jats:p>

doi:10.1111/ajfs.70061.title: Forecasting Variable Insurance Surrender Rates in Korea: Explainable Machine Learning and Macro‐financial Transmission
doi:10.1111/ajfs.70061.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study examines aggregate life insurance surrender risk as a macro‐financial transmission mechanism linking household contract adjustment to insurer balance sheets. Using monthly data for Korean Variable Annuity Insurance (VAI) and Variable Universal Insurance (VUI) from 2006 to 2019, we compare econometric and machine learning forecasts over 1‐, 3‐, 6‐, and 12‐month horizons. Forecast performance is evaluated over 2017–2019 using expanding and 120‐month rolling windows. No model dominates uniformly across products, horizons, and estimation windows. Tree‐based methods frequently perform well, but SARIMAX and LASSO remain competitive in other settings, indicating that the value of model flexibility is state‐, product‐, and horizon‐dependent. At the 1‐month horizon, the best rolling models reduce RMSE relative to lag‐1 persistence by 22.7% for VAI and 30.1% for VUI; the corresponding expanding window reductions are 28.2% and 34.2%. Scaling these improvements by average 2017–2019 in‐force amounts yields approximately KRW 30.7 billion and KRW 154.7 billion of exposure‐equivalent forecast error reduction for VAI and VUI, respectively. Out‐of‐sample SHAP analysis indicates that business cycle conditions, interest rates, surrender‐history variables, and selected insurance‐industry characteristics receive substantial but product‐specific predictive attribution. The findings suggest that explainable machine learning can complement conventional econometric forecasting by capturing nonlinear and product‐specific surrender dynamics.</jats:p>

doi:10.59024/jiti.v4i4.2588.title: Analisis Deteksi Manipulasi Gambar Menggunakan Error Level Analysis dan Deep Learning di SD Padedewatu
doi:10.59024/jiti.v4i4.2588.abstract: <jats:p>Digital images are increasingly used as documentation in educational environments, while image-editing tools make manipulation increasingly accessible. This study analyzes a workflow that combines Error Level Analysis (ELA) and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for preliminary detection of manipulated images using photographs from SD Padedewatu as a case study. The dataset initially consisted of 34 original photographs. Because the supplied photographs did not contain verified manipulation labels, controlled manipulated variants were generated from each source image using copy-move, splicing, and object-erasure operations. The resulting labeled dataset contained 136 images, consisting of 34 authentic and 102 manipulated images. ELA was applied by recompressing each image and visualizing the resulting compression-error differences. A CNN classifier was then trained on ELA representations. To reduce source-image leakage, 24 source-image groups were used for training and 10 source-image groups were reserved for testing, producing 96 training images and 40 testing images. The model achieved 75% test Accuracy, 75% precision, 100% recall, and an F1-score of 85.71%. However, the confusion matrix showed that all test images were predicted as manipulated, including the 10 authentic images. Therefore, the Accuracy value should not be interpreted as evidence of balanced or robust forgery detection. The experiment provides a reproducible local ELA-CNN workflow and identifies dataset balance, sample size, and external validation as important priorities for subsequent research.</jats:p>
