doi:10.3390/su181910167.title: Spatiotemporal Variation Analysis of Groundwater Storage in Huaihe River Basin Based on GRACE and Interpretable Machine Learning
doi:10.3390/su181910167.abstract: <jats:p>Groundwater represents an essential water resource across the Huaihe River Basin, and its sustainable use is important for maintaining regional water resource security. This study systematically examined the long-term evolution, seasonal variability, and major drivers of groundwater storage anomalies (GWSA) throughout the Huaihe River Basin over the period 2002–2024. GRACE satellite observations were combined with Seasonal-Trend decomposition (STL) and the XGBoost-SHAP interpretable machine learning framework to conduct the analysis. Results indicated that GWSA exhibited a significant declining trend (−4.08 mm/a), characterized by marked seasonal fluctuations with peaks in June and troughs in August. Spatially, groundwater storage depletion was predominantly observed in the northern and northwestern regions, whereas slight recovery occurred in parts of the central-southern plains. Feature attribution analysis identified population density (mean |SHAP| = 0.386) as the most important predictor of GWSA variability among the factors considered, followed by cropland area, temperature, precipitation, and NDVI. SHAP interaction analysis further revealed model-based interactions among anthropogenic and hydroclimatic factors. Spatial correlation analysis showed distinct spatial associations of GWSA with human-related and natural factors. And the temporal shift in SHAP values from negative to positive suggests changes in the associations between human-related factors and GWSA, which may be related to groundwater management and regional water-supply adjustments. These findings provide quantitative insights into the complex interplay between anthropogenic and climatic drivers on GWS, providing a scientific basis for groundwater management in the HRB.</jats:p>

doi:10.1088/1361-6501/aeaafb.title: A physics-constrained deep learning framework for feature recognition in long-distance natural gas pipelines
doi:10.1088/1361-6501/aeaafb.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The safety assurance of long-distance natural gas pipelines depends on accurate perception of their service condition, and this capability, in turn, relies on effective identification of features such as bending deformation, dents, and weld anomalies. However, when bending strain signals are used for feature recognition, existing methods still suffer from insufficient discrimination of composite pipeline features and limited classification accuracy. To address these issues, this paper proposes a physics-constrained deep learning framework for long-distance natural gas pipeline features. The framework introduces the Symmetric Temporal Convolutional Network and the Conformer-V module to extract high-dimensional spatiotemporal information from pipeline features, enhance the perception of bidirectional spatial context, and capture local geometric symmetry patterns. Taking the Euler–Bernoulli beam theory as an engineering prior approximation, the physics-constrained modulation module learns information related to local bending response through a curvature regression head and a physical consistency loss, and further maps the predicted curvature into gating weights to modulate the backbone features, thereby achieving collaborative feature recognition through data-driven learning and physical constraints. Validation, ablation, and comparative experiments conducted on a 200 km inertial measurement unit field measurement dataset from a long-distance natural gas pipeline show that the proposed method achieves a classification accuracy of 98.94%, demonstrating strong discriminative performance for composite pipeline features.</jats:p>

doi:10.29060/taps.2026-11-4/oa3772.title: Ultrasound learning experiences in a Japanese student-led circle: A descriptive study
doi:10.29060/taps.2026-11-4/oa3772.abstract:
<jats:p>Introduction: Peer-assisted learning (PAL) is widely used to support collaborative clinical skill development. In Japan, PAL is often organised through student-led extracurricular groups known as circles or “bukatsudō”. This descriptive study examined the educational characteristics of a student-led ultrasound circle, the Hamamatsu Emergency Room Ultrasound (HERUS), and explored students’ learning experiences.
Methods: We conducted a retrospective survey of sixth-year medical students who completed their clinical clerkships. The duration and extent of HERUS members’ (n = 14) and non-members’ ultrasound learning were compared. Additionally, HERUS members were surveyed to examine factors associated with learning frequency and faculty recognition. Qualitative open-ended responses about perceived educational benefits were analysed using content analysis.
Results: HERUS members gained earlier ultrasound experience in the cardiac, abdominal, and neck regions, and were more likely to have performed cardiac ultrasound on patients during clerkship, than non-members. HERUS members with ≥30 months of participation reported more departments where HERUS was discussed with faculty.  Half of the HERUS members practiced ultrasound with peers at least weekly. Content analysis indicated that wearing scrubs helped faculty identify HERUS members and provide them with opportunities for ultrasound practices on real patients. Self-motivating factors were collaborative PAL, perceived competence in ultrasound examinations in clinical settings, and self-paced, repetitive practice.
Conclusion: HERUS provided a culturally grounded, practical environment for student-led ultrasound learning. Qualitative patterns reflected factors corresponding to relatedness, competence, and autonomy in self-determination theory. These preliminary insights may help refine student-led PAL initiatives.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11252623/v1.title: An Integrated Explainable AI and Universal Design for Learning (UDL) Framework for Inclusive Special Education Systems
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11252623/v1.abstract: Background: Inclusion systems of special education have long struggled to provide individualized, transparent and equitable learning conditions. Traditional reactive models are not usually able to support learner variability, which is one of the roots of a global educational divide whereby millions of children with disabilities have inadequate access to quality education. As promising as an adaptive learning and intelligent tutoring tool may be, the black-box nature of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tends to erode trust and cast doubt on ethical aspects of automated decision-making. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) overcomes these drawbacks by improving the interpretability of algorithm processes. At the same time, Universal Design for Learning (UDL) offers a proactive pedagogical model that stresses variability of learners, their agency, and elimination of systemic barriers as further supported in the UDL 3.0 guidelines. Purpose: This review synthesizes the literature on XAI and UDL, demonstrating their complementary strengths and proposing an integrated XAI-UDL system to support the inclusive special education system. It also analyzes the applicability and implication of educational and research ecosystem of the United States in the promotion of this integrated system. Procedure: A systematic review of the literature was performed using Scopus, Web of science, ERIC, Pubmed and Google scholar to retrieve 2019-2026 publications. Search terms were: Explainable AI, Universal Design for Learning, special education, inclusive learning. The peer-reviewed journal articles, conference proceedings, and empirical studies were subjected to rigorous quality appraisal criteria, which resulted in a final dataset of 165 sources. Results: The synthesis demonstrates strong synergistic benefits from integrating XAI and UDL. XAI offers transparency and interpretability, builds trust, accountability, and learner agency, and UDL provides the pedagogical framework that is required to transform AI-driven insights into meaningful instructional practices. Empirical data show that digital literacy, learner self-efficacy, and system usability among students with disabilities greatly improved. Moreover, the educational and research ecosystem in the United States, which is characterized by strong policy frameworks, interdisciplinary research funding, technological innovation, and leadership on inclusive education, provides a highly conducive environment to the development, validation and large-scale application of the XAI-UDL framework. Federal requirements in favor of inclusive education, effective academia-industry partnership, and investment in the study of AI helps the ethical implementation of explainable systems in educational practice. Conclusion: The proposed XAI–UDL framework offers a viable pathway toward transparent, adaptive, and inclusive learning environments. Its congruency with the developed educational system and research capabilities of the United States further underpins its scalability and universal applicability. This synthesis offers crucial advice to researchers, educators, and policymakers to utilize AI in a responsible manner and enhance equity and inclusion in special education systems.

doi:10.1108/ijrdm-09-2025-0741.title: Learning by doing: diary study of attitude formation in voice-commerce
doi:10.1108/ijrdm-09-2025-0741.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Voice commerce (VC) is gaining momentum as a new channel and consumer touchpoint, with popular e-retailers adding it as an additional interface option on their websites. Its adoption and continuous usage are currently limited to low-involvement purchases. This research explores consumers' buying journey of high-involvement products using VC to understand how it influences actual buying behaviour.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A qualitative self-report diary was used to collect data. A total of 23 respondents completed the process with eight different products over 8 weeks.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Findings reveal that consumer behaviour in VC for high-involvement purchases is a self-reinforcement loop where consumer attitude and trust, arising from personal experiences, modify intentions and behaviour in VC. Further, this study identified learning-by-doing and immersive shopping experiences as drivers of consumers' preference for VC in high-involvement purchases. Also, individual factors such as regulatory focus and technophilic orientation moderate the behaviour.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This research contributes by extending the Stimulus-Organism-Behaviour-Consequence framework in explaining consumers buying behaviour in high-involvement products using VC. It identifies a self-reinforcement loop through the learning-by-doing effect and an immersive shopping experience as organismic factors that alter trust, making it a dynamic psychological mechanism that influences consumer behaviour in VC. Further, it uncovers the role of individual factors, such as a technophilic orientation and regulatory focus.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74048-8.title: A hybrid deep learning and cryptographic framework using signcryption for robust biometric template protection
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74048-8.abstract: Protecting biometric data is a crucial concern in the age of digital identity verification. A multimodal template protection system that safeguards iris and fingerprint modalities is presented in this work. Discriminative extraction of features using CNN and then binarized to produce compact binary representations. A robust multimodal feature vector is produced by fusing these binary codes using a Block-XOR method. A signcryption process is used to create protected templates for safe storage and authentication in order to further improve security. Data confidentiality, integrity, and trustworthy authentication are guaranteed by the suggested structure. With low Equal Error Rates of 0.0201%, 0.044%, and 0.496%, respectively, experimental evaluation on three benchmark datasets CMBD, CASIAV1 with FVC2004, and CASIAV3 with FVC2006 shows good performance.

doi:10.1017/s0272263126101995.title: Validating the theory-informed Tests of Aptitude for Language Learning (TALL) as predictors of L2 proficiency: Initial evidence from multiple regression analyses
doi:10.1017/s0272263126101995.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:italic>Tests of Aptitude for Language Learning</jats:italic>
                    (TALL) is a newly developed battery for L1 Chinese speakers that operationalizes language aptitude based on the early stages of Skehan’s (2016) Stages Approach through parallel aural and written suites. Each suite comprises subtests measuring associative memory, phonetic coding ability, language analytic ability, phonological short-term memory, and executive function of working memory. Using openly available data, this study examined TALL’s predictive validity through multiple regression analyses. Results from 165 L1-Chinese L2-English learners showed that the composite scores on the aural and written suites accounted for 12.5% and 13.1% of the variance in L2 proficiency, respectively. Models based on individual subtest scores accounted for 17.0% of the variance in L2 proficiency in the aural suite and 19.7% in the written suite. Dominance analyses identified language analytic and phonetic coding abilities as the strongest predictors, whereas other components contributed minimally. These findings provide initial evidence that TALL scores predict L2 proficiency. The study also offers a replicable procedure to facilitate further validation of this new battery. (Received 4 November 2025; revised 7 June 2026; accepted 6 August 2026) Keywords: aptitude battery; language aptitude; predictive validity
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11260636/v1.title: From Linguistic to Cultural Equivalence: An AI-Driven, Context-Aware Neural Machine Translation Framework for Arabic-English
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11260636/v1.abstract: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) and neural machine translation (NMT) has substantially refined the linguistic fluency, efficiency, and scalability of Arabic-English translation. Notwithstanding these advances, linguistic accuracy and surface-level correspondence don’t necessarily guarantee the preservation of contextual, pragmatic, and cultural meaning, particularly in the rendering of idioms, proverbs, metaphors, religious formulas, social expressions, politeness conventions, dialectal language, and other culture-specific linguistic forms. Addressing this limitation, the present study proposes Context-Aware NMT for Arabic-English (CANMT-AE), a theoretically grounded framework that reconceptualizes context, pragmatic, and cultural knowledge as integral computational inputs in the translation process rather than as post-editing considerations. Informed by perspectives from NMT, cognitive linguistics, pragmatics, translation studies, Arabic natural language processing (NLP), and culturally aware AI, the study critically integrates five major research streams, namely NMT architecture, context-aware NMT, Arabic dialectal machine translation (MT), idiomatic expressions translation, and generative AI translation. The study employs a qualitative conceptual-comparative approach to systematically examine theoretically motivated Arabic-English examples representing diverse forms of culturally and pragmatically complex language use. In light of these considerations, the proposed framework is conceptualized as a six-stage sequential process, comprising source-language identification, linguistic parsing, contextual interpretation, pragmatic and cultural inference, cultural equivalence selection, and target-language generation. The CANMT-AE framework moves beyond the assumption that literal or semantically equivalent translations are sufficient by distinguishing between linguistic, semantic, contextual, pragmatic, and cultural equivalence. The framework consequently facilitates the selection of alternative translation strategies, including preservation, adaptation, substitution, paraphrase, and explicitation, in accordance with communicative context and the degree of cultural density. The study contends that culturally aware Arabic-English translation calls for AI systems to move beyond sentence-level correspondence toward meaning construction that incorporates linguistic form with speaker intention, communicative context, pragmatic function, and shared cultural knowledge. Against this conceptual backdrop, the proposed framework offers a conceptual foundation for future empirical evaluation of culturally embedded Arabic-English translation, thereby contributing to the broader development of context-sensitive and culturally responsive AI-based translation systems.

doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1867114.title: Integrated multi-omics and machine learning identify core mechanobiology-associated immune genes in pulmonary arterial hypertension
doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1867114.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) involves vascular remodeling and altered mechanical signaling. The immune-associated transcriptomic changes accompanying this environment remain incompletely characterized.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We integrated bulk lung (GSE15197), PBMC (GSE33463), and single-cell RNA-seq (GSE169471) data using a curated set of 2, 537 mechanical-related genes. WGCNA, LASSO, random forest, and single-cell localization supported candidate prioritization. The four-gene panel was examined in a monocrotaline-induced PH rat model and PBMCs from 10 IPAH patients and 10 controls.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PAH transcriptomes showed enrichment of stress-fiber, actomyosin, ECM, and immune-related programs. CD83, CD86, IL6, and TLR7 were prioritized, with compartment-dependent expression patterns. Single-cell data localized CD83/CD86 to myeloid/APC compartments and IL6 to endothelial/fibroblast populations; TLR7 was sparsely detected. In MCT-treated rat lungs, CD86 and TLR7 proteins increased, whereas CD83 and IL-6 decreased. Clinical PBMCs showed corresponding expression directions, and each gene had an AUC &gt;0.7. The exploratory four-gene disease-state score achieved an internal cross-validated AUC of 0.765.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The four candidates provide a cellular and molecular context for investigating immune-stromal interactions in PAH, including responses to noninfectious vascular injury. The panel showed moderate internal discrimination. These findings support further clinical and functional investigation but do not establish direct mechanotransduction targets or a causal pathway linking mechanical stress to vascular inflammation.</jats:p>

doi:10.61994/educate.v4i2.2359.title: Pengasuhan Otoritatif dan Dukungan Teman Sebaya sebagai Prediktor Motivasi Akademik Siswa SMP
doi:10.61994/educate.v4i2.2359.abstract: <jats:p>Academic motivation is an important factor in students’ engagement and learning success and develops within social contexts. This study examined authoritative parenting and peer support as predictors of academic motivation among junior high school students. A quantitative cross-sectional explanatory survey design was employed. Participants were 320 students in Grades 7–9 from several junior high schools in Bekasi City and Bekasi Regency, Indonesia, recruited through voluntary response sampling. Data were collected using measures of academic motivation, authoritative parenting, and peer support, and analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results showed that authoritative parenting and peer support jointly predicted academic motivation significantly (R² = .418, F = 113.90, p < .001). Authoritative parenting showed a stronger standardized predictive contribution (β = .460, p < .001) than peer support (β = .307, p < .001). These findings suggest that both family and peer contexts are significantly associated with students’ academic motivation during early adolescence. The results also indicate that authoritative parenting has a stronger predictive contribution within the model, while peer support remains an important social factor. These findings highlight the importance of involving families and schools in creating social environments that support adolescents’ academic motivation.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/s42452-026-09608-8.title: Efficient latent-vision enabled generative data augmented pipeline for medical image analysis with hybrid deep learning approach
doi:10.1007/s42452-026-09608-8.abstract: Medical image analysis is an important process involved in diagnosing diseases, but a lack of data, class imbalance, and poor interpretability of deep learning models hamper it. In this study, these problems are overcome by proposing a hybrid generative data-augmented method for the classification of breast cancer and brain tumors using Vision Transformer (ViT) based learning. The proposed method uses Latent Diffusion Model (LDM)-based augmentation, EfficientNetV2 for extracting features from medical images, selection of important features through the Attention-based Feature Selection (AFS) technique, and use of Transformer networks for classification. The proposed model is evaluated by applying it to two datasets, CBIS (Curated Breast Imaging Subset of DDSM)- Digital Database for Screening Mammography (DDSM) and Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS2020), using a leakage-free patient-wise split method and a multi-run validation process. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves excellent performance with 96.54% accuracy on BraTS and 96.23% on CBIS-DDSM, and F1 scores of 96.40% and 96.11%, respectively, along with Receiver Operating Characteristic – Area Under the Curve (ROC AUC) scores of 0.999 for both datasets. Quality of the augmentation process can be validated through the Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) score that ranges between 0.82 and 0.91, as well as through the Dice score ranging between 0.78 and 0.89, which means structural information is successfully preserved during the training process. Statistical validation, it can confirm low variance within the dataset as well as significant improvements achieved when compared to state-of-the-art models. Incorporation of interpretability with the help of Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) contributes towards increased clinical relevancy by identifying tumor areas.

doi:10.1186/s40001-026-05318-4.title: Brain structure age in obstructive sleep apnea: a cross-sectional deep learning analysis
doi:10.1186/s40001-026-05318-4.abstract: Brain-age methods may summarize structural variation, but it is unclear whether brain structure age (BSA) differs between adults with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and controls. We tested global and region-specific BSA differences and associations with clinical measures. This cross-sectional observational analysis included 45 treatment-naive adults with OSA and 45 healthy controls. Participants underwent T1-weighted 3 T MRI and Montreal Cognitive Assessment; OSA participants additionally underwent polysomnography. Images were processed with the volBrain BrainStructureAges pipeline. The primary analysis compared global BSA between groups. Regional comparisons and clinical/polysomnographic correlations were secondary analyses, with Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction applied within each family. A sensitivity regression adjusted the global BSA comparison for chronological age, sex, and BMI. Global BSA did not differ significantly between groups (49.94 ± 11.98 years in OSA vs. 46.89 ± 11.75 years in controls; mean difference, 3.05 years; 95% CI, − 1.92 to 8.02; p = 0.226). The adjusted OSA group effect was 2.05 years (95% CI, −0.67 to 4.78; p = 0.138). Of 125 regional comparisons, 16 had nominal unadjusted p < 0.05, but none survived FDR correction (minimum q = 0.248). Global BSA was nominally associated with Epworth Sleepiness Scale score ( n = 34, r = 0.424, p = 0.013) and REM latency ( n = 34, r = −0.388, p = 0.023), but neither survived FDR correction across 15 clinical/polysomnographic correlations ( q = 0.175 for both). In this cohort, global BSA did not differ between OSA and controls, and no regional or clinical/polysomnographic association remained significant after multiplicity correction. The findings provide no evidence that BSA distinguishes OSA from controls or functions as a clinical biomarker for OSA. Larger longitudinal studies with polysomnography-confirmed controls are needed to determine whether smaller effects were missed.

doi:10.1007/978-3-032-37682-4_13.title: Interval Estimation in Water Distribution Systems Using Physics-Informed Graph Neural Networks
doi:10.1007/978-3-032-37682-4_13.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence in general and Machine Learning (ML) in particular has the potential to play a key role in critical infrastructure such as Water Distribution Systems (WDSs). In the face of urban population growth, ML can pave the way towards smart cities by not only solving various tasks in WDSs but also dealing with emerging uncertainties in WDSs. For instance, demands can be subject to uncertainty intervals and pipe attributes may vary over time. This study presents a novel physics-informed Graph Neural Network (GNN) based model for WDSs that predicts output feature intervals, given the input feature intervals. A comprehensive training scheme is developed to map multiple input intervals to the corresponding multiple output intervals. To address the varying ranges and magnitudes of state variables in WDSs, we introduce a theoretically grounded, reversible, and physics-preserving data normalization method. The proposed model demonstrates strong performance across five WDS datasets, achieving results comparable to those of the computationally intensive Monte Carlo sampling method.</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s12894-026-02345-5.title: Treatment-specific prediction of stone-free outcomes after SWL and RIRS using machine learning
doi:10.1186/s12894-026-02345-5.abstract: Predicting treatment success after shock wave lithotripsy (SWL) and retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) remains challenging. We aim to develop and validate treatment-specific machine learning models for predicting short-term stone-free outcomes following shock wave lithotripsy (SWL) and retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) using routinely available non-contrast CT (NCCT) parameters. A two-stage study was conducted. In the retrospective phase, 324 adult patients treated with SWL or RIRS for upper urinary tract stones were analyzed. Demographic variables and NCCT-derived stone characteristics, including size, volume, density, and heterogeneity, were used to train supervised machine learning models. Fifteen algorithms were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, and the best-performing model for each treatment modality was selected. In the prospective phase, model performance was tested in an independent cohort of 40 patients (20 SWL, 20 RIRS). Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis was applied to provide interpretability by quantifying the direction and relative contribution of individual CT-derived features to treatment-specific predictions. The CatBoost model demonstrated the highest predictive performance for SWL outcomes (accuracy 0.85, AUC 0.89), while Random Forest performed best in the RIRS cohort (accuracy 0.84, AUC 0.90). Mean stone density (Hounsfield units) and stone geometry (long edge for SWL, vertical edge for RIRS) emerged as the most influential predictors. In the prospective cohort, all SWL cases and 95% of RIRS cases were correctly classified. Patients undergoing RIRS exhibited larger stone size, greater volume, and a higher prevalence of challenging stone locations, reflecting confounding by indication in treatment allocation. Treatment-specific machine learning models using routinely available NCCT parameters promising predictive performance in estimating post-procedural stone-free outcomes after SWL and RIRS, though results require validation in larger prospective cohorts before clinical implementation. The integration of SHAP-based interpretability enhances clinical applicability, supporting their role as adjunctive tools for individualized patient counseling and expectation management rather than treatment selection.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1964406.title: HSV-Net: hybrid state-space and self-supervised vision fusion with progressive contour learning for CT pulmonary nodule segmentation
doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1964406.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Accurate voxel-level segmentation of pulmonary nodules on chest CT is needed for diameter and volume measurement, growth tracking, and quantitative assessment in lung cancer screening. The task remains difficult: nodules vary in attenuation, size, and contact with vessels or pleura, and clinically relevant morphology often lies in a thin, ambiguous margin. Existing systems commonly trade contour fidelity for speed—large prompt-driven foundation models can be accurate but slow, whereas compact CNN or SSM decoders are efficient yet tend to smooth spiculated and ground-glass borders. We propose HSV-Net (Hybrid State-space–Vision Network), a dual-stream 3D network that is prompt-free
                    <jats:italic>after</jats:italic>
                    nodule localization: an
                    <jats:italic>SSM3D</jats:italic>
                    stream provides whole-patch context with linear-complexity state-space blocks, and an
                    <jats:italic>OrthoLoRA</jats:italic>
                    stream adapts frozen DINOv2 features on axial, coronal, and sagittal slices. A Hybrid Gated Mixer (HGM) fuses the two streams before FPN decoding, and Progressive Contour Learning (PCL) supervises overlap, signed-distance-field geometry, and uncertainty-weighted contour refinement. On a 10-patient QIN Lung CT/QIN-LungCT-Seg development subset (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                    = 12 tumors; nested patient-level 5-fold CV), HSV-Net obtained the highest mean Dice (90.1% ± 1.0%; 95% CI [88.9, 91.3]) and Boundary F1 (86.3% ± 1.3%) among the compared methods on 128 × 128 × 64 patches, with a latency of 58 ms. A standard full-volume nnU-Net v2 baseline reached 88.6% ± 1.0% Dice on the same QIN folds, still below HSV-Net. On an independent LIDC-IDRI benchmark with expert volumetric consensus masks (186 patients/294 nodules; patient-level 5-fold CV within LIDC, not QIN→LIDC transfer), HSV-Net achieved 87.8% ± 1.1% Dice and 83.6% ± 1.3% Boundary F1, outperforming full-volume nnU-Net (87.1% ± 1.0% Dice). LUNA16 was retained only as a proxy size/localization check with diameter-matched spherical references, not as contour external validation.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.1002/rnc.70769.title: Observer‐Based Adaptive Sliding Mode Control for Fuzzy Markov Jump Systems Subject to Deception Attacks: A Q‐Learning Event‐Triggered Communication Protocol
doi:10.1002/rnc.70769.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This article addresses the secure control problem for nonlinear Markov jump systems subject to communication constraints and false data injection attacks. The Takagi–Sugeno (TS) fuzzy model is employed to describe the systems under consideration, and the Q‐learning concept is utilized to enhance the dynamic event‐triggered mechanisms (DETM) and reduce network load without compromising control performance. The main contribution of this work lies in designing an adaptive fuzzy sliding mode observer (SMO) with mismatched premise variables to estimate compromised system states and in synthesizing a sliding mode controller (SMC) to maintain the stochastic stability of the closed‐loop system while guaranteeing the reachability of the sliding‐mode dynamics. Moreover, a feasible solution algorithm based on a Real‐Valued Genetic Algorithm (RVGA) is proposed to synthesize the controller and observer gains and to optimize system performance. Finally, extensive simulations on the Chua chaotic system are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8074-2.ch003.title: Leadership, Identity, and Belonging in Times of Change
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8074-2.ch003.abstract: <jats:p>As educational institutions and organizations bring together Baby Boomers, Generation X, Millennials, and Generation Z, leaders must navigate generational difference while fostering trust, belonging, and shared purpose. Grounded in transformational leadership, this chapter frames leadership as a relational and developmental process that supports identity formation, equity, and organizational sustainability. Drawing on self authorship, challenge and support, and sense of belonging, it explores how leaders create environments where individuals across generations develop leadership capacity and see themselves as contributors. Through applied examples, the chapter highlights leadership identity development, mentorship, succession, and navigating resistance during change. It concludes with implications for leadership development and the future of work, emphasizing inclusive, adaptive, and people centered leadership.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/make8100317.title: Bridge-Aware Reinforced Compositional Exploration and Decomposition for Biomedical Multi-Hop Answering
doi:10.3390/make8100317.abstract: <jats:p>Biomedical question answering requires multi-hop reasoning over implicit relationships—e.g., identifying gene-associated diseases to retrieve target drugs. However, closed-book frontier language models achieve only ~14.57% precision on two-hop queries under single-answer prompting and answers drawn from parametric knowledge lack verifiable evidence, limiting their clinical utility. In this paper, we propose Bridge-Aware Reinforced Compositional Exploration and Decomposition (BRACED). A planner trained with Group-Relative Policy Optimization emits sub-queries, and a deterministic type-aware two-hop traversal over PrimeKG converts them into an answer set, so every returned entity is traceable to a graph path. On the BioHopR benchmark, BRACED reaches micro-F1 0.4241 and macro-F1 0.6381, improving over supervised fine-tuning of the same planner by 30.2%. With retrieval and the cap held fixed, five backbones of 1.7B–8B finish within 0.0034 of one another and BRACED reaches its result with one language-model call per question, from a 7B open-weight model that runs on the premises. Two typed hops already reach 95.1% of gold answers on this PrimeKG-derived benchmark: performance is bounded by candidate selection under the cap, not by decomposition quality.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11257052/v1.title: Advanced Portfolio Optimization: Integrating Classical Frameworks with Machine Learning and Modern Asset Allocation
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11257052/v1.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive evaluation of modern portfolio management methodologies, bridging the gap between classical foundational frameworks and cutting-edge computational intelligence. We begin by reviewing traditional asset allocation models, specifically the Markowitz Mean-Variance optimization framework, to anchor the core mathematical trade-offs between risk and expected return. Recognizing the practical limitations of classical frameworks—such as extreme sensitivity to input parameters and estimation errors—we systematically explore advanced allocation techniques. These include the Black-Litterman model, probabilistic scenario optimization, prospect theory, the Kelly criterion, and risk parity frameworks across diverse asset classes. Beyond traditional extensions, this research integrates advanced econometrics and machine learning algorithms to enhance predictive accuracy and portfolio robustness. We investigate the application of deep neural networks for asset return forecasting, genetic algorithms for heuristic constraint optimization, information theory for feature selection, and reinforcement learning for dynamic, multi-period policy execution. Through rigorous mathematical formalization and robust Python implementations, this paper demonstrates how combining statistical machine learning with behavioral and probabilistic asset allocation paradigms yields superior risk-adjusted performance in highly volatile market regimes. JEL Classification: G11, C45, C61, C63.

Rather than focusing on the disadvantages of these differences, as discussed in this paper, they are seen as opportunities for everyone to learn from one another and to utilize their knowledge. For instance, older leaders can provide a deep understanding of the business, its history, etc., whereas younger employees can provide new ideas, technology, and solutions to problems. By working as a team and making decisions in a group, individuals can develop leadership skills in these environments. However, at times, these leadership, communication, and expectation differences may lead to conflicts. As discussed in this paper, dialogue, trust, and learning from one another can play crucial roles in leadership for all generations.</jats:p>

doi:10.29060/taps.2026-11-4/oa3941.title: Investigating mental rehearsal’s applicability in guiding independent e-learning of eye examination skills during the pandemic – Part II (IMAGINE-II)
doi:10.29060/taps.2026-11-4/oa3941.abstract:
<jats:p>Introduction: Guided Mental Rehearsal (GMR), underpinned by the Theory of Motor Simulation, supports the learning of psychomotor skills. We hypothesised that (a) GMR is comparable to Guided Physical Practice (GPP) for learning Pupillary Examination (PE), and (b) Mental Imagery (MI) ability improves GMR practice.
Methods: This assessor-blinded, randomised controlled study included 53 pre-clinical students (GMR n=26, GPP n=27), with sample size calculated from pilot data (n=46, power=0.81, alpha=0.05). On day 1, baseline MI ability was assessed, followed by PE instruction. Subjects were practiced at week 1 and 3. PE performance and MI ability were reassessed using a checklist score sheet (month-1) and the Movement Imagery Questionnaire-3 (month-2). 
Results: Data is presented as median with interquartile range. The Mann-Whitney U test showed no significant differences in PE performance between GMR and GPP at month-1 (35.00 [14.00] vs. 33.25 [12.00], p=0.91) and 2 (40.00 [10.50] vs. 36.42 [12.00], p=0.50). In the GMR group, PE scores improved from month-1 to 2 (35.00 [14.00] vs. 40.00 [10.50], p=0.02, Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test). The Friedman test, followed by a post-hoc Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test with Bonferroni adjustment, indicated improved MI ability across baseline, month-1, and month-2 (Kinaesthetic Visualisation: 22.00 [8.00] vs. 23.00 [7.00] vs. 24.00 [6.00], p<0.01; External Visualisation: 24.00 [5.00] vs. 25.00 [6.00] vs. 26.00 [4.00], p=0.36), which was not observed in the GPP group.
Conclusion: Repeated GMR and GPP had no significantly different teaching outcomes, and MI ability improved with deliberate GMR practice. GMR may confer potential cost advantages with its hypothesised operational efficacy gains as an adjunct for teaching clinical examination skills.</jats:p>

doi:10.1021/acs.jchemed.6c00616.title: Transforming a Physical Card Game into a Browser-Based Learning Tool: AI-Assisted Digitization of Compound Chain
doi:10.1021/acs.jchemed.6c00616.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study reports the AI-assisted transformation of Compound Chain, a validated physical inorganic chemistry card game, into a browser-based learning application. The development used a “vibe coding” approach, in which educators describe functionality in natural language while an LLM generates and refines the code. We propose a five-step Pedagogical System Architect framework, intended for chemistry educators without programming experience, that covers architectural planning, data design, incremental implementation, AI-assisted debugging, and version control. The digital version extends the original game through automated rule enforcement, a zoom interface, and single-player mode, in a manner consistent with reduced extraneous cognitive load, and supporting self-regulated practice beyond class. In an exploratory classroom deployment, voluntary out-of-class usage (a self-reported approximation of 4.5 sessions per student) suggests that the digital format can transform a classroom activity into an intrinsically motivated practice resource. This exploratory evaluation documents engagement, usability, and voluntary practice; establishing conceptual learning gains from the digital version remains a question for future controlled study.</jats:p>

doi:10.1201/9781003542834-9.abstract: A stroke results in a serious disability due to sudden disruption in blood flow to the brain, which may cause fatal outcomes and is considered as the topmost cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide. The competence of artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning and for stroke detection using data from different sources such as EHRs, EEG, and MRI have been explored in this chapter. Different types of CNN and deep learning models are analyzed to classify various data types along with the identification of stroke signatures. The various advantages which are related with the AI based stroke detection such as timely and faster diagnosis leading to early treatment and higher accuracy which surpasses the traditional methods. Even the chances for remote patient monitoring have been increased due to AI which also has paved the way for incorporating AI in clinical environments without causing any disruption to current healthcare practices. Further, this chapter discusses the potential of using AI in personalized medicine where the risk assessment and treatment plans for the patient can be based on the medical history of the patient. The chapter further discusses about the long term efficacy of using AI models with the ongoing learning by making use of advances in medical knowledge and access to the data. This chapter ensures to guide the researchers and medical professionals with the deep understanding of using deep learning and AI for stroke diagnosis by exploring the potential benefits, challenges and future outlook for the methodology for early store detection.

doi:10.23876/j.krcp.26.020.title: Machine learning predicts major adverse kidney and cardiovascular events in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
doi:10.23876/j.krcp.26.020.abstract: Background: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) links to adverse kidney and cardiovascular events. However, current machine learning (ML)-based algorithms do not include comprehensive echocardiographic features or predict adverse kidney outcomes. Methods: We built ML models to predict 3-year all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and major adverse kidney events (MAKE) in retrospective HFrEF cohorts. Models were developed from 1,486 patients at Taipei Veterans General Hospital during 2011-2018 and externally validated in 246 patients from the heart-failure-post-acute-care program at Taichung Veterans General Hospital during 2020-2023. Model performance was compared to the traditional Meta-Analysis Global Group in Chronic Heart Failure score (MAGGIC), Logistic Regression (LR), and Kidney-Failure-Risk-Equation (KFRE). Results: For mortality, Ensemble had the highest area under receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROC, 0.863; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.814-0.913; p < 0.001), outperforming MAGGIC (AUROC, 0.741; 95% CI, 0.673-0.810) with net reclassification index (NRI) of 0.294 (95% CI, 0.147-0.440; p = 0.001). For MACE, Ensemble (AUROC, 0.816; 95% CI, 0.769-0.864; p < 0.001) surpassed LR (AUROC, 0.734; 95% CI, 0.677-0.791). For MAKE, Ensemble (AUROC, 0.858; 95% CI, 0.806-0.910; p < 0.001) exceeded KFRE (AUROC, 0.647; 95% CI, 0.560-0.735) with NRI of 0.267 (95% CI, 0.133-0.396; p < 0.001). External validation confirmed good Ensemble discrimination (AUROCs of 0.803, 0.808, and 0.859 for mortality, MACE, and MAKE, respectively). An online tool (https://vghhfrefai.com/) was created for application. Conclusion: Ensemble ML models with detailed clinical and echocardiographic features surpassed conventional risk scores, enabling early detection of major adverse cardiorenal events among HFrEF.

doi:10.14802/jmd.26140.title: Home-based visual perceptual learning improves contrast sensitivity in Parkinson’s disease: a proof-of-concept study
doi:10.14802/jmd.26140.abstract: Purpose: To assess whether visual perceptual learning (VPL) enhances contrast sensitivity function (CSF) in Parkinson's disease (PD); as a secondary exploratory aim, to describe whether the two protocols targeting different spatial frequency ranges produced differential effects. Methods: Seventeen patients with PD were randomized to two VPL protocols using dichoptic Gabor patch video-games for 30 minutes/day, six days/week, over 8 weeks. The M-H group trained at 8-16 cpd and the L-M group at 0.5-2 cpd. CSF was measured at baseline, 2, 4, and 8 weeks. BCVA and VIPD-Q were assessed at baseline and 8 weeks. Results: Significant progressive improvements in CSF were observed across all spatial frequencies and in the area under the log CSF curve from 1 month of training (p<0.001). VIPD-Q scores improved significantly in both groups (p=0.02 and p=0.008, respectively). Conclusions: Home based VPL was associated with significant improvements in CSF in PD; however, the absence of a control group means that these findings remain preliminary.

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8074-2.ch004.title: Reimagining Leadership for Generational Equity
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8074-2.ch004.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter introduces Generational Equity Leadership Theory (GELT), an equity-oriented framework for intergenerational leadership that synthesizes intergenerational justice philosophy, inclusive leadership scholarship, critical age studies, and organizational temporality research. Grounded in a critical realist ontology and an intersectional analytic, GELT treats generational location as causally consequential without reifying cohorts into fixed types. It advances three constructs—temporal stewardship, generational reflexivity, and equitable knowledge ecology—organized through Fraser's account of distributive, recognitional, and representational justice. The chapter specifies the tensions among them, proposes observable indicators, and presents a process model with practical implications.</jats:p>

doi:10.29060/taps.2026-11-4/oa4042.title: Innovative teaching-learning methods of pandemic module: A qualitative needs assessment in India
doi:10.29060/taps.2026-11-4/oa4042.abstract:
<jats:p>Introduction: COVID-19 pandemic has underscored critical deficits in global health preparedness. Traditional lecture-based teaching is frequently criticised for its limited effectiveness in practical skills required for real-world crisis response, creating significant "readiness gap". Hence, this study was done to evaluate perceived necessity and importance of innovative teaching-learning methods for the pandemic module amongst medical undergraduates.
Methods: Qualitative needs assessment was conducted using an interpretive description approach to explore stakeholder perspectives regarding the existing pandemic management teaching module and public health preparedness training within the undergraduate Community Medicine curriculum. Three focus group discussions were held with 28 purposively sampled participants at tertiary care teaching hospital, comprising faculty from Community Medicine (n=10), medical students who had completed pandemic training (n=10), and students awaiting training (n=8). Data were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using manual thematic analysis.
Results: Analysis identified four central themes. First, profound theory-practice gap in existing teaching, inadequately preparing students for real-world scenarios. Second, simulation and gamification were widely endorsed as promising, engaging solutions for teaching complex skills like outbreak investigation. Third, significant implementation barriers were anticipated, including resource limitations (time, technology), faculty capacity gaps, and need for cultural contextualisation. Fourth, stakeholders advocated for fundamental shift in assessment strategy towards practical, formative methods like OSCEs and peer feedback to align with innovative teaching.
Conclusion: This study provides clear, stakeholder-driven mandate for transforming pandemic module through experiential learning. While simulation and gamification are seen as viable solutions, successful integration requires structured approach addressing faculty development, resource allocation, co-design with stakeholders and realigned assessment framework.</jats:p>

doi:10.63671/ijsesr.v2i4.171.title: A Framework for Real-Time Phishing Resource Locator Detection Using Structural and Lexical Feature Analysis Based on Machine Learning
doi:10.63671/ijsesr.v2i4.171.abstract: <jats:p>Phishing attacks remains a leading, rapidly evolving threat in cybersecurity domain, where cyber-criminals deploy fraudulent websites that are deceptive in nature acts exactly same as legitimate platforms to transfer sensitive user credentials, financial data and corporate data to an external location. Traditional counter measures including blacklist-based systems and rule-based filters demonstrates limited efficiency against newly created malicious URLs and real-time generated phishing URLs. This paper presents PhishGuard+, a random forest-based phishing detection framework that performs real-time suspicious URL classification through complete structural and lexical feature analysis of the URL. The proposed system utilizes a dataset of 10,000 labeled URLs, from which 48 distinct features are extracted that includes URL patterns, domain characteristics, and heuristic indicators. A Random Forest classifier is trained on preprocessed data comprises min-max normalization and the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to address skewed data distribution. The trained model is deployed with a Flask-based RESTful API, that real-time inference through an interactive web interface. Experimental evaluation demonstrates an overall classification accuracy of 98.4%, with precision and recall exceeding 98% across both phishing and legitimate URL categories. The proposed framework offers a computationally efficient, low latency lightweight detection solution deployable in browser extensions, email security gateways, and corporate cybersecurity infrastructures, providing robust early-warning capabilities without requiring full webpage content analysis.</jats:p>
doi:10.63671/ijsesr.v2i4.171.venue: International Journal of Science and Engineering Science Research

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-73342-9.title: Deep learning-based segmentation of choroid plexus calcification on quantitative susceptibility mapping: a feasibility study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-73342-9.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Choroid plexus calcification (CPC) is a common age-related imaging finding associated with neuroinflammation and cognitive decline. Its accurate quantification remains challenging on computed tomography (CT), the current clinical gold standard, due to concerns regarding ionizing radiation exposure. Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) offers a non-invasive, radiation-free alternative for accurate assessment, but manual segmentation is impractical for large cohorts. We developed a deep learning-based framework for automated CPC segmentation using QSM. Using data from 106 subjects, we trained nnU-Net v2 models to evaluate input combinations comprising QSM, 3D T1-weighted images, and choroid plexus (CP) masks. The automated pipeline achieved its highest segmentation accuracy using QSM with CP and CPC masks and the strongest volumetric correlation with manual ground-truth annotations (
                    <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                     = 0.964) using both QSM and T1-weighted images. QSM-derived CPC volumes were strongly correlated with CT-derived volumes in a validation subset of 22 subjects (
                    <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                     = 0.728). In an additional cohort of 91 subjects, the framework revealed age-related changes in CPC, with volume increasing and susceptibility values becoming more diamagnetic with age. This framework provides a tool for direct CPC quantification on QSM that shows strong correspondence with CT-derived volumes, enabling large-scale, longitudinal investigations into the clinical implications of CPC.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.1142/s0219686728500394.title: Modal-Validated Topology Optimization of a Vertical Grinding Machine and Predictive Diagnostics
doi:10.1142/s0219686728500394.abstract: <jats:p>Finite element analysis (FEA) is used to investigate the modal characteristics of a vertical grinding machine, with the aim of aligning simulation conditions with real-world phenomena. Experiments were conducted using a percussion hammer, accelerometer, and spectrum analyzer to validate the findings. The analysis covered a frequency range of 1Hz to 300Hz, identifying structural frequencies of 64.3Hz, 93.4Hz, and 214.2Hz through simulation, and 76.8Hz, 87.0Hz, and 248.0Hz from experiments. Experimental data, processed using NOVIAN spectrum analysis software for fast Fourier transforms (FFT), provided detailed insights into frequency response functions, spectra, and correlations. An impact hammer with an ultra-soft rubber tip generated excitation, and the accelerometer captured the structural response. Simulation matched experiment within 16.2%, 7.3%, and 13.6% for the first three modes, and within 7.7%, 1.7%, and 0.3% against ODS measurements. Component-level topology optimization under a 90% volume constraint then reduced machine mass by 39.5 kg (2.4%), lowered spindle-to-worktable deformation from 19.2 μm to 18.6 μm (3.1%), and raised the first three natural frequencies by 8.7%, 19.5%, and 5.7%; the base alone contributed 33.5 kg (3.9%) while gaining 38.4% in first-mode frequency. Shifting the second mode from 93.4 Hz to 111.6 Hz widens the margin against 6000 rpm spindle excitation from 6.6% to 11.6%, and a PCA-GMM diagnostic system distinguished healthy from abnormal spindle states.</jats:p>

doi:10.51878/academia.v6i4.15772.title: PENGEMBANGAN MULTIMEDIA GAMIFIKASI INTERAKTIF BERBASIS MODEL DISCOVERY LEARNING UNTUK MENINGKATKAN PEMAHAMAN KONSEP PESERTA DIDIK PADA MATA PELAJARAN INFORMATIKA DI SMP N 1 KUTA SELATAN
doi:10.51878/academia.v6i4.15772.abstract:
<jats:p>Conceptual understanding is the most important aspect in informatics learning. However, learning that is still dominated by conventional material delivery causes conceptual understanding to not develop optimally. This study aims to develop interactive gamification multimedia based on discovery learning that is valid, practical, and effective in improving students' conceptual understanding in Informatics subjects in grade VII of junior high school. This study uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the ADDIE model which includes the stages of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. The research subjects consisted of content experts, media experts, design experts, Informatics subject teachers, and grade VII students at SMP N 1 Kuta Selatan. Data were collected through validation sheets, teacher and student response questionnaires, and pretest-posttest tests to measure conceptual understanding. Data analysis was carried out descriptively and inferentially using paired sample t-tests, N-gain calculations, and effect size. The results showed that the developed multimedia was categorized as very valid based on the assessment of content, media, and design experts, and very practical based on teacher and student responses. The results of the effectiveness test using a paired sample t-test showed a significant difference between the pretest and posttest scores (p<0.05), with an N-gain value of 0.62 (moderate category) and an effect size of 2.17, indicating a significant influence on improving conceptual understanding. Thus, interactive gamification multimedia based on discovery learning is proven to be suitable for use in strengthening students' conceptual understanding in Informatics learning.
ABSTRAK
Pemahaman konsep merupakan aspek yang paling penting dalam pembelajaran informatika. Namun, pembelajaran yang masih didominasi oleh penyampaian materi secara konvensional menyebabkan pemahaman konsep belum berkembang secara optimal. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan multimedia gamifikasi interaktif berbasis discovery learning yang valid, praktis, dan efektif dalam meningkatkan pemahaman konsep peserta didik pada mata pelajaran Informatika kelas VII SMP. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode Research and Development (R&D) dengan model ADDIE yang meliputi tahap analisis, desain, pengembangan, implementasi, dan evaluasi. Subjek penelitian terdiri atas ahli isi, ahli media, ahli desain, guru mata pelajaran Informatika, dan peserta didik kelas VII di SMP N 1 Kuta Selatan. Data dikumpulkan melalui lembar validasi, angket respons guru dan peserta didik, serta tes pretest-posttest untuk mengukur pemahaman konsep. Analisis data dilakukan secara deskriptif dan inferensial menggunakan uji paired sample t-test, perhitungan N-gain, dan effect size. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa multimedia yang dikembangkan berada pada kategori sangat valid berdasarkan penilaian ahli isi, media, dan desain, serta sangat praktis berdasarkan respons guru dan peserta didik. Hasil uji efektivitas menggunakan paired sample t-test menunjukkan perbedaan yang signifikan antara skor pretest dan posttest (p<0,05), dengan nilai N-gain sebesar 0,62 (kategori sedang) dan effect size sebesar 2,17 yang menunjukkan pengaruh yang besar terhadap peningkatan pemahaman konsep. Dengan demikian, multimedia gamifikasi interaktif berbasis discovery learning terbukti layak digunakan untuk memperkuat pemahaman konsep peserta didik dalam pembelajaran Informatika.
 
 </jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1973760.title: Transcriptomics-guided serum podoplanin and interpretable machine learning for early risk stratification of necrotizing enterocolitis in preterm infants
doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1973760.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To evaluate podoplanin (PDPN) as a circulating biomarker for early necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) risk stratification and to determine whether an interpretable machine-learning framework integrating PDPN with prediagnostic clinical and inflammatory variables could improve individualized risk estimation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PDPN expression was examined in two public NEC intestinal transcriptomic datasets. Serum PDPN was then measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in a nested case-control cohort of 132 preterm infants (66 with NEC and 66 gestational-age- and birth-weight-matched controls). All candidate predictors were obtained before NEC onset in cases and before the matched reference time in controls. Restricted cubic spline, receiver operating characteristic, precision-recall, LASSO, multivariable logistic regression, 11 machine-learning algorithms, SHAP, and nomogram analyses were performed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PDPN was upregulated in NEC intestinal tissue. Serum concentrations were higher in infants who developed NEC than in controls (48.36 ± 22.89 vs 19.75 ± 6.26 ng/mL, P &lt; 0.001) and in Bell stage III than in Bell stage II NEC [69.43 (58.91–77.95) vs 30.59 (24.06–42.79) ng/mL, P &lt; 0.001]. PDPN correlated weakly with the C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.905 and an area under the precision-recall curve of 0.925, and remained independently associated with NEC after multivariable adjustment. CatBoost showed the most favorable internal performance among 11 models, with PDPN as the leading SHAP contributor. The nomogram achieved an internally assessed area under the curve of 0.974.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Prediagnostic serum PDPN, particularly when combined with routinely available variables, may support early individualized NEC risk stratification. Prospective multicenter validation and mechanistic studies are warranted.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.17977/um065.v7.i4.2027.3.title: Differentiated Instruction as Proactive Classroom Management in Early Childhood Science Learning: A Multi-Site Qualitative Case Study
doi:10.17977/um065.v7.i4.2027.3.abstract: <jats:p>Early childhood classrooms are developmentally heterogeneous, making instruction and classroom management inseparable challenges. This study examined how differentiated instruction was enacted within science-based learning and how teachers perceived and managed the resulting classroom dynamics. A qualitative multi-site case study was conducted across four early childhood education institutions in Brebes Regency, Central Java, Indonesia. Participating teachers were purposively selected because they implemented differentiated instruction, used inquiry-oriented science activities, and had at least two years of early childhood teaching experience. Data were generated through non-participant classroom observations, semi-structured interviews, and analysis of daily lesson plans and instructional materials, then examined thematically. Three interconnected findings emerged. First, differentiation was enacted through adjusted task complexity, flexible grouping, varied hands-on activities, and responsive scaffolding. Second, these practices were associated with more sustained engagement, clearer routines and transitions, and less need for reactive behavior correction, suggesting that instructional design functioned as a form of proactive classroom management. Third, teacher competence and instructional flexibility supported implementation, whereas planning time and high teacher–child ratios constrained individualized support. The study proposes that differentiated science learning can support classroom management when differentiation, inquiry, routines, and responsive interaction are deliberately aligned. The findings offer implications for teacher professional learning, lesson planning, staffing, and inclusive early childhood practice.</jats:p>

doi:10.59992/ijci.2026.v5n10p1.title: Developing a Mehri–Arabic Neural Machine Translation System Using a Multilingual Transformer Model (mT5)
doi:10.59992/ijci.2026.v5n10p1.abstract: <jats:p>Machine translation for low-resource and endangered languages remains a challenging task due to the scarcity of parallel corpora and limited computational resources. Despite its linguistic and cultural significance, the Mehri language has received little attention in natural language processing research. This paper presents a Mehri–Arabic machine translation system based on a multilingual neural model. A custom Mehri–Arabic parallel corpus was constructed and preprocessed using rule-based techniques. The multilingual mT5 model was fine-tuned via transfer learning and evaluated using both automatic metrics and human assessment. Experimental results indicate that satisfactory Arabic translations can be achieved despite limited data availability. This work represents an early computational effort in Mehri– Arabic machine translation and highlights the potential of multilingual pretrained models for supporting under-resourced languages.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8074-2.ch005.title: An Ethical Discussion on Indian and Western Leadership Models in Higher Education
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8074-2.ch005.abstract: <jats:p>In this chapter, an exploration of the ethical aspects of leadership in both Indian and Western higher education systems is done based on their historical development and evolution, leadership model, and cultural impacts. It identifies similar values of integrity, vision, and commitment to education in both systems, and it discusses the similar ethical dilemmas, including finding a balance between interests of stakeholders, power dynamics management and achieving unfairness in decisions. This chapter compares the hierarchical leadership of India and the democratic decentralized models of the west with reference to the ethical significance of such structural differences. It offers the suggestions of coming up with hybrid leadership models where a synergy between the two traditions is arrived at to meet the challenges faced today like diversity, inclusion and technology. It, finally, promotes cross cultural education and good leadership standards to influence the future of institutions of higher learning.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8074-2.ch010.title: The Synergy of Experience and Innovation
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8074-2.ch010.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter advances an interdisciplinary framework by examining the Individualized Education Program (IEP) Team as a critical case study in intergenerational leadership, learning, and social identity. The IEP Team inherently embodies diverse generational cohorts whose collaboration directly impacts the child's educational outcomes and equity. We argue that the success of the IEP process depends on effective intergenerational dynamics, where leadership is shared rather than positional, and where mutual learning is essential for reconciling varied professional expertise and lived experiences. The authors analyze how the generational identities of team members mediate the exchange of knowledge and power, and how the team must foreground the child's identity to achieve true individualization and equity.</jats:p>
