doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1897946.title: A multidimensional analysis of generative AI adoption in academia: synthesizing TAM3 and UTAUT2 frameworks to predict students’ attitudes and learning effectiveness
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1897946.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools into higher education raises important questions regarding their impact on student learning. Based on established technology acceptance frameworks, this study develops and empirically tests an integrative model that explains students’ attitudes toward GenAI tools and their perceived learning effectiveness. Data were collected from 566 undergraduate students using a structured questionnaire. The main findings indicate that prior experience, perceived merits, and training in using GenAI tools are positively associated with and constitute strong predictors of both attitudes of students toward GenAI use and perceived learning effectiveness, while ethical knowledge and technological orientation do not emerge as significant predictors. Perceived drawbacks are also significant, suggesting that ambivalence and concerns about GenAI can diminish students’ positive attitudes and reduce their perceived usefulness. Differences across gender further suggest that technology adoption processes are not uniform but contingent upon user characteristics. Theoretically, this study contributes to the literature by extending technology acceptance models into the domain of GenAI and by linking attitudinal constructs with learning-related outcomes within a unified framework. Practically, the findings suggest that higher education institutions should not only provide access to GenAI tools but also complement this access with pedagogical support, including structured training, comprehensive ethical guidance, and the development of students’ GenAI literacy. Overall, the study provides a nuanced understanding of how GenAI tools are adopted and leveraged in academic contexts and offers a foundation for future research on GenAI-enabled learning.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1963429.title: Reconceptualizing outdoor geoscience learning for the generative AI era: a human-centered instructional model
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1963429.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) creates a distinctive problem for outdoor geoscience learning: it can broaden questioning and explanation, yet it can also pre-structure what learners notice and displace their interpretation of field evidence. Existing field-learning frameworks explain how conceptual, geographical, psychological, technical, and social novelty shape participation, but they do not fully explain this redistribution of epistemic work and authority. Extending established accounts of technological mediation to field settings, this Hypothesis and Theory article interprets GenAI as an epistemic reorganization of field inquiry rather than as technical novelty alone. It advances the central hypothesis that GenAI is more likely to augment, rather than displace, learners’ epistemic agency when it is introduced after direct observation and an initial learner interpretation, restricted to generating questions and candidate explanations, and subjected to human adjudication against field evidence. On this basis, the article proposes a six-stage human-centered model: preparing for field and GenAI use; attending to and recording field evidence; constructing an initial learner interpretation; engaging GenAI as a dialogic challenger; conducting human evidence-based adjudication; and completing reflective synthesis and epistemic accounting. Field evidence functions as an epistemic constraint, GenAI outputs remain provisional objects of scrutiny, and learners and teachers retain interpretive authority and responsibility. Six testable propositions specify expected effects of sequencing, initial interpretation, challenger-oriented prompting, explicit adjudication, substitution, and teacher orchestration. Operational criteria for distinguishing support, mediation, and substitution, and a thought experiment at a basalt outcrop, show how the model can be applied and tested. The model offers a falsifiable agenda for research in physical, hybrid, and virtual geoscience field learning while defining conditions under which GenAI use should be limited or withheld.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/s44163-026-02335-4.title: Pre-control scheme generation for extreme-weather power imbalance risk using multi-resource frequency regulation and deep reinforcement learning
doi:10.1007/s44163-026-02335-4.abstract: To address the power imbalance risk between renewable energy output and load demand under extreme weather conditions, this paper proposes a pre-control scheme generation method based on the integration of multiple frequency regulation resources and deep reinforcement learning. First, mechanism models for wind power and photovoltaic output, along with an hourly time-series energy storage model, are established to quantify the supply-demand imbalance risk under extreme weather scenarios. Second, a reward function embedded with active regulation flexibility physical rules is designed and incorporated into an improved deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm framework. During the policy update process, equipment operating boundary constraint penalties and flexibility incentives are introduced, and the physical consistency of the policy is enhanced through dynamic constraint construction, adaptive learning rate adjustment, and policy visualization. Third, based on the DDPG framework, an entropy-regularized twin-delayed network algorithm is incorporated, which employs a dynamic entropy term to enhance exploration capability and utilizes twin-delayed networks to mitigate overestimation of the value function. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a total cost of 120.6 CNY, a success rate of 94.7%, and a violation rate of 0.0% under extreme weather scenarios, all outperforming the comparative methods. Ablation experiments validate the synergistic contribution of each improved module, and visualization results further confirm the temporal rationality and boundary constraint compliance of the generated pre-control schemes.

doi:10.1161/circep.125.014659.title: Reclassifying Single Lead Sinus Rhythm ECGs for Improved AF Recurrence Detection With Deep Learning
doi:10.1161/circep.125.014659.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>BACKGROUND:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Atrial fibrillation (AF) remains a common outcome after catheter ablation, with recurrence observed in up to 50% of patients within 5 years. Despite extensive research, challenges remain in optimizing observation and prediction windows for AF recurrence assessment. Therefore, we developed and validated a novel deep learning model that reclassifies sinus rhythm based on past and future AF events using single-lead ECG strips from handheld devices.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>METHODS:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Of the 558 participants, 308 with no documented recurrence during study follow-up contributed Benign Sinus strips, while 250 with documented recurrence contributed sinus rhythm strips recorded within ±3 days of an AF event, defined as Severe Sinus strips. Both clinical feature-based models and a deep learning model were used to classify these ECGs according to their proximity to AF recurrence events. Performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>RESULTS:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The strip-level pretrained deep learning model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.86, with sensitivity of 0.79, and specificity of 0.76. The complementary participant-level clinical feature-based Random Forest benchmark achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.71, sensitivity of 0.58, and specificity of 0.69. Feature-based analyses identified associations involving heart-rate variability, mean R–R interval, female sex, left atrial volume, and mean P-wave duration.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>CONCLUSIONS:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our dynamic deep learning model reclassifies 30-second single-lead sinus rhythm ECGs based on AF events within ±3 days, transforming a brief ECG snapshot into a summarized indicator of short-term AF risk.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.51878/science.v6i4.15802.title: INTEGRASI MODEL PROBLEM BASED LEARNING DAN PENDEKATAN DEEP LEARNING TERHADAP KEMAMPUAN BERPIKIR KRITIS SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR PADA MATERI EKOSISTEM
doi:10.51878/science.v6i4.15802.abstract:
<jats:p>Substandard critical thinking skills among elementary school pupils are frequently triggered by teacher-dominated conventional instruction, which restricts opportunities for independent evaluation and synthesis. Prior scholarly investigations rarely addressed deep conceptual understanding through integrated problem-solving models in primary education, particularly concerning ecosystem topics. Therefore, this research is crucial for determining the empirical efficacy of integrating Problem Based Learning with a deep learning approach to elevate students' critical reasoning competencies. This quantitative study utilized a quasi-experimental non-equivalent control group design involving 52 fifth-graders at SD Negeri 021 Sungai Kunjang, divided into an experimental group (n=26) and a control group (n=26). Data were gathered via 15 validated multiple-choice test items administered across pre-test and post-test stages, subsequently analyzed using the non-parametric Mann-Whitney U test and normalized gain (N-gain) formulas. The results demonstrated no baseline discrepancy between groups (p=0.366), whereas post-intervention scores revealed a statistically significant divergence (p=0.005) with a moderate effect size (r=0.387) favoring the experimental class. This enhancement was substantiated by an experimental N-gain score of 0.33 (moderate category) compared to the control group’s minimal gain of 0.04 (low category). Consequently, embedding a deep learning framework into Problem Based Learning serves as an effective pedagogical catalyst for advancing primary school students' critical thinking faculties in ecosystem instruction.
ABSTRAK
Rendahnya kemampuan berpikir kritis siswa sekolah dasar kerap dipicu oleh pembelajaran konvensional yang didominasi oleh guru, sehingga membatasi kesempatan siswa dalam mengevaluasi dan menyintesis informasi secara mandiri. Penelitian terdahulu mengenai penggabungan model pemecahan masalah masih jarang menyentuh pemahaman konseptual mendalam pada jenjang pendidikan dasar, khususnya pada materi ekosistem. Oleh sebab itu, penelitian ini penting dilakukan guna menguji efektivitas integrasi model Problem Based Learning dan pendekatan deep learning dalam meningkatkan kemampuan bernalar kritis siswa. Penelitian kuantitatif ini menerapkan desain kuasi-eksperimen dengan rancangan non-equivalent control group design yang melibatkan 52 siswa kelas V SD Negeri 021 Sungai Kunjang, terbagi ke dalam kelas eksperimen (n=26) dan kelas kontrol (n=26). Data dikumpulkan melalui instrumen tes berpikir kritis berbentuk pilihan ganda sebanyak 15 butir valid dan reliabel yang diberikan melalui tahapan pre-test dan post-test, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji nonparametrik Mann-Whitney serta perhitungan skor perolehan ternormalisasi (N-gain). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kemampuan awal kedua kelompok tidak berbeda secara signifikan (p=0,366), namun pascaperlakuan menunjukkan perbedaan yang sangat signifikan (p=0,005) dengan nilai effect size sebesar 0,387 (kategori sedang) yang mengunggulkan kelas eksperimen. Capaian ini diperkuat oleh nilai rerata N-gain kelompok eksperimen sebesar 0,33 (kategori sedang), jauh melampaui kelompok kontrol yang hanya mencapai 0,04 (kategori rendah). Dengan demikian, integrasi pendekatan deep learning ke dalam model Problem Based Learning terbukti efektif sebagai katalisator dalam mengakselerasi keterampilan berpikir kritis siswa sekolah dasar pada topik ekosistem.
 </jats:p>

doi:10.51878/learning.v6i4.14086.title: KETERBACAAN BUKU TEKS GAYENG BASA JAWA KELAS X MENGGUNAKAN TEKNIK CLOZE TEST DI SMA AL-I’TISHOM BOARDING SCHOOL
doi:10.51878/learning.v6i4.14086.abstract:
<jats:p>The Gayeng Basa Jawa textbook serves as a primary instructional material for Javanese language learning at the senior high school level. However, its readability level and appropriateness for students in boarding school environments with diverse linguistic backgrounds have not been thoroughly examined. This study aims to analyze the readability level of texts in the Gayeng Basa Jawa textbook for tenth-grade students and describe its alignment with students' reading abilities at SMA Al-I'tishom Boarding School Grabag. The research employed a descriptive quantitative design utilizing the cloze test technique through a synonymy scoring approach. A total sampling technique was applied to recruit 17 tenth-grade students as respondents, with six Latin-script texts selected across six chapters serving as textual data. The cloze instruments omitted every third word mechanically regardless of grammatical function. The findings revealed that three texts fell into the instructional category, while the other three reached the independent level. The overall mean readability score was 58.9%, positioning the textbook within the instructional threshold. Consequently, the textbook is appropriate for classroom use, though active teacher mediation remains necessary to help students decipher unfamiliar archaic and borrowed vocabulary.
ABSTRAK
Buku teks Gayeng Basa Jawa merupakan salah satu bahan ajar utama dalam pembelajaran Bahasa Jawa di tingkat Sekolah Menengah Atas (SMA). Namun, kesesuaian tingkat keterbacaannya dengan kemampuan siswa di sekolah asrama dengan latar belakang bahasa ibu yang beragam belum banyak dikaji secara empiris. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis tingkat keterbacaan wacana dalam buku teks Gayeng Basa Jawa kelas X serta mendeskripsikan kesesuaiannya dengan kemampuan membaca siswa di SMA Al-I'tishom Boarding School Grabag. Metode yang digunakan adalah kuantitatif deskriptif dengan teknik cloze test menggunakan pendekatan synonymy methods. Pengambilan sampel dilakukan menggunakan teknik total sampling terhadap 17 siswa kelas X sebagai responden, dengan data berupa enam wacana beraksara Latin dari enam bab buku teks tersebut. Instrumen penelitian berupa tes rumpang yang melesapkan kata ketiga secara konsisten tanpa memperhatikan fungsi kata. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa tiga wacana berada pada tingkat instruksional dan tiga wacana berada pada tingkat independen. Rata-rata skor keterbacaan keseluruhan wacana adalah 58,9%, yang menempatkan buku teks ini pada kategori instruksional. Dengan demikian, buku teks ini layak digunakan sebagai bahan ajar, tetapi siswa tetap memerlukan pendampingan guru untuk memahami kosakata arkais dan istilah serapan yang belum familier.
 
 </jats:p>

doi:10.17158/eedrpa34.title: <b>Classroom Management of Teachers, Social-Emotional Competence, and Mathematics Learning Strategies of Students</b>
doi:10.17158/eedrpa34.abstract: <jats:p>Most secondary school students struggle to understand basic mathematical ideas and one potential reason for this problem is the failure to use appropriate strategies in learning mathematics. This study aimed to determine the influence of the classroom management of mathematics teachers and social-emotional competence on mathematics learning strategies of Grade 10 students. The study used adapted questionnaires. The descriptive correlation method was utilized in the research. Data were gathered from Grade 10 students at three selected public schools in Buhangin District, Davao City. These data were analyzed using the mean, standard deviation, and linear regression analysis. Both the two independent variables, classroom management of mathematics teachers and social-emotional competence, yielded a significant relationship to the mathematics learning strategies of students. Moreover, the mathematics learning strategies of Grade 10 students were influenced by the classroom management of mathematics teachers and the social-emotional competence of students.</jats:p>

doi:10.1080/14767724.2026.2741146.title: Voices quiet, bodies still: embodied governance of refugee learners through social and emotional learning
doi:10.1080/14767724.2026.2741146.abstract: This article examines social and emotional learning (SEL) in Education in Emergencies through critical embodiment theory. Drawing on interviews, ethnographic research, documentary materials, and six widely used EiE-SEL programmes, I trace recurring practices of bodily preparedness, impulse control, and emotional regulation. I argue that these practices reveal how humanitarian and educational governance can operate through the body by encouraging learners to regulate conduct, emotion, and expression. I develop a distinct conceptualisation of the embodiment of displacement to describe how institutional expectations attached to displaced status may become bodily enacted, negotiated, adapted, or resisted.

doi:10.1088/3049-4753/aeac30.title: Model architecture and calibration period sensitivity in controlled super-resolution reconstruction of near-surface air temperature
doi:10.1088/3049-4753/aeac30.abstract: Super-resolution reconstruction recovers fine-scale fields from coarse inputs, but its reliability across periods depends on whether relationships learned historically remain transferable. Using a controlled ERA5-Land 2-m temperature super-resolution reconstruction experiment over Africa, we compare U-Net, RCAN, SRCNN, XGBoost, and QDM trained on the 1950s, 1980s, and 2010s and evaluated on the same daily 2021–2025 data. In the multiyear evaluation, spatial convolutional models outperform the pixel-wise baseline, with U-Net achieving the lowest mean RMSE across calibration periods in every year. In percentile-based hot-context subsets, XGBoost exhibits substantially larger errors and stronger dependence on training-period recency. U-Net maintains the lowest error, while RCAN has smaller calibration-period spread than U-Net. QDM has the smallest spread but higher error than the unadjusted coarse input. Within this same-source reconstruction setting, calibration-period sensitivity is both model- and distribution-dependent: average performance can conceal failures in the hot tail, and model selection should evaluate calibration-period sensitivity and extreme-temperature behavior separately.

doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1947529.title: Development and internal validation of a predictive model for clinical deterioration in newly diagnosed lung cancer patients based on interpretable machine learning
doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1947529.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To develop and validate an interpretable machine learning–based model for the early identification of the risk of clinical deterioration during hospitalization in newly diagnosed lung cancer patients.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Clinical data of patients with newly diagnosed lung cancer admitted between July 2023 and December 2025 were retrospectively collected in this single-center study. A hybrid feature selection strategy integrating least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and the Boruta algorithm was employed to identify key predictors. Logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and support vector machine (SVM) models were constructed. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values were further applied to interpret the model's decision-making process.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A total of 1,001 newly diagnosed lung cancer patients were included, comprising 121 patients (12.1%) in the deterioration group and 880 patients (87.9%) in the non-deterioration group. Through the hybrid feature selection approach, five core predictive variables were identified, including Activities of Daily Living (ADL) score, lymphocyte count, C-reactive protein (CRP), respiratory rate, and neutrophil count. Among the models, the SVM model achieved the highest observed AUC of 0.822 (95% CI: 0.737–0.899) in the internal validation set, with a sensitivity of 0.750 (95% CI: 0.594–0.893) and a specificity of 0.792 (95% CI: 0.740–0.838). After Platt scaling calibration, the model achieved a Brier score of 0.083 (Hosmer-Lemeshow
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.649), with a calibration intercept of 0.141 and a slope of 1.126, indicating satisfactory agreement between predicted and observed risks. DCA suggested a potential net clinical benefit. SHAP analysis, in conjunction with multivariable regression results, consistently demonstrated that ADL score and lymphocyte count were associated with reduced risk of clinical deterioration, whereas CRP and neutrophil count were associated with increased risk.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The SVM model developed in this study may help identify patients at risk of clinical deterioration among hospitalized lung cancer patients and may assist healthcare professionals in achieving early risk identification and potential clinical decision support.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.31234/osf.io/bdnu2_v3.title: Caregivers’ multimodal actions scaffold word learning in the preschool years
doi:10.31234/osf.io/bdnu2_v3.abstract: Children learn language in face-to-face interactions with their caregivers where they are continuously exposed to multimodal input in which verbal content is combined with non-verbal signals (e.g., caregivers looking and pointing at an object while naming it). However, little is known about how caregivers’ use of the full range of multimodal behaviours is linked to children’s word learning. Using the ECOLANG Corpus, we examined how caregivers’ multimodal behaviours predict children’s word learning during a semi-naturalistic parent-child interaction. Thirty-seven caregivers (age: 29-48, 36 female; British and American English speakers) interacted with their child (age: 3-4, 19 female) talking about 12 unknown objects for 30 minutes. Caregivers’ verbal (e.g., label repetitions, speaking rate) and non-verbal (e.g., points, gaze, gestures) behaviours were annotated and used as predictors in regression analyses of children’s learning of the novel object labels along with child vocabulary scores. Results showed that, in the verbal domain, caregivers’ use of high pitch and more lexically diverse speech were associated with better word learning, while caregivers’ use of representational gestures was a significant non-verbal predictor. In particular, using more representational gestures when labelling unknown objects predicted better word learning specifically for children with lower vocabulary scores, suggesting that non-verbal cues such as manual gestures can provide additional support for children with less advanced linguistic abilities. This work presents the first comprehensive investigation of the combined role of verbal and non-verbal caregivers’ behaviours and provides robust evidence that multimodal caregiver communication can shape preschool-aged children’s lexical development.

doi:10.51878/learning.v6i4.15932.title: PEMBERDAYAAN GURU DALAM PEMBUATAN MODUL PEMBELAJARAN BERBASIS DEEP LEARNING MELALUI KOLABORASI GURU PADA MGMP BAHASA INDONESIA SE-KOTA PALANGKA RAYA
doi:10.51878/learning.v6i4.15932.abstract:
<jats:p>The implementation of the Deep Learning approach within the Kurikulum Merdeka framework requires teachers to design instructional modules that facilitate meaningful, mindful, and joyful learning experiences. However, a preliminary needs assessment among teachers in the Indonesian Language Subject Teachers' Consultation (MGMP) of Palangka Raya revealed that their pedagogical competence in embedding Deep Learning principles remained suboptimal. This community empowerment service aimed to improve teachers' professional competence through collaborative workshops and intensive mentoring in designing Deep Learning-based teaching modules. The intervention engaged 60 junior high school Indonesian language teachers through systematic stages comprising needs analysis, conceptual reinforcement, design workshops, clinical mentoring, peer review, product presentations, revisions, and evaluation. Program evaluation revealed an increase in conceptual comprehension scores from a pre-test average of 54.20 to a post-test average of 86.45, alongside a validation feasibility score of 88.75% (highly feasible category) for the developed modules. The tangible outputs comprise three complete Phase D Indonesian language teaching modules for Grades VII, VIII, and IX deposited in a digital cloud repository for instructional adoption. Consequently, this collaborative MGMP-based empowerment framework serves as an effective, sustainable capacity-building model adaptable to other teacher learning communities.
ABSTRAK
Penerapan Pembelajaran Mendalam (Deep Learning) dalam implementasi Kurikulum Merdeka menuntut guru memiliki keterampilan menyusun modul ajar yang mampu menghadirkan pengalaman belajar yang bermakna (meaningful), berkesadaran (mindful), dan menyenangkan (joyful). Berdasarkan analisis kebutuhan awal terhadap guru dalam Musyawarah Guru Mata Pelajaran (MGMP) Bahasa Indonesia Se-Kota Palangka Raya, kemampuan mengintegrasikan prinsip-prinsip pedagogis Deep Learning ke dalam modul ajar masih belum optimal. Pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan meningkatkan kompetensi profesional guru melalui lokakarya dan pendampingan penyusunan modul ajar berbasis Deep Learning secara kolaboratif. Program ini melibatkan 60 guru Bahasa Indonesia jenjang SMP dengan tahapan pelaksanaan meliputi analisis kebutuhan, penguatan konseptual, lokakarya perancangan, pendampingan intensif, peer review, presentasi produk, revisi, dan evaluasi. Evaluasi program menunjukkan peningkatan skor pemahaman konsep guru dari rata-rata pre-test sebesar 54,20 menjadi 86,45 pada post-test, serta capaian skor kelayakan modul ajar sebesar 88,75% (kategori sangat layak). Luaran nyata kegiatan berupa tiga modul ajar Bahasa Indonesia Fase D untuk kelas VII, VIII, dan IX yang terunggah dalam repositori digital dan siap diterapkan dalam pembelajaran. Dengan demikian, model pemberdayaan kolaboratif berbasis MGMP ini terbukti efektif dalam meningkatkan kompetensi profesional guru sekaligus berpotensi direplikasi pada komunitas belajar di daerah lain.
 
 </jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74710-1.title: Optimized hybrid machine learning for interpretable prediction of crack-healing percentage in self-healing concrete
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74710-1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Self-healing concrete can potentially repair cracks on its own; however, predicting its healing performance is challenging because of the complex interactions among mixture characteristics, crack properties, healing-agent content, and healing time. This research explores the use of machine learning methods to predict the crack-healing percentage of self-healing concrete and compares four modeling approaches: Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree optimized with Grey Wolf Optimization (DT + GWO), Artificial Neural Network optimized with Grey Wolf Optimization (ANN + GWO), and Least Squares Boosting optimized with Grey Wolf Optimization (LSBoost + GWO). A dataset of 1271 measurements was gathered from six independent studies, using initial crack width (ICW), mixture proportions, healing-agent content, and healing time as inputs, and crack-healing percentage as the output. Model performance was assessed using R, MSE, RMSE, MAE, MAD, and the a20 index, and 10-fold cross-validation was used to evaluate the variability and robustness of the predictive performance. LSBoost + GWO showed the strongest overall predictive performance among the evaluated models, with R values of 0.810, 0.704, and 0.666 for the training, testing, and validation sets, respectively. In comparison, the testing R values for DT + GWO, ANN + GWO, and LR were 0.678, 0.683, and 0.572, respectively. The 10-fold cross-validation of LSBoost + GWO produced an average R of 0.641, indicating variability across the folds. To further examine the observed differences between the two optimized models, a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test was conducted using the same cross-validation folds. The results revealed no statistically significant differences between DT + GWO and LSBoost + GWO for the main error- and correlation-based metrics. Although LSBoost + GWO achieved a higher a20 value than DT + GWO, this difference was not statistically significant after multiple-comparison correction (adjusted
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     = 0.334). SHAP analysis identified Healing Time, B/g, and ICW as the most influential input variables, while FA/C showed a moderate contribution, and CA/C and W/C exhibited relatively smaller global effects. Additionally, two-dimensional partial dependence analysis was used to explore interactions among selected input variables. Overall, the findings suggest that machine learning, especially LSBoost + GWO, can serve as a data-driven exploratory tool for estimating crack-healing percentage and investigating the relative importance and interactions of factors associated with the healing behavior of self-healing concrete.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.64898/2026.10.06.757046.title: Machine learning-assisted directed evolution yields dramatic improvement on novel AAV engineering task
doi:10.64898/2026.10.06.757046.abstract: <jats:p>Directed evolution enables the discovery of protein mutants with improved fitness through iterative rounds of selection and has been widely applied to adeno-associated virus (AAV) capsid engineering. Machine learning (ML) can augment this process by prioritising mutants for experimental validation, but whether its benefits outweigh the added cost of ML-designed library construction remains unclear. Here, we address this question by considering improvements in manufacturing efficiency of AAV capsids in the context of exosomal encapsulation, which is a technique for improving AAV immunogenicity. We generated a directed evolution dataset comprising 53,974 mutants across three rounds of selection and an independent assessment dataset of 472 ML-designed mutants with detailed profiling. Directed evolution alone yielded a 3-fold improvement, while ML-assisted directed evolution yielded a 41-fold improvement in manufacturing efficiency, demonstrating that ML-assisted directed evolution outperforms directed evolution alone. We show that data quality - specifically the number of selection rounds and the statistical power of mutant counts - has a greater impact on model performance than model architecture. Finally, we provide practical guidance on experimental design and implementation of ML tuning strategies that can augment model performance in protein engineering applications.</jats:p>

doi:10.1098/rsos.260335.title: Stacking ensemble learning and SHAP analysis for predicting CO2 solubility and guiding ionic liquid design
doi:10.1098/rsos.260335.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Excessive CO2 emissions constitute a primary driver of global climate change, creating an urgent need for efficient CO2 capture technologies. Ionic liquids (ILs) are considered highly promising absorbents. However, their vast chemical space poses significant challenges for experimental screening. In this study, Morgan fingerprint descriptors were combined with a stacking ensemble learning algorithm, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was employed to develop an accurate and interpretable framework for predicting CO2 solubility. The stacking ensemble model employs the light gradient boosting machine and the backpropagation neural network as base learners. The dung beetle optimizer and the grey wolf optimizer were used to determine optimal hyperparameter combinations for these learners, while linear regression was adopted as the meta-learner to produce the final CO2 solubility prediction. The results demonstrate that the stacking ensemble algorithm achieves the highest predictive accuracy, attaining a test-set coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9888, a mean absolute error of 0.0149 and a mean squared error of 0.0006. SHAP analysis further reveals that the [Tf2N] (bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)amide) anion exerts the most significant influence, followed by the alkyl chain length of imidazolium cations. Accordingly, combining the [Tf2N] anion with imidazolium cations bearing longer alkyl chains represents a promising strategy for synthesizing ILs with high CO2 absorption efficiency.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/s26196318.title: Lesion-Aware Multiple-Instance Learning for Grapevine Disease Recognition from Field RGB Images
doi:10.3390/s26196318.abstract: <jats:p>This retrospective offline study examines how dense manual regional annotations can be organized for image-level grapevine disease recognition using pre-acquired HERMOS RGB images. After audit and filtering, 491 source images and 13,765 Pascal VOC regions were retained. A leakage-safe source-image split was used across full-image classification, regional crop classification, crop-to-image aggregation, annotation-guided multiple-instance learning (MIL), and YOLO11 localization. MIL bags in training, validation, and testing were constructed from crops derived from manual boxes; the results therefore describe annotation-assisted aggregation rather than raw-image deployment. The original ConvNeXt-Tiny MIL model achieved macro-F1 0.922 (95% source-image bootstrap CI 0.882–0.956), compared with 0.836 (0.754–0.895) for full-image ConvNeXt-Tiny and 0.869 (0.804–0.917) for the best fixed crop aggregation. Paired macro-F1 differences favored MIL over these baselines by 0.087 (95% CI 0.029–0.163; Holm-adjusted p = 0.013) and 0.053 (0.005–0.114; adjusted p = 0.036), respectively. Downy mildew precision and recall were 1.000 on nine positive test images, but the corresponding exact 95% binomial intervals were 0.664–1.000. Controlled ablations produced lower point estimates without learned attention or the auxiliary instance loss, whereas removing context expansion did not reduce performance; none of the three paired ablation tests was significant after Holm correction. Increasing detector capacity from YOLO11n to YOLO11s did not improve full-image mAP@0.50 (0.175 versus 0.170). These findings support annotation-guided local-evidence aggregation as an offline exploratory benchmark, while not establishing split-to-split stability, computational efficiency, or external-vineyard generalization.</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s12879-026-14179-5.title: Enhancing the performance of machine learning models for the reliable diagnosis of hepatitis C virus
doi:10.1186/s12879-026-14179-5.abstract: Early and reliable detection of hepatitis C virus infection is essential for timely treatment and for reducing the risk of progressive liver damage and long-term complications. This study presents a methodological benchmarking framework to systematically evaluate the performance and stability of machine learning classifiers for HCV detection using routine biochemical attributes from a public benchmark dataset. A diagnostic framework was developed to address the problems associated with real-world medical datasets, particularly the problem of class imbalance and outliers, which can reduce model generalization. Feature importance was assessed using a decision tree-based recursive feature elimination approach to retain only the necessary predictors. Multiple machine learning classifiers including k-Nearest Neighbors, support vector machine, logistic regression, random forest, naive bayes, gradient boosting, extreme gradient boosting, and LightGBM, were trained and evaluated under a consistent experimental setting. The parameters for various models were optimized prior to testing using hyperparameter tuning. Performance was evaluated on an independent test cohort, and model generalizability was further verified using a stratified 5-fold cross-validation protocol. On the independent test cohort, the random forest model achieved the best diagnostic performance (98.38% accuracy, 100% precision, 93.02% F1-score). The subsequent 5-fold cross-validation confirmed high framework stability, with LightGBM delivering a top mean accuracy of \(95.77 \pm 1.45\%\) and an AUC of \(0.97 \pm 0.02\) . Other classifiers, especially support vector machine and logistic regression, also showed stable and competitive results, suggesting consistent generalization on unseen data. When compared to previous studies, the proposed models showed improved diagnostic sensitivity and stronger overall robustness, particularly when handling data imbalance and outliers. These findings confirm the value of data balancing, structured feature selection and careful model optimization for enhancing HCV diagnosis from clinical data. This benchmarking study demonstrates that integrating structured data balancing, feature elimination, and hyperparameter tuning significantly stabilizes classifier performance on routine laboratory data, establishing a reliable baseline methodology for future computer-aided screening research.

doi:10.51878/learning.v6i4.14141.title: PERSEPSI SIKAP KEPEDULIAN LINGKUNGAN SISWA TUNAGRAHITA: KAJIAN FENOMENOLOGI
doi:10.51878/learning.v6i4.14141.abstract:
<jats:p>Environmental care is an important character trait that should be instilled from an early age, including in students with mild intellectual disabilities. This study aimed to describe and analyze in depth the perceptions of students with mild intellectual disabilities in defining environmental care. A qualitative approach with a phenomenological design was employed. The participants consisted of ten students with mild intellectual disabilities as the main informants and one teacher as the supporting informant at SLB Manunggal Slawi, Tegal Regency. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, observations, and documentation. The data were analyzed using NVivo 15 through coding, theme development, and data interpretation. Data validity was ensured through technique triangulation. The findings revealed that students with mild intellectual disabilities possessed a fairly good perception of environmental care. They interpreted environmental care in simple terms, such as maintaining classroom cleanliness, disposing of waste properly, and caring for plants around the school. However, their perception of more complex concepts, such as organic and inorganic waste segregation, remained highly limited. This perception was subjectively constructed through concrete daily experiences, modeling from surrounding figures, and routine habituation implemented in the school environment.
ABSTRAK
Kepedulian lingkungan merupakan salah satu karakter penting yang perlu ditanamkan sejak dini, termasuk pada siswa tunagrahita ringan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan dan menganalisis secara mendalam persepsi siswa tunagrahita ringan dalam memaknai sikap kepedulian lingkungan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain fenomenologi. Subjek penelitian terdiri atas 10 siswa tunagrahita ringan sebagai informan utama dan satu guru sebagai informan pendukung di SLB Manunggal Slawi, Kabupaten Tegal. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan NVivo 15 melalui proses pengkodean, pengembangan tema, dan interpretasi data. Keabsahan data diuji menggunakan triangulasi teknik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa siswa tunagrahita ringan memiliki persepsi yang cukup baik mengenai kepedulian lingkungan. Mereka memaknai kepedulian lingkungan secara sederhana sebagai aktivitas menjaga kebersihan kelas, membuang sampah pada tempatnya, dan merawat tanaman di sekitar sekolah. Meskipun demikian, persepsi mereka terhadap konsep yang lebih kompleks, seperti pemilahan jenis organik dan anorganik, masih sangat terbatas. Persepsi ini terbangun dan dikonstruksikan secara subjektif melalui pengalaman konkret sehari-hari, proses meniru (modeling) figur di sekitarnya, serta pembiasaan rutin yang diterapkan di lingkungan sekolah.
 </jats:p>

doi:10.29210/027225jpgi0005.title: Pengaruh pendekatan pembelajaran mendalam (deep learning) terhadap kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis murid
doi:10.29210/027225jpgi0005.abstract: <jats:p>Kemampuan murid dalam memecahkan masalah matematis mesti diasah lewat proses belajar yang menuntut pemahaman yang mendalam sekaligus partisipasi aktif dari peserta didik. Riset ini dimaksudkan untuk menganalisis pengaruh pendekatan deep learning (pembelajaran mendalam) terhadap kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis murid kelas IX di UPTD SMP Negeri 1 Kec. Harau. Metode kuantitatif dipakai dalam bentuk kuasi-eksperimen dengan rancangan posttest-only control group. Subjek penelitian mencakup 30 murid pada kelompok eksperimen yang diajar memakai pendekatan deep learning, serta 30 murid pada kelompok kontrol yang diajar secara konvensional. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui tes akhir yang menilai empat indikator kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis, yaitu memahami masalah, menyusun strategi, menjalankan strategi, dan mengecek kembali hasil. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa kelompok eksperimen memperoleh rerata skor tes akhir yang lebih tinggi dibandingkan kelompok kontrol. Kelompok eksperimen memperoleh rerata skor 23,23, sedangkan kelompok kontrol memperoleh rerata 20,37. Hasil uji-t menunjukkan p-value sebesar 0,000, lebih kecil daripada taraf signifikansi 0,05, yang menunjukkan adanya perbedaan kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis antara kedua kelompok. Ukuran efek Cohen’s d sebesar 1,30 tergolong besar. Dengan demikian, pendekatan deep learning efektif meningkatkan kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis murid kelas IX sehingga dapat direkomendasikan sebagai alternatif pendekatan dalam pembelajaran matematika, khususnya dengan penguatan refleksi pada tahap memeriksa kembali hasil penyelesaian.</jats:p>

doi:10.1111/tme.70126.title: Convolutional neural network for red blood cell transfusion prediction: A machine learning based study
doi:10.1111/tme.70126.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Subjective, inconsistent clinician judgement on red blood cell (RBC) transfusion demand causes unnecessary blood wastage, increased perioperative safety risks, and poorly balanced hospital blood inventory. To tackle these persistent clinical limitations, we developed a workflow‐adapted clinical decision support tool: a one‐dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN) trained on routinely acquired haematological and clinical variables to stratify inpatient RBC transfusion volume categories.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using a retrospective cohort of 7,250 patients from Beijing Friendship Hospital (April 2024–June 2025), we trained a 1D CNN on 19 standardised pre‐transfusion variables to predict transfusion volume categories (1, 2, 3, 4, ≥5 units). The model was optimised with Adam and evaluated on a 30% hold‐out test set. Comprehensive characterisation of the cohort's baseline clinical features was also performed to clearly define the transfusion contexts and clinical indications of the study population.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>On the 30% hold‐out test set, the 1D CNN reached an overall accuracy of 0.7314 and converged without overfitting. The model accurately identified the predominant 2 units transfusion class (68.03% of cases, precision 0.7314). However, performance was limited in minority classes (≥5 units and 3 units), which showed low prevalence (< 5%) and overlapping haemoglobin values (60–80 g/L), indicating a critical safety limitation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The 1D CNN reliably forecasts routine transfusion requirements in a single‐center setting but under‐detects high‐volume transfusion events. External validation across diverse clinical centers, targeted data enrichment for minority classes, and development of indication‐specific sub‐models are mandatory to improve the model's generalizability and clinical utility.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1942376.title: Governance-aware autonomous retail coordination in artificial intelligence cities using multi-agent reinforcement learning, blockchain accountability, and federated learning
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1942376.abstract: <jats:p>When autonomous systems take operational authority over urban commerce, accountability and human oversight matter as much as efficiency. We present AAIRM, a governance-aware autonomous retail coordination framework addressing three requirements for trustworthy procurement: tamper-evident decision provenance, data sovereignty, and adaptive demand coordination. AAIRM couples a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) ordering policy, a permissioned Blockchain Trust Ledger (BTL) for multi-party audit trails, and a Federated Demand Learning (FDL) layer. Evaluation is simulation-based, using a multi-category synthetic environment and the public M5 dataset; no live retail deployment is claimed. At its cost-optimal operating point (92.3% fill), AAIRM lowers normalized inventory cost by 13.2% (95% CI 12.2–14.2) against a conventionally parameterized reorder-point/economic-order-quantity (ROP–EOQ) baseline and by 10.2% (95% CI 8.0–12.4) on M5. Service parity is obtained by moving AAIRM along its own cost–service frontier rather than by retuning baselines: At 96.1% and 97.4% fill, it retains 8.2-point and 4.9-point advantages. A layered ablation attributes 8.8 points of the advantage to the reinforcement learning (RL) policy and 3.8 points to the combined coordination-and-governance block, which we further decompose into feasibility projection, escalation logic, cross-category policy rules, supplier ranking, and negotiation. The language-model orchestrator contributes 0.6 points (95% CI −0.9 to 2.1), statistically indistinguishable from zero and practically equivalent within a ±2-point margin. Against a feasibility-matched multi-agent RL comparator, the residual cost gap does not survive multiple-comparison correction, so the defensible advantages are hard feasibility and auditability, not cost. The BTL adds 6.6% decision-cycle overhead; its 500-case mutation replay is an integration check, and we give an explicit adversary model showing that crash-fault-tolerant ordering does not resist colluding majorities. FedProx converges within 0.9 WAPE points of centralized training at a 1.3-point cost penalty, without secure aggregation or differential privacy; we analyze rather than evaluate when those mechanisms become necessary. A 500-SKU study exposes a reward-hacking failure in a high-spoilage category, corrected by category-specific governance. We close with an architectural, non-empirical reading of labor exposure and three governance instruments regulators can act on.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1962146.title: Psychological associations between perceived generative AI-supported learning and creative design performance in vocational design education: a within-course correlational study
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1962146.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in design courses, but evidence remains limited on how students’ appraisal of such support co-varies with domain cognition, creative confidence, engagement, and independently assessed creative work. This within-course correlational study examined within-course change and theory-specified contemporaneous associations in a 72-h Furniture Appreciation and Selection course involving 150 vocational design students in China. Sustainable design cognition and creative self-efficacy were measured before and after the course; perceived GenAI-supported learning and learning engagement were measured after it; and final creative design performance was rated independently by three experts. Paired-samples t tests described within-course change. Item-level CFA preceded the score-level association analyses, while standardized composite-score ordinary least squares models and 10,000-resample percentile bootstrap confidence intervals summarized theory-specified post-course associations and coefficient products. Sustainable design cognition increased from 3.326 to 3.792, t (149) = 10.362,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                    &lt; 0.001, d
                    <jats:sub>z</jats:sub>
                     = 0.846, and creative self-efficacy increased from 3.509 to 3.877, t (149) = 7.424,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                    &lt; 0.001, d
                    <jats:sub>z</jats:sub>
                     = 0.606; these values indicate change during the course as a whole rather than a GenAI-specific intervention effect. Among the direct post-course associations, learning engagement showed the largest coefficient with expert-rated creative design performance (β = 0.515,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                    &lt; 0.001; f
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.361). The theory-specified coefficient products were 0.076 for SDC-CSE-LE, 0.204 for CSE-LE-CP, and 0.0080 for AISL-SDC-CSE-LE-CP. Because the study followed one cohort without a comparison condition and most model variables were measured at the same post-course occasion, the findings support within-course change and contemporaneous association, not causal or temporally ordered effects.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.1007/s44217-026-02104-6.title: Virtual reality and gamification for STEM learning among speech impaired learners in Ghana
doi:10.1007/s44217-026-02104-6.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Virtual reality (VR) and gamification are increasingly used in STEM education to enhance student engagement and learning. However, it remains unclear how these technologies address the needs of students with speech impairments, particularly in low-resource settings in Ghana. This scoping review examines existing research on the use of VR and gamification in inclusive STEM education, with a specific focus on accessibility features and the representation of speech-impaired learners in the literature. Using PRISMA-ScR guidelines, 2501 records were identified from five databases. After screening, 40 studies published between 2020 and 2024 were included. However, very few studies explicitly address accessibility for learners with speech impairments, and only a small number consider low-resource or marginalized educational contexts. Most of the existing research originates from high-income countries and tends to focus on broader disability groups rather than on speech impairment as a distinct category.</jats:p>

doi:10.20319/ictel.2026.334335.title: DEVELOPMENT OF CLASSROOM WELL-BEING STRATEGIES FOR MANAGING BEHAVIOURAL ISSUES AMONG PRIMARY SCHOOL PUPILS USING THE FUZZY DELPHI METHOD
doi:10.20319/ictel.2026.334335.abstract: <jats:p>Behavioural issues among primary school pupils such as hyperactivity, excessive classroom noise, low motivation, lack of focus, and disruptive behaviour have become increasingly challenging for teachers in creating an effective learning environment. These behavioural challenges affect pupils’ engagement, classroom well-being, and teaching effectiveness. Therefore, this study aims to develop classroom well-being strategies for managing behavioural issues among primary school pupils using the Fuzzy Delphi Method (FDM). The study is grounded in the concepts of positive classroom management, pupil engagement, and classroom well-being. Employing a quantitative design through the Fuzzy Delphi Method, the study involved five experts from the fields of primary education, counselling, educational psychology, behavioural management, and classroom management. The experts were selected based on their professional experience and direct involvement in managing pupil behaviour in schools. The research instrument was developed through literature review and preliminary needs analysis. The findings demonstrated a high level of expert consensus, with all items fulfilling the threshold value (d ≤ 0.2), expert agreement exceeding 75%, and α-cut values above 0.5. The highest-ranked strategies included interactive learning activities, positive reinforcement, emotional support, movement-based activities, brain breaks, and positive teacher–pupil relationships. The study contributes practically by providing a structured framework to support teachers in managing behavioural challenges and improving classroom well-being in primary schools.</jats:p>

doi:10.55041/ijcope.v2i10.026.title: When the Machine Becomes the Other: Rethinking Consciousness, Attachment, and Personhood in Human–AI Relationships
doi:10.55041/ijcope.v2i10.026.abstract:
<jats:p>The increasing integration of artificial intelligence into everyday life has created relationships that are not adequately described as merely functional interactions between users and tools. Conversational systems, social robots and autonomous agents can be trusted, loved, relied upon and even moralized. Questions arise here about the nature of consciousness, about a psychological foundation for attachment, about the political construction of personhood and about the limits of human exceptionalism. This article explores these issues in Klara and the Sun by Kazuo Ishiguro, Machines Like Me by Ian McEwan, Autonomous by Annalee Newitz,

Agency by William Gibson, and Robopocalypse by Daniel H. Wilson. It is a synthesis of




psychoanalytic theory, critical posthumanism and philosophy of mind and ethics. Freud's concept of the uncanny, Bowlby's object-relations theory and the concept of attachment theory,

Winnicott's concept of the transitional object, and Lacan's concept of subject formation provide some explanation for how humans can develop emotionally significant relationships with artificial objects knowing that they are technologically manufactured. Hayles and Braidotti

complicate the dichotomy of human and machine by stressing the use of technology as a mediation, distributed cognition and the politics of the conditions under which personhood is recognized. The philosophical discussions about consciousness, moral status and agency argue that one should not simply assume that if a system behaves intelligently then it is human, and conversely that its artificiality should be given as conclusive evidence of ethical irrelevance. The article states that the human-AI relationship is relational, technologically mediated, and institutionally structured. Literature does not show that machines are conscious, rather literature becomes a place where the psychological and ethical implications of uncertainty can be explored. Keywords: human-AI relationship, psychoanalysis, critical post-humanism, consciousness, attachment, personhood, moral status, science fiction.</jats:p>
doi:10.55041/ijcope.v2i10.026.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management

doi:10.3389/fphys.2026.1923556.title: A hybrid deep learning framework combining CTGAN and transformers for personalized injury mitigation in elite sports
doi:10.3389/fphys.2026.1923556.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Optimizing training in elite sports while managing injury risk requires models that can learn from heterogeneous and imbalanced athlete records without contaminating evaluation data. This study presents PTI-GANFormer (Personalized Training and Injury Risk Prediction using Generative Adversarial Network-Former), an integrated decision-support framework. Its contribution is not CTGAN or self-attention in isolation; rather, it is the leakage-controlled combination of training-only conditional augmentation, three functionally separated attention pathways, five domain-engineered indicators, and a transparent risk-to-action recommendation layer.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>After median imputation, plausibility-aware outlier handling, categorical embedding, scaling, and feature engineering, the data were stratified into training and untouched testing partitions. CTGAN was fitted only to the training partition and generated minority-class records until each training class matched the original majority count of 7,894. The hybrid classifier distinguishes No Injury, Minor Injury, and Major Injury, while the recommendation engine converts predicted risk into advisory workload and recovery options that require practitioner review.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Across repeated stratified evaluation runs, PTI-GANFormer achieved an accuracy of 0.960 ± 0.004 (95% CI: 0.957–0.963), precision of 0.950 ± 0.006, recall of 0.960 ± 0.005, F1-score of 0.950 ± 0.005, and macro ROC-AUC of 0.981 ± 0.004.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These results support predictive risk stratification and decision support; they do not by themselves establish injury prevention or performance enhancement.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.63498/injelps112.title: Effectiveness of a psychological first aid-based intervention on the psycho-emotional health of teachers
doi:10.63498/injelps112.abstract: Aim: The transition to flexible instructional modalities and changing work arrangements has created psychological and emotional challenges for educators, which may affect their well-being and instructional functioning.This action research aimed to assess the impact of the Self-Care is my Share: A Psycho-emotional Support intervention, grounded in Crisis Intervention Theory and Psychological First Aid (PFA), on the psycho-emotional health status of 33 teaching personnel at Kalibo Pilot Elementary School.Methodology: Using a pre-test-post-test action research design, the study assessed the participants' psychoemotional health in terms of personal behavior, discernment regarding skeletal and work-from-home arrangements, and delivery of learning modalities.Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and a paired-samples t test to determine whether significant differences existed before and after the intervention.Results: Before the intervention, the participants demonstrated a state of frustration across all domains, with mean scores ranging from 3.12 to 3.33.Following the intervention, the mean scores decreased to a range of 1.17 to 1.42, corresponding to a happy state.The paired-samples t test revealed statistically significant differences between the preintervention and post-intervention psycho-emotional health status of the participants (p < .05),with an overall t value of 11.43. Conclusion:The findings indicate that the Self-Care is my Share intervention may serve as a useful, scalable, and low-intensity school-based support strategy for improving teachers' psycho-emotional well-being.The results highlight the value of integrating Psychological First Aid and structured psycho-emotional support initiatives into teacher development and school support programs while recognizing the importance of broader institutional measures that address workload, working conditions, and other sources of occupational stress.

doi:10.68490/ber.2026.1.333.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Concrete and Virtual Manipulatives on Students’ Learning of LCM and HCF and Classroom Engagement
doi:10.68490/ber.2026.1.333.abstract: <jats:p>This study looks at how students react to two different types of classroom tools. These tools are called manipulatives. They are designed to help elementary students understand concepts in math that are complex. This study focuses on students' engagement, and achievements in solving prime factorization, least common multiple (LCM), and highest common factor (HCF). The study was conducted in a 2-week period, with 5th grade students. This study used a quasi-experimental approach. The research design used was a pre-test post-test control group. Data was retrieved using pre and posttests in math, and using a scale to measure classroom behaviors. The data were analyzed using one way ANCOVA and two way ANOVA. The data indicates that both types of manipulatives enhanced students' math skills and engagement in class, with students using virtual tools benefiting more. This study can help teachers and those in charge of the curriculum make better teaching plans that help students achieve more in math and participate more in class.</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s12911-026-03888-1.title: Predictive contributions to five-year change in carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity using machine learning and penalized regression
doi:10.1186/s12911-026-03888-1.abstract: Arterial stiffness, assessed by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cf-PWV), is a validated biomarker of vascular aging and cardiovascular risk. However, the extent to which clinical and behavioral factors predict longitudinal changes in cf-PWV remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the extent to which selected baseline clinical and lifestyle variables could predict five-year change in cf-PWV in a population-based cohort. Data from the Influence of Different Risk Factors in Vascular Accelerated Aging (Estudio de Envejecimiento Vascular Acelerado, EVA study; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02623894), a prospective cohort of adults free from cardiovascular disease, were analyzed. XGBoost was used to capture nonlinear interactions and rank predictor importance. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis provided interpretability. Subsequently, Elastic Net regression was applied to derive a parsimonious, interpretable equation. Model tuning was performed using cross-validation within the training set, and performance was evaluated in the held-out test set. XGBoost identified smoking duration (years), adherence to the Mediterranean diet, HDL cholesterol, use of antidiabetic drugs, baseline age, and weekly sitting time (h/week) as key predictors. Mean absolute SHAP values were highest for smoking duration, baseline age, and weekly sitting time. The hierarchical Elastic Net model included baseline age (β = 0.31) and weekly sitting time (β = 0.02) as main effects and retained HDL-C (β = −0.13), use of antidiabetic drugs (β = −0.11), Mediterranean diet adherence (β = −0.008), and the age × weekly sitting time interaction (β = −0.24), with limited predictive performance (MAE = 1.27 m/s; RMSE = 1.70 m/s), which did not improve upon a mean-only benchmark (MAE = 1.27 m/s; RMSE = 1.68 m/s). This exploratory hybrid modeling approach characterized the predictive contributions of clinically relevant factors to five-year change in cf-PWV. Neither primary model improved upon the mean-only benchmark; therefore, the derived equation should be considered a hypothesis-generating research model requiring further development and independent external validation. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02623894. Registered on 8 December 2015. Retrospectively registered. (https//classic.clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT02623894).

doi:10.3390/rs18193421.title: An All-Weather Land Precipitable Water Vapor Retrieval Method Integrating Physical Constraints and Machine Learning
doi:10.3390/rs18193421.abstract: <jats:p>Atmospheric precipitable water vapor (PWV) is an essential geophysical parameter for weather forecasting, climate change research and hydrological studies. Spaceborne passive microwave sensors support all-weather PWV observation, yet accurate retrieval of land PWV still faces great difficulties owing to the spatiotemporal complexity and variability of land surface emissivity (LSE). This study proposes a novel all-weather land PWV retrieval approach using Fengyun-3D microwave radiation imager (MWRI) observations, which combines physical radiative transfer principles with machine learning techniques. By reorganizing the radiative transfer equation, this study constructs two characteristic factors that can effectively characterize LSE and PWV, and further incorporates them into the machine learning retrieval framework. Three typical machine learning algorithms, namely Random Forest (RF), Adaptive Kernel Extreme Learning Machine (AKELM), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), achieve the optimal retrieval accuracy, with an RMSE of 3.80 mm and an R2 of 0.91. Multiple validation results indicate that (1) compared with conventional physically constrained machine learning retrieval methods, the proposed method reduces the root mean square error (RMSE) by 16.5%; (2) against ground-based SuomiNet site observations, the minimum retrieval RMSE is as low as 2.95 mm; (3) the proposed method exhibits stable superiority over the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) MYD05 water vapor products with lower RMSE in all experimental cases. This study offers an effective and reliable technical scheme for all-weather land PWV retrieval, and can facilitate high-precision atmospheric monitoring and related practical operational services.</jats:p>

doi:10.23960/jpp.v16i4.pp1954-1974.title: Source-Based Inquiry Learning to Improve University Students’ Historical Literacy in South Asian History
doi:10.23960/jpp.v16i4.pp1954-1974.abstract: <jats:p>This study examined the effectiveness of source-based inquiry learning in improving university students' historical literacy in a South Asian History course. Historical literacy was conceptualized through students' abilities in sourcing, contextualization, corroboration, and evidence-based historical argumentation. A quantitative quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design involved 58 fourth-semester history education students. The experimental group comprised 29 students who received source-based inquiry learning, while the control group received conventional instruction. Data were collected using a source-based historical literacy essay test and analyzed through descriptive statistics, an independent-samples t-test, analysis of covariance, and normalized gain analysis. The experimental group achieved a higher posttest mean than the control group (78.93 vs. 64.90) and a greater improvement (28.15 vs. 14.48 points). The between-group difference was statistically significant, t(56) = 6.79, p < 0.001. Analysis of covariance confirmed a significant treatment effect after controlling for pretest scores, F(1, 55) = 110.82, p < 0.001, with a large effect size (0.668). The experimental group obtained a moderate normalized gain of 0.58, compared with 0.30 in the control group, which lay at the lower boundary of the low category. Sourcing and contextualization showed the greatest improvement. Source-based inquiry learning effectively strengthens historical literacy and disciplinary reasoning. Its integration into university history education can support more analytical, contextual, critical, and evidence-centered learning. Keywords: source-based inquiry learning, historical literacy, history education, primary historical sources, historical thinking.</jats:p>

doi:10.1117/12.3125555.title: Causality-informed disentangled representation learning for MCI conversion classification
doi:10.1117/12.3125555.abstract: <jats:p>Early identification of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is important for delaying progression to Alzheimer’s disease. We propose DeConf-GNN, a causality-inspired multimodal brain-graph classification model for MCI conversion classification. Based on a standard brain atlas, neuroimaging data are converted into graph representations and softly partitioned into a putative disease-relevant component and a complementary bias-related component through an edge-weight mechanism. A dual graph attention network learns subgraph-specific representations, which are fused during training with MedBERT-encoded clinical text representations generated from structured demographic and cognitive variables. In subject-level 6- fold stratified cross-validation, DeConf-GNN achieved an accuracy of 0.9000 ± 0.0894, a sensitivity of 0.9333 ± 0.1033, and an AUC-ROC of 0.8967 ± 0.0824. These results suggest that DeConf-GNN may improve imaging-only MCI conversion classification and provide a more interpretable prediction framework.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/s44163-026-02452-0.title: Dynamic weighted federated learning with client level differential privacy for DDoS detection in IoT networks
doi:10.1007/s44163-026-02452-0.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) networks has introduced substantial security threats from distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks to the availability of IoT systems. Existing intrusion detection systems (IDS) are often inefficient in IoT environments due to network heterogeneity, and privacy concerns associated with sharing sensitive data. To address the unresolved challenge of simultaneously handling non-IID data heterogeneity, dynamic client quality variation, and formally quantified privacy in distributed IoT DDoS detection, this paper proposes a client-level differential privacy (CLDP)-dynamic weighted federated learning (DWFL) framework that applies Gaussian-mechanism noise with Renyi differential privacy (DP) composition and privacy amplification by subsampling, combined with a quality-score-driven weighted aggregation mechanism, within a single unified architecture, where the weighting mechanism is deliberately lightweight to remain compatible with formal per-round privacy accounting rather than to outperform more elaborate trust or attention-based aggregation schemes. In the proposed framework, each IoT client trains on a local dataset. Later on, it applies update norm clipping and Gaussian noise injection on updates to enforce CLDP before transmitting model updates to a central aggregator. A dynamic weighted aggregation mechanism is added to combine client updates based on the data size, and quality of each client which ensures that contributions from more informative clients have a proportionally higher impact on the global model. The proposed framework is evaluated using two extensively recognized IoT datasets, CICIoT2023 and IoT23. Results demonstrate a maximum detection accuracy of 95.30% to 96.95%, and a formal privacy budget of ε (4.06 to 9.07) outperforming the standard FedAvg baseline by approximately 3.7% and FedProx by approximately 4.5%. An ablation study further validates the selection of key privacy hyperparameters, confirming that they represent an empirically optimal configuration. Overall, this research presents a practical, and formally privacy-preserving solution for DDoS detection.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/jrfm19100784.title: Risk and Return in Accelerator-Backed Ventures: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of MOIC by Industry Vertical and Founder Demographics
doi:10.3390/jrfm19100784.abstract: <jats:p>Startup accelerators have become a central mechanism in early-stage entrepreneurial finance, yet little empirical evidence exists on how the risk-return profile of accelerator-backed ventures varies across industry verticals and founder demographics. This study uses a proprietary panel dataset of 485 startups from a European startup accelerator, tracking Multiple on Invested Capital (MOIC), quarterly headcount, capital invested, and post-money valuation alongside founder gender composition and founder team size. We construct risk-adjusted return measures by combining realized MOIC with headcount growth volatility as a proxy for operational risk, and examine how these measures differ across founder team composition and industry vertical. Grounded in the Resource-Based View and Signaling Theory, we test whether founder gender composition is associated with differences in realized returns, and whether these differences reflect underlying operational risk or a valuation/allocation gap. Our results show that ventures with at least one female founder earn significantly lower average MOIC than all-male-founded ventures (a gap of roughly 20% in log terms, p = 0.021), yet show no significant difference in failure rates or in headcount volatility—and median MOIC is identical (1.0×) across both groups. This pattern suggests the gap is concentrated in the right tail of outcomes (large “home-run” exits) rather than in typical-case performance or operational risk, echoing prior evidence of a valuation gap that is not explained by fundamentals. We contribute one of the first vertical- and demographic-disaggregated risk-return analyses using accelerator-level panel data, with implications for investors, accelerator program design, and policy on capital allocation in early-stage venture ecosystems.</jats:p>
doi:10.3390/jrfm19100784.venue: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

doi:10.1088/1402-4896/aeac8e.title: Learning quantum eigenspaces under geometric symmetry breaking with Rayleigh–Ritz physics-informed neural networks
authors: Gregório Candido dos Santos Valadares de Almeida
Daniela Cristina da Silva Rodrigues Vitoria
doi:10.1088/1402-4896/aeac8e.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We develop a Rayleigh–Ritz physics-informed neural formulation for quantum eigenproblems on geometry-parametrized domains, in which the neural representation and its validation diagnostic track the spectral object selected by the physics rather than the eigenvalue index alone. Tested on the one-dimensional well, the square-to-rectangle and disk-to-ellipse deformations, and a controlled avoided crossing, the formulation recovers ordered excited states by explicit projection, degenerate eigenspaces by subspace Rayleigh–Ritz training without imposing a particular basis, symmetry-split branches by parity-adapted sectors, and near-degenerate bands by modal-overlap tracking. Additional controls show that the avoided-crossing behavior persists under purely geometric coupling, that explicit projection is more robust than residual and soft-orthogonality baselines, and that carrier-free subspace tracking extends to an asymmetric defected quantum dot. These results give a practical diagnostic hierarchy for neural eigensolvers of Hermitian operators under geometric deformation.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/978-3-032-37979-5_25.title: Children with Greater Sustainability and Equity Understanding Demand More from Educational Robots
doi:10.1007/978-3-032-37979-5_25.abstract: The application of social robots is changing learning landscapes, yet the environmental costs and social consequences of their deployment have received minimal attention. To effectively promote sustainable practices, it is crucial to identify how children’s knowledge of and attitudes towards sustainability and social equity evolve across different developmental stages. In this paper, we systematically investigated children’s understanding of robot sustainability and social equity through a survey study with 71 children aged 10-16 years. Our findings show that children’s understanding of sustainability and social equity informs a critical stance toward social robots, with more knowledgeable children demanding higher standards. By identifying age-related differences in children's knowledge and attitudes, this work provides a foundational understanding that can inform the design of age-appropriate technologies and curricula to foster a more responsible and sustainable future.
