doi:10.1186/s12885-026-17115-7.title: Machine learning model for the prediction of pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer
doi:10.1186/s12885-026-17115-7.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Breast cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant treatment may benefit from a presurgical assessment of complete response to avoid unnecessary surgeries. We aimed to develop a machine learning model that predicts pathological complete response (pCR) based on results from different image modalities as well as tumor and patient characteristics.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Clinical data from 388 cases of invasive breast cancer receiving neoadjuvant treatment were extracted in this retrospective, monocentric study. Findings from ultrasound, mammography and magnetic resonance imaging combined with patient and histopathological information were included. A Pearson Product-Moment correlation and a LASSO regularization were performed to preselect the most relevant features for the outcome. Based on the preselected variables, we developed and validated a machine learning algorithm (logistic regression with elastic net penalty (GLM)) to predict pCR. The model’s performance was evaluated via area under the curve (AUROC), false positive rate (FPR) and positive predictive value (PPV).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In the total cohort, pCR was detected in 158 out of 388 cases, resulting in a pCR rate of 40.7%. From 111 collected variables, 8 variables were removed due to a high correlation with other features. After the LASSO regularization, 14 variables were included as predictors for the final model. In the validation set, the GLM achieved an AUROC of 0.76 with a FPR of 8.7% and a PPV of 75%.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Through the combination of imaging and clinicopathological features, our machine learning model shows a promising approach to improve the prediction of pCR in breast cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant treatment. In combination with the LASSO regularization, it allows interesting insights into the predictive potential of different variables, which are available as part of standard clinical practice.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Trial registration</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Not applicable.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3846/cs.2026.22980.title: How to ‘escape’ from educational management: integrating online escape rooms into higher education for creative learning
doi:10.3846/cs.2026.22980.abstract: <jats:p>The aim of this article is to explore the integration of an online escape room (OER) into a postgraduate course as a gamified tool for creative learning and student self-assessment. A deductive thematic analysis of anonymous written student feedback revealed that: 1) gamification increased motivation and engagement; 2) the alignment of tasks with learning objectives supported meaningful learning; and 3) the structured and interactive format enhanced study skills and encouraged creative problem-solving. This innovative approach not only redefines traditional learning strategies but also demonstrates the potential of gamified self-assessment tools to foster creativity, critical thinking, and the practical application of knowledge, particularly within online and hybrid learning environments.</jats:p>

doi:10.1201/9781042046355-2.title: Automated Detection of Dermatological Disorders: AI-Assisted Image Processing and Machine Learning
doi:10.1201/9781042046355-2.abstract: Dermatology has transformed the early diagnosis and identification of skin conditions and disorders by incorporating artificial intelligence (AI). This chapter discusses the evolution and applications of AI-assisted image processing and machine learning (ML) algorithms to detect dermatological conditions automatically. Drawing on high-resolution dermatoscopic images, the system utilizes sophisticated preprocessing algorithms to improve image quality, followed by feature-detection algorithms for color, texture, and shape analysis. ML models (such as convolutional neural networks) have been trained to recognize skin diseases, including melanoma, psoriasis, eczema, and acne, with high levels of accuracy using annotated datasets. The systems using such models are compared with proposed and conventional diagnostic measures in terms of precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy and have shown higher accuracy. In addition, AI models can be visually interpretable in terms of how they developed their predictions, which is even more useful as it could be integrated into clinical workflows. Scaling such a system in teledermatology, particularly to patients in countries with scarce resources and limited dermatology services, presents major challenges. An AI-based dermatological tool has the potential to improve clinical outcomes for patients, reduce clinical burden, and enable population health surveillance by diagnosing and taking action in a timely and accurate fashion. The findings highlight the potential of ML to transform dermatology and pertinent conversations on ethics and data privacy in AI.

doi:10.4324/9781003654308.title: Health Communication and the Medical Humanities
doi:10.4324/9781003654308.abstract: Drawing upon actual case studies, this book introduces readers to how everyday interactions in the clinic can foster trust and impact diagnoses and reveals how often-overlooked communication processes fundamentally shape healthcare delivery and outcomes. The book treats communication not as a box to be checked or a skill to be mastered, but as a force that shapes provider and patient identities, a broker of relationships, and a central and pervasive presence in all systems of care. It explores topics such as end-of-life communication, physician burnout, professional hierarchies within healthcare teams, and AI in healthcare. It also integrates examples that extend beyond a U.S. framework, accounting for how different healthcare and political systems impact patient care. Each chapter is written in plain language and invites readers to think critically about what true patient-centered care looks like today. This book is tailored to both undergraduate and graduate medical humanities, health communication, medical sociology, and bioethics courses and a broad audience of healthcare professionals—from nursing students to attending physicians, technicians, and support staff. Online resources include links to readings, outside resources, and video components. They are available online at www.routledge.com/9781041102779 .

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-73211-5.title: Deep learning-driven joint blind source separation and noise suppression for audio signals: a performance optimization study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-73211-5.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Separating overlapping talkers and suppressing non-stationary noise are coupled problems, yet conventional pipelines solve them in isolation, so separation artifacts propagate untouched into the denoising stage. We therefore build a time–frequency joint separation–denoising network: a learnable encoder, a multi-scale dilated separator carrying channel and time–frequency attention, a per-stream noise-suppression module conditioned on the shared encoding, and an inverse-transform reconstructor, all reading one representation and trained end to end. A three-term objective binds scale-invariant signal-to-noise ratio, spectral magnitude and perceptual weighting, and training spans input signal-to-noise ratios down to − 5 dB. Evaluation draws on LibriMix, WHAM! and WHAMR! for separation, VoiceBank-DEMAND and MUSAN for noise, and MUSDB18-HQ for a full-band check outside speech. Against seven baselines retrained under an identical recipe, with every difference tested on 3000 mixtures across three seeds, the model reached 15.60 ± 0.10 dB SI-SNR improvement, 3.02 PESQ and 0.917 STOI at 0 dB with 3.9 million parameters. It surpassed Conv-TasNet, DPRNN, SepFormer, a diffusion-based cascade and a serial separate-then-denoise pipeline; TF-GridNet and MossFormer2 scored 0.50 to 0.80 dB higher at seven to eleven times the arithmetic cost, so the contribution is accuracy per unit of computation rather than absolute accuracy. Cost measurements report 6.8 G multiply–accumulate operations per second of audio, a real-time factor of 0.51 on a single CPU core and 0.41 J per second of processed audio, and a causal variant suited to streaming gives up 1.70 dB. Ablation separates the two attention paths, at 4.50% and 7.10%, from the joint denoising route at 10.30%. Cross-corpus, unseen-language and reverberant tests bound generalization: transfer costs 0.70 to 2.20 dB, and improvement falls to 7.80 dB once reverberation time exceeds 0.90 s. Code, configurations and per-utterance records accompany the article.</jats:p>

doi:10.22158/lecr.v6n2p47.title: Prospects and Constraints of Teaching and Learning Oral English in Senior Secondary Schools in Nigeria: A Case Study of Selected Secondary Schools
doi:10.22158/lecr.v6n2p47.abstract: <jats:p>This paper investigates the prospects and constraints in the teaching and learning of Oral English at the Senior Secondary School level in Nigeria, using selected secondary schools as case study. Oral English is a discrete aspect of the curriculum of English studies at the secondary school level of education in Nigeria. In Oral English, students are taught segmental and suprasegmental sounds of English RP (Received Pronunciation). Being non-native speakers of English, Senior Secondary School students/SSCE candidates are expected to be conscious of English sounds that are different from those in their native languages. One of the goals of teaching Oral English at the SSCE level of secondary school education in Nigeria is to address the problem of negative transfer of the phonological features of mother tongue (MT) into the phonological corpora of second language (L2), which is English (in the case of Nigeria). The theoretical frameworks of this study are Interference and Intraference theories. The study concludes that although proficiency in English guarantees learners the success they desire in SSCE and prepares them for career needs, the Oral English component of SSCE is not effectively taught owing to some factors which include teacher-incompetence and lack of language laboratories. Consequently, failure persists in the Oral English component of the SSCE, and because it is part of the English Language paper, overall performance in the subject declines.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/s16024-026-00466-3.title: Strategische Wahl von Lehr-Lern-Themen an Hochschulen zur Entwicklung interprofessioneller Kompetenzen
doi:10.1007/s16024-026-00466-3.abstract:
<jats:title>Zusammenfassung</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Hintergrund</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Interprofessional Education gewinnt in der Hochschulbildung zunehmend an Bedeutung, da sie gezielt die Entwicklung interprofessioneller Handlungskompetenzen unterstützt. Internationale Frameworks definieren zwar interprofessionelle Kompetenzen als intendierte Lernziele, benennen jedoch kaum konkrete Lehr-Lern-Themen für die curriculare Umsetzung.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methode</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Es wurden 12 leitfadengestützte Expert:inneninterviews mit Lehrenden aus Deutschland, Österreich und der Schweiz durchgeführt. Die Daten wurden mittels strukturierender qualitativer Inhaltsanalyse nach Kuckartz (2016) ausgewertet.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Ergebnisse</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass insbesondere praxisnahe und gemeinsame Lehr-Lern-Themen wie das Fallverstehen von den Expert:innen priorisiert werden. Darüber hinaus eignen sich aber auch gesellschaftsrelevante und professionsübergreifende Themen für die Interprofessional Education. Als zusätzliche Kompetenzen wurden hierarchiefreies Denken und die Reflexion beruflicher Stereotype identifiziert.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Diskussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Die Ergebnisse verdeutlichen, dass der Kompetenzerwerb in der Interprofessional Education vor allem in kontextgebundenen, handlungsorientierten Lernsettings erfolgt. Das Potenzial der Lehr-Lern-Themen für die Kompetenzentwicklung hängt maßgeblich von ihrer Auswahl und ihrer didaktischen Einbettung in kollaborative Lehr-Lern-Formate ab. Die identifizierten Lehr-Lern-Themen konkretisieren zudem die in internationalen Frameworks beschriebenen Kompetenzen.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Fazit</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Die gezielte Auswahl anschlussfähiger, praxisnaher und professionsübergreifender Lehr-Lern-Themen kann zur nachhaltigen curricularen Verankerung der Interprofessional Education beitragen, da diese den intendierten Kompetenzerwerb ermöglichen und die Wahl der Lehr-Lern-Formate mitbegründen.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/fmech.2026.1885264.title: Integrated multi-criteria optimization of production, transport, and storage assets in machine-building systems
doi:10.3389/fmech.2026.1885264.abstract: <jats:p>Optimizing equipment and transport utilization is a critical task in process planning. Traditional approaches are fragmented and lack a comprehensive hierarchy, leading to downtime and reduced efficiency. The disruption of interfunctional links requires the creation of a unified asset planning system across all operational and calendar horizons. A multi-criteria vector optimization model for production assets with a rigid hierarchy is proposed. It is based on the decomposition of five time levels (year, quarter, month, day, shift), where the results of the upper level constrain the lower ones. The model was tested in a machine-building shop for 2026 (two-shift operation, 83 product groups, 450 operations). The operation of 17 machines (turning, milling, boring, grinding) and three electric pallet trucks was optimized. Redistributing batches based on Pareto-optimal solutions increased annual equipment efficiency by 15.11% and reduced load variability on milling machines (by 6.78%) and grinding machines (by 8.65%). Vehicle capacity utilization increased by 37.06%, while downtime decreased by 28.86%. Quarterly, equipment load variability and downtime decreased by 34.68% and 54.24%, respectively, and at the shift level, by 36.59% and 14.28% (for vehicles). Overall, the overall system load variability decreased by 15.9%, and total downtime by 19.31%. The results confirm the practical value of the end-to-end hierarchical model. Its modular architecture ensures scalability and adaptability to failures or inventory changes. The model eliminates the gaps between production, logistics, and warehousing, reducing production cycle times, work-in-process inventory, and order delays.</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s40644-026-01132-7.title: CT venous-phase radiomics for preoperative differentiation of early and advanced gastric cancer: construction, comparison, and validation of machine-learning models
doi:10.1186/s40644-026-01132-7.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To construct various radiomics models based on CT venous-phase images for the quantitative assessment of gastric cancer (GC) invasion depth into the gastric wall, and to compare the diagnostic performance of different machine-learning models in distinguishing early (T1–T2 stage) from advanced (T3–T4 stage) GC, aiming to identify a robust and interpretable model and evaluate its potential for clinical application.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      In this retrospective study, 223 pathologically confirmed GC patients (66 early-stage, 157 advanced-stage) treated between January 2022 and May 2025 were enrolled. Patients were allocated into a training set (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 156) and an internal hold-out test set (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 67) through stratified random sampling at a 7:3 ratio. All patients underwent enhanced CT within one week prior to surgery. Venous-phase images were selected, and three-dimensional regions of interest (ROIs) encompassing the tumor were manually delineated using 3D Slicer for radiomics feature extraction. To rigorously exclude data leakage, all preprocessing steps—including feature standardization, LASSO feature selection, hyperparameter tuning, and threshold determination—were performed exclusively within the training set using a pipeline-based approach with 5-fold cross-validation. Feature selection stability was further assessed using 50 iterations of repeated stratified cross-validation. Four machine learning models were constructed: Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), and Support Vector Machine (SVM). Performance was evaluated using ROC curves, PR curves, confusion matrices, and decision curve analysis (DCA). SHAP analysis was applied to the LR model for interpretability.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A total of 107 radiomics features were extracted, from which 23 key features were selected by LASSO regression. Feature selection stability analysis revealed that 2 features were consistently selected across all 50 iterations (100% frequency), 1 feature was retained in ≥ 98% iterations; overall 6 features exhibited selection frequency ≥ 80%, and 8 features achieved frequency ≥ 50%, while the remaining features showed considerable selection variability. In the internal hold-out test set, the LR model achieved the AUC of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.860–0.978), followed by SVM (AUC = 0.915, 95% CI: 0.848–0.973), RF (AUC = 0.893, 95% CI: 0.814–0.960), and XGBoost (AUC = 0.889, 95% CI: 0.806–0.956). DeLong’s test revealed no statistically significant differences in AUC among the four models (all
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       > 0.05); the marginal difference between LR and RF (AUC difference = 0.033,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.051) only represented a weak numerical gap without statistical superiority of LR. The LR model demonstrated balanced performance with accuracy 0.836, sensitivity 0.830, specificity 0.850, PPV 0.929, NPV 0.680, F1-score 0.876, and average precision (AP) 0.972; notably, LR yielded the lowest false-negative rate (17.0%), which minimizes the clinical risk of undertreating advanced GC. Hosmer-Lemeshow test revealed good calibration for the Random Forest (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.586), XGBoost (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.081), and SVM (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.213) models, whereas the Logistic Regression model showed evidence of miscalibration (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001). Despite this calibration limitation, the LR model’s excellent discriminative performance (AUC = 0.926) supports its clinical utility as a binary classifier. DCA indicated that all four models provided clinical utility, with the LR model offering favorable net benefit across most threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis confirmed that the contribution directions of selected features such as LeastAxisLength and SurfaceVolumeRatio were consistent with pathological interpretations.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      All four machine learning models constructed based on CT venous-phase images showed comparable discriminative power, with no statistically significant inter-model AUC differences detected via DeLong test (all
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       > 0.05). Rather than possessing statistically superior predictive efficacy, the LR model had higher clinical translation potential due to its excellent interpretability, balanced classification metrics and minimal false-negative risk. The LR model, with transparent coefficient structure and good diagnostic efficacy, can serve as a quantitative auxiliary tool for preoperative staging and treatment decision-making, providing an objective basis for precise GC diagnosis and treatment. Further multi-center external prospective validation is mandatory before formal clinical deployment.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.51878/educational.v6i4.15821.title: PENGARUH METODE PEMBELAJARAN OUTDOOR LEARNING TERHADAP HASIL BELAJAR SISWA PADA MATA PELAJARAN PJOK KELAS V
doi:10.51878/educational.v6i4.15821.abstract:
<jats:p>Physical Education, Sports, and Health (PJOK) instruction in elementary schools frequently faces low student motivation and academic achievement due to conventional classroom-confined routines that restrict physical exploration. This pedagogical gap necessitates the implementation of contextual, nature-based learning methods capable of simultaneously stimulating kinesthetic activity and cognitive mastery. This study aims to determine the effect of the outdoor learning method on the PJOK learning outcomes of fifth-grade students concerning rounders/kasti games at SDN 060921 Medan Sunggal during the 2025/2026 academic year. A quantitative experimental approach with a one-group pretest-posttest design was utilized, involving 24 students from Class V-A selected through a purposive sampling technique. Data were collected via a 20-item multiple-choice achievement test, an observation checklist, and a student questionnaire, all validated through expert judgment. Inferential data analysis included the Shapiro-Wilk normality test and hypothesis testing using a paired-sample t-test processed via SPSS version 25 at a 5% significance level. The results revealed that the mean pretest score of 65.00 increased significantly to 78.33 in the posttest, accompanied by a Product Moment correlation coefficient of r = 0.717. The hypothesis test yielded t_"calculated" =4.621>t_"table" =2.074 with a significance value of 0.000 (< 0.05); therefore, H_0 was rejected and H_a was accepted. In conclusion, the outdoor learning method exerts a positive and significant effect on elementary school students' PJOK learning outcomes.
ABSTRAK
Pembelajaran Pendidikan Jasmani, Olahraga, dan Kesehatan (PJOK) di sekolah dasar sering kali menghadapi kendala rendahnya motivasi dan ketuntasan belajar akibat dominasi instruksi konvensional di dalam kelas yang membatasi ruang eksplorasi fisik siswa. Kesenjangan empiris ini menuntut diterapkannya metode pembelajaran kontekstual berbasis alam terbuka yang mampu merangsang keaktifan kinestetik dan pemahaman kognitif siswa secara bersamaan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh metode pembelajaran outdoor learning terhadap hasil belajar siswa pada mata pelajaran PJOK materi permainan kasti di kelas V SDN 060921 Medan Sunggal Tahun Pembelajaran 2025/2026. Pendekatan yang digunakan adalah kuantitatif eksperimen dengan desain one-group pretest-posttest design yang melibatkan 24 peserta didik kelas V-A yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan instrumen tes hasil belajar pilihan ganda sebanyak 20 butir soal, lembar observasi keterlaksanaan, dan angket respon siswa yang telah divalidasi ahli. Analisis data inferensial dilakukan melalui uji normalitas Shapiro-Wilk dan pengujian hipotesis menggunakan paired sample t-test berbantuan SPSS versi 25 pada taraf signifikansi 5%. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan nilai rata-rata pretest sebesar 65,00 meningkat menjadi 78,33 pada saat posttest, serta nilai korelasi Product Moment sebesar r=0,717. Pengujian hipotesis menghasilkan nilai t_"hitung" =4,621>t_"tabel" =2,074 dengan nilai signifikansi 0,000 < 0,05, sehingga H_0 ditolak dan H_a diterima. Dengan demikian, metode pembelajaran outdoor learning terbukti berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap peningkatan hasil belajar PJOK siswa sekolah dasar.
 
 </jats:p>

doi:10.52060/jppm.v7i2.4738.title: Pemberdayaan <i>Creative pedagogic</i> Guru Fisika dalam Mengimplementasikan Prinsip <i>Deep Learning</i> di Tulang Bawang Barat
doi:10.52060/jppm.v7i2.4738.abstract: <jats:p>Proses pembelajaran fisika di tingkat menengah umumnya masih didominasi oleh metode konvensional satu arah dan pengujian kognitif tingkat rendah, sehingga menghambat pemahaman konseptual mendalam serta keterampilan berpikir kritis dan kreatif peserta didik. Program pengabdian masyarakat berbasis penelitian aksi ini bertujuan untuk menguatkan keterampilan guru fisika di Kabupaten Tulang Bawang Barat dalam merancang Creative pedagogic berbasis prinsip Deep Learning. Mengadaptasi kerangka Teacher Professional Development (TPD) berkelanjutan, intervensi dilaksanakan melalui pendekatan Participatory Action Research (PAR) yang meliputi empat siklus: perencanaan (plan), tindakan (act), observasi/pendampingan (observe), dan refleksi (reflect). Subjek penelitian terdiri atas 19 guru fisika anggota MGMP Kabupaten Tulang Bawang Barat yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui angket evaluasi terstruktur pascapelatihan skala Likert 1-4, observasi keterlaksanaan pembelajaran, serta lembar validasi produk perangkat ajar. Hasil analisis statistik deskriptif menunjukkan bahwa program ini sangat efektif meningkatkan kompetensi profesional dan pedagogik guru. Dimensi kualitas materi dan penjelasan narasumber masing-masing memperoleh rerata skor 3,75 (93,7%) dan 3,80 (95,0%) dalam kategori Sangat Baik. Peningkatan pemahaman konsep Deep Learning dan keterampilan merancang Creative pedagogic guru mencapai rerata 3,63 (90,8%), serta pemahaman wawasan profesional mencapai skor tertinggi 3,89 (97,25%). Sebanyak 100% peserta berhasil menyusun modul ajar, LKPD berbasis fenomena kontekstual, dan instrumen asesmen HOTS yang valid. Pembentukan komunitas praktik di forum MGMP menjamin keberlanjutan penerapan Deep Learning secara mandiri.</jats:p>

doi:10.30703/cije.1853710.title: New Generation Learning: Integrating Bloom’s Digital Taxonomy into Mathematics Education
doi:10.30703/cije.1853710.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Today, integrating technology into the instructional process has become an essential component of students’ learning experiences. However, research examining the pedagogical effects of Bloom’s Digital Taxonomy in education remains limited. This study aims to investigate the effect of mathematics instruction based on Bloom’s Digital Taxonomy on students’ academic achievement and to explore students’ views regarding the instructional process. The sample consisted of 20 eighth-grade students enrolled in a public middle school in the 2024-2025 academic year. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed. Quantitative data were obtained using an achievement test prepared by the researchers, while qualitative data were collected through a written open-ended questionnaire. The quantitative findings indicated that instructional process based on Bloom’s Digital Taxonomy significantly increased students’ academic achievement. According to the qualitative findings, students expressed their views on the instructional process under four categories: positive experiences, negative experiences, contributions to the learning experience, and recommendations. Overall, the study offers a practice-oriented framework for designing technology-supported and student-centered learning environments.</jats:p>

doi:10.1021/jacs.6c12620.title: Cross-Scale Discovery of Surface Ligand-Modified Nanoparticles via Combined Transfer-Cascade Machine Learning
doi:10.1021/jacs.6c12620.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Surface ligand-modified nanoparticles (SMNPs), which immobilize surface ligands on nanoscale scaffolds, represent important nanomaterials for diverse applications. While surface ligands critically dictate the functions of SMNPs, their systematic discovery remains elusive. The major challenge in using artificial intelligence to predict and screen effective surface ligands and SMNPs across extensive chemical space is the scarcity of high-quality, standardized data sets. This impedes SMNP nanotechnology and leaves an enormous functional landscape largely unmapped. For antibacterial gold nanoparticles, available surface-ligand data sets are extremely sparse (&lt;102), whereas public small-molecule libraries exceed 1010 entries. Here, we introduce a cross-scale (from small molecules to nanoparticles) transfer-cascade learning framework, called TRADE, that transforms the structural–activity patterns of molecular antibiotics into predictive principles for the surface ligands of nanoparticle antibiotics. Within TRADE, we chemically deconstruct molecular antibiotics into conserved scaffolds and variable substituents for transfer learning and combine a multitier, coarse-to-fine cascade to narrow the search space. We identify a new class of 24 surface ligands with high predicted antibacterial efficacy for decorating gold nanoparticles across over 9 million molecules. The leading auricidin inhibits bacterial peptidoglycan biosynthesis and demonstrates potent antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens, including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium, with minimum inhibitory concentrations as low as 0.5–1 μg/mL. Across multiple animal infection models, auricidin exhibits exceptional therapeutic efficacy and robustness, superior to vancomycin, minimal toxicity, and low susceptibility to resistance evolution. This work proposes an intelligent strategy for discovering new functional nanoscale entities by integrating cross-domain transfer and cascade learning.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>
                    Clay content is an important determinant of soil physical and chemical behaviour, influencing water retention, nutrient availability, and agricultural productivity. Accurate spatial prediction of clay distribution is therefore important for digital soil mapping and sustainable land management. Clay content varied substantially (2.3–71.0%), with the ML models predicting higher values mainly along drainage corridors and lower landscape positions. Mean annual precipitation, elevation, Topographic Position Index, EVI, and slope showed the highest mean SHAP importance, although their relative contributions varied among models. Cubist achieved the highest validation accuracy (R

doi:10.1201/9781042044696-18.title: Intelligent Navigation System Design for Underwater Robot Using Reinforcement Learning
doi:10.1201/9781042044696-18.abstract: Underwater robots are becoming vital tools for ocean exploration, environmental monitoring, and underwater infrastructure inspection, yet their navigation remains a major challenge due to dynamic ocean currents, noisy sensor data, and the absence of GPS. Reinforcement Learning (RL) presents a powerful solution by allowing Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) to learn adaptive behaviors from experience instead of relying solely on predefined rules. This study provides a comprehensive review of nine key RL approaches designed for AUV navigation; model-free RL, model-based RL, policy gradient methods, hierarchical RL, multi-agent RL, safe RL, curriculum RL, imitation learning with RL, and RL combined with perception and SLAM. Each approach is analyzed through representative research works, examining their methodologies, implementations, and outcomes to understand how they tackle underwater navigation challenges. To further validate these insights, four prominent RL algorithms; DQN, DDQN, PPO, and SAC; were implemented and tested in a simulated underwater environment with currents and obstacles. Their performance was evaluated based on path smoothness, obstacle avoidance, goal achievement, and adaptability to dynamic conditions, with PPO showing the most balanced and reliable performance, DDQN offering better stability than DQN, and SAC displaying promise but with consistency issues. Overall, this work highlights the strengths and limitations of various RL strategies for underwater navigation and outlines future research directions, including real-world validation, improved sensor fusion, and multi-AUV collaboration, to drive the development of more intelligent and resilient underwater robotic systems.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62933-1.title: Multi-agent deep reinforcement learning for resilient recovery of electric–gas coupled energy systems under extreme disasters
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-62933-1.abstract: Under extreme disasters, there are still significant gaps in the cascading failure propagation and collaborative recovery decision-making of electric-gas coupled integrated energy systems, making it difficult to form effective dynamic recovery paths under high uncertainty conditions. This paper constructs a Markov decision process environment under disaster conditions, setting multi-dimensional state variables including node fault states, pressure and voltage distribution, and recovery resource constraints. It employs Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MA-DRL) combined with a centralized training and distributed execution architecture. Policy coordination between the power grid subsystem and the gas grid subsystem is achieved through joint action value evaluation and local policy execution. A cross-round reward structure is designed to cover factors such as energy availability, recovery speed, and recovery stability. A curriculum learning mechanism is introduced to address the exploration failure and reward signal sparsity that arise when policies are directly trained under high-disturbance conditions: by organizing training scenarios in order of ascending disaster intensity, the policy first acquires stable recovery behavior in low-disturbance environments and progressively transfers this structure to extreme disturbance conditions, yielding accelerated convergence and robust generalization across disaster scenarios. Delay effect modeling is incorporated to propagate the long-term consequences of repair decisions back to the learning signal. Experimental results show that, under disaster intensity level IV, the proposed MA-DRL collaborative recovery strategy achieves a system energy availability rate of 82.4% within 0–3 h post-disaster; during the post-disaster collaborative recovery process, the overall recovery completion time is 5.7 h, and the proportion of stable operation after recovery reaches 93.1%. This research demonstrates the effective path and technological potential of deep reinforcement learning in enhancing the resilience of coupled energy systems.

doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03254-z.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance at predicting diverse genomic modalities, yet their promise for biological discovery lies in how they are used after demonstrating their predictive performance. Here we describe the functionality of tangermeme, a highly optimized toolkit for ‘everything-but-the-model’ when it comes to genomic deep learning, and demonstrate how tangermeme can be used to distill the learned

doi:10.5815/ijitcs.2026.05.07.title: Comprehensive Feature Fusion in Deep Learning Models for Robust Epileptic Seizure Detection from EEG Signals
doi:10.5815/ijitcs.2026.05.07.abstract: <jats:p>Epilepsy is a prevalent neurological disorder characterized by recurrent epileptic seizures. After a stroke, it is a highly common neurological condition. For identifying seizures, the Electroencephalogram (EEG) is the gold-standard modality for capturing and recording the brain's electrical activity with high temporal resolution. The existing machine learning approaches have been leveraged before the emergence of deep learning. However, these models limited the performance as they included handcrafted features. The deep learning models perform the feature extraction automatically, which improves the classification accuracy compared with the conventional strategies. Therefore, in this article, an epileptic seizure detection approach on the basis of deep learning methods is developed to identify the abnormal brain functionalities in the initial stage. Initially, the EEG signal collection is carried out through standard benchmark databases. After that, the spectral and statistical features are directly extracted from the acquired EEG signals. Subsequently, the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) is applied to transform the EEG signals into spectrograms, and then the features from those spectrograms are extracted via Vision Transformer (ViT). Furthermore, the Wave-based features are also extracted, which provide a comprehensive view of the brain activities. After that, a Coordinate Attention-based Feature Fusion mechanism is employed to fuse these diverse feature types, which captures complementary details from the EEG signals. The fused features are subjected to the Adaptive Dilated dense Recurrent neural Network with a Novel Activation Function (ADRNet-NAF) for the Epileptic seizure detection. The detection accuracy of the proposed model is improved by optimizing the hyperparameters of the ADRNet-NAF model using Modernized Exploration of Magnificent Frigatebird Optimization (MEMFO) during network training. The empirical analysis over the traditional methods is conducted to validate the Epileptic seizure detection performance of the proposed model using various measures. The proposed model achieves 94.98% accuracy, 89.30% sensitivity and 99.08% specificity.</jats:p>

doi:10.5815/ijitcs.2026.05.04.title: Early Detection and Prediction of Osteopenia: A Pathway to Enhanced Bone Health using Machine Learning
doi:10.5815/ijitcs.2026.05.04.abstract: <jats:p>Early identification of osteopenia, an easy indicator of osteoporosis, is essential for fracture preventative measures and the restoration of long-term bone wellness. This research sets up and assesses a machine learning screening framework designed for detecting the beginning of osteopenia, utilizing enhanced clinical datasets that include demographic, medical, and bone health variables. The Custom Weighted Ensemble Model, through a comparative analysis with different classification algorithms, obtained the highest accuracy of 98.69%, surpassing standard models including Random Forest and Gradient Boosting, both at 98.48%. The ensemble approach demonstrates enhanced precision and F1-scores, underscoring its effectiveness in balancing both precision and sensitivity compared with prior research which concentrates primarily on osteoporosis. This investigation demonstrates the initial stage of osteopenia detection along with it suggests that optimized ensemble strategies significantly improve predictive performance. The findings indicate the potential of data-driven models to enhance preventive bone health care and decrease the risk of future fractured bones. Early recognition of osteopenia—widely noticed as the impassive initial level for osteoporosis—is essential for safeguarding the health of bones and avoiding severe fractures. This paper presents a detailed review of existing methodologies for diagnosing and predicting osteopenia, with a focus on the comprehensive overview of machine learning (ML). By combining insights from significant studies on osteoporosis prediction and choosing a comprehensive dataset incorporating with demographic, medical, and bone health parameters, we reveal essential predictive factors. Additionally, we offer a state-of-the-art framework for creating reliable machine learning models specifically suited for early detection. This study highlights how data-driven innovation can improve clinical care, slow the progression of osteopenia, and pave the way for a future free of fractures.</jats:p>

doi:10.54254/2753-8818/2027.mb37493.title: Per-Structure ROI-Weighted Loss Improves DVH Accuracy in Deep Learning-Based Radiotherapy Dose Prediction on the OpenKBP Benchmark
doi:10.54254/2753-8818/2027.mb37493.abstract: <jats:p>Radiotherapy dose prediction networks usually train with a single, spatially uniform loss such as voxel-wise mean absolute error (MAE), which weights errors in small, clinically critical structures the same as errors in unremarkable tissue. This study uses the official OpenKBP benchmark to test whether adding a per-structure, region-of-interest (ROI)-weighted term to a standard masked-MAE loss improves dose-volume histogram (DVH) accuracy without degrading dose accuracy. A 3-D U-Net dose predictor was reimplemented in PyTorch on the official OpenKBP data split (200/40/100 patients). Nine training runs varied loss (MAE baseline, MAE + ROI-weighted, ROI-only ablation), filter count, λ, and seed. The primary analysis compared the baseline and proposed losses at the main model capacity on the held-out 100-patient test set with a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test and the Hodges–Lehmann estimator, under a prespecified plan. The proposed loss reduced dvh_error for 99/100 test patients (mean 3.58 → 2.44 Gy; Hodges–Lehmann −1.13 Gy, 95% CI [−1.23, −1.04]; p = 4.5×10⁻¹⁸), supporting the primary hypothesis. dose_error also decreased (3.57 → 3.36 Gy) rather than being traded off. The effect held in direction under an independent seed and a smaller capacity, and an ablation confirmed the global MAE term remains necessary: removing it left dose_error far worse while leaving dvh_error unimproved. A simple, architecture-agnostic per-structure ROI-weighted term, added to rather than substituted for a standard masked-MAE loss, produced a robust, directionally consistent improvement in DVH accuracy on the OpenKBP benchmark without an offsetting dose-accuracy cost.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1917092.title: Early warning of academic risk from the first four weeks of online learning activity and assessment performance: a leakage-controlled, demographic-data-minimizing study on the OULAD benchmark
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1917092.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Early warning systems may identify academic risk while support remains possible, but published evaluations often use late-course data, sensitive background information, or leakage-prone splits. We tested prediction from the first four weeks of virtual learning environment activity and assessment performance, quantified the contribution of background/administrative data, and examined transfer across cohorts and modules. Using the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset (32,593 enrollments; analytic
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" id="IM1">
                        <mml:mi>n</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>=</mml:mo>
                        <mml:mn>27,553</mml:mn>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    still registered at day 28; 10.7 million activity records), we predicted failure or subsequent withdrawal from 13 behavioral and 9 background/administrative features. Splits and bootstrap resampling were grouped by student, with model selection by grouped cross-validation. The selected in-pool model reached ROC-AUC 0.7747 (student-cluster 95% CI 0.7624–0.7870); behavior alone reached 0.7504, a difference of 0.0243 (95% CI 0.0165–0.0321). A strict availability analysis excluding early grades, whose release date OULAD does not record, retained all-feature AUC 0.7381. At the operational top 5%, precision fell from 0.938 to 0.866 without the background set in-pool and from 0.746 to 0.569 across years. Subgroup disparities persisted after removal; the only gap surviving multiplicity correction was gender for the behavior-only model (0.054 AUC), and removal widened this gap in the main paired analysis. Thus, data minimization is not by itself a fairness remedy. Selection confined to 2013 chose an all-feature random forest that reached AUC 0.7470 (95% CI 0.7393–0.7549) in 2014. Transfer to unseen modules was uneven (0.64–0.79); an exploratory seven-module comparison found the weakest transfer where no assessment fell inside the prediction window, an association that is explicitly non-causal. The findings support a prospective, locally validated pilot of a week-four risk-ranking component without background profiling, provided subgroup performance is audited and calibration is assessed using completed cohorts before each new presentation. Code and outputs make every reported number traceable. This study establishes predictive feasibility, not that alerts or support interventions improve student outcomes.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s12882-026-05419-6.title: Development and interpretability of a machine learning-derived model for predicting the risk of subsequent short-term infection in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis: a retrospective cohort study
doi:10.1186/s12882-026-05419-6.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Infections are a major cause of mortality in hemodialysis patients, but early risk stratification remains difficult. This study developed and validated an interpretable ML model using routine baseline laboratory data to predict short-term infection risk.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A retrospective cohort of 622 hemodialysis patients with uremia was analyzed. The primary outcome was a confirmed infectious event (infection, sepsis, or pneumonia) occurring within a 2-month follow-up. To rigorously prevent data leakage, the cohort was strictly partitioned into training (70%) and test (30%) sets prior to missing value imputation and any downstream preprocessing. A LightGBM-based forward feature selection was executed exclusively within the training set. Nine ML algorithms were evaluated, and model robustness was validated via nested cross-validation, repeated cross-validation, and bootstrap optimism correction. Interpretability was achieved using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Subsequent infections occurred in 157 patients (25.2%). A parsimonious six-biomarker signature (CysC, HCT, TP, MONO_pct, MYO, ADA) was identified. The K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and LightGBM models demonstrated robust discriminative performance (Test AUROC: 0.727 and 0.719, respectively). Nested cross-validation confirmed generalization stability (e.g., ANN mean AUC: 0.722). SHAP analysis revealed elevated Cystatin C and lowered Hematocrit as the strongest contributors to the model’s risk ranking. Although the model showed high ranking ability, the default 0.5 threshold yielded low sensitivity; a prespecified F2‑optimized threshold of 0.30 improved sensitivity to 0.723 in the test set.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This interpretable machine learning‑based predictive model, using routinely available laboratory data, may serve as a potential adjunctive decision‑support tool for stratifying short‑term infection risk. External validation is required before clinical implementation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.58578/mikailalsys.v4i3.12265.title: Development of Interactive Learning Media Using the Genially Platform for Grade XI History Education in Senior High School
doi:10.58578/mikailalsys.v4i3.12265.abstract: <jats:p>A needs analysis at SMAN 1 Situjuah Limo Nagari identified a need for visual and interactive media to enhance student engagement and support understanding of historical events, figures, and chronology in Grade 11 history instruction. This study aimed to develop interactive learning media using Genially and assess its validity, practicality, and effectiveness. A research and development approach was employed using the ADDIE model, comprising analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. The product was validated by one subject-matter expert and two media experts. Practicality was assessed among Grade 11 students at the school, while effectiveness was evaluated using pretest and posttest scores from 33 students in Grade 11 class F2. Following revision, the two media experts assigned validation scores of 81.17% and 91.76%, categorized as valid and highly valid, respectively. Subject-matter validation yielded a mean score of 4.70, categorized as highly valid, while the practicality assessment yielded a mean score of 4.88, categorized as highly practical. Mean test scores increased from 48.18 on the pretest to 88.48 on the posttest, with a normalized gain score of 0.78, categorized as high. These findings indicate that the developed media met the study’s validity, practicality, and effectiveness criteria within the evaluated setting. The Genially-based media offers an alternative resource for diversifying history instruction and supporting interactive learning.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11163942/v1.title: Integrating UAV-Based Remote Sensing and Deep Learning for Early Detection of Bacterial Leaf Blight in Rice
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11163942/v1.abstract: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB) in rice can severely reduce rice yield, affecting farmers’ income when not detected early, missing the opportunity for timely management. The current popularity of unmanned aerial vehicles for crop health monitoring can be leveraged to detect early occurrence of BLB with the integration of machine learning for classifying plant disease severity and incidence. By deploying a UAV equipped with RGB sensor which was used to capture images during rice crop growth and development across two seasons from BLB inoculated field trials in the Philippines. The datasets obtained from the images were classified via transfer learning from pre-trained YOLOv26 deep learning model. The baseline YOLOv26 model was trained using transfer learning. Results indicated average classification accuracy of 75.94% for the three treatments across different days after inoculation. By feature extraction on the images across periods, BLB was detectable as early as 12 and 15 days after inoculation in wet season achieving high prediction accuracy range of 90.91% and 95.45%, respectively, for SL8H and IR24 medium treatments. This indicate that while UAV-based model using YOLOv26 is effective in distinguishing disease gradients and promising results for early detection of BLB, further refinement in accurate image acquisition on BLB infection in the field can enhance model performance, stability and better agreement with manual phenotyping.

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78295-1.title: Reward function compression facilitates goal-dependent reinforcement learning
doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78295-1.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Humans can uniquely assign value to novel, abstract outcomes to support reinforcement learning. However, this flexibility is cognitively costly and reduces learning efficiency. We propose that goal-dependent learning initially relies on capacity-limited working memory. With consistent experience, learners create a compressed reward function — a simplified rule — that transfers to long-term memory for automatic evaluation upon receiving feedback. This automaticity frees working memory resources, thereby boosting learning efficiency. Across six experiments, we demonstrate that learning is impaired by the size of the goal space but improves when this space allows for compression. Additionally, faster reward processing correlates with better learning. Although the algorithmic details remain to be established, computational modeling revealed that individual differences in compression efficiency, proxied by reward processing speed, led to higher choice accuracy. Together, our behavioral results and computational models suggest that efficient goal-directed learning relies on compressing complex goals into stable reward functions.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11036828/v1.title: Machine Learning Classification of Global Seismic Phases: A Cross-Validated, Physics-Informed Evaluation Using the IMS2.0 Automatic Arrival Bulletin
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11036828/v1.abstract: The International Monitoring System (IMS) of the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization (CTBTO) monitors the seismic activity around the clock worldwide by detecting, locating and characterizing seismic events. A high-density arrival bulletin was produced using the IMS2.0 automatic processing pipeline with over 1000 seismic phase picks on 15 August 2026 on global array and three component seismic stations. This research interest focuses on the physical and statistical properties of these arrivals, as well as on testing the performance of a Random Forest classifier using parametric metadata such as azimuth, slowness, signal to noise ratio, amplitude and duration. The results showed that there is a clear coherence of the teleseismic P phase, the regional crustal phase is mostly confused, and the T phase and noise-like detection remain a significant problem. The classifier achieved an overall accuracy of 0.87, demonstrating the potential of machine learning to enhance automatic seismic phase identification within IMS2.0 workflows. These results underscore the importance of combining physical seismology and state-of-the-art machine learning techniques in order to enhance the global monitoring network and the verification operations of the CTBTO.
