doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202659451.title: Estimating redshift distributions of Fermi blazars with multiple machine-learning models
doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202659451.abstract:
<jats:p>Approximately half of the Fermi-LAT-detected blazars lack spectroscopic redshift measurements, which limits population studies and investigations of the cosmological evolution of the gamma-ray blazar population.
We aim to develop a multi-model ensemble framework to systematically evaluate the performance of machine-learning models for blazar redshift estimation and provide predictive redshift probability distributions with quantified uncertainties for all blazars with  unknown redshifts.
We constructed an ensemble of 35 machine-learning regression models in the space. We combined predictions from the individual models to build nonparametric redshift probability density functions (PDFs) for each source, thereby explicitly characterizing the predictive uncertainty. We then stacked the source-level PDFs to derive population-level redshift distributions.
We find comparable predictive performance across the diverse models within our framework, indicating a feature-limited performance plateau. We compiled a catalog of predictive redshift distributions for 1590 blazars without measured redshifts. The stacked PDFs recover the characteristic double-peaked redshift structure of blazars without using source-class labels. For blazar candidates of uncertain type, the predicted redshift distribution exhibits a bimodal structure, suggesting a slightly larger contribution from FSRQ-like sources.
Our multi-model statistical framework achieves competitive predictive performance while retaining faint sources. We provide predicted redshift distributions with quantified uncertainties for 1590 blazars without measured redshifts, offering improved support for population and evolutionary studies. More broadly, this approach highlights the practical value of uncertainty-aware multi-model regression ensembles in astronomical data analysis.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10305486/v1.title: Auditable Federated Learning for Multimodal Brain Tumor Classification under Label Skew and Client Dropout
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10305486/v1.abstract: Federated learning (FL) allows hospitals to collaboratively train deep learning models without exchanging patient images, but reported FL studies in medical imaging often assume independent and identically distributed (IID) client data and full participation in every communication round both conditions seldom hold in real clinical networks. Furthermore, although the entire premise of FL rests on the iterative averaging of client weight updates, the optimisation dynamics of those weights are rarely audited at the round level, limiting clinicians' and regulators' ability to inspect how the global model evolves under stress. This study presents an auditable federated framework for binary brain-tumour classification from a combined multimodal dataset of 4618 axial computed-tomography (CT) and 5000 magnetic-resonance imaging (MRI) slices, totalling 9618 labelled images. A lightweight three-block convolutional neural network is trained across five simulated clients using FedProx with proximal coefficient µ = 0.01 and FedAvg aggregation, under two contrasting client partitions: an IID scenario in which each client receives a balanced sample of healthy and tumour cases, and a deliberately aggressive non-IID scenario in which each client is assigned an 80% majority class. Clinically realistic stress is added by dropping a randomly chosen client in approximately 30% of rounds. At every round, for every active client, the framework records three weight summaries initial (received from the server), updated (after local training), and aggregated (new global model) together with per-client accuracy, loss, precision, recall, F1-score, communication payload, wall-clock round time, and process memory. After ten communication rounds, the global model attains 96.05% accuracy and an F1-score of 0.9641 on the held-out test set under the IID partition, and 94.96% accuracy with F1 0.9547 under the 80% label-skew non-IID partition, corresponding to an IID-to-non-IID degradation of only 1.09 percentage points despite the severe class skew and 30% per-round client dropout. Inspection of the weight-audit trace reveals a consistent and measurable shift in the output-layer mean under non-IID training that is invisible in conventional accuracy curves, suggesting that round-level weight auditing can serve as a lightweight forensic signal of distributional drift in federated medical AI.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10305486/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1932626.title: A multi-class fundus disease classification framework based on self-supervised contrastive learning and dual-branch network
doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1932626.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Fundus diseases including diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and age-related macular degeneration are primary causes of blindness worldwide. Manual interpretation of retinal images is time-consuming and heavily reliant on clinical expertise. Although deep learning has shown promise in automated fundus image analysis, its performance remains highly data-dependent, requiring large amounts of expert annotations. Moreover, single-architecture models may have limited capacity to capture the diverse pathological features present in fundus images.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study proposes a unified framework integrating self-supervised contrastive pre-training with a hybrid dual-branch architecture. Pre-training on unlabeled fundus images enables the model to learn generalizable representations, thereby reducing reliance on manual annotations. The dual-branch design combines EfficientNet-B4 for fine-grained detail extraction and MambaOut for large receptive field modeling. Their outputs are adaptively fused via a learnable cross-fusion module. A dendritic classifier is adopted to further improve classification performance. Comprehensive evaluations were conducted on two public datasets, OIHC and FIVES.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>On the OIHC dataset, the proposed model achieved an F1-score of 96.32 ± 0.38% and a Kappa coefficient of 95.89 ± 0.43%. On the FIVES dataset, it attained 95.10 ± 0.54% and 93.49 ± 0.71%. The macro-average AUC exceeded 98% on both datasets. Ablation studies demonstrated the contribution of each component to the overall performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study indicates that combining self-supervised pre-training with a hybrid dual-branch architecture is a feasible approach for multi-class fundus disease classification. Interpretability analyses suggest that the model's attention regions partially overlap with clinically relevant pathological features. The framework achieved competitive performance on both datasets, showing its potential utility in scenarios with limited annotated data. Future work will focus on multi-center validation and model compression for lightweight architecture design.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1186/s12909-026-10590-3.title: Creative drama and case-based learning for forgiveness education in difficult patient encounters among nursing students: a randomized controlled trial
doi:10.1186/s12909-026-10590-3.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to evaluate the effects of creative drama-supported and case-based forgiveness training on nursing students’ forgiveness of others and self-forgiveness in the context of difficult patient encounters.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Difficult patient behaviors may evoke negative emotions such as anger, frustration, and helplessness among nurses and nursing students. Although forgiveness has been suggested as a potential coping resource for managing these emotions, evidence regarding effective approaches for fostering forgiveness in nursing education remains limited.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A randomized controlled pretest-posttest study.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The study was conducted with 80 fourth-year nursing students enrolled in the nursing department of a university in eastern Türkiye. Participants were randomly assigned to either the creative drama group (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 40) or the case-based learning group (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 40). Data were collected using the Personal Information Form, the Forgiveness of Others Scale, and the Self-Forgiveness Scale. Both groups participated in four educational sessions (200 min in total). Data were analyzed using independent-samples
                      <jats:italic>t</jats:italic>
                      -test, paired-samples
                      <jats:italic>t</jats:italic>
                      -test, analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), Mann–Whitney U test, and Wilcoxon signed-rank test, as appropriate.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Both educational approaches significantly increased students’ forgiveness of others scores (
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001). However, after controlling for baseline Forgiveness of Others Scale scores using ANCOVA, posttest forgiveness of others scores were significantly higher in the creative drama group than in the case-based learning group (F(1, 77) = 12.899,
                      <jats:italic>p =</jats:italic>
                       0.001, partial η
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                       = 0.143). The creative drama intervention demonstrated a very large within-group effect (d = 1.42), whereas the case-based learning intervention demonstrated a large effect (d = 1.00). No significant changes were observed in self-forgiveness scores in either group (
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       > 0.05).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings suggest that forgiveness skills in the context of difficult patient encounters can be supported through structured educational interventions. Both creative drama and case-based learning increased nursing students’ forgiveness of others. However, creative drama produced a stronger effect, suggesting that experiential learning processes may be particularly effective in fostering forgiveness of others. In contrast, neither educational approach resulted in a significant improvement in self-forgiveness levels.</jats:p>

doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010131/v1.title: Machine Learning of Methacrylated Dextran Phase Separation for Prediction, Transferability, and Adaptation
doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010131/v1.abstract:
<jats:p>
                  Thermoresponsive polymers are promising materials for separations, sensing, drug delivery, and other biomedical applications, but their phase behavior depends on numerous polymer and solution variables, which creates a formulation space that is impractical to explore exhaustively by experiments. Here, we develop machine-learning (ML) models for predicting the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) of methacrylated dextran (Dex-MA), a biocompatible polysaccharide-based polymer, using 403 unique experimentally measured formulations spanning polymer molecular weight, degree of methacrylation, concentration, salts, surfactants, and other additives. The dataset is nonuniformly sampled because of practical synthesis constraints and application priorities. Despite this nonuniformity, descriptor-and molecular-embedding-based XGBoost and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models achieved mean absolute errors of 3.6
                  <jats:sup>o</jats:sup>
                  C to 3.7
                  <jats:sup>o</jats:sup>
                  C and 5.4
                  <jats:sup>o</jats:sup>
                  C to 5.7
                  <jats:sup>o</jats:sup>
                  C, respectively, for within-domain LCST prediction and mean phase-behavior classification accuracies of 89.4–89.6% and 85.3–86.6%, respectively. However, strong within-domain performance did not uniformly transfer to unseen formulation domains. Systematically withholding entire polymer, surfactant, and salt domains produced domain-dependent losses in predictive accuracy; for example, withholding 86 and 250 kDa Dex-MA increased LCST prediction errors to 11.4
                  <jats:sup>o</jats:sup>
                  C and 17.5
                  <jats:sup>o</jats:sup>
                  C, respectively, whereas errors for held-out surfactants were 5.6–7.2
                  <jats:sup>o</jats:sup>
                  C. Progressive incorporation of target-domain measurements recovered predictive accuracy, but the recovery rate varied substantially with additive and salt identity and polymer molecular weight. This work provides a framework not only for predicting thermoresponsive-polymer phase behavior but also for evaluating model transferability to new formulation domains and guiding experimental data collection for model adaptation.
                </jats:p>

doi:10.1002/jdd.70402.title: 3D‐Printed Models to Enhance Dental Anatomy Learning: Students’ Perspective
doi:10.1002/jdd.70402.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Mastering tooth morphology is essential for first‐year dental students, yet conventional teaching methods may not fully support spatial understanding of tooth anatomical structures. To provide students with an additional visual and tactile learning resource, we incorporated enlarged 3D‐printed tooth models into a dental anatomy course at the University of Maryland School of Dentistry. Students used the models to identify key anatomical landmarks before transitioning to waxing activities and subsequently provided feedback on their experience. Students generally found the enlarged models helpful for recognizing anatomical structures and building confidence with tooth morphology. However, some students still struggled to identify specific landmarks and highlighted the importance of timely instructor feedback. The experience suggests that enlarged 3D‐printed models can supplement traditional dental anatomy instruction, particularly when combined with structured guidance and faculty feedback.</jats:p>

doi:10.32782/2710-4656/2026.4/24.title: MACHINE TRANSLATION POST-EDITING COMPETENCE IN THE AGE OF GENERATIVE AI: A CORPUS-BASED INVESTIGATION OF STUDENT TRANSLATORS' SKILLS
doi:10.32782/2710-4656/2026.4/24.abstract:
<jats:p>The main aim of the article is to investigate how translation students interact with AI-generated translations and examines the relationship between AI literacy and post-editing performance. Using a corpus-based mixed-methods approach, the study compares human translation, neural machine translation post-editing, and generative AI post-editing. The findings reveal that generative AI improves fluency and lexical diversity but introduces AI-specific challenges, including hallucinations and contextual distortions. Statistical analysis demonstrates that AI literacy, critical evaluation skills, and prompt formulation abilities significantly influence post-editing quality. The study proposes an AI-enhanced MTPE competence framework integrating linguistic, technological, evaluative, and collaborative dimensions. The results contribute to current discussions on translator competence and provide practical recommendations for translator education in AI-mediated environments.
The study employs a mixed-methods research design combining corpus linguistics, quantitative statistical analysis, and qualitative thematic analysis. Data were collected from 60 undergraduate and graduate translation students divided into three groups: Human Translation (HT), Neural Machine Translation Post-Editing (NMTPE), and Generative AI Post-Editing (GAI-PE). The learner corpus consisted of approximately 90,000 words. Translation quality, error frequency, lexical diversity, and AI literacy indicators were analyzed using corpus tools and statistical procedures.
The study expands traditional translation competence models by incorporating AI literacy, prompt engineering, hallucination detection, and human–AI collaboration as essential dimensions of MTPE competence. Unlike previous studies focusing mainly on translation quality and productivity, this research examines how AI-related competencies influence student translators' performance in generative AI environments.
The findings indicate that generative AI enhances translation fluency and lexical richness while simultaneously creating risks associated with factual inaccuracies and hallucinations. AI literacy emerged as a significant predictor of post-editing performance, highlighting the growing importance of critical evaluation skills in translator training. The study concludes that future translator education should integrate AI literacy, prompt engineering, and critical assessment strategies to prepare students for technology-rich professional environments.</jats:p>

doi:10.1117/12.3113405.title: Object recognition in hazy conditions using deep learning
doi:10.1117/12.3113405.abstract: Object detection in traffic surveillance systems is significantly affected by adverse atmospheric conditions such as haze and fog, which reduce image contrast and obscure fine structural details. This study presents a systematic evaluation of deep-learning object detection architectures under progressively increasing atmospheric scattering. A custom dataset containing 13,627 traffic images and 26,932 object annotations across eight vehicle classes was used for the experiments. Synthetic haze was generated using the Koschmieder atmospheric scattering model, while monocular depth maps were estimated with the Depth Anything V2 (DAv2) model to produce realistic degradation at four scattering levels. Three detection frameworks were evaluated: a single-stage YOLO26 Nano detector, a conventional Faster R-CNN detector, and a hybrid architecture combining class-agnostic localization with ResNet50 classification. In addition, three training strategies, including an adaptive mixed-training approach, were compared using five-fold cross-validation. Experimental results demonstrate that the adaptive training strategy substantially improves robustness to atmospheric scattering. Among the evaluated models, the single-stage YOLO26 detector maintained the most stable detection performance under severe haze, outperforming both conventional two-stage detection and image restoration–based approaches. These findings suggest that exposure to physically modeled atmospheric degradation during training enables object detectors to learn features that generalize more effectively to adverse weather conditions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74806-8.title: PredKlebAMR: A machine learning framework prioritizing sensitivity in Klebsiella pneumoniae resistance profiling
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74806-8.abstract: The global increase in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) has undoubtedly changed the management of infectious diseases. Meropenem resistance in K. pneumoniae is a response to bacterial strategies, these includes production of carbapenemases (KPC, NDM, OXA-48), a reduction in membrane permeability through mutation of porin (OmpK35/36), and genomic plasticity via gene amplification and/or plasmid exchange. This study developed a machine learning model that targets “Very Major Errors” (VMEs) and predicts antimicrobial resistance (AMR) for prognosis. Genomic datasets (6000) were retrieved from the Bacterial and Viral Bioinformatics Resource Center (BV-BRC) database and preprocessed. Gene-based feature engineering was performed using Kleborate, and a Random Forest model was trained and deployed via an interactive R Shiny web application. Internal validation of the tool PredKlebAMR was done using a stratified 80/20 split of the training dataset, and a 5-fold cross-validation was implemented to optimize the Random Forest hyperparameters. While benchmarking against ResFinder 4.1 and AMRFinderPlus 4.2.7 was done using an independent external cohort consisting of three-tiered datasets from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) database. PredKlebAMR , trained using 5,942 K. pneumoniae genomes (38 Kleborate-derived predictors), achieved a strong performance on a held-out global test set (accuracy 91.92%, sensitivity 94.67%, specificity 89.47%; Kappa 0.839), with key predictors including fluoroquinolone mutations, high-risk sequence types, KPC-2/KPC-3, and OmpK35/36 porin changes. When benchmarked against AMRFinderPlus 4.2.7 and ResFinder 4.1, PredKlebAMR delivered a higher sensitivity and fewer VMEs in the global cohort (95.45% vs 90.91% | 86.36% sensitivity; VMEs 1 vs 2 | 3), the African cohort (95.56% vs 91.11% | 82.2% sensitivity; VMEs 2 vs 4 | 8), and the Thailand cohort (95.62% vs 92.5% | 63.12% sensitivity; VMEs 7 vs 12 | 59) with statistically significant sensitivity improvement in Africa (McNemar’s p = 0.041). PredKlebAMR, with its high sensitivity to VMEs, and via an interactive dashboard ( https://igmr.org/software/predklebamr ) that translates predictions into biological rationale, will support clinicians in making life-changing decisions while managing patients.

doi:10.3389/fneur.2026.1951986.title: A robust adversarial learning framework for EEG emotion recognition
doi:10.3389/fneur.2026.1951986.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Electroencephalography (EEG) provides an objective means of capturing neural patterns associated with emotion, but substantial inter-subject variability limits the ability of existing models to generalize to unseen subjects.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We propose a robust adversarial domain generalization framework for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition. In the first stage, long short-term memory-based encoders are jointly trained to learn domain-invariant and domain-specific representations using reconstruction, emotion classification, and adversarial domain objectives. This process preserves emotion-relevant information while suppressing subject-specific distribution shifts. In the second stage, the invariant encoder and emotion classifier are further refined through distributionally robust optimization with gradient-guided feature augmentation. Theframework is evaluated on the AMIGOS and DREAMER datasets using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The proposed method achieves mean accuracies of 69.94% and 68.97% and F1 scores of 0.59 and 0.65 on AMIGOS and DREAMER, respectively, outperforming the comparison methods on both datasets. Ablation results further show that adversarial learning provides the primary improvement in cross-subject generalization, while distributionally robust optimization offers complementary robustness.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings indicate that combining representation learning that is invariant across domains with distributionally robust optimization effectively reduces distribution shifts across subjects and improves EEG emotion recognition for unseen subjects.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/fneur.2026.1884682.title: A machine learning model for predicting cognitive improvement after scalp cluster needling therapy in patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment
doi:10.3389/fneur.2026.1884682.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Cognitive recovery varies substantially among patients with post-stroke mild cognitive impairment (PSCI-MCI), whereas individualized models for predicting post-treatment cognitive improvement remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a machine learning model for predicting cognitive improvement after 1 month of scalp cluster needling therapy with prolonged needle retention (SCNT-PR) in patients with PSCI-MCI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This retrospective study included hospitalized patients diagnosed with PSCI-MCI between January 1, 2010, and January 1, 2023. Baseline data included demographics, vascular risk factors, stroke severity, imaging features, cognitive and functional assessments, emotional and sleep-related indicators, treatment-related variables, and laboratory findings. The outcome was defined as an increase of at least 2 points in the corrected Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score after treatment compared with baseline. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and the Boruta algorithm were used to identify key predictors. Seven supervised machine learning algorithms were applied to develop pretreatment prediction models. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) were used for model interpretation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A total of 750 patients were included and randomly assigned to a training set (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 526) and a validation set (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 224). Seven key predictors were identified from the intersection of LASSO regression and Boruta. Among the evaluated models, LightGBM showed the acceptable performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.759. Calibration curves and decision curve analysis indicated acceptable calibration and favorable clinical utility. SHAP analysis identified baseline corrected MoCA score, years of education, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale total score, Barthel Index score for activities of daily living, age, frontal lobe lesion, and diabetes as the major contributors to model prediction. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated consistent predictor patterns under alternative outcome definitions and predictor configurations.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We developed and internally validated a machine learning model based on multidimensional pretreatment clinical data to predict cognitive improvement after SCNT-PR in patients with PSCI-MCI. This model may provide preliminary support for patient stratification and individualized clinical assessment, although external validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical implementation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1007/s00500-026-11554-x.title: Consider stock indices and technical indicators to conduct price forecasting for gold and oil: a reinforcement learning perspective
doi:10.1007/s00500-026-11554-x.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Rising oil prices often trigger inflation, whereas higher gold prices reflect risk aversion. Analyzing daily data from 2011 to 2025, this study proposes a novel framework to predict commodity prices: (1) raw materials, stock indices, and technical indicators are integrated as the predictors, (2) key performance indicators (KPIs) are identified using MARS (multivariate adaptive regression splines), RF (Random Forest), and XGB (eXtreme gradient boost), and (3) machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL) models including LSTM (long short-term memory) and GRU (gated recurrent unit), and reinforcement learning (RL) strategies such as A2C (advantage actor–critic) and PPO (proximal policy optimization) are compared. Specifically, one-shot splitting starts from 2011 to 2022 for training and uses 2023–2025 is for testing. In dynamic splitting, four-year training and one-month testing is adopted. Results show that average exchange rate of US dollar (USD), coal, India’s stock, Shanghai’s stock, US10YY (10-year yield rate of US treasury bond), Japan’s stock, DJI (US Dow Jones index), and NASDAQ (US technology index) affect oil prices while silver, S&P 500, German’s stock, SOX (US semiconductor index), India’s stock, and NASDAQ influence gold prices. Dynamic splitting and RL models outperform one-shot splitting because they can capture short-term variations and abrupt changes.</jats:p>

doi:10.59261/jequi.v8i4.440.title: Intelligent Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Power Transformers Using Machine Learning
doi:10.59261/jequi.v8i4.440.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: Power transformers play an integral role in power generation and transmission. Transformer failures can lead to service interruptions, reduce system reliability, and incur significant failure-related costs. Efficient transformer maintenance requires accurate condition assessment and effective maintenance decision-making.
Objective: The purpose of this paper is to develop a machine-learning-based decision-support framework for power transformer maintenance that integrates health index estimation, Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, and Life Cycle Cost (LCC) evaluation.
Methods: The framework draws on multimodal monitoring data from 166 oil-immersed power transformers collected over a ten-year period. Six machine learning models (XGBoost, Random Forest, Support Vector Regression, Convolutional Neural Networks, Ridge Regression, and K-Nearest Neighbors) were evaluated using various feature sets.
Results: Among the evaluated models, XGBoost achieved the best performance under the basic feature configuration, with an RMSE of 0.285 years, an MAE of 0.199 years, and an R² of 0.956. The robustness evaluation showed that the model retained satisfactory predictive performance under moderate feature reduction. Based on the Life Cycle Cost assumptions applied in this study, the predictive maintenance scenario was estimated to reduce the total cost of the transformer fleet by approximately 47%.
Conclusion: The proposed approach combines accurate RUL prediction with technical and economic analyses to provide a practical decision-making tool for transformer asset management.</jats:p>

doi:10.67167/vertex.754.abstract: <jats:p>This study assessed time management strategies and   the level of academic performance of Grade 5 Mathematics learners among the select public elementary Schools at Madridejos District, DepEd Cebu Province Division during School Year 2025-2026, as basis for Time Management Skills Activities. This study employed   descriptive-quantitative method of research. The respondents of this research were the Grade 5 Mathematics  learners among the select public elementary schools in Madridejos District of Cebu Province Division during the School Year 2025 – 2026.  The population has a total of 65 respondents with 10 teachers and 55 learners. The quality of Mathematics instruction is closely associated with teachers' professional competence, continuous learning, and instructional experience. Significant relationship between status of the time management   strategies and the academic performance of the grade 5 mathematics learners stating that there is no significant relationship between the status of the time management strategies and the academic performance of the Mathematics learners is partially rejected. The hypothesis is rejected for the dimensions and competencies where the computed probability values are less than the 0.05 level of significance, particularly in setting boundaries in Completing Homework, Balancing Time for School Work, and Balancing Time for Playing, while it is retained for dimensions where the probability values exceed the 0.05 alpha level. As a result, effective time management becomes an essential component of quality Mathematics instruction because it supports learner engagement, strengthens self-discipline, and provides greater opportunities for meaningful mathematical learning.  Findings provide empirical evidence that effective time management practices contribute meaningfully to improving learners' academic productivity in Mathematics and support the development of organized learning behaviors that facilitate mastery of the Most Essential Learning Competencies. Based on the conclusions reached in this research, it is highly Recommended “the Time Management Oriented Activities   can be   submitted to the concerned /  school officials for consideration and implementation.</jats:p>

doi:10.51178/jetl.v8i3.3752.title: Diksi dan Eufemisme dalam Komunikasi Pejabat Publik: Implikasi bagi Pembelajaran Bahasa Indonesia
doi:10.51178/jetl.v8i3.3752.abstract: <jats:p>Bahasa pejabat publik tidak hanya berfungsi sebagai sarana penyampaian informasi dan kebijakan, tetapi juga menjadi sumber daya strategis untuk membangun makna, mengelola persepsi publik, dan merespons tekanan sosial. Dalam konteks tersebut, pilihan diksi dan penggunaan eufemisme menjadi penting, terutama ketika pejabat menyampaikan isu sensitif seperti kontroversi kebijakan, kritik, kesalahan, dan keresahan masyarakat. Penelitian mengenai eufemisme dalam wacana politik telah menunjukkan bahwa bentuk bahasa tidak langsung dapat digunakan sebagai strategi retoris untuk memperhalus makna, membangun citra positif, dan mengelola respons publik. Namun, pemanfaatan komunikasi pejabat publik sebagai sumber pembelajaran bahasa Indonesia, khususnya untuk pengembangan literasi kritis, masih perlu dikaji lebih lanjut. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis bentuk, penggunaan kontekstual, dan fungsi komunikatif diksi serta eufemisme dalam komunikasi pejabat publik serta mengidentifikasi implikasinya bagi pembelajaran bahasa Indonesia. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif dengan analisis wacana berbasis korpus. Data berupa 40 pernyataan pejabat publik yang dikumpulkan dari konferensi pers, pidato resmi, dan komunikasi melalui media sosial resmi selama tahun 2026. Data didokumentasikan, diverifikasi berdasarkan sumber yang tersedia, kemudian dikodekan, dikategorikan, dan diinterpretasikan berdasarkan pilihan leksikal, konteks, referen, dan fungsi komunikatif. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan lima pola komunikasi awal, yaitu asertif, akomodatif, retoris-populis, evasif, dan defensif. Eufemisme paling menonjol dalam komunikasi defensif dan evasif, terutama melalui pilihan kata yang berfungsi memperhalus makna negatif, mengurangi kesan terhadap kritik atau persoalan, menunda kepastian, mengalihkan perhatian, dan mempertahankan citra positif pejabat. Temuan juga menunjukkan adanya kecenderungan penggunaan strategi kebahasaan yang berbeda pada saluran komunikasi yang berbeda. Secara pedagogis, data komunikasi pejabat publik berpotensi menjadi bahan ajar autentik untuk melatih peserta didik membedakan makna denotatif dan kontekstual, mengidentifikasi eufemisme, menafsirkan makna tersirat, serta mengembangkan kemampuan membaca wacana publik secara kritis.</jats:p>

doi:10.46453/jader.2035778.title: Comparative Machine Learning Approaches to Landslide Susceptibility in Southeastern Türkiye
doi:10.46453/jader.2035778.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards in mountainous regions, causing severe economic losses and infrastructure damage. Reliable susceptibility mapping is essential for hazard mitigation and sustainable land-use planning, particularly in tectonically active areas such as southeastern Türkiye. This study aims to compare the predictive performance and spatial consistency of six widely used machine learning algorithms—Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Naïve Bayes (NB), and Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt)—together with an Ensemble model, under identical geomorphological and environmental conditions. A GIS-based framework was applied using eleven conditioning factors derived from topographic, geological, hydrological, and land-cover datasets. A landslide inventory verified by field observations was used for model training and validation. Model performance was assessed using Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis and the Area Under the Curve (AUC). All models achieved high predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.877–0.959). The NB model performed best (AUC = 0.959), while the Ensemble model produced the most spatially consistent susceptibility patterns. High- and very high-susceptibility zones were consistently associated with steep slopes and weak lithological units. Comparative machine learning approaches provide reliable and transferable tools for regional landslide susceptibility assessment. The results highlight the importance of algorithm selection and ensemble strategies in susceptibility mapping.</jats:p>

doi:10.1142/s0218625x26501076.title: IMPROVED EDM PRECISION WITH ADVANCED ENSEMBLE MACHINE LEARNING PREDICTION FOR INC-625 SUPERALLOY
doi:10.1142/s0218625x26501076.abstract: <jats:p>This research examines the influence of the electrical discharge machining (EDM) parameters, including servo voltage, current, angle of cut, pulse-on and pulse-off times, on surface roughness (SR) and material removal rate (MRR) in the machining of the INC-625 superalloy. The L[Formula: see text] machining trials were conducted using Response Surface Methodology–Central Composite Design (RSM-CCD) to execute the machining trials. According to ANOVA, servo voltage was the most significant factor affecting both the SR (80.01%) and the MRR (77.33%). The SR decreased by 28.13% when the maximum servo voltage (70[Formula: see text]V) was employed and the MRR increased by 41.36% when the minimum servo voltage (50[Formula: see text]V) was employed. In addition, Desirability Analysis (DA) has been utilized to construct a response model to estimate the optimal setting values. Additionally, this study introduces a new heterogeneous ensemble machine learning model combining Ridge Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Neural Networks to predict EDM performance metrics. The model achieves high accuracy ([Formula: see text] for SR, [Formula: see text] for MRR) using an optimized weighted average ensemble model. The ensemble method effectively represents the complex relationship between important process parameters and machining outputs. The validated ensemble model enables real-time EDM process optimization and provides actionable parameter recommendations for different manufacturing objectives. For quality-focused machining, a high servo voltage (70[Formula: see text]V), low pulse-on time (8[Formula: see text] [Formula: see text]s), and low current (3[Formula: see text]A) produced the lowest SR. For productivity-focused machining, higher pulse-on time (16[Formula: see text] [Formula: see text]s) and current (5[Formula: see text]A) maximized MRR. A balanced machining strategy was achieved at intermediate parameter settings ([Formula: see text]s, [Formula: see text]s, [Formula: see text]–65[Formula: see text]V, [Formula: see text] [Formula: see text]A, [Formula: see text]), offering an effective compromise between machining efficiency and surface quality. These recommendations provide practical decision support guidelines for facilitating data-driven decision-making in industrial EDM applications.</jats:p>

doi:10.25258/ijddt.16.63s.53.title: DEEP LEARNING APPROACH FOR FRUIT QUALITY ANALYSIS
doi:10.25258/ijddt.16.63s.53.abstract: In order to maintain market standards and customer satisfaction, grading the quality of a fruit is a crucial procedure in the Agroprocessing sector.Grading has historically been done by hand using visual inspection, which is laborious, subjective, and vulnerable to human errors.The proposed work suggests an autonomous fruit quality evaluation system based on a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and deep learning approaches to get around these restrictions.Fruit photos are divided into three quality categories by the suggested system: Fresh, Mild, and Rotten.Training and validation are done using the FruQ-DB dataset.The dataset images are loaded into the unique CNN which automatically extract discriminative features from images after doing the necessary preprocessing steps.The suggested deep learning model outperforms conventional image processing and machine learning methods in terms of classification accuracy, according to experimental results.The system is effective, scalable, and appropriate for fruit grading applications in the real world.

doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.59687.title: The Effect of Learning Motivation on Junior High School Students’ Mathematical Representation Ability
doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.59687.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to examine the effect of learning motivation on junior high school students’ mathematical representation ability. This research employed a quantitative approach using a survey method. The population of this study consisted of all seventh-grade students at SMP Negeri 13 Semarang in the 2025/2026 academic year, with a sample of 30 students selected through cluster random sampling. The research instruments included a mathematical representation ability test and a learning motivation questionnaire. The data were analyzed using normality and linearity tests, followed by a simple linear regression test. The results showed that learning motivation has a positive and significant effect on students’ mathematical representation ability, as indicated by a significance value of 0.000 (< 0.05). The coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.486, meaning that learning motivation contributes 48.6% to students’ mathematical representation ability. This finding suggests that students with higher learning motivation tend to have better ability in representing mathematical ideas through various forms of representation. In conclusion, learning motivation plays an important role in improving students’ mathematical representation ability. Therefore, teachers are encouraged to enhance students’ motivation in order to support better mathematics learning outcomes.</jats:p>

doi:10.63944/yrms05.nhe.title: <i><b>Academic Leadership and Learning Effectiveness of Students at Yinhai Sanya High School in Nanning</b></i>
doi:10.63944/yrms05.nhe.abstract: <jats:p>The objectives of this research were 1) to examine the academic leadership of administrators at Yinhai Sanya High School in Nanning, China; 2) to examine the learning effectiveness of students at the school; and 3) to investigate the relationship between administrators’ academic leadership and students’ learning effectiveness. The sample consisted of 186 teachers and administrators purposively selected from a population of 360. The research instrument was a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire comprising 30 items across 10 dimensions of academic leadership and 20 items across three dimensions of learning effectiveness. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Pearson’s correlation coefficient. The findings revealed that: 1) the overall level of academic leadership was moderate (M = 3.406), with shared academic vision receiving the highest mean score (M = 3.548) and data-informed decision-making the lowest (M = 3.294); 2) the overall level of students’ learning effectiveness was moderate (M = 3.342), with academic performance receiving the highest mean score (M = 3.353) and learning strategies the lowest (M = 3.329); and 3) all dimensions of academic leadership were significantly and positively correlated with all dimensions of students’ learning effectiveness (p < .01). The strongest correlations were found between curriculum leadership and academic performance (r = .467), innovation support and academic performance (r = .443), and innovation support and learning strategies (r = .432).</jats:p>

doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.62114.title: Does Educational Background Matter? The Role of Competency Alignment in Learning Outcomes among Fashion Education Students
doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.62114.abstract: <jats:p>Students entering vocational higher education often have different secondary educational backgrounds, which are commonly assumed to influence their academic achievement. This study examined whether educational background affects learning outcomes when students learn competencies that are relatively new to all learners. A quantitative causal-comparative (ex post facto) design was employed involving 83 undergraduate students enrolled in the Fashion Education Study Program who had completed the Fabric Construction Techniques course. Participants were classified into graduates of SMK Fashion (n = 32) and graduates of senior high schools (SMA) or non-fashion vocational high schools (n = 51). Learning outcomes were analysed using descriptive statistics and an independent-samples t-test. Students from SMK Fashion achieved a slightly higher mean score than the comparison group (83.47 vs. 82.45), but the difference was not statistically significant, t(81) = 0.793, p = .430, with a small effect size (d = 0.18). These findings indicate that secondary educational background explained little variation in learning outcomes. The study suggests that academic performance in vocational higher education depends less on school type than on the alignment between prior learning experiences and university competencies. The findings highlight competency alignment as an important explanation of learning outcomes in vocational higher education.</jats:p>

doi:10.25258/ijddt.16.62s.33.title: Efficient Smart Home Energy Consumption Management Using IoT and Hybrid Deep Learning Models
doi:10.25258/ijddt.16.62s.33.abstract: Background: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has accelerated the development of sophisticated smart home solutions for efficient energy management.However, precisely estimating household energy consumption is still difficult due to the dynamic, nonlinear nature of appliance usage patterns.This study describes an IoT-enabled smart home energy consumption prediction system that uses machine learning and deep learning to increase energy efficiency and reduce excessive power use.Objective: In this paper, we aim to develop an efficient IoT-enabled smart home.This study analyzes smart home energy data using machine learning and deep learning approaches to increase prediction accuracy and reduce energy waste.Various classical, ensemble, and deep learning models are implemented and compared to determine the most effective technique for intelligent and sustainable energy management in smart homes.Material/methods: In this paper, we have used the 14-classifier to predict an efficient smart home using machine learning and deep learning.We utilized the Appliances Energy Prediction dataset to achieve the task.Out of the 14 classifiers, some are traditional, such as ET, RF, LR, XGBoost, LightGBM, KNN, GB, SVR, DT, and AdaBoost, and deep learning models like Hybrid LSTM-GRU, LSTM Network, Proposed Ensemble, and Optimized Extra Trees.Result: Our experimental observation revealed that the proposed Hybrid LSTM-GRU mode performs well, with an MAE of 5.21, an RMSE of 6.43, and an R² score of 0.9435, compared to the other models.The suggested framework improves the forecast of smart home energy consumption while also supporting intelligent, sustainable, and energyefficient IoT-based smart home management systems.

doi:10.48175/ijarsct-38763.title: Reinforcement Learning in Machine Learning
authors: Prerna Wayakole, Prof. P. P. Chavan
Prof. A. J. Shaikh , Dr. H. B. Jadhav
doi:10.48175/ijarsct-38763.abstract: <jats:p>Reinforcement Learning (RL) is a machine-learning approach for problems in which decisions are made repeatedly and their quality becomes clear through feedback. Instead of depending on a fixed collection of labelled answers, an RL agent interacts with an environment, observes its changing state, receives rewards or penalties, and improves its decision policy through experience. This review examines the basic RL framework and discusses deep reinforcement learning, offline learning, multi-agent systems, and human-guided learning. Applications in robotics, games, education, finance, healthcare, and autonomous systems are considered. The review also identifies sample inefficiency, computational cost, instability, delayed rewards, limited generalization, and safety as important challenges. The paper concludes by identifying research opportunities for efficient, reliable, explainable, and adaptable RL systems.</jats:p>

doi:10.15294/jcs.v9i3s.57489.title: Development of Google Sites-Based Learning Media Integrated with Wizer.me Using CBL-STEM Approach for Relations and Functions
doi:10.15294/jcs.v9i3s.57489.abstract: <jats:p>Advances in digital technology call for innovative, interactive mathematics learning media to facilitate the understanding of abstract concepts, such as relations and functions. This research and development study aims to describe the design process, the level of technical feasibility, and the effectiveness of using Google Sites-based learning media integrated with Wizer.me interactive digital worksheets. Using a descriptive method in a limited-scale pilot study, the study subjects included 32 eighth-grade students from Class VIII-F at SMP Negeri 15 Semarang and a mathematics teacher serving as an expert validator. Data were collected through validation sheets, classroom observation, post-instructional interviews, student reflections, and learning outcome assessments. The results indicate that the learning medium met the criteria for “highly suitable,” with a validation score of 86.76% from the subject teacher; the implementation process was effective, with an average class assessment score of 76.16; and the majority of students provided positive feedback, although internet infrastructure constraints remained the primary technical challenge in the field. These results conclude that the integration of Google Sites and Wizer.me has great potential to serve as an alternative platform to support digital mathematics learning in schools.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/educsci16101677.title: Belonging, Visibility, and Voice: Perceptions and Practices Promoting Social–Emotional Support in Online Learning in Teacher Education
doi:10.3390/educsci16101677.abstract: <jats:p>The consolidation of online learning in higher education raises a question teacher education can no longer defer: How is social–emotional –support created when teaching and learning are mediated by screens? This study explored how preservice teachers experienced social-emotional learning (SEL) in an online course, focusing on three dimensions: belonging, visibility, and voice. Using reflexive thematic analysis within a constructivist orientation, the study analyzed the summative written reflections, composed as letters to the lecturer, of preservice teachers (N = 27) in a year-long synchronous online course at a teacher education institution. The cohort, aged 19 to 35, was heterogeneous in life circumstances, professional experience, and learning profiles. The analysis constructed four themes: belonging built through structured relational rituals; visibility as pedagogical noticing across the screen; voice as graduated, chosen participation; and the intended translation of experienced online SEL (O-SEL) into a professional toolbox for inclusive teaching. The findings indicate that the online space is double-edged: it heightens the risks of invisibility and disconnection, yet its affordances, written channels, structured formats, and learner control over self-presentation, can deepen inclusion when deliberately designed. Because the letters were addressed to the lecturer–researcher, the findings are read as situated accounts of perceived support and intended practice rather than as evidence of effectiveness or of classroom implementation. The discussion links the findings to systemic and transformative SEL and online disinhibition theory, and proposes a practice architecture for preparing teachers for inclusive classrooms.</jats:p>

doi:10.51574/kognitif.v6i4.5554.title: Analysis of Students’ Numeracy Literacy in Terms of Self-Efficacy through Problem-Based Learning (PBL) Supported by Flipbooks with an Ethnomathematics Approach
doi:10.51574/kognitif.v6i4.5554.abstract: <jats:p>Students’ numeracy skills in Indonesia remain relatively low due to a lack of attention to the aspect of self-efficacy. In addition, there is a need for instructional models and media capable of improving numeracy skills. This study aims to analyze students’ numeracy skills in terms of self-efficacy following the implementation of an ethnomathematics-based Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model aided by a flipbook. This study employed a mixed-methods approach with an explanatory sequential design, involving 32 eighth-grade students at SMP Negeri 13 Semarang during the 2025/2026 academic year. Instruction focused on the topic of function relationships, integrating the ethnomathematics of Semarang City. The research instrument consisted of a numeracy literacy test that met validity criteria (a significance value of  for each item) and was deemed reliable based on a Cronbach’s Alpha coefficient of 0,640. The data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics through normality tests, individual achievement tests, class achievement tests, simple linear regression tests in the experimental class, and descriptive analysis based on self-efficacy categories. The results of the study indicate that there was an increase in numeracy literacy skills in the class taught using Problem-Based Learning with an ethnomathematics approach aided by a flipbook ( to ), and that self-efficacy had a positive and significant effect on numeracy literacy skills with a coefficient of determination  of  We also found that students with high self-efficacy met all numeracy literacy indicators, whereas students with moderate and low self-efficacy met only some of the indicators. These findings indicate that the implementation of ethnomathematics infused Problem Based Learning supported by flipbooks effectively improves students’ numeracy literacy skills, as evidenced by a higher N-Gain of 0,74 in the experimental class which falls into the high category compared to the control class’s N-Gain of 0,59, which falls into the moderate category.</jats:p>

doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.59256.title: The Effectiveness of the Timeline Method on Student Learning Outcomes in Islamic Cultural History Class 4 MI PAS Baitu-l-Quran Gontor
doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.59256.abstract: <jats:p>This study explores the efficacy of the Timeline method on the academic performance of fourth-grade students in Islamic Cultural History at MI PAS Baitul Quran Gontor. The Timeline method presents events chronologically to help students better understand historical sequences. A quantitative experimental approach with a Pretest-Posttest Control Group Design was used. Forty students were selected through Simple Random Sampling, with 20 in both experimental and control groups. Data was analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test with SPSS software. The results indicate a significant difference between the experimental class, which used the Timeline method, and the control class. The experimental class's post-test average was 85.25 compared to the control class’s 71, supported by a Mann-Whitney significance value of Sig. (2-tailed) 0.000 < 0.05. This shows the Timeline method's effectiveness in improving learning outcomes in Islamic Cultural History. Recommendations include encouraging students to enhance motivation and understanding, supporting educators in using innovative teaching methods, and urging institutions to foster creativity in the learning process.</jats:p>

doi:10.51178/jetl.v8i3.3750.title: Exploring Students' Pictorial Representation of Reading Texts Through Gallery-Based Summarizing in a Basic Reading Course
doi:10.51178/jetl.v8i3.3750.abstract: <jats:p>Reading comprehension requires students not only to identify information but also to construct, organize, and retain meaning. This study examines how undergraduate students create pictorial representations of reading texts through a Gallery-Based Summarizing activity in a Basic Reading course. Using a qualitative approach, the study analyzed semi-structured interviews with seven undergraduate students at a university in West Java, Indonesia, supplemented by observational notes collected during the creation of pictorial summaries and the subsequent gallery walk. The analysis revealed four themes. Students used deliberate comprehension strategies before drawing, particularly rereading texts and marking keywords. The drawing process involved initial planning, chronological organization of ideas, and deliberate selection of symbols to represent textual information. Students also experienced difficulties in visualizing abstract concepts and selecting information within limited visual space. Despite these challenges, participants reported greater engagement with the texts, increased attention to previously overlooked details, and support for information retention. All seven participants achieved the highest performance category, with a mean score of 14.29 out of 16. Overall, the findings suggest that Gallery-Based Summarizing offers a multimodal approach to reading that connects textual processing, visual meaning-making, and peer interaction. The activity may therefore provide an alternative technique for Basic Reading instruction, particularly for supporting active engagement and the transformation of textual information into visual representations.</jats:p>

doi:10.5256/f1000research.208077.r524560.title: Peer Review Report For: Beyond Flexible Learning: A Smart HyFlex Ecosystem for Green Workforce Development in Vocational Education [version 1; peer review: 1 not approved]
doi:10.5256/f1000research.208077.r524560.abstract: Vocational education needs to adapt to the digitalization and sustainability challenges by introducing innovative learning models that combine flexibility, technology, and sustainability skills. Hybrid Flexible (HyFlex) learning has proven to be a successful model, but its potential in developing Green skills, occupational health and safety (OHS) competence and environmental sustainability awareness is yet to be thoroughly investigated, especially in the realm of smart learning ecosystems. This study used a sequential explanatory mixed methods design. Quantitative phase, a survey was conducted on 172 vocational education students who were analyzed using Partial Least Square Structural Equation Model (PLS-SEM) to test the relationship between HyFlex learning, smart learning ecosystem, learning engagement, and sustainability related outcomes. The qualitative phase involved using semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions to interpret and elaborate on the quantitative results, based on thematic analysis. The results show that the smart learning ecosystem (β = 0.68, p < 0.001) and learning engagement (β = 0.52, p < 0.001) are significant positive factors of HyFlex learning. Smart learning ecosystem and learning engagement, in turn, have a significant impact on green skills, OHS competence, and awareness of environmental sustainability. The direct impacts of HyFlex learning on outcomes related to sustainability, however, are relatively smaller and indicate that the impact of HyFlex learning is channelled through the smart learning ecosystem and learning engagement. Qualitative results also indicate that digital readiness, instructional design and hands-on learning practices are important determinants in the effectiveness of implementing HyFlex. This research shows that HyFlex learning is not enough to train learners on sustainability competency without the presence of a strong smart learning ecosystem and active participation of learners. The results show the need to combine technological infrastructure, pedagogical design and the incorporation of concepts related to sustainability learning approaches to improve the results of vocational education.

doi:10.51178/jetl.v8i3.3753.title: The Analysis of Bilingualism Use in Teaching English at the Eighth Graders of SMP Negeri 2 Manderehe Barat
doi:10.51178/jetl.v8i3.3753.abstract: <jats:p>Bilingualism is commonly used in English language teaching to facilitate students’ understanding of instructional materials and classroom communication. In English learning, the use of English and Indonesian may help teachers accommodate students with different levels of English proficiency. This study aimed to analyze the types of bilingualism used in teaching English to eighth-grade students at SMP Negeri 2 Mandrehe Barat. This research employed a qualitative descriptive design. The participants were one English teacher and 18 eighth-grade students. Data were collected through non-participant classroom observation, semi-structured interviews, and documentation. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings showed that three types of bilingualism were found in English teaching: coordinate bilingualism, subordinate bilingualism, and compound bilingualism. Coordinate bilingualism occurred most frequently at 34.9%, followed by subordinate bilingualism at 33.3% and compound bilingualism at 31.7%. The teacher used bilingualism to help students understand learning materials, classroom instructions, vocabulary, grammar, and speaking activities. Students also responded positively because bilingual use helped them understand explanations, participate in classroom activities, and feel more confident. The study concludes that bilingualism was consistently used as part of English classroom instruction at the research site. The study contributes a description of bilingual practices in an Indonesian junior high school context and provides a basis for further research involving broader participants and other aspects of language learning.</jats:p>

doi:10.15294/jcs.v9i2.54736.title: Development of Wedang Ronde Ethnomathematics Teaching Materials in a Problem-Based Learning Model for Social Arithmetic
doi:10.15294/jcs.v9i2.54736.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to develop ethnomathematics-based teaching materials integrated with the Problem Based Learning (PBL) model on Social Arithmetic using the traditional culinary context of wedang ronde. This research is motivated by the low mathematical problem-solving ability of students due to mathematics learning that is still abstract and less contextual.1 The research method used is Research and Development (R&D) with the ADDIE development model which includes the stages of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation.2 The developed product was validated by material experts, media experts, and mathematics learning experts. Data collection techniques were carried out through observation, validation sheets, student response questionnaires, and formative assessments. The validation results showed that the teaching materials were in the very feasible category with scores between 73 and 100 out of a maximum score of 100. A limited trial of 25 seventh grade students showed that the teaching materials were easy to understand, visually appealing, and able to support student involvement in understanding the concept of Social Arithmetic. The integration of local cultural context and PBL syntax encourages students to think critically, collaborate actively, and connect mathematical concepts to real-life situations. Research findings indicate that ethnomathematics-based teaching materials have the potential to support meaningful mathematics learning while fostering an appreciation for local culture.</jats:p>

doi:10.23960/jpp.v16i4.pp1993-2008.title: Constructing an Adaptive Learning Framework Integrating STEAM–Gamification for Numeracy and Computational Thinking in Remote Indonesian Elementary Schools
doi:10.23960/jpp.v16i4.pp1993-2008.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to construct and validate the design of an adaptive learning framework that integrates STEAM–gamification principles with Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD)–Item Response Theory (IRT) to simultaneously develop numeracy literacy and computational thinking among elementary school students in Indonesia’s 3T (remote, frontier, underdeveloped) regions. A mixed-methods sequential exploratory design integrated with Design-Based Research (DBR) was applied over eight months in Pinrang Regency, South Sulawesi, across 10 schools in the qualitative phase and 20 schools in the quantitative phase. Qualitative data were drawn from interviews and focus group discussions with 30 teachers, 10 principals, 30 students, and 20 stakeholders, alongside 30 classroom observations; quantitative data were collected from 300 Grade IV–V students and 60 teachers using structured surveys, IRT-calibrated diagnostic tests (3PL; α = .83), and an ICT infrastructure audit. The framework synthesized qualitative and quantitative findings into four integrated layers: Pedagogical (STEAM), Motivational (gamification), Adaptive (ZPD–IRT), and Assessment (computational thinking + numeracy). Expert design validation employed LORI, Aiken’s V, and Fleiss’ Kappa with eight domain specialists. The needs analysis showed that 85% of teachers relied exclusively on conventional instruction, 78% identified a strong need for interactive learning media, and only 30% of schools had adequate ICT infrastructure. The composite numeracy mean was 50.1/100 and the computational thinking mean was 48.3/100, with geometry the weakest numeracy domain (34.7). Economic feasibility yielded a benefit-cost ratio of 1.42, a positive NPV, and an internal rate of return of 18.3%. Expert design validation yielded a LORI mean of 4.38/5, a Fleiss’ Kappa of 0.74, and an Aiken’s V of 0.79, all exceeding acceptability thresholds. The four-layer adaptive framework, among the first to integrate STEAM, gamification, ZPD–IRT adaptive learning, and computational thinking as a coherent system for Indonesia’s 3T elementary schools, provides a replicable theoretical model and an expert-validated design basis for subsequent product development and efficacy trials Keywords: adaptive learning framework, STEAM–gamification, numeracy literacy, computational thinking, 3T elementary schools.</jats:p>

doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.64362.title: Effect Of the Edutainment Learning Model Assisted by Monopoly Game Media on The Learning Outcomes of Grade V Students in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) at SDn 067246 Medan Tuntungan, Academic Year 2026/2027
doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.64362.abstract: <jats:p>This study was motivated by the low learning outcomes of fifth-grade students in the Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) subject at SDN 067246 Medan Tuntungan. This condition was reflected in the lack of students’ attention and participation during the learning process, as well as the monotonous classroom atmosphere. The study aimed to determine the effect of the Edutainment learning model assisted by Monopoly game media on students’ learning outcomes in the IPAS topic “Indonesia Kaya Raya” among fifth-grade students at SDN 067246 Medan Tuntungan in the 2026/2027 Academic Year. This research employed a quantitative approach using a pre-experimental method with a One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. The sample consisted of 25 fifth-grade students. Data were collected through tests, observations, questionnaires, and documentation. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics, normality testing, correlation analysis, coefficient of determination analysis, and hypothesis testing. The results showed that the average pretest score was 50.88, while the average posttest score increased to 84.80. The correlation test yielded a coefficient of 0.951, indicating a very strong relationship, while the coefficient of determination was 90.44%. The hypothesis test produced a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05, resulting in the rejection of H₀ and acceptance of Hₐ. Therefore, it can be concluded that the Edutainment learning model assisted by Monopoly game media had a significant effect on the learning outcomes of fifth-grade students in IPAS at SDN 067246 Medan Tuntungan in the 2026/2027 Academic Year.</jats:p>

doi:10.26577/jmmcs201000426.title: ALGORITHMIC LEARNING OF SUBSPACES IN COMPUTABLE VECTORSPACES
doi:10.26577/jmmcs201000426.abstract: <jats:p>Algorithmic learning of algebraic structures connects computability theory with artificial intelligence. Classical inductive inference mainly deals with formal languages and recursive functions. In contrast, analyzing vector spaces allows us to explore the theoretical limits of automated scientific discovery. This study investigates the algorithmic learnability of subspace families in computable vector spaces over a computable field. We focus on the fundamental family of all finite-dimensional subspaces and examine whether learnability is an isomorphism invariant. By combining constructive model theory with Gold’s paradigm of identification in the limit, our results identify the exact recursion-theoretic barriers to learning algebraic invariants. We use the classical model of explanatory learning in the limit from positive data (Ex-learning), where Turing machines act as learners. By applying canonical index numberings of finite sets and effective quotient space constructions, we establish two fundamental theorems. Our first result shows that if a computable vector space has a decidable linear dependence relation, the family of all its finite dimensional subspaces is Ex-learnable.. Second, we construct a computable vector space where the relation of linear dependence is undecidable. By using an effective priority-style diagonalization argument, we prove that the family of finite-dimensional subspaces in this space fails to be Ex learnable. These results prove that algorithmic learnability is not an isomorphism invariant of an abstract algebraic structure. Instead, it is strictly governed by the algorithmic complexity (Turing degree) of the linear dependence predicate. This finding provides a theoretical foundation for automated theorem proving and neuro-symbolic AI systems.</jats:p>

doi:10.1002/chem.71784.title: Unveiling Methane Selectivity on Cu‐Based Single‐Atom Alloys for CO <sub>2</sub> Electroreduction via Synergistic DFT and Machine Learning
doi:10.1002/chem.71784.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Electrochemical CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    reduction offers a sustainable route for converting CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    into value‐added fuels and chemicals, yet achieving efficient methane production remains challenging because of the complex reaction network and insufficient catalyst selectivity. Herein, density functional theory combined with interpretable machine learning were employed to investigate the structure‐activity relationship of Cu‐based single‐atom alloys constructed by incorporating 13 transition‐metal atoms into Cu(100)/(111) surfaces. The calculations reveal that isolated metal atoms effectively regulate the electronic structures of both the dopant and neighboring Cu atoms, thereby altering the energetics of HCOO* formation. More importantly, the synergistic interaction between the isolated metal atom and adjacent Cu sites stabilizes the CH
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    OO*, redirecting the reaction pathway toward highly selective CH
                    <jats:sub>4</jats:sub>
                    , in sharp contrast to pristine Cu surfaces. Among all investigated catalysts, Ge
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    /Cu(100) is most active, with a limiting free energy as low as 0.24 eV while effectively suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. Machine learning analysis further identifies electron affinity and catalyst‐support charge transfer as the two dominant descriptors governing catalytic activity, providing quantitative insight into the origin of the structure‐activity relationship. This combined DFT‐ML framework establishes descriptor‐guided design principles for methane‐selective CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    reduction and offers a general strategy for the rational development of high‐performance single‐atom alloy electrocatalysts.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.42780.title: Collaborative Learning in Inclusive Education: Constructing Tolerant Attitudes of Students at Pondok Modern Darussalam Gontor
doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.42780.abstract: <jats:p>Learning strategies that are focused not just on academic success but also on the development of social attitudes—particularly tolerance in the setting of a heterogeneous society—are required by inclusive education. The purpose of this study is to examine how collaborative learning in inclusive education helps students at the Pondok Modern Darussalam Gontordevelop attitudes of tolerance. This study combined a case study design with a qualitative methodology. Students, instructors, and caregivers at Islamic boarding schools participated in semi-structured interviews, participant observation, and documentation to gather data. Thematic analysis approaches were used to analyze the data. The study's findings show that regular use of collaborative learning techniques fosters an inclusive and engaging environment for social interaction in both the Islamic boarding school's formal and informal learning activities. Through processes of positive interdependence within groups, open discourse, collaborative reflection, and institutional support for the inclusion concept, students develop tolerance attitudes. Students can observe firsthand how to manage conflict, appreciate diversity, and develop empathy in the Islamic boarding school's communal life through collaborative learning. By supporting collaborative learning as an educational approach that contributes to the development of emotive and social values, this study makes a theoretical contribution. The study's practical conclusions suggest that enhancing collaborative learning is essential to creating inclusive Islamic boarding school-based instruction.</jats:p>

doi:10.51659/josi.25.243.title: Innovation Practice as a Mediator between Organizational Learning and Organizational Performance in Case of Flower Firms in Ethiopia
doi:10.51659/josi.25.243.abstract: <jats:p>Organizational learning (OL) and innovation practices (IP) have an impact on firm performance. To enhance their performance and persist in running, firms must learn, share knowledge and create new ideas. These practices can also benefit the environment in the floriculture industry through waste reduction, better utilization of resources and the introduction of new technologies. Organizational performance (OP) was selected as the outcome variable and the mediating variable was IP in the mediation role in nexus of OL on OP among floriculture firms in Ethiopia. The data collection method used was quantitative with descriptive and explanatory research designs. 415 questionnaires were sent out, with 391 of those being returned. The proposed nexus and mediation were tested using SEM. Outcomes observed that OL meaningful influences IP. IP also has a positive influence on OP, but significant. But OL has not a significant direct impact on OP. It also indicates that the nexus in OL and OP is completely mediated by the presence of IP. The study recommends to floriculture companies to increase the strength of OL and IP to enhance OP. Innovation, improved resource utilization and sustainable growth are possible with effective knowledge sharing and the use of new technologies.</jats:p>
