doi:10.31955/mea.v10i3.7495.title: PENGARUH TRANSFORMATIONAL LEADERSHIP, EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT DAN ORGANIZATIONAL LEARNING TERHADAP ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE DIMEDIASI ORGANIZATIONAL RESILIENCE
doi:10.31955/mea.v10i3.7495.abstract: <jats:p>Studi ini dirancang untuk menyelidiki dampak kepemimpinan transformasional, partisipasi pegawai, serta proses belajar di lingkungan perusahaan terhadap hasil kerja keseluruhan organisasi. Pengumpulan informasi dilakukan melalui kuesioner yang disebarkan kepada staf, dengan menggunakan teknik analisis numerik melalui model penelitian berbasis survei. Data diperoleh dari 350 responden yang merupakan karyawan pada perusahaan ekspedisi di Batam. Pengolahan data dilaksanakan memakai SmartPLS guna menguji kaitan antara beberapa variabel. Hasil pengamatan memperlihatkan bahwa proses belajar organisasi, partisipasi pegawai, dan gaya kepemimpinan transformasional mempunyai dampak berarti dan baik terhadap performa organisasi.Selain itu, terbukti bahwa ketahanan organisasi berperan sebagai variabel mediasi yang memperkuat hubungan terhadap kinerja organisasi. Hal ini memungkinkan organisasi dengan tingkat ketahanan tinggi untuk mampu beradaptasi, bangkit kembali dari krisis, serta meningkatkan kinerja secara berkelanjutan. Penelitian ini juga memberikan saran bagi manajemen perusahaan agar meningkatkan ketahanan organisasi melalui kepemimpinan, keterlibatan karyawan, dan pembelajaran berkelanjutan. Secara empiris, temuan ini menambah literatur manajemen khususnya dalam industri logistik dan layanan pengiriman, sehingga dapat menjadi rujukan untuk pengkaji kemudian dalam memajukan penyelidikan terkait kepemimpinan, keterlibatan pekerja, pembelajaran institusi, dan ketangguhan institusi dalam menaikkan prestasi.</jats:p>

doi:10.62131/mlaj-v4-n3-017.title: Comparación de modelos estadísticos y aprendizaje automático para predecir rendimiento académico universitario con datos abiertos
doi:10.62131/mlaj-v4-n3-017.abstract: <jats:p>Predicting academic performance using statistical models and machine learning algorithms may provide useful information for the early identification of university performance patterns. However, meaningful comparisons require homogeneous validation protocols and control of information leakage. This study aimed to compare the performance of one statistical model and three machine learning algorithms for predicting university academic performance before the final examination. A quantitative, observational, analytical, comparative, and predictive study was conducted using 560 open academic records. The target variable was Categories, comprising five performance levels. Seven predictors available before the final examination were used: Quiz, Midterm, Assignment_1, Assignment_2, Assignment_3, Project, and Presentation. Multinomial logistic regression, decision tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting were compared using an 80/20 stratified split and five-fold stratified cross-validation. Macro-F1 was the primary metric. Random Forest showed the best overall profile, with a Macro-F1 of 0.7360 in cross-validation and 0.7633 on the test set, followed by Gradient Boosting with 0.7099 and 0.7477, respectively. Random Forest achieved an Accuracy of 0.7768 and an F1 score of 0.8571 for Fail. Midterm showed the highest permutation-based predictive importance. Ensemble-based models showed a predictive advantage over the statistical reference model, although the findings are limited to the analyzed dataset and require external validation.</jats:p>

doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.63176.title: The Application of Interactive PowerPoint to Improve Learning Concentration in Pancasila Education Learning for Class XI of SMA Negeri 6 Semarang
doi:10.15294/jpp.v43i2.63176.abstract: <jats:p>Student concentration during Grade XI Pancasila Education lessons at SMA Negeri 6 Semarang was not optimal. Preliminary observations revealed that a number of students failed to pay attention to the teacher's explanations, engaged in conversations with peers, or busied themselves with activities unrelated to the lesson, thereby hindering the effective reception of instructional information. This study aimed to improve the learning concentration of Grade XI students through the implementation of interactive PowerPoint media. A classroom action research design was employed, conducted over two cycles; each cycle comprised the stages of planning, action implementation, observation, and reflection. Data were collected via observation sheets, questionnaires, and documentation, then analyzed both quantitatively and qualitatively, with a success criterion set at a minimum of 80% of students achieving a "good" category rating. The results demonstrated consistent improvement across stages: the initial condition showed an average score of 56.46 with a class mastery rate of 5.56%; this rose to an average of 61.91 with 61.11% mastery in the first cycle and reached an average of 72.57 with 100% mastery in the second cycle. Thus, the use of interactive PowerPoint media proved effective in enhancing student concentration during Pancasila Education lessons; it is therefore recommended as an alternative instructional medium that could be further developed for other subjects to foster active student engagement during the learning proces.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/agriculture16202197.title: Predicting Lentil Seed Yield from Agronomic Traits Using a Foundation-Augmented Machine Learning Ensemble
doi:10.3390/agriculture16202197.abstract: <jats:p>Accurate agricultural yield prediction is crucial for crop management and data-driven decision-making. This study proposes a machine learning framework for predicting total lentil seed yield using 264 observations collected during a single growing season at one location in Sivas, Türkiye. Seven regression models and the tabular foundation model TabPFN were evaluated through nested cross-validation. The fixed post hoc Foundation-Augmented Averaging Ensemble (FAAE) combined TabPFN, Extra Trees, CatBoost, and XGBoost using equal weights, while the primary fully nested evaluation selected the four ensemble members within each outer training fold. The fully nested FAAE achieved R2 = 0.891 ± 0.045, comparable to the strongest individual models, while the fixed post hoc FAAE yielded R2 = 0.897 ± 0.038. Split conformal prediction produced well-calibrated uncertainty intervals at 80%, 90%, and 95% coverage. SHAP and LOCO identified pods per plant and biological yield as the dominant predictors of lentil yield. Overall, these findings indicate that FAAE can provide competitive predictive performance within a leakage-controlled framework while also supporting uncertainty quantification and biologically meaningful interpretation. Because the dominant predictors, pods per plant and biological yield, are measured at or near physiological maturity, the proposed framework is more suitable for end-of-season yield estimation than for early-season forecasting. The framework therefore shows potential for within-trial yield assessment, although validation using replicated material across additional years and locations is required before broader generalization.</jats:p>

doi:10.1117/12.3109904.title: Photonic convolution neural networks for machine learning via energy-free Fourier-optics
doi:10.1117/12.3109904.abstract: Convolutional operations are computationally intensive in artificial intelligence (AI) services, and their overhead in electronic hardware limits machine learning scaling. Here, we introduce a photonic joint transform correlator (pJTC) using a near-energy-free on-chip Fourier transformation to accelerate convolution operations. The pJTC reduces computational complexity for both convolution and cross-correlation from O(N^4) to O(N^2) , where N2 is the input data size. Demonstrating functional Fourier transforms and convolution, this pJTC achieves 98.0% accuracy on an exemplary Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology inference task. Furthermore, a wavelength-multiplexed pJTC architecture shows potential for high throughput and energy efficiency, reaching 305 TOPS/W and 40.2 TOPS/mm^2, based on currently available foundry processes. An efficient, compact, and low-latency convolution accelerator promises to advance next-generation AI capabilities across edge demands, high-performance computing, and cloud services.

doi:10.1117/12.3118465.title: Performance modeling of photonic accelerators for attention kernel
doi:10.1117/12.3118465.abstract: In modern machine learning models such as Transformers, the attention kernel serves as the core computational kernel and is typically accelerated using transistor-based systems. Photonic in-memory computing offers a promising alternative by leveraging high optical bandwidth and operating frequencies for efficient multiply-accumulate operations. However, photonic compute arrays, such as photonic-SRAM (pSRAM) in-memory compute arrays, cannot support the large on-chip storage required for intermediate data in the attention kernel, necessitating integration with conventional electronic external memory. In addition, non-linear operations such as softmax require electronic execution. These constraints require a hybrid photonic-electronic architecture for attention acceleration. Developing such an accelerator requires understanding how hybrid photonic-electronic system parameters influence sustained performance. Therefore, a system-level performance model is necessary to identify and tune parameters and guide the design decisions required to achieve the target performance. We address this need by developing a system-level performance model for photonic accelerators that quantifies the impact of pSRAM compute arrays and electronic external memory on sustained performance (TOPS) for the attention kernel. We decompose the attention kernel into computation primitives and map them onto pSRAM-based compute arrays fabricated using GlobalFoundries’ standard silicon photonics process. We evaluate pSRAM configurations with 256x64 array size, 4-16-bit precision, 40-200 WDM channels, and electronic external memory such as HBM3E. Using our system performance model, we identify operating regions where photonic acceleration yields significant performance gains with sustained performance reaching up to 85 PetaOps/s at 200 WDM channels, as well as regions where memory overhead dominates.

doi:10.1186/s12981-026-00952-8.title: Optimizing HIV testing uptake among pregnant women in Burkina Faso: machine learning prediction and scenario-based intervention simulations using 2021 Demographic and Health Survey data
doi:10.1186/s12981-026-00952-8.abstract: HIV testing uptake among pregnant women remains a public health priority in Burkina Faso. This study aimed to identify and rank key predictors of HIV testing uptake using machine learning (ML) approaches and to estimate potential gains under scenario-based intervention simulations. We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 2021 Burkina Faso Demographic and Health Survey, including 4,703 women aged 15–49 years who had given birth within the two years preceding the survey. HIV testing uptake was defined as having been tested for HIV and having received the test result during antenatal care (ANC) or before delivery. Four ML algorithms (penalized logistic regression, Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting, and Support Vector Machine with a radial basis function kernel) were trained and evaluated. Model performance was assessed using weighted AUC-ROC and other standard classification metrics. Scenario-based intervention simulations targeting modifiable predictors were then conducted using the best-performing model. Overall, 55.0% (95% CI: 52.7–57.3%) of women reported HIV testing uptake during ANC or before delivery, with substantial regional disparities, ranging from 17.0% (95% CI: 11.2–22.9%) in the Est region to 81.0% (95% CI: 76.5–85.4%) in the Centre region. RF achieved the best cross-validated discrimination (AUC-ROC = 0.785) and showed comparable performance on the independent test dataset (AUC-ROC = 0.792). The five most important predictors of HIV testing uptake were region (relative importance = 100%), knowledge of HIV and/or prevention of vertical transmission (PVT) (95.6%), wealth index (43.1%), mother’s occupation (37.4%), and area of residence (32.3%). Scenario-based simulations suggested that increasing the coverage of good HIV/PVT knowledge to 80% could increase predicted HIV testing by 8.6% (95% CI: 6.9–10.6%). Compared with knowledge-only interventions at corresponding knowledge targets, the combined scenario incorporating media exposure and education yielded modest additional relative gains across regions, ranging from 0.6% to 13.8%. HIV testing uptake among pregnant women in Burkina Faso is characterized by substantial regional inequalities, and knowledge of HIV and/or PVT emerged as the dominant modifiable predictor. Combining national efforts to improve knowledge with region-specific strategies targeting media exposure and educational attainment may provide a promising approach for developing context-specific interventions to increase HIV testing uptake among pregnant women and reduce regional disparities.

doi:10.1186/s13007-026-01597-4.title: STAMPformer: spectral-prior-guided multi-view attention learning for hyperspectral prediction of continuous frost damage severity in field-grown tea plants
doi:10.1186/s13007-026-01597-4.abstract: Frost damage severely constrains the growth, development and quality formation of tea plants, underscoring the need to develop accurate field-scale methods for the assessment of frost damage severity. In this study, hyperspectral data and eight key physicochemical indicators were collected from tea plants across natural field frost damage gradients. To characterize frost damage severity on a continuous scale, a comprehensive tea cold stress response index, termed TCSRI, was developed by integrating multidimensional physiological responses. To enable the accurate and non-destructive prediction of physicochemical indicators and TCSRI under high-dimensional and small-sample conditions, we propose STAMPformer, a spectral-prior-guided multi-view attention pooling model. It incorporates a parameter-free attention convolution extraction module to jointly model raw spectra and first-order derivative spectra, thereby enhancing local spectral features and suppressing noise. A multi-view attention pooling module further adaptively aggregates sequence features from different feature subspaces to strengthen key spectral responses. The experimental results showed that STAMPformer achieves the best performance across all nine prediction tasks, with R 2 values above 0.87 and RPD values above 2.80. Ablation experiments, paired tests with multiple random seeds, and SHAP analysis confirmed the contributions of the proposed modules and reveal physiologically meaningful key wavelengths associated with pigment degradation, photosynthetic impairment, and cellular structural disruption. Independent external validation further demonstrated the model’s predictive ability on unseen samples. Overall, the proposed TCSRI and STAMPformer provide an accurate, interpretable and non-destructive framework for assessing tea plant frost damage severity, supporting frost monitoring, cold-tolerant germplasm evaluation, and smart tea garden management.

doi:10.1007/s13202-026-02240-7.title: A new insight into digital rock analysis using deep learning: a comparative study on the effect of hyperparameter selection and data augmentation
doi:10.1007/s13202-026-02240-7.abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have proven to be powerful tools in deriving rock properties from micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) images, providing a data-driven alternative to conventional digital rock physics workflows. However, the reliability performance and computational efficiency of CNN-based predictions remain strongly dependent on architectural and training choices that are often determined empirically. This study presents a systematic sensitivity-based evaluation of 3D CNN design and training factors, examining their effects on predictive performance and computational cost across multiple rock properties and dataset sizes. A 3D CNN-based workflow was evaluated for the prediction of five pore-scale properties, including porosity, average pore size, throat size, coordination number, and pore shape factor, from micro-CT images of a carbonate rock. The effects of kernel size progression, network width, number of convolutional layers (network depth), activation function, and learning rate, were quantitatively assessed in terms of predictive accuracy and computational cost. The role of data augmentation was additionally investigated across different dataset sizes. The results showed that (1) despite the high effectiveness of network depth on model accuracy, it has no significant impact on training runtime; (2) Odd-sized kernels with progressive spatial reduction generally outperformed even-sized and aggressively reduced kernel configurations, particularly for complex morphological descriptors such as pore shape factor; (3) data augmentation imporved performance for smaller datasets but provided limited or negative gains for larger datasets; and (4) Computational runtime was influenced primarily by kernel size and network width rather than network depth, learning rate schedules, and activation functions. A comparative sensitivity assessment further revealed that pore shape factor was the most hyperparameter-sensitive property, while porosity showed the highest robustness across different CNN configurations and also network width exhibited the smallest overall influence on predictive performance. Grad-CAM-based analysis provided additional insight into the image regions associated with CNN predictions. Porosity predictions showed the strongest association with pore-space regions, whereas pore radius and throat radius exhibited positive relationships with local pore-space geometry. Overall, the results provide a systematic framework for evaluating CNN hyperparameters, computational cost, and data augmentation in micro-CT-based digital rock analysis.
doi:10.1007/s13202-026-02240-7.venue: Journal of Petroleum Exploration and Production Technology

doi:10.1007/s10791-026-10691-z.title: Systematic review of machine learning models for plant and leaf disease detection and classification
doi:10.1007/s10791-026-10691-z.abstract: Plant leaf diseases significantly affect crop yield and quality, posing ongoing challenges across the agriculture sectors, including cereals, vegetables, fruits, and floriculture. In response, a wide range of machine learning (ML) techniques have been explored for effective disease detection and classification. This systematic review provides a comprehensive analysis of 102 peer-reviewed studies published between 2001 and 2024, exclusively focused on ML-based approaches for identifying plant leaf diseases. Based on the PRISMA methodology, studies were selected from four major databases and organized under eight research questions (RQs), covering the end-to-end ML pipeline. The review investigates key components such as dataset collection methods, model architectures, evaluation strategies, and comparative model performance. It further analyzes the distribution of studies by plant type, disease category, and publication source. Special emphasis is placed on dataset characteristics, model generalization across domains, and challenges in real-world implementation. The review also highlights performance metrics, cross-validation strategies, and the need for scalable, explainable, and lightweight models. Gaps in the literature—such as limited availability of high-quality datasets, lack of standard benchmarking, and poor model transferability—are identified to guide future research. This focused review offers a structured, comparative overview of ML-driven leaf disease classification efforts and serves as a roadmap for researchers and practitioners aiming to enhance agricultural productivity through intelligent, data-driven plant health diagnostics.

doi:10.1080/0954898x.2026.2744620.title: DSCrisk: A dual-view and substructure aware based method for drug-drug interaction risk-level prediction enhanced by contrastive learning
doi:10.1080/0954898x.2026.2744620.abstract: Combination pharmacotherapy remains a fundamental strategy in contemporary clinical practice. However, the concurrent use of multiple drugs substantially increases the risk of harmful drug-drug interaction events (DDIEs). Developing reliable computational methods for DDIE detection is therefore essential, yet existing approaches still face notable limitations in modelling interaction-relevant chemistry, relational context, and interpretability. In this study, we propose DSCrisk, a deep‑learning framework that employs graph neural networks (GNNs) to encode a dual-view representation comprising molecular graphs and the DDI topology network. DSCrisk further integrates a partner-guided attention readout to highlight interaction-relevant substructures within drug pairs and leverages contrastive learning over DDIE pairs to strengthen representation learning. Experiments show that DSCrisk achieves an accuracy exceeding 95%. Moreover, the partner-guided attention mechanism improves interpretability by revealing critical substructures associated with DDI risk. DSCrisk is available at https://github.com/liqingwen98/DSCrisk.

doi:10.1186/s12880-026-02893-0.title: Multimodal integration of deep learning and radiomics enables early detection of subjective cognitive decline
doi:10.1186/s12880-026-02893-0.abstract: Deep learning has become a promising strategy for improving disease features in medical imaging, but its application in neurodegenerative diseases is still limited. Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) is a key preclinical stage of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), but its recognition is challenging due to subtle and heterogeneous changes in the brain. A total of 234 normal controls and 229 individuals with SCD were included from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database. Preprocess structured T1 weighted MRI data using standardized procedures. We extracted MRI radiomics features and vision transformer-based deep learning features. To integrate complementary information, we propose a Hybrid Vision-Radiomics Aggregation (HVRA) framework based on Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR) derived feature selection and weighted feature concatenation. Consensus features were identified through the feature selection procedure, and model performance was evaluated using a repeated cross-validation strategy within the ADNI cohort to assess internal validation performance. The HVRA model achieved the best performance with an accuracy of 88.98% ± 3.42% and an AUC of 0.941, outperforming all unimodal methods. Compared with conventional fusion strategies, including direct concatenation and learnable fusion approaches, HVRA demonstrated superior classification performance. Four consensus features were consistently selected and demonstrated significant correlations with cognitive performance. Furthermore, these features showed associations with cognitive performance, suggesting their potential relevance for characterizing SCD-related brain alterations. Integrating deep learning and radiomics features provides a more comprehensive characterization of brain alterations associated with SCD, supporting its potential for improving SCD classification.

doi:10.1186/s12880-026-02899-8.title: A deep learning-based study on automatic extraction and measurement of macular hole parameters
doi:10.1186/s12880-026-02899-8.abstract: This study aims to develop LMMR-YOLO—a lightweight deep learning-based lesion detection fusion model optimized for medical images—to efficiently and accurately identify Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) images, measure key parameters of Macular Hole (MH), and assess MH lesion severity in patients. This retrospective study utilized 606 OCT images from 61 patients. LMMR-YOLO is built upon Mask R-CNN and YOLOv12-obb, with targeted dataset expansion via Mask R-CNN, image enhancement through the Image Enhancement Algorithm (IEA) alongside conventional augmentation ablation experiments, and YOLOv12-obb optimization including a grayscale image adaptation module integrated with Efficient Channel Attention (ECA), C2f_Ghost and A2C2f_Lite lightweight backbone modules for feature extraction, an Oriented Bounding Box (OBB) detection head, and a Fusion Detection Algorithm (FDA) that integrates Mask R-CNN and IEA for detection. Model performance was assessed using precision, recall, mAP@0.5, F1‑score and accuracy. On the internal test set, LMMR‑YOLO achieved an mAP@0.5 of 92.69%, accuracy of 94.78%, precision of 97.14%, and recall of 87.88% for key‑point detection of MH parameters, with an F1‑score of 92.28%. Normalized classification accuracy for Central Choroidal Thickness (CCT) was 0.97, mirror misidentification rate between Left Hole Height (LHH) and Right Hole Height (RHH) was 0.03, and the model featured 3.34 M trainable parameters, 11.10 GFLOPs, 9.44 FPS inference speed, and short training time, balancing lightweight performance and detection efficiency. LMMR-YOLO enables accurate MH parameter measurement from OCT images, supports ophthalmic MH diagnosis, staging, and personalized care, and offers a new paradigm for medical grayscale image analysis and model training. Not applicable.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74435-1.title: Effect of features burdened with classical error, misclassifications, Berkson error, and group-summary assignments on machine learning performance and interpretability
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74435-1.abstract: Abstract Measurement error is widespread in modern data pipelines, but its influence on predictive modeling and variable importance assessments in machine learning is often underestimated. Our study examines how input measurement error affects both prediction accuracy and interpretability across four common additive error types: classical error, misclassification of predictive features, Berkson error, caused by algorithmic or model-based assignment errors, and group-summary (aggregation) assignment errors. Using controlled Monte Carlo simulation experiments that cover regression and classification, we evaluate five popular machine learning models: generalized linear models, support vector machines, random forests, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptrons, across various error levels. To distinguish the effect of the error from optimization issues, hyperparameters are tuned separately for each dataset, and performance is measured using standard predictive metrics and permutation feature importance. Results show that measurement error generally reduces predictive performance and can significantly alter the ranking and estimated contribution of highly predictive features, with different degradation patterns depending on the error type and model. These findings clarify when performance declines might be mistaken for distributional shifts, among other things, and highlight the importance of diagnosing and correcting measurement error before drawing conclusions about model robustness, generalization, or variable relevance.

doi:10.59499/ep267146356.title: Methods For Improving The Operational Behavior Of Binder Jetting Gears Made Of 17-4 PH
doi:10.59499/ep267146356.abstract: <jats:p>The conventional powder metallurgical process for manufacturing gears is die pressing, which is only cost-effective for large-scale production due to its high initial investment. Powder bed–based additive manufacturing processes such as Binder Jetting (BJT) offer a flexible alternative for small-batch production, enabling near-net-shape manufacturing. Although previous studies have demonstrated the feasibility of BJT for gear manufacturing, approaches to improve the operational behavior of BJT gears have not been investigated.In this study, the tooth bending strength of heat-treated as well as shot-peened BJT gears made of 17-4PH is investigated and compared to that of gears with the same geometry and material made of wrought steel. In addition, preliminary tests regarding the tooth flank load capacity of the heat-treated BJT and wrought steel gears were conducted. Finally, the excitation behavior of a DfAM-optimized BJT variant was analyzed and compared to that of an unoptimized BJT and a wrought steel gear.</jats:p>

doi:10.32628/ijsrset2613529.title: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Models for Pan-Cancer Prediction and Explainable Feature Analysis
doi:10.32628/ijsrset2613529.abstract: <jats:p>Cancer classification based on molecular information is a more complex multiclass learning problem, as tumors from different tissues can present with different expression profiles and cancers with similar molecular characteristics can occur in different tissues. The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) gene-expression data is used to create a practical pan-cancer classification framework that is described in this paper. The working dataset consisted of 11,062 labelled samples representing 33 cancer types, after preparation and labelling. Representation of the input was reduced to 500 gene-expression features using a feature-selection stage. A single XGBoost multiclass classifier was then trained to understand the relationship between the chosen expression profile and the 33 cancer classes. The implementation performed with an accuracy of 94.49%, precision of 94.66%, recall of 94.49%, and F1 score of 94.27% on held-out test data. To make the model easier to inspect, a feature-importance analysis based on SHAP was added. The trained model was deployed into a Streamlit dashboard, with a FastAPI backend to upload a gene-expression sample and display the predicted cancer type, probabilities of cancer classes and explanation information. The system is a research and educational prototype, not a clinically validated diagnostic system; an independent validation should be required before clinical interpretation.</jats:p>
doi:10.32628/ijsrset2613529.venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science, Engineering and Technology

doi:10.1186/s40712-026-00609-4.title: Interpretable prediction of polymer material viscosity using machine learning models incorporating shear rate, salinity, concentration, and temperature effects
doi:10.1186/s40712-026-00609-4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Viscosity is a fundamental property of polymer materials and solutions that strongly influences their flow behavior, processing, and performance in various industrial and engineering applications. Polymer materials and polymer solutions are vital components in many industrial and engineering processes, in which viscosity is an important characteristic determining their flow behavior and performance. This paper presents predictive modeling of logarithmic viscosity (LV) of polymer solutions using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). 420 samples were collected through a public Kaggle database. Logarithm Shear Rate (LS), Polymer Concentration (PC), NaCl Concentration (NA) and Temperature (TE) are considered as input variables. The collected dataset is randomly divided into training (70%), validation (15%) and test set (15%). From the results, the error histogram revealed that the majority of the prediction errors are centred around −21.35, while the ANN model performed optimally during validation with MSE of 67,522.49 at epoch 20. A representative ANFIS prediction yielded an LV value of 11.7 cP for an input combination of LS of 55.8 s
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    , PC of 0.175 wt%, NA of 2.05 wt%, and TE of 57.5 °C. ANFIS was found to perform exceptionally well compared to ANN, based on an RMSE of 31.50, an MAE of 6.49, and an R2 value of 0.9846. In addition, the logarithm shear rate of 0.69, polymer concentration of 0.21, and NaCl concentration of 0.11 are established as highly influential factors based on SHAP analysis. Logarithmic viscosity increases drastically with an increase in polymer concentration. Overall, the findings confirm that the ANFIS is an effective method to predict the viscosity of polymer solutions through reliable, accurate, and comprehensible means. Possible applications of this technique include polymer processing, formulation, chemical processing, enhanced oil recovery, and flow control systems in industry.
                  </jats:p>
doi:10.1186/s40712-026-00609-4.venue: Journal of Materials Science: Materials in Engineering

doi:10.20897/ejsteme/19561.title: Learning for strengthening scientific literacy of pre-service teachers in elementary education programs
doi:10.20897/ejsteme/19561.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Strengthening scientific literacy among pre-service elementary teachers requires learning experiences that connect scientific reasoning, reflection, problem solving, and communication with pedagogical meaning. This study aimed to develop, implement, and evaluate the EXARIS-PBL framework across different institutional contexts. A sequential exploratory mixed methods design was employed involving pre-service elementary teachers from three Indonesian universities. The research consisted of qualitative exploration, framework development, multi-institution implementation, quantitative assessment, and qualitative investigation of learning processes. Quantitative findings showed that EXARIS-PBL implementation was associated with positive changes in students’ scientific literacy achievement, although the magnitude and statistical evidence varied across institutional contexts. The strongest effectiveness evidence was identified at UNNES, while the UPI implementation showed no significant adjusted posttest difference between groups. The UNP development evaluation demonstrated descriptive improvement following model implementation. Qualitative findings revealed three interconnected developments: progressive pedagogical awareness, professional teacher identity formation, and evidence-based collaboration and scientific communication. Integration of quantitative and qualitative evidence indicated that EXARIS-PBL supports scientific literacy development through structured processes of problem exploration, evidence analysis, reflection, conceptual and pedagogical integration, collaboration, and communication. The findings suggest that EXARIS-PBL provides a context-responsive framework for supporting scientific literacy development and professional preparation of future elementary teachers, while emphasizing the importance of institutional conditions and implementation contexts.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75645-3.title: Bearing capacity and safety factors of ring foundations in spatially variable soils: a hybrid FELA-machine learning approach
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75645-3.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Ring foundations efficiently support axisymmetric structures like silos, storage tanks, chimneys, and cooling towers with reduced concrete volume compared to solid circular foundations. Their ultimate bearing capacity is strongly affected by asymmetric loading and spatial variability in soil properties. This study presents a hybrid machine learning framework to predict normalized bearing capacity factors and safety factors for ring foundations in spatially variable cohesive-frictional (c-φ) soils. Datasets were generated via finite element limit analysis (FELA) in OptumG2, incorporating random field modeling of effective cohesion (c’) (lognormal, depth-linear mean: µ
                    <jats:sub>c’</jats:sub>
                     = 10 kPa, k = 1 kPa/m, COV = 0.3) and friction angle (φ’ up to 40°). Four loading configurations (complete, internal half, middle half, external half), inner-to-outer radius ratios of 0–0.9, rough/smooth interfaces, and nine anisotropic scale-of-fluctuation cases (horizontal: 10–60 m; vertical: 2–8 m) were analyzed. A Convolutional Neural Network processed random field images and parameters, achieving R² > 0.95 and relative errors < 3%. External half and complete loading gave highest capacities; internal half reduced them by up to 40%. Spatial variability in c’ and φ’ contracted failure envelopes by 10–25%, emphasizing reliability-based design. The framework dramatically reduces computational cost versus traditional FELA/Monte Carlo while retaining accuracy, supporting preliminary design, optimization, and risk assessment.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-73498-4.title: From wetting-front coalescence to urban road collapse: interpretable machine learning of hydro-mechanical failure under coupled rainfall and pipeline leakage
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-73498-4.abstract: Abstract Urban ground collapse poses a severe threat to public safety, road operation and underground infrastructure in densely developed cities. This study investigates the hydro-mechanical failure mechanism of road collapse induced by coupled rainfall infiltration and pipeline leakage through physical model testing, finite element simulation and interpretable surrogate modelling. A validated numerical model incorporating saturation-dependent strength and stiffness degradation was used to generate 120 cases with different pipe burial depths, rainfall intensities and leakage pressures.The results indicate that collapse develops through shallow-soil pre-wetting, leakage-induced wetting-zone expansion, convergence of the upper and lower wetting fronts, and upward propagation of deformation. Leakage pressure is the dominant factor, contributing 86.42%, 87.79% and 92.77% to the variations in collapse depth, near-saturated zone area and wetting-front depth, respectively. Rainfall mainly dissipates matric suction and lowers the failure threshold, whereas burial depth regulates the wetting-front convergence and deformation-transfer path. GPR/Kriging achieved test-set (R 2 ) values of 0.997–0.998, while XGBoost-SHAP confirmed the mechanism of leakage-pressure domination, rainfall amplification and burial-depth regulation. Risk zoning further shows that increasing rainfall shifts high-risk conditions towards lower leakage pressures, particularly at intermediate burial depths. The proposed framework provides an efficient tool for identifying vulnerable pipeline sections and supporting targeted inspection and collapse prevention.

doi:10.32628/cseit2612529.title: AI-Based UFDR Report Analysis and Intelligent Digital Forensic Investigation Assistant using Explainable Machine Learning
doi:10.32628/cseit2612529.abstract: <jats:p>Mobile and application-derived artefacts are becoming more central to digital forensic investigations; however, they can be a diverse set of evidence in a UFDR which are hard to prioritize manually. Mobile and application derived-artifacts are becoming more important to digital forensic investigations, and can be a diverse set of evidence in a UFDR that is difficult to manually prioritize. In the paper, the authors propose an Artificial Intelligence-based UFDR report analysis and intelligent digital forensic investigation assistant to transform the extracted report information into a structured and explainable analysis flow. The prototype now supports reading reports in JSON, XML, CSV and ZIP formats, validates the uploaded report, calculates an integrity checksum (SHA-256), and stores proof of the integrity in SQLite. Twenty behavioral features are created in communication, temporal, browser, application, and file activity. The trained Random Forest (RF) classifier enables three-way classification, and a trained Isolation Forest (Anomaly scoring) is used. A suspicious detector based on the 4 parameters is set, and activates when late-night activity is detected, or when suspicious incoming/outgoing communication, suspicious text indicators or high anomaly scores are detected. The conditions are combined using UNION logic and deduplicated by evidence identifier to return suspicious and/or critical records to the investigators. Risk engine helps transform the model and indicator outputs are mapped to a 0-100 score, and with the help of SHAP Tree Explainer, it is possible to get feature contributions by the model and a human-readable “WHY?” explanation based on evidence. An evidence-based assistant retrieves case, analysis and explanation information from the database and provides a deterministic answer when the language-model service is not available. The accuracy of the test split was 93% and F1-score, recall and macro precision were all approximately 0.93 for the synthetic benchmark that was reproduced using the project. Suspicious-detector tests were also conducted successfully, with special emphasis on specific tests. This system instead of the automatic finding of criminal conduct presents a non-automatic triage system, explainability and a conversational workflow for forensic decision support.</jats:p>
doi:10.32628/cseit2612529.venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science, Engineering and Information Technology

doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78580-z.title: Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78580-z.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/s43621-026-04864-5.title: An intersection of machine learning and advanced econometric techniques to analyse sustainable development in Europe through resource efficiency, institutional quality, and ICT
doi:10.1007/s43621-026-04864-5.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Sustainable development is a critical challenge as well as an opportunity for modern economies, especially for European countries, where technological and institutional frameworks are increasingly evolving and reshaping. This prospective study investigates the role of resource efficiency, institutional quality and information and communication technologies (ICT) to promote sustainable development in 26 European countries for 2000–2023. The study uses a comprehensive methodology, including econometric methodologies such as the Three-Stage Least Squares (3SLS), Generalized Method of Moments (GMM), and Full Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML), along with machine learning models, so that the results are accurate and have predictive depth. Based on the results, there are significant factors that promote sustainability in Europe countries such as better resource utilization, improved institutional quality and advanced ICT infrastructure. All these effects are positive and statistically significant, with institutional quality (coefficient = 0.023–0.030), ICT (0.011–0.025) and resource efficiency (≈ 0.008–0.016) being the most influential drivers, while CO₂ emissions have a significant negative effect. High percentage of the variation in the Sustainable Development Index is explained by the econometric models (3SLS R² = 0.96) and machine learning models have high out-of-sample accuracy (Gradient Boosted Trees R² = 0.948).</jats:p>

doi:10.59499/ep267159438.title: Development Of Novel Superalloys By Using Computational Materials Science And Production By Powder Metallurgy
doi:10.59499/ep267159438.abstract: <jats:p>In this project, innovative alloys have been developed using both artificial neural networks and first-principles techniques, incorporating experimental data. The effects of alloying elements have been investigated both experimentally and through computational materials engineering. DFT-based CASTEP software was used within the scope of computational materials science. Structure and geometry optimization, as well as unit cells and elastic constants, have been determined for alloys with different compositions. Additionally, phase transformation temperatures have been studied with the help of data obtained from preliminary trials using artificial neural networks. The alloys have been produced using powder metallurgy method. The calculations were performed on a high-performance computing server (supercomputer).</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74837-1.title: BurnAreaNet: a deep learning method for total body surface area estimation from 2D masks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74837-1.abstract: Accurate estimation of total body surface area (TBSA) is critical for burn diagnosis, triage, and prognosis. It represents the burned area as a proportion of the total body surface area, and is usually expressed as a percentage value. Traditional methods are subjective, while existing computer-aided approaches require specialized equipment or suffer from projection errors. To address these limitations, we constructed MassHumanBurn, a synthetic dataset comprising 5,000 diverse human models with simulated burns across eight TBSA levels, yielding 320,000 rendered views with paired body and burn masks. We propose BurnAreaNet, a neural network that estimates TBSA from frontal and dorsal whole-body and burn region masks. On ground-truth masks, BurnAreaNet achieved a descriptive mean absolute error (MAE) of \(0.55\% \pm 0.49\%\) , substantially outperforming the direct area ratio baseline ( \(1.99\% \pm 1.66\%\) ). To evaluate the impact of segmentation errors, we further constructed SAM_Preprocessed_MHB, where masks were generated using Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2). When masks were generated by SAM2 using box prompts derived from ground-truth masks, BurnAreaNet achieved an MAE of \(0.68\% \pm 0.70\%\) , while the baseline method yielded an MAE of \(2.48\% \pm 3.52\%\) . In a preliminary evaluation on four high-resolution human scan models (HSR_Burn dataset), BurnAreaNet outperformed the baseline on three of four models, while performance was lower for one high-BMI model (BMI 39.1) that may be underrepresented in the training distribution. These results suggest that BurnAreaNet represents a promising step toward rapid, objective, and device-independent TBSA estimation. Future work should incorporate more diverse human model sources, more controllable burn synthesis methods, and support for additional viewpoints to address occluded surface regions, while further validation on real patient data remains essential.

doi:10.67317/ijmsrt26aug062.title: A Real-Time Machine Learning-Based Intrusion Detection and Prevention System for Decentralized Networks using Random Forest and Isolation Forest
doi:10.67317/ijmsrt26aug062.abstract:
<jats:p>Decentralized networks—spanning Internet-of-Things deployments, edge computing platforms and peer-to-peer
systems—offer improved scalability, resilience and the elimination of single points of failure. At the same time, their
distributed structure makes continuous monitoring and timely intrusion response substantially more difficult. Traditional
signature-based intrusion detection systems (IDS) are effective only against previously catalogued attacks; they cannot
reliably detect zero-day or heavily obfuscated threats and typically require the centralised collection of raw traffic,
thereby raising privacy, bandwidth and single-point-of-failure concerns.
This paper presents a complete real-time machine-learning-based user detection and intrusion prevention system
expressly designed for decentralised environments. A lightweight monitoring agent executes on every registered physical
node, continuously captures live network packets, groups them into traffic flows and extracts a compact set of
discriminative features: packet rate, bandwidth usage, latency, failed login attempts and connection duration. These
features are classified by a Random Forest ensemble that distinguishes authorised from unauthorised activity.
Concurrently, an Isolation Forest anomaly detector flags behavioural outliers that may correspond to previously unseen
(zero-day) attacks. For every prediction the system computes a continuous risk score, assigns a discrete threat level (Low,
Medium, High or Critical), records an immutable event log entry, displays a real-time alert together with an AI-generated
explanation on the administrator dashboard, and—when prevention mode is enabled—automatically installs firewall rules
that block the offending traffic.
Because only summarised detection results are forwarded to the central monitoring dashboard, raw packet data never
leave the local node; privacy is preserved and inter-node communication overhead is minimised. Extensive evaluation on
labelled network traffic demonstrates an accuracy of 96.80%, precision of 95.40%, recall of 94.20% and F1-score of
94.80%, markedly surpassing a conventional signature-based baseline. The system maintains normal network
performance under both typical and elevated traffic loads, confirming that intelligent detection need not be purchased at
the expense of operational efficiency.</jats:p>

doi:10.32628/ijsrset2613521.title: Mental Health Detection using Advanced Machine Learning
doi:10.32628/ijsrset2613521.abstract: <jats:p>There are a number of factors that can impact on students' wellbeing, such as academic workload, financial concerns, sleep patterns, social support, lifestyle and other factors. This research presents the web application MindScope Lab, which is based on machine learning algorithms and was designed to illustrate how simulated mental health-related risk patterns can be identified in student profiles. A synthetic dataset of 30,000 student records was generated with attributes based on the students' demographics, academic, wellbeing, lifestyle and support. The data comprises age, gender, department, CGPA, PHQ-9 score, anxiety score, academic stress, financial stress, sleep duration, sleep quality, social support, physical activity, family history, counselling history. The dataset was split in 80:20 stratified fashion and a Random Forest classifier was trained on the same. The model obtained a high accuracy of 96.92% for unseen synthetic test data. The trained pipeline was then integrated into a web application built using Flask that would take in a fake student profile from a user and give them a lower-risk pattern and guidance or a higher-risk pattern and guidance. The application was kept alive by a GitHub repository and deployed as a web service. The project illustrates the complete process of synthesizing the data, preprocessing, building a machine-learning model, testing it, developing a web-interface, and deploying it. The underlying data and target labels are synthetic data, and the system is for academic and technical demonstration only. It is not a medical diagnostic system, clinical screening tool or a substitute for mental health services.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75117-8.title: Explainable machine learning for shear capacity prediction of reinforced concrete deep beams
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75117-8.abstract: The shear capacity prediction of reinforced concrete (RC) deep beams remains a challenging issue in design of concrete structures. Although the code-based strut-and-tie method is widely accepted, it is often time-consuming for routine design applications, while existing empirical equations are unable to fully capture the highly nonlinear interactions among material properties, geometric characteristics, and reinforcement variables. To address this limitation, this study proposes an explainable machine learning framework for predicting the shear capacity of RC deep beams. A comprehensive database of 419 experimentally tested specimens was compiled from the literature, and eight supervised machine learning models were developed with hyperparameters optimized using the Optuna framework. Comparative analysis showed that the optimized Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) model achieved the best predictive performance, with a test coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.93. A synthetic Gaussian input-perturbation study was conducted to assess the numerical sensitivity of the models under progressively disturbed inputs. To interpret the black-box behavior of the model, Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and three-dimensional Partial Dependence Plots (3D-PDPs) were employed. The resulting feature-response patterns were broadly consistent with established deep-beam behavior, particularly the positive effect of concrete compressive strength and the negative influence of the shear-span-to-depth ratio, along with important nonlinear interactions among key variables. Finally, a user-friendly graphical user interface integrating the optimized GBDT model was developed to provide rapid and interpretable shear-capacity estimation for practical engineering applications.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70741-w.title: An adaptive federated deep learning approach for efficient DDoS detection in IoT edge networks
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70741-w.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has expanded the attack surface of modern networks, motivating the need for accurate detection of DDoS and botnet activity in resource-constrained settings. Centralised intrusion detection systems (IDS) face privacy, scalability, and heterogeneity challenges that limit their suitability for IoT. This study suggests a Federated Learning-based Intrusion Detection System (FL-IDS) for IoT edge networks in order to get around these restrictions. Each client trains a hybrid CNN-LSTM model locally, and a central server aggregates client updates with Federated Averaging (FedAvg). An adaptive global decision-threshold optimisation is used post-training to the pooled predictions of the global model on the held-out test partition in order to address class imbalance. The system is evaluated on the N-BaIoT benchmark together with preliminary validation on a recent public healthcare IoT dataset, with the nine N-BaIoT devices treated as independent federated clients during the primary federated evaluation. The global model achieves an accuracy of 0.9238, precision of 0.9265, recall of 0.9963, F1-score of 0.9601, ROC-AUC of 0.8133, and PR-AUC of 0.969 at the optimal operating point
                    <jats:inline-formula>

                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    . SHAP-based post-hoc analysis identifies the traffic features that most influence model decisions.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69897-2.title: Causality-driven hybrid intrusion detection with entropy-aware feature learning and federated intelligence
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-69897-2.abstract: Modern IDSs should be capable of detecting and recognizing new forms of attack traffic (including both attacks from known adversaries) and to do so in ways that remain computational feasible when deployed across multiple, geographically distributed sites. Rule based, representation learning, and federated approaches have been used separately, or in combination in some cases. However, each approach operates independently in many cases. Therefore, they fail to support causal interpretability, efficient use of feature information, stable performance against adversarial attacks, and generalizability across multiple sites. This paper outlines a causality driven hybrid ids framework. The hybrid framework includes the Causal-Adaptive Signature Learning Engine; the Entropy-Guided Feature Compression Network; the attention-based Hybrid Cognitive Detection Synthesizer; the Adversarial Robustness Calibration Module; and the trust-weighted Federated Threat Intelligence Evolution Framework. The proposed framework has been tested on three separate publicly available network traffic datasets (cicids2017, unsw-nb15, and IoT-23). Testing included: use of dataset specific partitions that controlled for leakage in training; five fold validation to test the ability to learn patterns within the training data; ten different random seed controlled evaluations. A comparison of the hybrid ids framework was made to: block chain-based collaborative ids frameworks; traditional machine-learning based ids frameworks; optimized XGBoost-based ids frameworks. All comparisons were completed under similar preprocessing conditions and distributions of classes. The proposed ids framework produced detection accuracies of 97.4% and 96.1% on the cicids2017 and unsw-nb15 datasets respectively. An overall detection accuracy rate of 95.6% was achieved on the IoT-23 dataset. Additionally, the proposed framework reduced the number of features retained to 18 (a reduction of 70.9%) compared to the original number of features present in each of the datasets. Across ten iterations, the reported aggregate performance metrics were: overall accuracy = 96.37%; precision = 95.97%; recall = 95.43%; F1-score = 95.68%. In addition, the proposed framework had an average processing time per inference of 18.6 milliseconds. Finally, testing performed under bounded gradient-based perturbation conditions indicated that the proposed framework maintained high levels of detection accuracy (>91.5%).

doi:10.32628/ijsrset2613528.title: Two-Stage Deep Learning Pipeline for Brain Tumor MRI Classification with Explainable AI
doi:10.32628/ijsrset2613528.abstract: <jats:p>Brain tumor recognition from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is one of the crucial applications of medical image analysis. MRI scans are difficult to analyze manually and require considerable time, while variations in tumor appearance can make classification challenging. Deep learning models can facilitate this process by learning relevant visual patterns directly from MRI images. However, classification systems that provide only a predicted class may offer limited information about the regions influencing the decision. In this work, a two-stage deep learning pipeline for brain tumor classification from MRI images is proposed. In Stage 1, a MobileNetV2 model performs normal and abnormal screening. Images identified as abnormal are further processed in Stage 2 using a VGG16 network enhanced with a Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention block. The Stage 2 model performs four-class classification into glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and non-tumor. Grad-CAM is incorporated to visualize the image regions contributing to the classification result. The trained models are deployed in a Flask-based web application for image uploading and result visualization. Experiments were conducted using the Kaggle Brain Tumor MRI Dataset containing 7,023 MRI images. The MobileNetV2 screening model achieved an accuracy of 96.38%. Among the models evaluated in Stage 2, the VGG16 model with SE attention achieved the highest accuracy of 93.94%. The system integrates normal/abnormal screening, detailed classification, visual explanation, and web-based access within a single two-stage pipeline.</jats:p>

doi:10.58445/rars.4166.title: Cognitive Contributions to Adolescent Motor Learning
doi:10.58445/rars.4166.abstract: Motor skill acquisition underlies both everyday and specialized human activities, yet individuals differ substantially in the rate at which they learn new movements.Although Fitts and Posner's (1967) three-stage model describes a universal trajectory from conscious to automatic performance, it does not explain why some learners progress through these stages faster than others.Cognitive ability has been proposed as one source of this variability, with working memory (WM) and processing speed implicated as the components most relevant to motor learning.However, most existing research has sampled children or adults, with adolescents underrepresented, and few studies directly compare higher and average-intelligence groups on learning rate rather than final performance.This review outlines currently known contributions of working memory and processing speed to motor learning rate, which appear to vary across learning stages, task types, and practice conditions.Implications for how cognitive ability should be considered in research and practice with adolescent populations are discussed.

doi:10.1007/s10791-026-10573-4.title: An empirical performance comparison of deep learning models for apple leaf disease recognition
doi:10.1007/s10791-026-10573-4.abstract: Currently, Biotic and abiotic factors, in agriculture, are estimated to be responsible for around 22% of the total losses in crop production. It is therefore very important, but at the same time very difficult for farmers to identify these constraints at the earliest possible stage. The most recent developments in computer vision have made it possible to identify as well as classify plant lesions at a primary level. Various deep learning techniques have made it possible to detect biotic stress in apple plant leaves with a very high degree of accuracy. Hence, automated segmentation of images of diseased leaves has become a leading research theme all over the world. In this paper, a dataset from FGVC7, which is an open, source dataset and contains four different classes of leaf diseases of the apple crop is used to measure the performance of the proposed model. A three, step image preprocessing procedure is conducted, which involves image enhancement, removal of background noise, and object identification through a variety of approaches. Using UNet, PSPNet, and UNet++, disease areas are identified. UNet + + delivering the most precise object segmentation. The segmented patch data are then fed into a fusion, based classification model as input. Patch segmentation makes it possible to separate the various disease areas, thus increasing the classification accuracy. The proposed framework combines several CNN architectures, namely, VGG16, InceptionV3, AlexNet, and GoogleNet, in order to take advantage of their complementary strengths, then a Vision Transformer (ViT) is used to identify distinct local features via early feature fusion. After this, the efficiency of the proposed model is check in comparison with the pre-trained CNN models individually. Comparing with all other models the proposed model has shown the accuracy of highest order i.e. 98.85%, clearly out performing individual CNN models.

doi:10.9734/ajgr/2026/v9i4482.title: A Review of Machine Learning in Species Distribution Modeling under Climate Change in West Africa
doi:10.9734/ajgr/2026/v9i4482.abstract: <jats:p>Species distribution modelling (SDM) has become a central instrument for anticipating how biodiversity is redistributed under climate change, and machine learning now supplies most of the algorithmic capacity behind these predictions. West Africa combines high climatic exposure, dense reliance on wild biological resources, and thin biodiversity records, so the region is a demanding setting in which the strengths and weaknesses of machine learning SDMs are exposed. Scope. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026 were synthesised to describe how correlative SDMs, tree-based ensembles, and deep learning have been applied to West African flora, fauna, disease vectors, and agricultural pests, and to assess the treatment of data quality, model transferability, and reporting standards. Key findings. Maximum entropy modelling remains the dominant approach, yet tree-based ensembles and, more recently, deep neural networks are being adopted where occurrence volume permits. Reported discrimination is high across algorithm families, with area under the curve values frequently above 0.90, though internal validation was shown to overstate reliability when sampling bias and extrapolation into novel climates were left uncorrected. Plant studies concentrated in Benin, Togo, Nigeria, and Burkina Faso projected habitat contraction for a majority of exploited woody species, with northward and upslope displacement of suitable conditions, while vector and pest models projected expansion of climatically suitable areas for several malaria vectors and invasive insects across the region. Persistent occurrence-data scarcity, spatial sampling bias, and inconsistent reporting were identified as the leading constraints on inference. Implications. Bias-aware calibration, spatially independent validation, standardised reporting, and investment in regional occurrence data are needed before machine learning SDMs are used to guide conservation prioritisation, protected-area design, and public-health planning in West Africa. This review positions the regional evidence within methodological developments and defines data-supported priorities for the next phase of work.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/electronics15204621.title: SemLRA: Lightweight Robust Aggregation Against Poisoning Attacks in Semantic Federated Learning
doi:10.3390/electronics15204621.abstract: <jats:p>Semantic federated learning couples task-oriented semantic communication with distributed training, reducing on-device training burden and end-to-end inference latency. However, poisoning through local data, task labels, or transmitted semantic features can degrade task performance and system reliability. We propose semantic lightweight robust aggregation (SemLRA) for an information-separated dual-server architecture. SemLRA calibrates task losses already generated during split training using the within-round median and median absolute deviation to construct bounded client reliability coefficients. These coefficients jointly reweight client- and server-side model aggregation and regulate subsequent server-side optimization. SemLRA estimates reliability without reference data, client-update inspection, or prior knowledge of the malicious-client count or fraction, while retaining FedAvg-order aggregation complexity. On CIFAR-10, SemLRA maintains accuracy close to its clean-training level under continuous attacks, exceeding the strongest competing defense in mean final-stage accuracy by 3.77 percentage points under label flipping. Under burst attacks, SemLRA provides the strongest accuracy retention across all evaluated scenarios. Measured training runtime shows negligible additional overhead.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/act15100532.title: Robust PD-Type Iterative Learning Fault-Tolerant Control for Discrete Systems with Polytopic Uncertainties and Actuator Faults
doi:10.3390/act15100532.abstract: <jats:p>For a class of discrete systems with polytopic uncertainties and actuator faults, a robust PD-type iterative learning fault-tolerant control scheme is investigated in this article. By providing a two-dimensional analysis of the learning process, the fault system of a repetitive nature is equivalently converted into an uncertain linear repetitive process. Additionally, employing repetitive process stability theory, new sufficient conditions with less conservatism for the robust stability of the designed fault-tolerant controller are derived in terms of linear matrix inequality constraints. The controller gain matrices are exactly given as well. Finally, simulation results of an industrial SCARA robot demonstrate the efficiency and feasibility of the proposed strategy in comparison to the developed robust P-type iterative learning fault-tolerant control strategy.</jats:p>

doi:10.22219/bimantara.v5i02.44821.title: Organizational Learning as a Mediating Mechanism: Transformational Leadership, IT-Business Alignment, and Service Innovation in Indonesian Healthcare
doi:10.22219/bimantara.v5i02.44821.abstract: <jats:p>The digital health transformation in Indonesia presents a critical challenge for healthcare institutions, where digital maturity often lags behind national integration mandates. This study addresses this research gap by examining the roles of transformational leadership and IT-business alignment in driving service innovation performance. While numerous studies have examined the impact of digital transformation on broader organizational performance, considerably less attention has been directed toward understanding how organizational learning serves as the underlying mechanism through which leadership and technology alignment translate specifically into service innovation outcomes within healthcare settings. Using a quantitative causal methodology, data were obtained from 117 employees at hospitals and community health centers through purposive sampling. Data analysis was performed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS software. The findings demonstrate that IT-business alignment has a favorable and significant effect on service innovation performance. While transformational leadership does not directly influence innovation performance, it serves as a significant driver of organizational learning. These results highlight the necessity for healthcare management to prioritize synergy between digital strategies and business goals while fostering a collective learning culture. In conclusion, ensuring robust IT alignment and a supportive learning environment is fundamental for achieving sustainable service innovation in the healthcare sector.</jats:p>
