doi:10.69667/ajs.261006.title: An Integrative Model Based on Artificial Intelligence for Enhancing Integration among Sciences in Interdisciplinary Learning and Scientific Research: A Field Study on Postgraduate Students at the Libyan Academy – Janzour
doi:10.69667/ajs.261006.abstract: <jats:p>The recent rapid advancement in artificial intelligence technologies has brought about a fundamental transformation in higher education and scientific research institutions by providing new opportunities to enhance interdisciplinary learning and cognitive integration across various scientific fields. This study aimed to propose an integrative model based on artificial intelligence to analyze the impact of using AI tools in enhancing interdisciplinary learning and scientific research among postgraduate students at the Libyan Academy–Janzour. The study adopted the descriptive-analytical approach, and data were collected from a sample of (94) master's and doctoral students using a questionnaire specifically designed for this purpose. The reliability test results indicated that the study instrument possessed a high degree of reliability, with a Cronbach's alpha coefficient of (0.912). The results of the descriptive analysis indicated that the sample members possessed a high level of digital competence, with a mean score of (3.92) and a standard deviation of (0.64). The findings also revealed a high impact of using artificial intelligence tools on improving the quality of scientific research and research productivity, with a mean score of (4.15) and a standard deviation of (0.58), in addition to a positive role in enhancing interdisciplinary integration, with a mean score of (3.88) and a standard deviation of (0.71). Furthermore, the results of the inferential analysis showed no statistically significant differences in the participants' attitudes toward the proposed model attributed to academic specialization (F = 1.42, p = 0.241) or academic level (t = 0.85, p = 0.398), which confirms the applicability of the model across various specializations and academic levels. Additionally, the findings revealed a strong, statistically significant positive correlation between digital competence and interdisciplinary research integration (r = 0.684, p < 0.001), indicating that developing digital skills directly contributes to enhancing students' ability to employ artificial intelligence tools in producing more integrated and interdisciplinary research. The study findings confirm that artificial intelligence represents an effective tool for supporting interdisciplinary integration, improving scientific research efficiency, and facilitating knowledge exchange and academic collaboration across different disciplines. This study also contributes to enriching the scientific literature related to the employment of artificial intelligence in higher education and provides a practical framework that can be utilized in developing smart academic environments that support interdisciplinary learning and scientific research.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75391-6.title: Development and validation of a deep learning model for differentiating cytomegalovirus and herpes simplex virus esophagitis using endoscopic images
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75391-6.abstract: Abstract Background: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) and herpes simplex virus (HSV) are the most common causes of infectious esophagitis in immuno-compromised patients. However, their endoscopic features frequently overlap, making real-time etiologic differentiation difficult and often requiring delayed confirmation by immunohistochemistry. Methods: We developed and validated a deep learning model to distinguish CMV from HSV esophagitis using endoscopic images from biopsy-proven cases at a tertiary referral center. The model was trained with domain-specific pretraining and a curriculum learning strategy that sequentially introduced cases according to diagnostic difficulty, mimicking clinical learning processes. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using an independent test set and compared with experienced endoscopists. Results: The curriculum learning–based model demonstrated improved classification performance over conventional training approaches, achieving an AUROC of 0.783 (95% confidence interval 0.680–0.885). Its sensitivity and specificity were comparable to those of expert endoscopists. Model visualization showed attention to clinically relevant mucosal abnormalities. Conclusion: Deep learning analysis of routine endoscopic images can assist in differentiating CMV and HSV esophagitis. A curriculum learning strategy may enhance clinical applicability by improving performance in visually ambiguous conditions, potentially supporting earlier therapeutic decision-making while awaiting histopathologic confirmation

doi:10.57033/mijournals-2026-3-0331.title: Individualized English Language Learning for Students with Disabilities through Adaptive Educational Technologies
doi:10.57033/mijournals-2026-3-0331.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of adaptive educational technologies into language education creates new opportunities for providing individualized learning experiences for students with disabilities. Traditional approaches to English language teaching may not always adequately address the diverse cognitive, sensory, communicative and learning needs of such students. The development of flexible and accessible learning environments is therefore becoming increasingly important, particularly in home-based education. This study explores the potential of adaptive educational technologies for individualizing English language learning for students with disabilities. Particular attention is given to the adaptation of learning materials, instructional pace, task complexity, communication formats and assessment strategies. The study argues that digital resources, multimedia tools, interactive exercises, speech technologies and applications based on artificial intelligence can facilitate differentiated instruction and increase students’ engagement and autonomy. At the same time, technology should not be regarded as a substitute for pedagogical interaction. Its effectiveness depends largely on the teacher’s ability to select and adapt technological tools according to the learner’s individual educational needs. The findings suggest that a combination of individualized instruction and adaptive technologies can contribute to a more accessible, flexible and learner-centred approach to English language education.</jats:p>
doi:10.57033/mijournals-2026-3-0331.venue: The Journal of Interdisciplinary Human Studies

doi:10.3390/sym18101683.title: An IoT Malware Detection Framework Based on Large Language Models and Deep Learning Techniques
doi:10.3390/sym18101683.abstract: <jats:p>Rapid growth in IoT devices has led to the creation of crucial cybersecurity threats since existing methods of malware detection which use signature matching and numerical feature analysis are incapable of capturing the contextual behavioral semantics of IoT attacks. The presented work proposes an innovative malware detection framework incorporating a pipeline of behavior-to-text transformation together with transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs) to perform binary classification of IoT network traffic. Selected through the process of SHAP-based feature importance analysis, the numerical features of network flows from the initial set of 41 features are transformed into natural language descriptions, allowing encoder-based LLMs to capture the context of IoT traffic behavior. Four LLMs, including DistilBERT, BERT-base, RoBERTa, and DeBERTa, were fine-tuned and rigorously tested against four Deep Learning baselines, Neural Network, LSTM, BiLSTM, and CNN, and four Machine Learning baselines, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, using the CIC-IoT-2023 dataset under three experimental setups: balanced classification, realistic imbalanced distribution, and unseen variant detection. Additionally, a four-class multi-class classification experiment and an ablation study were conducted to further validate the framework. On a balanced dataset consisting of 400,000 samples, BERT-base and RoBERTa achieved the highest F1-scores of 98.94% with precision above 99.96%. In the imbalanced case of 90% attack and 10% benign traffic, the precision of all models was equal to 99.99%. The framework attained an F1-score of 99.99% for unseen variant detection on a completely unseen Mirai botnet variant with zero false negatives. The four-class multi-class experiment achieved a Macro F1-score of 88.80%. Statistical analysis across three independent runs confirmed high result stability with standard deviations below 0.03%. SHAP analysis revealed that packet count, ACK flag number, and HTTPS indicator were the most discriminative features, while attention visualization confirmed token-level interpretability. All LLMs consistently outperformed all Deep Learning baselines, providing evidence for the effectiveness of the behavior-to-text transformation paradigm for IoT malware detection, while classical ML models achieved marginally higher F1-scores due to their efficiency with numerical features, providing evidence for the effectiveness of the behavior-to-text transformation paradigm for IoT malware detection.</jats:p>

doi:10.66031/jinea.v2i3.742.title: Islamisasi Ilmu Pengetahuan: Analisis Konseptual Pemikiran Syed Muhammad Naquib Al-Attas dan Implikasinya terhadap Pendidikan Kontemporer
doi:10.66031/jinea.v2i3.742.abstract: <jats:p>Kajian ini bertujuan menganalisis secara filosofis-konseptual gagasan Islamisasi ilmu pengetahuan dalam perspektif Syed Muhammad Naquib al-Attas serta relevansinya terhadap pendidikan kontemporer. Kajian dilatarbelakangi krisis epistemologis pendidikan modern yang ditandai sekularisasi ilmu, dikotomi pendidikan, degradasi moral, dan lemahnya orientasi transendental. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif melalui studi kepustakaan (library research) dengan analisis filosofis-kritis terhadap karya primer al-Attas dan artikel ilmiah relevan. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa Islamisasi ilmu merupakan proses dewesternisasi ilmu modern melalui eliminasi unsur sekularisme, dualisme, relativisme, dan humanisme antroposentris, kemudian mereintegrasikannya dalam worldview Islam berbasis tauhid. Worldview Islam dan adab menjadi fondasi ontologis, epistemologis, dan aksiologis pendidikan. Pemikiran al-Attas relevan bagi pendidikan kontemporer melalui pengembangan kurikulum integratif, penguatan karakter berbasis adab, rekonstruksi epistemologi pendidikan Islam, serta reposisi guru sebagai agen transformasi intelektual dan spiritual. Dengan demikian, Islamisasi ilmu dapat diposisikan sebagai paradigma alternatif dalam merespons krisis pendidikan kontemporer.</jats:p>
doi:10.66031/jinea.v2i3.742.venue: JINEA: Journal of Innovation in Education and Learning

doi:10.67693/bjcr-8bwgis2a.title: CHARLES: Continuous Homeostatic Adversarial Resilience through Learning and Epistemic Sifting
doi:10.67693/bjcr-8bwgis2a.abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) and reinforcement learning (RL) in cybersecurity introduces the possibility of autonomous cyber agents capable of observing an environment, learning from interaction, and selecting sequential actions with limited human intervention.This development creates a challenge for conventional defensive strategies, which frequently depend on relatively stable system configurations, predefined detection rules, and human-led response processes.Cyber deception and moving target defense (MTD) provide mechanisms for increasing uncertainty and changing the environment encountered by an attacker, while game theory and reinforcement learning provide mathematical and computational approaches for modelling adaptive attacker-defender interactions.This paper proposes CHARLES (Continuous Homeostatic Adversarial Resilience through Learning and Epistemic Sifting), a conceptual defensive architecture designed to continuously manage the information and environmental conditions available to an autonomous attacker.Rather than attempting only to detect an attack after malicious activity has occurred, CHARLES proposes a feedback-based approach consisting of epistemic sifting, adaptive state transformation, adversarial learning estimation, and adversarial utility management.The framework aims to investigate whether controlled environmental variability and strategically deployed deception can reduce the stability of an attacker's learned policy, increase uncertainty, and alter the expected utility of attack strategies.The paper develops a simple mathematical model for representing attacker utility, environmental uncertainty, and defensive transformation.A simulation-based methodology is proposed to compare static and adaptive defensive environments against learning-based attackers.The work does not claim that continuous transformation universally defeats autonomous attackers; instead, it establishes a testable framework for investigating the relationship between defensive environmental adaptation and autonomous attacker learning.

doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26apr2218.title: Bloodstain Pattern Analysis Using Deep Learning and Convolutional Neural Networks for Forensic Crime Scene Reconstruction
doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26apr2218.abstract: <jats:p>Bloodstain pattern analysis (BPA) is a critical forensic science tool for reconstructing crime scene events and understanding the dynamics of violent incidents. Traditionally conducted through manual analysis by trained experts, this process is time-consuming, subjective, and prone to contextual bias. This paper presents a comprehensive deep learning frame-work integrating convolutional neural networks (CNN) for auto-mated detection, classification, and impact angle determination of bloodstain patterns.</jats:p>
doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26apr2218.venue: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology

doi:10.59944/postaxial.v3i4.2082.title: Does TikTok Really Matter for Academic Achievement? Self-Regulation and Use Duration Among University Students
doi:10.59944/postaxial.v3i4.2082.abstract: <jats:p>The increasing use of TikTok among university students has raised questions about its relationship with academic achievement. Previous studies have reported mixed findings. This study examined the association between self-regulated learning (SRL)-based TikTok use regulation and semester grade point average (GPA) in the full sample and two daily-use duration groups. It extends previous research by examining how students plan, control, and evaluate TikTok use beyond duration or problematic use alone. Separate subgroup analyses explored the association within each duration group. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey involved 197 university students. Analyses included descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, Pearson correlation, simple linear regression, and robustness checks. The full-sample association was near zero and nonsignificant (r = −0.038, p = 0.600). Associations were also nonsignificant in the groups reporting more than two hours and two hours or less of daily use. Spearman correlations were nonsignificant, and HC3 and bootstrap analyses provided no evidence of significant linear coefficients, although diagnostic concerns limit interpretation. The measured regulation score alone provided little information about differences in semester GPA in this sample. Broader academic behaviors warrant further investigation to clarify the practical relevance of digital self-regulation. These findings do not establish that TikTok use is academically harmless or that associations are statistically equivalent across duration groups</jats:p>
doi:10.59944/postaxial.v3i4.2082.venue: International Journal of Post Axial: Futuristic Teaching and Learning

doi:10.66031/jinea.v2i3.695.title: Physical Fitness Profiles of First-Year Students: An Assessment Using the Multistage Fitness Test
doi:10.66031/jinea.v2i3.695.abstract: <jats:p>First-year students entering Sports Education programs are often assumed to possess high physical fitness, yet this assumption requires empirical verification at entry. This study profiled the cardiorespiratory fitness of first-year Sports Education students using the Multistage Fitness Test (MFT) and described variation by sex. Forty students (25 male, 15 female; 19.8 ± 0.7 years) completed the MFT. Overall estimated VO₂max was 37.47 ± 4.76 mL·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹ (range: 28.9–48.1), with 77.5% classified as poor (45.0%) or fair (32.5%), compared with 15.0% good and 2.5% excellent. Male students showed higher estimated VO₂max than females (39.68 ± 4.21 vs. 33.80 ± 3.09 mL·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹), while females were more concentrated in the very-poor and poor categories. Mean BMI was 21.7 ± 2.7 kg/m², providing anthropometric context but not evidence of a fitness determinant. Overall, the findings challenge the assumption that Sports Education enrollment reflects uniformly high cardiorespiratory fitness and instead demonstrate substantial variation in students’ fitness at entry. The MFT-derived profile provides an institution-specific baseline for differentiated conditioning, curriculum planning, and subsequent fitness monitoring.</jats:p>
doi:10.66031/jinea.v2i3.695.venue: JINEA: Journal of Innovation in Education and Learning

doi:10.1007/s42399-026-02752-7.title: Association of Albuminuria with Preserved eGFR and Mortality in Pooled NHANES 2007–2018: Conventional and Machine Learning Survival Analyses
doi:10.1007/s42399-026-02752-7.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background/Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) provide complementary information about kidney disease risk and adverse outcomes, including mortality. Using pooled National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2007–2018 data, we evaluated the association between albuminuria and all-cause mortality among adults with preserved eGFR and compared conventional and machine-learning survival approaches for mortality prediction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We analyzed pooled NHANES 2007–2018 data with linked mortality follow-up. The primary cohort was restricted to adults with eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m²; albuminuria was defined as urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) ≥ 30 mg/g, with UACR < 30 mg/g as the reference. Survey-weighted Cox regression estimated the association with all-cause mortality after multivariable adjustment. Standard Cox, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) Cox, Elastic Net Cox, and Random Survival Forest models were evaluated for mortality prediction in a held-out test set.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among 29,918 adults with preserved eGFR, 3,090 had albuminuria and 1,943 died during follow-up. Median potential follow-up was 86 months (95% CI, 84–87). Compared with UACR < 30 mg/g, albuminuria was associated with higher all-cause mortality in the fully adjusted survey-weighted model (HR, 2.10; 95% CI, 1.82–2.42). In the held-out test set, C-indices were 0.8400 for standard Cox, 0.8392 for LASSO Cox, 0.8393 for Elastic Net Cox, and 0.8407 for Random Survival Forest; paired bootstrap analysis showed no meaningful predictive advantage of Random Survival Forest over standard Cox.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among adults with preserved eGFR, albuminuria was associated with higher all-cause mortality after multivariable survey-weighted adjustment. More complex machine-learning survival models did not show a meaningful improvement in mortality prediction beyond standard Cox regression.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.47820/recima21.v7i10.9270.title: <b>O JOGO COMO RECURSO PARA A APRENDIZAGEM E FATOR DE DESENVOLVIMENTO HUMANO</b>
authors: Joslaine Antonia da Silva Monteiro Volgarim
doi:10.47820/recima21.v7i10.9270.abstract: <jats:p>Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar, com base na literatura científica, de que maneira o jogo pode contribuir para os processos de aprendizagem e para o desenvolvimento humano em suas diferentes dimensões. A pesquisa caracteriza-se como uma revisão narrativa da literatura, de abordagem qualitativa e natureza básica. Foram analisados artigos científicos, livros, dissertações e teses relacionados ao jogo, à aprendizagem e ao desenvolvimento humano, por meio de uma leitura interpretativa voltada à identificação de argumentos, aproximações, diferenças e contribuições presentes nas produções selecionadas. Os resultados mostraram que o jogo pode envolver tomada de decisões, elaboração de estratégias, resolução de problemas, compreensão de regras, interação social e reflexão sobre as próprias ações, relacionando-se a dimensões cognitivas, afetivas, sociais, motoras e culturais. A análise também indicou que a presença do jogo, isoladamente, não garante aprendizagem ou desenvolvimento, sendo necessário considerar planejamento, mediação, objetivos pedagógicos, características dos participantes e contexto de realização. Conclui-se que o jogo constitui uma prática complexa que pode integrar processos educativos e de desenvolvimento humano, desde que sua utilização não seja reduzida ao entretenimento ou tratada como solução automática para dificuldades de aprendizagem.</jats:p>

doi:10.67119/s8c4mc88.title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Methods for Financial Market Volatility Classification
doi:10.67119/s8c4mc88.abstract: <jats:p>Financial market forecasting remains difficult because asset prices are strongly affected by randomness, noise, and limited short-term predictive information. Methods that aim to estimate precise future returns therefore often struggle to achieve consistently reliable results. To address this issue, this study reformulates the prediction task as a classification problem that distinguishes between different levels of market volatility, taking advantage of the persistence and clustering commonly observed in volatility dynamics. Ten machine learning methods are evaluated under a unified experimental framework, covering linear classifiers, support vector machines, instance-based approaches, decision trees, and ensemble techniques. The empirical results show that all tested models achieve classification accuracies above 80\%, indicating that future volatility states can be identified with relatively consistent performance across different model families. These findings suggest that volatility classification provides a comparatively stable and practically useful machine learning formulation for supporting financial decision-making.</jats:p>
doi:10.67119/s8c4mc88.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Green Manufacturing

doi:10.14445/23488549/ijece-v13i9p103.title: Development and Evaluation of Enhanced Machine Learning Models for Tumor Severity Classification Through Integrated Feature Extraction and Selection Techniques
doi:10.14445/23488549/ijece-v13i9p103.abstract: <jats:p>The precise categorisation of the severity of tumours is an important function in medicine, as it is a vital part of deciding treatment and predicting patient outcome. We offer an integrated pipeline for developing and evaluating the latest machine learning methods for tumour severity classification. We apply advanced methods for feature extraction and selection to improve the model’s accuracy, interpretability, and robustness. Ultimately, the framework organises diverse biomedical datasets for later analysis through domain-specific preprocessing approaches. Methods such as PCA, wavelet transform, and texture features are used to extract important information from raw data, thereby reducing dimensionality and preserving diagnostic information. More advanced techniques for feature selection are then used, such as Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE). Moreover, mutual information, which identify the most relevant features in the input dataset to reduce computational cost and the risk of overfitting. The models are validated using cross-validation techniques, with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Curve (AUC-ROC) as metrics. The results demonstrate that combining feature extraction and selection boosts classification accuracy and model generalisation across multiple datasets. Furthermore, explainability analysis clarifies the contribution of selected features to model predictions, which is crucial for building trust and transparency in clinical applications. However, really, what it demonstrates is the promise of all these things in concert. State-of-the-art machine learning, combined with rigorously designed features, will ultimately address some of those more difficult diagnostic challenges. These findings also pave the way for scalable, interpretable and clinically applicable AI-based solutions which may help in cancer detection and management. In this work, we will extend the proposed pipeline to other medical imaging modalities and explore real-time implementations.</jats:p>
doi:10.14445/23488549/ijece-v13i9p103.venue: International Journal of Electronics and Communication Engineering

doi:10.51574/kognitif.v6i4.5469.title: Effect of Canva-Assisted Project-Based Learning on Students’ Conceptual Understanding and Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills
doi:10.51574/kognitif.v6i4.5469.abstract: <jats:p>Effective techniques must be applied in the design of mathematics instruction to ensure that learning objectives are achieved. Conceptual understanding and mathematical problem-solving skills are considered the primary learning objectives for students. However, in reality, many students still struggle to fully understand concepts or solve mathematical problems systematically. This study aims to determine the effect of using a Project-Based Learning (PjBL) approach supported by Canva on students’ conceptual understanding and mathematical problem-solving skills. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest non-equivalent control group design involved 50 students, with 25 in each group. During three 40-minute sessions, the experimental group used Canva to create scaled house floor plans on the topic of ratios and scale, while the control group received traditional instruction. Data were collected using validated essay tests scored with a predetermined rubric and analyzed using independent-samples t-tests. Significant between-group differences were found in conceptual understanding, t(48)=-2.135, p=0.038, Cohen’s d=0.60, and problem-solving skills, t(48)=-2.254, p=0.029, Cohen’s d=0.64. These findings suggest that Canva-supported PjBL offers promise for supporting both learning outcomes, although the intervention was limited to three sessions</jats:p>

doi:10.5539/hes.v16n4p435.title: Self-Directed but Not Business-Ready: The Entrepreneurial Learning Paradox among Generation Z Communication Arts Graduates
doi:10.5539/hes.v16n4p435.abstract: <jats:p>This qualitative study examined how Generation Z Communication Arts graduates directed their learning while preparing for entrepreneurship and how they perceived their readiness. Twenty recent graduates from nine Thai universities were purposively selected. Data from semi-structured discussions were analyzed using Braun and Clarke&rsquo;s six-phase thematic analysis. Five interconnected themes emerged: establishing learning purposes, recognizing competency gaps, seeking knowledge through digital resources, learning through practice and repetition, and reflecting on outcomes. Participants described initiative, creativity, and active resource seeking alongside perceived gaps in finance, accounting, taxation, management, and risk assessment. Digital resources offered accessible information, but verification practices varied. Peers, mentors, and specialists provided feedback and complementary expertise. The findings identified a readiness paradox: ownership of learning coexisted with uncertainty about meeting business demands. This distinction suggests that learning initiative should not be treated as evidence of business competence. Entrepreneurship education could address this gap by integrating disciplinary strengths with foundational business knowledge, critical information evaluation, practical experimentation, structured reflection, and accessible mentoring. These recommendations may support comparable graduate transitions when adapted to specific disciplinary contexts.</jats:p>

doi:10.66031/jinea.v2i3.696.title: Beyond Screen Time: Peran Keluarga dalam Penggunaan Smartphone dan Regulasi Diri Emosional Anak Usia Dini
doi:10.66031/jinea.v2i3.696.abstract: <jats:p>Regulasi diri emosional anak usia dini tidak memadai untuk dipahami hanya melalui durasi screen time, karena pendekatan tersebut mengabaikan bagaimana praktik keluarga membentuk pengalaman penggunaan smartphone. Penelitian ini bertujuan memahami bagaimana praktik keluarga membentuk penggunaan smartphone dan bagaimana pengalaman tersebut berkelindan dengan regulasi diri emosional anak. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus, melibatkan 2 orang tua/pengasuh dan 5 anak berusia 3–7 tahun. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, observasi naturalistik, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis secara tematik dengan triangulasi teknik dan sumber. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa akses, tujuan penggunaan, aturan, pendampingan, respons terhadap permintaan, serta strategi pembatasan dan penghentian membentuk pengalaman anak dalam menghadapi keinginan, penundaan, negosiasi, dan kehilangan akses smartphone. Regulasi diri emosional paling tampak pada situasi menunggu, menerima pembatasan, dan beralih setelah penghentian, dengan variasi antarkasus terkait konsistensi aturan dan strategi transisi, terutama pemberian peringatan sebelum penghentian. Temuan menegaskan bahwa durasi screen time semata tidak menjelaskan pengalaman regulasi emosional anak. Kontribusi penelitian terletak pada pergeseran fokus dari “berapa lama” menuju “bagaimana praktik keluarga membentuk pengalaman smartphone dan situasi regulasi diri emosional”, dengan smartphone dipahami sebagai arena interaksi keluarga tempat anak mengalami dan mengelola emosinya.</jats:p>
doi:10.66031/jinea.v2i3.696.venue: JINEA: Journal of Innovation in Education and Learning

doi:10.3390/heritage9100417.title: Attention-Guided Digital Enhancement of Museum Artifact Photographs Using Progressive Curriculum Learning
doi:10.3390/heritage9100417.abstract: <jats:p>Physical deterioration and image-quality loss can reduce the legibility of museum photographs and limit their value for digital access, cataloging, and visual analysis. This study evaluates an Attention ResUNet for grayscale enhancement under heterogeneous degradation and revisits the contribution of progressive training using compute-matched controls. A curated set of 5816 Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access objects was divided at the object level into 4071 training, 872 validation, and 873 test objects. In the original five-epoch Phase-II ablation, staged initialization outperformed direct five-epoch training, but this advantage did not persist after total optimization exposure was matched. Direct 15-epoch ResUNet reached 29.777 dB PSNR and direct 15-epoch Attention ResUNet reached 29.862 dB, compared to 29.340 and 29.419 dB for their staged counterparts under the same 43,125-step budget. An independent set of 45 photographs captured on site at the Peshawar Museum was reserved for post-selection evaluation. Direct enhancement of the untouched photographs was assessed with no-reference indicators, with NIQE decreasing from 4.996 to 4.237 and BRISQUE from 23.171 to 18.479. A separate reference-based experiment retained each original photograph as an image-domain target, added deterministic Gaussian noise (σ=10), and restored the degraded input with the compute-matched Attention ResUNet (C15). Across all 45 photographs, mean PSNR increased from 28.149±0.045 to 29.740±0.914 dB, SSIM from 0.8136±0.0555 to 0.8985±0.0183, and LPIPS decreased from 0.1140±0.0459 to 0.0668±0.0242. SSIM and MAE improved in all 45 cases, while PSNR improved in 40/45 and LPIPS in 44/45 cases. A structured blinded assessment on 15 paired cases found the C15 output closer to the pre-corruption reference in 14/15 comparisons; a second independent reviewer provided qualitative corroboration but did not complete a second image-level score sheet. The paired experiment establishes recovery from a known image-domain corruption, not reconstruction of the artifact’s historically pristine physical state. The method remains limited to grayscale structural and luminance enhancement, and processed outputs should remain linked to the original photographs.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/jmmp10100418.title: Lightweight Cross-Condition Tool Wear Prediction via Transfer Learning for Resource-Constrained Edge Manufacturing
doi:10.3390/jmmp10100418.abstract: <jats:p>In resource-constrained manufacturing environments, accurate prediction of tool wear under variable cutting conditions remains challenging due to the trade-off between computational overhead and prognostic reliability. Conventional signal processing and deep learning methods suffer from high model complexity, cross-domain distribution discrepancies, and excessive computation cost, limiting their practical deployment on edge devices. This paper proposes an optimized cloud–edge collaborative transfer learning framework for lightweight remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of milling tools. On the cloud side, a low-complexity stacked auto-encoder built on a 1D-SqueezeNet is trained with cross-domain adaptation constraints to improve generalization across working conditions. Pretrained model parameters are then transferred to edge hardware for deep feature extraction. A kernel extreme learning machine (KELM) is further adopted for fast on-site tool wear regression prediction. When validated on full-lifecycle milling vibration data collected under real machining conditions, the proposed approach achieves nearly identical prediction performance on edge devices compared with cloud-side inference while also reducing edge inference latency to 0.01–0.021 s. These results demonstrate that the presented framework can deliver accurate prediction of milling tool RUL and provide rapid response under limited edge computational resources.</jats:p>
doi:10.3390/jmmp10100418.venue: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing

doi:10.14445/23488549/ijece-v13i9p109.title: Optimal Trajectory Prediction System for Automated Driving using Deep Learning
doi:10.14445/23488549/ijece-v13i9p109.abstract: <jats:p>Research in the field of autonomous driving has revealed that one of the main focuses is on predicting the future trajectories of vehicles. These accurate forecasts enable safe navigation and efficient route planning. A hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) framework integrated with the Robot Operating System (ROS) is presented in this work. The aim of the framework is to estimate future vehicle trajectories in real time. The network was trained using vehicle motion data from the Argoverse Motion Forecasting dataset. CNN layers extract local temporal and kinematic patterns from input sequences, and LSTM layers model their temporal evolution. Once trained, the model is incorporated into an ROS-based pipeline where nodes dedicated to processing incoming trajectory information publish predicted paths for real-time visualisation in RViz. Performance of the model was evaluated using Mean Squared Error (MSE), Average Displacement Error (ADE) and Final Displacement Error (FDE), and was then compared to that of classical motion prediction methods. Research results are promising, as they enable the computational efficiency required for real-time operation alongside predictive accuracy. Additionally, robotic middleware, deep learning and a publicly available benchmark dataset were combined to develop a reproducible experimental framework that will facilitate the replication and evaluation of autonomous driving systems.</jats:p>
doi:10.14445/23488549/ijece-v13i9p109.venue: International Journal of Electronics and Communication Engineering

doi:10.1159/ajn/ablag010.title: Mesenchymal stromal cell derived membrane particles improve metabolic activity and functional performance during porcine kidney normothermic machine perfusion
doi:10.1159/ajn/ablag010.abstract: <jats:p>Introduction Kidneys from donation after circulatory death (DCD) donors are increasingly used to alleviate organ shortage but highly vulnerable to ischemia-reperfusion injury, leading to poor graft outcomes. Normothermic machine perfusion (NMP) enables targeted intervention during donor kidney preservation. Membrane particles (MPs) derived from mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) have shown regenerative potential. We aimed to investigate MPs as a potential therapeutic strategy to improve metabolism and function in porcine DCD kidneys during NMP. Methods Six pairs of porcine kidneys underwent 4-hour NMP. Within each pair, one kidney received perfusate containing MPs derived from 1.0×107 MSCs, while the contralateral kidney served as a control. Hemodynamics, sodium reabsorption, oxygen consumption, and injury markers were monitored. Gene expression related to inflammation and metabolism were analyzed. Results MP administration did not affect renal blood flow or intrarenal resistance. Injury markers (AST, LDH, IL-6) were increased over time in both groups, without significant difference between MP-treated and control kidneys. In contrast, MP-treated kidneys showed significantly higher expression of metabolic genes (PDHB, ATP6V0D2, NDUFS8). Functionally, MP administration enhanced sodium reabsorption, urinary creatinine excretion, and oxygen utilization efficiency compared with controls. Conclusion MSC-derived MPs can be safely delivered to porcine kidneys and promote kidney functional performance and metabolic activity. These findings support MPs as a promising cell-free therapeutic strategy to improve the quality of kidneys during NMP.</jats:p>

doi:10.61230/reflection.v4i3.168.title: Developing Future Biomedical Innovators Through Challenge-Based Learning Using Breast Milk-Derived Bioactive Peptides in Cancer Research Education
doi:10.61230/reflection.v4i3.168.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of emerging biomedical research into higher education offers opportunities to develop scientific reasoning, biotechnology literacy, and innovation-oriented competencies. This study explores the potential of Challenge-Based Learning (CBL) through breast-milk-derived bioactive peptides and cancer research as an authentic context for biotechnology education. A qualitative descriptive research design is employed, involving students from biotechnology, biology, biomedical science, or related higher education programs. Data are collected through students’ written reflections, group discussions, and proposed solutions developed during structured learning activities. The data are analyzed thematically to examine three dimensions: biotechnology literacy and understanding of scientific evidence, scientific reasoning and critical thinking, and biomedical innovation and responsible problem-solving. The study positions breast-milk-derived bioactive compounds as a context for examining molecular biology, evaluating experimental and clinical evidence, and understanding the translation of scientific discoveries into potential therapeutic applications. Rather than treating emerging biomedical research as established clinical practice, the learning framework emphasizes scientific accuracy, recognition of uncertainty, and ethical responsibility. This study is expected to contribute to biotechnology education by providing insights into the use of authentic biomedical challenges to support interdisciplinary learning and responsible innovation. The findings may inform the design of educational activities that connect scientific knowledge with contemporary biomedical research without requiring specialized laboratory facilities.</jats:p>
