doi:10.5539/hes.v16n4p480.title: The Development of Micro Game-Based Learning Model on Intelligent Metaverse Learning Environment
doi:10.5539/hes.v16n4p480.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to synthesize, develop, and evaluate the Micro Game-Based Learning Model on Intelligent Metaverse Learning Environment. The study integrated Microlearning, Game-Based Learning, Artificial Intelligence, and Metaverse technologies to create a learning environment that provides short learning units, interactive game-based activities, and simulated communication situations. The research objectives were to (1) synthesize the learning process, (2) develop the learning model, and (3) evaluate the learning model. The evaluation panel consisted of three experts from various academic institutions. The experts were selected based on their experience at least 3 years in education, instructional design and development, particularly in teaching English for communication. The research instruments consisted of the learning model, learning platform, and an expert evaluation questionnaire based on a 5-point Likert scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics according to the research objectives. The findings indicated that the appropriateness of the developed learning model was evaluated at a highest level (Mean = 4.93, SD = 0.24). The findings suggest that integrating Microlearning, Game-Based Learning, Artificial Intelligence, and an Intelligent Metaverse Learning Environment provides a feasible approach for developing technology-supported English communication learning.</jats:p>

doi:10.22219/raden.v6i2.46134.title: Instructional supervision and differentiated literacy learning for students with special needs in an inclusive school
doi:10.22219/raden.v6i2.46134.abstract: <jats:p>Background-Principals in inclusive schools must supervise instruction for students with special needs (SEN), yet little is known about how supervision reaches differentiated literacy instruction where specialist staff are scarce. Objectives- This study analyzes how a principal, as supervisor and educator, manages the instructional program and oversees differentiated literacy learning for SEN students. Methods- An instrumental single-case study was conducted at SDN 8 Sintang, an inclusive elementary school in West Kalimantan, Indonesia. Participants included one principal, one classroom teacher, one special assistant teacher (SAT), and five SEN students. Interviews, observations, and documents were analyzed using NVivo 15. Results-Participants described scheduled supervision aimed at differentiation and a redefinition of literacy achievement as individual progress. Differentiation appeared divided between the classroom teacher (content) and the SAT (process and assessment), although observed collaboration was inconsistent and students' communication about reading content was limited. Reported barriers were structural: the SAT ratio, incomplete individualized education program documentation, and limited special-pedagogy training. Conclusions-Within this school, the principal's dual role was perceived to support differentiated literacy work; the findings are tentative given one informant per adult role and five heterogeneous students. The study offers a context-bound proposition linking supervision, teacher SAT collaboration, and affective literacy habituation for testing.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1957576.title: Course reassignment and learning engagement: the intervention strategy of AI-attributed reassignment
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1957576.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Course reassignment is a common practice in university registration systems, yet reassigned students often exhibit lower learning engagement than those in self-selected courses, and the underlying psychological mechanism remains unclear. This study examined the impact of course reassignment on learning engagement, the mediating role of self-efficacy, and the buffering effect of AI-attributed course reassignment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Two scenario-based online experiments were conducted with university students randomly assigned to conditions. Experiment 1 (
                      <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                      = 393) used a single-factor between-subjects design comparing reassignment vs. self-selection. Experiment 2 (
                      <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                      = 293) added an AI-attributed reassignment condition in which an AI engine matched students' interests, traits, and abilities with the most suitable available courses (participants in the AI condition read a simulated AI-generated learning analysis report.). Participants completed a learning task and reported learning engagement and self-efficacy. Mediation analyses were conducted using bootstrapping.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Experiment 1 showed that course reassignment was associated with lower learning engagement compared with self-selection, and this effect was mediated by self-efficacy (indirect effect B = 0.198, SE = 0.051, 95%CI [0.096, 0.299]). Experiment 2 demonstrated that AI-attributed reassignment attenuated this negative effect. Learning engagement in the AI-attributed condition did not differ from self-selection and was significantly higher than in random reassignment. Moreover, the indirect effect through self-efficacy became non-significant (B = 0.140, SE = 0.113, 95% CI [−0.077, 0.362]).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings identify self-efficacy as a key psychological mechanism through which course reassignment impairs learning engagement, and demonstrate that AI-attributed reassignment can restore both self-efficacy and engagement by signaling person-course fit. This study extends self-efficacy theory to the course selection context and offers a feasible, technology-driven intervention for mitigating the negative consequences of course reassignment in higher education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.69685/hhev4736.title: The profile of secondary education teachers in relation to the degree of utilization of digital learning objects in the educational process
doi:10.69685/hhev4736.abstract: <jats:p>The increasing demands in education, along with the use of technology tools, have changed the learning process for the benefit of students. The use of online educational material during lessons is constantly increasing. Digital learning objects (DLOs) are new educational resources that support instructional planning with the help of technology. Teachers plays an important role in this process, as they must manage and correctly use the new conditions by incorporating digital learning objects into teaching. The purpose of the present study was to portray the profile of secondary education teachers regarding the use of DLOs in teaching in relation to their demographic characteristics. Data were collected through a questionnaire used in the research of Tserola (2023). The analysis of the results showed that the specialty, teaching experience, teacher training and the school where they serve influenced the degree of utilization of DLOs in the classroom.</jats:p>

doi:10.54254/2755-2721/2026.ba37690.title: Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Coordinated Emergency Building Sweeps
doi:10.54254/2755-2721/2026.ba37690.abstract: <jats:p>We develop a Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) framework for coordinating emergency responders during building sweeps. The problem is formulated as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) that captures building topology, occupant vulnerability, dynamic hazards, and partial observability. In the six-room office baseline, MADDPG reaches a 134-second sweep time after 5,000 episodes, within 6.3% of the 126-second theoretical optimum and outperforming PPO and DQN. Extensions to a two-story school and a U-shaped warehouse achieve 120 seconds with five responders and 105 seconds with four responders, respectively, with diminishing returns beyond these staffing levels. Under communication failure, coverage remains about 98% while sweep time rises 15–20%; reduced staffing triggers workload redistribution, and dynamic hazards cause threatened areas to be prioritized. Occupancy sensing, mesh networks, and environmental sensing are projected to reduce sweep time by 35–50%. Sensitivity analysis confirms robust performance across realistic parameter ranges.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpls.2026.1932877.title: PPNet: a deep learning framework for rice seedling localization and distribution from UAV orthomosaics
doi:10.3389/fpls.2026.1932877.abstract: <jats:p>Field-scale information on rice seedling distribution is crucial for transplanting quality assessment, site-specific seedling-stage management, and precision agricultural operations. However, seedlings in UAV orthomosaics are small, closely spaced, and easily confused with soil, shallow water, plastic mulch, and shadows, which makes accurate localization challenging. Meanwhile, under high-density planting, existing segmentation-based networks often generate adhesive responses between neighboring seedlings, leading to missed detections and biased counting. To address these issues, this study proposed PPNet, a deep learning framework for rice seedling localization and distribution mapping from UAV orthomosaics. The framework uses root-based point annotation and integrates a rice-point perception module (RPPM), an adjacent decoupling module (ADM), and an aggregated attention module (AAM). These modules enhance seedling-point responses, separate adjacent seedlings, and introduce row-structure information. Experiments were conducted on a UAV orthomosaic dataset containing 3,013 image tiles and 220,553 seedling point annotations from different rice-growing regions. PPNet achieved an F1 score of 0.9029, an AP of 0.8881, a counting MAE of 6.99, and an R2 of 0.9553. The method also generated field-scale seedling point maps and density maps under different planting densities and field backgrounds. The results demonstrate that PPNet can provide reliable seedling localization and counting information for crop establishment assessment and targeted seedling management, supporting intelligent agricultural machinery decision-making in precision farming operations.</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/imefm-01-2026-0070.title: Geopolitical conflict, global uncertainty and equity market resilience in the MENA region: evidence from a quantile machine-learning framework
doi:10.1108/imefm-01-2026-0070.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examines how global uncertainty and domestic geopolitical conflict affect equity market resilience in six Middle East and North Africa (MENA) economies across stress, normal and expansion regimes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using monthly MSCI country-index series with country-specific starting dates between 2010 and 2016 and observations through 2025, the study constructs a Geopolitical Fatal Conflict Index (GFCI) from ACLED violent events and fatalities. The GFCI is combined with the Geopolitical Risk Index (GPR), the Financial Stress Index (FSI) and the Volatility Index (VIX) in a Quantile Gradient Boosting (QGB) framework. SHAP values are used to compare the relative contribution and direction of these predictors at Q10, Q50 and Q90.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results are heterogeneous across countries and quantiles rather than following a single regional pattern. At Q10, global indicators lead the SHAP ranking in Egypt, Morocco and Tunisia, whereas GFCI is the leading predictor in Jordan, Palestine and Saudi Arabia. At Q50 and Q90, GFCI remains or becomes prominent in Egypt, Palestine and Saudi Arabia, while VIX or FSI remain important in Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia. In the reported Q50 robustness comparison, including GFCI reduces MAE and RMSE and increases R² in all six markets.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings support country- and quantile-specific monitoring that combines global uncertainty indicators with country-level violent-conflict data. The results are intended for equity-market risk assessment and scenario monitoring rather than causal policy evaluation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study introduces the Geopolitical Fatal Conflict Index (GFCI) as a country-level measure of violent conflict intensity within a quantile machine-learning framework. It distinguishes domestic conflict dynamics from global geopolitical and financial uncertainty and shows that their relative predictive importance varies across countries and conditional quantiles.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.1108/imefm-01-2026-0070.venue: International Journal of Islamic and Middle Eastern Finance and Management

doi:10.54254/2753-7048/2026.37667.title: Growth Mindset and Confidence in Self-Directed Learning among Students in Four Southeast Asian Countries: The Mediating Role of Mathematics Self-Efficacy
doi:10.54254/2753-7048/2026.37667.abstract: <jats:p>Growth mindset has been widely studied in relation to students' motivation and academic achievement, yet less is known about how it relates to students' confidence in managing their own learning. This study examined whether mathematics self-efficacy helps explain the association between growth mindset and confidence in self-directed learning among Southeast Asian students. PISA 2022 data from 4,693 students in Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and Thailand were analysed using Pearson correlations and structural equation modelling, with gender and socioeconomic status included as covariates. Growth mindset was positively associated with mathematics self-efficacy (β = .086), while mathematics self-efficacy showed a stronger positive association with confidence in self-directed learning (β = .373). The direct association between growth mindset and confidence in self-directed learning was not significant (β = −.019). However, a small but significant indirect association through mathematics self-efficacy was observed (β = .032, 95% CI [.017, .042]). These findings suggest that mathematics self-efficacy may represent one pathway linking broader beliefs about the development of ability with students' confidence in managing their learning. The results also indicate that growth-mindset approaches may be more meaningful when accompanied by opportunities to strengthen task-specific confidence.</jats:p>
doi:10.54254/2753-7048/2026.37667.venue: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11156651/v1.title: Meta-Learning-Driven Deep Reinforcement Learning for Green Resource Management in 5G/6G Networks
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11156651/v1.abstract: Future sixth-generation (6G) mobile networks must satisfy demanding service requirements while operating under increasingly stringent sustainability constraints and variable energy conditions. Static heuristics and conventional deep reinforcement learning (DRL) policies can adapt slowly to changes in traffic, radio conditions, and energy availability, leading to inefficient resource use andavoidable emissions. We propose a meta-reinforcement learning framework that combines Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML) with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for energy-aware network orchestration. The method learns an initialization that can be adapted with a small number of gradient updates, supporting rapid response to changing operating conditions. We instantiate the framework in the Access and Mobility Management Function (AMF) of a virtualized core network, where joint CPU and memory allocation is formulated as a continuous-control problem with energy and carbon-intensity objectives.Evaluations against PPO, A2C, DQN, TD3, and SAC show improvements of up to 37% across energy efficiency, energy consumption, carbon footprint, and convergence-related metrics, while maintaining near-optimal service-level agreement compliance. These results indicate that meta-learned policy adaptation can support more sustainable resource management in dynamic 5G/6G corenetworks.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11156651/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010329/v1.title: Certifying the Kinetics of Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials from Single-Point Energies
doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010329/v1.abstract: <jats:p>Machine-learned interatomic potentials are validated by force errors on equilibrium configurations, yet activated rates depend on transition regions that equilibrium sampling rarely visits. In a onedimensional metastable double well, the worst-case rate sensitivity to force error grows as eβB/2 with barrier height B; a path-space bound valid at any friction shows that force error certifies rare-event frequencies only to within a factor that grows at the same rate. The leverage density weights energy errors by their influence on reactive transport: it is the normalised dissipation density of the reactive current. For reversible overdamped dynamics, the Dirichlet and Thomson principles give two-sided capacity bounds, converted to metastable rate bounds by basin population corrections. A path representation evaluates their averages from reactive trajectories, committor values and single-point energies. Sampling uses reference paths to assess sampled transitions and model paths to expose additional or overpopulated pathways. In alanine dipeptide, closely matched force errors produce rate changes from 0.49 to 3.5, consistent with estimated intervals. In Li3OCl, mechanism-resolved upper endpoints track six models’ vacancy-hop rates with a systematic underestimation of about 7%. Labels selected from both ensembles improve kinetics even as force errors rise. We propose reporting the energy-error contrast M between the leverage density and the basins, and the spread σν under the leverage density, alongside force error; both are independent of the energy zero.</jats:p>

doi:10.12688/f1000research.190609.1.title: MRI-based machine learning models for differentiating Parkinson’s disease and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
doi:10.12688/f1000research.190609.1.abstract: <ns3:p>Background Parkinson’s disease (PD) and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) are neurodegenerative disorder which have Parkinsonism as core clinical feature. PD and PSP are often misdiagnosed in early phases by conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Hence the objective of the study is to evaluate accuracy of MRI based machine learning (ML) models for differentiating PD and PSP. Methods This is a retrospective study including total of 96 subjects (32 PD, 32 PSP and 32 healthy controls). The basal nuclei region such as substantia nigra (SN), caudate nucleus (CN), putamen, globus pallidus (GP), red nucleus (RN), and subthalamic nucleus (STN) were manually segmented in T2 weighted fluid attenuation inversion recovery (T2W-FLAIR) images and radiomics features (RF) were extracted. The top 20 RF were used to train and test ML models. Performance measures of ML models for differentiating PD, PSP and HC were evaluated. Results For differentiating PD from PSP, SN consistently showed highest performance achieving accuracy, F1score and AUC values of 0.95–1.00 across all the tested ML models. RN and STN also demonstrated near perfect classification with several ML models with accuracy and AUC values of 1.00. CN, putamen and GP showed moderate performance (accuracy 38% - 85%). Among classifiers, AdaBoost provided robust performance achieving AUC up to 0.89 and MCC up to 0.72 in test data sets. Conclusion MRI based radiomics models from SN, STN and RN provide the most accurate classification of PD and PSP. It can also help in diagnosis of PD and PSP which are undifferentiable in early stages of disease.</ns3:p>

doi:10.3991/ijet.v21i04.62294.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence: Ethical Considerations and Its Impact on Students’ Cognitive Skills
doi:10.3991/ijet.v21i04.62294.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming higher education, influencing how students learn, produce knowledge, and engage in assessments. This study examines the ethical implications of AI integration in university courses and its perceived impact on students’ cognitive skills. Using a mixed-methods secondary data analysis, survey data from 23,218 students across 109 countries and 252 teachers from China, Romania, India, and Brunei were analyzed to explore perceptions of AI capabilities, ethical boundaries, behavioral intentions, and cognitive outcomes. The results have shown that although students are aware of the potential of AI in improving the efficiency and content creation and assistance in the learning process, there are still concerns about overdependence, plagiarism, and lack of critical thinking. The views of faculty underline moral direction and the necessity of systematic assimilation. Developing upon these insights, a theoretical framework is developed that connects antecedent variables, behavior intentions and institutional context to two outcomes the cognitive impact and institutional influence. This framework offers a guide on how universities should introduce generative AI in a responsible manner, and strike a balance between ethical principles and training higher-order cognitive abilities.</jats:p>
doi:10.3991/ijet.v21i04.62294.venue: International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning (iJET)

doi:10.1186/s12544-026-00852-y.title: Pedestrian interaction with highly automated vehicles in shared spaces: the roles of vehicle kinematics, external human–machine interfaces, and social cues
doi:10.1186/s12544-026-00852-y.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Highly automated vehicles (HAVs; SAE Levels 4–5) will increasingly operate in mixed traffic, raising challenges for pedestrian interaction—especially in shared-space environments where coordination relies on negotiation rather than formal right-of-way rules. Prior research has largely examined one-to-one pedestrian–HAV encounters, while the role of social cues from additional pedestrians remains underexplored. This study investigated how pedestrians integrate (a) an additional pedestrian’s behavior (absent vs. present–stopping vs. present–continuing to walk), (b) vehicle kinematics of the HAV (yielding vs. non-yielding), and (c) a visual light-based external human-machine interface (eHMI; present vs. absent) when forming willingness to cross and perceived safety in a shared-space scenario. In a video-based online experiment (
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                     = 136; 3 × 2 × 2 within-subjects), participants rated willingness to cross and perceived safety after each 9-s rendered video clip. Vehicle kinematics had a strong influence on both willingness to cross and perceived safety. The eHMI increased willingness to cross and perceived safety under yielding kinematics, but had no effect under non-yielding kinematics, indicating that eHMIs are beneficial primarily when congruent with vehicle kinematics. Additional pedestrian behavior affected both willingness to cross and perceived safety, but only when the HAV displayed yielding kinematics. Together, the findings suggest that, in shared-space interactions, vehicle kinematics emerged as the dominant cue, while eHMIs and social cues act as supportive signals whose influence depends on the vehicle’s kinematic. Further research is recommended to explore the influence of multiple pedestrians and more complex traffic scenarios.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.3991/ijet.v21i04.62656.title: Towards a Viability Approach for the Development of Task-Skill Mappings for the Validation of Prior Learning
doi:10.3991/ijet.v21i04.62656.abstract: <jats:p>Inclusive learning aims to guarantee equitable access to educational opportunities by validating competencies acquired across diverse contexts. In Côte d’Ivoire, where a major share of the active population operates within the informal sector, the Validation of Prior Learning (Validation des Acquis de l’Expérience – VAE) constitutes a critical lever for certifying these skills. However, its operational implementation remains complex due to cumbersome evaluation procedures and the rigidity of certification frameworks. This paper proposes an innovative dynamic systems approach rooted in viability theory to automate and optimize the design of the “task-skill” mappings essential to VAE. By leveraging graph Laplacian operators and differential inclusions, this method models the propagation of knowledge flows within a bounded viability kernel. Experimental validation conducted on a cohort of 300 artisans from the Lagunes region demonstrates the robustness of the model: the stabilized profiles achieve high topological congruence with the official CQP (Professional Qualification Certificate) framework, yielding a Jaccard similarity index of 0.92 and a Cohen’s Kappa coefficient of 0.84, while ensuring rapid asymptotic convergence within 150 iterations. The results confirm that this viability approach improves the reliability of didactic diagnostics and reduces the temporal overhead of assessment sessions, thereby facilitating certification access for individuals from informal backgrounds and mitigating educational inequalities. Moving forward, this adaptive model paves the way for hyperparameter self-calibration and sectorial transposition to other evolving professional fields.</jats:p>
doi:10.3991/ijet.v21i04.62656.venue: International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning (iJET)

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-0353-4.ch004.title: Epistemic Leadership in Higher Education and the Challenge of Disinformation
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-0353-4.ch004.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter introduces the concept of epistemic leadership as a framework for strengthening trust, credibility, and knowledge legitimacy in higher education. Drawing on Social Epistemology, Social Constructivism, and Social Identity Theory, it argues that universities function not only as learning organizations but also as epistemic organizations that govern the production, evaluation, and dissemination of knowledge. The chapter examines how trust, identity, and credibility shape learning cultures and explores the risks of epistemic fragmentation in an era of misinformation and disinformation. It proposes epistemically resilient learning cultures supported by transparent governance, shared standards of inquiry, constructive disagreement, and inclusive participation. Educational leaders are conceptualized as stewards of institutional epistemic environments, responsible for cultivating trustworthy knowledge systems and sustaining institutional resilience.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-0353-4.ch004.venue: Shaping Learning Cultures Through Effective Leadership

doi:10.5194/gstm2026-12.title: Machine Learning-Based Accelerometer Transplantation for GRACE and Future Quantum-Enabled Satellite Gravimetry
doi:10.5194/gstm2026-12.abstract: <jats:p>Accurate and continuous determination of the Earth’s time-variable gravity field is essential for monitoring mass redistribution related to hydrological, climatic, and geodynamic processes. GRACE and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) have demonstrated the high capability of low-low satellite-to-satellite tracking (LL-SST) technique for global gravity field recovery; however, the resulting accuracy strongly depends on the quality of the involved sensors, e.g., the accelerometers (ACC) used to account for non-gravitational forces. While conventional electrostatic accelerometers (EA) provide high short-term sensitivity, their performance is affected by drift at low frequencies. Emerging quantum-based sensors, particularly Cold Atom Interferometry (CAI) accelerometers, offer promising characteristics to overcome the later issue for future satellite gravimetry.This study investigates accelerometer observation transplantation to reduce the number of accelerometers required onboard future satellite gravimetry missions. Different configurations involving EA, CAI, and hybrid EA–CAI accelerometers are evaluated using closed-loop LL-SST simulations. Four scenarios are considered, ranging from the conventional EA-only configuration to an ideal configuration in which both satellites carry complete hybrid accelerometers. Particular attention is given to a reduced-sensor configuration in which EA and CAI observations are transplanted between satellites, enabling a virtual hybrid configuration with fewer physical accelerometers.In addition to conventional analytical transplantation, machine-learning (ML) approaches, including Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), are investigated to improve the transplanted accelerometer observations. The configurations are evaluated directly at the gravity-field level. The results show that the complete dual-hybrid configuration provides the highest performance, while the ML-based reduced-sensor configuration significantly improves upon analytical transplantation and approaches the performance of the ideal hybrid configuration.The data-driven transplantation concept is further assessed using real GRACE accelerometer observations. During GRACE and GRACE-FO, accelerometer degradation or failure affected the availability and quality of non-gravitational acceleration observations, requiring their reconstruction. An LSTM-based dynamic mapping using GRACE-A accelerometer observations and auxiliary non-gravitational force models is developed to reconstruct GRACE-B accelerations. The reconstructed observations are introduced into monthly gravity field recovery and evaluated through degree variances, equivalent-water-height representations, and RMS variability over the oceans. The results demonstrate successful reconstruction of the missing accelerometer information and improvements in the resulting monthly gravity field solutions. The same framework can also be adapted to degraded accelerometer observations in GRACE-FO.Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of ML for recovering missing or degraded accelerometer observations and enabling reduced-sensor architectures for future satellite gravimetry. Combining quantum sensing, accelerometer transplantation, and ML provides a promising pathway toward high-performance, less complex, and potentially more cost-effective future gravimetry missions.Keywords: Satellite gravimetry; GRACE; GRACE-FO; accelerometer transplantation; Cold Atom Interferometry; hybrid accelerometers; machine learning; time-variable gravity field.Acknowledgement: This work was supported by Germany’s Excellence Strategy – EXC-2123 “QuantumFrontiers” – 390837967.</jats:p>

doi:10.68178/xn89ft66.title: <b>Autoconcepto y estrategias de aprendizaje en estudiantes de enfermería</b>
doi:10.68178/xn89ft66.abstract: <jats:p>Objective: To determine the relationship between self-concept and learning strategies among nursing students. Methods: Quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional correlational study. The population comprised 610 students in the 8th, 9th and 10th academic terms; 236 participants were selected by simple random probabilistic sampling. A version of the AF5 questionnaire assessing academic, emotional and social self-concept and a learning strategies scale covering cognitive and learning-control strategies, learning support, and study habits were administered. Normality was assessed with the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test and associations with Spearman's rho. Results: Medium self-concept was observed in 62.3% of participants and medium learning strategies in 68.6%. Overall self-concept was positively and moderately correlated with learning strategies (rho=0.604; p<0.001). Significant correlations were also found for academic self-concept (rho=0.604; p<0.001) and social self-concept (rho=0.418; p<0.001), whereas emotional self-concept was not associated (rho=0.027; p=0.683). Conclusion: Higher self-concept, particularly its academic and social components, was associated with greater use of learning strategies. The cross-sectional design does not allow causal inference. Keywords: self-concept; learning strategies; nursing students; higher education; self-regulated learning.</jats:p>
doi:10.68178/xn89ft66.venue: Perspectivas en Ciencias Médicas y Biológicas

doi:10.69685/qgqe7580.title: Creative Teaching and Learning: Applying Edward de Bono’s Six Thinking Hats Method in Education
doi:10.69685/qgqe7580.abstract: <jats:p>Creativity is a fundamental skill of the 21st century, and its cultivation in Primary Education is crucial. The purpose of this study was to investigate the effect of Edward de Bono’s Six Thinking Hats method on the creative writing of third-grade students. A mixed-methods approach was adopted, with an intervention-based pre- and post-measurement design without a control group, involving a sample of 22 students. Data were collected through questionnaires, observation, and analysis of written texts, and were analyzed using descriptive statistics and thematic categorization. The results showed that 86% of the students understood the method, 77% increased their production of creative ideas, and 64% improved the structure of their texts. Additionally, participation and organization of thought were enhanced. Despite the limitations, the findings suggest a positive contribution of the method to the development of creative thinking.</jats:p>

doi:10.48175/ijarsct-38827.title: Smart Plant Disease Detection Using Deep Learning
authors: Nisha Amar Bhosale and Dr. Kiran Tikar
doi:10.48175/ijarsct-38827.abstract:
<jats:p>Plant diseases can damage crops and reduce both the quality and quantity of agricultural production. Finding a disease early is important because farmers can take action before it spreads. However, checking plant leaves by looking at them manually is not always easy, especially when different diseases have similar symptoms.
This research presents a Smart Plant Disease Detection system that uses deep learning and image classification. The system is designed to identify tomato leaf conditions from images and classify them into three categories: Healthy, Early Blight, and Late Blight. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was trained using a plant disease image dataset. The images were prepared and used to teach the model the visual patterns of different leaf conditions.
 The trained model was tested with a new image and successfully identified the condition of the leaf. In the project test, a healthy tomato leaf was predicted with 99.99% confidence. A simple Gradio interface was also created, allowing a user to upload a leaf image and get a prediction. The system can make plant disease identification quicker and easier and may help farmers and other agriculture-related users take early action..</jats:p>
doi:10.48175/ijarsct-38827.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1907942.title: Lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio and improved prognostication of renal cell carcinoma: machine learning-based analysis
doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1907942.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To investigate utility of a novel ratio, lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio (LCR), for improved prognostic stratification in RCC.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted a retrospective machine learning–based analysis in a multicenter RCC cohort who underwent surgery (Radical or Partial Nephrectomy). Cut-off for “low” or “high” LCR was delineated by receiver operating characteristics/area under curve (ROC/AUC). Multivariable Analysis was conducted for predictors of all-cause mortality (ACM) and cancer-specific mortality (CSM). LCR, along with UCLA Integrated Staging System (UISS) factors, were included into MVA model to evaluate CSM. Employing Classification and Regression Tree (CART), we developed a decision tree based on hazard ratios (HR). The predictive performance was calculated using ROC/AUC.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We analyzed 2071 patients [low LCR n=598/high LCR n=1473; cut-off=237.87 (AUC = 0.80)], median follow-up 60 months). Low LCR is an independent risk factor for ACM (HR = 2.75, p&lt;0.001) and CSM (HR = 2.70, p&lt;0.001). Including LCR (HR = 2.60, p&lt;0.001), tumor stage (Stage II: HR = 6.7, Stage III: HR = 6.5, Stage IV: HR = 26.8, p&lt;0.001) nuclear grade (HR = 3.0, p&lt;0.001) and ECOG (HR = 1.6, p=0.002) in the CART, patients were re-stratified [(HR&lt;1.0 (low-risk), HR = 1.0-2.0 (intermediate-risk), HR&gt;2.0 (high-risk)]. AUC of 0.91 was revealed for the modified UISS model (AUC = 0.85 in the classic UISS model). Our findings are limited by retrospective design.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study provides evidence supporting the prognostic significance of LCR in RCC. While low LCR was associated with poorer survival outcomes, incorporating LCR into the UISS model enhanced prognostic stratification in RCC patients. Further investigation is requisite to validate our findings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1007/s12186-026-09396-7.title: Workplace Social Support for Apprentices During the COVID-19 Pandemic – A Mixed-Methods Study on the Perceptions of Vocational Trainers and Apprentices in Switzerland
doi:10.1007/s12186-026-09396-7.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Apprentices in dual vocational education and training (VET) rely strongly on workplace social support (WSS), including guidance, feedback, recognition, and social integration. During the COVID-19 pandemic, training firms had to reorganise work and learning processes, which may have affected how such support was provided and experienced. This study investigates how WSS for apprentices changed during the pandemic in Swiss dual VET and how these changes were linked to different firm-level crisis conditions. It also examines how trainers’ and apprentices’ perspectives complement each other. The study applies a convergent mixed-methods design, combining survey data from 1,380 vocational trainers with 16 focus group interviews involving 119 apprentices. The analysis compares four pandemic-related conditions: short-time work, working from home, increased workload, and marginal impact. Trainers tended to report that WSS was largely maintained, with particularly positive assessments in firms affected by short-time work and working from home. Apprentices presented a more differentiated picture. They described support as less spontaneous, less consistently accessible, and more dependent on specific work and training arrangements. In short-time work and remote settings, support often became more formalised and was accompanied by fewer task opportunities. In increased workload settings, apprentices more often reported limited guidance, feedback, and emotional support. The findings suggest that crises do not merely reduce or preserve WSS; they reshape its accessibility and meaning. Combining provider and recipient perspectives is therefore essential for understanding support in disrupted training contexts.</jats:p>

doi:10.31098/cset.v5i1.1215.title: Medicinal Plant Leaf Classification: From Hand-Crafted Features to Real-Time Mobile Deep Learning
doi:10.31098/cset.v5i1.1215.abstract: <jats:p>Medicinal plant leaves are central to traditional healthcare in biodiversity-rich countries such as Indonesia, yet high visual similarity between species makes manual identification error-prone. Classification methods for medicinal and herbal leaves have shifted from hand-crafted feature classifiers to deep convolutional and attention-based architectures, and more recently to real-time, on-device deployment. This narrative review traces that progression and identifies open gaps. Twenty primary studies published between 2016 and 2026 were identified through Scopus, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and Springer and grouped into five categories: hand-crafted features, CNN transfer learning, attention-based fusion, YOLO-based detection, and mobile/edge deployment. Unlike earlier reviews, each study is also coded for whether its model was validated on physical mobile or embedded hardware. The review finds a clear shift toward deep transfer learning models, many reporting accuracies above 90%, and toward architectures designed for on-device use. However, only three of the nine medicinal-leaf-specific studies tested their models on real hardware; these rarely report standardized latency or frame-rate figures, and public benchmark datasets for Indonesian species remain scarce. These gaps motivate work that evaluates classification accuracy and on-device inference performance together.</jats:p>
doi:10.31098/cset.v5i1.1215.venue: RSF Conference Series: Engineering and Technology

doi:10.3389/fradi.2026.1963539.title: Deep learning prediction of overall survival in glioblastoma patients using pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data
doi:10.3389/fradi.2026.1963539.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits variable treatment response and patients shown a median survival of 15 months. A major challenge lies in the difficulty of reliably assessing treatment response at an early stage, as it can usually only be evaluated on anatomical MRI performed up to three months after the start of treatment, when early interpretation may be complicated by the risk of pseudoprogression. Accurately predicting short-term and long-term survivors before radiotherapy and chemotherapy is therefore crucial. The objective of this study is to develop an AI model designed to predict survival outcomes based exclusively on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 1,575 retrospective T1-Gd brain images were obtained from 175 patients treated for GBM between 2018 and 2023. A ResNet-51Q model pretrained on ImageNet was fine-tuned on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI using transfer learning. To incorporate clinical data, deep hybrid learning (DHL) models were trained.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>At patient-level, the AI model achieved 81.08% (CI 95%: 67.57–91.89), 68.42% (CI 95%: 47.06–88.89) and 94.44% (CI 95%: 81.82–1.00) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively, for the classification of short-term and long-term survivors using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI. At patient-level, the three-class model using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI, achieved 87.18% (CI 95%: 76.92– 97.44), 87.18% (CI 95%: 76.68–96.97), and 93.59% (CI 95%: 88.03–98.41) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively. In comparison at slice-level, the three-class model using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI, achieved 81.77% (CI 95%: 70.66–91.45), 81.77% (CI 95%: 71.07–91.33), and 90.88% (CI 95%: 85.25–95.74) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively. In comparison the DHL model with clinical data achieved an accuracy of 84.62% (CI 95%: 71.79–94.87), a sensitivity of 84.62% (CI 95%: 72.54–95.24) and a specificity of 92.31% (CI 95%: 86.07–97.53) and 76.32% (CI 95%: 63.16–89.47), 76.11% (CI 95%: 61.63–88.75) and 92.06% (CI 95%: 87.51–96.23) for four overall survival classification. For multiclass tasks, metrics were calculated using a macro-averaged approach.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The combination of pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data using the DHL model for early survival prediction; however, adding clinical variables yielded comparable prognostic performance rather than a demonstrable enhancement over imaging features alone. The use of AI models to predict survival outcome in GBM from pre-chemoradiotherapy data may support pre-chemoradiotherapy prognostic stratification.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1835503.title: Predictors of guideline-concordant treatment intensification in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer: an explainable machine learning study
doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1835503.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Treatment intensification with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) combined with docetaxel, an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor, or selected triplet regimens is recommended for eligible patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC). Despite increasing adoption, implementation remains variable in routine clinical practice.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To characterize temporal trends in first-line systemic treatment for mCSPC and identify factors associated with receipt of guideline-concordant treatment intensification using exploratory explainable machine learning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>National treatment patterns were evaluated using the Pfizer Oncology Quality Care Insight Tool derived from IQVIA Anonymized Patient Longitudinal Data, and institutional patterns were evaluated within Avera Health. The exploratory cohort included 42 patients with documented mCSPC treated between 2018 and 2023. Guideline-concordant treatment intensification was defined as ADT combined with docetaxel or a novel hormonal therapy within 90 days of ADT initiation. Potential outcome-derived variables were excluded before modeling. Six predictive approaches were evaluated using repeated nested stratified cross-validation, with 5-fold outer cross-validation repeated 20 times and 5-fold inner cross-validation repeated three times. Recursive feature elimination was performed within outer training folds, and class imbalance was addressed using SMOTE within resampling.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Thirty-two (32) of forty-two (42) patients (76.2%) received guideline-concordant treatment intensification. Treatment-pattern analysis showed increasing use of first-line novel hormonal therapy and declining ADT monotherapy over time. Under repeated nested validation, discrimination was modest and variable across models. The Decision Tree achieved the highest patient-level AUC (0.675; 95% CI, 0.421–0.929), whereas Random Forest achieved an AUC of 0.650 (95% CI, 0.383–0.917), accuracy of 85.7%, precision of 88.2%, recall of 93.8%, and F1 score of 0.909. Feature-selection stability identified insurance coverage for novel hormonal therapy as the most consistently selected predictor, followed by positive core proportion and smoking history. These three variables were retained in the final explanatory Random Forest model, and global SHAP and Random Forest importance analysis showed broadly concordant rankings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Treatment intensification for mCSPC increased substantially in routine practice. Repeated nested validation produced more conservative and variable performance estimates than the original single-split analysis, underscoring the exploratory nature of this small cohort. Healthcare access and selected clinical factors warrant further evaluation in larger, multicenter datasets.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3390/machines14101185.title: A Preclinical Human–Machine Reliability and Operational Safety Assessment Framework for a Rehabilitation Massage Robot Prototype
doi:10.3390/machines14101185.abstract: <jats:p>With the increasing use of massage robots as direct-contact rehabilitation devices, their evaluation must address both equipment failures and use-related risks. This study presents a prototype-stage assessment framework for a seated knee-adjustment bionic massage robot that integrates failure mode, effects, and criticality analysis (FMECA), task analysis, and fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (FAHP) weighting based on a fuzzy complementary judgment matrix. FMECA identified 28 failure modes across the actuation, sensing, and drive-control subsystems. Simulated-use testing involving 15 operators and 15 healthy adults acting as simulated patients comprised 19 observable subtasks and recorded 66 use errors across 285 subtask opportunities. The normalized scores for the actuation, sensing, drive-control, and operational-safety indicators were 0.796, 0.691, 0.808, and 0.768, respectively. Interval-based aggregation yielded Q = 0.848 (“Very Good”), whereas direct weighting of the same normalized inputs yielded Scont = 0.767, within the “Good” interval. Across η ∈ [0, 1], Q ranged from 0.753 to 0.902. A same-panel expert assessment yielded 0.904 and the same grade, although this comparison did not constitute independent validation. Inaccurate pressure-sensor output had the highest risk priority number of 32, while confusion between left- and right-side pressure readings was the most frequent use error, with 11 occurrences. The framework supports prototype-stage risk identification and prioritization but does not establish clinical efficacy, certified safety, or long-term reliability.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/computers15100709.title: Risk-Adaptive Behavioral Attenuation via Episode-Latched Policy Gating and Bounded Relearning for Deployed Reinforcement Learning Agents
doi:10.3390/computers15100709.abstract: <jats:p>Reinforcement learning behaviors can become harmful after deployment even when the policy is unchanged, a risk existing methods address mainly before or during training rather than through reversible correction. This paper proposes a risk-adaptive attenuation framework for a frozen context-conditioned policy encoding validated nominal and safe endpoint behaviors. Recurring harm is identified through evidence accumulation, and a severity-aware selector applies gradual, accelerated, or hard-switch attenuation latched for the full episode. Verified probes support bounded relearning, and recurrent harm reactivates the intervention. The selector is a fixed rule, and only the base policy is trained with reinforcement learning. Evaluation uses Risk Corridor, a stochastic-cost gridworld, with ten policies tested across fixed, mixed, and noisy-observation conditions against shield and Recovery RL baselines. Under mixed-severity deployment the selector reached a final hazard rate of 0.00 and task completion of 1.00 at a safety cost of 3.98, above hard switching (2.83) and Recovery RL (0.00). Deviation cost was 44.36, versus 61.20 for Recovery RL (27.5% lower) and 27.81 for the shield, which completed only one of three phases. The framework is best described as a safety–utility trade-off rather than superior safety. Mode-selection accuracy remained above 0.96 at 0.10 observation noise, safety and reversibility held across all tested conditions, and aired differences were consistent for at least nine of ten policies, reaching the exact test’s minimum attainable significance (p=0.00195) for four of five comparators.</jats:p>

doi:10.3991/ijet.v21i04.62876.title: Toward an Integrative Framework for Valid Research in Educational Technology: Insights from Virtual Reality Learning
doi:10.3991/ijet.v21i04.62876.abstract: <jats:p>This methodological and conceptual contribution develops an integrative framework for research on educational technology that systematically links internal and external validity, different research approaches, and heterogeneous outcome dimensions. Drawing on the recurring disappointment regarding the limited learning benefits of digital technologies— illustrated by the example of virtual reality (VR)—the article argues that technological innovations can only be adequately assessed if their effects can be clearly attributed and transferred to authentic learning contexts. Using central research logics, including media comparison, value-added, and ATI/LTI approaches, it shows how the choice of research approach shapes the type of evidence generated and the associated validity requirements. In addition, the article extends existing outcome models by incorporating a behavioral dimension to reflect the multidimensional nature of teaching and learning processes. The proposed framework illustrates that progress in educational technology research depends on the combination of methodological rigor, context-sensitive evidence, and multidimensional outcome assessment. Finally, practice-oriented recommendations are presented to support cumulative evidence development, transparent reporting standards, and the integration of laboratory and field research.</jats:p>
doi:10.3991/ijet.v21i04.62876.venue: International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning (iJET)

doi:10.1515/icos-2026-0031.title: Mutual Learning Between Islamic and Confucian Civilizations: Historical Interactions and Modern Implications
doi:10.1515/icos-2026-0031.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study examines the historical contacts and contemporary implications of reciprocal learning between Islamic and Confucian civilizations. The exchanges between these two significant traditions, although frequently overwhelmed by the East–West narrative, have profoundly influenced knowledge, culture, and governance throughout Asia and beyond. This study emphasizes the profound intellectual exchange facilitated by historical interactions, including the Silk Road, the contributions of Ibn Battuta and Zheng He, and the experiences of the Hui Muslim communities in China. The common principles of ethics, education, justice, and government establish a foundation for ongoing discourse, particularly pertinent in the 21st century. The article contends that leveraging these traditions can aid in tackling global issues such as sustainable development, ethical governance, and multicultural harmony.</jats:p>

doi:10.4208/cicc.2026.191.01.title: Machine-Learning-Integral-Based Density Functional Theory: mi-DFT
doi:10.4208/cicc.2026.191.01.abstract: <jats:p>Kohn–Sham density functional theory (KS-DFT) has achieved widespread success owing to its favorable balance between computational accuracy and efficiency. However, its application to molecular aggregates remains challenging because the steep increase in the number of atoms leads to an explosive growth in two-electron integral evaluations, with the computational bottleneck manifesting directly in the construction of high-dimensional Kohn–Sham (KS) matrices. To address this issue, we have developed a Machine-Learning-Integral-Based Density Functional Theory (mi-DFT), which is specifically suited for studying molecular aggregates. By leveraging a machine-learning integral strategy, mi-DFT significantly reduces the cost of constructing high-dimensional KS matrices while exhibiting favorable scalability. Benchmarked against the mi-DFT-Bench dataset—which encompasses one- and two-dimensional $CO_2$ and $H_2O$ systems, as well as one-dimensional ethylene and benzene aggregates—mi-DFT was systematically validated for wavefunctions, energies, and electron densities. The results demonstrate that the energy error of mi-DFT relative to standard DFT is less than 0.3 mH. Furthermore, for one-dimensional $CO_2$ and $H_2O$ systems comprising 2520 atomic-orbital (AO) basis functions, mi-DFT achieves a speedup of 2–5 fold over standard KS-DFT. Although the acceleration is modest at this scale, mi-DFT exhibits a near-linear scaling with system size owing to its local-block prediction strategy, enabling the method to be extended to much larger aggregates: DFT calculations with 30000 basis functions can be completed within 10 hours, where conventional methods would require weeks under equivalent hardware. This method provides a practical pathway for large-scale KS-DFT electronic-structure predictions of molecular aggregates that simultaneously preserves accuracy, transferability, and computational efficiency.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fmolb.2026.1853169.title: Deciphering isonicotinylation and mast cell-associated pathogenic patterns in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: evidence from ensemble learning-driven multi-omics and in vitro validation
doi:10.3389/fmolb.2026.1853169.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is dystrophin-deficiency skeletal and cardiac muscle disease. Protein post-translational modification (PTM) and aberrant immune cell activation play a key role in its pathogenesis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our study aims to investigate isonicotinylation (Kinic)-associated signature modulatory patterns in mast cells and DMD pathogenesis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We first performed integrated bioinformatic methods, such as WGCNA, GSVA, and CIBERSORT to identify Kinic and mast cell (KM)-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in DMD patient muscle bulk profiles (GSE38417 and GSE109178). Next, consensus clustering and assembling machine learning pipeline identified KM-associated diagnostic model and molecular subgroups in training the DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE6011), and then, diagnostic model performance was examined in the independent DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE32720). In addition, SHAP analysis decoded the main contributor in KM-associated diagnostic model construction, and contributor molecular and immune characters in DMD were estimated in GSE6011 and the DMD mouse muscle single-cell transcriptomic dataset (GSE213925) assisted by computational virtual cells. In addition, the deep learning framework and network pharmacology identified the drug synergy strategy for the treatment of DMD. Finally, the
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      assay identified expression patterns of the main contributor.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>KM-associated molecular patterns can potentially guide the diagnostic and molecular stratification for DMD patients. USP18 can be considered an upregulated and mast cell-distributed hub gene involved in pathogenesis of DMD. In addition, finafloxacin with BRD-K10482608 can be considered two potential therapeutic candidates for DMD patient clinical applications.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our investigation described a novel forecasting and therapeutic model for DMD patients, which potentially enhances DMD patient clinical translation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.46799/adv.v4i10.675.title: The Effect of Interactive Learning Media on Student Engagement: A Systematic Literature Review
doi:10.46799/adv.v4i10.675.abstract: <jats:p>Interactive learning media are increasingly used to create more participatory learning experiences; however, evidence regarding their contribution to student engagement varies across media types and implementation contexts. This systematic literature review synthesizes empirical findings on how interactive learning media influence behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement, identifies the types of media reported as effective, and examines the implementation challenges most frequently reported. The review followed a systematic literature review process informed by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and covered publications from 2021 to 2025. The manuscript reports that 32 candidate articles were retrieved from Google Scholar using search terms related to interactive learning media and student engagement. After title and abstract screening, 12 articles were excluded, leaving 20 studies for narrative synthesis. The reviewed evidence consistently associated interactive media with increased participation, motivation, attention, exploration, and learning interaction. Gamified platforms such as Quizizz and Wordwall were associated with greater active participation and motivation, interactive video supported participation and learning achievement, and virtual reality (VR) provided immersive learning experiences. However, no single medium was consistently superior across contexts; effectiveness depended on alignment with learning objectives, student characteristics, pedagogical design, and implementation conditions. Common challenges included limited infrastructure, educators' digital competence, insufficient institutional support, distraction, and concerns regarding information validity. Overall, interactive media can strengthen student engagement when technology is integrated into a coherent pedagogical design rather than used as an isolated technological intervention.</jats:p>

doi:10.51878/secondary.v6i4.15433.title: IMPLEMENTASI PEMBELAJARAN MENDALAM MELALUI PROJECT-BASED LEARNING YANG DIDUKUNG AI-BASED MICROLEARNING TERHADAP HASIL BELAJAR TEKNIK KOMPUTER DAN JARINGAN PADA MATERI SERANGAN SIBER KELAS XI SMK MUHAMMADIYAH 1 PEKANBARU
doi:10.51878/secondary.v6i4.15433.abstract:
<jats:p>This study was motivated by the low learning outcomes of students in the cyberattack topic in the 11th-grade Computer and Network Engineering (TKJ) class at SMK Muhammadiyah 1 Pekanbaru. This study aimed to describe the implementation of Deep Learning through the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model supported by AI-Based Microlearning and to analyze changes in students’ learning outcomes after the implementation of the learning approach. The study employed a quantitative approach using a pre-experimental method with a One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. The participants consisted of 25 students from the 11th-grade TKJ class. Data were collected through learning outcome tests, product assessments, presentation assessments, and documentation. The data were analyzed using normality tests, the Paired Sample t-Test, N-Gain, and effect size analysis using Cohen’s d. AI-Based Microlearning was used as conceptual reinforcement by presenting concise learning materials on the types, characteristics, impacts, and prevention of cyberattacks before students conducted case analyses, participated in group discussions, and completed projects in the form of educational posters and presentations. The product assessment score for the posters was 88.3%, while the presentation assessment score was 90.3%, both categorized as very good. These scores reflected students’ achievement in project activities and were not used as the sole indicators of the overall implementation of the learning process. The mean learning outcome score increased from 61.46 in the pretest to 83.39 in the posttest. The Paired Sample t-Test showed a significant difference between the pretest and posttest scores (p < 0.001). The mean N-Gain score was 0.569, categorized as moderate, while Cohen’s d of 1.43 indicated a large effect size. These findings indicate that the implementation of Deep Learning through PjBL supported by AI-Based Microlearning was associated with improved student learning outcomes; however, the improvement cannot be fully attributed to the intervention because the study did not employ a control group. The integration of these three approaches may serve as an alternative strategy for contextual and problem-solving-oriented learning in Computer and Network Engineering.
ABSTRAK
Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya hasil belajar peserta didik pada materi serangan siber di kelas XI Teknik Komputer dan Jaringan (TKJ) SMK Muhammadiyah 1 Pekanbaru. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan implementasi Pembelajaran Mendalam melalui model Project-Based Learning (PjBL) berbantuan AI-Based Microlearning serta menganalisis perubahan hasil belajar peserta didik setelah penerapan pembelajaran tersebut. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode pra-eksperimen dan desain One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 25 peserta didik kelas XI TKJ. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes hasil belajar, penilaian produk, penilaian presentasi, dan dokumentasi. Data dianalisis menggunakan uji normalitas, Paired Sample t-Test, N-Gain, dan ukuran efek menggunakan Cohen’s d. AI-Based Microlearning digunakan sebagai penguatan konsep dengan menyajikan materi singkat mengenai jenis, karakteristik, dampak, dan pencegahan serangan siber sebelum peserta didik melakukan analisis kasus, diskusi kelompok, serta menyelesaikan proyek berupa poster edukasi dan presentasi. Hasil penilaian produk poster sebesar 88,3% dan presentasi sebesar 90,3%, keduanya berkategori sangat baik. Kedua hasil tersebut menggambarkan capaian peserta didik dalam aktivitas proyek dan tidak digunakan sebagai satu-satunya indikator keterlaksanaan keseluruhan pembelajaran. Rata-rata hasil belajar meningkat dari 61,46 pada pretest menjadi 83,39 pada posttest. Hasil Paired Sample t-Test menunjukkan perbedaan yang signifikan antara skor pretest dan posttest (p < 0,001). Nilai rata-rata N-Gain sebesar 0,569 berada pada kategori sedang, sedangkan Cohen’s d sebesar 1,43 menunjukkan ukuran efek yang besar. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa penerapan Pembelajaran Mendalam melalui PjBL berbantuan AI-Based Microlearning berkaitan dengan peningkatan hasil belajar peserta didik; namun, peningkatan tersebut belum dapat sepenuhnya diatribusikan pada perlakuan karena penelitian tidak menggunakan kelompok kontrol. Integrasi ketiga pendekatan tersebut dapat menjadi alternatif strategi pembelajaran TKJ yang kontekstual dan berorientasi pada pemecahan masalah.</jats:p>

doi:10.1088/2051-672x/aeae56.title: Z-Map-based iterative modelling and parameterised experimental comparison of the scraped surface topography of machine-tool guideways

At the trend level, the model reproduces the stage-wise progression of PPI and POP. At the value level, the core load-bearing height and volume parameters agree in order of magnitude but show a systematic relative underestimation associated with the idealised geometric-removal description, whereas the extreme-value parameters dominated by random deep valleys diverge as expected. doi:10.69685/glfg0964.title: A Multimodal Learning Medium: The Electronic Book in Foreign Language Education
doi:10.69685/glfg0964.abstract: <jats:p>The digital era has radically transformed the way readers approach texts, turning the book from a passive repository of information into an interactive learning environment. The contemporary electronic book is characterized by its multimodal nature, as meaning is constructed through the interaction of linguistic, visual, and auditory elements. At the same time, the integration of digital books into foreign language teaching is closely linked to the development of New Literacies, which broaden the concept of literacy and redefine the processes of meaning-making within the modern educational context. The present study was based on interviews with ten teachers and aims to investigate their perceptions regarding the use and selection of electronic books in foreign language teaching.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1989345.title: Teacher-student interaction and self-regulated learning in online higher education: a grounded theory model of interaction convertibility
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1989345.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Online higher education places greater demands on students’ self-regulation while making instructional support increasingly dependent on digitally mediated interaction. Although teacher–student interaction has been associated with self-regulated learning (SRL), less is known about how interaction becomes incorporated into students’ regulatory processes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using a Straussian grounded theory approach, this study examined the online learning experiences of 30 Chinese university students through semi-structured interviews conducted between April and May 2025. A relational model was developed through the analysis of 24 interviews, followed by six additional interviews used to assess theoretical saturation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Online learning conditions shaped opportunities for regulatory coupling. Interaction supported SRL when interactional input was recognized, taken up, and translated into changes in attention, understanding, strategy, or subsequent action. Resource mobilization, monitoring and reflection, and environment, time, and task management further helped stabilize this coupling across learning phases.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study develops the concept of interaction convertibility to explain how teacher–student interaction becomes, or fails to become, a usable regulatory resource in online higher education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Distinct treatment strategies for small‐cell lung cancer (SCLC) and non‐small‐cell lung cancer (NSCLC) brain metastases require accurate noninvasive subtyping.</jats:p>

                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To develop and externally validate a biparametric MRI‐based 2.5D multi‐instance learning (MIL) deep learning (DL) model for discriminating SCLC from NSCLC brain metastases, with performance compared against clinical, radiomics, and 3D‐DL models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
