This review draws on research carried out between 2020 and 2025 in order to look at how cloud architecture can support these types of workloads on an enterprise level while taking into account the Saudi situation regarding rapid digital transformation, the adoption of cloud services, data governance and the modernisation of various sectors. The review applies a structured evidence-synthesis approach focused on infrastructure architecture, workload orchestration, MLOps, cloud-edge distribution, security, reliability, cost control and organisational readiness. The evidence shows that scalable AI infrastructure should be viewed as a coordinated platform rather than as a set of separate services; effective designs incorporate elastic pools of CPU and GPU resources, container orchestration, tiered data services, automated model pipelines, observability, policy controls, workload-aware scheduling and selective edge execution. The Saudi Enterprise AI Cloud Framework proposed in this review combines these capabilities into six layers and includes a closed operational loop that links demand prediction, placement, execution, telemetry, policy evaluation and lifecycle learning. The review maintains that scalability must be assessed together with availability, cost predictability, data sovereignty, operational resilience and discipline in managing the model lifecycle. It ends with an implementation roadmap and a research agenda for businesses that wish to industrialise AI as part of their digital transformation aligned with Vision 2030.

doi:10.1201/9781003519348-13.title: Introduction to Outcome Weighted Learning for Optimal Treatment Regimes
doi:10.1201/9781003519348-13.abstract: Precision medicine has received much attention among statisticians, computer scientists, and clinicians. Its goal is to improve patient outcomes by delivering the right treatment, at the right dose, at the right time. Patients often show considerable heterogeneity in response to treatments. This heterogeneity suggests a transition from the traditional “one-size-fits-all” approach toward modern precision medicine.
doi:10.1201/9781003519348-13.venue: Empirical Processes and Statistical Reinforcement Learning

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1968133.title: Pre-service physics teachers as designers of AI-based pedagogical infrastructure: supporting metacognitive learning in STEM classrooms
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1968133.abstract: <jats:p>This study explored how pre-service physics teachers design artificial intelligence (AI)-based pedagogical infrastructure to support metacognitive learning in STEM classrooms. A qualitative interpretive design was employed with 30 pre-service physics teachers enrolled in a physics teacher education program at a university in Kazakhstan. Following two preparatory workshops, participants developed, tested, and refined AI-supported STEM lesson scenarios over 12 weeks. Testing involved peer-based micro-teaching with fellow pre-service teachers acting in simulated student roles; no school students participated. Data comprised individual semi-structured interviews, lesson plans, AI interaction scenarios, prompt sequences, and reflective notes and were examined using reflexive thematic analysis. Six interrelated themes were identified: designing AI-supported STEM lessons; supporting metacognitive regulation and formative assessment; aligning AI use with the physics curriculum and STEM objectives; preserving student agency and ensuring responsible AI use; developing teacher design agency; and addressing conditions for sustainable implementation. Participants' designs generally shifted from using AI to generate ready-made materials toward integrating it more purposefully into structured learning sequences. Pedagogically meaningful scenarios required learners to formulate an initial prediction or solution before consulting AI, verify AI-generated responses using physical laws, calculations, experiments, and reliable sources, and reflect on and revise their reasoning. Reported challenges included inaccurate AI responses, preparation time, unequal access to digital resources, technical difficulties, and variations in the quality of Kazakh- and Russian-language outputs. The findings highlight the importance of preparing pre-service physics teachers for subject-specific, ethically responsible, and pedagogically grounded AI integration. They illustrate design practices intended to scaffold planning, monitoring, scientific verification, evaluation, and reflection. However, the findings concern participants' pedagogical designs and professional perceptions and do not establish improvements in school students' metacognitive regulation or learning outcomes.</jats:p>

doi:10.26599/lles.2026.9660020.title: Prediction on tensile mechanical properties of engineered cementitious composites using a fully automated deep learning method
doi:10.26599/lles.2026.9660020.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Accurately predicting tensile mechanical properties of Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC), including tensile strength (TS) and ultimate tensile strain (UTS), remains challenging, particularly for the ultimate tensile strain, which exhibits high data dispersion that hinders reliable predictions. While machine learning (ML) has shown significant promise in predicting the mechanical properties of ECC, it faces several challenges: (1) limited predictive accuracy; (2) complexity and time-consuming nature of hyperparameter tuning; (3) insufficient research into predicting the UTS of ECC. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a fully automated deep learning model enhanced by Bayesian optimization for predicting the tensile mechanical properties of polyethylene fiber-reinforced engineered cementitious composites (PE-ECC). First, convolutional neural network (CNN) model was employed to enhance feature extraction and predictive accuracy. Second, Bayesian optimization was utilized to automatically construct the network and optimize various hyperparameters, resulting in an optimized network. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed Bayesian-optimized convolutional neural network (BO-CNN) method in predicting PE-ECC's TS and UTS, utilizing a dataset of 154 experimental samples from published literature, achieving coefficients of determination () of 0.911 and 0.775, respectively. The BO-CNN method not only outperforms CNNs and artificial neural networks (ANNs) optimized through grid search but also surpasses other eleven traditional ML models. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was employed to interpret input features' contributions in the prediction of tensile mechanical properties. Overall, the proposed method provides an efficient and reliable solution for predicting the tensile mechanical properties of ECC.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1201/9781003519348-5.title: Statistical Inference in Reinforcement Learning: A Selective Survey
doi:10.1201/9781003519348-5.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is concerned with how intelligence agents take actions in a given environment to maximize the cumulative reward they receive. In healthcare, applying RL algorithms could assist patients in improving their health status. In ride-sharing platforms, applying RL algorithms could increase drivers' income and customer satisfaction. For large language models, applying RL algorithms could align their outputs with human preferences. Over the past decade, RL has been arguably one of the most vibrant research frontiers in machine learning. Nevertheless, statistics as a field, as opposed to computer science, has only recently begun to engage with RL both in depth and in breadth. This chapter presents a selective review of statistical inferential tools for RL, covering both hypothesis testing and confidence interval construction. Our goal is to highlight the value of statistical inference in RL for both the statistics and machine learning communities, and to promote the broader application of classical statistical inference tools in this vibrant area of research.
doi:10.1201/9781003519348-5.venue: Empirical Processes and Statistical Reinforcement Learning

doi:10.1088/1361-6501/aeadc2.title: Generalizable domain-invariant feature learning method for rail insulation fault localization under unseen load conditions in DC metro systems
doi:10.1088/1361-6501/aeadc2.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The running rails typically carry traction current back to the substation in DC metro systems (DC MS). However, with the extension of service years, the operating environment of DC metro lines deteriorates, degradation of running rail insulation is prone to occur. Direct grounding of the running rails under severe conditions can cause abnormal increases in rail potential (RP) and stray current, thereby posing significant safety risks. Therefore, this paper proposes a generalizable domain-invariant feature learning method for rail insulation fault localization under unseen load conditions in DC MS, aiming to enable accurate insulation fault localization under unseen load conditions. For each source domain, a domain feature extractor is utilized to characterize its domain-related information. The input signals are subsequently processed by an encoder–decoder network, which maps them into a feature representation while suppressing domain specific components. Domain-invariant classifier is then constructed to integrate generalizable knowledge from the source domains and support fault localization in unseen load conditions. Experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively localizes insulation faults in unlabeled RP data across different load conditions.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11344548/v1.title: An Ultra-Compact, BRAM-Free Streaming 2D Convolution Accelerator on Low-Power FPGAs
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11344548/v1.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) spatial convolution represents the primary computational workload in edge computer vision and deep learning inference. However, conventional implementations on resource-constrained embedded platforms suffer from severe memory bandwidth bottlenecks and latency penalties when buffering full video frames in external memory or on-chip Block RAM (BRAM). In this paper, we present an ultra-compact, streaming 3 × 3 2D convolution hardware accelerator tailored for single-channel image streams on low-power Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). The proposed architecture ingests continuous raster-scan pixel streams at one pixel per clock cycle and reconstructs 3 × 3 spatial neighbourhoods on the fly using dual line buffers entirely mapped onto Look-Up Table (LUT)-based shift-register primitives (SRLC32E), eliminating Block RAM utilization entirely. The spatial neighbourhood is processed by a three-stage pipelined Multiply Accumulate (MAC) datapath featuring nine parallel DSP48E1 multipliers, a balanced adder tree, and a mathematically derived 20-bit internal accumulator that guarantees exact, overflow-free accumulation across all valid input and weight combinations. An output narrowing stage incorporates monotonic 16-bit saturation clamping and optional Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation to prevent signed overflow wrap-around artifacts. Control flow is orchestrated by a three-state Moore finite state machine (FSM) providing input stream gating and output-sample-based drain accounting, ensuring complete pipeline flushes without stall overhead. The architecture was synthesized and implemented for a Xilinx Zynq-7020 SoC (xc7z020clg400-1) under a 10ns (100MHz) clock constraint. Post-synthesis reports confirm zero Block RAM usage, 231 Slice LUTs (0.43%), 417 flip-flops (0.39%), and 9 DSP48E1 slices (4.09%), achieving a worst negative slack of +3.724ns (estimated fmax ≈ 159.3MHz) and an active compute power of only 9mW (0.159W total on-chip). The pipeline achieves an initial latency of 2W + 7 cycles (71 cycles for 32 × 32 frames) and sustains a peak throughput of one output pixel per cycle (100Mpixel/s, 900MMAC/s). Exhaustive multi-tier verification confirms zero mismatches, including a 900/900 bit-exact match against an independent 32-bit software golden model on natural photography and an exact 1860-window geometric match on non-square images.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11344548/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.58230/edutech.v4i1.136.title: StarQuest Qur'an: A Reward-Based Interactive Media for Teaching Surah Al-Humazah to Grade II MI Students
doi:10.58230/edutech.v4i1.136.abstract: <jats:p>Qur'an learning for Grade II Madrasah Ibtidaiyah students needs to be adjusted to the thinking of children aged seven to eight years, who prefer real things, attractive visuals, and pleasantly packaged presentations. This research uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the ASSURE model, including needs analysis, goal setting, material selection, media utilization, student involvement, and evaluation, to produce StarQuest Qur'an interactive learning media on Surah Al-Humazah. Development starts with analyzing student characteristics, preparing materials, and designing a child-friendly display. Two experts' feasibility assessment showed that material experts rated it 93.75% and media experts 94.79%, both in the very feasible category. This research is limited to product feasibility assessment and does not test its direct impact on students. This media is expected to be an interesting learning alternative that supports students in understanding the meaning and moral message of Surah Al-Humazah, and further research is suggested to test its direct impact on students.</jats:p>

doi:10.5256/f1000research.202559.r529412.title: Peer Review Report For: Designing Virtual Reality Game-Based Learning for Computational Thinking Competency Development: Evidence from Vocational Education [version 1; peer review: 1 approved with reservations]
doi:10.5256/f1000research.202559.r529412.abstract: * Computational thinking has become an essential skill in vocational education; however, many instructional approaches struggle to deliver authentic, engaging, and practice-oriented learning experiences. Virtual reality (VR) game-based learning presents a promising solution to address these challenges by blending immersive environments with problem-solving activities that support the development of competencies. This study explores the design and effectiveness of a VR game-based learning environment to enhance computational thinking skills in vocational education. A quasi-experimental research design was implemented, involving vocational high school students who participated in a VR-based game learning intervention integrated into their regular instructional framework. To assess computational thinking competencies, pre- and post-tests were conducted, aligned with the core components of computational thinking, and supplemented by performance-based learning tasks. The findings reveal that students experienced significant improvements in their computational thinking skills following the intervention, indicating that the VR game-based learning environment effectively supported competency development. Furthermore, the results emphasize the importance of incorporating authentic vocational scenarios and game mechanics to foster active engagement and practical problem-solving. This study contributes valuable empirical evidence to the growing body of research on game-based learning, demonstrating how thoughtfully designed virtual reality learning environments can enhance the development of computational thinking competencies in vocational education contexts.

doi:10.1108/dlo-07-2026-0428.title: Reconceptualizing green innovation as an organizational capability: an integrated approach
doi:10.1108/dlo-07-2026-0428.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper reconceptualizes green innovation as an integrative organizational capability rather than a standalone environmental or technological initiative. It examines how organizational, institutional and technological conditions shape its contribution to sustainable organizational performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper adopts a narrative literature review, drawing on the natural resource-based view (NRBV) to synthesize research on organizational capabilities, organizational learning, stakeholder relationships, institutional conditions and digital technologies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The review shows that green innovation contributes to sustainable performance when supported by complementary capabilities, organizational learning, stakeholder collaboration, favorable institutional conditions and digital technologies. It further suggests that technologies alone are insufficient; outcomes depend on aligning organizational capabilities with contextual conditions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As a conceptual review, the proposed framework requires empirical validation across different organizational and institutional contexts.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Managers should embed green innovation within organizational strategy, strengthen learning, strengthen stakeholder collaboration, leverage digital technologies and adopt context-specific sustainability strategies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper advances an integrative capability-based perspective by positioning green innovation capability as the mechanism through which organizational resources, learning, stakeholder relationships, institutional conditions and digital technologies are combined to generate sustainable performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.2118/233864-ms.title: Comparative Evaluation of Physics-Based and Machine-Learning Models for CO2–Brine Relative Permeability Prediction
doi:10.2118/233864-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Relative permeability (kr) is one of the governing parameters of multiphase flow in porous media and directly influences predictions of CO2 plume migration, trapping efficiency, and injectivity in Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) projects. However, measuring CO2–brine relative permeability under reservoir conditions is experimentally challenging and time-intensive. Consequently, several predictive approaches have been proposed. This study evaluates the accuracy of empirical, capillary-pressure-based, and machine-learning models by benchmarking them against experimentally measured CO2–brine relative permeability data obtained under representative reservoir conditions.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Primary-drainage CO2–brine relative permeability was measured using unsteady-state coreflooding on a Nugget Sandstone core at 150°F and 1,500 psi. Relative permeability values were normalized using permeability to water at full water saturation (kw at Sw = 1 ~ absolute permeability, k). The experimental dataset captures primary-drainage behavior over gas saturations from 0 to approximately 0.66. Mercury Injection Capillary Pressure (MICP) measurements on the same core were used to characterize pore-throat-size distribution. Because MICP is performed in a mercury–air system, the capillary-pressure curve was converted to equivalent CO2–brine conditions using experimentally measured CO2–brine interfacial tension at the same pressure and temperature. The contact angle was estimated using Neumann's equation of state, allowing the MICP data to be scaled to the CO2–brine system before applying capillary-pressure-based models. Seven prediction methods were evaluated individually: Corey and Lomeland, Ebeltoft, and Thomas (LET) correlations, Brooks–Corey and Van Genuchten capillary-pressure models, Purcell and Burdine models derived from capillary-pressure data, and a machine-learning model based on gradient boosting trained on published CO2–brine datasets. Curves from all seven methods were evaluated at 13 experimental saturation points; principal error statistics use the 11 points with both phases measured, with the two terminal-stage points assessed separately as endpoint evidence. Hybrid formulations using different models for the gas and water phases were also tested. In total, 49 combinations (seven gas-phase × seven water-phase models) were evaluated using performance metrics: root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and coefficient of determination (R2).</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Results show clear differences in predictive performance, and separate calibrated fits from independent predictions: Corey and LET were fit by least squares to 11 of the 13 measured points and evaluated on that same set. Brooks–Corey/Burdine, Van Genuchten/Burdine, Purcell, direct Burdine, and the machine-learning model were not calibrated to this core's measured krg/krw data. Among the independent predictions, Brooks–Corey/Burdine gave the most accurate water-phase result (RMSE = 0.0087, R2 = 0.999), but all four capillary-pressure-derived methods systematically overpredicted gas relative permeability. Corey and LET fit the calibration data closely (LET: krg R2 = 0.995, krw R2 &gt; 0.999), but comparison with the two terminal krg responses—excluded from response fitting—shows that LET fails to extrapolate beyond its calibration range, while Corey extrapolates only partially. The machine-learning model reproduced the water-phase curve reasonably well (R2 = 0.97) but overpredicted gas mobility at intermediate saturations. Purcell showed the largest deviations of any model, reflecting its sensitivity to entry pressure and the absence of a tortuosity correction. Among all 49 gas/water pairings, LET applied to both phases gave the lowest combined error, though this reflects its calibration advantage rather than independent hybrid performance; the best true two-model hybrid was LET (gas) with Corey (water), and the best pairing among only the independently predicted methods was Brooks–Corey/Burdine applied to both phases.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This study provides a systematic comparison of empirical, capillary-pressure-derived, machine-learning, and phase-paired CO2–brine relative-permeability methods that explicitly distinguishes calibrated fits from independent predictions and evaluates terminal krg responses separately from response fitting. As expected, the calibrated correlations achieved lower in-sample error than the independent predictions; however, this does not establish superior predictive accuracy. The terminal-response comparison further shows that close calibration does not guarantee reliable extrapolation beyond the fitted range. These findings provide practical guidance for selecting and validating relative-permeability models for CO2 storage and CCUS reservoir simulations.</jats:p>

doi:10.32782/3041-2021/2026-3-23.title: ВИКОРИСТАННЯ ЦИФРОВИХ ЗАСОБІВ ДЛЯ ФОРМУВАННЯ ЕМОЦІЙНОГО ІНТЕЛЕКТУ ПІД ЧАС НАВЧАННЯ ІНОЗЕМНОЇ МОВИ
doi:10.32782/3041-2021/2026-3-23.abstract: <jats:p>У процесі дослідження проаналізовано дефініції емоційного інтелекту та встановлено, що в сучасному науковому дискурсі він розглядається як інтегративна характеристика особистості, яка поєднує здатність до усвідомлення, розуміння, регулювання власних емоцій і емоцій інших людей, забезпечуючи ефективну професійну комунікацію, соціальну взаємодію та психологічну адаптацію. Зазначено, що в умовах цифрової трансформації освіти і модернізації системи професійної підготовки особливої актуальності набуває проблема використання цифрових освітніх засобів для цілеспрямованого розвитку емоційного інтелекту під час навчання іноземної мови. У процесі дослідження ми намагалися максимально повноцінно використати потенціал комплексного, компетентнісного й системного наукових підходів. Їх поєднання дало можливість здійснити всебічний аналіз психолого-педагогічної літератури, сучасних міжнародних і вітчизняних досліджень, присвячених розвитку емоційного інтелекту, цифровізації освіти та іншомовної підготовки здобувачів вищої освіти. Особливу увагу приділено характеристиці сучасних цифрових інструментів, зокрема мультимедійних презентацій, платформ LearningApps, Wizer.me, сервісів спільної взаємодії та інших інтерактивних ресурсів, які забезпечують персоналізацію навчання, розвиток комунікативної активності, позитивної академічної мотивації, емоційної саморегуляції, емпатії та міжкультурної взаємодії. Запропоновано практичні рекомендації щодо цілеспрямованої інтеграції цифрових засобів у процес іншомовної підготовки, спрямовані на створення емоційно безпечного цифрового освітнього середовища та комплексний розвиток соціально-емоційних компетентностей здобувачів вищої освіти. Результати проведеного дослідження дають можливість дійти висновку, що використання цифрових освітніх технологій під час навчання іноземної мови є ефективним педагогічним інструментом розвитку емоційного інтелекту, оскільки забезпечує формування навичок емоційної усвідомленості, саморефлексії, співробітництва та міжкультурної взаємодії.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1780678.title: Predicting the risk of chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in clinical practice: an interpretable machine learning approach based on routine laboratory data
doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1780678.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression (CIM) is the most common adverse reaction of tumor chemotherapy and may lead to treatment delay, dose reduction, life-threatening infection, and poor prognosis. Current predictive methods remain suboptimal, with insufficient interpretability and limited clinical application. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model for early CIM risk prediction using routine laboratory data.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 1,000 cancer patients from Northeast Yunnan Central Hospital between January 2024 and January 2025 were enrolled and divided into a case group (n=500, with myelosuppression) and a control group (n=500, without myelosuppression).All observed samples were randomly split into a training set (70%) and a validation set (30%). The Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) was used to select optimal variables for model construction. The predictive performance of 15 different ML models was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), F1-score, Youden’s index, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), decision curve analysis (DCA), and residual boxplots. The best-performing model was selected for SHAP-based interpretability analysis and internally validated using a confusion matrix, clinical impact curve, and calibration curve.Additionally, 488 patients treated at Northeast Yunnan Provincial Central Hospital between June 2025 and November 2025 were selected as an independent external validation cohort for external validation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      After screening, 15 clinical indicators were used for ML model development. All models demonstrated excellent discrimination. The LightGBM model showed the best overall performance (AUC: 0.999 [0.998–1.000]; sensitivity: 0.986; specificity: 0.989; accuracy: 0.987; PPV: 0.989; NPV: 0.986; F1-score: 0.987; Youden’s index: 0.974). According to the LightGBM model, CIM risk increased when the following feature thresholds were met: white blood cell count &lt;5×10
                      <jats:sup>9</jats:sup>
                      /L, mean hemoglobin concentration &lt;325 g/L, monocyte percentage (MONO%) &gt;10%, red blood cell count &lt;4×10
                      <jats:sup>12</jats:sup>
                      /L, mean platelet volume &lt;8 fL, and plateletcrit &lt;0.1%.In the independent external validation (n=488), the LightGBM model remained stable and reliable, with an AUC of 0.940 (95% CI: 0.920–0.959), sensitivity of 0.818, specificity of 0.888, accuracy of 85.2%, and favorable calibration and clinical net benefit.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The LightGBM prediction model developed in this study can enable early identification of high-risk patients, providing a reference for healthcare providers to implement early interventions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3390/s26206492.title: A High-Resolution Remote Sensing Image Building Extraction Model Based on Spectral Index Gated Attention and Transfer Learning
doi:10.3390/s26206492.abstract: <jats:p>High-resolution remote sensing building extraction often requires large amounts of manually labeled data, and models trained on one dataset may not perform equally well on another without additional annotations. To reduce this dependency on labeled target data, we propose SIGA-UNet3+, which combines a Spectral Index Gated Attention (SIGA) module with a transfer learning strategy. The SIGA module fuses DSBI, NDVI, and NDWI to emphasize building features and suppress vegetation/water interference. Pre-training on the public SpaceNet dataset followed by fine-tuning on a self-built GF-2 dataset (Changchun, China) allows the model to adapt with limited local labels. On SpaceNet, SIGA-UNet3+ achieves F1 = 83.21% and IoU = 70.19%, obtaining the best overall segmentation performance among the compared methods. On the GF-2 dataset, it attains F1 = 84.56% and IoU = 72.17%. Moreover, using only 10% of the GF-2 training samples, transfer learning improves the F1 score by 6–8 percentage points compared to training from scratch. These results indicate that SIGA-UNet3+ can provide a promising and data-efficient approach for high-resolution remote sensing building extraction.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1903005.title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based prediction model for emergence agitation in geriatric patients undergoing orthopedic surgery: a prospective cohort study
doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1903005.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to identify factors associated with emergence agitation in geriatric patients undergoing orthopedic surgery and to develop a machine learning model for predicting the risk of emergence agitation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      This prospective cohort study included 612 geriatric patients who underwent elective orthopedic surgery at the First Affiliated Hospital of Jinzhou Medical University in Liaoning Province between April 2025 and April 2026. The patients were randomly divided into a training set (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 430) and a test set (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 182) at a 7:3 ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression and multivariable logistic regression analysis were used to identify predictors. Six machine learning algorithms were employed to develop prediction models. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The optimal model was interpreted using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The incidence of emergence agitation among geriatric patients who underwent orthopedic surgery was 27.61%. Preoperative anxiety, preoperative cognitive function, dexmedetomidine use, intraoperative hypothermia, intraoperative blood loss, and postoperative NRS pain score were identified as key predictors. The random forest (RF) model demonstrated the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.905, accuracy of 0.819, sensitivity of 0.820, specificity of 0.818, F1 score of 0.713, and Brier score of 0.111 on the test set. DCA showed that the model had the highest clinical net benefit. SHAP analysis revealed that intraoperative blood loss was the most significant predictor, followed by postoperative NRS pain score and preoperative cognitive function.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We developed and internally validated six machine learning models to predict the risk of emergence agitation in geriatric patients undergoing orthopedic surgery. The RF model achieved the best performance. Following successful external validation in multicenter cohorts, the model may assist clinicians in identifying patients at increased risk of emergence agitation during early PACU recovery and in prioritizing intensified monitoring and timely supportive management.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/frhs.2026.1927175.title: A machine learning framework for predicting healthcare insurance claim denials
doi:10.3389/frhs.2026.1927175.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The denial of healthcare insurance claims imposes a significant burden on providers, leading to decreased revenue and inefficient operations. This research presents a predictive model to assist providers in managing claim submissions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The framework uses a rule-based claim scrubber that authenticates submissions before sending them, matching them against known denial patterns. It also employs a two-stage supervised pipeline. The study analyses 678,881 professional claim service lines submitted to a single U.S. payer between 2017 and 2024, of which 31.9% were denied. Stage 1 classifies a submitted line as accepted or denied using a Random Forest over 26 features</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>On a temporally ordered, claim-grouped held-out partition of 139,615 lines that retains the natural denial prevalence, it attains a precisionrecall AUC of 0.777 (95% CI 0.770-0.784) against a no-skill baseline of 0.330, ROC-AUC 0.865, accuracy 0.794, balanced accuracy 0.784, recall 0.756 and Matthews correlation 0.552. Stage 2 assigns a reason code over a 67-class label space covering 98.8% of denials, reaching 0.269 Top-1 and 0.498 Top-3 accuracy; the same model reaches 0.918 Top-3 when candidates are restricted to the five most frequent codes, and we report both because reason-code accuracy depends heavily on the label space. Because Stage 2 scores only lines Stage 1 has flagged, end-to-end performance is the product of the two stages: the correct code appears among the first three candidates for 38.8% of all denied lines. Class imbalance was addressed with the Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique applied within training folds only; an ablation shows no measurable benefit at this prevalence (difference in average precision −0.0002, 95% CI −0.0009 to +0.0006) and worse calibration, which we report rather than omit. Tuned XGBoost and LightGBM baselines on the identical partition are statistically indistinguishable from the Random Forest.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The solution provides providers with a claim validation and denial-forecasting tool that reduces the denial rate and simplifies the revenue cycle.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1932507.title: Prediction of residual stones after ESWL for ureteral calculi using deep learning-radiomics-based stone heterogeneity and body composition: an interaction analysis
doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1932507.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To investigate the association between deep learning-radiomics-based stone heterogeneity, body composition, and residual stones after extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) for ureteral calculi.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This retrospective study included 200 patients with ureteral stones who underwent ESWL between January 2024 and December 2025, comprising the development cohort. An additional 57 patients treated between January 2026 and June 2026 were included as the temporal testing cohort. Baseline clinical data and imaging data were collected. Deep learning (DL) and radiomics features of ureteral stones were extracted, and feature selection was performed to construct a DL-radiomics model (Radscore). TotalSegmentator was used to quantify visceral fat, skeletal muscle, and subcutaneous fat volumes within the T12-S4 region. The predictive performance of the clinical-body composition model, DL-radiomics model, and nomogram model was compared. Subgroup analyses were conducted to evaluate the stability of the nomogram model. The interaction between the Radscore and body composition in relation to residual stones was further explored using the optimal cutoff values derived from the training set.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The development cohort was randomly divided into a training set and a validation set in a 7:3 ratio. Visceral fat and skeletal muscle volumes were included in the clinical-body composition model, yielding AUCs of 0.792 (0.706, 0.878), 0.821 (0.577, 1.000) and 0.827 (0.710, 0.943), respectively. The DL radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.778 (0.679−0.876), 0.704 (0.363−1.000) and 0.742 (0.547−0.937). The nomogram model showed AUCs of 0.893 (0.835, 0.952), 0.824 (0.630, 1.000) and 0.898 (0.807, 0.989). Subgroup analyses of stone location, side of the stone, and perinephritis revealed no significant interaction in the nomogram model (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       &gt; 0.05). Calibration and decision curve analyses demonstrated good agreement and clinical utility of the nomogram model. In the interaction analysis between Radscore and body composition, visceral fat volume significantly attenuated the risk of residual stones associated with a high stone Radscore.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Deep learning-radiomics-based stone heterogeneity demonstrates good predictive performance for residual stones after ESWL. Moreover, lower visceral fat volume significantly attenuates the impact of stone heterogeneity on residual stone formation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1108/ejtd-01-2026-0009.title: Manufacturing leaders’ perspectives on green employability skill development through multi-level organizational learning
doi:10.1108/ejtd-01-2026-0009.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine how manufacturing industry leaders understand the development of green employability skills through multi-level organizational learning (OL) processes and the role this development plays in building organizational sustainability competencies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An interpretive qualitative design was used using reflexive thematic analysis. Sixteen manufacturing leaders representing diverse organizational sizes, functional areas and geographic regions across the United States were recruited through purposive and snowball sampling in collaboration with a state-level manufacturing trade association.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Three themes emerged: Learning Agility for Green Role Evolution, in which individual employees develop adaptive capacity for continuous skill renewal as green roles evolve; Green Employability Co-Design with Educational Ecosystems, in which organizations and educational institutions collaboratively develop sustainability-aligned curricula and credentials; and Green Learning Culture as a Catalyst for Organizational Change, in which embedded sustainability values and Human Resource Development (HRD) infrastructure drive enterprise-wide transformation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Manufacturing leaders and HRD practitioners would benefit from designing learning interventions that operate across individual, team and organizational levels, integrating sustainability competencies into talent management systems, educational partnerships and leadership development rather than treating green skill development as a standalone training initiative.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study presents a three-level OL framework comprising adaptive, generative and transformational green learning that advances green HRD theory by systematically integrating individual employability development, team-based knowledge creation and organizational cultural transformation, providing a theoretically grounded architecture for manufacturing sustainability workforce development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1201/9781003519348-7.title: Efficiently Learning Synthetic Control Models for High-Dimensional Disaggregated Data
doi:10.1201/9781003519348-7.abstract: The Synthetic Control method (SC) has become a valuable tool for estimating causal effects. Originally designed for single-treated unit scenarios, it has recently found applications in high-dimensional disaggregated settings with multiple treated units. However, challenges in practical implementation and computational efficiency arise in such scenarios. To tackle these challenges, we propose a novel approach that integrates the Multivariate Square-root Lasso method into the synthetic control framework. We rigorously establish the estimation error bounds for fitting the Synthetic Control weights using Multivariate Square-root Lasso, accommodating high-dimensionality and time series dependencies. Additionally, we quantify the estimation error for the Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT). Through simulation studies, we demonstrate that our method offers superior computational efficiency without compromising estimation accuracy. We apply our method to assess the causal impact of COVID-19 Stay-at-Home Orders on the monthly unemployment rate in the United States at the county level.

doi:10.3389/fcell.2026.1967483.title: Machine-learning-assisted integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics characterizes glioblastoma ecosystem states and immune-associated programs
doi:10.3389/fcell.2026.1967483.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by marked malignant-cell plasticity and a complex tumor ecosystem composed of heterogeneous malignant and microenvironmental cell populations. We integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to characterize reproducible GBM cell and ecosystem-associated states, evaluate cross-platform concordance, and examine immune-associated transcriptional programs while distinguishing descriptive associations from mechanistic inference.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The deposited Smart-seq2 (7,930 cells) and 10x (16,201 cells) expression matrices from GSE131928/SCP393 were analyzed on their verified expression scales. Official annotations and malignant-state modules were audited, four broad malignant states were recomputed, and a tumor-held-out machine-learning label-transfer framework was applied to the 10x dataset. Public TCGA-GBM RNA-seq data were used to evaluate state- and microenvironment-associated transcriptional programs and to perform nested prediction benchmarking. Selected ecosystem-associated genes were additionally examined by RT-qPCR in glioma cell lines and normal human astrocytes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among Smart-seq2 cells, 6,576 malignant cells had valid state scores, whereas 287 alias-affected records were excluded from state-score denominators. The machine-learning label-transfer model achieved an out-of-fold accuracy of 0.998, and malignant-state fractions showed moderate-to-strong concordance across six shared tumor labels. At the tumor-label level, MES-like fraction was not significantly associated with macrophage fraction (Spearman rho = 0.171, P = 0.395), indicating that ecosystem-level transcriptional association should not be interpreted as a simple directional immune-to-state mechanism. In TCGA-GBM, MES and myeloid-associated programs correlated with immune and stromal expression signatures, whereas survival and 12-month prediction performance remained modest and specification-sensitive. RT-qPCR further demonstrated increased STAT3, CHI3L1, SPP1, and VEGFA expression in glioma cell lines relative to normal human astrocytes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis supports reproducible characterization of malignant-cell heterogeneity and immune-associated ecosystem features in IDH-wildtype GBM. Machine-learning-assisted cross-platform analysis provides a reproducible framework for evaluating tumor ecosystem-associated states, while the observed immune-mesenchymal associations remain descriptive rather than causal. Experimental RT-qPCR provides expression-level support for selected ecosystem-associated genes and highlights testable hypotheses for future functional and spatial studies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/fmats.2026.1967190.title: Deep learning for biodegradable metallic biomaterials: from degradation modeling to performance prediction with a practical case study
doi:10.3389/fmats.2026.1967190.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Biodegradable metallic implants are transitioning from laboratory concept to clinical deployment, yet predicting their corrosion rate and residual strength in the physiological environment remains a substantial scientific challenge. The interplay of electrochemical, mechanical, and biological factors creates a high-dimensional problem that conventional modelling cannot easily capture, while experimental datasets are often too sparse and fragmented for traditional statistical approaches. Deep learning architectures, including graph, recurrent, and transformer networks, combined with physics-informed loss functions, now offer accurate forecasts of degradation rates, yield strength, and biological responses. Interpretation tools such as SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) and attention mapping further reveal which alloying elements and processing parameters dominate performance, tightening the prediction-experiment loop. This work also demonstrates MAGIC (Multi-task Alloy Gated-network with Integrated Constraints), a multi-task learner that fuses composition and processing modalities through learned uncertainty weighting. On a magnesium alloy dataset of 600 records it delivers cross-validated
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" id="m1">
                        <mml:mrow>
                          <mml:msup>
                            <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mi>R</mml:mi>
                            </mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mrow>
                              <mml:mn>2</mml:mn>
                            </mml:mrow>
                          </mml:msup>
                        </mml:mrow>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    values of 0.864 for ultimate tensile strength and 0.907 for yield strength, with root-mean-square errors of 28.0 and 26.8 MPa for ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and yield strength (YS), outperforming seven standard baselines and providing a reproducible template. The boundary of this contribution is explicitly emphasised: MAGIC predicts the pristine (as-processed) ultimate tensilestrength and yield strength of undegraded material; it does not predict corrosion rates or post-implantation residual strength, and the coupling between corrosion damage and mechanical degradation is identified as a key open direction rather than a solved capability. Substantial barriers persist, notably the gap between
                    <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic>
                    environments, scarce openly shared data, and the rigorous demands of clinical validation. Nevertheless, deep learning is progressively integrating into biodegradable metal research, and the central question is evolving from feasibility to whether the community can establish the required data infrastructure and interdisciplinary trust.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fnbot.2026.1920739.title: Embodied multimodal human-computer interaction for English language learning: integrating speech, gestures, emotion, and adaptive feedback
doi:10.3389/fnbot.2026.1920739.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Current English language learning systems are often limited by single-dimensional learning-state perception, insufficient modeling of affective-cognitive characteristics, and delayed or inflexible feedback regulation. To address these limitations, this study proposes an affective-cognitive gated cross-modal transformer (ACG-CMT) for embodied multimodal human-computer interaction in English language learning. The framework integrates learners’ speech, gestures, and affective responses as multimodal inputs. The speech encoder learns low-level acoustic-prosodic representations from Mel-spectral, energy, pitch/prosodic, and temporal patterns rather than receiving rubric-derived target scores; a spatiotemporal motion encoder captures gesture and posture dynamics; and an affective encoder models facial-action and vocal-affect cues. A cross-modal transformer captures temporal dependencies and contextual interactions among linguistic output, embodied behavior, and affective fluctuations. During fusion, an affective-cognitive gate adjusts modality-specific contributions using latent affective/cognitive context and pre-decision task context available at inference time, without access to ground-truth target labels. A multi-task decision module then supports learning-state recognition, affective-cognitive load estimation, and feedback-policy matching. ACG-CMT achieves an accuracy of 0.892, a macro-F1 of 0.884, an AUC of 0.941, and a difficult-state F1 of 0.877 for learning-state recognition; R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                     = 0.836, RMSE = 0.084, and MAE = 0.068 for the operational affective-cognitive load reference index; and a feedback-policy matching rate of 0.861 with an average latency of 438 ms. These results indicate that the framework can integrate multimodal behavioral information for learner-state estimation and adaptive feedback, while the internal gating patterns are interpreted as model-level associations rather than causal psychological mechanisms.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fmech.2026.1967578.title: A model for timing anomaly detection and prediction of CNC machine tools based on multi-scale feature fusion and self-attention
doi:10.3389/fmech.2026.1967578.abstract: <jats:p>In order to solve the bottleneck problem of existing deep learning models being easily affected by feature interference and overfitting under strong noise, this paper proposes a Multi-scale Feature Fusion and Self-Attention based Time-Series Anomaly Detection and Prediction Network(MSFF-SATADPN). This paper first uses progressive dilated convolution to truncate local transient features in multiple frequency bands, and then dynamically maps global degradation dependencies through self attention mechanism. In addition, this paper applies orthogonal projection regularization of singular value decomposition to the hidden layer space, thereby decoupling steady-state principal components and anomalous disturbances at the physical representation level. Finally, independent blind testing across tools showed that within the range of structural mutations, compared to the Informer model exhibiting residual oscillations of −0.058–0.059 mm, the model predicted residual convergence to −0.015–0.018 mm. The global average absolute error of all test samples reached 0.062 mm, and the average absolute error distribution of each sample was 0.08 mm. The global average absolute error directly aggregated the absolute errors of all time steps, and each sample value averaged the absolute errors within each sample before sample aggregation. Both values were lower than the corresponding values of PatchTST in paired t-test (p &lt; 0.01). In the abnormal classification under natural noise cutting conditions, the overall F1 score converged to 0.938 (± 0.008). This study overcomes the confusion of multi frequency features through a clear orthogonal decoupling mechanism, providing a reliable sequence analysis method for practical industrial operation and maintenance decisions.</jats:p>

doi:10.1002/app.71639.title: Preparation of Low‐Carbon Rapidly Vulcanizable Nitrile Rubber via Synergistic Effect of Emulsifier and Accelerator Assisted by Wet Mixing
doi:10.1002/app.71639.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This study aims to reduce the environmental impact of traditional rubber vulcanization by proposing a greener process. Accelerators and emulsifiers were introduced into acrylonitrile‐butadiene rubber (NBR) using a wet mixing method after polymerization, thereby improving dispersion and efficiency. Two accelerator systems, RH‐EZ and RH‐ZTC, were constructed based on NBR LZ3305 and compared with the commercial fast‐curing NBR3445F. The results revealed distinct advantages for each system. The RH‐EZ system significantly enhanced the vulcanization rate (reducing t
                    <jats:sub>90</jats:sub>
                    ), with NBR/19RH‐EZ showing a 67% reduction over base LZ3305 and about 43% compared to NBR3445F. Conversely, the RH‐ZTC system excelled in processability and low‐temperature properties; NBR/13RH‐ZTC maintained 95% of its initial Mooney viscosity after 30 days, and NBR/17RH‐ZTC achieved a glass transition temperature of −25.4°C. Both systems exhibited excellent mechanical strength, crosslink density, and oil resistance. The Coran model confirmed that the RH‐EZ system effectively increased the E
                    <jats:sub>precursor</jats:sub>
                    and E
                    <jats:sub>crosslinking</jats:sub>
                    of the base LZ3305. This research provides a new pathway for preparing high‐performance, low‐carbon, and efficient vulcanized NBR and is expected to enable green and low‐carbon production of NBR.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.2118/234108-ms.title: Comparative Human Factors Analysis of Exxon Valdez (1989) and Ever Given (2021) Accidents with FRAM – Learning from Complex Decisions in Maritime High-Risk Operations
doi:10.2118/234108-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Maritime operations are complex sociotechnical systems in which environmental conditions, technological resources, organizational arrangements, and human performance interact continuously and non-linearly. This paper comparatively reanalyzes two emblematic maritime accidents separated by 32 years: the Exxon Valdez grounding and oil spill in Prince William Sound in 1989 and the Ever Given grounding and blockage of the Suez Canal in 2021. The Functional Resonance Analysis Method (FRAM), under a Human Factors approach, was applied to model the functional interactions and performance variability involved in both events, considering navigation, bridge coordination, pilotage, traffic management, environmental conditions, organizational arrangements, and shore-based support. The comparison shows that neither accident can be adequately explained by a single human error or isolated failure. In the Exxon Valdez, environmental variability associated with glacial ice and nighttime navigation interacted with organizational conditions involving staffing, workload, Vessel Traffic Service supervision, and structural protection, developing predominantly as a route-deviation and route-recovery problem. In the Ever Given, wind, sand, confined-water hydrodynamics, and vessel dimensions progressively reduced maneuvering margins, interacting with pilotage, Port Control, bridge coordination, tugboat availability, and stabilization support. Despite substantial technological advances between 1989 and 2021, the comparison demonstrates that fundamental organizational challenges related to ship–shore coordination, timely operational support, adequate resources, and adaptation to changing environmental demands remain relevant. The study demonstrates how FRAM can reveal these systemic interactions while shifting accident learning from individual blame toward strengthening the entire maritime sociotechnical system. Human adaptability should therefore be understood not primarily as a source of failure, but as an essential resource for resilience and safe performance in complex maritime operations.</jats:p>
doi:10.2118/234108-ms.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

doi:10.1021/acs.jpcc.6c04558.title: Molecular Structure Design of Heat-Resistant Cycloolefin Polymer Based on Machine Learning
doi:10.1021/acs.jpcc.6c04558.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Traditional biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) is widely used in capacitors of converter valves, but its high-temperature performance is gradually approaching its design limit. Cycloolefin copolymer/polymer (COC/COP) materials are explored as promising alternatives due to their high glass transition temperature, wide band gap, thermal stability, and low conduction loss. To overcome the lack of large-scale COC/COP polymer databases and the limitations of experimental validation, molecular dynamics, and conventional machine-learning screening, this work proposes a graph convolutional neural network (GCN)-based workflow for inverse design and property prediction of cycloolefin polymer monomers. An initial database of nearly 200,000 COC/COP candidates was constructed through library skeleton design and converted into molecular graph representations for model training, latent-space sampling, and molecular generation. Using a GCN-based forward prediction model, we screened for 12 potential heat-resistant polymers. Combined with subsequent calculations of molecular dynamics (MD) and retrosynthetic analysis, we ultimately identified P9 and P11 as the final candidate heat-resistant polymers. This work provides a case-study approach for the design and screening of high-temperature-resistant polymer dielectrics.</jats:p>

doi:10.4108/ew.14196.title: Multiscale Digital-Twin Modeling of Energy-Storage Materials by Integrating First-Principles Calculations and Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
doi:10.4108/ew.14196.abstract: <jats:p>Conventional modeling of energy-storage materials is constrained by the computational cost of first-principles calculations, limited electrochemical-state awareness in machine-learning interatomic potentials, and weak coupling between materials-scale models and online battery decision-making. This study proposes a first-principles-constrained electrochemically conditioned machine-learning interatomic potential (FP-EMLP) integrated with a multiscale digital-twin framework (FP-EMLP-DT). A multistate configuration space spanning ion concentration, temperature, defects, strain, and phase boundaries is combined with active learning based on committee uncertainty, structural novelty, and physics-based risk. The equivariant graph model incorporates electrochemical-state gating, charge-conserving projection, and differentiable long-range electrostatics, and is trained using energies, forces, stresses, equilibrium voltages, and migration barriers. Predicted diffusion coefficients, free energies, elastic tensors, and chemical expansion coefficients are transferred to an electrochemical-mechanical-thermal-damage model. The resulting model is further integrated with a physics-based reduced-order network, uncertainty-gated residual learning, online data assimilation, and degradation-aware control. FP-EMLP achieves mean absolute errors of 6.5 meV atom−1, 33 meV Å−1, 0.051 V, and 0.038 eV for energy, force, voltage, and migration barrier, respectively, with a 4.8% aggregate relative error across multiscale fields. Active learning reduces required first-principles labels by 33.3% while covering 91.2% of high-risk configurations. FP-EMLP-DT achieves mean absolute errors of 0.93% for state of charge and 1.21% for state of health. Degradation-aware control reduces maximum material stress and damage increment by 16.5% and 36.8%, respectively, demonstrating an effective multiscale pathway from electronic structure to online battery management.</jats:p>
doi:10.4108/ew.14196.venue: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Energy Web

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11063645/v1.title: Designing Digital Game Based Learning in Early Childhood Teacher Education Using the ADDIE Model
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11063645/v1.abstract: Teacher education programs increasingly need to prepare preservice teachers to make pedagogically sound decisions about digital technology rather than simply operate digital tools. This study examined an ADDIE-guided redesign of an Educational Technology for Early Childhood course for preservice early childhood teachers at Universitas Mataram, Indonesia. The development process included curriculum analysis, redesign of the Semester Learning Plan (RPS), expert review by 10 lecturers, implementation across 16 course meetings, and evaluation of seven student-developed digital game prototypes. Eight randomly selected students rated each prototype on originality, innovation, aesthetics, functionality, relevance, and perceived impact using a five-point scale. Expert feedback prompted revisions to learning-outcome alignment, assessment, technology ethics and safety, learning resources, and interactive learning activities. Six prototypes were rated in the study's good range and one in the adequate range. Product-level means ranged from 3.65 to 4.38, with an overall mean of 3.97/5. Functionality received the highest cross-product dimension mean (4.16), whereas aesthetics was the lowest (3.75). The findings show that a curriculum-embedded design project can provide observable evidence of preservice teachers' capacity to apply technological and pedagogical knowledge in authentic product development. Because the study did not include a pretest-posttest competence measure or comparison group, the findings indicate demonstrated design performance rather than causal improvement in competence.
