doi:10.2118/233827-ms.title: A Physics-Informed Machine Learning Framework for Real-Time Predictive Diagnostics and Conformance Control in Produced Water Management
doi:10.2118/233827-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The global hydrocarbon exploration and production (E&P) industry is severely impacted by increasing produced water management challenges, evidenced by average water-oil ratios (WOR) frequently approaching 9:1. This excessive aqueous phase volume significantly escalates operational expenditure (OPEX) through costly handling, separation, and treatment processes, simultaneously diminishing the net efficiency of hydrocarbon recovery. Current conventional water conformance control strategies exhibit an estimated success rate of approximately 40%, primarily due to the latency in intervention deployment and the diagnostic ambiguity in precisely characterizing the spatial origin and mechanism of water influx within the reservoir-wellbore system.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This study introduces a novel methodology predicated on integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms for advanced, real-time diagnostic analytics of produced fluid dynamics. The core ML models are trained on a globalized, multivariate production dataset comprising production profiles and sensor telemetry from over 25 distinct operational wells. The algorithms are specifically engineered to perform spatiotemporal pattern recognition within the WOR signature. This enables the system to differentiate diagnostically between near-wellbore conformance issues (e.g., inadequate cement bond, channeling) and deeper reservoir-scale heterogeneity effects (e.g., thief zones).</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The trained ML models yield high-fidelity predictive analytics, capable of forecasting future water production trends and accurately predicting the imminent onset of significant water breakthrough events. These proactive capability transitions produced water management from a reactive framework to a data-driven decision support system (DSS). The real-time integration of high-frequency sensor data enhances the system's responsiveness and adaptive capability. The resulting output guides operators toward the timely deployment of optimized, targeted chemical or mechanical water shutoff treatments, moving beyond reliance on conventional, time-averaged flow measurements.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The proposed AI-enabled workflow represents a significant innovation in reservoir management. By achieving early and precise identification of conformance breaches, the system empowers operators to implement remediation strategies that are both mechanistically specific and spatially optimized. This approach is crucial for: (1) maximizing hydrocarbon recovery efficiency, (2) substantially reducing OPEX by minimizing the volume of treated water, and (3) sustaining optimal reservoir sweep performance. Selected case studies will be presented to quantitatively demonstrate the potential efficacy of this methodology in delivering superior water conformance control and optimizing overall field economics.</jats:p>
doi:10.2118/233827-ms.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

doi:10.1201/9781003519348-6.title: Fair Sufficient Representation Learning
doi:10.1201/9781003519348-6.abstract: The main objective of fair statistical modeling and machine learning is to minimize or eliminate biases that may arise from the data or the model itself, ensuring that predictions and decisions are not unjustly influenced by sensitive attributes such as race, gender, age, or other protected characteristics. In this paper, we introduce a Fair Sufficient Representation Learning (FSRL) method that balances sufficiency and fairness. Sufficiency ensures that the representation should capture all necessary information about the target variables, while fairness requires that the learned representation remains independent of sensitive attributes. FSRL is based on a convex combination of an objective function for learning a sufficient representation and an objective function that ensures fairness. Our approach manages fairness and sufficiency at the representation level, offering a novel perspective on fair representation learning. We implement this method using distance covariance, which is effective for characterizing independence between random variables. We establish the convergence properties of the learned representations. Experiments conducted on healthcase and text datasets with diverse structures demonstrate that FSRL achieves a superior trade-off between fairness and accuracy compared to existing approaches.
doi:10.1201/9781003519348-6.venue: Empirical Processes and Statistical Reinforcement Learning

doi:10.1201/9781003519348-9.title: Efficient Learning Using U-Statistics with a Valid Instrumental Variable
doi:10.1201/9781003519348-9.abstract: U -statistics provide a principled way to compare potential outcomes across treatment groups, especially for rank-type estimands such as the probabilistic index and win ratio. However, most of the existing methods rely on the strong assumption of no unmeasured confounding. In this chapter, we extend the U -statistic estimation to settings with hidden confounders by leveraging instrumental variables. We consider three target populations, namely, overall, complier, and nudge, and present identification results under appropriate structural assumptions. Building upon the framework of debiased machine learning, we derive semiparametric efficient influence functions for these estimands and introduce a tailored cross-fitting strategy that facilitates theoretical analysis. The resulting estimators are asymptotically normal and achieve the semiparametric efficiency bound, thus enabling robust and efficient causal inference with observational data.
doi:10.1201/9781003519348-9.venue: Empirical Processes and Statistical Reinforcement Learning

doi:10.22158/eltls.v8n5p66.title: Aligning Tourism English Learning With Workplace Tasks Through College-Enterprise Partnerships
doi:10.22158/eltls.v8n5p66.abstract: <jats:p>College–enterprise partnerships offer access to work, but that access does not specify what students learn in English. This framework-development study combines project document analysis with descriptive secondary analysis of 896 student, 63 enterprise, and 57 vocational English teacher questionnaire records. An ESP-informed audit examines whether the instruments and teaching resources identify communication purposes, audiences, genres, opportunities for English use, learning support, and performance criteria. The documents specify occupational activities more clearly than language demands; the surveys provide contextual signals about participation and mentoring rather than measures of English needs or project effects. The proposed framework links each identified gap to a language task, a responsible mentor, a feasible participation arrangement, and evidence for assessment. Its contribution is a context-specific integration of ESP task design and work-integrated learning under seasonal, staffing, and supervision constraints. Policies issued in 2025–2026 guide prospective alignment rather than explain earlier data. The framework requires local needs analysis and pilot evaluation, given the uncertain survey provenance and lack of implementation evidence.</jats:p>
doi:10.22158/eltls.v8n5p66.venue: English Language Teaching and Linguistics Studies

doi:10.3389/fdgth.2026.1929794.title: A story for Pepper and Nao: applying the learning by teaching paradigm in children with patterns of neuromotor impairment
doi:10.3389/fdgth.2026.1929794.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Social robots are increasingly used in educational and clinical contexts to enhance engagement and learning, particularly in children with neurological and neurodevelopmental disorders. The Learning by Teaching paradigm, in which children actively teach social robots, promotes cognitive and metacognitive processes such as planning, self-efficacy, and executive functioning; however, controlled and systematic evidence supporting its effectiveness remains limited. Children with neuromotor disorders frequently present with closely intertwined motor and cognitive planning difficulties, which significantly impact learning and everyday functioning. In this context, social robot–mediated interventions based on the Learning by Teaching paradigm may represent a promising approach. The current multicenter randomized controlled trial (RCT) explores the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach to enhance cognitive and motor planning in children with neuromotor impairments, and to examine potential generalization effects on other cognitive domains and engagement.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The main aim of this RCT study is to evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of a social robot-mediated Learning by Teaching intervention in children aged 7–16 years with neuromotor impairments. Eighty participants will be randomly assigned to an Experimental Group (EG) receiving social robot training or to a Control Group (CG) continuing standard care. The intervention consists of 20–25 sessions in which children teach a humanoid social robot (Pepper or NAO) to order picture-based stories of increasing complexity. Assessments will be performed at baseline (T0), post-intervention or control period (T1), and follow-up/post-treatment (T2). Primary outcomes include planning abilities assessed through picture arrangement and an
                      <jats:italic>ad hoc</jats:italic>
                      motor planning task. Secondary outcomes encompass executive functions, visuo-spatial memory, attention, inhibition, narrative production, visual-perceptual skills, and reading comprehension. Engagement will be measured using a multimodal approach integrating behavioral, cognitive, emotional, and physiological indicators derived from video, audio, and wearable sensors.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study will examine improvements in planning and motor programming abilities and potential generalization effects on executive functions and reading comprehension. Additionally, the predictive and mediating role of engagement in intervention effectiveness will be reported.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This research protocol proposes an innovative, engagement-focused rehabilitation approach integrating cognitive, motor, and narrative processes through social robotics. Findings are expected to inform the development of evidence-based, personalized interventions for children with neuromotor disorders and to advance methodological approaches for assessing engagement in human–robot interaction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Clinical Trial Registration</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      <jats:ext-link>ClinicalTrials.gov</jats:ext-link>
                      , identifier NCT06797050.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/fpls.2026.1965848.title: AgroXAI: a multi-XAI deep learning system for explainable multi-species plant disease classification
doi:10.3389/fpls.2026.1965848.abstract: <jats:p>Automated plant disease classification can benefit from models that provide both predictive performance and interpretable evidence for their decisions. This study presents AgroXAI, a Multi-XAI deep learning framework for explainable multi-species plant disease classification under a controlled, leakage-aware evaluation protocol. A publicly available dataset containing 2,815 leaf images from seven plant species was organized into 14 joint species–health classes and partitioned into fixed group-disjoint training, validation, and held-out test sets containing 1,970, 422, and 423 images, respectively. Preprocessing and architecture selection were conducted using only the training and validation partitions, leading to the AgroX-Swin classifier based on Swin Transformer-Tiny with 384 × 384 Original RGB inputs. Explainability was quantitatively evaluated using Grad-CAM++, SHAP, LIME, and their complementary fusions on a predefined class-balanced subset of 42 held-out images. Across five independently initialized training runs, AgroX-Swin achieved a mean held-out accuracy of 87.19% and macro-F1 of 0.8300 ± 0.0122, while the five-model probability ensemble achieved 87.94% accuracy and 0.8355 macro-F1. Deterministic aggregation of the same 14-class predictions yielded 99.29% species-recognition accuracy and 88.42% binary health-status accuracy, with a diseased-class F1-score of 0.9160. Temperature scaling reduced the representative model's expected calibration error from 0.0792 to 0.0310. At the 20% perturbation level, Grad-CAM++ + LIME produced the largest mean confidence drop (0.2540), while Grad-CAM++ showed the highest transformation stability (0.8371) and SHAP + LIME showed the highest attribution-burden stability (0.7954), demonstrating complementary rather than uniformly superior behavior among individual and fused explanation methods. Model-randomization analysis further examined the dependence of Grad-CAM++ explanations on learned model parameters. AgroXAI provides an integrated framework combining leakage-aware model development, multi-seed training-stability assessment, held-out classification, calibration, statistical uncertainty analysis, and quantitative evaluation of complementary XAI methods. The resulting attribution maps are interpreted as prediction-relevant visual explanations rather than validated lesion localization or quantitative disease-severity estimates. External robustness and real-world agricultural generalization remain to be established using independently acquired field datasets.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fped.2026.1951655.title: Totally single-incision laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision with intracorporeal hand-sewn Roux-en-Y reconstruction in children: clinical outcomes and learning curve
doi:10.3389/fped.2026.1951655.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To evaluate the feasibility, perioperative outcomes, and learning curve of totally single-incision laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision with intracorporeal hand-sewn Roux-en-Y reconstruction in children.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We retrospectively reviewed children who underwent laparoscopic choledochal cyst excision between January 2018 and December 2024. Thirty-five children underwent totally single-incision laparoscopic intracorporeal hand-sewn reconstruction (TSILC), and 40 underwent conventional single-incision laparoscopic-assisted reconstruction (SILC). Baseline characteristics, operative outcomes, recovery, complications, and follow-up were compared. Multivariable linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors was used to adjust continuous outcomes for baseline differences. The TSILC learning curve was assessed using cumulative sum (CUSUM) analysis of jejunojejunostomy time.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      TSILC patients were older (29.86 ± 12.99 vs. 19.60 ± 13.62 months,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.001), heavier (14.90 ± 5.07 vs. 9.22 ± 4.40 kg,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.001), and had a different sex distribution (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.030). After adjustment, total operative time did not differ significantly (adjusted
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                      =8.75 min, 95% CI −12.10 to 29.60;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.411), whereas jejunojejunostomy time remained longer with TSILC (adjusted β=12.02 min, 95% CI 3.02 to 21.02;
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.009). TSILC was associated with less blood loss, a shorter incision, and earlier first flatus and defecation (all adjusted
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.001); oral intake time did not differ significantly after adjustment (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       = 0.568). Early complications occurred in 3/35 TSILC and 5/40 SILC patients. Thirty-three TSILC procedures were completed without an additional port or open conversion; one required an additional port and one required open conversion. Median follow-up was 40.0 months (IQR 21.5−59.5) for TSILC and 46.5 months (IQR 27.2−66.2) for SILC. The CUSUM curve peaked at case 17, suggesting relative stabilization after case 18.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>TSILC with intracorporeal hand-sewn Roux-en-Y reconstruction was technically feasible in selected children and showed a measurable learning curve. The findings suggest that TSILC may offer perioperative advantages in appropriately selected older and larger children.</jats:p>

doi:10.51878/teaching.v6i4.14822.title: PENERAPAN PENDEKATAN DEEP LEARNING DALAM PEMBELAJARAN DAN KOMPETENSI PROFESIONAL GURU UNTUK MENINGKATKAN MUTU PEMBELAJARAN DI SDN 18 GUNUNG AGUNG
doi:10.51878/teaching.v6i4.14822.abstract:
<jats:p>Learning quality in elementary schools still faces challenges in the form of entrenched conventional learning paradigms and teachers' limited understanding of the deep learning approach. This study aims to describe the implementation of the Deep Learning approach and teachers' professional competence in improving learning quality at SDN 18 Gunung Agung. This study employs a qualitative approach with a descriptive design and a case study method. Data collection was conducted through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation, involving the principal, teachers, and students as data sources. Data analysis follows the Miles and Huberman model, encompassing data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, validated through technique and source triangulation as well as member checking. The results indicate that the implementation of the Deep Learning approach has transformed learning through the integration of three main dimensions: Mindful Learning, which builds students' mental readiness and reflection; Meaningful Learning, which connects the material to real-life contexts; and Joyful Learning, which creates an enjoyable learning atmosphere through the utilization of technology and interactive media. Teachers' professional competence serves as a catalyst for this transformation through their ability to design differentiated learning, integrate technology pedagogically, implement authentic assessment, conduct continuous reflection, and build professional learning communities. Obstacles such as the diversity of student characteristics, time constraints, and technology infrastructure were addressed through differentiated learning, the utilization of formative assessment, and strengthened collaboration through Teacher Working Groups (KKG). This study concludes that the synergy between the Deep Learning approach and teachers' professional competence significantly enhances learning quality, as evidenced by the development of Higher Order Thinking Skills, active participation, and the holistic competence of students.
ABSTRAK
Mutu pembelajaran di sekolah dasar masih menghadapi tantangan berupa paradigma pembelajaran konvensional yang mengakar dan pemahaman guru yang terbatas terhadap pendekatan pembelajaran mendalam. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan penerapan pendekatan Deep Learning dan kompetensi profesional guru dalam meningkatkan mutu pembelajaran di SDN 18 Gunung Agung. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis deskriptif dan metode studi kasus. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi, wawancara mendalam, dan dokumentasi yang melibatkan kepala sekolah, guru, dan peserta didik sebagai sumber data. Analisis data mengikuti model Miles dan Huberman melalui tahapan reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan yang divalidasi melalui triangulasi teknik dan sumber serta member check. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penerapan pendekatan Deep Learning telah mentransformasi pembelajaran melalui integrasi tiga dimensi utama: Mindful Learning yang membangun kesiapan mental dan refleksi peserta didik, Meaningful Learning yang mengaitkan materi dengan konteks kehidupan nyata, dan Joyful Learning yang menciptakan suasana belajar menyenangkan melalui pemanfaatan teknologi dan media interaktif. Kompetensi profesional guru berperan sebagai katalisator transformasi melalui kemampuan merancang pembelajaran berdiferensiasi, mengintegrasikan teknologi secara pedagogis, menerapkan asesmen autentik, melakukan refleksi berkelanjutan, dan membangun komunitas belajar profesional. Kendala berupa keberagaman karakteristik peserta didik, keterbatasan waktu, dan infrastruktur teknologi diatasi melalui pembelajaran berdiferensiasi, pemanfaatan asesmen formatif, serta penguatan kolaborasi melalui Kelompok Kerja Guru. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa sinergi antara pendekatan Deep Learning dan kompetensi profesional guru secara signifikan meningkatkan mutu pembelajaran yang ditandai dengan berkembangnya Higher Order Thinking Skills, partisipasi aktif, dan kompetensi peserta didik secara holistik.</jats:p>

doi:10.2118/233821-ms.title: Bridging Arps Decline Theory and Deep Learning: A Physics-Constrained Neural Network Framework for Multi-Horizon Production Forecasting Across 864 Tight-Gas Wells in the Piceance Basin
doi:10.2118/233821-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Reliable production forecasts are required for reserves surveillance, workover ranking, gathering commitments, and field economics in mature tight-gas assets. Classical decline-curve analysis (DCA) is transparent but must be fitted and quality-controlled well by well; recurrent networks learn across a field but may extrapolate unstably beyond observed history. This study couples the two approaches. A recurrent encoder reads monthly gas-rate history and estimates bounded Arps hyperbolic parameters qi, Di, and b; the differentiable decline equation generates the forecast. The framework is evaluated against an unconstrained LSTM, a soft-penalty LSTM, classical DCA, and hybrid residual models on 864 Mancos-interval wells in the Piceance Basin (232,678 monthly records, 2000-2024). Splits are by well, neural predictions average three random seeds, and paired uncertainty is estimated by a well-clustered bootstrap. Two protocols separate an idealized retrospective comparison from deployment: peak-aligned windows identify decline behavior with hindsight, whereas calendar-forward windows use only information available at the forecast date. Results are strongly horizon-dependent. For a 24-month forecast after 36 months of history, all competent models are statistically tied (pooled RMSE 19.6-21.9 MCF/day; R2 approximately 0.98-0.99); neither physics terms nor sparse static features improve accuracy. When only 24 months are observed and the forecast extends to 48-96 months, explicit decline behavior becomes important. Neural-DCA reduces median rate RMSE relative to the unconstrained LSTM by 35.0-47.1% under peak alignment and by approximately 21% at calendar-forward H = 48 and 96 (4.21 versus 5.32 and 5.06 versus 6.41 MCF/day; both p ≤ 0.0002). It matches a bounded hyperbolic refit retrospectively and is modestly more accurate under calendar-forward placement at H = 96 (5.06 versus 6.10 MCF/day). The soft-penalty and structured models perform nearly identically, indicating that the benefit comes from decline-shaped physical content rather than a unique architecture. For wells forecast from only 12 observed months, PAED has the best pooled RMSE (28.76 MCF/day), but its well-level advantage is not significant (p = 0.39), and performance on true early-life wells remains poorly resolved. No consistent cumulative-volume gain is found under peak alignment. Calendar-forward Neural-DCA reduces finite-horizon cumulative error relative to hyperbolic DCA (10.8% versus 16.0%), but this is not an EUR or reserves result. The engineering implication is practical: use simple history-based models for near-term surveillance; retain explicit decline behavior, through classical DCA or a physics-constrained network, for long-horizon rate forecasting.</jats:p>
doi:10.2118/233821-ms.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

doi:10.3389/fenvs.2026.1909483.title: Corporate sustainable development effects of the artificial intelligence pilot zone policy: evidence from China based on double machine learning
doi:10.3389/fenvs.2026.1909483.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As digital transformation becomes increasingly intertwined with green development, whether the artificial intelligence pilot zone (AIPZ) policy improves corporate sustainable development performance warrants empirical examination.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023, we treat the establishment of AIPZs as a quasi-natural experiment and apply double machine learning to estimate the policy effect.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The AIPZ policy significantly improves corporate sustainable development performance, and the result is robust across alternative specifications and tests. Decomposition analysis shows improvements in environmental performance, the joint development level, and the balance between economic and environmental performance, despite a decline in return on assets. Mechanism tests point to green innovation, lower agency costs, and human capital upgrading as potential channels. The effect is stronger among non-state-owned enterprises, firms outside heavily polluting industries, and high-tech firms.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings suggest that governance arrangements, environmental constraints, and technological capabilities shape firms’ responses to the policy. They provide firm-level evidence on how place-based artificial intelligence policy may support green corporate transformation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.58421/gehu.v5i5.2100.title: The Effect of Self-Regulated Learning on Critical Thinking Skills and IPAS Teaching Readiness Among Elementary Education Students in the Era of the Merdeka Curriculum
doi:10.58421/gehu.v5i5.2100.abstract: <jats:p>Critical thinking skills and teaching readiness are essential competencies that elementary education (PGSD) students must possess to prepare for the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum. One factor believed to contribute to these two competencies is self-regulated learning. This study aims to analyze the influence of self-regulated learning on the critical thinking skills and teaching readiness of PGSD students in the IPAS program. The study employed a quantitative approach with a correlational design. The study sample consisted of 54 PGSD students from Muhammadiyah University of Mataram and Mataram University, selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected via a Likert-scale questionnaire that had passed validity and reliability tests, then analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics, including normality tests, Pearson’s correlation, simple regression, and the coefficient of determination (R²). The results indicate that self-regulated learning has a positive and significant effect on critical thinking skills, contributing 56.4%, and a positive and significant effect on readiness to teach IPAS, contributing 9.5%. These findings suggest that enhancing self-regulated learning can strengthen critical thinking skills while supporting students’ readiness as prospective elementary school teachers. The implications of this study underscore the importance of integrating strategies for developing self-regulated learning into the curriculum.</jats:p>
doi:10.58421/gehu.v5i5.2100.venue: Journal of General Education and Humanities

doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26oct078.title: Extent of the Heads of Schools’ Supervision in Improving Collaborative Learning Among Students in Public Secondary Schools in Arusha District Council, Tanzania
doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26oct078.abstract: <jats:p>The study examined the extent to which heads of schools’ instructional supervision enhances collaborative learning among students in public secondary schools in Arusha District Council, Tanzania. The study involved 11 public secondary schools and 525 participants, comprising 11 Heads of Schools, 152 teachers, and 362 students. Instructional Leadership Theory guided the study. The study employed a convergent design under a mixed-methods research. Quantitative data were collected using teachers’ and students’ questionnaires, while qualitative data were collected through an interview guide administered to Heads of Schools. The validity of the data collection instruments was established through review by three experts in Educational Planning and Administration from Mwenge Catholic University (MWECAU). A pilot study was conducted in one public secondary school that was not included in the actual study.</jats:p>

doi:10.1088/2515-7639/aeae74.title: Screening novel cathode materials from the Energy-GNoME database using foundation machine learning force fields and DFT
doi:10.1088/2515-7639/aeae74.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The development of new cathodes is essential for enabling next generation energy storage technologies. Here, we introduce a multi-fidelity workflow that bridges AI-based candidate identification and density functional theory refinement for accelerated discovery of cathode materials. Starting from the Energy-graph networks for materials exploration (GNoME) database, we use foundation machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) as an intermediate-fidelity layer to screen Li-, Na-, K-, Mg-, and Ca-ion intercalation cathodes. We assess dynamical stability and simulate intercalation voltage profiles to determine the average operating voltage and specific energy. The surviving candidates are further prioritized using experimentally motivated filters based on space-group prevalence, elemental availability, and cost, followed by DFT+U refinement of the most promising structures. Finally, combined MLFF and DFT nudged elastic band calculations are used to assess ion-migration kinetics and identify candidates with the potential for good rate capability. The workflow reduces 615 high-confidence Energy-GNoME cathodes to 10 prioritized candidates with favorable electrochemical properties and manageable volume changes. In addition to delivering a shortlist of promising candidates, this work benchmarks the consistency of Energy-GNoME, ML interatomic potential, and DFT predictions and demonstrates how MLFFs can transform AI-prioritized materials databases into physics-grounded discovery pipelines.</jats:p>

doi:10.2118/237272-stu.title: Hierarchical Phase-Adaptive Machine Learning Framework for Real-Time Non-Productive Time Prediction in Offshore Drilling
doi:10.2118/237272-stu.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>NPT remains one of the largest financial burdens in the oil and gas industry, costing operators hundreds of millions of pounds per year and consuming 20–30% of total drilling time. The objective of this study was to develop a hierarchical phase-adaptive machine learning framework capable of dynamically adjusting feature importance and classification boundaries based on the type of drilling being conducted (vertical, curve, or lateral). As part of the validation process, the proposed method was applied to two wells located at the Volve Field in the Norwegian North Sea. Activity-level data were extracted from WITSML Daily Drilling Reports (DDRs) to construct a 31-feature transferable dataset using within-well normalized statistics, rates of change, and activity-based operational signals. Three phase-specific Random Forest classifiers were trained using SMOTETomek resampling on the primary well (15/9-F-10, 848 records, 90 NPT events). Cross-well validation on an entirely unseen well (15/9-F-9, drilled 18 months earlier) demonstrated that the phase-adaptive framework achieves F1=0.436 and AUC=0.798, representing improvements of +11.6 percentage points for F1 and +11.9 percentage points for AUC over static single-model baselines. Phase-specific analysis revealed that curve-phase operations are the most predictable (CV F1=0.966), while mud density and inclination variability emerge as universal NPT precursors across all drilling phases. The phase-adaptive framework achieved an average precision of 0.412, a 2.0-fold improvement over the static RF baseline, confirming the feasibility of transferable, operationally interpretable NPT prediction across wells and time periods.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1976905.title: Navigating dual pathways: learning-oriented and instrumental identities in AI-mediated informal digital learning of English
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1976905.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Generative AI is increasingly reshaping how learners engage in informal English learning beyond the classroom, making AI-mediated informal digital learning of English (AI-IDLE) an important emerging learning context. Yet research has predominantly focused on intra-personal psychological factors, the social dimensions of learning, particularly how learners construct their social identities in relation to AI, remain significantly underexplored. This qualitative study examines the social identity categories and their construction processes among 12 Chinese university EFL learners engaged in AI-IDLE. Drawing on Social Identity Theory (SIT), data from semi-structured interviews, reflective journals, and AI chat logs were analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings reveal two distinct identity pathways: learning-oriented academic identities, characterized by deep-learning commitment, humble mindset toward AI, and sustained immersion in the student role; and an instrumental identity, organized around a
                    <jats:italic>user</jats:italic>
                    category defined by transactional engagement, service satisfaction and surface learning approaches. Within this instrumental pathway, a more intensified
                    <jats:italic>fast-food consumer</jats:italic>
                    orientation emerged, which was explicitly self-identified by one participant and analytically inferred from behavioral patterns across several others. The study demonstrates that AI-IDLE does not simply erase or replace existing social identities but selectively reinforces and reconfigures them through group norms, prototypical markers, and evaluative comparison. These findings extend SIT by revealing how technological affordances and social configuration shape identity pathways that support or undermine meaningful learning engagement. Practical implications are proposed for AI developers, digital learning designers, educators, and curriculum designers to foster learning-oriented identity pathways in AI-mediated informal learning environments
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.2118/234174-ms.title: Automatic History Matching of Strain Data Using Machine Learning and Markov Chain Monte Carlo: Comparative Study of Two Wells in the Delaware Basin
doi:10.2118/234174-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Fiber-measured strain can infer fracture geometry and cluster-level production profiles, enabling completion design optimization and improved production. This study develops a machine learning-assisted Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) workflow for automated history matching strain measured by Rayleigh Frequency Shift Distributed Strain Sensing (RFS-DSS). The workflow is demonstrated on two comparable wells (B4H and 3H) in Delaware Basin to diagnose the deep drivers of the lower strain by comparing fracture geometry, rock-mechanical properties, and wellbore characteristics.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Approximately 2,000 coupled fluid flow and geomechanics single fracture simulations spanning 9 input features are generated. 4 strain-measured depth (MD) attributes (Peak, Width, Min, Area) are extracted as targets to train machine learning surrogates. Models are trained on 90% of cases using five-fold cross validation, with 10% held out for independent validation to assess generalization performance. A MCMC inversion history matches field in-well production strain (IWPS) data to infer posterior distributions of these 9 features. The MCMC P50 estimates are fed back into the numerical model to simulate the full-well production profile.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>For 3H, field data show no statistically significant differences in peak magnitudes across the five completion designs. However, the 4 PCs Stages exhibit more uniform strain peaks. The MCMC history-matching results indicate that this improved uniformity arises from more consistent distributions in fracture conductivity, fracture half-length, fracture height, and skin factor, which in turn yields a more uniform cluster-level oil rate contribution. Comparing the two wells, 3H exhibits lower strain-peak magnitudes than B4H. MCMC-inferred posteriors attribute this to lower fracture conductivity, shorter fracture half-length, higher Young's modulus, and higher skin factor in 3H. Consistent with these posteriors, P50 forward simulations predict a lower oil rate for 3H than for B4H. The underlying driver is consistent with completion inputs: 3H was placed with a lower proppant load per cluster than B4H, leading to reduced effective conductivity and diminished production.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This paper develops a machine learning assisted MCMC workflow that automatically history matches strain from fiber measurements to identify the key subsurface features controlling the strain distribution and to infer the corresponding production profile. The workflow is broadly applicable to future any in-well production strain applications, allowing engineers to constrain subsurface uncertainty and rapidly evaluate completion designs and production performance.</jats:p>
doi:10.2118/234174-ms.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

doi:10.2118/234142-ms.title: A History-Response-Conditioned FiLM-CNN and Transfer Learning–Based Approach for Pressure Transient Analysis of Multiphase Fractured Horizontal Wells
doi:10.2118/234142-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Pressure-transient responses of fractured horizontal wells under multiphase-flow conditions are jointly affected by phase behavior, relative permeability, saturation distribution, and fracture conductivity, resulting in complex pressure and pressure-derivative signatures. Conventional numerical simulation is computationally expensive, whereas direct deep-learning training is constrained by the limited availability of multiphase samples. To address these challenges, a history-response-conditioned FiLM-CNN combined with transfer learning is proposed for multiphase pressure-transient analysis. Based on parameter combinations generated using Sobol sequence sampling, a semi-analytical model is employed to construct a large-scale single-phase database, and a commercial numerical simulator is used to generate approximately 800 oil–gas two-phase samples. Early-time pressure responses and key static parameters are jointly encoded as conditioning information and injected into the CNN through feature-wise linear modulation, enabling the network to adaptively adjust its intermediate features according to different reservoir conditions and fracture parameters. A dual-task learning objective with a pressure–pressure-derivative consistency constraint is introduced to improve prediction performance. In the multiphase prediction stage, static-input reconfiguration, pretrained-weight inheritance, and a freeze–unfreeze fine-tuning strategy are adopted to transfer the pretrained single-phase model to the multiphase prediction task. The results show that the proposed model achieves a pressure-prediction R2 of 0.9996 on the single-phase test set. Dual-task learning reduces the MAPE of the pressure derivative by 77.96%, while transfer learning reduces the pressure and pressure-derivative prediction errors for most multiphase test samples compared with training from scratch. The proposed framework improves multiphase prediction capability under limited-sample conditions and provides an efficient and stable surrogate model for pressure-transient analysis of fractured horizontal wells.</jats:p>
doi:10.2118/234142-ms.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

doi:10.2118/233853-ms.title: Field-Scale Demonstration of Model-Free Reservoir Characterization and Rapid Production Forecasting Using Physics-Informed Machine Learning
doi:10.2118/233853-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Building geological models from diverse field data may require considerable multidisciplinary effort depending on the reservoir and decision complexity. Furthermore, dynamic model calibration for production forecasting using historical data typically necessitates numerous full-physics simulations in traditional history matching workflows, often leading to prohibitive computational cost for field-scale applications. Purely data-driven machine learning (ML) models can bypass high-fidelity model construction by learning statistical correlations between measured inputs and forecast targets and enable production forecasting. However, such models require extensive training data, lack physical interpretability and mostly exhibit limited predictive capability. To address these limitations, we propose a physics-informed ML framework for reservoir characterization and production forecasting based on observed well data without the need to construct high-resolution reservoir models.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The proposed physics-informed neural network (PINN) is built on a reduced physics model in which each well is modeled as a single node with associated pore volume and transmissibilities for each injector-producer pair. The inputs to the network are observed operational responses, including water injection rates and bottomhole pressures and the network predicts nodal pressures and phase saturations as outputs. Phase-wise production rates are subsequently computed using calibrated physical parameters inferred by the network. The ML loss function combines data misfit terms with a physics-based regularization term defined as the node-wise material-balance residual derived from the conservation equations. During training, both the neural network parameters and physical parameters are calibrated, including nodal pore volumes, inter-well transmissibilities, well indices and relative permeability functions. The trained model provides not only rapid forecasting capability but also physical interpretability under the conditions tested.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The proposed PINN was applied to a field-scale waterflooding case with 4.5 years of highly fluctuating historical data and complex reservoir structures, including several large faults. To evaluate the importance of physical constraints and prior geological information, we compare three cases: (1) solely (observed) data based loss function, (2) physics- and data-based loss function without prior geologic information, and (3) physics- and data-based loss function with prior information. The prior information provides field-informed initial estimates of nodal pore volumes and inter-well transmissibilities. Incorporating the physics loss improves predictive performance relative to the purely data-driven case, and prior information further enhances accuracy, demonstrating that low-resolution prior information is beneficial even in scenarios without access to high-fidelity models. The calibrated physical parameters characterize well-wise drainage volumes and inter-well connectivity, successfully capturing preferential flow paths and weak connections across faulted compartments. The inferred connectivity trends are validated against streamline-based connectivity computed from a full-physics simulation on a high-fidelity dynamic model.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The proposed PINN framework demonstrated the ability to deliver rapid forecasting of phase-wise well production rates, well allocation factors and inter-well connectivities for a realistic field case based on observed well measurements without the need for constructing and calibrating high-fidelity reservoir models under the conditions tested.</jats:p>
doi:10.2118/233853-ms.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

doi:10.59841/saber.v4i4.4240.title: Pengaruh Model Project Based Learning Berbasis Pembelajaran Mendalam terhadap Kemampuan Menulis Teks Deskripsi Siswa Kelas VII SMP Muhammadiyah 16 Lubuk Pakam Tahun Pelajaran 2025/2026
doi:10.59841/saber.v4i4.4240.abstract: <jats:p>This study examined the descriptive text writing ability of seventh-grade students at SMP Muhammadiyah 16 Lubuk Pakam before and after implementing Project-Based Learning integrated with a Deep Learning approach and assessed the significance of the difference between their scores. The study employed a quantitative experimental method with a one-group pretest–posttest design. The population comprised all seventh-grade students at the school, while 20 students from the VII Leader class were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using descriptive text writing tests administered before and after the intervention. Students’ writing was assessed using a rubric covering content, text structure, language conventions, vocabulary, spelling, and punctuation. The learning activities integrated project work with meaningful, mindful, and joyful learning principles. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and a paired-samples t-test in SPSS version 32. The findings showed that the mean pretest score was 46.09, categorized as poor, whereas the mean posttest score increased to 86.71, categorized as very good. The mean score increased by approximately 40.63 points. The paired-samples t-test indicated a statistically significant difference between pretest and posttest scores (t = −38.216, p < 0.001), below the 0.05 significance threshold. These findings indicate that students demonstrated substantially improved descriptive writing performance following the learning intervention. The assessment focused on students’ ability to communicate descriptions clearly and systematically. The study concludes that Project-Based Learning integrated with Deep Learning was associated with a significant improvement in descriptive text writing ability among seventh-grade students at SMP Muhammadiyah 16 Lubuk Pakam during the 2025/2026 academic year.</jats:p>
doi:10.59841/saber.v4i4.4240.venue: SABER : Jurnal Teknik Informatika, Sains dan Ilmu Komunikasi

doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010439/v1.title: Validation Design Governs the Apparent Predictive Performance of Machine Learning for PLGA Drug Release
doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010439/v1.abstract: <jats:p>Reliable generalization is essential for machine-learning models intended to predict drug-release behavior across heterogeneous experimental settings. However, multi-study experimental data often contain closely related formulations generated under shared materials, processing conditions, release protocols, and laboratory practices, creating hidden dependencies between training and test data. Such dependencies can make model performance appear stronger than its ability to generalize to genuinely new experimental domains. Here, we examine how validation topology governs the apparent predictability of poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) microparticle drug release using a public dataset containing 321 formulations and 4,913 release observations collected across 113 studies. Using a common LightGBM prediction framework, we compare validation schemes ranging from random observation splitting to strict study-grouped holdout. Predictive performance decreases markedly as train–test independence becomes more stringent, with 𝑅! declining from 0.939 under random point splitting to 0.616–0.625 under formulation-level holdout and 0.372 when entire studies are withheld. Controlled overlap experiments further show that retaining samestudy sibling formulations in the training set systematically increases apparent performance, while nearest-neighbor analysis reveals lower prediction error for formulations lying closer to the training distribution, particularly when their nearest training counterpart originates from the same study. These results show that formulation-level independence alone does not ensure experimental-domain independence and demonstrate that apparent drug-release predictability is strongly conditioned by validation design. Study-aware validation therefore provides a more rigorous basis for assessing generalization of machine-learning models trained on heterogeneous multi-study experimental data.</jats:p>

doi:10.5194/gstm2026-66.title: Signal separation in GRACE and GRACE-FO data using a deep learning algorithm
doi:10.5194/gstm2026-66.abstract: <jats:p>Time-variable gravity data as derived from the GRACE and GRACE-FO satellite missions contain the superposition of various mass change signals such as terrestrial water storage or ice mass change, as well as strong correlated noise. A common strategy for extracting specific geophysical signals from the data is to apply de-noising filters such as the DDK or VDK filters for suppressing the noise, and subsequently reducing non-targeted signals using physical forward models. Since both of these steps introduce and propagate errors to the extracted geophysical target signal, we propose an alternative strategy using a deep learning algorithm.The method consists of two subsequent steps: In the first step, the neural network is trained to co-predict several gravity signal components and a noise component when given their sum. For this training step, realistic forward-modeled signal components given by the ESA Earth System Model and a numerically simulated noise component assuming a GRACE-type gravity mission are used. In the subsequent testing step, the trained algorithm is applied to real GRACE/-FO monthly anomalous gravity grids. The proposed pipeline covers both the de-noising and signal separation step, and thereby represents an alternative processing method for (unfiltered) Level-2B to Level-3 GRACE/-FO data processing. Comparing the achieved results to equivalent state-of-the-art GRACE/-FO Level-3 data products such as those provided by the GFZ GravIS portal shows the proposed method to be beneficial in terms of the de-noising performance, as well as the preservation of small-scale details in the estimated signals.</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/mscra-03-2026-0027.title: Industry 4.0 technologies and environmental sustainability performance in supply chains: an exploratory statistical and machine learning analysis
doi:10.1108/mscra-03-2026-0027.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how key Industry 4.0 technologies relate to environmental sustainability performance in supply chains. Specifically, it examines Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence, Big Data Analytics, Blockchain, Digital Twin and Cloud Computing, and explores their relative associations with sustainability outcomes using both statistical and machine learning techniques.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected from 268 supply chain and logistics professionals across multiple industries. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS software version 31.0.2. Machine learning analysis was carried out using Orange Data Mining to perform feature importance ranking and decision tree modeling, with model performance evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Correlation and hierarchical regression analyses reveal no statistically significant association between any individual Industry 4.0 technology and environmental sustainability performance and tested pairwise interaction effects are likewise non-significant. Exploratory machine learning feature rankings order the technologies differently across three methods, and cross-validated models do not outperform a mean-only baseline, indicating no detectable predictive signal in these data.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study is based on cross-sectional survey data, which limits causal interpretation and does not capture changes in technology adoption and sustainability performance over time. The sample, although adequate for the applied analyses, is restricted to 268 respondents and may not fully represent all industries and geographical contexts. Future research should use longitudinal designs, larger international samples and additional Industry 4.0 technologies to extend the understanding of digital transformation and sustainability relationships in supply chains.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings caution against expecting sustainability improvements from technology adoption alone. No individual technology, and no tested combination, showed a statistically significant association with environmental sustainability performance, and cross-validated models showed no predictive signal. The results redirect managerial attention from technology acquisition toward the mediating organizational practices through which digital technologies may generate sustainability value.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study measures six Industry 4.0 technologies as separate constructs within a single sample, combines conventional statistical testing with exploratory, cross-validated machine learning, and transparently reports a null result for direct technology–performance associations a finding that complements prior mediation-based evidence by suggesting that direct effects of individual technologies may be weak in the absence of mediating capabilities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.1108/mscra-03-2026-0027.venue: Modern Supply Chain Research and Applications

doi:10.2118/234085-ms.title: Physics-Encoded Learning for DAS-Based Flow Allocation: A Comparative Study
doi:10.2118/234085-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) has become an important surveillance technology for injection and production wells because it enables dense acoustic measurements along the wellbore using fiber-optic sensing channels. Each DAS channel behaves as a distributed strain-sensitive acoustic measurement over a finite gauge length, recording broadband acoustic disturbances generated by flow-induced vibrations. The resulting high-resolution spatial and temporal measurements provide a rich dataset that can support a wide range of applications, including flow allocation, event detection, completion-integrity monitoring, flow-assurance diagnostics, production surveillance, and well testing. Despite these capabilities, quantitative interpretation of DAS data, particularly for flow allocation, remains challenging. Conventional workflows often depend on high signal-to-noise ratios, long spatial apertures, transient low-frequency events, or calibration against controlled measurements. Such requirements can limit applicability in field operations because calibration conditions may change with time, drift from actual downhole conditions, or fail to capture the complexities of multiphase flow and completion heterogeneity. Here, we present a physics-encoded neural network (PeNN) framework for estimating downhole flow parameters from acoustic measurements. The proposed method combines physics-informed preprocessing, multi-domain feature extraction, and a neural network architecture in which prior physical knowledge is embedded directly into the model structure. The preprocessing workflow includes de-drifting, denoising, sound-transmission-loss compensation, attenuation-informed frequency-wavenumber filtering, noise matching, phase-based stacking, and data standardization. Extracted features include time-domain, spectral, higher-order spectral, cepstral, frequency-wavenumber, and spatial-wavelet descriptors. The proposed PeNN model encodes physical relationships, such as turbulent-flow behavior, noise-logging relationships, and mechanistic constraints, directly into the model layers. This structure is designed to improve generalization, reduce dependence on large, labeled datasets, and support the transition from instance-based learning to continuous learning. The workflow is further extended through federated learning, enabling local assets to train models on site while sharing only model updates with a central server. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, a synthetic injection-well case study was developed using computational fluid dynamics simulations of a 2.5 m water-injection section with two injection zones. The proposed PeNN model was compared with a conventional neural network of identical architecture but without embedded physical constraints. Results showed that the physics-encoded model required approximately 2.5 times fewer labeled training samples to achieve comparable prediction performance under sparse-label conditions.</jats:p>
doi:10.2118/234085-ms.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

doi:10.2118/233892-ms.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Numerical Simulation of Multiphase Multicomponent Flow Coupled with Geochemical Reactions
doi:10.2118/233892-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Fully coupled compositional and reactive transport simulations are critical for accurately characterizing multiphase multicomponent phase behavior and geochemical processes in petroleum development and carbon sequestration. However, conventional iterative solvers for phase equilibrium flash calculation and cell-wise geochemical kinetics introduce extremely high computational overhead, which has become the core bottleneck restricting large-scale multi-physics coupled simulations. Traditional acceleration schemes often face inherent tradeoffs among accuracy, robustness and applicability. To break through this limitation, this study proposes a deep learning-assisted numerical simulation framework, in which two dedicated deep neural network (DNN) surrogate models are developed to replace the iterative flash calculation module and geochemical reaction kinetics solver respectively. For the compositional simulation module, the DNN flash model is trained on 1.2 million two-phase thermodynamic samples. Offline evaluation shows that the model achieves an overall mean relative error of 0.98% and an R2 of 0.999993 for liquid fraction and phase compositions, with over 900-fold speedup at the million-sample scale. When seamlessly integrated into the MRST compositional solver and validated via a quarter five-spot CO2 flooding case, the model yields average relative errors below 0.15% for oil and gas production rates, and below 0.6% for all grid-scale state variables over the 2-year simulation period, without numerical instability or error accumulation. For the reactive transport module, an 18-input, 9-output DNN kinetic surrogate is trained on physically consistent reaction solutions from core-scale CO2 flooding cases. It realizes non-iterative batch inference with approximately 80-fold speedup at the million-sample scale. Coupling tests confirm that the model generalizes accurate numerical solutions across all grid cells, with log-domain mean absolute errors below 0.01 for all aqueous and solid species, verifying favorable generalization performance. Overall, the proposed framework provides a fast, robust and physically consistent solution for compositional and geochemical calculations, offering an efficient pathway for large-scale multi-physics coupled simulations.</jats:p>
doi:10.2118/233892-ms.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10380615/v1.title: Weak-Strong Steady-State Microbunching Accelerator Light Source
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10380615/v1.abstract: We propose a phase space manipulation involving one energy modulation sandwiched by two dispersion sections which converts a bunched particle beam or bunch train to ultra-high-harmonic density modulation, while the energy modulation in principle can be arbitrarily weak. The same scheme can also be used for energy bunching, creating energy levels in a bunched beam. We further propose a mechanism invoking three laser modulators in a storage ring to longitudinally focus the electron beam both weakly and strongly, such that a microbunch train and its high-density-harmonics or energy bunching form and sustain turn-by-turn. We call this mechanism weak-strong steady-state microbunching (Weak-Strong SSMB). The longitudinal beta function can vary by seven orders of magnitude along such a ring, with the minimal value squeezed to 10 nm. An example application of Weak-Strong SSMB for kW coherent EUV radiation is presented. Extension to X-ray can be anticipated. An energy-leveled electron beam enables $\gamma$-ray frequency comb production. The ideas can be scaled to wavelengths like RF and THz, for bunch length and energy spread control, ultrashort X-ray and coherent THz generation. Our work establishes a new paradigm for longitudinal dynamics study, accelerator light source development, and opens great potential for accelerator physics and technology.
