                    <jats:p>The review shows that DL-based AMD is architecturally diverse, but its supporting evidence remains incomplete. Most studies report datasets, feature sources, model architectures, and conventional metrics, whereas robustness testing, artifact-grounded explainability, reproducibility assets, and deployment evidence remain inconsistent. The empirical validation shows that although all models achieve strong clean cross-validation performance, class-wise analysis, malware false-negative behavior, repeated-run stability, and multi-level test-time feature masking reveal architecture-dependent reliability differences that are not captured by aggregate accuracy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study contributes an architecture–artifact–validation triad and a claim-aligned reliability audit to align AMD claims with the maturity of supporting evidence. Overall, the findings support a transition from accuracy-centric benchmarking to reliability-centric evaluation, where models are assessed using credible datasets, realistic validation, robustness, interpretability, reproducibility, and operational feasibility.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.18296/set.1603.title: Movement in mathematics teaching and learning
doi:10.18296/set.1603.abstract: <jats:p>As mathematics and dance teachers, we are interested in how movement, dance, and mathematics are entwined. Increasingly, research shows how movement is integral to mathematical thinking and knowing—for novice to expert—and for exploring early mathematical concepts to more complex mathematical ideas. With movement so integral to mathematical thinking, how can we recruit movement into the mathematics classroom? What kinds of movement will enhance students’ mathematical thinking and knowing? We share some practical activities designed to support the mathematical learning of our ākonga by developing their mathematical thinking and knowing through movement.</jats:p>

doi:10.2118/233862-ms.title: Integrated Drilling–Production Optimization Framework Using Reinforcement Learning and Digital Twin Simulation
doi:10.2118/233862-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As drilling becomes more complex and the need for intelligent use of drilling life cycles intensifies, the petroleum industry is embracing advanced digital technologies at a faster rate. Although there has been great advancement in the automation of drilling and the use of data to optimize drilling, production, and economic performance are still considered as engineering functions separate from one another. As a result, an operating strategy that aims for optimal short-term drilling productivity can unintentionally impact reservoir productivity, shorten reservoir life, and have a negative economic effect in the long-term. To solve this challenge, an integrated optimization framework is needed that can take all drilling, reservoir, production forecasting, and economic parameters into account during the development of a field.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In this study, a novel Digital Twin–Reinforcement Learning (DT–RL) framework is proposed that is capable of real-time drilling monitoring, virtual well modelling, adaptive optimization, production forecasting, and economic evaluation in one intelligent decision support environment. The Digital Twin is constantly updating the real drilling data with the virtual representation of the well, allowing real-time monitoring of the critical drilling parameters: Weight on Bit (WOB), rotary speed (RPM), drilling torque, standpipe pressure, drilling fluid circulation and bit performance. At the same time, a Reinforcement Learning (RL) agent analyzes a few of those operational scenarios on the fly and keeps on optimizing drilling strategies to achieve maximum long-term technical and economic efficiency instead of maximizing drilling efficiency on a single instant. The framework provides a feedback loop between drilling and production forecasting to allow decisions to be made to ensure the integrity of the reservoir and maximize future hydrocarbon recovery.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To illustrate the feasibility of the methodology proposed, a conceptual case study was carried out with representative drilling and production data for the realistic conditions of petroleum engineering operation. The conceptual evaluation showed that the total drilling time was reduced by around 12.5 % whereas the average Rate of Penetration (ROP) was improved by 13.6 % with the integrated DT–RL compared with a conventional drilling strategy. Furthermore, the optimized drilling conditions resulted in the reduction of the average drilling torque by 11.5% and the reduction of the Mechanical Specific Energy (MSE) by 10.3%, which means that the energy used for rock-cutting is more efficient and the rock-cutting performance is improved. The Formation Damage Index estimated between 25% reduction indicating better preservation of NWI and better reservoir quality after the drilling operations.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The advantages of the scheme proposed did not only apply to the drilling part of the business but also to performance in production. The conceptual evaluation resulted in an estimated 8.7% increase in cumulative hydrocarbon production and an estimated increase in recovery factor from 34.2% to 37.1% due to reduced formation damage and increased reservoir connectivity. Moreover, the highest production rate rose from 1,050 BOPD to 1,120 BOPD while the average production rate rose from 865 BOPD to 940 BOPD in the first 12 months of production. Economically, the integrated optimization strategy lowered drilling costs and improved the profitability of the project, achieving a 14.2% improvement in the Net Present Value (NPV) and a higher Return on Investment (ROI) than the conventional drilling optimization strategies.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The presented results show that using Digital Twin technology in combination with Reinforcement Learning offers a viable approach to optimizing drilling operations intelligently by directly connecting drilling actions with reservoir behavior, production forecasting and economic performance. The current contribution is conceptual; it provides a technically consistent base for the realization of future implementation with field scale data, real-time sensor integration and Digital Twin operational platforms. The proposed methodology provides a potential solution for constructing next generation intelligent wells, optimizing drilling operations with autonomy, asset management for the whole well lifecycle, and thus a safer operating environment, more hydrocarbon recovery, better decision-making and economically viable development of petroleum fields.</jats:p>
doi:10.2118/233862-ms.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

doi:10.2118/233903-ms.title: A Machine Learning Based Workflow for Frac Hit Assessment, Pattern Recognition, and Production Restoration
doi:10.2118/233903-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Frac hits, hydraulic-fracturing interactions between infill (child) wells and existing (parent) wells, can significantly impair shale gas production. Accurate assessment of frac-hit severity, recognition of hit patterns, and implementation of effective production-restoration strategies are critical to mitigating frac-hit damage and accelerating post-hit recovery. However, an integrated workflow combining these tasks remains absent, owing to complex pressure–production responses and the reliance on time-consuming manual interpretation. In this study, such a workflow is developed based on geological, operational, and production data from 208 shale gas frac-hit events in the Weiyuan shale gas field, China. Within this workflow, frac-hit severities are quantitatively assessed using a severity factor derived from information-entropy weighting combined with expert scoring. Treating geological and operational parameters as inputs and the derived severity factors as targets, a frac-hit severity assessment model is established using a Random Forest (RF) algorithm, with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) employed for model interpretation, achieving a root mean square error of 0.0202 on the test set. Subsequently, an adaptive ensemble model combining Extremely Randomized Trees (ExtraTrees) and Bootstrap-Aggregated Decision Trees (TreeBagger) is constructed to automatically identify frac-hit patterns, using geological and operational parameters as inputs and field-specific criterion-determined patterns as targets. The adaptive ensemble model achieves an overall pattern recognition accuracy of 90.5%, outperforming standalone ExtraTrees, TreeBagger, Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), and deep neural network (DNN) models. Finally, a DNN–RF ensemble model is developed to predict production restoration percentage and recommend restoration strategies, incorporating geological and operational parameters, restoration-strategy variables, the predicted severity factor, and the identified frac-hit pattern. Application of the workflow to a representative field case indicates that the recommended strategy could increase the predicted production restoration percentage by 14.51 percentage points compared with the implemented strategy. This study offers new insights into the integrated management of frac hits in shale gas development.</jats:p>
doi:10.2118/233903-ms.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

doi:10.58578/yasin.v6i6.12303.title: Penerapan Model Experiential Learning Berbasis Culturally Responsive Teaching untuk Meningkatkan Hasil Belajar Materi Penerapan Norma
doi:10.58578/yasin.v6i6.12303.abstract: <jats:p>Students’ difficulties in analyzing the application of norms and determining appropriate actions indicate the need for Pancasila Education instruction that connects concepts with everyday experiences. This study aimed to improve students’ learning outcomes on the topic of applying norms through an experiential learning model based on culturally responsive teaching (CRT) that integrates the cultural context of Madura. The study employed the Kemmis and McTaggart classroom action research (CAR) design and was conducted over two cycles involving 27 students in Class V-A at UPTD SDN Kamal 2. Data were collected through tests, observation, and documentation, then analyzed using quantitative descriptive analysis based on mean scores and the percentage of students in the class achieving learning mastery. Reflection on Cycle I informed improvements to the intervention in Cycle II by shifting concrete experiences from role play to learning stations, simplifying instructions, and grouping students according to their learning readiness. The results showed an increase in the mean score from 57.04 in the pre-cycle phase to 63.70 in Cycle I and 88.89 in Cycle II. The percentage of students achieving learning mastery increased from 33.33% in the pre-cycle phase to 59.26% in Cycle I and 88.89% in Cycle II. These findings indicate that implementing CRT-based experiential learning, accompanied by improvements to the intervention based on reflection, supports improved learning outcomes in the class studied. This study provides practical guidance for developing Pancasila Education instruction that connects concrete experiences, cultural contexts, and students’ learning readiness. Further research could extend its application to different topics and cultural contexts using more varied forms of assessment.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fdgth.2026.1912106.title: Machine learning–based personalized prediction of developmental dysplasia of the hip using risk factors and clinical examination
doi:10.3389/fdgth.2026.1912106.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Machine learning–based disease prediction models can assist with disease diagnosis and early detection. This study aimed to identify the risk factors for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) and develop multiple machine learning–based models to support screening and risk stratification for DDH.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A retrospective analysis of 12,105 infants screened for DDH between January 2020 and December 2022 at Shenzhen Children’s Hospital was performed to collect information on physical examination and risk factors. After univariate and multivariate screening, age-stratified sampling was performed on 11,898 DDH-negative patients to match the age distribution of 207 DDH-positive patients, thereby reducing potential bias. These balanced cohorts were randomly split into training and test sets (at an 8:2 ratio) under both 1:1 and 1:2 positive-to-negative ratios. Predictive modeling was based on random forest, support vector machine, logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor, light gradient boosting machine, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Twelve variables were included in the model. The XGBoost model trained on 1:1 data was chosen as the best model [area under the curve (AUC): 0.883, accuracy: 0.807, precision: 0.744, F1 score: 0.800, recall (sensitivity): 0.865, and specificity: 0.761]. External validation using data from Jinhua Municipal Central Hospital provided preliminary evidence of transferability [AUC: 0.909, accuracy: 0.838, precision: 0.829, F1 score: 0.840, recall (sensitivity): 0.850, and specificity: 0.825]. Skin pattern asymmetry, restriction of hip abduction, swaddling, breech presentation, and female sex were the top five most important predictive variables.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The XGBoost model can be used to support early clinical screening and risk stratification for DDH, helping clinicians identify infants who should undergo hip ultrasonography.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.4171/9ecm/41.title: Learning physics simulations for improving design processes in the industry
doi:10.4171/9ecm/41.abstract: This article is the written version of the Felix Klein prize lecture, given on 16 July 2024, at the 9th European Congress of Mathematics in Seville.In the same fashion as the lecture, general ideas and results are given, and references are provided for the reader interested in details and rigorous developments.In an industrial group like Safran, numerical simulation of physics phenomena is used in the majority of the design processes of its manufactured products.At Safran's corporate research center, we develop technologies to improve these processes by deriving fast and reliable surrogate models for various domains of physics.We address two technologies developed in recent years.First, a physical reduced-order modeling method for non-linear structural mechanics and thermal analysis.This method is applied to the lifetime computation of high-pressure turbine blades and the fast heat analysis of high-pressure compressors.Second, the learning of physics simulations under nonparameterized geometrical variability using classical machine learning tools, thanks to nonlinear deterministic dimensionality reduction (involving morphing and principal component analysis) and Gaussian process regression, with predictive uncertainties.We also present some of our contributions to the open-source and open-data community.

doi:10.37034/residu.v4i3.225.title: Implementation of Peer-Assisted Learning to improve selected SHS students’ output submission rate in English subjects
doi:10.37034/residu.v4i3.225.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to determine how Peer-Assisted Learning (PAL) helps students improve their assignment submission rates in an English class. PAL is an adaptive learning technique that pairs students with low academic performance (mentees) with high-performing students. The researcher selected 10 students from the class to serve as mentees. The study employed a qualitative design using purposive sampling to select participants. Prior to the implementation of PAL, the mentees' average assignment submission rate was only 10%. Following implementation, the submission rate rose to an average of 61.43% during the period between the third and twelfth weeks. In focus group discussions, students evaluated the project as a positive and beneficial strategy for both mentors and mentees, as reflected in their experiences throughout the activity. Teachers should master peer-support learning strategies to minimize student passivity in the classroom while fostering a spirit of collaboration and accountability among students.</jats:p>
doi:10.37034/residu.v4i3.225.venue: Journal of Research and Investigation in Education

doi:10.3390/medsci14060672.title: Deep-Learning-Based Assessment of Breast Arterial Calcification on Mammography: Technical Validation, Cardiovascular Prognostic Value, and Clinical Translation—A Narrative Review
doi:10.3390/medsci14060672.abstract: <jats:p>Breast arterial calcification (BAC) is a manifestation of medial arterial calcification frequently detected incidentally on screening mammography. Increasing evidence suggests that BAC may also serve as a marker of cardiovascular risk. This narrative review critically synthesizes the evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-based detection, segmentation, and quantification of BAC. It also evaluates the cardiovascular prognostic significance of automatically quantified BAC and examines the requirements for clinical translation. A targeted literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar was conducted for English-language publications available from database inception through 3 September 2026, with additional studies identified from reference lists. Deep-learning approaches included convolutional neural networks, U-Net-derived segmentation architectures, transfer-learning models, and semi-supervised methods. Reported technical performance varied according to task and validation strategy. Representative segmentation models achieved Dice/F1 scores ranging from 0.666 to 0.756 and Jaccard indices from 0.581 to 0.614. Case-level BAC detection achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of up to 0.95–0.96 in selected test cohorts. However, external validation, learning-curve reporting, multivendor evaluation, and robustness assessment remained inconsistent. Prognostic studies demonstrated graded associations between automated BAC burden and cardiovascular outcomes. In a cohort of 21,514 women without known cardiovascular disease, age-adjusted BAC burden was associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) among women classified as low risk, with adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.66 and 2.31 for BAC below and above the age-specific median, respectively. In 123,762 women from two healthcare systems, MACE risk increased progressively with BAC burden after adjustment using the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease EVENTs (PREVENT) equations, reaching approximately 2.8- to 3.3-fold higher risk with severe BAC. Nevertheless, incremental predictive improvement may be small—in one study, the addition of BAC changed the 5-year AUC from 0.645 to 0.646. Overall, available evidence supports the feasibility of scalable AI-based BAC assessment and demonstrates consistent associations between AI-quantified BAC and cardiovascular outcomes. However, technical performance and independent prognostic associations alone do not establish clinical utility. Standardized BAC definitions, genuinely independent external validation, and prospective implementation studies are required before BAC-guided cardiovascular management can be recommended.</jats:p>

doi:10.2118/233800-ms.title: Gas Lift Evaluation and Production Forecasting Through a Transfer Learning Dual-Track Machine Learning Framework
doi:10.2118/233800-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As reservoirs deplete and natural flow declines, artificial lift becomes necessary to sustain production, and gas lift is one of the most applied methods in unconventional horizontal wells. Injecting high-pressure gas lowers the density of the flowing column and increases drawdown, but the production response is not proportional to the gas injected. It is governed by nonlinear interactions among injection rate, wellbore pressures, geometry, and fluid properties. Beyond an optimum, additional gas reduces production. Machine learning captures such relationships well and predicts oil rate with high accuracy, yet that accuracy is almost always measured within the same wells a model was trained on. A companion study of 11 Eagle Ford wells (Al Raisi et al., 2026) reported R2 as high as 0.960 under a random split but strongly negative values under leave-one-well-out (LOWO) evaluation, because field measurements cluster in a narrow band of conditions and much of the gas lift domain is never observed.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This study's framework combines two tracks. Track A applies data-driven models to daily field data from the 11 wells. Track B uses a steady-state multiphase flow simulator to build a physics-consistent synthetic dataset in two complementary designs: a broad dataset of 6,000 nodal-analysis cases sampled by Latin Hypercube Sampling, establishing which operating conditions exist and where gas lift helps, and a controlled sweep of 700 scenarios evaluated at 11 injection rates each, resolving how production responds to injection. Together these required 13,700 simulation cases. A deep learning neural network is then trained through a staged transfer learning procedure that pre-trains on the broad dataset, refines on the sweep dataset, and fine-tunes on field data.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The simulations reproduce established gas lift behavior, which is what makes them usable as a training signal. Feasibility rises from 90% to 99% with gas lift, 285 of 295 otherwise non-productive cases are enabled, and the resulting performance curves fall into monotonic, plateau, and post-peak decline classes separated by tubing size, wellhead pressure, and fluid properties. Under LOWO evaluation, staged transfer learning raises the average R2 from 0.149 to 0.414, reduces MAE from 70 to 56 STB/D, and lowers MAPE from 56% to 38%. Neither dataset suffices alone: broad-only pre-training yields 0.146 and sweep-only 0.322, so breadth and structure are both required and the order matters. The gains concentrate on wells the baseline fails, most notably Well 4, which moves from a strongly negative to a positive R2.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Applied to a well-level injection scenario, the model ranks lift responsiveness across operating states in the physically expected order, supporting open-loop screening and gas allocation. The study also reports a useful negative result: despite 135 post-peak-decline scenarios in training, predicted curves rise monotonically and do not reproduce over-injection. Expanded coverage and explicit physical constraints are therefore complementary rather than interchangeable.</jats:p>
doi:10.2118/233800-ms.venue: SPE Annual Technical Conference and Exhibition

doi:10.1186/s41239-026-00629-2.title: ChatGPT’s feedback credibility and students’ perceived learning: the role of agent-related social perceptions
doi:10.1186/s41239-026-00629-2.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This paper examines whether students’ agent-related social perceptions of ChatGPT are associated with the perceived credibility of its feedback in academic tasks and whether such credibility, in turn, is related to students’ perceived learning. It also investigates whether the relationship between feedback credibility and perceived learning varies according to students’ sensitivity to the quality of their academic work and their sensitivity to grade-based rewards. To address this, we develop a theoretical model grounded in social perception theory and prior research on students’ experiences with AI-based tools. The model is tested using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) on data collected from 230 students who completed an academic writing task. The findings reveal that students’ agent-related social perceptions—particularly perceived competence and human-like empathy—are positively connected to the credibility students attribute to its feedback. In turn, perceived feedback credibility is interestingly related to students’ perceived learning in the context of academic writing. Furthermore, the positive link between credibility and perceived learning is weaker among students with higher grade-based reward sensitivity. This research contributes to the educational technology literature by advancing understanding of how students evaluate the credibility of ChatGPT-generated feedback and how such evaluations are associated with learning perceptions. It also shows that agent-related social perceptions play a significant role in students’ credibility judgements. Finally, the findings offer practical implications for educators and students seeking to integrate ChatGPT effectively into academic activities.</jats:p>
doi:10.1186/s41239-026-00629-2.venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education

arxiv:2610.20413.title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
arxiv:2610.20413.abstract: Momentum is a classical tool for accelerating convex optimization and a standard component of modern large language model training. Yet recent empirical work has questioned the usefulness of first-moment momentum in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We study this question through a bandit formulation of RLVR with bias-corrected exponential moving average (EMA) momentum, where the EMA coefficient $β$ controls how quickly the weights on past gradients decay. When policy gradients are evaluated exactly, we prove that increasing $β$ within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization. When gradients are estimated from sampled responses, a positive expected gain can be obscured by sampling fluctuations. We show that as the learning rate $η$ decreases, the expected gain with fixed $β$ vanishes faster than these fluctuations, whereas increasing $β$ to keep $η/(1-β)$ within the safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain that eventually dominates them. Bandit simulations quantitatively validate these predictions. RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base using SGD with EMA and AdamW support our principle of choosing larger coefficients in practical LLM post-training. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing $β_1$ improves mean validation accuracy by nearly $2$ percentage points over the conventional choice, demonstrating the principle's effectiveness at a larger model scale.

arxiv:2610.20392.title: FOLD: Position-Free Far Memory with Local Order for Long-Context Speculative Decoding
arxiv:2610.20392.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM generation through lightweight drafting and parallel verification. It is particularly promising for long inputs, where KV-cache access costs can be amortized over multiple accepted tokens. Yet most drafters are trained on short sequences and degrade on long inputs, while long-context training is costly. Existing training-free approaches restrict the context window, rescale positions, or augment recent context with retrieved distant entries. Drafters, however, read target hidden states that already encode contextual and positional information, and their lightweight architecture makes full-history attention affordable. We propose FOLD, a training-free method that preserves exact local positions and treats all distant entries as far memory at a shared position. To counter attention dilution as the memory grows, we sharpen attention within it to emphasize relevant entries while separately controlling its total weight relative to the local window. Across six target-drafter pairs and diverse benchmarks of up to 256K tokens, FOLD predominantly delivers the highest speedup, with the best case more than doubling the speedup over autoregressive decoding, from 2.08$\times$ to 4.22$\times$.

arxiv:2610.20203.title: Investigating Behavior Cloning from Few Demonstrations for Autonomous Driving based on Bird's-Eye View in Simulated Cities
arxiv:2610.20203.abstract: This paper investigates the use of Behavior Cloning (BC) for autonomous driving from a bird's-eye view (BEV) perspective in simulated urban environments. BC uses supervised learning to mimic expert driving behaviors. Previous works have applied BC in the CARLA simulator but did not fully address the challenges of traffic light compliance. Our approach enhances BC by integrating a kernel density estimator to adjust training sample weights based on action density, thereby improving the learning of rare but critical actions such as stopping at red lights and accelerating at green lights, specially in scenarios of scarce number of expert demonstrations. Using BEV inputs, which provide an abstract top-down view of the driving environment, our method simplifies the policy learning process. The trained convolutional neural network (CNN) outputs steering and acceleration actions based on these BEV inputs and additional state variables. Experimental results in the CARLA simulator demonstrate that our weighted BC method significantly improves driving performance, achieving higher route completion compared to standard BC. This weighted approach proved to be crucial in learning correct driving behaviors, particularly in test environments not encountered during training, highlighting its potential for enhancing autonomous vehicle navigation.

arxiv:2610.20136.title: Seeing at the Edge: Energy Characterization of Vision-Language Model Inference on Edge Platforms
arxiv:2610.20136.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are moving onto edge devices, but little is known about how much energy they draw on single-board computers with NPU or GPU accelerators, or where that energy goes. We measure total-system energy, latency, and thermal behavior of Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct and its text-only sibling on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo-10H NPU and on a Jetson Orin Nano Super, on both CPU and accelerator, and separate the fixed energy of each request from the energy that grows with output length. Because the accelerators use different quantization and serving software, we compare deployment stacks rather than silicon. Three findings stand out. First, NPU offloading makes the Pi a much more efficient VLM platform: it cuts energy per generated token by about two-thirds, leaves the host CPU largely free, and avoids the thermal throttling that the CPU backend reaches in sustained use. Second, an image adds both fixed and per-token energy, but at typical response lengths generating the answer costs far more than processing the image. Third, the Jetson GPU favors short responses through its lower fixed cost per request, whereas the Pi NPU favors longer ones through its lower cost per output token; their energy curves cross near 40 output tokens.

arxiv:2610.19878.title: Neural Wasserstein Splines: Representation-Invariant Second-Order Priors for Trajectory Inference
arxiv:2610.19878.abstract: Population dynamics are often observed only as unpaired snapshots, which leave the evolution between measurements underdetermined. Second-order regularization can constrain it, but a penalty on the accelerations of sampled particles is a prior on joint particle paths, and different particle representations of the same marginal curve can have different acceleration costs. We therefore introduce Neural Wasserstein Splines (NWSP), a sample-based method that learns a continuous population curve under a Wasserstein smoothness prior. A neural network maps latent variables to the control points of a cubic spline in time, so samples at any time come from the spline basis without numerical integration. We project the generator's velocity onto gradients of a finite dictionary of scalar potentials and differentiate this measure-dependent projection in time, obtaining a finite-dimensional surrogate for the intrinsic Wasserstein acceleration, trained jointly with distributional fit losses. For a fixed dictionary and ridge parameter, we prove that the population penalty depends only on the marginal curve and bound its sensitivity to moment-estimation errors. Learned potentials (NWSP-N) sharpen acceleration estimates. On various synthetic and single-cell benchmarks, NWSP is highly competitive with transport and flow-based methods, ranking in the top two in 11 of 16 settings. The penalty improves on an unregularized spline in 13 of 16 settings and, while competitive with a particle-acceleration penalty, adds provable representation invariance.

arxiv:2610.19607.title: A Graph-Based Analysis of Comparability, Scale, and Attribution in Private Transformer Inference
arxiv:2610.19607.abstract: Rising privacy concerns around large language models have accelerated research in private Transformer inference (PTI). Synthesizing the empirical claims in this line of research, however, is hindered by multi-dimensional cryptographic progress and inconsistent evaluation contracts. In this work, we systematize the field by constructing an empirical graph of 62 PTI systems, mapping system attributes to node features and evaluation compatibility to edges. A three-tiered analysis of this graph illuminates the state of private inference. Node-level attribution shows that cryptographic progress drives performance gains across most systems, yet always co-occurs with other factors (model fidelity, hardware, cost accounting). Edge-level auditing shows that only 1 of 1891 candidate system pairs is directly comparable under shared assumptions. Finally, graph-level analysis shows that the scaling frontier of private inference has plateaued at 13B parameters and projects the cost of deploying current PTI techniques on production-scale Transformers. Overall, this graph-based framework equips the community to evaluate PTI claims transparently and channel technical speedups into deployment-scale private inference.

arxiv:2610.19494.title: Robust Real-Time Monocular Human Pose Estimation with Insole-Based Sensor Fusion
arxiv:2610.19494.abstract: Real-time monocular human pose estimation is an important sensing component for human-centered intelligent systems. While recent camera-based methods have achieved impressive accuracy, fundamental challenges persist, particularly when visual observations are incomplete, such as during lower-body occlusion or short out-of-frame intervals. In these challenging but common scenarios, vision-only systems often struggle to reconstruct physically plausible lower-limb motion and reliable foot-ground contact. Due to the highly unobtrusive and wearable nature of smart insoles, this paper investigates whether simple plantar pressure and acceleration sensors can effectively resolve these visually induced limitations. To systematically investigate this, we first collect a synchronized multimodal dataset and then propose a part-decoupled temporal fusion framework. The proposed model fuses foot-sensing features into the lower-body branch to compensate for incomplete visual evidence, while a lightweight coordinator exchanges information between the upper- and lower-body temporal representations to maintain whole-body consistency. The framework is evaluated with three representative real-time visual backbones based on 2D keypoints, 3D landmarks, and SMPL-based human mesh recovery. We evaluate our framework on three representative real-time visual backbones. Quantitative experiments demonstrate that incorporating simple foot sensors consistently improves pose accuracy, motion smoothness, and gait-related measurements over vision-only baselines, with the most significant gains observed under occlusion and short visual-dropout conditions. Ultimately, our results demonstrate that unobtrusive foot sensing provides vital and complementary physical observability when camera observations are temporarily unavailable.

arxiv:2610.18924.title: TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch
arxiv:2610.18924.abstract: Interpreting electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra commonly requires repeated forward simulation and optimization of spin Hamiltonian parameters. Established software provides mature simulation and fitting methods, but these calculations are not generally available as differentiable components within machine-learning workflows. We present TorchSpin, an open-source PyTorch framework that ports the organization and numerical conventions of EasySpin into a tensor-based computational environment. Representative calculations spanning continuous-wave EPR, ENDOR, pulse EPR, spin dynamics, trajectory simulation, and magnetometry closely reproduced corresponding EasySpin results. In matched benchmarks, TorchSpin CPU execution was faster than EasySpin for six of nine workloads although performance depended strongly on the calculation. We therefore focused on the capabilities enabled by automatic differentiation in PyTorch. In a Cu(II) powder-spectrum demonstration, feedback propagated through TorchSpin improved the quality of a supervised convolutional neural network (CNN) without using parameter labels during refinement. Models trained from randomly initialized CNNs using only noisy spectra and TorchSpin reconstruction loss achieved median similarities of $\geq$ 0.99. CNNs trained on TorchSpin-generated libraries also transferred without adaptation to independently generated EasySpin spectra with performance comparable to EasySpin-trained controls. Once trained, the CNN produced initial parameter estimates in approximately 1 ms per spectrum while a batch of 512 was processed in approximately 1.3 ms with GPU acceleration. TorchSpin therefore provides both a tested Python implementation of established EPR calculations and a differentiable physical layer for rapid learned inference, spectral refinement, and parameter-label-free training.

arxiv:2610.03709.title: From Mixing to Tearing: Graph Decomposition in Decentralized Optimization via Message Passing
arxiv:2610.03709.abstract: We study decentralized minimization of sums of smooth strongly convex functions, one per agent, with communication restricted to neighbors in a graph. Existing decentralized algorithms typically emulate a {\it centralized} method; {\it the network serves only to exchange information}, from which agents approximate the global quantities that the method needs. This paper breaks with this paradigm. We introduce a {\it graph decomposition framework} that uses the network to design the method, not merely execute it. It jointly determines how agreement is imposed, which variables are optimized jointly (blocks), and which connected subgraphs host the agents solving each block. The convergence analysis quantifies the trade-offs among these choices. GATE (Graph-Tearing message passing) instantiates the framework by assigning one dual variable per edge and partitioning the edges into trees. Agents interleave edge updates with local message passing recursions that summarize optimization within each tree (block). Its surrogate variant, GATE-S, uses tractable local models and compact messages to reduce computation and communication. We establish linear convergence and show that the topology-aware design acts as a \emph{preconditioner}: the rate depends {\it jointly} on topology and function geometry through the coupling between subproblems defined on the selected subgraphs, whereas consensus-based optimization methods pay the worst case of each separately, the centralized condition number times the inverse spectral gap. On tree-dominant graphs, convergence is provably faster: the rate scales with the tree {\it diameter}, linearly in the number of agents on rings and barbells against quadratically for non-accelerated consensus-optimization methods. Experiments support the predicted scaling and savings in iterations and communication.

arxiv:2610.20494.title: Quantifying privacy risks in foundation model representations of brain MRI
arxiv:2610.20494.abstract: Pretrained representations are increasingly used to share and reuse information from medical images without exposing the original scans, but it is unclear how much patient-specific information these representations retain. We investigate this question for brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) by evaluating five frozen pretrained encoders spanning different architectures, pretraining objectives, and training domains on two longitudinal T1-weighted datasets, OASIS-2 and MIRIAD. Under an attacker model with access to released embeddings, the corresponding public encoder, and auxiliary MRI scans, we evaluate patient linkage and sensitive-attribute inference. Across the evaluated representations, we observe substantial subject-specific information: rank-1 patient linkage reaches up to 99\% on MIRIAD and exceeds 90\% on OASIS-2 for the highest-risk representation, despite the absence of an identification objective during encoder training. We further show that the released embeddings retain information about a demographic attribute, with recorded-sex prediction reaching balanced accuracy of 90.9\% on OASIS-2 and 95.5\% on MIRIAD. Overall, our results demonstrate that replacing raw brain MRI with learned embeddings does not, by itself, eliminate patient-linkage or attribute-inference risk, and is therefore insufficient on its own to establish anonymity.

arxiv:2610.19919.title: Beyond DFT electronic band structures via dual-space orbital learning
arxiv:2610.19919.abstract: Accurate electronic band structures are essential for predicting material properties, but high-fidelity calculations are computationally demanding. We introduce O-kRystal, a dual-space orbital-learning framework that uses a lower-cost Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) calculation as both an energy baseline and a source of structured orbital information. Combining PBE band energies with real- and reciprocal-space orbital matrices, O-kRystal predicts higher-level corrections for individual electronic states as a function of crystal momentum and spin. For states within 5 eV of the band-edge midpoint, it predicts Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof (HSE06) band energies with a mean absolute error of $0.171 \pm 0.009$ eV across nearly 6,000 three-dimensional materials spanning insulating, metallic, magnetic, and nonmagnetic systems. On a separate benchmark of six strongly correlated materials, it reduces the corresponding PBE band-energy MAE by 68.7% and resolves orbital-dependent changes in the relative placement of transition-metal d and ligand p states. Despite training only at high-symmetry points, it maintains comparable accuracy at unseen points along band paths and reconstructs HSE06 densities of states from dense Brillouin-zone predictions. Finally, training O-kRystal on $G_0W_0$ quasiparticle energies for two-dimensional materials demonstrates its applicability across levels of theory and the potential of orbital learning for higher-fidelity, momentum-resolved electronic-structure prediction beyond density functional theory.

arxiv:2610.19894.title: DeepPV-MRF: End-to-End Partial-Volume Fraction Estimation from MR Fingerprinting Time Series
arxiv:2610.19894.abstract:
Background: Estimating subvoxel tissue fractions from magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) is challenging. Conventional dictionary matching and segmentation pipelines can propagate errors from intermediate parametric maps into tissue fraction estimates.
  Purpose: We introduce DeepPV-MRF, a deep learning framework that directly estimates voxel-wise tissue fractions from raw MRF signals.
  Methods: A cascaded spatial-temporal network was trained on subject-derived Bloch simulations with radial k-space undersampling. The network combines temporal encoding and spatial U-Net refinement to estimate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), gray matter (GM), and white matter (WM) fractions without intermediate T1/T2 maps. We compared DeepPV-MRF with partial-volume dictionary matching (PV-DM) and pseudoinverse estimation (PV-Pinv) using simulated and in vivo data.
  Results: DeepPV-MRF outperformed both methods across acquisition settings. In single-shot simulations, CSF/WM/GM mean absolute errors were 0.0418/0.0744/0.0757, versus 0.1281/0.2443/0.2958 for PV-DM and 0.2021/0.2793/0.2630 for PV-Pinv. Corresponding structural similarity values were 0.960/0.916/0.922. In vivo results showed sharper anatomical boundaries and smoother tissue transitions, while cross-shot analysis indicated improved consistency across volunteers.
  Conclusions: DeepPV-MRF enables accurate and efficient direct tissue fraction estimation from MRF signals, particularly with limited shots. Further validation is needed before clinical deployment.

doi:10.1103/dpvk-3vt5.title: Orbit correction for a rapid cycling synchrotron using an adjacent-difference-constrained neural network
doi:10.1103/dpvk-3vt5.abstract: In a rapid cycling synchrotron (RCS), closed-orbit correction is an important task for maintaining high beam quality and machine stability. Since the orbits in RCS change during energy ramping, response matrix-based orbit correction is performed in segments, which can result in the corrector current ramp rates exceeding safety limits and accuracy loss in orbits. To address these issues, this paper employs machine learning for orbit correction in RCS. An adjacent-difference-constrained neural network (ADCNN) was built and tested in both simulations and machine experiments at the China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS). The correction results demonstrate the feasibility of using neural networks for RCS orbit correction. The ADCNN exhibits a correction effect equivalent to that of response matrix-based correction while effectively limiting the current ramp rates of the correctors.

doi:10.1103/bjx3-vlj8.title: Machine Learning on Heterogeneous, Edge, and Quantum Hardware for Particle Physics
doi:10.1103/bjx3-vlj8.abstract: The next generation of particle physics experiments will face an era of challenges in data acquisition, due to unprecedented data rates and volumes along with extreme environments and operational constraints. Harnessing these data for scientific discovery demands real-time inference and decision-making, intelligent data reduction, and efficient processing architectures beyond current capabilities. Crucial to the success of this experimental paradigm are several emerging technologies, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning, silicon microelectronics, and the advent of quantum algorithms and processing. Their intersection includes areas of research such as low-power and low-latency devices for edge computing, heterogeneous accelerator systems, reconfigurable hardware, codesign and synthesis strategies, readout for cryogenic or high-radiation environments, and analog computing. This white paper presents a community-driven vision to identify and prioritize research and development opportunities in hardware-based ML systems and corresponding physics applications, contributing toward a successful transition to the data frontier of fundamental science.

doi:10.5281/zenodo.23327207.title: BI and AI in the Operational Efficiency of Radiotherapy Services
doi:10.5281/zenodo.23327207.abstract: The provision of radiotherapy (RT) varies across regions worldwide. In addition, challenges related to treatment operations, particularly linear accelerator availability and patient flow, may reduce the capacity to deliver care. This scoping review mapped the literature on business intelligence (BI) and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) for the operational efficiency of RT services. Searches in six electronic databases in July 2026 retrieved 4,424 records, 3,298 remained after deduplication. A semi-automated selection process combined deterministic text rules, manual assessment of 81 candidate records, and a 20% random audit of 490 unflagged records. 46 studies were included. Predictive equipment maintenance was the most frequently addressed theme (19/46, 41%), followed by scheduling and patient flow (12/46, 26%), workflow optimization (8/46, 17%), and BI/dashboards (7/46, 15%). Twenty-four studies (52%) were published from 2023 to 2026, 23 (50%) involved model development or retrospective validation, and five (11%) measured operational outcomes after real-world implementation. The evidence indicates growing technical feasibility but limited prospective and implementation-level validation. Because most unflagged records were not manually screened and some database exports lacked abstracts, eligible studies may have been missed. Future research should prospectively evaluate BI systems and predictive AI/ML models using predefined, comparable operational metrics.
doi:10.5281/zenodo.23327207.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

doi:10.64643/ijirt.208742-459.title: A Machine Learning Approach for Fake News Detection Using NLP-Based Feature Extraction
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208742-459.abstract: The rapid growth of digital media and social networking platforms has made it easier for information to be created and distributed at a large scale.Although online platforms provide fast access to news, they also enable the rapid spread of fake news, misleading information, and fabricated content.Fake news can influence public opinion, create social unrest, damage reputations, and affect political, economic, and publichealth decisions.Therefore, automated fake-news detection has become an important research area in Natural Language Processing (NLP) and machine learning.This paper presents a machine-learning approach using text preprocessing, TF-IDF representation, n-gram analysis, linguistic features, and supervised classification.Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, and Random Forest can be compared using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrices.The approach is efficient and comparatively interpretable, but its reliability depends on dataset quality, labeling, changing language patterns, and external verification.
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208742-459.venue: International Journal of Innovative Research in Technology

doi:10.1680/jwarm.25.00035.title: Machine learning vs. conventional regression models in public hospital waste forecasting
doi:10.1680/jwarm.25.00035.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to predict healthcare waste generation and identify associated features. It utilises monthly data from 2019 to 2023 from a representative public hospital in Bahrain. Two models were developed using the conventional multiple linear regression (MLR) and the machine learning (ML) methods. The ensemble voting regressor, which comprises a light gradient boosting machine and three random forest algorithms, emerged as the best model, demonstrating robustness and successfully explaining 90.4% of the total variance with the lowest error. In contrast, the MLR model explains 47.7% of the total variance. The key features for predicting healthcare waste generation, ranked by the ML model from most important to least important, are the number of inpatients, population, number of surgeries, and number of outpatients. These findings provide insights into the factors influencing the rate of healthcare waste generation in public hospitals, and the effectiveness of the ML model in estimating amounts of healthcare waste.</jats:p>
doi:10.1680/jwarm.25.00035.venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Waste and Resource Management

doi:10.64643/ijirt.208542-459.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning for Phishing URL Detection: A Comparative and Interpretability-Driven Evaluation
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208542-459.abstract: Phishing attacks continue to grow in scale and sophistication, using deceptive URLs to imitate legitimate platforms and compromise sensitive user data.Blacklist-and rule-based defenses may struggle to detect newly emerging and short-lived phishing domains, creating a need for data-driven detection approaches.This paper presents a comparative and explainable machine learning framework for phishing URL detection using lexical and domain-level URL features.Four machine learning classifiers, namely Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), are evaluated using publicly available phishing URL datasets.The models are compared using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (ROC-AUC).To improve model transparency, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are incorporated to quantify the contribution of individual URL features to model predictions.The study further analyzes the most influential features associated with phishing classification and compares the interpretability of the selected models.The proposed approach aims to combine effective phishing detection with transparent and understandable predictions, enabling cybersecurity practitioners to examine the factors influencing classification decisions.The findings are expected to support the development of practical, auditable, and reproducible phishing URL detection systems.
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208542-459.venue: International Journal of Innovative Research in Technology

doi:10.5194/gstm2026-34.title: Downscaling and Gap-Filling GRACE-Based Terrestrial Water Storage Anomalies Using Bias-Aware Machine Learning
doi:10.5194/gstm2026-34.abstract: <jats:p>This study presents a methodological framework to temporally reconstruct and spatially downscale GRACE Terrestrial Water Storage (TWS) anomalies using a bias-aware Random Forest model for the transboundary Bug River Basin (Poland–Ukraine–Belarus). The approach incorporates three main innovations that enhance satellite-based TWS estimation. First, missing monthly TWS anomalies were reconstructed using an RF model driven solely by lagged GRACE values and calendar-month information, which avoided information leakage from auxiliary hydrological predictors and yielded a temporally continuous TWS record despite data gaps, including the 2017–2018 GRACE–GRACE-FO hiatus. Second, RF was used to downscale the reconstructed GRACE-derived TWS to a 0.1°×0.1° resolution, using precipitation, evapotranspiration, river runoff, and soil moisture as predictors, together with elevation, lithology, and land-cover class as static physiographic attributes. Third, a bias-aware, mass-conserving block-wise correction was applied to reconcile the downscaled fields with the original GRACE water mass at coarse resolution, by redistributing monthly systematic errors within spatial blocks using river-runoff-based weights, thereby enforcing exact mass-balance closure while preserving physically meaningful sub-grid variability.The results indicate that GRACE-derived TWS dynamics are best captured by a predictor with an integrated origin — river runoff — rather than by individual hydrometeorological drivers, underscoring the importance of multivariate approaches to downscaling. The combined use of hydrometeorological parameters allows the model to capture complementary aspects of the storage balance that are not evident from any single predictor alone. In terms of predictive skill, the 1-month lag dominates, consistent with strong month-to-month persistence in TWS. Month (the seasonal indicator) shows moderate importance. Among the independent predictors, hydrological variables were the dominant controls on the predicted GRACE-derived TWS values, with the three-month rolling mean of river runoff being the most influential predictor. The northern regions of the Bug River Basin exhibit stronger and more regular seasonal cycles, which enhances the effectiveness of the lagged predictors and seasonal encoding used in the imputation model. By contrast, the southern areas tend to show more episodic hydrological variability, potentially driven by localized precipitation extremes, rapid runoff responses, or human water management, which reduces temporal autocorrelation and limits predictability based solely on past GRACE observations. The spatial distribution of linear trends in GRACE-derived TWS reveals a coherent pattern of long-term storage decline over the full 2002–2024 period, with pronounced spatial heterogeneity: the magnitude of decline increases toward the southern part of the study area, where the strongest negative trends are observed.The proposed methodological framework, strengthened by rigorous spatiotemporal cross-validation and physically based mass-conservation constraints, enables improved monitoring and forecasting of groundwater in transboundary catchments and facilitates the reconstruction of continuous TWS changes over time and space, which is particularly valuable for regions with sparse or conflict-disrupted in-situ observation networks.</jats:p>

doi:10.4143/crt.2025.707.title: Deep Learning–Based Multimodal Prediction of Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Response in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer by Integrating MRI and Proteomics
doi:10.4143/crt.2025.707.abstract: <jats:p>Purpose Locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) exhibits significant heterogeneity in response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC), with poor responders facing delayed treatment and unnecessary toxicity. Although magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides spatial pathophysiological information and proteomics reveals molecular mechanisms, current single-modal approaches cannot integrate these complementary perspectives, resulting in limited predictive accuracy and biological insight.Materials and Methods This retrospective study developed a multimodal deep learning framework using a cohort of 274 LARC patients treated with NAC (2012-2021). Graph neural networks analyzed proteomic profiles from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissues, incorporating Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes/gene ontology pathways and protein-protein interaction networks, while a spatially enhanced 3D ResNet152 processed T2-weighted imaging. A LightGBM classifier integrated both modalities with clinical features using zero-imputation for missing data. Model performance was assessed through area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)–receiver operating characteristic, decision curve analysis, and interpretability techniques (SHAP and Grad-CAM).Results The integrated model achieved superior NAC response prediction (test AUC 0.828, sensitivity 0.875, specificity 0.750), significantly outperforming single-modal approaches (MRI ΔAUC +0.109; proteomics ΔAUC +0.125). SHAP analysis revealed MRI-derived features contributed 57.7% of predictive power, primarily through peritumoral stromal heterogeneity quantification. Proteomics identified 10 key chemoresistance proteins, including CYBA, GUSB, ATP6AP2, DYNC1I2, DAD1, ACOX1, COPG1, FBP1, DHRS7, and SSR3. Decision curve analysis confirmed clinical utility across threshold probabilities (0-0.75).Conclusion Our study established a novel MRI-proteomics integration framework for NAC response prediction, with MRI defining spatial resistance patterns and proteomics deciphering molecular drivers, enabling early organ preservation strategies. The zero-imputation design ensured deployability in diverse clinical settings.</jats:p>

doi:10.64643/ijirt.208519-459.title: Privacy-Preserving and Explainable Phishing Website Detection Using Federated Continual Learning
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208519-459.abstract: Phishing websites are continuously modified to imitate legitimate services, evade static blacklists, and exploit user trust. Machine-learning-based detection can identify previously unseen patterns, but conventional centralized training requires sensitive URL, browsing, webpage, and behavioral information to be collected at a central location. This paper proposes FedXPhish, a privacy-preserving and explainable phishing website detection framework that unifies multimodal feature analysis, federated learning, continual learning, differential privacy, secure aggregation, robust aggregation, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). Each participating client extracts URL lexical, domain/TLS, HTML/text, visual, and behavioral features locally. A local multimodal classifier is trained without transferring raw data. Protected updates are securely aggregated to obtain a global model. Continual learning enables adaptation to emerging phishing campaigns while replay and proximal regularization reduce catastrophic forgetting. SHAP and LIME are used to provide global and instance-level explanations. The paper defines a timeaware, non-IID evaluation protocol covering detection performance, privacy, continual adaptation, communication efficiency, explanation quality, and robustness to malicious clients. The work is positioned as a conference-ready research framework; numerical results are deliberately not fabricated and should be inserted after implementation and experimentation.

doi:10.58764/j.im.2026.7.213.title: Pemetaan Tren dan Perkembangan Riset Manajemen Sumber Daya Manusia Periode 2018-2024: Analisis Bibliometrik Menggunakan VOSviewer
doi:10.58764/j.im.2026.7.213.abstract: <jats:p>Aims: This study aims to map the development and trends of Human Resource Management (HRM) research during the 2018–2024 period, identify countries, institutions, and journals that have made significant contributions and influence, and explore collaboration patterns and the direction of global HRM literature. Method: This study employs bibliometric analysis using VOSviewer software to visualize networks and relationship patterns within HRM literature. The research data were obtained from, Dimensions, and databases, covering publications from 2018 to 2024. The analysis was conducted using bibliographic coupling and collaboration network mapping based on countries, institutions, and journals to identify key contributors and the structure of HRM research development. Results: The findings indicate that HRM research during the 2018–2024 period has developed dynamically, characterized by increasingly interconnected scientific collaboration networks across countries and institutions. China, the United States, Pakistan, and Australia emerged as countries with substantial contributions and strong connectivity within the HRM research network. Higher education institutions from Europe and Asia also demonstrated significant roles in strengthening academic collaboration. In terms of publication sources, The International Journal of Human Resource Management and Human Resource Management Review emerged as dominant and influential journals in the development of HRM literature. Novelty: The novelty of this study lies in its integrated mapping of the structure and dynamics of HRM literature through bibliometric analysis of countries, institutions, journals, and scientific collaboration patterns. The findings provide an overview of key actors and major centers of HRM knowledge development globally and may serve as a basis for researchers in establishing future research directions and academic collaborations. Future studies should expand their focus on emerging HRM themes, strengthen cross-country and cross-institutional collaboration, and identify emerging research topics relevant to changes in the workplace and organizational transformation.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1944175.title: PharmAI: domain-specific QA generation by adaptive learning and fine-tuning of small language models
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1944175.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Domain-specific medical question-answering (QA) models face bottlenecks due to scarce labeled data, specialized terminology, and constrained computational hardware.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study aims to develop an efficient pharmaceutical question-answering (QA) system that can be trained and deployed on consumer-grade hardware using Small Language Models (SLMs).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials and methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The pipeline processes four pharmaceutical textbooks containing 3,977 total pages, producing 7,370 semantically similar text chunks and 2,144 synthetic QA pairs under four questioning categories: definition, mechanism, comparison, and clinical application. Three Small Language Models (SLMs), namely SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5–1.5B-Instruct, and Llama-3.2–1B-Instruct, are fine-tuned under the same QLoRA (Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation) configurations and then evaluated with retrieval metrics (Recall@K, Mean Reciprocal Rank) and generation metrics (ROUGE-1/2/L, Semantic Similarity, BERTScore). Architectural decisions including NF4 4-bit quantization, CPU-based FAISS indexing, and completion-only loss masking are implemented due to hardware constraints and validated via ablation analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5–1.5B-Instruct, and Llama-3.2–1B-Instruct demonstrated identical retrieval performance, achieving a Recall@1 of 0.517, Recall@3 of 0.732, Recall@5 of 0.797, and an MRR of 0.628. Similarly, the generation performance evaluation revealed that Qwen2.5–1.5B FT outperformed the other fine-tuned SLMs, achieving the highest scores across all metrics (ROUGE-1 = 0.47, ROUGE-2 = 0.25, ROUGE-L = 0.38, and BERTScore = 0.72). In comparison, SmolLM2-1.7B FT and Llama-3.2–1B FT exhibited comparable performance, with ROUGE-1 scores of approximately 0.35, ROUGE-2 scores of 0.16–0.17, ROUGE-L scores of 0.25–0.26, and BERTScores of 0.66, indicating lower lexical and semantic alignment with the reference outputs than Qwen2.5–1.5B FT.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We evaluate retrieval and generation performance using comprehensive metric suites, incorporating a category-wise breakdown that reveals comparison questions to be the most challenging for single-passage retrieval architectures.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1907483.title: Machine learning and deep learning for diagnosis of endometriosis: systematic review and meta-analysis
doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1907483.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To assess the diagnostic accuracy of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models for endometriosis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420251231469). Databases were searched through November 24, 2025. Twenty-two eligible studies were included. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2. Pooled analysis was conducted in Stata 18.0.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Pooled sensitivity was 0.90 (95% CI 0.86–0.93), specificity 0.75 (95% CI 0.64–0.84), and SROC-AUC 0.92 (95% CI 0.89–0.94). A positive prediction increased disease probability from 10% to 29%, whereas a negative prediction reduced it to 1%. Multicenter design and DL were associated with lower sensitivity. Results were robust.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>ML/DL models demonstrate high diagnostic performance and are promising for non-invasive auxiliary diagnosis. Large multicenter prospective studies and multimodal models are needed to enable clinical translation.</jats:p>

doi:10.1210/jendso/bvag236.title: Leveraging Machine Learning Methods to Predict Post-Transplant Diabetes in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients
doi:10.1210/jendso/bvag236.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Post-transplant diabetes mellitus (PTDM) is a common complication following solid organ transplantation and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to identify both generalizable and solid organ-specific predictors of PTDM with machine learning methods.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials & Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this study, we used 2002-2023 data from the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) to examine the risk of PTDM development across the liver (n = 128 016), kidney (n = 360 562), heart (n = 45 505) and lung (36 260) transplant recipients. We examined various features at baseline using logistic regression and random forest models. Performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), Brier scores, sensitivity, and specificity. Shapley Additive exPlanations were used for model interpretation and to identify key relevant features.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The incidence of PTDM ranged from 9.5% in kidney to 20.2% in lung recipients. Compared to logistic regression, random forest demonstrated modestly improved discrimination (AUROC: 0.62-0.63) and calibration (Brier: 0.124-0.156). It was found across all models that age and BMI were consistent predictors.</jats:p>
                    <jats:p>Prednisone and cyclosporine maintenance were often found to be associated with higher PTDM risk while mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) was seen as protective. SHAP analysis demonstrated complex, nonlinear interactions and supported known risk patterns such as increased age and male sex.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our machine learning model identified risk factors common to post-transplant diabetes across organ transplant recipients, guiding more optimal patient survival post-transplant.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11369905/v1.title: From learning obstacles to reasoning: Didactical design of a problem-based electronic module on trigonometric ratios
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11369905/v1.abstract: Trigonometric ratios remain difficult for many secondary students, yet few problem-based digital resources are designed from the obstacles students actually encounter. This didactical design research developed a problem-based electronic module on trigonometric ratios for Grade 10 students in Indonesia. Tests and interviews with three students and two teachers identified four obstacles: confusing sides relative to the reference angle, relying on memorized formulas, omitting justification, and modeling contextual problems. These obstacles informed a hypothetical learning trajectory and the module, which three experts rated very valid (means 4.33–4.82 on a five-point scale). In a one-lesson trial with 27 students, an observer rated the module very practical (mean 4.23), and reasoning scores rose from 14.78 to 62.37 ( t (26) = 14.59, p < .001; mean normalized gain 0.56). The observed trajectory and the group worksheets, however, showed that side confusion and unjustified answers persisted, and only two of seven groups solved the opening contextual problem. Designing from documented obstacles made these shortfalls visible and indicated directions for revision.

doi:10.1080/17439884.2026.2746967.title: Teachers’ reflexive valuations of digital platforms in schools: a comparative study of Chile and England
doi:10.1080/17439884.2026.2746967.abstract: Digital platforms have become central infrastructures in contemporary schooling, mediating administrative processes, communication with families, and everyday pedagogical practices. Critical scholarship on the platformisation of education has provided important insights into the structural dynamics of EdTech industries, data infrastructures, and platform governance, while other studies have examined how educators experience and use these systems in practice. This article builds on these strands of research by integrating structural analyses of platformisation with an examination of teachers’ concerns, interpretations, and everyday practices. Adopting a critical realist perspective, the study explores how teachers reflexively engage with digital platforms and how new professional practices emerge from their interaction with institutional and technological structures. Drawing on qualitative interviews with twelve teachers in Chile and England – two contexts that differ in educational governance and the development of EdTech markets – the analysis shows how teachers evaluate communicative expectations, organisational constraints, and managerial visibility associated with digital platforms. Through these reflexive processes, platforms contribute to the emergence of new forms of communicative labour, boundary negotiation with families, and micropolitical dynamics within schools. By foregrounding reflexivity and emergence, the article proposes a framework connecting structural analyses of platformisation with teachers’ situated experiences of digital infrastructures in schooling.

doi:10.64643/ijirt.208448-459.title: Crop Disease Detection and Severity Estimation Using Machine Learning
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208448-459.abstract: Plant disease outbreaks destroy crops around the world, cutting into food supplies and hurting farm incomes.Although state-of-the-art deep learning models perform well on clean lab images, they often fail on real farms for three main reasons: they only provide a single disease label without assessing the severity of infection, outdoor lighting and soil backgrounds confuse them, and they misclassify leaves among different plant species.To overcome this, we suggested a practical multi-task model with an EfficientNet-B0 backbone.The network learns shared visual features and feeds them to two parallel heads: one predicting 38 disease classes, and the other estimating severity levels (Early (≤ 15%), Moderate (15-50%), Severe (> 50%)).We proposed a Species-Constrained Logit Masking step, which constrained the predictions to the selected crop in testing, decreasing cross-species false alarms from 18.4% to 0.0%.We also added Grad-CAM heatmaps for the final conv layer (features.8)as a visual verification.We observed the network detect initial lesion edges and color shifts in the first convolution (112x112) and early down sampling layers (56x56) prior to abstract feature grouping by looking at feature maps.For the performance test, we constructed a dataset consisting of 90,446 photos, mixing the laboratory images (87,848 from PlantVillage) and real field images (2,598 from PlantDoc).The model scored 99.4% accuracy on lab images and 96.2% on field photos, with a 20.8 MB file size and a 28.4 MS processing speed.
