doi:10.64643/ijirt.208523-459.title: An Affordable Six-Wheel Arduino Rover for Hands-On Learning in Planetary Robotics and Environmental Sensing with A Path Toward Edge AI
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208523-459.abstract: This work reviews recent literature (2021-2026) on low-cost rover platforms, educational robotics, six-wheel mobility, environmental sensing, and embedded machine learning, and positions an affordable six-wheel Arduino rover within this landscape.The platform pairs an Arduino Uno with six DC geared motors driven through an L298N dual H-bridge, while an HC-05 Bluetooth module links the chassis to an Android handset for basic teleoperation.A modular sensing bay can accommodate the DHT11 temperaturehumidity sensor, the BMP280 barometric sensor, the HC-SR04 ultrasonic ranger, soil-moisture and light probes, MQ-series gas detectors, and the MPU6050 inertial unit.The chassis is designed in CAD for fabrication from acrylic sheet, keeping the projected build cost within a few thousand Indian rupees.The review synthesises peer-reviewed literature indexed in major scholarly databases, supplemented by an authenticated NASA technical memorandum, spanning flight autonomy on Perseverance, deep-learning terrain classification, rocker-bogie suspension optimisation, lowcost sensor calibration, and meta-analytic findings on robotics-supported learning.Five recurring management concerns emerge: purpose, hardware, sensing, process, and reliability.We organise these into a development framework for student-built rovers and map a staged upgrade path toward future TinyML inference, autonomous obstacle avoidance, GPS-assisted navigation, and IoT telemetry.AI is therefore positioned as a future capability rather than a demonstrated onboard function, with the present design providing the sensing, control, and data-acquisition foundation for subsequent TinyML deployment.The platform is an educational terrestrial rover, not flightqualified planetary hardware.The literature supports hands-on robotics as a means of developing computational thinking and STEM engagement, while the proposed platform provides a practical setting for such learning.
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208523-459.venue: International Journal of Innovative Research in Technology

doi:10.17559/tv-20260326003486.title: Research on Adaptive Learning Recommendation Algorithm for Vocational Education Based on Big Data Analysis
doi:10.17559/tv-20260326003486.abstract: To achieve personalized recommendation for vocational education courses, this study designs an adaptive learning recommendation algorithm. It aims to meet the learning needs of learners at different stages. The study starts from the basic concept of big data-based adaptive learning. It reviews relevant models and work processes. Then it elaborates on the implementation process of this learning model. It also compares and analyzes its differences from traditional teaching. Applying big data adaptive learning helps students better master knowledge points. It improves academic performance and enhances learning enthusiasm. The system consists of three core components. They are a learning analysis module, an intelligent tutoring module, and a personalized recommendation engine. On this basis, a personalized teaching framework is constructed. The framework integrates learner profiling, precise content delivery, personalized learning path planning, and intelligent assessment with feedback.

doi:10.68414/nksa6726.title: StockForecastGenie Pro: A Volatility-Aware Machine Learning Decision-Support System for Short-Horizon Equity Index Forecasting
doi:10.68414/nksa6726.abstract: <jats:p>Forecasting short-term movements in financial markets remains challenging because market prices are influenced by rapidly changing economic conditions, investor sentiment, and volatility. While machine-learning methods have demonstrated promise for financial forecasting, many forecasting tools remain difficult for non-technical users to interpret and often provide predictions without contextual explanations. This paper presents StockForecastGenie Pro, a volatility-aware machine-learning decision-support system designed to forecast short-horizon movements in major United States equity indices while providing transparent and interpretable signals. The system forecasts future index levels, point gains, and percentage returns for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average using a stacked ensemble of machine-learning models. Forecast outputs are combined with market-volatility information derived from the CBOE V olatility Index (VIX) to generate plain-language signals ranging from Strong Negative to Strong Positive. The platform also incorporates confidence estimates, simple benchmark comparisons, and broader market context to support user interpretation. A rolling historical evaluation was conducted, and results indicate that forecasting performance improves substantially as forecast horizon increases. At the five-day horizon, the stacked ensemble achieved directional accuracy of 73.2% for the Dow Jones Industrial Average and 70.9% for the S&P 500. Compared with a no-change benchmark, the system reduced forecast error by approximately 24.3% for the Dow Jones Industrial Average and 22.4% for the S&P 500. The results demonstrate that machine-learning ensembles can provide meaningful improvements over simple forecasting approaches while maintaining interpretability for research, educational, and decision-support applications.</jats:p>

doi:10.64643/ijirt.208755-459.title: AI-Based IoT Intrusion Detection Using Deep Learning
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208755-459.abstract: Security teams face a growing challenge as IoT devices multiply across smart homes, healthcare systems, industrial plants, and transportation networks, with each new device widening the pool of potential entry points for attackers.Traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), built on fixed signatures and hand-coded rules, are poorly matched to this setting: IoT traffic is highly varied, devices are resource-limited, data volumes are large, and such systems typically fail to catch zero-day or newly evolving attacks.To close this gap, we present an AI-driven IDS built around a hybrid CNN-LSTM architecture, in which a 1D convolutional layer extracts spatial patterns from individual traffic features while a recurrent LSTM layer captures how those patterns evolve across sequences of packets, jointly aiming for high detection accuracy alongside a low false-alarm rate.The model is built and tested on two widely used IoT security datasets, BoT-IoT and Edge-IIoTset, using a processing pipeline that cleans the raw data, one-hot encodes categorical fields, applies Min-Max scaling, constructs sliding-window sequences, and splits the data into stratified training and test sets.We evaluate performance using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1score, comparing the hybrid model against Decision Tree, Random Forest, SVM, and a standalone Artificial Neural Network baseline.As detailed in Section 6, the hybrid CNN-LSTM model reaches 99.4% accuracy on BoT-IoT and 98.9% on Edge-IIoTset, with strong per-class F1scores for DDoS, DoS, and reconnaissance traffic, though performance drops somewhat, while remaining solid, for harder-to-detect information-theft attacks.We close with a discussion of what deploying this system on resource-constrained IoT hardware would require, and point to federated learning and explainable AI as promising directions for future work.

doi:10.59141/jiss.v7i10.2592.title: Game-Based Learning Experience and Occupational Health and Safety Learning Achievement: The Mediating Role of Learning Engagement in Vocational Training
doi:10.59141/jiss.v7i10.2592.abstract: <jats:p>Occupational health and safety is a mandatory component of public vocational training; however, lecture-based instruction may not sufficiently engage adult learners. This study examined the effect of the game-based learning experience on learning achievement, with learning engagement as a mediating variable, among occupational health and safety trainees at the South Jakarta Regional Job Training Center, Indonesia. A quantitative explanatory survey was conducted with all 174 participants enrolled in the 2026 Batch 1 regular and Mobile Training Unit classes using saturated sampling. All participants completed a game-based learning session on the Wayground platform, formerly known as Quizizz. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire adapted from established instruments and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The game-based learning experience had a positive and significant effect on learning engagement (β = 0.854, p < 0.001) and learning achievement (β = 0.592, p < 0.001), while learning engagement had a positive and significant effect on learning achievement (β = 0.343, p = 0.016). Learning engagement partially mediated the effect of the game-based learning experience on learning achievement (indirect effect = 0.293, p = 0.017). The model explained 72.9% of the variance in learning engagement and 81.6% of the variance in learning achievement. Approximately one-fifth of participants reported technical barriers, primarily unstable internet connections, system lag, device limitations, and game time limits perceived as too short. The findings suggest that game-based learning activities can enhance learner engagement and perceived learning achievement in occupational health and safety training for adult vocational learners, provided that adequate technical readiness is ensured.</jats:p>

doi:10.21460/sendimasxi2026.v11i1.100.title: Exploring Future-Oriented Decision Making among Adolescents through Community-Based Experiential Learning
doi:10.21460/sendimasxi2026.v11i1.100.abstract: <jats:p>Senior high school students face a critical transition toward higher education and the workforce, yet they often make decisions without linking them to the long-term consequences for their health, financial standing, and psychological well-being. LEAP 2036 (Life Experience & Action Planning) is a community-service program that developed a digital experiential-learning simulation titled "The Decision Engine," inviting students to experience a sequence of life decisions across the 2026–2036 period along three modalities: health, finances, and mental health. The activity was implemented on 3–5 August 2026 in two senior high schools. Data were analyzed descriptively, covering final scores on the three modalities, narrative profile classification, personal values, and the consistency of participants' decisions with the life goal they set at the outset of the simulation. Results show that grade-12 participants had the highest average financial score but the lowest average health score among the three grade levels, about a quarter of participants (24.3%) followed a decision sequence that drifted away from their self-chosen life goal, and family was chosen as a core value by 91.0% of participants yet was set as the primary life goal by only 3.6%. This program did not evaluate the effectiveness of the simulation implemented. Nonetheless, these findings may serve as preliminary material for school counseling services in designing more adaptive future-readiness support for students, while also modeling a community-service collaboration between higher education institutions and secondary schools.</jats:p>

doi:10.64643/ijirt.208533-459.title: Machine Learning-Based Nutritional Prediction of Recipes Using Structured Ingredient Data
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208533-459.abstract: As more recipe and nutrition data becomes available, machine learning can now automatically analyze the nutritional value of food recipes.Manually judging whether a recipe is healthy or nutrient-dense can be slow and tough especially when you're reviewing lots of recipes.This study presents a machine learning approach to multi-label classification, helping identify the nutritional profile of recipes.We worked with 725 recipes, cleaning the data, filling in missing info, prepping ingredients, picking key features, and building new ones to make them useful.The final dataset had 15 key attributes, and ingredient info was turned into numbers to ready it for training.The study focuses on six key nutrition categories: Healthy, Protein_Rich, Fibre_Rich, Calcium_Rich, Iron_Rich, four machine learning algorithms-Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and XGBoost were trained and evaluated using a dataset split of 580 samples for training and 145 for testing.XGBoost came out on top with 75.68% accuracy, while SVM scored the best F1-0.5760.The results show machine learning can help automatically sort recipes by various nutritional labelsbut how well it works varies by category.

doi:10.64643/ijirt.208753-459.title: Cyberattack Detection Using Data Analytics and Machine Learning: A Review
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208753-459.abstract: The rapid growth of digital networks, cloud services, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and online applications has increased the risk of cyberattacks.Traditional cybersecurity approaches, particularly signature-based detection, are effective for known threats but may have difficulty identifying new, modified, or sophisticated attacks.Data analytics and machine learning provide promising approaches for analysing large volumes of network and security data and identifying suspicious behaviour.This paper reviews existing research on machine learning and deep learning techniques for cyberattack and network intrusion detection.Five Scopus-indexed studies are examined to understand commonly used detection approaches, datasets, algorithms, evaluation measures, and research challenges.The reviewed literature covers techniques including supervised learning, unsupervised learning, anomaly detection, deep neural networks, recurrent neural networks, convolutional neural networks, autoencoders, and ensemble-based approaches.The literature also emphasizes the importance of appropriate datasets and evaluation methods for reliable intrusion detection.The review indicates that machine learning and data analytics can support automated detection of malicious network behaviour, but challenges remain in false positives, dataset quality, changing attack patterns, computational cost, privacy, and generalization to realworld environments.The paper proposes a general datadriven framework for cyberattack detection and identifies future directions including real-time detection, adaptive learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and privacy-preserving machine learning.

doi:10.1108/ijius-05-2026-0177.title: Lightweight deep learning-based multicarrier modulation classification for UAV-assisted 5G communication systems
doi:10.1108/ijius-05-2026-0177.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)–assisted communication leverages Automatic Modulation classification (AMC) to enhance wireless transmission efficiency. The classification of multicarrier modulation (MCM) signals is a critical component AMC, enabling robust signal demodulation and adaptive resource allocation. However, existing deep learning-based solutions for MCM signal classification often entail significant computational overhead, posing substantial limitations for real-time deployment in resource-constrained and edge environments. To overcome these limitations, this work presents an AMC framework that utilizes Erlang spectrograms for time-frequency feature extraction and introduces a Squeeze-Excitation Lightweight CNN SELight-CNN, a novel deep neural architecture incorporating Squeeze-and-Excitation mechanisms with L2-regularized convolutions for accurate classification of MCM signals. The proposed SELight-CNN model demonstrates high classification accuracy across 10 multicarrier modulation types under different Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) conditions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This work presents an AMC framework that utilizes Erlang spectrograms for time-frequency feature extraction and introduces a Squeeze-Excitation Lightweight CNN SELight-CNN, a novel deep neural architecture incorporating Squeeze-and-Excitation mechanisms with L2-regularized convolutions for accurate classification of MCM signals. The proposed SELight-CNN model demonstrates high classification accuracy across 10 multicarrier modulation types under different SNR conditions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The proposed SELight-CNN consistently outperforms the baseline CNN across all SNR levels, achieving 99% accuracy at −10 dB and reaching 100% from −6 dB onwards. In contrast, the baseline model attains only 95% at −10 dB. Performance is evaluated using recall, precision and F1-score. SELight-CNN stands out by achieving high classification accuracy even in low-SNR conditions, all while keeping the model lightweight and fast. This makes it a practical and efficient choice for real-time use in 5G networks, IoT devices and edge computing systems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In the front-end, Erlang spectrograms are applied to raw signals from the 5G Waveforms dataset, introducing a novel time-frequency representation for AMC tasks. For classification, the back-end employs SELight-CNN, a lightweight CNN that integrates squeeze-and-excitation (SE) blocks with L2 regularization to effectively learn discriminative features from the Erlang spectrograms of MCM signals. SELight-CNN is benchmarked against a baseline CNN without SE blocks using standard evaluation metrics including F1 score, precision, recall and accuracy, demonstrating improved classification performance, particularly under low SNR conditions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.47852/bonviewjcce62027931.title: Self-Supervised One-Class Tabular Deep Learning for Intrusion Detection in Artificial Intelligence of Things Systems
doi:10.47852/bonviewjcce62027931.abstract:
<jats:p>The emergence of the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) has led to increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks. For many of these threats, labeled training data are scarce or unavailable, which increases the need for label-free intrusion detection systems. To address this issue, this study proposes a self-supervised one-class TabNet framework, termed SS-OC-TabNet, for intrusion detection in tabular network traffic. The framework combines self-supervised representation learning and one-class compactness learning within a two-stage training process. In the first stage, masked-feature reconstruction is used to learn the feature structure of normal traffic from
unlabeled data. In the second stage, a hypersphere compactness objective is applied to make the latent representations of normal traffic more compact for anomaly detection. TabNet is used as the backbone to support sequential feature selection, which also improves interpretability. The proposed model was evaluated on the NSL-KDD dataset and further validated through comparison with related works on the ToN-IoT dataset, achieving an accuracy of 93.20% with a false alarm rate of 2.13%. Further, the interpretability results show which traffic features influence the model’s decisions. The compact design and low computational complexity of the proposed
framework also support energy-efficient deployment in resource-constrained AIoT environments. These results indicate that SS-OC-TabNet is a viable tool for label-free intrusion detection in AIoT environments.

doi:10.21460/sendimasxi2026.v11i1.125.title: From Learning to Caring: Implementasi Project Compassion Mahasiswa Keperawatan dalam Membangun Kepedulian Sosial di Panti Asuhan
doi:10.21460/sendimasxi2026.v11i1.125.abstract: <jats:p>Pembentukan nilai compassion perlu diinternalisasikan kepada mahasiswa sejak di bangku pendidikan melalui kegiatan pengabdian masyarakat.  Compassion yang menjadi bagian dari caring, menjadi nilai dasar pada bidang keperawatan. Kegiatan ini bertujuan mengimplementasikan Compassion Project yangd apat menumbuhkan dan memotivasi mahasiswa menerapkan nilai – nilai yang telah dipelajari ke dalam komunitas. Kegiatan dilaksanakan selama 3 jam dengan melibatkan 17 anak pantisuhan dan 7 mahasiswa. Kegiatan diawali dengan observasi kebutuhan peserta, kemudian dilanjutkan dengan perkenalan, permainan interaktif, edukasi dan demonstrasi menyikat gigi serta mencuci tangan yang benar, makan bersama, dan sharing secara berkelompok. Evaluasi dilakukan melalui observasi partisipasi dan respons peserta selama kegiatan. Seluruh peserta menunjukkan antusiasme dan respons positif terhadap setiap rangkaian kegiatan. Permainan interaktif meningkatkan keterlibatan dan kebersamaan, sedangkan edukasi kesehatan memberikan pengalaman praktik langsung mengenai kebersihan gigi dan tangan. Sesi sharing berkelompok menjadi bagian yang paling bermakna karena memberikan ruang bagi anak-anak untuk berinteraksi secara terbuka, mengungkapkan kondisi dan perasaan, serta memperoleh perhatian dan dukungan mahasiswa. Kegiatan juga memberikan pengalaman langsung kepada mahasiswa dalam menerapkan caring melalui kehadiran, komunikasi, empati, dan kepedulian. Sehingga pembelajaran tidak hanya berlangsung di ruang kelas, tetapi juga melalui pengalaman sosial yang nyata. Compassion Project dapat menjadi pendekatan pembelajaran berbasis pengalaman untuk mendukung internalisasi nilai caring mahasiswa keperawatan sekaligus menciptakan interaksi positif dan bermakna bagi anak-anak panti asuhan.</jats:p>

doi:10.64643/ijirt.208572-459.title: Comparative Analysis of Classical Machine Learning Vs. Deep Learning for Resource-Constrained Edge Devices
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208572-459.abstract: Deploying machine learning models directly onto ultra-low-power microcontrollers and edge hardware (TinyML) is increasingly vital for real-time, privacy-preserving Internet of Things (IoT) applications.However, selecting the optimal algorithm under severe hardware constraints typically under 512 KB of RAM and tight power budgets presents a fundamental tradeoff between computational overhead and predictive power.This paper presents a systematic comparative analysis evaluating traditional machine learning algorithms (Decision Trees, Random Forests, and Support Vector Machines) against lightweight, quantized Deep Learning architectures (compact CNNs and Multilayer Perceptrons).Benchmark experiments are conducted across standardized datasets for tabular, acoustic, and vision tasks deployed on representative microcontroller platforms (e.g., ARM Cortex-M series, ESP32).Models are evaluated across three primary dimensions: inference latency, memory footprint (Flash and peak SRAM usage), and predictive accuracy.Findings indicate that classical algorithms achieve significantly lower SRAM overhead and near-instantaneous inference times on structured sensor data, making them highly effective for ultra-low-memory nodes.Conversely, quantized neural networks achieve higher accuracy and generalization on complex spatio-temporal features, though they require higher Flash allocation and nontrivial peak RAM.Based on these empirical trade-offs, we propose a lightweight decision matrix to guide model selection based on strict device hardware limits and application demands.

doi:10.22219/raden.v6i2.45092.title: Local potential-based encyclopedia development for senior high school biology learning: A scoping review
doi:10.22219/raden.v6i2.45092.abstract: <jats:p>Background--The characteristics of local potential-based encyclopedia development for senior high school (SMA/MA) biology learning need to be mapped to clarify the representation of formats, development models, local objects, and topics. Objective--To map publication patterns and the characteristics of local potential-based encyclopedia development in SMA/MA biology learning in Indonesia. Method--This study used a scoping review reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. The search was conducted on May 8, 2026, in Google Scholar using Publish or Perish version 8, with a limit of the top 300 records. Title–abstract screening, full-text eligibility assessment, and data extraction were carried out by two independent reviewers; disagreements were resolved through consensus. A total of 34 open-access articles in Indonesian or English, published between January 2016 and May 2026 in journals accredited at SINTA 1–4 at the time of the search, were synthesized descriptively and narratively. No formal assessment of methodological quality or risk of bias was conducted. Results--The most publications were found in 2024, at 15 articles (44.1%). The print format accounted for 23 articles (67.6%), the digital format for 10 articles (29.4%), and the combined print and digital format for 1 article (2.9%). The most frequent model was ADDIE, in 14 articles (41.2%), followed by 4D, in 10 articles (29.4%). Flora was the dominant object in 24 articles (70.6%), while biodiversity was the most frequent topic, in 21 articles (61.8%). Conclusion--The findings show that development is concentrated on the print format, flora, and biodiversity in the selected corpus, without establishing the superiority or effectiveness of any product. Diversification of digital functions, objects, and topics needs to be accompanied by adequate evaluation of learning outcomes. The findings are limited to articles captured through the Google Scholar–SINTA search and do not represent the entire research field.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fneur.2026.1931764.title: Routine laboratory biomarker signature combined with machine learning for rapid differentiation of intracerebral hemorrhage from acute ischemic stroke
doi:10.3389/fneur.2026.1931764.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Rapid and reliable differentiation between intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and acute ischemic stroke (IS) is essential for appropriate triage and treatment. We aimed to develop and validate a laboratory-based machine learning model using routine clinical chemistry and hematology parameters to discriminate ICH from IS.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We retrospectively analyzed the clinical and laboratory data of 12,213 hospitalized stroke patients (including 3,251 with ICH and 8,962 with IS) and 2,893 hypertensive controls at Xijing Hospital between 2013 and 2023. A temporal validation cohort comprising 153 ICH and 342 IS patients admitted from January to December 2024 was also established. To address class imbalance, BorderlineSMOTE-2 (BS2) was applied. Candidate variables were screened using three feature selection strategies, including RFECV-ADA, Lasso, and Boruta. Six supervised machine learning models were trained using ten-fold cross-validation. Model performance was evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. Feature importance was interpreted using SHAP analysis. Mendelian randomization and colocalization analyses were performed as exploratory complementary analyses.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Ten routine laboratory parameters were retained for model construction: white blood cell count, neutrophil percentage, cystatin C, uric acid, total protein, potassium, sodium, chloride, fibrinogen degradation product, and D-Dimer. In the test cohort, the final model (BS2_LightGBM_V10) achieved AUCs of 0.926 for discriminating ICH from IS, 0.979 for discriminating ICH from controls, and 0.923 for discriminating IS from controls. For the three-class classification task (ICH, IS, and controls), the overall accuracy reached 79.07%. SHAP analysis indicated that neutrophil percentage, cystatin C, D-Dimer, and total protein were the most influential predictors. Mendelian randomization analysis suggested that uric acid had a potential causal association with the risk of ICH (OR = 1.309), whereas uric acid (OR = 1.0008), cystatin C (OR = 1.0011), and potassium (OR = 1.0040) had potential causal associations with the risk of IS. Colocalization analysis identified 18 genes linked to uric acid in the context of ICH.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A diagnostic model based on ten routine laboratory indicators accurately differentiated ICH from IS. Uric acid may also play a causal role in the pathogenesis of both disorders.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.17559/tv-20251201003176.title: Partial Differential Function Integrated Generative Learning for Reducing Intermittent Message Disseminations in Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks Connectivity
doi:10.17559/tv-20251201003176.abstract: Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks (VANETs) are described by their volatile connections, rapid network dynamics, and frequent neighbor changes. Due to these characteristics, message dissemination is unreliable, and periodic neighbor discovery increases the routing overhead. To provide a reliable solution for this problem, this article proposes a Partial Differential Generative Learning (PD-GL) for a connectivity assessment model. The differential connections between the vehicles are derived using the partial function, followed by the connection probability assessment using generative learning. In this process, the change in network dynamics initiates the partial differential function to verify communication links between the vehicles. This probability assessment is repeated until the maximum driving distance of the vehicle is supported by communication. The change in network dynamics using the GL identifies low probability vehicles to pre-exclude from the communication, reducing the overhead. The proposed PD-GL model improves the message delivery by 13.61% and connection probability by 13.84%. This model reduces the dissemination overhead by 12.68%, connection loss by 13.29%, and dissemination delay by 12.61%, for the maximum acceleration.

doi:10.33619/2414-2948/131/70.title: Feedback as a Component of the Assessment System in Distance Learning
doi:10.33619/2414-2948/131/70.abstract: <jats:p>This article examines feedback as a key component of the student assessment system in a distance learning context. It explores the nature, functions, and role of feedback in ensuring the quality of the educational process, with particular emphasis on its formative, diagnostic, motivational, and corrective functions. The study analyzes the primary forms of feedback implementation within the digital educational environment, such as automated comments, personalized instructor recommendations, online consultations, and peer and self-assessment. It demonstrates that the effectiveness of feedback depends on its timeliness, substance, specificity, accessibility, and focus on the further improvement of learning outcomes. The article identifies key challenges associated with distance assessment, including a lack of comment personalization, delays in instructor responses, technical limitations, information overload, and a decline in student motivation. It argues for the necessity of a systematic combination of automated and personalized feedback, taking into account learning objectives, individual student needs, and the specific characteristics of the academic discipline. The conclusion is drawn that well-structured feedback enhances assessment objectivity, fosters student autonomy and reflection, enables timely adjustments to the learning process, and improves the overall quality of distance education.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fendo.2026.1771964.title: A predictive model for osteoporosis in frail elderly patients with cerebral infarction: an integrated analysis based on machine learning and care-sensitive indicators
doi:10.3389/fendo.2026.1771964.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To identify key risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly patients with frailty and cerebral infarction using three machine learning algorithms—Least Absolute and Selective Operator (LASSO) regression, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Random Forest (RF)—and establish a risk prediction model to provide data support for clinical prevention.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A retrospective study was conducted using clinical data from 120 elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction admitted to our hospital between April 2024 and October 2025. Patients were categorized into an osteoporosis occurrence group (n=41) and a non-occurrence group (n=79) based on medical records indicating osteoporosis development. Clinical data were collected and compared. Risk factors were screened using “overlap-covering” screening with three machine learning methods: LASSO regression, XGBoost, and RF. The intersecting variables were incorporated into a logistic regression model to analyze risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction. Data analysis was performed using R software. RF to screen risk factors using “overlap coverage.” Intersecting variables were incorporated into logistic regression to analyze factors influencing osteoporosis in elderly patients with frailty and cerebral infarction. A nomogram prediction model was developed using R software, internally validated via Bootstrap resampling (1000 iterations), and its predictive accuracy assessed through calibration curves. Clinical utility was evaluated using decision curves.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Significant differences (P &lt; 0.05) were observed between the occurrence and non-occurrence groups in gender, age, affected circulatory system, disease severity, Tilburg Frailty Inventory (TFI) score, Global Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI), Barthel Index, and Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) score. Through machine learning screening using LASSO regression, XGBoost, and RF, five common risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction were identified: age, TFI score, GNRI, Barthel Index, and SAS score as five common risk factors for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction. These were incorporated into a logistic regression model. Analysis revealed that age, TFI score, and SAS score were risk factors for osteoporosis in this population (OR = 1.102, 2.876, 1.177, P&lt;0.05). GNRI and Barthel Index were protective factors (OR = 0.913, 0.838, P&lt;0.05). The Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test yielded χ²=2.345, P = 0.969&gt;0.05, indicating acceptable model fit. Based on the logistic regression results, a risk prediction model for osteoporosis in elderly frail patients with cerebral infarction was constructed using a nomogram. The AUC was 0.955 (95% CI: 0.920–0.991). Calibration curves showed Cox-Snell R² = 0.755 and Nagelkerke R² = 0.546, indicating strong explanatory power and high calibration of the model. The clinical decision curve generally exceeded both extreme curves, demonstrating that the nomogram effectively captured the risk distribution. Nagelkerke R²: 0.546, indicating strong explanatory power and high calibration for the dependent variable. The clinical decision curve generally exceeded both extreme curves, demonstrating that the factors included in the nomogram provide high net benefit for predicting osteoporosis in patients.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Key factors influencing osteoporosis development in frail elderly patients with cerebral infarction include age, TFI score, GNRI, Barthel Index, and SAS score. The risk prediction model constructed using these factors demonstrates predictive value, high calibration accuracy, and clinical utility, providing theoretical guidance for clinical practice.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.21460/sendimasxi2026.v11i1.106.title: A Collaborative Initiative Between a University and a Village to Map the Physical Vulnerabilities of Settlements in the Lembang Fault Zone Using UAV Photogrammetry Through Project-Based Learning in Jayagiri Village
doi:10.21460/sendimasxi2026.v11i1.106.abstract: <jats:p>Jayagiri Village, Lembang Sub-district, West Bandung Regency, is located directly above the Lembang Fault, making it highly prone to earthquakes, yet spatial data on the physical condition of residential buildings remains limited as a basis for vulnerability mapping and disaster mitigation planning. This community service activity aims to document the integration of unmanned aerial vehicle photogrammetry with a Project-Based Learning approach in the Mapping Laboratory course, while also producing spatial data on the physical condition of settlements in RT 04/RW 11 of Jayagiri Village as a foundation for developing a physical vulnerability map of the fault-prone area. The method consisted of three stages actively carried out by students, namely flight operation planning, aerial photographic data acquisition in the field, and data processing into three-dimensional models, orthophoto maps, and digital surface models using photogrammetric processing software, following applicable national technical standards. The results show that students were able to independently complete all stages, from planning to the presentation of the mapping products, demonstrating the successful implementation of the project-based learning approach in bridging theoretical understanding and practical technical skills. The resulting spatial products also proved beneficial to the village as an initial database on the physical condition of settlements that had not previously been available. In conclusion, the integration of unmanned aerial vehicle photogrammetry and project-based learning in this practicum successfully enhanced students' independent learning while making a real contribution to disaster preparedness at the village level, although limitations remain in the merging of data blocks and the completeness of the three-dimensional models, which need to be improved in future learning cycles</jats:p>
doi:10.21460/sendimasxi2026.v11i1.106.venue: Sendimas 2021 - Seminar Nasional Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat

doi:10.4995/muse.2026.26470.title: Responsible integration of generative AI and LLMs in higher education: Empirical insights and a framework for teaching and learning
doi:10.4995/muse.2026.26470.abstract: <jats:p>Generative AI (GenAI) tools are rapidly reshaping university learning environments, yet pedagogical and ethical frameworks have not developed at the same pace as their adoption. Adopting a multidisciplinary approach, this study combines empirical evidence from a survey of 117 undergraduate Engineering and Health Sciences students with the pedagogical perspectives of university lecturers. It examines how students currently use GenAI and how these tools can be meaningfully integrated into teaching and learning. Findings show that students’ first exposure to GenAI is mainly driven by informal social media channels rather than institutional guidance, resulting in uneven and often unguided adoption. The study also identifies a “contradictory profile” in 11% of the sample: students who perceive GenAI use as a form of cheating while also expressing a strong demand for formal training on its academic integration. From the lecturers’ perspective, GenAI offers opportunities to support content creation, assessment design, and instructional workflows, provided that human-led teaching remains central. By integrating observed student behaviors with expert recommendations, this research proposes an ethical framework and practical guidelines for the responsible integration of GenAI in higher education. The study highlights the urgent need for institutional policies that address emerging socio-ethical tensions and ensure that GenAI enhances, rather than circumvents, foundational knowledge, academic integrity, and critical thinking.</jats:p>
doi:10.4995/muse.2026.26470.venue: Multidisciplinary Journal for Education, Social and Technological Sciences

doi:10.5194/gstm2026-4.title: Towards hydrological extreme event monitoring using deep learning-downscaled simulated NGGM and MAGIC data and GRACE(-FO) observations
doi:10.5194/gstm2026-4.abstract: <jats:p>Terrestrial Water Storage Anomalies (TWSA) derived from satellite gravimetry provide a unique, spatially integrated measure of large-scale hydrological conditions and are widely used to characterize basin-scale wet and dry states. However, their applicability to regional hydrological monitoring remains limited by their coarse spatial resolution, which hampers the detection of localized storage anomalies relevant to flood onset, evolution, and groundwater variability.Here, it is investigated an unsupervised deep-learning framework based on convolutional neural networks to enhance the spatial resolution of TWSA products across simulated and real mission scenarios. The method relies on a U-Net architecture driven by ERA5-Land hydro-climatic variables, and is first applied to end-to-end closed-loop simulations of the NGGM and MAGIC next-generation gravity missions. Particular attention is given to 5-daily solutions, which represent a key expected advancement of future gravimetric constellations compared with the monthly solutions currently provided by GRACE(-FO). In this setting, simulated TWSA fields are downscaled from 3° to 1°, while monthly 2° simulations are also considered to assess the framework under GRACE-like temporal conditions. For the syntetic products, the downscaled fields are validated using the ESA Earth System Model 3.0 as the reference signal.Results show that the downscaled products preserve consistency with native gravimetric observations while recovering finer-scale spatial structures. To assess transferability, the same pipeline is applied to real GRACE(-FO) observations, downscaling monthly 3° TWSA products into 1° maps.The framework is also extended to GRACE-derived groundwater storage anomalies (GWSA) over France, downscaled from 0.5° to 0.1° and evaluated against independent in situ groundwater observations.Finally, downscaled synthetic TWSA fields are exploited for extreme-event monitoring using threshold-based indicators derived from climatological anomalies. The analysis assesses whether the increased spatial resolution retains localized anomaly patterns otherwise smoothed at coarse scales, supporting the monitoring of flood-prone conditions.</jats:p>

doi:10.4251/wjgo.122464.title: Deep learning-enhanced peritumoral radiomics predicts early recurrence after hepatocellular carcinoma ablation: A two-center study
doi:10.4251/wjgo.122464.abstract:
<jats:p>BACKGROUND</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Early recurrence (ER) remains a major challenge after ablation therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and is closely associated with poor prognosis. Peritumoral imaging features may reflect tumor microenvironmental alterations related to recurrence. However, the most informative peritumoral range for extracting deep learning (DL) features to predict ER after HCC ablation remains unclear.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>AIM</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To determine the best-performing peritumoral region for predicting ER after HCC ablation using DL features.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>METHODS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This retrospective cohort study enrolled 296 ablation-treated HCC patients from two centers. The patients were divided into a primary cohort (n  = 222) and an external cohort (n  = 74). The 3D ResNet-18 was used to extract DL features from contrast-enhanced computed tomography images of the tumor and the 3-mm, 5-mm, 10-mm, and 20-mm peritumoral regions. ER-related features were selected with least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, recursive feature elimination, and importance ranking. Six machine learning algorithms were used to construct predictive models to determine the region whose features resulted in optimal performance. A combined model incorporating the optimal peritumoral features with clinical imaging features (postoperative neutrophil count, intratumoral necrosis) was also developed. The models were evaluated with receiver operating characteristic curve analysis [including calculation of the area under the curve (AUC)], calibration/decision curve analysis, and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>RESULTS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The 10-mm peritumoral model outperformed both the tumor model and the other peritumoral models, with AUC values of 0.818 (95%CI: 0.802-0.833), 0.804 (95%CI: 0.779-0.829) in the training and internal validation sets, respectively. Incorporation of the clinical features into a combined model with the peritumoral features improved the predictive accuracy further, with AUCs of 0.855 (95%CI: 0.841-0.869), 0.852 (95%CI: 0.832-0.871) and 0.841 (95%CI: 0.811-0.871) in the training, internal and external validation sets, respectively. Calibration curve and decision curve analysis also indicated favorable performance with the combined model. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated that the combined model effectively stratified patients in terms of progression-free survival and overall survival probabilities.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CONCLUSION</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>DL features extracted from the 10-mm peritumoral region showed the best numerical predictive performance for ER in HCC patients after ablation. The combined model demonstrated favorable predictive performance and effectively stratified patients by survival risk and thus could aid in developing personalized treatment strategies.</jats:p>

doi:10.1093/9780198986201.003.0060.title: Getting to Climate Change Adaptation
doi:10.1093/9780198986201.003.0060.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This article covers transdisciplinary knowledge co-production as essential for understanding and dealing with climate change. It brings together key aspects of conceptual discourse for climate adaptation, the diversity of sources of knowledge, approaches, and adaptation pathways for knowledge co-production in order to identify promising possibilities for further development. Transdisciplinary approaches are especially important when Indigenous Peoples are involved, given their unique worldviews and people–nature relationships. As well, relationality and holism, two major distinctive features of Indigenous and local knowledge, are relevant to adaptation. Several potentially useful models, such as bridging, exist to help visualize how Western science and Indigenous and local knowledge can work together. Such knowledge co-production should be context based, pluralistic, goal oriented, interactive, and include attention to political and power dynamics. As well it should be based on trust and mutually respectful, inviting cross-cultural social learning. Climate change is not a smooth and gradual process but tends to involve extreme events (e.g., hurricanes, floods, wildfires), often with disproportional adverse effects upon Indigenous and vulnerable peoples. Attention to justice and equity, the ability to learn from disaster experiences, and to use this learning towards adaptive governance to build resilience are therefore necessary. The diversity of cases shows that there is no one correct formula to approach knowledge co-production: all efforts need to be adaptive to address the dynamics of climate change and disaster risk reduction, dealing with uncertainty that is inherent in complex adaptive systems.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1849699.title: A multicohort proteomics-based machine learning score (MASHPredict) for noninvasive diagnosis and long-term prognostication of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis
doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1849699.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) can progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, yet the invasiveness of liver biopsy limits its clinical utility. Accurate noninvasive diagnostic tools are essential for improved patient risk stratification.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A machine learning study was conducted using plasma proteomics from 142 participants (83 MASH cases, 59 controls) recruited from a Chinese hospital, randomly divided into training and validation cohorts (7:3 ratio). Key proteins were identified via feature selection using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression and the Boruta algorithm. Ten machine learning models were developed to create the MASHPredict score, with external validation in two test cohorts. Prognostic evaluation focused on liver-related events, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD)-related mortality, and all-cause mortality.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>MASHPredict demonstrated robust diagnostic performance, with Area Under the Curve (AUC) values of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.74–0.92) in the training cohort, 0.80 (0.66–0.94) in the validation cohort, 0.79 (0.67–0.91) in test cohort 1, and 0.79 (0.76–0.83) in test cohort 2. It outperformed established noninvasive tests, including the Fibrosis-4 Index, AST to Platelet Ratio Index, AST/ALT Ratio, and NAFLD Fibrosis Score. High-risk individuals exhibited significantly increased hazards for liver-related mortality (HR = 8.18), MASH (HR = 12.07), cirrhosis (HR = 3.37), liver cancer (HR = 3.11), ASCVD-related mortality (HR = 1.64), and all-cause mortality (HR = 1.42) (all p &lt; 0.001).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The MASHPredict score is a validated, noninvasive diagnostic tool with broad applicability. Its superior performance in diagnosing MASH and prognosticating liver-related outcomes supports its potential role in early detection, risk stratification, and clinical decision-making.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.5194/gstm2026-2.title: Learning from ocean bottom pressure differences between GRACE and a state estimate constrained by GRACE
doi:10.5194/gstm2026-2.abstract: <jats:p>Observations from GRACE and its follow-on mission have been used to constrain the ocean bottom pressure (OBP) fields in the state estimates produced by the project for Estimating the Circulation and Climate of the Ocean (ECCO). Here we examine the OBP residuals, i.e., the remaining differences between a recent optimized ECCO solution and the GRACE data, to identify potential issues with both the observations and the ocean model used in ECCO. The GRACE-ECCO residuals are dominated by long-term trends and seasonal variability and exhibit mostly large-scale structures. The trends can be partly related to unmodeled earthquake signals and gravitational, rotational and deformational (GRD) effects on the GRACE-derived OBP fields. Land hydrology processes and associated GRD effects can also contribute to seasonal residuals. In regions of high eddy energy (e.g., Agulhas Retroflection, Gulf Stream), residuals are partly caused by the impact of mesoscale signals on GRACE-derived OBP fields, which is not represented in the coarse-resolution ECCO model.  Other possible contributions to the residuals include uncertainties in glacial isostatic adjustment models and poor horizontal resolution in both data (leakage of land signals in GRACE retrievals) and model (inadequate representation of coastal domains). </jats:p>

doi:10.68414/omvn2247.title: Blockchain-Anchored Detection and Recovery for Resilient Reinforcement Learning-Based Cyber-Physical Systems
doi:10.68414/omvn2247.abstract: <jats:p>Reinforcement learning (RL) controllers in cyber-physical systems (CPS) assume that sensor observations describe the true plant state, yet replay, sensor-drift, and false-data-injection (FDI) attacks can corrupt the observation stream at inference time, and detection alone does not tell the controller what to use after an alarm. This study evaluates a proof-of-concept defense that combines a SHA-256 hash-linked ledger, which provides exact-match replay detection and a tamper-evident recovery anchor, with a Long Short-Term Memory autoencoder (LSTM-AE) for audit alarms and a fixed Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) controller. Ten independently trained policies per environment are evaluated in paired episodes on CartPole-v1 and LunarLander-v3. Content-hash matching detects every injected bitwise replay with zero false matches in 379,396 clean steps. However, perfect detection does not guarantee safe recovery: exact-gated ledger hold raises LunarLander replay return from 178.4 to 264.6 (paired mean +86.2, 95% CI [64.8, 107.6]) but lowers CartPole from 411.1 to 376.2 (−34.9, not significant after Holm adjustment). A trigger-by-anchor factorial ablation shows that local and ledger anchors are control-equivalent under a fixed trigger, while LSTM-AE-gated hold is harmful in every tested cell. A 4,800-episode sensitivity study across three severity levels per attack shows that the recovery effect scales with severity in opposite directions: +5.8 to +225.0 on LunarLander and −4.6 to −60.3 on CartPole. The ledger contributes exact-replay lookup, provenance, and tamper evidence rather than an automatic control advantage; safe general recovery further requires dynamics-aware substitution and distributed, physical validation.</jats:p>
doi:10.68414/omvn2247.venue: Proceedings of the 7th National HBCU Blockchain, Fintech & AI Conference

doi:10.2355/isijinternational.isijint-20.title: Federated Learning of Creep Rupture Time and High Temperature Tensile Strength Prediction Models
doi:10.2355/isijinternational.isijint-20.abstract: Creep testing is time-consuming and costly, leading institutions to limit the number of tests conducted to the minimum necessary for their specific objectives. By pooling data from each institution, it is anticipated that predictive models can be developed for a wide range of materials, including welded joints and degraded materials exposed to service conditions. However, the data obtained by each institution is often highly confidential, making it challenging to share with others. Federated learning, a type of privacy-preserving computation technology, allows for learning while keeping data confidential. Utilizing this approach, it is possible to develop creep life prediction models by leveraging data from various institutions. In this paper, we constructed global deep neural network models for predicting the creep rupture life of heat-resistant ferritic steels in collaboration with eight institutions using the federated learning system we developed for this purpose. Each institution built a local model using only its own data for comparison. While these local models demonstrated good predictive accuracy for their respective datasets, their predictive performance declined when applied to data from other institutions. In contrast, the global model constructed using federated learning showed reasonably good predictive performance across all institutions. The distance between each institution's data was defined in the space of explanatory variables, with the NIMS data, which had the largest dataset, serving as the reference point. The global model maintained high predictive accuracy regardless of the distance from the NIMS data, whereas the predictive accuracy of the NIMS local model significantly decreased as the distance increased.

doi:10.3389/frsus.2026.1767324.title: Learning from degrowth: strengthening circular economy approaches through case studies of plastic packaging and textiles
doi:10.3389/frsus.2026.1767324.abstract: <jats:p>To date, the circular economy (CE) and degrowth literatures have had a substantially separate existence. Whilst a CE is increasingly regarded as a central element of sustainable development, its meaning is far from uniform, with diverse interpretations in both literature and practice. This heterogenous discourse mirrors the tension between green growth, degrowth and post-growth approaches in the wider sustainability debate. Moreover, whilst the idea of a CE has taken a firm hold with policymakers, there are questions regarding its adequacy for the challenges faced, especially in terms of achieving absolute reductions in environmental impacts and positive social outcomes. By contrast, the concept of degrowth calls for significant societal changes to achieve a functioning but smaller and more equitable economy. It is less politically and economically palatable than CE. Degrowth strategies, however, overlap significantly with those favored by some of the CE literature. The potential for these overlaps to support a CE capable of delivering a more sustainable future has received little attention. This paper offers both theoretical and empirical insights by exploring how degrowth and circular economy principles intersect in case studies focused on textiles and plastic packaging. Using integrative literature reviews and empirical data, the case studies assess the extent to which different stakeholders approach the CE, drawing on semi-structured interviews with textile manufacturers in Germany and stakeholders of plastic packaging on the east coast of England. Our analysis finds that the far-reaching socio-ecological transformation towards short-loop options likely necessary for a CE to confront urgent sustainability crises is seldom addressed in the literature and lies beyond the current scope of stakeholders to action or comprehend. We argue that there remains a significant implementation gap between CE and (de)growth policies with an urgent need for analysis of how a transformation of specific sectors could be achieved linking company, networking and policy approaches.</jats:p>

doi:10.64643/ijirt.208438-459.title: How AI Writing Tools Change Student Learning Habits: A Review of Previous Research
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208438-459.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) writing tools are increasingly becoming part of students' learning and academic writing practices.Previous research shows that these tools can help students generate ideas, improve language, revise their work, and receive quick feedback.Recent research on university students has also found that AI-supported writing can improve writing fluency, accuracy, and vocabulary.For example, a 2025 study of IT students learning Russian as a second language reported a 23% increase in essay length, a 31% reduction in language errors, and an improvement in lexical diversity after using AI writing tools with guided learning activities.The study also found that students considered AI useful for improving writing clarity and revision, while concerns about over-reliance and ethical use were also reported.Importantly, 70% of students showed greater awareness of authorship, transparency, and academic integrity.These findings suggest that AI writing tools can support learning when they are used with proper guidance rather than replacing students' own efforts.This review paper examines how AI writing tools are changing student learning habits, particularly in writing, information searching, revision, independent learning, and engagement.It also discusses the benefits, challenges, ethical concerns, and possible effects of excessive dependence on AI.Overall, previous research suggests that responsible and guided use of AI can support students' learning while maintaining critical thinking, creativity, and academic integrity.
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208438-459.venue: International Journal of Innovative Research in Technology

doi:10.64643/ijirt.208499-459.title: Adversarial Robustness of Deep-Learning-Based Near-Field Beam Prediction In XL-MIMO Systems
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208499-459.abstract: Deep learning is increasingly used in sixth generation (6G) extremely large-scale MIMO (XL-MIMO) systems to predict beams directly from channel observations to alleviate the overhead of exhaustive nearfield beam search.However, these channel-based observations also provide an attack surface to learned beam-selection models.In this paper, we consider the adversarial robustness of a deep learning-based nearfield beam predictor for XL-MIMO.We train a fully connected neural network to classify 45 near-field candidate beams generated for a simulated 8x8 planar array and evaluate its vulnerability under the Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) and Projected Gradient Descent (PGD).The beam classification accuracy drops from 74.07%under clean condition to 28.70% under FGSM and 26.11% under PGD at perturbation budget of ε=0.05.Adversarial training improves the respective accuracies to 36.11% and 33.70% while maintaining comparable accuracy on clean data.Specifically, this classification-level degradation does not yield a proportional calculated communication-level impact: the beamforming gain ratio stays close to unity and the derived effective SNR, theoretical BPSK BER and Shannon-based spectral-efficiency estimate only change slightly, with a maximum reported effective-SNR loss of 0.014 dB.Results show that the near-field XL-MIMO beam predictors are vulnerable at the classification level under the input-space threat model considered, while the impact on communication-level is highly dependent on the spatial structure of the beam codebook.
doi:10.64643/ijirt.208499-459.venue: International Journal of Innovative Research in Technology

doi:10.1108/ebhrm-07-2025-0304.title: Fostering innovative work behaviors through high-commitment work systems: the mediating role of ambidextrous learning
doi:10.1108/ebhrm-07-2025-0304.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The main objective of this study is to investigate the relationship between HCWS and innovative work behavior (IWB). For this purpose, we propose a model that examines the interaction between high-commitment work systems (HCWS) and IWBs, with a particular focus on how ambidextrous learning mediates this relationship.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A cross-sectional, non-experimental study was conducted using data from 188 medium and large firms in Ecuador, selected from a national ranking of top-performing companies. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was employed to test the proposed hypotheses.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Contrary to expectations, the direct effect of HCWS on IWB was not statistically significant. However, ambidextrous learning fully mediated this relationship, indicating that HCWS foster innovative behaviors primarily through the development of both exploitative and explorative learning capabilities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes to the HRM and innovation literature by opening the “black box” linking HCWS to IWB. It identifies ambidextrous learning as the key mediating mechanism through which commitment-oriented HR systems translate into employee innovation. By testing this model in an underrepresented Latin American context and demonstrating the robustness of the findings, the study offers valuable insights for both scholars and practitioners seeking to enhance innovation by designing HR systems that activate ambidextrous learning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.1108/ebhrm-07-2025-0304.venue: Evidence-based HRM: a Global Forum for Empirical Scholarship

doi:10.59944/postaxial.v4i3.2095.title: Capacity Building for Village Government Officials Through Non-Formal Education: The Implementation of Computer Training tt PKBM Asoka, Oku, and its Implications for Empowerment Policy
doi:10.59944/postaxial.v4i3.2095.abstract: <jats:p>Capacity building for village government officials is essential for improving governance quality and public service delivery at the village level. The advancement of information technology requires village officials to develop adequate digital competencies to perform administrative tasks effectively, efficiently, and accountably. In this context, non-formal education through computer training can serve as a strategic approach to strengthening officials’ professional capacity. This study aims to analyze the implementation of computer training for village government officials at the Asoka Community Learning Center (Pusat Kegiatan Belajar Masyarakat/PKBM Asoka) in Ogan Komering Ulu (OKU), examine changes in participants’ digital competencies, identify supporting and inhibiting factors, and explore the implications for policies on village official empowerment. This study employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive research design. Data were collected through observations, in-depth interviews, and documentation involving PKBM administrators, instructors, and village officials participating in the training. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate improvements in participants’ practical competencies in operating computer devices, using word-processing and spreadsheet applications, preparing administrative documents, and organizing digital records. These improvements were examined qualitatively by comparing participants’ demonstrated abilities and work practices during training with their initial competencies, as documented through observations, instructor assessments, interviews, and training-related documentation. Participants’ increased ability to prepare official correspondence, manage administrative files, and use office applications suggests that the training strengthened their readiness to perform routine administrative tasks and support public service delivery. However, the extent of improvement varied according to participants’ initial digital literacy, learning motivation, access to facilities, and opportunities for practice. Instructor competence, the relevance of training materials to administrative needs, and post-training assistance also influenced the learning process. Limited facilities, differences in participants’ initial abilities, and the relatively short training period remained significant challenges. These findings suggest that computer training through non-formal education can support the capacity building of village officials when learning outcomes are assessed through observable practical competencies and reinforced through sustained mentoring. Accordingly, empowerment policies should prioritize needs-based training, adequate digital infrastructure, competent instructors, and continuous collaboration among PKBMs, village governments, and local governments.</jats:p>
doi:10.59944/postaxial.v4i3.2095.venue: International Journal of Post Axial: Futuristic Teaching and Learning

doi:10.3389/fenvs.2026.1963502.title: Topology-aware and constraint-guided deep reinforcement learning for climate-resilient control of urban stormwater systems
doi:10.3389/fenvs.2026.1963502.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Urban stormwater systems are increasingly challenged by extreme precipitation events, leading to hydraulic surcharge when system capacity is exceeded. Traditional rule-based control (RBC) is reactive, whereas standard deep reinforcement learning (DRL) does not explicitly exploit drainage‐network topology or ensure physically consistent control. This study introduces Constraint-guided Graph-PPO (PIG‐PPO), a topology‐aware reinforcement learning framework designed to improve stormwater control under extreme precipitation conditions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PIG‐PPO integrates a graph convolutional network (GCN) state encoder with proximal policy optimization (PPO). A soft mass-balance residual penalty is incorporated into the reward function to encourage physically consistent control. The framework was trained on 20 moderate design storms and evaluated on 30 held‐out extreme storms and 20 long‐duration monsoon‐like events. Performance was assessed across 10 independent PPO seeds, with comparisons against RBC and a topology‐agnostic MLP‐PPO ablation. Few‐shot adaptation, cross‐topology validation using a second PyStorms scenario after retraining, and parameter‐count analysis were also conducted.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Across 10 independent PPO seeds, PIG‐PPO reduced mean overflow by 31.2% relative to RBC and reduced the control‐effort metric by 78.3% relative to the MLP‐PPO ablation, with Holm‐adjusted p‐values below 0.001. Few‐shot adaptation reduced overflow during monsoon-like events by 58.8% relative to zero‐shot transfer. Parameter‐count analysis demonstrated a 106.69-fold encoder‐size advantage over a flat MLP at 1,000 nodes. However, this result reflects parameter efficiency rather than direct validation at city scale.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results indicate that topology‐aware state encoding and constraint-guided reward shaping can improve stormwater control performance and support adaptation to previously unseen precipitation regimes. Cross‐topology evaluation provides additional evidence of the framework’s applicability beyond the initial network configuration. Nevertheless, the climate‐resilience implications are limited to performance under synthetic extreme precipitation regimes designed to emulate intensifying rainfall patterns associated with climate change; direct validation against observational climate-projection datasets was not conducted.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.4324/9781003743705-14.title: Integration of Active Learning and Metacognitive Practice into Introduction to Cell and Molecular Biology
doi:10.4324/9781003743705-14.abstract: As a part of my participation in Rethinking Instructional Design for Learning Engagement (RIDLE), I designed my Introduction to Cellular and Molecular Biology course. This is a large enrollment (∼200–400) course that serves as the first course of our year-long general biology series. As a part of the course design, I integrated metacognitive and active learning components into the course. Learners engage in metacognition in the course via pre-class check-in questions and weekly written reflections on the learning process. Learners engage in active learning through paper in-class activities that allow them to derive course content. Following in-class activities learners revisit their in-class work by independently completing a corrections assignment. As a whole, the course design increased in-class time talking about biology and out of class interactions with the course. This course now has a medium level of structure, as compared to the low structure of a traditional lecture course. Increasing course structure has been demonstrated to reduce achievement gaps, specifically for URM and first-generation learners.

doi:10.1108/ejms-03-2026-0046.title: Shaping entrepreneurial mindset through local cultural orientation and multicultural learning: intercultural sensitivity and global thinking orientation as moderators
doi:10.1108/ejms-03-2026-0046.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Universities are increasingly focusing on nurturing students' entrepreneurial spirit, but the culture that fosters it in multicultural academic settings remains under-researched. Drawing on cultural intelligence theory (CIT), a conceptual model is developed that links local cultural orientation (LCO), a multicultural learning environment (MLE) and an entrepreneurial mindset (EM). Further, the moderating effects of intercultural sensitivity (ICS) and global thinking orientation (GTO) on the relationships were explored.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of 624 students in higher education institutions in Southern India. After checking the measurement model, the structural model was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling with Smart PLS 4.1.1.7.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings indicate that (1) LCO and MLE are positively related to entrepreneurial mindset, (2) ICS moderated the relationship between LCO and MLE, (3) GTO moderates the relationship between LCO and entrepreneurial mindset and (4) GTO moderates the relationship between MLE and entrepreneurial mindset. The findings did not show any relationship between LCO and MLE. This study underscores the importance of LCO and MLE in influencing the entrepreneurial mindset.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings contribute to the CIT by illustrating the interaction effects of ICS and GTO in hypothesized relationships. This study provides useful insights for curriculum developers in academic institutions on strategies to develop entrepreneurial mindset among culturally diverse student groups. To the best of our knowledge, the conceptual model developed and tested is the first of its kind, particularly in the context of a large developing country, India.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11095022/v1.title: Investigation of the Performance of Machine Learning Algorithms of Casson-Micropolar Nano Particles Around a Cylindrical Shape: ANN and PINN
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11095022/v1.abstract: Present study deals with a comprehensive analysis of Micropolar-Casson fluid model in two dimensional through a porous cylinder. In order to represent an accurate complex transport scenario encountered in Industrial and engineering applications formulated mathematical model incorporates Joule heating, heat source, mixed convection, chemical reaction and radiation. Convective boundary conditions were assumed. Non-similar transformations were employed to proposed system of nonlinear equations to get ordinary equations. Transformed system of nonlinear differential equations were resolved via two intelligence-based approaches i.e. Physics-informed neural network and artificial neural network. PINN based predictivity is examined at different number of iterations i.e. 1000-20,000. Mean absolute error decays as we increased number of epochs. ANN and PINN based highly authentic and stable solutions compared with BVP4c solutions were obtained. Comprehensive analysis of ANN\PINN and BVp4c shows overlapped, stable, authentic and convergent outcomes at 20,000 epochs. It guarantees efficient, robustness and reliable approach for solving nonlinear system of equations alternate to conventional numerical approaches.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11095022/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.19166/htr.v10i2.11904.title: THE INFLUENCE OF LEARNING ATMOSPHERE, PEER INTERACTION, AND FACILITATOR COMPETENCE ON PARTICIPANT SATISFACTION IN ENGLISH CLUB PROGRAMS
doi:10.19166/htr.v10i2.11904.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates what drives participant satisfaction in community-based English training programs. The English Club Program serves as the research context, designed as an interactive platform to improve English communication skills among university students. Beyond instructional content, program quality is shaped by the learning atmosphere, peer interaction, and facilitator competence. This study therefore examines the influence of these three factors on participant satisfaction. Findings from 169 respondents show that all three contribute positively to satisfaction, with facilitator competence emerging as the strongest predictor. These results underscore the importance of building a supportive and interactive learning environment, guided by competent facilitators, to improve the overall quality of English language training programs.</jats:p>
