doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11096122/v1.title: Machine Learning for Gene-Expression-Based Prediction of Alcohol Use Disorder with an Integrate Web-Based Dashboard
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11096122/v1.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a complex condition associated with molecular alterations in brain regions involved in reward, motivation, and behavioral regulation. Gene-expression profiling can provide valuable molecular information for studying AUD; however, the high dimensionality and correlation structure of transcriptomic data present challenges for predictive modeling and interpretation. This study develops a machine-learning approach for predicting AUD status from gene-expression profiles and introduces GENO, a web-based dashboard designed to support laboratory users in interpreting the resulting predictions. Publicly available bulk RNA-sequencing data from postmortem brain tissue of 114 individuals, including 58 AUD cases and 56 non-AUD controls, were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus repository (GSE253155). Gene-expression data were standardized, and dimensionality was reduced using ANOVA F-test and mutual-information-based feature selection. An Elastic Net logistic regression model was then developed to manage high-dimensional and correlated predictors while maintaining model interpretability. On the held-out test set, the model achieved an accuracy of 86%, an F1-score of 0.865, and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.895. For each input profile, the model generates a probability-based prediction of membership in the AUD class and estimates gene-level contributions to the prediction. GENO integrates this predictive pipeline into a web-based interface that supports data upload, automated analysis, result visualization, and structured report generation. A preliminary task-based usability assessment with laboratory users further demonstrated the feasibility of completing the platform’s primary workflow. These findings provide preliminary evidence that interpretable regularized machine learning can predict AUD status from postmortem gene-expression profiles within the analyzed dataset.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11096122/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1892111.title: Explainable machine learning using pretreatment complete blood count parameters and demographic characteristics for gastric cancer risk stratification: a temporal validation study
doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1892111.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Gastric cancer (GC) is often diagnosed at an advanced stage, while endoscopy is invasive and conventional serum tumour markers have limited sensitivity. A low-cost, widely available tool that can identify patients at higher risk and prioritise them for endoscopic evaluation could therefore strengthen early-detection pathways. The complete blood count (CBC) is routinely available and well suited to such first-contact risk stratification; however, existing CBC-based machine-learning models are often developed in cohorts that mix prevalent, postoperative, on-treatment and surveillance records, potentially confounding the haematological signal. We therefore developed and temporally validated an explainable CBC-based model to stratify the risk of newly diagnosed GC versus benign gastric disease in a rigorously verified, treatment-naïve cohort.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this retrospective single-centre study, 2,044 patients (477 pathologically confirmed, newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve GC and 1,567 benign gastric-disease controls) were assembled through case-by-case chart review, patient-level identity de-duplication and application of the same prespecified comorbidity-screening criteria. The baseline CBC was obtained at admission before treatment. A parsimonious model incorporated six routinely available variables: age, sex, and neutrophil, lymphocyte, monocyte and platelet counts. Eight algorithms were trained using five-fold cross-validation in the training cohort (n = 1,309) and evaluated in a temporally separated validation cohort (n = 735). Random forest was designated as the reference explainable model and interpreted using SHAP. Model behaviour in tumour-marker-negative GC and robustness in sensitivity analyses were also assessed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Discrimination was similar across algorithms. In temporal validation, random forest achieved an AUC of 0.831 (95% CI 0.798–0.864), which was numerically similar to that of the highest-AUC model, XGBoost (AUC 0.832), with substantially overlapping 95% confidence intervals. Random forest had a low Brier score (0.133) and showed positive net benefit across the evaluated threshold-probability range. SHAP identified lymphocyte count, male sex and age as the leading predictors, with an identical feature ranking under XGBoost (Spearman ρ = 1.00). Adding derived inflammatory ratios did not improve discrimination (ΔAUC −0.010, p = 0.139). Among temporal-validation patients with triple-negative GC, defined as CEA-, CA19-9- and CA72-4-negative disease, the model classified 62.7% (95% CI 50.0–73.9) as high risk.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A six-variable model combining pretreatment CBC parameters with age and sex discriminated newly diagnosed GC from benign gastric disease in a temporally separated validation cohort and showed broadly acceptable graphical calibration and a low Brier score. The model classified a substantial proportion of tumour-marker-negative GC cases as high risk, supporting further evaluation as a low-cost pre-endoscopic triage aid. External multicentre validation is required.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

arxiv:2610.22340.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
arxiv:2610.22340.abstract: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model. During inference, the same play policy then guides model-predictive control (MPC) by proposing candidate action sequences for evaluation under the learned world model. To accelerate inference, we also introduce a method for distilling a closed-loop, goal-conditioned policy through self-play within the learned world model. We evaluate this framework on underactuated pushing and any-to-any in-hand pose reorientation with a multifingered hand, in simulation and real world. In real world experiment, our method outperforms hindsight behavior cloning by 69.6% in success rate and achieves comparable success to reinforcement learning with 490 times less interaction data. These results demonstrate that supervised play can autonomously collect interaction data, guide model-based planning, and enable policy learning without any task-specific demonstrations or sim-to-real transfer.

arxiv:2610.22238.title: Query-Efficient Rejection Sampling for Parallel Masked Diffusion
arxiv:2610.22238.abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) accelerate generation by unmasking multiple tokens in parallel, but sampling these tokens independently ignores their correlations and biases the output. Anari et al. (2026) corrected this bias with rejection sampling, decomposing the log acceptance probability into a sum of token-level terms, but the evaluation requires one score query per unmasked token. We propose the Single-Increment Rejection Sampler (SIRS), which provides an estimate of the log acceptance probability from a single randomly sampled increment at the cost of one query. SIRS then converts a Poisson number of clipped estimates into accept/reject decisions through a Bernoulli factory adapted from Chen et al. (2026). Since each query returns the conditionals of all remaining tokens in the block, we further Rao-Blackwellize each increment by averaging over these tokens at no extra cost, thereby reducing clipping. We show that the KL-divergence between the data distribution and the SIRS output is bounded by a clipping term plus the model's training error. With exact scores, parallel decoding pays the full within-block dependence, whereas SIRS pays only the part beyond the clipping range.

arxiv:2610.22230.title: Architecting for Hardware Diversity: Meta's End-to-End Co-Design for High-Performance AI Training on AMD GPUs
arxiv:2610.22230.abstract: Meta deploys a heterogeneous fleet comprising NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and proprietary MTIA accelerators to reduce costs and mitigate vendor lock-in. However, the extensive history of NVIDIA-specific optimizations hinders performance portability to other hardware. This paper presents our methods for optimizing alternative accelerators, using AMD Instinct MI350X versus NVIDIA B200 for recommendation model training as a case study. We propose three reusable principles. First, hardware-model co-design is essential: rather than directly porting models from NVIDIA GPUs, revising model structures and software recipes allows full exploitation of accelerator-specific strengths (e.g., MI350X's 1.6x HBM capacity relative to B200). Second, our analytical performance model enables zero-warmup optimal kernel selection across diverse datatypes and matrix shapes in production models, drastically simplifying tuning. Third, increasingly mature agentic workflows have lowered the barrier to porting from the CUDA ecosystem; we extend these workflows for microarchitecture-aware kernel optimizations and custom shim generation. Compared to the directly ported baseline, these methods deliver up to 1.5x improvement in end-to-end training throughput. To our knowledge, this is the first hyperscaler report on productionizing AMD GPUs for large-scale training. Our contributions have been upstreamed to the open-source PyTorch, Triton, and ROCm ecosystems.

arxiv:2610.22020.title: DemoStream: Batched Task-and-Motion-Plan Optimization for Automated Learning from Demonstration
arxiv:2610.22020.abstract: Learning from demonstration is an effective strategy for endowing robots with manipulation capabilities but requires training on datasets comprised of massive amounts of demonstrations. Existing demonstration collection approaches either require constant human involvement, for example, via teleoperation or are specialized for a single task. Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) systems are able to autonomously solve and therefore generate demonstrations for general-purpose tasks; however, learning from their demonstrations has proven difficult due to multi-modality in their solutions. In this work, we build on recent work leveraging GPU acceleration for TAMP and propose DemoStream, a TAMP system that optimizes demonstration quality in order to improve behavior cloning success rates. First, we introduce batched TAMP sampling operations along with a new TAMP algorithm that correspondingly performs batched constraint satisfaction in order to explore many solutions in parallel. We conduct simulation experiments ablating different action spaces, cost functions, and batch sizes to analyze the effect of these choices on downstream policy success rates. Finally, we show that we can leverage the safety guarantees of TAMP to directly collect real-world demonstrations at an average rate of 66 demos per hour. See our website for policy rollout videos: demostream.github.io.

arxiv:2610.21825.title: Compiling Multi-Threshold Operators for Quantized Non-Monotonic and Fine-Granular Activations in Custom-Tailored DNN Accelerators
arxiv:2610.21825.abstract: Aggressive quantization of neural networks can expose activation functions as bottlenecks for efficient hardware acceleration. Implementing quantized activations as multi-threshold operations has been shown to be a promising optimization, allowing for efficient hardware implementation of few-bit activations. However, current implementations are limited to monotonically increasing functions, quantization schemes with one-dimensional (per-channel) granularity and a small set of predefined activation-quantizer combinations. We formalize the multi-threshold representation to extend it to non-monotonic functions and fine-granular parameters, i.e., multi-dimensional thresholds. For automated conversion of quantized function compositions into threshold representation, we propose a systematic approach via algebraic rules integrated into the ONNX-based compiler infrastructure. We experimentally validate our solution on a selection of monotonic and non-monotonic functions by extending the binary search based multi-threshold operator that is integrated into the FINN framework for end-to-end synthesis of custom-tailored FPGA accelerators. The cost of hardware support for non-monotonicity and fine-granularity is characterized in comparison to an alternative approach utilizing existing operators via graph-level decomposition. We compare our method to prior work as well as the approach taken by the hls4ml framework. As an outlook, we demonstrate the prospects of using the multi-threshold representation during the training of a neural network as a form of quantization aware training.

arxiv:2610.21695.title: ShiftQAT: Quantization-Aware Training for the Numerical Contract of a Fixed-Function Edge CNN Accelerator
arxiv:2610.21695.abstract: Fixed-function CNN accelerators make edge inference fast and energy-efficient, but they execute only networks that obey a precise numerical contract. On the MAX7800x family, this contract requires power-of-two, per-tensor, symmetric scales, 8-bit activations and biases, integer-only arithmetic, and one statically configured shift per layer. We present ShiftQAT, the quantization-aware training (QAT) flow we developed for this family, which produces networks satisfying the contract by construction. It is the default training path of ai8x-training, the family's open-source training toolchain. ShiftQAT resolves residual, concatenation, and weight-sharing dependencies so that activation scales propagate statically and each layer's requantization reduces to one offline-configured shift. It also trains weights and biases on a joint power-of-two grid that fits the 8-bit bias budget. Among the compared methods, only ShiftQAT satisfies all of the contract's scaling constraints, including signed 8-bit activation storage. Even so, on ImageNet it matches the W8A8 accuracy drop of less constrained QAT methods and stays within 2.9 percentage points of FP32 at W4A8. On MAX78002 silicon, ShiftQAT-trained MobileNetV2 and ResNet-18 classify ImageNet images in 14.6 and 8.4 ms at 5.1 and 2.8 mJ per inference.

arxiv:2610.21433.title: ManiFusion: Unlocking the High-Throughput Generation via Superposition in Manifold Space
arxiv:2610.21433.abstract: Diffusion models achieve high-quality image generation but remain computationally expensive due to iterative denoising across many timesteps. Existing acceleration methods mainly reduce per-sample latency, but gains along this axis are becoming saturated. We instead explore an orthogonal throughput-oriented direction by processing multiple samples within a single denoising evaluation. To this end, we propose ManiFusion, a backbone-agnostic framework for multi-sample generation through fused-space computation. ManiFusion jointly processes multiple samples by fusing them before the denoising backbone and separating them afterward through unfusion. We provide a geometric perspective on how multiple samples can share a fused representation while retaining the information needed to guide their individual generation trajectories. To better align fusion allocation with denoising stages, ManiFusion uses Trajectory-Fusion Scheduling (TFS), which dynamically adjusts fusion factors throughout sampling. ManiFusion generalizes across diffusion families, including both U-Net and transformer backbones in pixel and latent spaces. We further show that ManiFusion composes with existing acceleration methods and reaches throughput regimes unattainable by prior approaches with minimal quality degradation.

arxiv:2610.21337.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Need to Complete Every Rollout?
arxiv:2610.21337.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher knowledge to a student through feedback on student-generated rollouts, but generating complete rollouts and computing per-token teacher feedback are computationally expensive. Existing truncation methods save computation by stopping rollouts early. However, they do not compensate for truncated token gradients, which biases the gradient estimates and changes Vanilla OPD's original training objective. Furthermore, their truncation decisions rely on assumptions about supervision quality or criteria that may not generalize across settings. We introduce Stochastic Truncated On-Policy Distillation (STOPD), which accelerates OPD by randomly truncating student rollouts and correcting the resulting sampling bias with blockwise inverse-probability weighting (IPW). At each training step, we sample a stopping position for each rollout before generation and let the student generate until that position or natural termination. We obtain teacher feedback on every generated token and use blockwise IPW to compensate for the lower probability of retaining later tokens while controlling the weights. We prove that this weighting preserves Vanilla OPD's gradient sum in expectation and derive one-step update-error bounds for SGD, Adam, and Muon. We evaluate STOPD across multiple teacher-student model pairs, task domains, and optimizers. STOPD reduces generated tokens by 25-48% while maintaining accuracy comparable to Vanilla OPD, achieving 1.3-2.2x training speedups.

arxiv:2610.21201.title: Hard Way, The Only Way: Provable Merits of Training on Hardest Examples
arxiv:2610.21201.abstract: Despite a surge of empirical interest in the ``unreasonable effectiveness'' of drastic data pruning for AI systems, a unified theoretical understanding of this phenomenon remains elusive. In this work, we provide a precise high-dimensional theory of learning under data pruning via weighted empirical risk minimization (ERM). As in previous work, we analyze a setting where pruning is performed along a one-dimensional subspace of the input space. Our analysis precisely characterizes the limiting test error curves in the regime where the input dimension N and sample size P tend to infinity with a fixed ratio N/P. The resulting theory recovers several recent results in the literature as special cases and provides a general lens to evaluate how pruning strategies interact with the loss function and label noise. Crucially, we characterize the optimal pruning strategy in the high-sample regime where P greatly exceeds N. We demonstrate that strategic pruning can accelerate the decay of classification test error from the classical sqrt(N/P) rate, typical of vanilla ERM with loss functions without exponential tail (e.g., quadratic loss), to the much faster Bayes-optimal scaling of order N/P. In this setup, we prove that, surprisingly, this optimal performance is achieved by a drastic pruning strategy: discarding almost all training data except for a small proportion, consisting strictly of the 2N hardest training examples.

arxiv:2610.21060.title: Bellman-Consistent Trajectory RL for LLM Arithmetic Reasoning
arxiv:2610.21060.abstract: To address sparse terminal rewards in LLM arithmetic reasoning, we propose a Bellman-consistent trajectory RL method. Our framework introduces Trajectory Bellman Residual Minimization (TBRM) to transform sparse rewards into dense token-level signals. We integrate a Reinforce Leave-One-Out (RLOO) group strategy to reduce gradient variance of Bellman residuals and use hindsight goal relabeling to accelerate intermediate learning. Evaluated on the Countdown task, our method alleviates optimization bottlenecks and stabilizes gradient variance significantly better than GRPO. The TBRM-RLOO framework boosts Pass@1 to 0.55--0.64 and achieves a state-of-the-art Pass@16 accuracy of 76.0--84.0\%, outperforming the SFT, IPO/DPO, and RLOO baselines. Our approach demonstrates exceptional single-sample efficiency and successfully circumvents standard performance plateaus via test-time scaling.

arxiv:2610.21020.title: Acceleration and its Limits in Gaussian Variational Inference
arxiv:2610.21020.abstract: We study whether the classical momentum-based acceleration that improves the condition-number dependence of gradient descent from $κ$ to $\sqrtκ$ for strongly convex, smooth objectives extends to Gaussian variational inference (GVI) for strongly log-concave, log-smooth target distributions. With exact Gaussian expectations, a convex composite formulation of GVI yields the classical accelerated $\sqrtκ$ convergence rate. However, when only pointwise derivatives are available, we construct a family of strongly log-concave targets for which any randomized algorithm requires $κ^{1-o(1)}$ queries to achieve a fixed objective accuracy, even when the initial objective gap is bounded independently of $κ$. Thus curvature bounds alone cannot guarantee uniform accelerated total-query complexity. We then ask which additional structure permits acceleration and give positive examples: under a Hessian-Lipschitz assumption, variance-reduced stochastic methods yield accelerated guarantees when the Hessian variation is sufficiently small. Finally, experiments on real datasets show substantial empirical speedups from acceleration across a broad range of methods.

arxiv:2610.20999.title: EigDiff: Eigensample Diffusion - or how to significantly reduce training dataset size with marginal performance variation?
arxiv:2610.20999.abstract: Diffusion models are notoriously expensive to train, requiring large-scale datasets to learn how to gradually reverse the noise from images over multiple small denoising steps. Current approaches focus on distilling the number of diffusion steps, neglecting potential redundancies of the training data. In this paper, we explore the potential of harnessing eigensamples to train diffusion models on significantly smaller datasets, while preserving model performance. To mitigate the sensitivity to affine transformations of eigenimages, we harness the latent space of a pre-trained CLIP model. We next compute latent eigenvectors by performing principal component analysis (PCA) in CLIP space. Further, we employ eigenvectors as reference points to guide the selection of a representative training set comprising comprising both exemplars (images whose embeddings are closest to eigenvectors) and diverse images. Our comprehensive experiments with different diffusion models applied on multiple datasets indicate that our approach (EigDiff) can reduce training data by up to 14x and accelerate subset selection by up to 1607x, with marginal performance differences.

arxiv:2610.20925.title: Planning to Learn: Real-Time Robust Adaptive Control on the GPU with Guaranteed Future Learning
arxiv:2610.20925.abstract: Robust adaptive control is vital for keeping robots safe while actively reducing uncertainty in unfamiliar settings. However, traditional methods are often conservative since they fail to account for guaranteed future parameter learning during planning and struggle to scale to high-dimensional systems. In this work, we present A-SLS, a learning-aware robust adaptive model predictive control (RAMPC) framework based on system-level synthesis. A-SLS forecasts future parameter uncertainty and preserves correlations between process disturbances, parameter error, and estimate updates to construct tight, guaranteed reachable sets that account for future information gain. We also develop a GPU-accelerated A-SLS solver to enable real-time performance. Across nonlinear robotic systems, A-SLS reduces reachable-tube conservativeness, maintains real-time performance, and scales to whole-body control for a quadruped with 61 states, 8 uncertain parameters, and 12 control inputs. We further demonstrate the approach on hardware, where a physical Crazyflie drone learns an uncertain dynamics parameter online to stabilize on the fly.

arxiv:2610.20761.title: Purify Before You Align: Improving Representation Alignment for Diffusion Models
arxiv:2610.20761.abstract: Representation alignment improves and accelerates diffusion training by encouraging intermediate features to match a pretrained visual encoder. However, standard alignment matches pretrained representations without distinguishing what information may be more useful for generation. We introduce local appearance purification (LAP), which improves generation quality and makes encoders such as MAE more effective alignment targets by removing locally predictable content and aligning to the residual. LAP modifies only the alignment target, and requires no changes to diffusion training or inference. Through controlled interventions within a fixed encoder, we show that effective alignment depends on what information the target emphasizes, not simply how much image information it contains. Our theory gives a variational interpretation of standard alignment and, for fixed local predictors, a sum of token-wise information bounds conditioned on local appearance. To understand why purification benefits some encoders more than others, we derive an exact constant-readout test that measures how well the target can be matched without using the diffusion model's hidden state. LAP improves generation quality across five pretrained representations (MAE, AIMv2, CLIP, DINOv2, DINOv3), with the largest gain for MAE: on ImageNet-256 with SiT-B/2, it reduces FID from $53.1$ to $42.3$. Its gains persist with stronger alignment recipes and tokenizers. Computed before diffusion training, the constant-readout score predicts the benefit of purification (Spearman $ρ=0.94$ across 13 encoders).

arxiv:2610.20669.title: Value-Informed Schedule Trimming for Accelerated Sequential Monte Carlo Guidance in Discrete Diffusion
arxiv:2610.20669.abstract: Reward-guided discrete diffusion enables test-time alignment with downstream objectives, but applying Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) guidance at every denoising step is computationally expensive. Active guidance steps require additional reward evaluations and, for gradient-based proposals, value-gradient computations. Sparse guidance reduces this cost by guiding only a subset of timesteps, but commonly used schedules are fixed heuristics whose effectiveness can vary substantially across tasks. We propose VISTA, a training-free method that automatically selects guided timesteps under a fixed budget. VISTA formulates sparse guidance as approximation of the ideal full-guidance probability path and derives an estimable upper bound on \(\ell_1\) path deviation. Using value statistics collected from a small number of full-guidance warmup generations, VISTA optimizes the resulting empirical surrogate exactly via dynamic programming. The warmup generations can be retained as model outputs, and after schedule selection VISTA has the same per-generation guidance complexity as other sparse schedules with the same budget. Across text, biological sequence, and image generation tasks, VISTA discovers task-dependent schedules and outperforms hand-designed sparse schedules in most tested settings, while approaching or exceeding full-guidance performance on several task metrics. In toxic-text generation, for example, VISTA attains a 0.99 unique-toxic ratio compared with 1.00 for full guidance while reducing post-selection per-generation latency from 204.23 s to 38.16 s, a 5.35$\times$ speedup.

arxiv:2610.20655.title: Global-in-time Spectral Duhamel-Picard Method for Post-Exposure Bake Simulation and Physics-Informed Neural Operators for EUV Lithography
arxiv:2610.20655.abstract: We present a global-in-time spectral Duhamel-Picard method with polynomial expansions for post-exposure bake (PEB) simulation. The coupled acid-quencher reaction-diffusion equations are reformulated as nonlinear Volterra integral equations using the Duhamel principle. Full trajectories are represented by finite polynomial expansions, with temporal coefficient fields determined over the bake interval by Anderson-accelerated Picard iteration, thereby avoiding sequential time marching. In 3-D PEB simulations, we employ Chebyshev and Legendre temporal bases while evaluating the Duhamel integrals using the corresponding Gaussian quadrature rules. We demonstrate that the proposed method simulates a large domain of $1200\times1200\times100$ voxels on the order of one minute. The representation is further incorporated into a physics-informed neural operator (PINO) with a mixed-transform variant of a factorized Fourier neural operator, which is trained without precomputed solution trajectories. Together, the integral formulation and its PINO extension enable accelerated, time-marching-free prediction of concentration fields at arbitrary times within the bake interval.

arxiv:2610.20894.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent: A Nonlinear Time Series Perspective
arxiv:2610.20894.abstract: This paper investigates the statistical behavior of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) with constant step size under the framework of iterated random functions. Compared to previous studies establishing the convergence of SGD in probability measure, e.g., Wasserstein distance, our approach directly provides the convergence in Euclidean distance by showing the Geometric Moment Contraction (GMC) of SGD. This new convergence can address the non-stationarity of SGD due to fixed initial points and can provide a more refined asymptotic analysis of SGD. Specifically, we prove quenched central limit theorem, invariance principle and $α$-stable convergence for averaged SGD (ASGD) regardless of initialization. Furthermore, we provide a novel perspective to understand the impact of step sizes in SGD by studying its derivative with respect to the step size. The existence of stationary solutions for the derivative processes is shown, enabling the use of interpolation to recover the full-trajectory of SGD. Subsequently, we utilize multiple step sizes and show an enhanced Richardson-Romberg extrapolation with improved bias representation, which brings ASGD estimates closer to the global optimum. Finally, we propose a new online inference method and a bias-reduced variant for the extrapolated ASGD. Empirical confidence intervals are constructed and the coverage probabilities approach the nominal level as $n$ grows.

doi:10.48550/arxiv.2610.14280.title: DFIT: A Framework for Building Instrumentation Tools Across Heterogeneous Dataflow Accelerators
doi:10.48550/arxiv.2610.14280.abstract: Emerging dataflow accelerators offer exceptional energy efficiency and throughput for machine learning workloads, yet remain largely opaque to developers for performance analysis. Unlike CPUs and GPUs, where instrumentation frameworks enable fine-grained introspection, dataflow hardware exposes little information. This lack of transparency limits the ability of compiler engineers, system designers, and application developers to analyze, tune, or debug accelerator behavior. In this paper, we introduce DFIT (DataFlow Accelerator Instrumentation Tool), an instrumentation framework designed specifically for dataflow architectures. DFIT directly instruments operations, regions, and compiler transformations at the graph IR and backend-lowering stages using semantic program representation. DFIT captures high-level, semantically meaningful data that reflect the true dataflow of computation. These data can be exported for visualization and analysis. Our approach demonstrates how instrumentation can be generalized beyond traditional hardware to support heterogeneous architectures, providing portability without modifying tool logic. By opening the black box of dataflow execution, DFIT establishes a foundation for new classes of performance analysis tools for AI accelerators. It provides a practical path toward reproducible, architecture-aware introspection across heterogeneous systems, bridging the long-standing visibility gap between compiler design, runtime scheduling, and hardware realization. Evaluation across Cerebras, SambaNova, and TPU shows practical overhead of 3.53%-13.62% across instrumentation modes with robust cross-platform portability.

doi:10.48550/arxiv.2610.16164.title: ML-Assisted Power Side-Channel Attacks on ML Accelerators in Shared FPGAs
doi:10.48550/arxiv.2610.16164.abstract: Cloud providers offer on-demand access to Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs), and multi-tenant FPGAs let multiple users share one device to improve utilization. This sharing introduces security risks: an adversary co-located with a victim on the same FPGA can mount power side-channel attacks against the victim's Machine Learning (ML) accelerator. Prior on-chip attacks on such accelerators based on Time-to-Digital Converter (TDC) sensors have recovered only small, MNIST-scale grayscale inputs, including with ML-assisted reconstruction. This work is the first on-chip, TDC-based attack to produce full-scale color reconstructions of ImageNet-scale inputs, by combining ML-based upscaling and recoloring with TDC measurements of a remote victim's ML accelerator. We frame this as a proof-of-concept leakage study: the victim implements the first convolution layer of a CNN processing 224x224 ImageNet inputs on a shared FPGA, which we isolate to characterize the input-dependent leakage, and we quantify how much of each reconstruction reflects genuinely recovered information versus ML-generated post-processing. As a preliminary countermeasure, we study a pixel-substitution defense that replaces each pixel value, within a fixed intensity budget, with one of different Hamming Weight, producing a different TDC signature. We find that this transformation costs the victim's own model more accuracy than it costs the attacker and, because it applies the same fixed, publicly reconstructable mapping to every image, is largely defeated by an attacker retrained on the transformed data; robust defenses will require randomized or input-dependent transformations.

doi:10.29303/goescienceed.v7i4.3491.title: Pengaruh Discovery Learning Berbantuan Edpuzzle terhadap Pemecahan Masalah Siswa SMA
doi:10.29303/goescienceed.v7i4.3491.abstract: <jats:p>Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh model discovery learning berbantuan Edpuzzle terhadap pemecahan masalah siswa pada materi gelombang bunyi di kelas XI SMA, dengan metode kuasi eksperimen pretest-posttest control group design. Populasi penelitian seluruh siswa kelas XI MAN 2 Model Medan. Sampel penelitian terdiri dari 2 kelas. Kelas XI F1B  sebagai kelas eksperimen menggunakan model discovery learning berbantuan Edpuzzle dan XI F1C sebagai kelas kontrol menggunakan model discovery learning, masing- masing kelas berjumlah 30 siswa. Teknik pengambilan sampel secara cluster random sampling. Instrumen penelitian terdiri dari tes pemecahan masalah yang sudah valid. Instrumen penelitian pemecahan masalah terdiri dari 9 soal berbentuk uraian. Hasil pretest dan posttest pemecahan masalah kelas eksperimen 36,10 dan 76,96, kelas kontrol 34,04 dan 51,86. Data dianalisis menggunakan uji manova dan N-gain dengan syarat data berdistribusi normal dan homogen. Hasil uji manova diperoleh ada pengaruh yang signifikan dengan penerapan discovery learning berbantuan Edpuzzle terhadap pemecahan masalah siswa. Peningkatan N-gain kelas eksperimen pemecahan masalah 0,66 kategori sedang dan kelas kontrol 0,26 kategori rendah.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11381470/v1.title: Predictive Multi-Objective Energy--Latency Optimization in Cloud Environments Using Ensemble Learning
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11381470/v1.abstract: The trade-off between energy consumption and communication latency in cloud data centers is strongly coupled and nonlinear, making static or single-objective policies wasteful or unsafe. We present a predictive multi-objective framework that learns surrogate models of server energy and queueing latency from production traces and uses them to select energy-aware operating points. Targets are generated by physically grounded power and queueing maps, yielding a trace-driven emulation validated against those maps. On public Bitbrains traces of seven virtual machines at five-minute resolution, 60.3 percent of intervals lie at or beyond the 0.95 stability threshold. Within the stable envelope, linear regression collapses on latency (R-squared 0.565), while ensembles reach at least 0.986 and cut error by up to 90.5 percent with inter-fold deviations below 0.014. A gradient-boosting controller cuts energy by 72.4 percent versus peak speed and 58.9 percent versus reactive scaling at zero violations and 0.29 s mean latency, against 3.80 percent violations for energy-only minimisation, holding the 99th percentile at 1.25 s. Savings stay at 64.8--73.3 percent under parameter perturbations and 72.8 percent leave-one-machine-out, showing generalisation beyond a single trace.

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1944779.title: Academic buoyancy and engagement in EFL learning: a latent growth curve modeling analysis of their dynamic relationship
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1944779.abstract: <jats:p>Grounded in the conservation of resources theory, this 16-week longitudinal study tracked the developmental trajectories of academic buoyancy and learning engagement among college-level English-as-a-foreign-language (EFL) learners in China via repeated questionnaire administrations. Employing latent growth curve modeling (LGCM), this research analyzed changes in both constructs and explored developmental associations between academic buoyancy—a core personal learning resource—and engagement over time. Key findings include: (1) Both academic buoyancy and learning engagement exhibited overall upward trends across the semester, with substantial individual variability observed in initial states and growth rates; (2) Higher latent intercept of academic buoyancy correlated with greater subsequent growth in this construct, whereas the initial state of learning engagement showed no significant association with its own developmental trajectory; (3) The latent intercept of academic buoyancy was positively associated with both the intercept and growth rate of learning engagement, while growth in academic buoyancy aligned with parallel growth in engagement. This study illuminates the dynamic, malleable nature of academic buoyancy and learning engagement in EFL contexts and illustrates the value of LGCM for examining developmental patterns in second language acquisition research.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fdgth.2026.1791066.title: Do machine learning models really encode cross-cultural lifestyle-health differences? A leakage-free reanalysis of two university cohorts in India and Japan
doi:10.3389/fdgth.2026.1791066.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Machine-learning (ML) studies increasingly compare feature-importance rankings between small, unevenly sized cohorts and interpret the differences as evidence of culturally specific “risk architectures.” We show that such comparisons can be highly misleading without leakage-free evaluation, using a worked example from our own cross-sectional lifestyle and health data collected during June-August 2024 from two universities in India and Japan. Three problems were identified in our preliminary analysis: (1) an outcome (obesity, defined as BMI ≥ 25) that was tautologically predicted by including BMI itself as a model input; (2) model evaluation without a held-out test set; and (3) feature-importance comparisons that ignored sampling variability from an eightfold difference in cohort size.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We addressed each problem using penalized logistic regression, Random Forest, and gradient-boosted trees with proper train/test splitting, held-out permutation importance, and bootstrap confidence intervals. We also ran a sensitivity analysis that repeatedly subsampled the Indian cohort down to the size of the Japanese cohort.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Removing body mass index (BMI) as a predictor collapsed obesity-model discrimination from perfect (AUC = 1.00) to chance level (AUC = 0.50-0.57), confirming that the BMI-obesity association was definitional rather than empirical. Held-out predictive performance for the remaining viable outcome, elevated self-rated stress, was modest at best (AUC 0.49-0.71). Critically, in the subsampling analysis, every feature-importance value observed in the actual Japanese data fell within the range produced by sample-size noise alone.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We present this analysis as a transparent, reproducible case study of specific, checkable pitfalls: label leakage, missing train/test evaluation, unadjusted small-sample comparison, and mislabeled psychometric instruments. These should be routinely screened for before ML feature importance is interpreted as evidence of population-level or cultural differences in digital health research.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1142/s0218539326500531.title: Intelligent Maintenance of Ship Lubricating Oil System by Integrating Dynamic Bayesian Network and Deep Learning Model
doi:10.1142/s0218539326500531.abstract: <jats:p>The ship lubrication system is susceptible to multiple influencing factors—including temperature, pressure, oil quantity, and oil quality—under complex operating conditions, leading to nonlinear fault evolution patterns that make traditional monitoring methods inadequate for timely and accurate early warning. To address these challenges, this study proposes an intelligent maintenance model integrating an improved Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN) with a Convolutional Neural Network-based Bidirectional Gate Recurrent Unit (CNN-BiGRU). The approach enhances system evolution modeling capabilities through optimized dynamic state transition mechanisms, utilizes CNN-BiGRU to extract multivariate time-series features, and combines probabilistic inference for abnormality detection and risk assessment. Experimental results on the Open Ship Machinery Data Set (SMD) and Oil Analysis Data Set (OAD) demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an F1-score of 95.52% and an AUC of 0.971, outperforming multiple competing models. Furthermore, the model exhibits superior early warning performance and stability under various abnormal operating conditions and load fluctuations. These findings confirm that the proposed methodology significantly improves fault monitoring accuracy and intelligent maintenance efficiency for ship lubrication systems, providing robust technical support for reliable equipment operation under complex environments</jats:p>
doi:10.1142/s0218539326500531.venue: International Journal of Reliability, Quality and Safety Engineering

doi:10.1108/jwl-10-2025-0346.title: AI-enabled HR practices and agile talent deployment: the role of trust in AI and digital culture climate
doi:10.1108/jwl-10-2025-0346.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled human resource (HR) practices foster agile talent deployment within startup firms, particularly highlighting the mediating role of trust in AI and the moderating influence of digital culture climate.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Drawing on self-determination theory, the authors propose and empirically test a moderated mediation model using data collected from a three-wave, multisource survey of 298 employees working in three technology-oriented startups in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Structural equation modeling was used to examine the measurement and structural models and to test the hypothesized relationships among AI-enabled HR practices, trust in AI, digital culture climate and agile talent deployment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Results reveal that AI-enabled HR practices positively influence agile talent deployment through increased employee trust in AI. In addition, the mediated relationship is stronger within organizations characterized by a robust digital culture climate, indicating that a digitally supportive organizational context enhances the effectiveness of AI-enabled HR initiatives.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper advances AI-enabled human resource management research by framing trust in AI as a mechanism translating supportive, transparent HR systems into agile talent deployment rather than technology acceptance. It identifies digital culture climate as an enactment condition enabling trust to become adaptive action. Practically, HR leaders should align explainable AI, trust-building practices and digital norms to strengthen workforce agility.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.64823/ijstm.2601002.title: AI-Enabled Wearable Sensor Technologies for Athlete Performance Monitoring: A Critical Review of Signal Processing, Machine Learning, and Real-Time Embedded Systems
doi:10.64823/ijstm.2601002.abstract:
<jats:p>Abstract
Wearable sensing and artificial intelligence (AI) are increasingly being used to quantify athlete movement, physiological response, training load, and recovery in field and laboratory settings. However, the practical value of these systems depends not only on the predictive capability of an algorithm but also on sensor validity, signal quality, hardware constraints, real-time processing, and the transferability of models across athletes and sports. This review examines the technical pipeline linking wearable electronic sensors to athlete-monitoring decisions, with particular attention to inertial measurement units, global navigation satellite systems, photoplethysmography, electrocardiography, electromyography, pressure sensing, and multimodal systems. It synthesizes evidence on signal conditioning, segmentation, feature engineering, classical machine learning, deep learning, sensor fusion, edge inference, and embedded implementation. Existing reviews indicate that wearable devices can support useful monitoring, but accuracy varies by metric, device, movement pattern, and validation setting; performance under controlled conditions should not be assumed to generalize to competition. Key challenges include motion artifacts, inconsistent protocols, small and imbalanced datasets, leakage between training and test sets, limited external validation, battery and communication constraints, privacy, and unclear decision thresholds. The review proposes a layered reference architecture and a validation framework that links engineering performance to sport-specific usefulness. Future research should prioritize synchronized multimodal datasets, athlete-independent testing, interpretable and uncertainty-aware models, energy-efficient edge AI, secure data governance, and transparent reporting. The article’s contribution is an engineering-oriented synthesis that connects sensor physics and embedded constraints with the needs of physical education and sports science.
Keywords: Inertial Measurement Units; Physiological Sensing; Sensor Fusion; Edge Computing; Sports Biomechanics

Keywords: edge computing; Keywords: Inertial Measurement Units; Physiological Sensing; Sensor Fusion; Sports Biomechanics</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-1393-9.ch004.title: Deep Learning Methods for Video Classification and Tagging
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-1393-9.ch004.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter aims to provide an overview of deep learning methods for video classification and tagging. Videos contain not only spatial but also temporal information, making it more complex than static image data. Firstly, the chapter will introduce the basic concepts of video classification, video tagging, single-label classification, multi-label classification and challenges of video data. Secondly, the main part of the chapter will review major deep learning architectures used for video understanding, including CNN-based methods, CNN-RNN models, 3D CNNs, two-stream networks, SlowFast networks, video transformers, and self-supervised learning and discuss multi-modal learning methods that combine visual, audio, textual, and metadata features for more effective video tagging. Finally, the following evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, etc. will be introduced in this chapter. Moreover, practical use cases in education, surveillance, intelligent transportation systems, social media, and digital content management will be discussed.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4488-9.ch002.title: Pedagogical Wellness, Meaning-Centered Learning, and Learning as Becoming
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4488-9.ch002.abstract: <jats:p>Student persistence and retention are shaped by complex factors. Although existing retention frameworks emphasize institutional support, less attention has been given to the classroom as a site where students construct meaning, identity, and purpose. This chapter proposes a conceptual model connecting Pedagogical Wellness, Meaning-Centered Learning Design, and Learning as Becoming to student persistence and retention. Pedagogical Wellness addresses the conditions that support well-being and engagement; Meaning-Centered Learning Design focuses on intentionally creating meaningful, relevant, and connected learning experiences; and Learning as Becoming provides a developmental lens for understanding how students interpret those experiences and develop as learners. Four pedagogical dimensions illustrate the model in practice: identity-reflective practices, co-constructed and collaborative learning, assessment as meaning-making, and iterative feedback. The model proposes that pedagogical conditions may influence meaning-making and development and contribute to persistence and retention.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4488-9.ch002.venue: Transforming Student Persistence in Higher Education

doi:10.3389/fcimb.2026.1935756.title: Systemic immune dysregulation and local barrier failure as predictors of septic shock in acute appendicitis: a large-scale multicenter interpretable machine learning study
doi:10.3389/fcimb.2026.1935756.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The transition from localized acute appendicitis to systemic septic shock is driven by complex immune and metabolic dysregulation combined with anatomical barrier failure. Accurately predicting early hemodynamic deterioration remains clinically challenging. This study aimed to develop an interpretable multimodal machine learning model by integrating systemic immunological profiles with local sonographic characteristics.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This multicenter cohort study included 3000 patients with acute appendicitis. Following rigorous data reduction using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, eight supervised machine learning algorithms were constructed. The optimal predictive algorithm was comprehensively evaluated across training, internal testing, and independent external validation cohorts. The SHapley Additive exPlanations framework was utilized to provide transparent model interpretability, and the final algorithm was deployed as a dynamic digital calculator.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Six independent predictors were identified, including the Systemic Immune Inflammation Index, C-reactive protein to albumin ratio, glucose to lymphocyte ratio, Prognostic Nutritional Index, periappendiceal fluid, and the sonographic loss of the submucosal echogenic layer. The Random Forest model demonstrated the highest discriminative performance among the evaluated algorithms, achieving an area under the curve of 0.914. The model’s discrimination, calibration, and decision-analytic performance were consistently evaluated in the internal testing and external validation cohorts. SHAP analysis indicated that systemic inflammatory indices and sonographic features reflecting local disease severity made important contributions to the model’s predicted risk of septic shock. These findings should be interpreted as predictive associations rather than evidence of biological causality or synergy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This multicenter study developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for early risk stratification of septic shock. The publicly accessible calculator may support individualized risk assessment; however, prospective impact evaluation is required to determine whether its clinical implementation facilitates earlier resuscitation or improves patient outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.3389/fcimb.2026.1935756.venue: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11253630/v1.title: A Two-Population Delayed Evolutionary Game with Bayesian Learning for Cyber Defense
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11253630/v1.abstract: Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) exploit detection latency, yet evolutionary models of cyber defense typically assume instantaneous adaptation. We formulate a two-population evolutionary game where defenders observe the attacker mix (aggressive vs. stealthy) only through a delayed Poisson alert stream, filtered via a Bayesian approach. The mean-field limit of this Kalman--Bucy filter is a belief equation whose gain $\kappa$ grows with sensor coverage. This model couples two replicator equations and the filter through a detection delay $\tau_d$ and a remediation delay $\tau_r$. For $\tau_r=0$, we prove a closed-form detection-delay threshold $\tau_d^*(\kappa)$ where the interior Nash equilibrium undergoes a Hopf bifurcation, supercritical throughout the parameter ranges examined, leading to recurrent attacker--defender cycles. When attacker adaptivity exceeds congestion damping, stability requires a minimum learning speed regardless of latency. With both delays present, a moderate remediation lag can non-additively enlarge the admissible detection delay. A semi-empirical calibration on 303,220 incidents from Microsoft's GUIDE dataset estimates the learning speed at $0.07$ per day for a single organization, rising to $3$ per day for pooled telemetry, multiplying the admissible detection delay by $1.3$--$2.4$ when $m/b^2=0.6$. Incident-management logs (ServiceNow, BPIC~2013) show congestion relaxation takes 3--6 days, placing incident queues close to the remediation threshold when accounting for heavy-tailed resolution times. The classical threshold is recovered as the frozen-attacker limit.

doi:10.1108/eisfl-06-2026-0103.title: From pedagogical intention to ecosystem readiness: multi-stakeholder evidence on integral learning innovation in Colombian primary schools
doi:10.1108/eisfl-06-2026-0103.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how teaching practices, student experience, family support and institutional conditions align to sustain future-oriented integral learning in primary education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A convergent mixed-methods secondary analysis was conducted using an anonymised dataset from three Colombian primary schools. The quantitative strand calculated instrument-specific descriptive summaries, while the qualitative strand synthesised pre-assigned multilabel themes from de-identified records. A school-by-dimension joint display distinguished cross-method convergence from cross-stakeholder and within-stakeholder/self-report consistency, while also retaining complementarity, divergence, single-source findings, absence of evidence and source asymmetries.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Across the three cases, the same EESSAX-18 form yielded generally favourable student self-reports; teacher and family records were also favourable within their respective instruments. Mixed-source integration nevertheless identified contextual constraints in resources, ICT, monitoring and school-family communication. Because leadership evidence comprised only six records from non-equivalent instruments, evidence on institutional implementation conditions was treated as a limited contextual signal and interpreted alongside teacher, qualitative and documentary sources rather than as a cross-school estimate. The integrated pattern indicated that favourable pedagogical intention could coexist with constraints in enabling ecosystem conditions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study contributes a preliminary, traceability-oriented analytical framework for integrating heterogeneous multi-stakeholder evidence while preserving source-specific limits and asymmetries. Practically, the framework can help schools identify misalignments among teaching practice, student experience, family support, institutional implementation conditions and socio-emotional and values-based learning before selecting improvement actions. It contributes situated evidence from Latin American primary education on how schools may move from valuable practices to sustainable integral learning innovation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.1108/eisfl-06-2026-0103.venue: Education Innovations: Systems and Future Learning

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-1393-9.ch005.title: Automated Video Classification and Annotation Using Deep Learning
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-1393-9.ch005.abstract: <jats:p>The explosion in video content generated through surveillance, streaming, social media, and scientific research is driving the need for large-scale automated video classification and annotation frameworks. The rise of deep learning algorithms has been the solution, advancing from simple CNN algorithms that use only frame information to 3D CNNs, two-stream models, recurrent architectures, and transformer algorithms. This chapter provides an organized survey of deep learning techniques used in video understanding, including major datasets, benchmarks, evaluations techniques, and applications in surveillance, healthcare, sport analysis, media indexing, and autonomous systems. Some of the current issues associated with video understanding using deep learning algorithms include computational efficiency, temporal modeling, lack of annotations, domain adaptation, explainability, and fairness.</jats:p>

                        </mml:mrow>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    ) confirming hypoxic exposure. Participants completed eight standing conditions designed to manipulate visual, vestibular, and somatosensory inputs. For each condition, 15 postural sway measures were extracted from center of pressure signals. Statistical analysis indicates that hypoxia-induced changes in postural stability are multidimensional and are most detectable under conditions that increase sensory integration demands, particularly foam based and tandem stance tasks. Moderate hypoxia increased sway variability and disrupted automatic postural control, whereas more severe hypoxia under complex task conditions elicited a constrained motor strategy. In the machine learning approach, four tree-based ensemble classifiers, including Extra Trees, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Decision Trees, and XGBoost, were employed for altitude classification using the selected postural sway features. A feature-selection framework using Extra Trees feature importance and participant-grouped nested cross-validation was implemented. The optimized Extra Trees classifier achieved the highest accuracy of 70% using 27 selected features. The selected features highlighted the contribution of specific sway characteristics that were not fully captured by conventional univariate metrics. These findings show that moderate hypoxia, in sensory challenging environments, induces detectable multidimensional postural instability before the onset of conventionally recognized symptoms. Our results highlight the importance of task selection and multivariate analysis for detecting subtle impairments. These findings have potential applications in aerospace environments.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.17759/cpse.2026000002.title: Psychological support for students with disabilities in home-based learning: results of an applied study
doi:10.17759/cpse.2026000002.abstract: <jats:p>Context and relevance. In the context of modern education, the importance of psychological assistance to students with disabilities (SWD) who are educated at home is increasing (Articles 41, 273 of the Federal Law, 2012/12/29). In the regions of the country, there is a high proportion of students with SWD who are educated at home. Objective: to analyze the results of a survey of educational psychologists providing psychological assistance to students with disabilities at home. Hypothesis. In the structure of psychological assistance for children with disabilities at home, work on the diagnosis and treatment of cognitive and emotional disorders predominates, while the social aspect (communication development, social adaptation) is underrepresented and is considered secondary by specialists. Psychological assistance for the reintegration of students into the school community is not systematic: activities are fragmented, there is a lack of unity between diagnostic, correctional-developmental, and assessment components, and there is weak interdisciplinary coordination and little coherence among participants in the educational process. Methods and materials. A survey of 415 educational psychologists working in inclusive schools with students with disabilities receiving education at home from 7 regions of the Russian Federation based on a questionnaire of 10 closed and 1 open questions. Results. Only slightly more than a third of educational psychologists (37%) work directly with children; 63% limit themselves to consulting with parents or teachers. A third of specialists discuss strategies for a child's transition to school during consultations. The main challenges faced by students with disabilities (on average by educational level) addressed by educational psychologists are cognitive (29.4%), emotional-volitional (26.2%), social-adaptive (15.7%), and communicative (18.4%). Conclusions. Age-related dynamics were identified: behavioral issues predominate in the younger grades, while motivational and career-related issues predominate in the older grades. The need for a systemic, two-stage model of psychological support is discussed.</jats:p>

doi:10.1002/aur.70381.title: Establishing Diagnosis Models for Autism Spectrum Disorder With Auditory Brainstem Response Using Machine Learning Methods
doi:10.1002/aur.70381.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study aimed to develop and validate models built using machine learning methods for the diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). A total of 851 children with suspected ASD were enrolled. Related features were acquired using the Autism Behavior Checklist and Auditory Brainstem Response (ABR) outcomes. The Shapley additive explanation (SHAP) values were used to explain the feature impact used in the models with the best performance. In addition, different methods were used to depict group differences. Our study found that significant results in ABR outcomes among children with different phenotypes mainly depend on stimulation intensity. The predominant finding is that signal conduction from the cochlear nerve to the inferior colliculus in children with ASD may be associated with autistic behaviors in a way that displays region‐specific (e.g., cochlear nerve, olivary) and intensity‐dependent (e.g., 45, 65 dB) complexity. The XGBoost models outperformed the other candidates, with the highest prediction accuracy (85.9%) and AUROC (0.779). Wave III and V were identified as the features with largest impact. These findings highlight atypical ABR patterns in ASD and their association with autistic behaviors, contributing to the growing literature on understanding alterations in bioelectrical performance in children with ASD.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4508-4.ch003.title: Technological Tools to Support Mathematics Learning in Students With Specific Learning Disabilities
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4508-4.ch003.abstract: <jats:p>Students with specific learning disabilities face challenges in literacy skills; consequently, they experience learning difficulties in math, ranging from mild to severe, and need remedial support. Students with specific learning disabilities have difficulty with tasks ranging from memorizing basic number facts to applying abstract reasoning skills, solving word problems, and making inconsistent calculations. If not addressed early, these difficulties may result in students having difficulty understanding numerical concepts that would help them integrate into everyday situations. The main purpose of this book chapter is to provide an overview of instructional technologies that support mathematics learning for students with specific learning disabilities.</jats:p>
