doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1943572.title: A global machine learning framework for classifying national CO2 emission levels: responsible and explainable artificial intelligence for sustainable climate governance
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1943572.abstract: <jats:p>We investigate whether trade openness, governance, environmental taxation and selected macroeconomic indicators can classify the contemporaneous CO2 emission level of countries observed over 2000 to 2023, using data from the World Development Indicators and the OECD. CO2 emissions per capita are divided into three ordinal levels, low, medium and high, using tertile cut points estimated on the training data only within every validation split. Four classifiers, Random Forest, XGBoost, a support vector machine and a multinomial logistic regression, are tuned and compared alongside two models designed specifically for ordinal outcomes, an ordered logistic regression and an ordinal decomposition of XGBoost, under four validation designs: a country grouped holdout and country grouped 5 fold cross validation, in which no country appears in both the training and test sets; a chronological holdout; a 1 year ahead forecasting task; and a random stratified country year split, retained only as a reference point. Under country grouped cross validation, no classifier achieves a decisively higher accuracy than the others: nested cross validation gives a mean accuracy of 0.644 for XGBoost, 0.648 for Random Forest, 0.671 for the support vector machine, 0.674 for the multinomial logit, 0.676 for the ordered logit and 0.637 for the ordinal XGBoost model, with overlapping confidence intervals throughout. This is markedly lower than the 0.91 accuracy obtained under a random country year split with the same tuned pipeline, a gap of 12.5 percentage points for XGBoost, confirming that a substantial part of the high accuracy obtainable under random splitting reflects the model recognizing previously seen country profiles rather than generalizing to unseen countries. Accuracy falls less sharply under the chronological holdout and the 1 year ahead forecasting task, in the region of 0.65 to 0.74, indicating that the classifiers generalize better across time within a country than across countries. Permutation importance, SHAP and LIME consistently identify government effectiveness, urban population growth and environmental tax revenue as the features most strongly associated with model predictions, with a moderate contribution from trade openness and the smallest from GDP growth, a ranking that is stable across importance methods, learning algorithms and cross validation folds. These variables are predictors of the model's output, not estimated causal determinants of emissions, and the results are best read as evidence for climate risk monitoring and further policy evaluation rather than as a causal policy assessment.</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/jarhe-05-2026-0969.title: Professional identity development in digitally mediated work-integrated learning: a longitudinal qualitative study of paid online tutoring
doi:10.1108/jarhe-05-2026-0969.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how non-preservice university students developed professional identities through sustained paid online tutoring within a university-designed work-integrated learning (WIL) program. Pupil outcomes were outside the study scope.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using a longitudinal qualitative design, this study combined narrative inquiry and video-reflexive ethnography across seven semesters (Fall 2022–Fall 2025). Seventeen tutors who participated for four to seven semesters contributed 89 reflective reports and 47 purposively selected recordings of tutoring sessions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Analysis identified three overlapping interpretive orientations of professional identity development: Transactional Technician, Adaptive Designer, and Holistic Mentor. Across time, tutors demonstrated changes in role metaphors, learner framing, motivational descriptions, and instructional practice. Changes in wait-time practices and in interpretations of learner silence were consistent with these shifts. Narrative and interactional data together provided convergent qualitative indications of evolving professional orientations rather than evidence of uniform developmental progression across participants. Participants described compensation as supporting accountability and continued participation, while Serial Matching, Collaborative Curriculum Design, and video-reflexive review provided recurring contexts for reflection, adaptation, and professional identity work.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings concern sustained participants and are subject to survivorship bias. The single-site, non-comparative qualitative design supports contextual interpretation and longitudinal association, not causal claims about program effects.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study provides longitudinal qualitative evidence of professional identity development among non-preservice university students engaged in paid online tutoring and shows how established concepts of professional identity formation and identity work operate in a setting where participants lack formal professional preparation. Its contribution is analytical and contextual rather than theoretical or predictive.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.1108/jarhe-05-2026-0969.venue: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education

doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1985801.title: Computational modeling and optimized machine learning for multidrug solubility prediction in supercritical carbon dioxide
doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1985801.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Reliable prediction of pharmaceutical solubility in supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ) is complicated by strong compound-specific behavior and response values. This study investigated whether sparse measurements from a newly introduced drug can calibrate transferable machine-learning predictions for computational estimation of solubility in wide range of parameters. A curated workbook containing 1,618 observations for 60 drugs was modeled using molecular weight, melting point, temperature, and pressure. Solubility was transformed as log₁₀(S), and XGBoost, CatBoost, and multilayer perceptron regression were each tuned using tree-structured Parzen estimation, differential evolution, and particle swarm optimization. Evaluation used five-fold nested group cross-validation, with complete drugs held out from training and tuning. For each test drug, predictions were assessed before calibration and after 1, 3, or 5 randomly selected measurements, repeated ten times. Within the present evaluation framework, the lowest-log-MAE zero-shot configuration was XGBoost optimized by tree-structured Parzen estimation (log-MAE = 0.584; R² = −0.087; RMSE = 1.713 g/L), showing that the four descriptors were insufficient for reliable extrapolation to unseen compounds. Sparse calibration substantially improved transfer: the lowest-log-MAE one-shot result was obtained by CatBoost–particle swarm optimization (log-MAE = 0.418; R² = 0.166), whereas XGBoost–tree-structured Parzen estimation had the lowest log-MAE at three shots (log-MAE = 0.298; R² = 0.317) and at five shots (log-MAE = 0.251; R² = 0.452; RMSE = 1.223 g/L). Median absolute relative deviation decreased from 82.4% to 42.9% between zero and five shots. These results establish sparse, leakage-controlled calibration as a more defensible use case than unconditional prediction for unseen drugs, while identifying the need for richer molecular descriptors and external prospective validation. In practical terms, this few-shot strategy can reduce the experimental burden for a newly introduced drug by using a small screening set to calibrate a global model before mapping the remaining pressure-temperature domain.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1936750.title: Interleukin pathway genotype and the grandiosity dimension of psychosis: a machine learning gene set analysis with unsupervised anomaly detection controls
doi:10.3389/fimmu.2026.1936750.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Immune involvement in psychosis is well supported, although most of the evidence comes from studies of negative and deficit symptoms. Grandiosity, in comparison, has received little attention. It is, however, the one symptom for which the two main accounts of inflammation in psychosis, activation and reward blunting, make opposite predictions. We tested these predictions in 489 patients with schizophrenia from the Poznań cohort, genotyped for 26 functional variants in eight interleukin-pathway genes and rated with the Operational Criteria Checklist (OPCRIT). Grandiosity was scored from the two OPCRIT items for inflated self-esteem and grandiose delusions. The panel was first tested as a whole, and each gene was then analyzed as a set with the sequence kernel association test (SKAT), with false-discovery-rate control and selection-adjusted permutation. For any gene that passed, we localized the signal within it and estimated the effect with Firth penalized logistic regression. Its stability was examined by held-out splits, jackknife, fragility analysis, comparison with five other symptom dimensions, and anomaly detection. The panel as a whole did not predict grandiosity (out-of-fold Spearman rho = 0.041, permutation p = 0.159). One gene, IL10, showed an association (SKAT p = 0.0028, q = 0.023; selection-adjusted p = 0.025), which was confined to the −819/−592 promoter locus. Carriers of two copies had a Firth odds ratio of 5.28 (95% CI 2.37 to 12.48, p = 4.5 × 10
                    <jats:sup>-5</jats:sup>
                    ), consistent with a recessive effect, and 65% of the 26 carriers had grandiosity, against 24% of non-carriers. The effect was specific to grandiosity (standardized beta 0.19, p = 2 × 10
                    <jats:sup>-5</jats:sup>
                    ) and moderately reproducible across split halves (r = 0.36; mania control r = 0.03). It did not depend on sex, age, or age at onset, and it was unchanged under alternative SKAT kernels, under panel principal components, and after adjustment for neuroleptic response. Two-copy carriage did not differ between the 466 cases and 482 controls. We propose a recessive IL10 −819/−592 effect specific to grandiosity as a hypothesis for independent replication.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpos.2026.1845968.title: Community learning drives children’s digital literacy development: evidence for reconstructing broken education ecosystems
doi:10.3389/fpos.2026.1845968.abstract: <jats:p>Digital literacy development in children is widely assumed to occur primarily through formal schooling, yet growing evidence suggests that community learning—encompassing families, peers, and non-formal organizations—has become the dominant pathway through which children acquire digital skills and competences. This article focuses on the current distribution of digital literacy education responsibilities across formal and informal actors, examines how community-based learning both mitigates and reproduces inequality, and analyses the implications of rights-based frameworks for children’s digital participation and protection. Drawing on quantitative survey data collected from primary and secondary school students, their teachers, school leaders, and parents in Hungary and the Netherlands within the framework of the EFFEct (effective family and community engagement in technology) horizon Europe project, qualitative and quantitative research from the EU-funded DRONE (digital literacy and combat of disinformation among vulnerable groups of adolescents) and legal research in the SAILS (supporting and advocating for inclusive learning spaces) projects, and a systematic review of recent international scholarship, the study provides multi-level empirical evidence on stakeholder roles in digital literacy education ecosystems. across all four student groups surveyed, 100% of substantive responses indicated no perceived school-based instruction on foundational digital citizenship and online safety skills, despite near-universal device access, revealing a systematic curricular gap that contrasts sharply with children’s high levels of digital connectivity. Parent data from 135 participants across six European countries in the DRONE project showed that families bear primary responsibility for teaching digital literacy to their children. This finding is associated with both the limited availability and delayed implementation of structured school-based programs, and the increasingly early engagement of children with digital technologies, through which digital skills and habits are formed prior to entry into formal schooling. Addressing this fragmentation requires an urgent and systemic reconstruction of digital literacy education through coordinated multi-stakeholder governance, curricular reform, teacher empowerment, and inclusive community-based approaches that explicitly recognizes the central role of families and communities in children’s digital development.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-73436-4.title: Adaptive federated ensemble learning with hyperparameter optimization for distributed healthcare IoT
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-73436-4.abstract: The rapid evolution of IoT-enabled healthcare systems has resulted in large-scale distributed data generation across various institutions. While federated learning enables collaborative model training without centralized data, it degrades non-identical data distributions and statistical imbalance across clients. Moreover, the convergence instability and hyperparameter sensitivity remain critical challenges in heterogeneous healthcare environments. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Stability-Aware Secure Federated Ensemble Framework integrated with LampyraCetacea Optimization (ASEFE-LCO). The platform integrates FedAvg and FedProx algorithms with an adaptive multi-model ensemble mechanism to ensure convergence stability under non-IID conditions. To enhance predictive robustness, LampyraCetacea Optimization is employed for dynamic hyperparameter adaptation in non-convex environments. To offer formal privacy tamper-proof protection, an integrated blockchain layer is applied to ensure decentralized auditability. The proposed architecture offers an end-to-end intelligent platform that combines optimization stability, security assurance, scalability, and distributed knowledge integration. As a core tenet of the proposed model, the experimental evaluation of the IoT healthcare security benchmark dataset achieves 99.94% accuracy, indicating a robust, secure, and clinically interpretable solution for an intelligent healthcare system.

doi:10.1088/2752-5295/aead0e.title: Thermal amplification of drought and hydroclimatic regime shift in the Pantanal wetland
authors: Juliane Kayse Albuquerque da Silva Querino
doi:10.1088/2752-5295/aead0e.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The Pantanal, the world’s largest tropical wetland, is experiencing increasing hydroclimatic stress under sustained warming. Drought duration, severity, and intensity increased significantly after the early 2000s, resulting in the most persistent multi-year drought within the study period. This study assesses whether drought dynamics are becoming increasingly thermally amplified. The assessment integrates data and methods, including reanalysis data from 1980–2022, SPEI-12, Run Theory, climate-extreme indices, Random Forest analysis, land-cover and surface water changes, and CMIP6 projections. Although declining precipitation remained important, warm-day frequency (TX90p) showed the strongest bivariate relationship with SPEI-12 across all Pantanal sectors (
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.68–0.71) and the greatest explanatory importance among the evaluated extremes. This association is consistent with increasing thermal amplification, although TX90p and Thornthwaite-based SPEI-12 share sensitivity to air temperature. CMIP6 projections indicate TX90p increases under all scenarios, while the TX90p–SPEI-12 relationship becomes more coherent under SSP245 and especially SSP585. Land-surface transformation, wetland contraction, and surface water loss coincided with drought intensification and may have weakened hydrological buffering, although their individual contributions could not be separated from climatic forcing. Overall, the Pantanal is shifting from a rainfall-buffered wetland toward more water-limited, thermally amplified drought conditions. Monitoring and adaptation should integrate temperature extremes, precipitation, soil moisture, evapotranspiration, and surface water persistence rather than rainfall anomalies alone.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.29303/goescienceed.v7i4.3476.title: Penggunaan Media Diorama Lingkungan 2D dalam Model Problem Based Learning untuk Meningkatkan Hasil Belajar IPAS Materi Lingkungan Jadi Rusak Siswa Kelas VB SDN 05 Madiun Lor
doi:10.29303/goescienceed.v7i4.3476.abstract: <jats:p>Pembelajaran IPAS pada materi Lingkungan Jadi Rusak memerlukan strategi dan media pembelajaran yang mampu melibatkan peserta didik secara aktif serta menghadirkan permasalahan lingkungan secara konkret. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan hasil belajar peserta didik melalui penggunaan media Diorama Lingkungan 2D dalam model Problem Based Learning (PBL). Penelitian ini menggunakan Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) yang dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus dengan subjek penelitian sebanyak 26 peserta didik kelas VB SDN 05 Madiun Lor. Setiap siklus terdiri atas tahap perencanaan, pelaksanaan tindakan, observasi, dan refleksi. Teknik pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui tes, observasi, dan dokumentasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan media Diorama Lingkungan 2D dalam model Problem Based Learning diikuti peningkatan hasil belajar peserta didik. Rata-rata nilai peserta didik meningkat dari 67,31 pada pra siklus menjadi 76,54 pada siklus I dan meningkat menjadi 85,38 pada siklus II. Persentase ketuntasan belajar juga meningkat dari 42,31% menjadi 69,23% dan mencapai 88,46% pada siklus II. Dengan demikian, penggunaan media Diorama Lingkungan 2D dalam model Problem Based Learning dapat digunakan untuk meningkatkan hasil belajar IPAS materi Lingkungan Jadi Rusak pada peserta didik kelas VB SDN 05 Madiun Lor.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4508-4.ch009.title: Learning Support for Students With Hearing-Impairment Using Speech Recognition in Elementary School
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4508-4.ch009.abstract: <jats:p>Children with hearing impairments attending regular classrooms are often surrounded by children with normal hearing, and are therefore more likely to face difficulties due to their hearing impairments compared to children attending schools for the deaf. For this reason, there is an urgent need to consider effective information access for children with hearing impairments, and pioneering, evidence-based recommendations using equipment that aligns with the current advancements in ICT technology. This paper introduces four case studies that utilizes speech recognition to explore the potential of speech recognition-based support for elementary school students with hearing impairments.</jats:p>

doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010566/v1.title: Machine Learning Identifies an Information-Sufficiency Regime for Critical-Mineral Recovery
doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010566/v1.abstract: <jats:p>The recovery of critical minerals from spent lithium-ion batteries is governed by coupled feedstock chemistry, solvent composition, and processing conditions, yet heterogeneous experimental reporting makes it difficult to determine which information is essential for reliable prediction across heterogeneous experimental systems. Here, using deep eutectic solvent-based recovery as a representative resource recovery platform, we curate 814 experimental observations from 38 publications and develop an interpretable machine learning framework to identify an informationsufficiency regime. Five descriptors, including temperature, electrode material type, leaching time, target metal, and hydrogen-bond donor identity, retain 98.3% of the predictive performance of the full 13-descriptor model while reducing the descriptor space by 61.5%. Reducing the representation from five to four descriptors causes a pronounced performance loss, whereas adding a sixth provides negligible additional benefit. Descriptor removal and domain ablation analyses further show that temperature and target metal identity contain the least replaceable predictive information, while material identity, solvent chemistry, and processing conditions provide complementary information. These results identify a compact, chemically structured information core for critical-mineral recovery and provide a quantitative basis for prioritizing experimental measurements, improving cross-study data consistency, and developing more transferable datadriven frameworks for battery resource recovery.</jats:p>

doi:10.1126/sciadv.aeg9183.title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning
doi:10.1126/sciadv.aeg9183.abstract: <jats:p>Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a “dirty” mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting “dirty” irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical “gene of scrap compatibility,” this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.</jats:p>

doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aea41b.title: A Statistical Study of Ion-scale Waves at 1 au Using Machine Learning
doi:10.3847/1538-4357/aea41b.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Circularly polarized waves at ion scales are thought to play vital roles in the heating and acceleration of coronal plasma, though the extent of their roles throughout the heliosphere remains an open question. In this work, a 1D convolutional neural network trained to identify waves in magnetic field time-series data is used to classify the Wind spacecraft data set at 1 au for the yr 2005–2024. Approximately 1.8 million intervals out of about one hundred million intervals are found to contain circularly polarized wave signatures with amplitudes >0.1 nT and spacecraft-frame frequencies >0.16 Hz. Wave intervals are observed most often in both the fast, hot wind and in slow Alfvénic wind. The number of wave intervals per day fluctuates at frequencies that closely follow the harmonics of solar rotation, implying a connection between wave occurrence and large-scale solar wind features. Comparison of the measured temperature anisotropy and proton plasma beta in wave intervals to kinetic instability criteria shows a correlation between wave occurrence and the proton cyclotron and mirror instabilities. However, local generation mechanisms associated with core proton temperature anisotropy instability only account for ≈30% of the identified waves.</jats:p>

doi:10.36074/grail-of-science.16.10.2026.title: THE DEVELOPMENT OF LEARNING SKILLS IN SCHOOLCHILDREN AND THE ROLE OF LEARNING STRATEGIES
doi:10.36074/grail-of-science.16.10.2026.abstract: <jats:p>In traditional teaching models, subjects are typically taught in isolation; consequently, while students may master individual fields of knowledge, they often struggle to comprehend them as a unified whole. The integrated approach bridges this gap by fostering interdisciplinary connections, allowing topics to be examined from diverse perspectives, and facilitating the real-world application of acquired knowledge. Thus, the learning process extends beyond the mere transmission of information, serving instead to cultivate flexible thinking, problem-solving capabilities, creative approaches, and independent decision-making skills in students. In this context, one of the key advantages of integration is the stimulation of students&#x27; cognitive activity. Through the synthesis of various fields of knowledge, they compare facts, establish cause-and-effect relationships, and connect what they have learned to real life. This makes the teaching process more engaging and meaningful, fostering a sustained interest in learning among students.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70583-6.title: A hybrid reinforcement learning and Harris Hawks Optimization framework for multi-objective resource management in IIoT
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-70583-6.abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is revolutionizing industrial processes by interconnecting sensors, machines, and computing resources to enable intelligent automation, real-time monitoring, and predictive maintenance. Despite its potential, efficient allocation and management of resources in IIoT networks remain a significant challenge due to the dynamic, heterogeneous, and large-scale nature of industrial environments. Traditional static or heuristic resource allocation methods often fail to satisfy conflicting objectives such as minimizing latency, maximizing throughput, ensuring energy efficiency, and maintaining system reliability. To address these challenges, this paper presents the design and development of an AI-based multi-objective resource management system for IIoT systems. The system integrates reinforcement learning (RL) for adaptive, real-time decision-making with Harris Hawks Optimization (HHO) for multi-objective optimization, balancing competing performance metrics across sensing, communication, computing, and control layers. The RL agent predicts system states and dynamically adjusts resource allocation, while HHO fine-tunes the solutions to achieve optimal performance under multiple constraints. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed system outperforms conventional static and heuristic approaches, achieving higher efficiency, faster adaptability, and improved scalability. By intelligently managing resources and optimizing system behavior, this system enhances overall operational reliability and Quality-of-Service in IIoT networks. The results indicate that combining AI-driven decision-making with advanced nature-inspired optimization provides a robust and efficient solution for next-generation industrial applications, paving the way for more intelligent, resilient, and resource-efficient IIoT systems.

doi:10.1093/9780197852514.003.0008.title: Learning to Listen, Yielding to Pain
doi:10.1093/9780197852514.003.0008.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter addresses the challenges that emerge when members of perpetrator societies are asked to consider how they contribute to the legacies of silence that perpetuate trauma and racism. The author shares illustrations of what happens when members of the majority in Germany, Canada, and the United States seek to understand and reflect on the impact of past atrocities and current injustices. Despite the different contexts and memory cultures in which these illustrations take place, there are clear parallels between them that highlight the defensive postures of participants when they are asked to confront their responsibility to remember or consider their implication in racial injustice. In the face of these challenges, the author considers possibilities for reparative listening and emphasizes the importance of moving towards rather than away from the feelings of discomfort that this process evokes.</jats:p>

doi:10.54254/3049-5458/2026.37658.title: An interpretable machine learning risk stratification model for the imaging burden of cerebral small vessel disease: integrating echocardiography, carotid ultrasound, and serological indicators
doi:10.54254/3049-5458/2026.37658.abstract: <jats:p>This study enrolled 401 subjects, who were stratified according to the total imaging burden score of Cerebral Small Vessel Disease (CSVD) and divided into a training set (280 cases) and a validation set (121 cases) at a ratio of 7:3. Six variables—age, left ventricular posterior wall end-diastolic thickness, E/e′ ratio, maximum carotid plaque thickness, history of hypertension, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol—were included, and Logistic regression, K-nearest neighbor, and partial least squares models were separately constructed. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity, specificity, and decision curve analysis. The results showed that the K-nearest neighbor model achieved the best performance in the validation set (AUC 0.869, accuracy 82.6%, sensitivity 65.0%, specificity 95.1%). SHAP analysis clarified the contribution of each feature, with E/e′ being the strongest predictor (mean absolute SHAP value 0.194), followed by maximum carotid plaque thickness and age (0.085 and 0.062, respectively). Decision curve analysis showed that the model yielded the greatest net benefit at a disease-risk threshold of 35%. With a specificity of 95.1%, the model performed prominently in risk stratification of CSVD patients, could effectively identify low-risk populations and reduce unnecessary imaging examinations, but its sensitivity was relatively low (65.0%), making it more suitable for clinical secondary diagnosis.</jats:p>
doi:10.54254/3049-5458/2026.37658.venue: Journal of Clinical Technology and Theory

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11381790/v1.title: A deep learning method for solving American double Heston model
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11381790/v1.abstract: We propose a deep learning framework based on mixture of deep neural network (DNN) solutions formulated via multiplicative ensembling for solving the American double Heston model as a free boundary problem. In this framework, we first consider the model under constant interest rate. Furthermore, we fix the free boundary known as the early exercise boundary which result to a fixed-free boundary problem. We then design a DNN architecture from which the network model MLA-MoS-1 is formulated. In addition, we extend to consider the American double Heston model involving stochastic interest rate under both sparse and dense correlation matrix structures. The obtain deep neural network architecture is denoted as MLA-MoS-2. Both MLA-MoS-1 and MLA-MoS-2 predict the early exercise simultaneously with the value function and Greeks after training. The predictive performances of the proposed network models are further illustrated with examples and comparison with existing methods.

doi:10.1108/ijotb-01-2025-0018.title: Green knowledge to sustainability: the role of inter-organizational learning and technological innovation
doi:10.1108/ijotb-01-2025-0018.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this paper, sustainable manufacturing is discussed in the manufacturing sector of Pakistan to enhance the interplay of green intellectual capital (GIC), inter-organizational learning (IOL) and technological innovation (TI) as drivers of sustainable performance. Drawing on the Resource-Based View (RBV), Natural Resource-Based View (NRBV) and Dynamic Capabilities View (DCV), the study examines how GIC contributes to sustainable performance through IOL and under the boundary condition of TI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 14001-certified companies' top-level and middle-level managers performed the data collection method by distributing 300 online questionnaires; data was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling in SMART-PLS 4.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings specify that GIC directly influences sustainable performance with IOL allocation as a mediator and TI as a moderator, approving the applicability of the RBV. The results highlight the importance of strategic resource management and technological incorporation in progressing sustainable manufacturing practices. Structural equation modeling demonstrates that hypotheses are significantly positive for this study.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The limitations of this study include its cross-sectional design and the fact that has few generalizability factors, suggesting future research to explore cultural differences, alternative methods, and additional variables.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings suggest that manufacturing managers should strengthen green knowledge and skills, promote IOL with external partners, and align TI with sustainability-related operational improvements.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study advances a resource-conversion explanation of sustainable performance by distinguishing GIC as a strategic green knowledge resource, IOL as the mechanism through which this resource is mobilized across organizational boundaries, and TI as the technological boundary condition that strengthens the translation of learning into sustainable performance. By integrating the complementary roles of RBV, NRBV, and DCV, the study explains not only whether GIC contributes to sustainable performance, but also how and under what technological conditions this contribution is realized in an emerging-economy manufacturing context.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.1108/ijotb-01-2025-0018.venue: International Journal of Organization Theory & Behavior

doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1512.c6081.title: From Conventional Design to Artificial Intelligence: Automation of Systematic Design in Machine Tools
doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1512.c6081.abstract: <jats:p>This paper introduces an automated and systematic conceptual design framework developed for complex mechanical assemblies, with a specific focus on machine tool engineering. To resolve the structural constraints of traditional design paradigms and perform rapid trade-off analyses during the initial design phases, a knowledge-based expert system has been developed and integrated. The architecture employs the mass structural index of alternative configurations as its core evaluation metric to drive optimal component allocation. Powered by a specialized technical database and a rule-based logic engine, the expert system automates the synthesis of machine tool sub-assemblies by processing conditional logic paths derived from initial operational boundaries. The implementation of this advanced engineering framework substantially lowers R&D expenditures and dramatically compresses the overall product development lifecycle.</jats:p>

doi:10.1002/arp.70071.title: Archaeological Prospectivity and Terrace Morphometry Using Open Geospatial Data: A Reproducible GIS–Machine‐Learning Workflow for the Cuyes River Valley, Ecuador
doi:10.1002/arp.70071.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This study develops and evaluates a reproducible archaeological prospectivity workflow for data‐scarce tropical landscapes by integrating restricted legacy archaeological documentation with openly accessible environmental geospatial datasets. The Cuyes River Valley in southern Ecuador, located on the eastern‐Andean foothills where montane environments descend toward the Upper Amazon basin, provides the test case. Archaeological reports produced in 2009–2010 were converted into a structured inventory of 78 terrace records from Espíritu Playa, San Miguel de Cuyes and Nueva Zaruma. Terrace morphometry was analysed using area, height, length–width ratio and elevation, whereas
                    <jats:italic>K</jats:italic>
                    ‐means clustering identified recurrent forms. A presence–background random forest model combined known terrace locations with Copernicus DEM‐derived elevation, slope and roughness and WorldClim temperature and precipitation covariates. Spatial cross‐validation yielded a mean ROC‐AUC of 0.753 and mean average precision of 0.604, indicating useful but spatially variable ranking performance. Annual precipitation, elevation and annual mean temperature were the strongest model predictors. The results distinguish higher, cooler and drier upper valley systems from a lower, warmer and wetter Nueva Zaruma context, whereas morphometric clustering separates moderate upper valley terraces, large construction units, lower valley compact terraces and small elongated features. Exact archaeological coordinates were withheld and public outputs spatially generalized. Beyond the case study, the workflow demonstrates how legacy archaeological records can be transformed into reproducible, ethically constrained prospectivity products for survey prioritization and heritage management where field data and high‐resolution remote sensing remain limited.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.53629/sakaefd.1978281.title: The Effect of Multisensory-Based Materials on the Reading Skills of Children with Learning Disabilities
doi:10.53629/sakaefd.1978281.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Reading material that appeals to multiple senses can provide readers with an interactive, active reading and learning environment. This study investigates the effectiveness of reading activities with multisensory materials on the fluent reading skills of students diagnosed with specific learning disabilities. For this purpose, the students were asked to use the material by first listening, then reading, then acting out the story with puppets, and finally rereading it with the book “My Book, My Friend”, a material developed using a multisensory method. The study was designed using a qualitative approach and conducted through action research. Five students and three teachers included in the study were given a material book developed based on multisensory concepts to practice in the support education room in general education schools and were asked to use it. Then, the LAB (Literacy Assessment Battery) was applied to determine the effectiveness of the material. As a result of the research, it was observed that using multisensory materials improved students’ reading, reading comprehension and writing.</jats:p>

doi:10.33487/edumaspul.v10i2.520.title: The Utilization of Digital Technology to Support Self-Directed Learning Among Vocational High School Students: A Systematic Literature Review
doi:10.33487/edumaspul.v10i2.520.abstract: <jats:p>Advancements in digital technology offer Vocational High School (SMK) students opportunities to access learning resources flexibly and cultivate learning autonomy. However, the use of digital technology does not automatically guarantee the development of learning autonomy, as it is influenced by various factors such as digital literacy, learning motivation, instructional design, and teacher support. This study aims to analyze the use of digital technology in supporting learning autonomy among SMK students, specifically examining the types of technology employed, the dimensions of learning autonomy fostered, and the factors that facilitate or hinder its implementation. The study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) methodology, adhering to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. Data were sourced from relevant scholarly articles published between 2021 and 2026 and subsequently analyzed using descriptive analysis and thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that digital technologies such as Learning Management Systems (LMS), digital learning media, web-based learning, instructional videos, and artificial intelligence have the potential to support student initiatives in learning, time management, progress monitoring, and self-evaluation. Therefore, the integration of digital technology must be accompanied by instructional strategies that encourage student responsibility and self-regulation to ensure the optimal development of learning autonomy.</jats:p>

doi:10.5256/f1000research.207019.r526692.title: Peer Review Report For: Reflective Practice and Teacher Growth Mindset in Collaborative School Cultures: The Moderating Role of Professional Learning Community among Indonesian In-Service Teachers [version 1; peer review: 1 approved, 1 approved with reservations]
doi:10.5256/f1000research.207019.r526692.abstract: Background Teacher growth mindset has been increasingly recognized as an important factor in teachers’ professional development and instructional improvement. However, limited research has examined how teacher growth mindset is associated with reflective practice and whether professional learning community (PLC) influences this relationship. This study investigated the relationship between reflective practice and teacher growth mindset and examined the moderating role of PLC among Indonesian in-service teachers. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted involving 244 teachers from various educational levels. Data were collected using the Reflective Practice Questionnaire (RPQ), the Professional Learning Community Assessment-Revised (PLCA-R), and an adapted teacher growth mindset scale. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results The results showed that reflective practice positively predicted teacher growth mindset (β = 0.497, p < .001), while PLC also had a significant positive effect on teacher growth mindset (β = 0.373, p < .001). PLC significantly moderated the relationship between reflective practice and teacher growth mindset in a negative direction (β = −0.079, p = .039). Conclusions This finding indicates that although reflective practice remains positively associated with teacher growth mindset, its contribution becomes relatively weaker in schools with stronger PLCs. The findings suggest the presence of a compensatory mechanism in which collective professional learning partially substitutes for individual reflective processes in supporting teacher growth mindset. This study contributes to the literature by integrating reflective practice, PLC, and teacher growth mindset within a single model and highlights the importance of combining individual reflection and collaborative professional learning in teacher development initiatives.

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4488-9.ch007.title: Designing for Persistence in Practice-Oriented Higher Education
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4488-9.ch007.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter advances an integrated, proactive pedagogical model for student retention and persistence in practice-oriented higher education. Drawing on social cognitive theory, cognitive load theory and situated learning, the model combines three elements: feed-up to clarify expectations, feed-forward to provide guidance during complex tasks and experiential learning to ground assessment in professional practice. An empirical case study from Australian real estate education illustrates the model in practice and demonstrates that an assessment-embedded feed-forward intervention produced statistically significant gains in general and task-specific self-efficacy, with the strongest effects for students with limited prior industry experience. The chapter argues that proactive learning design is an equity strategy: by reducing avoidable uncertainty and making professional norms visible, it disproportionately benefits students who lack tacit familiarity with professional environments. A practical implementation framework supports adaptation across practice-oriented disciplines.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4488-9.ch007.venue: Transforming Student Persistence in Higher Education

doi:10.36074/grail-of-science.16.10.2026.title: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF THRESHOLD, REFERENCE AND MACHINE-BASED APPROACHES TO ASSESSING THE CORRECTNESS OF REHABILITATION EXERCISES
doi:10.36074/grail-of-science.16.10.2026.abstract: <jats:p>The task of automatically assessing the correctness of rehabilitation exercise performance based on key body points extracted from video is considered. Three approaches — threshold-based, reference-based (dynamic time warping, DTW) and machine-based (Random Forest) — are compared on the REHAB24-6 dataset for three exercises (arm abduction, leg abduction, squats). Group cross-validation by participant and McNemar&#x27;s exact test are applied; the results are compared against trivial baseline classification levels. A useful predictive signal is shown not to be present for all exercises: for arm abduction the machine-based approach achieved an accuracy of 82.1 % against a baseline of 56.2 %, whereas for squats no approach exceeded the baseline. The advantages and limitations of each approach for use in home telerehabilitation systems are identified.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fped.2026.1939157.title: Multihipposenet: multi-task deep learning for automated DDH assessment in infant hip ultrasound
doi:10.3389/fped.2026.1939157.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is a common skeletal condition in infants and young children. For infants under six months, diagnosis relies on Graf ultrasonography to measure the α and β angles, which assess hip-joint development. However, this method requires experienced sonographers with expertise in complex anatomy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this study, we propose an end-to-end multi-task learning network that improves DDH assessment by jointly exploiting complementary anatomical information. First, we use ResNet-50 with a feature pyramid network (FPN) and a contextual semantic fusion module to extract multi-scale features from hip anatomy. Second, we employ a multi-expert gated channel transformation (ME-GCT) unit that explicitly models the relationships between tasks and channels to balance collaboration and conflict across tasks. Finally, a multi-task graph adaptive learning mechanism (MT-GALM) mines the hidden dynamic dependencies between adjacent channels across tasks. Two datasets comprising 1,355 annotated hip ultrasound images from 566 infants were constructed for this work.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Across the patient-level cross-validation test folds, 97.97% and 96.81% of the estimated α and β angles fall within 5 degrees of the expert reference.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Because validation was restricted to Graf type I and type II hips, these results should be interpreted as evidence of technical feasibility rather than of established clinical utility; evaluation on type III and type IV hips is required before clinical deployment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4488-9.ch013.title: Experiential Learning and Student Persistence in Cambodian Higher Education
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4488-9.ch013.abstract: <jats:p>Persistence among students has remained an expansion challenge facing higher education (HE) in many parts of the world, especially in developing countries, where financial, structural, and pedagogical issues contribute significantly to students dropping out. Over the past few years, various forms of experiential learning models, including cooperative education (co-op) and work-integrated learning (WIL), have attracted much interest as a way of improving students' engagement, motivation, employability skills, and learning outcomes. This review chapter focuses on the association between experiential learning and student persistence within the Cambodian HE sectors. Using relevant student persistence theories, models of experiential learning, and current literature about co-op and WIL, the chapter analyzes the contribution of experiential learning to students' academic performance and institutional attachment within the Cambodian HE sectors.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-2600-4488-9.ch013.venue: Transforming Student Persistence in Higher Education

doi:10.55990/20250042.title: Social Networking Usage, Informal Workplace Learning and Personal Professional Development: A Structural Equation Model on the Teachers’ Attitudes and Beliefs towards ICT Adoption in Public Schools
doi:10.55990/20250042.abstract:
<jats:p>The objective of this study was to determine the influence of social networking use, informal workplace learning, and personal professional development on teachers' attitudes and beliefs towards ICT adoption among public secondary school teachers in Region XI, Philippines. Standardized survey questionnaires were adopted and contextualized to suit the regional educational setting. The instruments were administered to 417 randomly selected teachers using stratified random sampling. This study employed a quantitative, non-experimental research design, using means, Pearson's r, and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) for data analysis.

The results revealed generally low to very low levels of social networking usage, informal workplace learning, personal professional development, and attitudes and beliefs toward ICT adoption. Despite these modest levels, significant positive relationships were found between social networking use and teachers' attitudes toward ICT adoption, as well as between personal professional development and these attitudes. Furthermore, the structural equation modeling results indicated that the three independent variables significantly influenced teachers' attitudes and beliefs toward ICT adoption, with social networking usage emerging as the strongest predictor among the constructs. The findings underscore the importance of enhancing digital engagement, strengthening informal learning cultures, and providing sustained professional development initiatives to foster more positive attitudes and stronger readiness for ICT integration in schools.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fendo.2026.1873245.title: Interpretable machine learning identifies predictors of IGF-1 during growth hormone therapy in boys
doi:10.3389/fendo.2026.1873245.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) is widely used to guide growth hormone (GH) therapy, yet its predictors during the maintenance phase and puberty remain incompletely understood. We aimed to predict IGF-1 standard deviation scores (SDS) at 3 and 12 months in GH-treated boys and to identify key predictors of IGF-1 dynamics using interpretable modeling approaches.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Data from 72 boys with growth hormone deficiency or idiopathic short stature from a previous Swedish clinical trial were analyzed using early-life characteristics, GH treatment variables, and puberty-related measures. Linear regression, Elastic Net regression, and explainable boosting machine (EBM) models were evaluated with nested five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation. Performance estimates were patient-balanced, with 95% confidence intervals based on 2,000 patient-cluster bootstrap resamples.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Elastic Net had the highest point estimates at 3 months, but confidence intervals did not establish a difference between the primary models. No clear differences between models were found at 12 months. Current IGF-1 SDS was the most prominent predictive feature, while additional treatment- and puberty-related variables were also selected across cross-validation models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Interpretable modeling approaches provided moderate predictive performance for future IGF-1 SDS during the maintenance phase and puberty. The findings indicate that prediction is informed by current IGF-1 SDS together with additional clinical variables, but further validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical application.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1108/jarhe-03-2026-0372.title: Interplay between online tertiary education, academic curriculum viability and students’ experiences: the dynamics of digital learning ecosystems
doi:10.1108/jarhe-03-2026-0372.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study investigates the structural interplay among Digital Learning Ecosystems (DLE), Viability of Online Academic Curriculum (VOAC), Quality of Online Education (QOE) and Students’ Lived Experiences (SLE) within a tertiary education context in Ghana.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A quantitative survey design was employed, collecting data from 668 graduate students. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) using AMOS was applied to test four hypothesized relationships linking curriculum viability, perceived quality, digital ecosystems and experiential outcomes. Factor analysis ensured construct reliability, and model fit was evaluated using standard SEM indices.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Findings indicate that VOAC significantly associates with QOE, while DLE strongly relates with SLE. Interestingly, QOE does not automatically relate with SLE, suggesting a structural disjunction between institutional quality metrics and students’ lived realities. VOAC minimally associate with SLE, implying indirect pathways mediated by DLE. Overall, the digital ecosystem emerged as dominantly and contextually related to student experience.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes to a more nuanced understanding of online education in sub-Saharan African contexts by differentiating structural quality from lived experience, highlighting the centrality of digital ecosystems and providing actionable guidance for institutions navigating the challenges of digitally mediated learning. For policymakers and educational leaders, these findings imply that investments in digital infrastructure (e.g. reliable connectivity, institutional platforms, device access) should be prioritized alongside curricular reform.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Social implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study outcome benefits the society, as recipients of academic knowledge and skills, and will serve as a useful guide by educational institutions for the effective design of online education programs that moves beyond technical implementation to the fostering of genuine societal and human-centric interaction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study differentiates perceived quality from lived experience, repositions digital learning ecosystems as central to online education and provides a systemic framework for understanding online tertiary education in Sub-Saharan Africa. Implications highlight the need for integrated curriculum reform, ecosystem readiness and experiential design to achieve equitable and sustainable online education transformation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.1108/jarhe-03-2026-0372.venue: Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education

doi:10.1108/itse-06-2026-0241.title: Different prompts – different online learning behavior? Investigating generic, specific, and adaptive specific prompts
doi:10.1108/itse-06-2026-0241.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In digital learning environments, learners need to regulate their learning, yet many do not engage in effective self-regulated learning strategies. Prompts can scaffold these processes, but their effectiveness may depend on their specificity and alignment with learners’ ongoing learning behavior. The purpose of this study is to address the limited evidence on the effects of generic, specific, and behavior-adaptive prompts on learning processes and outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study (n = 64) uses an experimental between-subjects design investigating generic (GP), specific (SP) and adaptive specific (AP) and no prompts with regard to learning performance, perceived learning support and navigation behavior.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>No significant group differences were found for declarative knowledge, whereas significant differences emerged for knowledge transfer, perceived learning support and navigation behavior. Independently of the experimental condition, higher transfer performance was associated with navigation that deviated more strongly from the course structure.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Future research should investigate learners’ interactions with and reactions to prompts, for example through eye-tracking, screen-recording, and brief self-report measures.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>By comparing fixed generic, fixed specific, adaptive specific and no prompting, this study considers prompt specificity and behavior-contingent adaptivity together. It also combines learning performance and perceived learning support with trace-based navigation behavior. Fixed generic prompts were less effective for knowledge transfer than adaptive specific prompts or no prompting, while adaptive specific prompts did not outperform fixed specific prompts or the control group. The findings therefore challenge the assumption that providing prompts or increasing their adaptivity is inherently beneficial and highlight the importance of prompt specificity, timing and fit with learners’ ongoing behavior.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1108/jwl-06-2026-0406.title: How digital learning shapes managerial skills in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)
doi:10.1108/jwl-06-2026-0406.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are a critical pillar of the European economy, contributing to employment, regional and global development. However, many SMEs face heightened failure risks linked to limited financial resources, labour market pressures and significant knowledge loss. Developing strong managerial competencies has emerged as a key strategy for improving organisational performance and long-term sustainability. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the shift from traditional training to online learning, yet research remains limited, this paper examines how digital learning environments can support the development of managerial capabilities within SMEs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To understand how online learning can enhance knowledge acquisition, retention and sharing within management teams in European technology SMEs, Ireland was chosen as a case study in the tech sector to identify start-ups launching trends through FAME database analysis, followed by a critical literature review to design a theoretical framework that adopts pedagogical approaches to business education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings contribute to theory by developing a conceptual framework which helps start-up executives reassess their role in working with knowledge as a critical managerial capability through online learning mechanisms. This pathway leverages critical enablers, overcomes barriers and boosts managerial skills development. This framework supports knowledge acquisition, retention practices and knowledge sharing across teams to support business performance and competitive advantage.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The effectiveness of online learning depends on organisational culture, digital readiness and alignment between learning goals and managerial tasks. The conceptual framework developed in this study highlights the pathways by which SMEs can leverage online learning to build robust knowledge management capabilities. In addition, the framework offers practical managerial recommendations for its use.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1021/acsomega.6c06887.title: Deep Learning for Protein Secondary-Structure Segmentation in Intermediate-Resolution Cryo-EM Maps: A Resolution-Stratified Benchmark Dataset and Controlled Evaluation
doi:10.1021/acsomega.6c06887.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Accurate segmentation of protein secondary structures in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) maps is crucial for protein tracing and atomic model building, yet remains challenging at intermediate resolutions. Although deep learning architectures have recently been applied to this task, there remains a lack of standardized evaluation protocols and systematic resolution-stratified analyses. Consequently, it remains unclear how segmentation performance varies across finer resolution ranges within the intermediate-resolution regime and how different volumetric segmentation architectures compare under controlled experimental conditions. To address these gaps, we present a nonredundant, resolution-stratified benchmark dataset and a controlled evaluation framework for protein secondary-structure segmentation in intermediate-resolution cryo-EM maps. The dataset comprises 972 nonredundant protein-chain samples from 495 cryo-EM protein structures resolved at 4.5–8.0 Å, with voxel-level annotations for helices, sheets, and non-periodic secondary-structure (NPSS) regions. The dataset is stratified into three resolution ranges─4.5–5.5, 5.5–6.5, and 6.5–8.0 Å─to enable systematic analysis of resolution-dependent segmentation performance. Using this benchmark, we evaluate five representative convolutional and transformer-based volumetric segmentation architectures─U-Net, Residual U-Net, Attention U-Net, UNETR, and Swin-UNETR─under standardized preprocessing, training, and evaluation protocols. Residual U-Net achieves the highest macro-averaged foreground (Macro-FG) F1 score in all three resolution bins, while helices are segmented more accurately than sheets and NPSS regions. All five architectures achieve their highest Macro-FG F1 scores in the highest-resolution bin, whereas performance varies between the two lower-resolution bins across architectures and secondary-structure classes. Overall, this benchmark enables fine-grained analysis of resolution-dependent segmentation performance, supports reproducible method development, and facilitates controlled comparison of future cryo-EM secondary-structure segmentation approaches.</jats:p>

doi:10.9734/jeai/2026/v48i104578.title: Optimization of Solar Powered Cleaning Cum Sieving Machine for Vegetable Seeds
doi:10.9734/jeai/2026/v48i104578.abstract:
<jats:p>This study focuses on the optimisation of a solar-powered cleaning-cum-sieving machine for vegetable seed processing, specifically targeting chilli seeds. The machine operates on the principle of vibration generated by an eccentric rotating mass, which facilitates the separation of impurities based on size. It is designed with a cylindrical (SS 316) frame with overall dimensions of 490 × 464 mm (H × W) and is powered by solar energy. The machine’s operational parameters, including motor speed (1900 rpm, 2100 rpm, 2300 rpm), feed rate (500 g, 750 g, 1000 g), and eccentric weight (20 g, 22.5 g, 25 g), were optimised to achieve the best performance. The optimal conditions were found to be a motor speed of 2300 rpm, a feed rate of 522 g, and an eccentric weight of 23 g. These conditions resulted in a cleaning efficiency of 98.15%, a capacity of 37.27 kg/h, a specific power consumption of 0.252 Wh/kg, a cleaning performance index of 0.981, and losses of 0.185%. Furthermore, the optimised machine significantly improved seed viability, as indicated by a germination percentage of 97% on the 14th day. The solar-powered machine offers an energy-efficient, cost-effective solution for small-scale farmers to enhance seed quality, reduce processing losses, and increase yields.
Practical Utility: The optimised cleaning-and-sieving machine provides a reliable, energy-efficient solution for producing and preserving high-quality vegetable seeds. By removing impurities such as broken or immature seeds, the machine enhances the viability and germination potential of processed seeds, thereby directly contributing to higher crop yields. This versatile machine is suitable for processing various vegetable seed types and is particularly effective in small-scale agricultural operations and seed-processing units. It provides a sustainable and efficient alternative to labour-intensive manual seed-cleaning methods.</jats:p>

doi:10.1126/sciadv.aef0605.title: Deep learning reveals ecological decoupling and rate heterogeneity in Hymenoptera wing evolution
doi:10.1126/sciadv.aef0605.abstract: <jats:p>Quantifying biomorphological evolution and integrating phenotypic data into large-scale ecological and evolutionary studies are often limited by the scalability, subjectivity, and poor interpretability of existing methods. We introduce HAIKA (Hierarchical Attention-based Interpretable K-dimensional Autoencoder), a self-supervised residual channel-attention autoencoder that extracts continuous morphological representations from unlabeled standardized images and highlights the image regions that contribute to those representations. Applied to insect forewings across broad pterygote lineages, HAIKA outperformed most baseline deep learning models and conventional descriptors in clustering, dimensionality reduction, and morphological embedding. When applied to Hymenoptera (i.e., ants, bees, and wasps), the HAIKA-derived continuous characters improved morphology-based phylogenetic reconstruction and illuminated the evolutionary dynamics of wing shape and venation. Our results reveal that wing morphological evolution in Hymenoptera proceeds at decoupled rates across shape and venation modules and is not consistently aligned with key ecological transitions such as parasitoidism or eusociality. HAIKA provides a scalable, image-based route for phenotypic analyses, broadly applicable across diverse taxa and to both 2D and 3D datasets.</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/ijlss-12-2025-0350.title: Agility as a capability amplifier: the co-evolution of organizational learning, big data and digital transformation in manufacturing
doi:10.1108/ijlss-12-2025-0350.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Manufacturing firms face persistent digital upgrading bottlenecks, yet existing literature overlooks the co-evolutionary dynamics between organizational learning (OL), multi-dimensional data capabilities and agility in driving digital transformation (DT). This study aims to undertake a systematic empirical investigation of how OL (exploratory vs exploitative), big data capabilities (BDCs) and organizational agility (OA) synergistically shape the trajectory of DT. By synthesizing the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capability Theory, this study further clarifies the mediating role of BDC dimensions and the boundary condition of OA in this process.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A quantitative research design was adopted using a structured questionnaire distributed to manufacturing managers across China. After a pre-survey validation, 505 valid responses were collected through online and offline channels. The proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling via SmartPLS to examine direct, mediating and moderating effects.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Both exploratory and exploitative OL significantly advance DT, operating primarily through improvements in data analysis and integration capability and data application capability. OA positively moderates the impact of BDCs on transformation outcomes. Data acquisition capability alone shows no significant direct/indirect influence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study develops a framework that articulates the interactive mechanisms between OL, BDCs and agility in driving manufacturing DT, addressing the gap of treating these factors as isolated drivers in prior studies. This study empirically validates the differential mediating roles of three BDC dimensions and the moderating effect of agility.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
