doi:10.2514/1.i011755.title: Application and Assessment of Machine Learning Methods for Aircraft Design Problems
doi:10.2514/1.i011755.abstract: <jats:p>In this work, we present a comparative study on machine-learning-based surrogate modeling for multidisciplinary aerospace applications. The main objective of the work is to demonstrate the predictive capability of traditional machine learning methods, including linear regression, random forest, gradient boosting, extreme gradient boosting, support vector regression, Gaussian process regression, and multilayer perceptron, on multidisciplinary engineering problems. The selected datasets are determined at different complexity levels and disciplines. These methods are first applied to two benchmark functions with different mathematical characteristics and then to four engineering design problems. The models are evaluated using different training sample sizes and multiple random data partitions to assess their predictive performance and robustness. The models are compared in terms of the coefficient of determination ([Formula: see text]), normalized root mean squared error, normalized mean absolute error, and computational cost. The obtained results show that the relative performance of the surrogate models varies with problem dimensionality and training sample size. In particular, Gaussian process regression and support vector regression provide consistently high predictive accuracy across the investigated engineering problems, while the computational requirements and sensitivity to data partitioning differ among the methods.</jats:p>

doi:10.1103/kjvf-jgqj.title: Heisenberg-Limited Hamiltonian Learning Without Short-Time Control
doi:10.1103/kjvf-jgqj.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Characterizing quantum systems by learning their underlying Hamiltonians is a central task in quantum information science. While recent algorithmic advances have achieved near-optimal efficiency in this task, they critically rely on accessing arbitrarily short-time dynamics. This reliance poses severe experimental challenges due to finite control bandwidth and transient pulse errors. In this work, we demonstrate that Heisenberg-limited Hamiltonian learning can be achieved without short-time control. We introduce a framework in which every query to the unknown dynamics has duration at least a prescribed minimum time
                    <a:math xmlns:a="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <a:mi>T</a:mi>
                    </a:math>
                    , and show that this restriction does not preclude Heisenberg-limited scaling. The key ingredient is a method for emulating the continuous quantum control required by iterative learning algorithms using only such lower-bounded evolution times. This reduces the learning task to sparse pure-state tomography. Notably, for logarithmically sparse Hamiltonians, our algorithm achieves the information-theoretically optimal
                    <c:math xmlns:c="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <c:mn>1</c:mn>
                      <c:mo>/</c:mo>
                      <c:mi>ε</c:mi>
                    </c:math>
                    scaling in total evolution time for  arbitrary constant minimum evolution time
                    <e:math xmlns:e="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <e:mi>T</e:mi>
                    </e:math>
                    . For many-body (polynomially sparse) systems, we uncover a rigorous quantitative tradeoff, showing that the minimum required evolution time can be significantly relaxed from the standard limit at a polynomial cost in total evolution time. Our results affirmatively resolve a prominent open problem in the field and reveal that high-bandwidth, ultra-short pulses are not fundamentally necessary for optimal quantum learning.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.1080/10494820.2026.2749410.title: Exploring collaborative problem-solving in AI-assisted robotics education
doi:10.1080/10494820.2026.2749410.abstract: Prompt engineering (PE) involves creating, improving, and deploying prompts to improve large language model (LLM) performance. Despite its increasing importance, many students lack skills in this area. Although frameworks for prompt design and process exist, theory-based instructional tools for improving prompt engineering skills are uncommon for developing collaborative problem-solving (CPS) skills in Robotics Education. This study adopted a PE strategy in AI-assisted robotics education, particularly for developing CPS. PE has four scaffolding stages: Alignment, Adaptation, Autonomy, and Innovation, and was analysed through four PE codes: Alignment Specification, Adaptive Refinement, Auditing, and Innovation. This study adopted a non-randomised, multi-site, criterion-group comparative design, with 243 undergraduate students categorised according to their ability group. This study used epistemic network analysis (ENA) to identify the co-occurrences of PE and CPS skills and examine the differences in conversation patterns among ability groups. The findings revealed distinct PE–CPS discourse configurations across ability groups. These results underscore the pedagogical value of scaffolding in developing PE skills and fostering students’ productivity in a synergetic learning environment.

doi:10.3390/buildings16204080.title: Machine Learning-Based Evaluation of Tower Foundation Frost Jacking in the Marginal Permafrost of Northeast China
doi:10.3390/buildings16204080.abstract: <jats:p>Rapid localized permafrost degradation heightens geological risk and threatens the long-term stability of transmission towers in cold regions. Based on systematic field investigations of 336 towers in the marginal permafrost of Northeast China, thirteen conditioning factors were incorporated to evaluate five machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Logistic Regression) for foundation frost jacking susceptibility assessment, with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Geographical Detector (GeoDetector) used to quantify factor contributions and interactions. Results show that differential frost jacking poses the greatest structural hazard. Peat-rich wetland geohydrological settings constitute the highest-risk terrain for foundation uplift. Random Forest achieved the highest area under the curve of 0.987 and showed competitive performance across multiple evaluation metrics. Ground ice content was the most influential predictor, followed by land cover, soil type, and surface water. Ice content and land cover exhibited the strongest explanatory power (q = 0.78). These findings provide a quantitative and interpretable basis for frost-jacking susceptibility assessment and preliminary engineering screening within the investigated transmission corridor.</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s41935-026-00592-z.title: Smartphone-based biological sex identification from palatal rugae images: a comparative transfer learning study of pretrained convolutional neural networks
doi:10.1186/s41935-026-00592-z.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Palatal rugae are distinct anatomical ridges on the anterior part of the palate that exhibit individual-specific morphological patterns, making them valuable markers for personal identification and forensic analysis. With advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning methods have emerged as effective tools for extracting discriminative features from medical and biometric images. This study investigates the potential of transfer learning-based convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for biological sex classification using palatal rugae images captured through a smartphone camera.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>All pretrained models successfully learned discriminative biological sex -related features from palatal rugae images. Among them, Residual network 50 (ResNet50) and Visual Geometry Group 16 (VGG16) achieved the highest classification accuracy with optimal precision and recall, while EfficientNet-B0 and Dense Network 121 (DenseNet) demonstrated comparable but slightly lower performance. The Receiver Operating Curve (ROC curve) exhibited high Area under the Curve (AUC) values, confirming the strong separability between male and female classes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings confirm that smartphone-based imaging combined with transfer learning offers a promising, low-cost, and non-invasive approach for biological sex identification using palatal rugae patterns, as an adjunct tool for forensic odontology. Among the evaluated models, ResNet50 showed the most robust performance. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and incorporating explainable Artificial Intelligence methods to support clinical and forensic applicability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1177/20427530261498360.title: Reframing education 5.0 through capability theory: A framework for human-centered digital learning
doi:10.1177/20427530261498360.abstract: <jats:p>Industry 5.0 has reoriented technology-driven transformation around human-centricity, sustainability, and resilience, complementing rather than replacing Industry 4.0, with direct implications for education. Existing accounts of the resulting “Education 5.0” paradigm remain largely descriptive, synthesising a dispersed literature without an explicit theoretical mechanism or a transparent, auditable procedure for deriving the constructs they propose. This paper addresses both gaps. First, it anchors the Education 4.0-to-5.0 transition within the capability approach, using capability expansion, not technology adoption, as the mechanism linking Industry 5.0’s human-centric, sustainable, and resilient logic to curricular practice, and specifies the boundary conditions under which the framework should, and should not, be expected to hold. Second, it derives an integrative five-pillar curriculum framework - human-centric pedagogy, resilient and lifelong learning ecosystems, sustainability-embedded curricula, well-being and leadership development, and creativity through human–AI co-creation - through an explicit three-step synthesis procedure that traces each pillar to recurring literature constructs, reported as an auditable construct crosswalk rather than asserted as self-evident. Third, it formalises the framework as a computable model: an Education 5.0 Readiness Index (ER5.0I), built from Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) pillar weights, and an Industry 5.0–Education 5.0 Alignment Coefficient (IEAC), computed as cosine similarity between pillar-emphasis vectors. All numeric weights and scores are explicitly labelled as illustrative placeholders demonstrating the model’s mechanics, not empirical findings; the paper specifies the Delphi/AHP expert-panel protocol, a candidate measurement instrument, a single-institution pilot case study, and the psychometric (CFA/SEM) validation route required before the framework can be treated as measurement rather than illustration. The paper closes with theoretical and practical implications and a concrete research agenda - including a proposed Scopus/Web of Science search strategy - for validating the framework advanced here.</jats:p>

doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.6c02338.title: Beyond Co-Localization: DeepCoEx Learns Exclusion-Aware Spatial Representations in Mass Spectrometry Imaging via Dual-Contrastive Learning
doi:10.1021/acs.analchem.6c02338.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) provides spatially resolved molecular profiles, yet the existing computational workflows are heavily biased toward co-localization and remain limited in characterizing exclusion-like spatial relationships, especially when reliable negative labels are scarce. To address this challenge, we present DeepCoEx (Deep Co-localization and Exclusion), a self-supervised framework that learns exclusion-aware spatial representations through dual-contrastive learning for spatial metabolomics analysis. Instead of relying on large collections of annotated negative ion pairs, DeepCoEx embeds positive spatial consistency and exclusion-aware separation into a unified representation space. This design enables the model to preserve spatially coherent ion patterns while improving the separability of spatially complementary distributions. Compared with conventional similarity metrics and dimensionality reduction baselines, DeepCoEx provides more consistent and interpretable retrieval of candidate negative spatial associations. In representative control and PM2.5-exposed rat brains, the framework reveals localized spatial redistribution patterns and brainstem-related complementary ion associations that are not readily captured by conventional correlation-based analysis. In barley seeds, the learned embeddings help resolve chemically related ion species, including protonated and sodiated adducts of phosphatidylcholine species and glycosylated hordatine derivatives. Furthermore, DeepCoEx supports subregion-specific network construction, enabling exploratory analysis of localized molecular association patterns under different tissue or treatment contexts. By establishing an exclusion-aware representation learning strategy for MSI, DeepCoEx expands spatial metabolomics beyond co-localization and provides a practical workflow for analyzing complementary molecular organization in complex tissues.</jats:p>

doi:10.54005/geneltip.1866460.title: Evaluation of MRI-Based Radiomic Texture Analysis and Ensemble Machine Learning Models in the Diagnosis of Hemifacial Spasm
doi:10.54005/geneltip.1866460.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Aim: To investigate whether MRI-derived texture (radiomic) features combined with machine learning can provide objective diagnostic discrimination between patients with hemifacial spasm (HFS) and healthy controls, and to evaluate the added value of high-resolution 3D T2-SPACE imaging.Materials and Methods: This retrospective study included 35 patients with clinically diagnosed HFS and 36 age- and sex-matched controls. All subjects underwent 3-Tesla MRI with axial T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and a subgroup of 21 HFS patients and their matched controls also underwent 3D T2-SPACE imaging. Segmentation was performed across axial slices encompassing the brainstem, the entire posterior fossa, and the inner ear, middle ear, and mastoid portions, with the anterior boundary extending to the clivus, using a single manually drawn region of interest (ROI) to capture comprehensive radiomic features. 137 radiomic texture features were extracted using the PyRadiomics platform. Multiple machine learning classifiers, including k-nearest neighbors, Naive Bayes, discriminant analysis, decision trees, and ensemble learning methods, were evaluated. Data were split into 80% training and 20% testing sets, and performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and ROC-AUC over 20 randomized repetitions.Results: Among all tested models, the Ensemble Bagged Trees classifier demonstrated the highest overall performance among the tested models. Using T2WI, the model achieved a mean accuracy of 0.71 ± 0.10, sensitivity of 0.72 ± 0.15, specificity of 0.70 ± 0.18, and ROC-AUC of 0.76 ± 0.16. In the subgroup analyzed with high-resolution 3D T2-SPACE imaging, performance further improved, yielding a mean accuracy of 0.80 ± 0.12, sensitivity of 0.67 ± 0.23, specificity of 0.95 ± 0.12, and ROC-AUC of 0.85 ± 0.11. High-resolution T2-SPACE images provided an improvement in specificity compared with conventional T2WI.Conclusions: Radiomic texture features extracted from conventional and high-resolution MRI, when combined with ensemble machine learning methods, show potential for facilitating discrimination between patients with hemifacial spasm and healthy controls. The particularly high specificity achieved with 3D T2-SPACE imaging suggests that this approach may serve as a promising complementary diagnostic tool, supporting conventional imaging and clinical assessment and offering a step toward objective, image-based biomarkers for HFS.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10858203/v1.title: Development of a Foundation AI-Based Multimodal Human Machine Interaction Framework for Intelligent Accelerometer-Assisted Robotic Hand Glove Control in Parkinson's Disease
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10858203/v1.abstract: This study proposes a Foundation Artificial Intelligence (Foundation AI)-based multimodal human–machine interaction framework for an intelligent accelerometer-assisted robotic hand glove to support personalized upper-limb rehabilitation in Parkinson's disease patients. Approximately 150 participants (120 Parkinson's disease patients with Hoehn and Yahr Stage II–III and 30 healthy elderly volunteers) perform six clinically relevant Activities of Daily Living (ADLs), including grasping, eating, drinking, writing, dressing, and opening doors, to capture realistic neuromuscular movement patterns. The lightweight soft robotic glove integrates surface EMG sensors, an IMU incorporating a three-axis accelerometer and gyroscope, flex sensors, force-sensitive resistors, pressure sensors, vibration sensors, and temperature sensors to continuously monitor muscle activity, hand kinematics, tremor characteristics, grip force, wrist orientation, and movement acceleration. The embedded accelerometer enhances movement intention recognition by detecting motion direction, velocity, posture transitions, and dynamic hand activities. To improve accessibility, the framework incorporates three intelligent human–machine interaction modules: voice command control using Whisper and a Bidirectional Transformer for speech-driven robotic assistance; vision-based control via an external webcam, employing MediaPipe Hands for real-time hand landmark detection and Vision Transformer (ViT) for gesture recognition and movement intention estimation; and a mobile healthcare platform supporting personalized rehabilitation, remote monitoring, and secure telemedicine communication through Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), MQTT, and AES-256 encryption. The visual features extracted from the webcam are fused with multimodal physiological and motion signals through a Multimodal Foundation Transformer (MFT) incorporating cross-modal attention and self-supervised contrastive learning to estimate movement intention, tremor severity, hand gesture, finger trajectory, grasp type, and grip force. An Adaptive Impedance Controller subsequently personalizes robotic assistance by regulating actuator torque, finger motion, and wrist orientation in real time while continuously adapting to patient-specific neuromuscular conditions. The proposed framework establishes an intelligent multimodal perception and control architecture for personalized robotic rehabilitation and provides the computational foundation for future Digital Twin-enabled adaptive neuro-rehabilitation.

doi:10.67695/elay6553.title: They Deserve Training Too! Online Program Development Training for Deans and Chairs
doi:10.67695/elay6553.abstract: <jats:p>Academic Program Leaders (APL), including department chairs, associate deans, and deans, are essential to the successful development of fully online programs. However, APLs may lack academic training or direct experience with online instructional design, online pedagogy, online course quality assurance, and federal requirements for online/distance education. This paper describes the development of a training and resource course to help APLs be able to explain the course development process and the roles involved in online course development, articulate their responsibilities during online program planning process, identify specific ways that they can support the faculty subject matter experts and instructional designers in the course development process, evaluate an online template course for program alignment and discipline requirements and facilitate communication between the instructional design team and faculty teaching the course during deployment.</jats:p>

doi:10.55933/pjga.v7i1.1341.title: The Application of Visual Media-Assisted Direct Instruction to Improve Forward Roll Learning Outcomes
doi:10.55933/pjga.v7i1.1341.abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to examine the development of students’ forward roll learning outcomes through Direct Instruction with progressively added visual support among seventh-grade students in Class VII E at SMP Negeri 1 Semarang. The study employed Classroom Action Research based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model over two cycles, preceded by a pre-intervention phase. The participants were 32 students, consisting of 15 boys and 17 girls. Data were collected through observation and practical assessment using a forward roll skill rubric with five indicators, each scored from 1–5, with a maximum score of 25. Cycle I implemented Direct Instruction without video through teacher explanation, demonstration, guided practice, verbal feedback, and repeated practice. Based on reflection from Cycle I, Cycle II maintained Direct Instruction and added video demonstrations and a movement poster as visual support. Data were analyzed descriptively by comparing mean scores and the percentage of students achieving a minimum score of 20. The mean score increased from 9.84 in the pre-intervention phase to 16.60 in Cycle I and 19.87 in Cycle II. Students achieving a minimum score of 20 increased from 0% to 9.37% and 62.50%. The findings indicate progressive development in forward roll learning outcomes during the classroom action research process.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10346520/v3.title: A Unified Model of Learning and Habituation under Mechanical Stimulation in the protozoan Stentor coeruleus
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10346520/v3.abstract: Repeated mechanical stimulation of Stentor coeruleus can produce an early enhancement of contraction probability, habituation, recovery, and altered responses after rest. These observations have usually been studied in different protocols and laboratories. In this study, I developed a single model combining response enhancement, habituation, and stimulus history. Each simulated cell updates its states from its own binary contraction events; the population fraction is predicted by averaging across their histories. The model was fitted to a limited subset of the weak–strong pairing experiments of Doan and colleagues, the repeated bout experiments of Ramdas and colleagues, and recovery curves digitized from the experiments of Rajan and Marshall. Other complete protocols were reserved for evaluation. Mean held-out protocol RMSE in contraction probability was 0.041 for the pairing experiments, 0.057 for the repeated-bout experiments, and 0.240 for the digitized recovery experiments. Mechanistic parameter ablations increased errors in the domains most affected by their corresponding states. The large error in the digitized Rajan and Marshall recovery data, especially after long training at the lower stimulation frequency, shows that a shared stimulus scale does not account for between-cohort and between-laboratory differences. The model therefore connects several forms of learning-like behavior in one quantitative framework while placing a clear limit on its present generality. I propose a reporting framework for mechanical stimulation experiments that can separate stimulus calibration, initial state, and recovery dynamics.

doi:10.26877/jettle.v2i2.4615.title: Utilization of Kito-Pin Media through the PBL Model to Improve the Mathematics Learning Outcomes of Grade III Students
doi:10.26877/jettle.v2i2.4615.abstract: <jats:p>This study was motivated by the issue of low mathematics learning outcomes among Grade III A students at SDN Pandeanlamper 03 Semarang. To address this problem, the implementation of an appropriate learning model and media is essential to support improved student achievement. The aim of this study was to determine the effectiveness of using the Kito-Pin learning media through the Problem Based Learning (PBL) model in enhancing students' mathematics learning outcomes. This research employed a Classroom Action Research (CAR) method based on the Kemmis and Taggart model, which consists of four stages: planning, action, observation, and reflection. The study was conducted in two cycles, with two meetings in each cycle. The research subjects were 28 students, comprising 13 male and 15 female students. The results showed an improvement in students’ learning outcomes. In Cycle I, classical completeness reached 75% with an average score of 74.64, which increased in Cycle II to 89.29% with an average score of 85.36. These findings indicate that the use of Kito-Pin media through the PBL model is effective in improving students’ mathematics learning outcomes. Moreover, the learning process became more meaningful, enjoyable, and encouraged students to be active, enthusiastic, and to understand the material more deeply through their learning experiences.</jats:p>
doi:10.26877/jettle.v2i2.4615.venue: Journal of Emerging Technology in Teaching and Learning (JETTLe)

doi:10.3390/bioengineering13101203.title: Label-Free Biochemical Characterization and Subtype Classification of Human Breast Pathologies Using Fingerprint Raman Spectroscopy and Machine Learning
doi:10.3390/bioengineering13101203.abstract: <jats:p>Breast cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, highlighting the need for improved molecular characterization of breast pathologies. Raman spectroscopy (RS) provides a label-free, non-destructive approach for probing tissue biochemical composition. This study investigated Raman spectral alterations across five human breast histopathological categories and explored their potential for machine learning-assisted classification. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue specimens were obtained from five patients, with one patient representing each category: normal breast tissue, intraductal papilloma, high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC), and invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC). A total of 100 Raman spectra (20 per patient) were acquired using 785 nm excitation over the fingerprint region (500–2000 cm−1). Spectral preprocessing involved Savitzky–Golay smoothing, asymmetrically reweighted penalized least-squares (arPLS) baseline correction, and vector normalization. The investigated spectra exhibited reduced relative lipid-associated contributions near 1063, 1300, and 1445 cm−1, accompanied by increased relative protein- and nucleic-acid-associated features near 1003, 1420, and 1600–1650 cm−1. The phenylalanine-to-lipid intensity ratio (I1003/I1445) increased from ≤0.2 in normal tissue to ≥1.5 in invasive lesions, suggesting a potential spectroscopic descriptor of biochemical remodeling. Exploratory subtype-associated differences were also observed, including a prominent aromatic C=C-associated feature near 1618 cm−1 in IDC and an enhanced carbohydrate-associated contribution near 890 cm−1 in ILC. A support vector machine (SVM) classifier was evaluated using patient-independent leave-one-patient-out (LOPO) cross-validation. Across the five held-out patients, the model correctly classified 89 of 100 spectra, achieving an overall spectrum-level accuracy of 89.0%, sensitivity of 90.0%, specificity of 87.5%, and F1-score of 90.8%. Although these findings demonstrate encouraging discrimination within the investigated cohort, the limited number of biologically independent patients and the representation of each histopathological category by a single patient restrict the generalizability of the results. This study provides preliminary proof-of-concept evidence supporting the integration of Raman-derived biochemical features with machine learning for breast pathology characterization, warranting further validation in larger, multi-patient and multicenter cohorts.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/math14203766.title: Safety-Certified Hierarchical Control of DC Microgrids via Continuous Deep Reinforcement Learning and Covariance-Weighted Sliding Mode Synthesis
doi:10.3390/math14203766.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a hierarchical safe control approach for DC microgrids, combining learning-based energy management with rigorous constraint enforcement. The main novelty is a covariance-aware coupling mechanism that simultaneously informs CBF constraint tightening, sliding-mode gain scheduling, and DRL state augmentation. A continuous Soft Actor-Critic agent generates smooth current references and a flexible load-shedding ratio. A predictive CBF quadratic program acts as a safety filter, using online confidence intervals from a recursive least-squares predictor. The filter ensures a sampled-data safety property with an inter-sample margin, applying to the actual uncertain microgrid via a robust-CBF term, provided the QP is feasible with zero slack and the true voltage stays within the confidence interval. The same covariance information serves as an online uncertainty metric for adaptive gain and weight scheduling. A composite Lyapunov–CBF theorem proves uniform ultimate boundedness and constraint satisfaction. Simulations under severe conditions show high-probability constraint satisfaction with negligible slack, while improving transient recovery and reducing battery stress. Comparisons with fuzzy logic, discrete DQL, and plain SAC isolate the CBF contribution, and ablation studies assess individual components. While robust MPC can also enforce constraints, the proposed method achieves comparable satisfaction with lower complexity. A clear distinction is maintained between theoretical guarantees and simulation observations.</jats:p>

doi:10.1117/1.oe.65.10.103103.title: Physics-inspired lightweight deep learning for holographic imaging with computational dimensionality reduction
doi:10.1117/1.oe.65.10.103103.abstract: <jats:p>Holographic imaging poses an ill-posed inverse problem of reconstructing complex optical fields from measured diffraction intensity patterns. Existing deep-learning-based holographic imaging methods tend to rely mainly on statistical relationships learned from training data, which may compromise their reliability in practical imaging configurations. We propose a physics-inspired lightweight deep learning approach for holographic imaging with computational dimensionality reduction. The experimentally acquired full-resolution hologram is computationally reduced by deterministic 2×2 block averaging for complex-field reconstruction, while the full-resolution hologram is retained for axial distance estimation and hologram-domain physical consistency. This asymmetric reduced-input/full-resolution coupling constitutes the principal system-level architectural contribution and does not imply reduced camera exposure, sensor readout, or physical acquisition time. A computational super-resolution network reconstructs full-resolution amplitude and phase from the reduced-dimensional hologram, followed by a refined module to improve reconstruction fidelity. LIght Spatial Transition (LIST)-based lightweight modifications further reduce model complexity. Compared with physics-inspired optimal transmission-driven cycle-consistent generative adversarial network, the proposed lightweight model reduces the parameter count, multiply-accumulate operations (MACs), and peak inference memory, although its measured single-frame graphics processing unit (GPU) inference latency is slightly higher. Experiments on microspheres, red blood cells, and irregular cellular morphologies demonstrate competitive complex-field reconstruction and distance estimation while substantially reducing model size and computational requirements.</jats:p>

doi:10.4324/9781003747628.title: Healthcare That Learns
doi:10.4324/9781003747628.abstract: Healthcare has more evidence, data, and artificial intelligence (AI) than ever. A risk model can flag a patient, a dashboard can reveal a gap, and a guideline can recommend the next step. But if no one owns the response, if the workflow cannot support action, or if the patient’s reality is not part of the loop, better information does not become better care. Healthcare That Learns: Value-Based Care and the AI-Enabled Learning Health System argues that the central challenge is not discovery, technology, or payment reform. It is conversion: turning practice into data, data into knowledge, knowledge into standards, standards into routines, and routines back into better practice. Written for health system executives, clinical leaders, informaticians, quality and safety professionals, policymakers, clinicians, and trainees, this book offers a practical operating model for the AI-enabled learning health system. It shows how value-based care, AI, informatics, operations, governance, equity, implementation, and workforce readiness must work together to close the know–do gap and make better care routine. Through real-world cases and a clear learning architecture, the book explains why AI creates value only when connected to trustworthy data, legitimate standards, owned workflows, response capacity, monitoring, and patient partnership. It also shows how organizations can reduce avoidable variation, govern AI responsibly, design for bioequity, and measure return on learning rather than isolated project gains. At a moment when health systems are investing heavily in digital transformation while struggling to improve outcomes at sustainable cost, Healthcare That Learns offers a road map for organizations that must learn continuously, act responsibly, and improve care that matters.

doi:10.67512/jcseam.v1.i3.2.title: A Smart Energy System Design Using Neuro-Inspired Models and Evolutionary Optimization
doi:10.67512/jcseam.v1.i3.2.abstract: Brain-inspired artificial intelligence offers a potential avenue for enhancing adaptive, efficient and intelligent computing systems in various applications. This research seeks to investigate the structure, efficiency and implementation of neuro-inspired algorithms and models for improving machine learning in health care, edge computing and smart systems. This study adopts a holistic approach to integrating recent research on brain-inspired algorithms, such as evolutionary algorithms, synaptic learning rules, and hybrid deep learning models, and compares their efficiency, adaptability and interpretability. The findings show that neuro-inspired models offer substantial enhancements in learning efficiency, energy-efficiency, and decision-making, particularly in complex and big data environments like medical applications and IoT systems. Moreover, incorporating hardware technologies such as memristor chips and AI accelerators also improves speed and scalability. The results also demonstrate the ability of these models to enable continuous learning and dynamic adaptation. In summary, neuro-inspired AI offers a novel avenue to build next-generation energy-efficient and adaptive intelligent systems, but there are also challenges in scaling and practical implementation that need to be addressed.

doi:10.48550/arxiv.2610.20673.title: HPCAgent-Bench: A Framework for Sound Benchmarking of Code-Optimizing Agents, Harnesses, and Skills
doi:10.48550/arxiv.2610.20673.abstract: Coding agents are increasingly used to optimize code, but existing benchmarks fix one accelerator, programming model or harness, so they cannot isolate what each component contributes or show whether added skills and tools repay their cost. We present HPCAgent-Bench with 689 kernels in three tracks: loop-level optimization challenges, kernels extracted from HPC codes, and machine-learning models. The framework specifies each kernel once in NumPy, derives C and Fortran references, accepts submissions through a common C ABI or Python interface, and runs them on CPUs or GPUs, on one or multiple nodes. An external judge checks correctness on hidden fuzzed inputs and times each submission, closing paths agents use to exploit the testing system. We introduce two metrics for reporting results: \textit{intervention efficacy} measures an intervention, such as adding a tool, through paired runs on speedup, success rate and cost, and \textit{weighted token cost} reports input, cached-input and output tokens under explicit weights. Agents reach up to $4.2\times$ speedup over automatic parallelizers, and their optimizations transfer to another machine: $93$--$99\%$ of answers without device-specific code remain correct, and per-kernel speedups keep a rank correlation of $r_s\ge0.84$. Across 40 matched setups, interventions significantly change speedup only twice but token cost by up to $3.0\times$. Because token weighting decides whether a saving is significant, we state the weights and release every token count as a standard for cost reporting. We provide the first comprehensive, broad and hardened benchmark for the sound evaluation of agentic optimization, with transparent cost metrics.

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-76381-4.title: An adaptive congestion-aware graph neural routing framework with hybrid microcoded event-driven control for network-on-chip systems
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-76381-4.abstract: Network-on-Chip (NoC) architectures have become a fundamental communication backbone for many-core processors, artificial intelligence accelerators, edge-computing platforms, and high-performance embedded systems. However, achieving efficient packet routing in large-scale NoCs remains challenging due to dynamic traffic variations, congestion propagation, limited global network visibility, and stringent hardware constraints. Conventional deterministic and heuristic routing algorithms suffer from reduced adaptability under non-uniform traffic conditions, whereas existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based routers primarily rely on local state representations and finite-state-machine (FSM) controllers, limiting their scalability, topology awareness, and hardware deployability. To address these limitations, this work proposes an Adaptive Congestion-Aware Graph Neural Routing Framework with Hybrid Microcoded Event-Driven Control for Network-on-Chip Systems. The proposed framework integrates three complementary components: (i) an Adaptive Congestion-Aware Graph Neural Network (ACA-GNN) encoder that generates compact topology-aware embeddings by capturing local and multi-hop congestion dependencies through congestion-aware message propagation, (ii) a quantized Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) agent that performs low-latency adaptive routing decisions using compact graph embeddings, and (iii) a Hybrid Microcoded Event-Driven Controller (H-µEDC) that replaces conventional FSM-based control with programmable event-triggered micro-routines to ensure deterministic routing execution. The proposed architecture is implemented on a Xilinx Zynq-7000 FPGA and evaluated using BookSim2 cycle-accurate simulation, Orion 3.0 power modeling, synthetic traffic patterns, and PARSEC/Rodinia benchmark workloads. Experimental results demonstrate up to 48% lower packet latency, and 31% lower energy per flit compared with state-of-the-art heuristic and machine-learning-based routing approaches. Hardware implementation further requires only 1.2% LUTs, 1.4% flip-flops, three DSP blocks, one BRAM, and 0.556 W power consumption while maintaining deterministic single-cycle routing decisions using cached ACA-GNN embeddings. These results demonstrate that the proposed ACA-GNN-HµEDC framework effectively combines topology-aware routing intelligence, congestion adaptivity, hardware efficiency, and scalability, making it a practical solution for next-generation many-core Network-on-Chip systems.

doi:10.3390/en19204903.title: Vehicle Type Heterogeneity in Battery Electric Vehicle Energy Consumption: A Multi-Perspective Analysis Using Real-World Fleet Data
doi:10.3390/en19204903.abstract: Real-world energy consumption of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) varies with trip conditions, driving behavior, and vehicle state. Treating vehicle type merely as a control variable may mask substantial heterogeneity in energy consumption mechanisms. This study treats vehicle type as a source of mechanism heterogeneity and examines how the determinants of energy consumption rate (ECR) differ among sedans, logistics vehicles, and buses. Using 41,933 trips in China, we combined statistical analysis, machine learning, and CausalForestDML. Statistically, ECRs of sedans and logistics vehicles decrease as trip distance increases, but trip distance is nearly irrelevant for buses. Aggressive driving raises logistics vehicle ECR by 22.2% yet barely affects sedans. For prediction, permutation importance further reveals the divergence: trip distance and duration dominate sedan prediction, whereas energy recovery ratio and accelerator-pedal, which are marginally important for sedans, become primary predictors for logistics vehicles and buses. Causal estimates confirm that directional divergences persist after conditioning on covariates. For example, trip duration has opposite effects on buses versus sedans and logistics vehicles. Moreover, the causal framework decomposes each factor’s effects across its value range, revealing patterns beyond correlation alone. These findings provide actionable guidance for vehicle-specific eco-driving strategies and battery management system optimization.

doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1528.c6167.title: Endüstriyel Kalite Kontrolde Derin Öğrenme Tabanlı Görsel Muayene Sistemleri: Yöntemler, Anomali Tespiti ve Gerçek Zamanlı Uygulamalar
doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1528.c6167.abstract: <jats:p>Endüstriyel görsel muayene sistemleri; yüzey kusurları, eksik veya hatalı montaj, geometrik bozukluklar, baskı ve etiket hataları, renk farklılıkları ve yabancı nesneler gibi üretim hatalarının otomatik olarak belirlenmesinde kullanılmaktadır. Klasik makine görmesi uygulamalarında eşikleme, kenar çıkarımı, morfolojik işlemler ve elle tasarlanmış özniteliklere dayalı yöntemler kullanılabilirken, ürün görünümündeki değişkenlik, karmaşık yüzey dokuları ve değişen üretim koşulları sabit kurallara dayalı yöntemlerin uygulanmasını zorlaştırmaktadır. Derin öğrenme tabanlı yöntemler ise görüntü özelliklerinin doğrudan veriden öğrenilmesine olanak sağlayarak sınıflandırma, nesne tespiti, segmentasyon ve anomali tespiti gibi farklı görsel muayene problemlerinde kullanılabilmektedir. Bu bölümde derin öğrenme tabanlı görsel muayene yaklaşımları algoritmik performansın yanı sıra üretim hattında uygulanabilirlik açısından incelenmiştir. Etiketli kusurlu örneklerin bulunduğu uygulamalar ile kusurlu örneklerin sınırlı olduğu anomali tespiti problemleri değerlendirilmiş; zero-shot ve few-shot yaklaşımlar, sentetik anomali üretimi ve veri dengesizliği ele alınmıştır. Kamera çözünürlüğü, optik sistem, aydınlatma, hareket bulanıklığı, gerçek zamanlı çıkarım, edge deployment ve PLC tabanlı üretim hattı entegrasyonu tartışılmıştır. Bu nedenle sistem başarısı yalnızca model doğruluğuyla değil; minimum tespit edilebilir kusur boyutu, yanlış kabul ve yanlış ret oranları, toplam karar gecikmesi, proses senkronizasyonu ve gerçek üretim koşullarındaki doğrulama sonuçlarıyla birlikte değerlendirilmelidir.</jats:p>

doi:10.18260/jet.43.2.5.abstract: <jats:p>This exploratory study presents an abstraction hierarchy model as a preliminary course design framework for assessing the information and functions associated with applied ML classroom projects from engineering and technology courses.</jats:p>

doi:10.67903/ijroms0494.title: Lived Experiences of Music, Arts, Physical Education, and Health Teachers and Students in Teaching and Learning Music 8 in Zumarraga District
doi:10.67903/ijroms0494.abstract: <jats:p>This qualitative study explored the lived experiences of Music, Arts, Physical Education, and Health (MAPEH) teachers and students in teaching and learning Music 8 in selected public secondary schools in the Zumarraga District, Schools Division of Samar. Guided by a phenomenological research design, data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 5 MAPEH teachers selected through total enumeration sampling and 21 Grade 8 students selected through purposive sampling based on academic performance and participation. Transcribed interview data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis framework to identify recurring patterns, core themes, and shared essences. Findings revealed that teaching Music 8 is both deeply meaningful and pedagogically challenging. Teachers demonstrated adaptability and resourcefulness despite structural constraints—such as limited musical instruments, insufficient instructional materials, and diverse learner abilities by utilizing local improvisation, digital multimedia tools, and performance-based teaching strategies. Students reported that Music 8 was highly enjoyable and engaging, fostering creativity, self-confidence, and self-expression, yet they encountered notable difficulties mastering technical musical skills, such as reading notation and maintaining rhythm, due to restricted practice opportunities and inadequate facilities. Teacher guidance, peer collaboration, and sustained institutional support were identified as crucial factors for elevating student learning outcomes. The study concluded that effective, inclusive music instruction requires adaptive teaching methodologies, equitable resource distribution, and robust organizational support systems. Based on these insights, a policy framework titled Enhanced Music 8 Instructional Support and Capacity Building Policy was proposed to strengthen teacher competence particularly for non-MAPEH majors and promote sustainable, meaningful music education in rural public secondary schools.</jats:p>

doi:10.31223/x59b92.title: Leveraging satellite data and machine learning to quantify rooftop rainwater harvesting reliability and tank requirements for schools and health care facilities in Uganda
doi:10.31223/x59b92.abstract: <jats:p>Many schools and health facilities in Uganda lack a reliable water supply, yet most have roofs that could collect rain. For 41,592 facilities (32,881 schools and 8,711 health facilities), we estimated how much water their roofs can supply, how large a tank each one needs, and how often that supply fails. Roof areas came from AI-derived building footprints (Google Open Buildings v3) and daily rainfall for 1981 to 2025 from CHIRPS. A daily yield-after-spillage tank model gave the supply available on 90% of days and the smallest tank that meets each facility's demand on 90% of days. On a standard 200 m² roof, a 10 m³ tank supplied a median of 359 litres per day on 90% of days, from 255 L in the Northern region to 411 L in the Eastern region; at the same annual rainfall, Northern facilities received about 40% less because their rain falls in one long season. With mapped roofs, 77.1% of schools and 62.2% of health facilities could reach the target with a tank of 200 m³ or less, and among these the median school needed 39.5 m³ and the median health facility 5.0 m³. The school share ranged from 42.3% to 92.8% across enrolment scenarios and fell to 44.1% if only buildings within 60 m are connected and to 37.8% if only 30% of the mapped roof feeds the tank. A machine-learning model trained on the simulations predicted the required tank within 25% for 97.0% of facilities in spatial cross-validation, against 8.3% for the dry-period rule of thumb. With a 20% margin its tanks met the target at 97.5% of facilities, but at only 74.5% when the nearest training data were at least 110 km away, where the rule's larger tanks were more dependable. Reliability rose slightly over 1981 to 2025, with a significant trend at 15.1% of facilities. A retrospective seasonal analysis found useful skill only for September to November, coming from tank storage and recent rain rather than El Niño or Indian Ocean Dipole indices. The results are screening estimates that need confirmation on site; the code and data are released openly.</jats:p>

doi:10.63090/ijters/3049.1614.0056.title: From Synthetic Fluency to Authentic Learning: Redesigning ESL Teaching and Assessment Methodologies in the Age of AI
doi:10.63090/ijters/3049.1614.0056.abstract:
<jats:p>This paper emerges from a practical concern observed in ESL classrooms: students are producing increasingly polished written work with AI support, yet struggling to demonstrate the same level of competence under exam conditions. This gap raises important questions about how teaching, learning, and assessment currently align. Recent studies indicate significant discrepancies between AI-supported coursework and performance in proctored examinations, raising concerns about the validity of traditional assessment practices. This paper conceptualises this phenomenon as synthetic fluency, where students produce linguistically accurate outputs without corresponding internalised competence.

Focusing on ESL provision within General Foundation Programme (GFP) in Oman, the study argues that the core issue is not academic misconduct, but a systemic failure of pedagogical alignment. Drawing on recent international research and practice-based insights and based on the analysis of GFP results for summative assessments in different settings, the paper analyses how AI has disrupted the relationship between teaching methodologies, learning processes, and assessment systems.

In response, the study proposes an integrated framework for redesigning ESL pedagogy in AI-augmented environments. We can reconceptualise teaching as a process of cognitive apprenticeship supported by guided AI use, while assessment will shift from product-based evaluation to process-based validation through interconnected tasks, AI transparency, and oral defence mechanisms. The paper introduces a three-layer model consisting of AI-declared work, cognitive trace, and authenticity validation.

This model can be realistically implemented in GFP contexts, with direct implications for how we design assessment, support learning, and define academic integrity.</jats:p>
doi:10.63090/ijters/3049.1614.0056.venue: International Journal of Teacher Education Research Studies (IJTERS)

doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0016.title: Time-Series Anomaly Detection: Benchmark Flaws, Evaluation Metrics and Strong Baselines
doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0016.abstract: <jats:p>Dozens of deep architectures for time-series anomaly detection have been published since 2018, most of them reporting higher scores than their predecessors on the same handful of datasets. A series of critical studies now suggests that much of this progress is an artefact. The datasets have flaws that make them easy or mislabelled. The most common scoring protocol, point adjustment, inflates results so strongly that random scores can compete with trained models. And when classical or deliberately simple methods are run under the same conditions, they often match the deep ones. This review assembles that evidence. We describe the method families briefly, then examine the benchmark critiques, the evaluation metrics and their failure modes, and the large comparison studies. A small worked example, constructed by hand and labelled as such, shows the arithmetic of point adjustment. We end with a reporting checklist and with the open question of whether pretrained time-series models change the picture. Apart from that worked example, no new result is reported.</jats:p>
doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0016.venue: Eduschool International Journal of Data Science and Machine learning (EIJDSML)

doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0015.title: Temporal Variability of Nocturnal Wind Direction over India: A Non-Parametric Circular Statistical Approach
doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0015.abstract: <jats:p>Wind direction is an inherently circular variable, and conventional linear statistical techniques are therefore inadequate for describing its variability and its evolution over time. This study examined the temporal variation of nocturnal wind direction using high-frequency meteorological observations recorded at monitoring stations across India during August 2023. Observations were pooled across stations and assigned to eight consecutive hourly intervals spanning 21:00 to 05:00 local time. Wind direction was treated as the principal circular variable and wind speed as the associated linear variable, from which wind power density was derived. Equality of the eight directional distributions was tested using the Mardia–Watson–Wheeler uniform-scores test, a non-parametric procedure for comparing several circular populations. Directional concentration was quantified by the mean resultant length, the association between wind speed and wind direction by Mardia's circular–linear correlation coefficient, and the directional structure of wind occurrence and wind energy by rose diagrams. The eight hourly wind-direction distributions differed significantly (W = 1916.26, df = 14, p < 0.001), indicating a systematic reorganisation of nocturnal wind circulation rather than random directional fluctuation. Directional concentration was greatest during 21:00–22:00 (R̄ = 0.6383), fell to a minimum of approximately 0.08 between 23:00 and 02:00, and recovered only partially by 04:00–05:00 (R̄ = 0.2492). The circular–linear correlation coefficient, which measures strength of association only and does not carry a sign, was 0.3060 for the pooled data. Interval-wise values were highest early in the night (0.4722 at 21:00–22:00) and again at 23:00–00:00 (0.4568), reached a minimum at 01:00–02:00 (0.1929), and recovered to 0.3212 by 04:00–05:00; the association therefore weakened around the middle of the night rather than declining steadily. These results are relevant to wind-resource assessment, boundary-layer meteorology, aviation operations and short-term weather forecasting.</jats:p>
doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0015.venue: Eduschool International Journal of Data Science and Machine learning (EIJDSML)

doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0014.title: Federated and Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning: Methods and Trade-offs
doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0014.abstract: <jats:p>Federated learning trains a shared model across many decentralized clients while keeping raw data on the device, which addresses data silos and tightening privacy regulation such as GDPR and HIPAA. This paper reviews the methods and the practical trade-offs of federated and privacy-preserving machine learning. The discussion begins with the FedAvg protocol and the distinction between cross-device settings, with millions of intermittent participants, and cross-silo settings, with a small set of reliable institutions. Statistical heterogeneity, where client data is non-IID, slows convergence and biases the global model; proximal correction in FedProx and control variates in SCAFFOLD reduce this client drift. Because the uplink is often the bottleneck, the survey covers gradient compression, quantization, and sparsification that cut communication cost by an order of magnitude. Sharing model updates is not by itself private: membership inference and gradient leakage attacks can recover sensitive information, so the paper examines differential privacy, secure aggregation, and homomorphic encryption as defenses, together with the accuracy cost each one carries. Personalization methods that adapt the global model to local distributions are summarized, followed by applications in healthcare, mobile keyboards, and finance. Illustrative experiments on a non-IID benchmark show SCAFFOLD reaching a target accuracy in fewer rounds than FedAvg, and a differential-privacy sweep quantifies the privacy-utility curve. The results are illustrative and do not describe a deployed production system.</jats:p>

doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0013.title: Enhancing Cardiac Auscultation with Machine Learning and Deep Learning: A Survey on Heart Sound Analysis
doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0013.abstract: <jats:p>Cardiovascular disease kills more people than anything else. Early detection changes outcomes, and heart sounds are one of the cheapest places to look for the first signs. Phonocardiogram (PCG) recordings carry information about valve function that a trained ear can pick up, which is why auscultation has survived two centuries of newer imaging and why it is still the first test a patient meets. But listening is slow. It needs experience, and two clinicians can disagree about the same murmur. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) offer a way to automate that step and make it reproducible. This review asks what the literature has actually achieved, and what it has not. We searched IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, PubMed, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar for work published between 2015 and 2024. Section 2 gives the search strings, the screening steps and the inclusion rules. Thirty-seven primary studies survived. Each was read in full, and its dataset, signal processing chain, model and reported performance were recorded in a comparison table that covers thirteen of them in detail. Reported accuracy in this field is high and rising. It is also, taken at face value, misleading. The studies reviewed here use different corpora, different class definitions, different segmentation strategies and different validation protocols, so 99.80% in one paper and 73.6% in another are not measuring the same thing. Standardised datasets are missing. So are agreed metrics. Paediatric recordings are thin on the ground, recording conditions vary, and almost nothing here has been tested in the clinic where it would have to work. The review pulls recent advances together, then sets the reported numbers against the methodological limits that decide how much those numbers are worth, which surveys in this area tend to skip.</jats:p>
doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0013.venue: Eduschool International Journal of Data Science and Machine learning (EIJDSML)

doi:10.46838/jbic.v7i2.1410.title: Pengembangan E-Engklek Math Game Berbasis Web dengan Pendekatan Hypothetical Learning Trajectory pada Materi Bilangan Rasional untuk Meningkatkan Kemampuan Berpikir Kritis Matematis Siswa Kelas VII SMP
doi:10.46838/jbic.v7i2.1410.abstract: <jats:p>Seventh-grade students at SMP Nurul Khoir Jambi showed very low mathematical critical thinking: on an essay-type preliminary test taken by 25 students, the mean score was 31.50% of the maximum, and interpretation was the weakest indicator (3.0%). This article aims to design E-Engklek Math Game, a web-based mathematics learning game that adapts the Indonesian hopscotch game Engklek to the topic of rational numbers through a Hypothetical Learning Trajectory (HLT) approach. The study is Research and Development using the ADDIE model, and this article reports only the Analysis and Design phases. Data were collected through classroom observation, a teacher interview, a student needs questionnaire, the preliminary test, and a review of the Phase D curriculum, and were analysed using descriptive statistics and qualitative data reduction. The analysis translated the test profile and classroom conditions into four functional requirements, the most decisive being that students must state the known and asked information before calculating. The design phase produced product specifications, a mapping of game actions to rational number concepts and four critical thinking indicators, a six-stage HLT specifying predicted responses, likely errors, and planned feedback, a nine-screen storyboard, and draft evaluation instruments. The design contribution lies in using the HLT to make an interpretation step a required condition on every game square and to link hints and feedback to anticipated errors. The product has not yet been developed, validated, or tested; its validity, practicality, and effectiveness will be examined in the Development, Implementation, and Evaluation phases.</jats:p>

doi:10.14738/assrj.1310.12327.title: Developing Policy Recommendations for Vocational Education Management at Community Learning Centers in Crisis Situations
doi:10.14738/assrj.1310.12327.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines how Community Learning Centers (CLCs) in Cambodia managed vocational education during the COVID-19 pandemic and develops evidence-based policy recommendations to strengthen institutional resilience in future crises. Adopting policy evidence-based qualitative research design, the study was conducted in two phases. Phase 1 involved semi-structured interviews with 18 participants-three administrators, six trainers, and nine learners-and applied thematic analysis to examine policy implementation, learning models, management challenges, and learning outcomes. Phase 2 translated these empirical findings into policy action through systematic gap analysis and expert validation, engaging 17 experts from Cambodia, Thailand, and the United States to assess proposed guidelines in terms of relevance, feasibility, sustainability, and potential impact. The findings reveal that vocational education management at CLCs during the pandemic was severely constrained by chronic underfunding, weak institutional capacity, limited digital infrastructure, low trainer digital competence, and the absence of formal accreditation under the Cambodian National Qualifications Framework (CNQF). Although on-site, online, and on-hand learning models represented adaptive responses to crisis conditions, they were implemented in a largely reactive manner and resulted in fragmented learning experiences with limited practical skill development, particularly in rural areas. Consequently, learning outcomes were weak, and graduates reported low employability and continued socio-economic vulnerability. Gap analysis identified six critical deficiencies: inadequate trainer digital capacity, lack of flexible technology-enabled learning models, unequal access to internet infrastructure, weak evaluation and quality assurance mechanisms, outdated and poorly aligned curricula, and fragile sustainability arrangements. These deficiencies were validated by experts as highly relevant and feasible policy priorities. The study concludes that targeted investment in digital capacity building, infrastructure expansion, curriculum modernization, accreditation alignment, and sustainable governance mechanisms is essential to reposition CLCs as resilient, inclusive, and community-anchored institutions. By integrating field-based qualitative evidence with expert certification, this study contributes a replicable, context-sensitive framework to guide crisis-responsive vocational education and training (TVET) reform in Cambodia and similar developing contexts.</jats:p>
doi:10.14738/assrj.1310.12327.venue: Advances in Social Sciences Research Journal

doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0011.title: Conformal Prediction for Distribution-Free Uncertainty in Machine Learning Models
doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0011.abstract: <jats:p>A point prediction says nothing about how far it might be wrong. Conformal prediction repairs that with very little machinery: hold out some labelled data, score how badly the model misses on it, and widen each new prediction by a quantile of those scores. The resulting set contains the true label with a chosen probability, for any model and any data distribution, provided the data are exchangeable. This review reads the literature with one question in mind, namely what exactly is promised and under which assumption. We go through the split recipe and the adaptive scores built for regression and classification, then the limits of the guarantee, which is marginal and not per individual. Most of the article concerns what happens when exchangeability fails: covariate and label shift, drifting streams, time series. We close with risk control, counterfactual inference and generative language models, and with a short list of checks a practitioner should run before trusting a reported coverage figure. No new experiment is reported; every number quoted is a theoretical bound taken from the cited source.</jats:p>

doi:10.1080/14623943.2026.2749780.title: Towards visual learning analytics-supported reflective practices: a longitudinal study of teachers’ reflections regarding synchronous online mathematics instruction
doi:10.1080/14623943.2026.2749780.abstract: Since the pandemic, teachers have become familiar with using synchronous online activities to create additional learning opportunities for students. However, challenges have persisted in terms of students’ participation and teachers’ ability to notice relevant events for post-lesson video-based reflections. In this study, we used visual learning analytics (VLA) derived from videos of online lessons to support secondary school mathematics teachers’ reflections on discourse practices. We examined a VLA-supported, peer-mediated reflective system centred on a teacher in our professional development programme alongside his peers through three stages over 20 months. Initially, the focal teacher observed and learned from his peers, then practised his own online lessons. Subsequently, he served as a critical friend and used VLA to support his peer’s reflections on and for action. Narratives from the teachers’ reflective journals and interviews suggest that the process was associated with greater awareness of using progressive examples and questioning techniques. A comparison of the peer teacher’s first and second implementations revealed improvements in students’ participation in class discussions and learning outcomes. These findings suggest the potential value of VLA and peer facilitation in supporting teachers’ reflective practices and contribute to addressing the challenges associated with teachers’ noticing for reflection and instructional improvement.

doi:10.57235/sakola.v3i2.9276.title: Penerapan Rendam Air Hangat terhadap Penurunan Kram Kaki Ibu Hamil Trimester II dan III Di Wilayah Puskesmas Purwodiningratan
doi:10.57235/sakola.v3i2.9276.abstract: <jats:p>Latar Belakang : Kram kaki merupakan keluhan yang sering dialami ibu hamil trimester II dan III akibat perubahan fisiologis selama kehamilan. Kram kaki memiliki prevalensi yang cukup tinggi, yaitu sekitar 50–60% pada ibu hamil, dan dapat mengganggu kualitas tidur, aktivitas sehari-hari, serta menurunkan kualitas hidup ibu. Salah satu penanganan nonfarmakologis yang aman dan mudah dilakukan adalah terapi rendam air hangat, yang dapat meningkatkan sirkulasi darah dan merelaksasi otot sehingga membantu mengurangi kram. Tujuan : untuk mengetahui mendeskripsikan pengaruh terapi rendam air hangat terhadap penurunan tingkat kram kaki pada ibu hamil trimester II dan III di wilayah kerja Puskesmas Purwodiningratan. Metode : Penelitian ini menggunakan metode deskriptif dengan desain studi kasus pada dua ibu hamil trimester II dan III yang mengalami kram kaki. Pemilihan responden dilakukan berdasarkan kriteria inklusi dan eksklusi. Intervensi terapi rendam air hangat diberikan selama 15 menit setiap hari selama lima hari. Pengukuran dilakukan dengan mengamati perubahan tingkat kram kaki sebelum dan sesudah intervensi. Hasil : Berdasarkan hasil penerapan yang dilakukan, terdapat penurunan tingkat kram kaki pada kedua responden setelah diberikan terapi rendam air hangat selama 5 hari. Responden 1 mengalami penurunan skala nyeri sebesar 4 poin (dari skala 6 menjadi 2), sedangkan responden 2 mengalami penurunan sebesar 5 poin (dari skala 6 menjadi 1). Kedua responden mengalami perubahan tingkat nyeri dari nyeri sedang menjadi nyeri ringan. Kesimpulan : Terapi rendam air hangat terbukti membantu menurunkan skala nyeri kram kaki pada ibuhamil.</jats:p>

doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1529.c6172.title: Sürücü Davranışlarının Bilişsel Mimarilerle Modellenmesi: Ontoloji Tabanlı Bilgi Temsili ve Hiyerarşik Öğrenme
doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1529.c6172.abstract: <jats:p>Akıllı ve otonom sürüş sistemlerinde karar üretimi, sensörden gelen verilerin doğrudan fiziksel kontrol eylemlerine eşlenmesinin ötesinde; çevresel bilginin semantik olarak anlamlandırılmasını, zamansal bağlamın korunmasını, farklı soyutlama düzeylerindeki sürüş davranışlarının yapılandırılmasını ve sürücüye özgü deneyimin karar sürecine dahil edilmesini gerektirmektedir. Bu çalışmada, açık bilgi ile deneyimden öğrenilen davranış bilgisini ortak bir karar sürecinde ilişkilendiren ontoloji destekli bilişsel bir sürücü davranışı mimarisi önerilmektedir. Mimaride gözlemsel temsil, ontolojik bilgi modeli aracılığıyla semantik sürüş durumuna temellendirilmekte; bu durum zamansal geçmiş, mevcut sürüş amacı ve sürücüye özgü tercih bilgisiyle ilişkilendirilerek bilişsel bağlam oluşturulmaktadır. Karar üretimi amaç–davranış–manevra–eylem hiyerarşisi içerisinde yapılandırılmakta; sürücüye özgü öğrenilmiş politikalar ise bilişsel bağlam altında seçilen davranış ve manevraların fiziksel eylemlere dönüştürülmesini sağlamaktadır. Pekiştirmeli ve hiyerarşik öğrenme, önerilen bilgi ve karar yapısı üzerinde uygulanabilecek örnek öğrenme mekanizmaları olarak ele alınmakta; mimari belirli bir öğrenme algoritmasına bağlı tutulmamaktadır. Öğrenilmiş politikalar tarafından üretilen aday eylemler açık trafik, güvenlik ve uygulanabilirlik kısıtları altında semantik olarak denetlenirken, karar sürecindeki ara temsiller bağlamsal ve semantik izlenebilirlik sağlamaktadır. Mimarinin uçtan uca işleyişi temsili bir otoyol sürüş senaryosu üzerinden gösterilmektedir. Çalışma, belirli bir kontrol veya öğrenme algoritması geliştirmekten ziyade, akıllı sürüş sistemlerinde gözlemsel bilgi, semantik anlam, bilişsel bağlam, hiyerarşik davranış, sürücüye özgü öğrenme ve fiziksel eylem arasındaki bilgi dönüşümünü açık biçimde yapılandıran bütünleşik bir kavramsal mimari ortaya koymaktadır.</jats:p>

doi:10.63090/ijters/3049.1614.0063.title: Assessment‑Embedded Learning in ESL Classrooms: A Conceptual and Reflective Practice Framework
doi:10.63090/ijters/3049.1614.0063.abstract: <jats:p>Formative assessment plays an important role in the ESL/EFL Program. It spreads across the length of the course and uses various methods to monitor and assist in the process of learning. On one hand, through these activities teachers can learn more about students’ understanding and take informed decisions on their lesson plan. On the other hand, students benefit through their active participation in tasks that require them to reflect and communicate with peers in target language. However, due to practical concerns such as limited time, insufficient resources, cultural behavior and inadequate planning, most formative assessment tasks fail to focus on these aspects and remain mostly summative in nature. This presentation focuses on different methods that allow assessment embedded in the learning process in ESL/EFL courses. The aim of these activities is to encourage student engagement on a consistent basis and to develop their language skills by providing them with context and purpose. Students develop critical thinking and gain confidence through their participation. At the same time, teachers will be able to assess students’ performance by focusing on their use of language and provide feedback, creating a cycle where formative assessment works as the fulcrum of the learning process in which students’ participation and teachers’ feedback work in tandem as the load and the effort on the language learning process.</jats:p>
doi:10.63090/ijters/3049.1614.0063.venue: International Journal of Teacher Education Research Studies (IJTERS)

doi:10.63090/ijters/3049.1614.0042.title: Integrating Digital Resources and AI Tools in Language Learning
doi:10.63090/ijters/3049.1614.0042.abstract: <jats:p>This action research explores the impact of integrating AI supported digital resources into reading comprehension for foundation level English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners at the National University of Science and Technology in Oman. Following a curriculum revision that introduced Unlock 4 (Third Edition), students encountered persistent difficulties related to lexical density, complex academic discourse, and conceptual demands, resulting in reduced reading confidence and fluency. To address these challenges, the study implemented a structured intervention using AI based tools that provided vocabulary support, text simplification, summaries, and guided comprehension practice. Sixty foundation students participated in pre and post intervention reading tasks under traditional and AI supported conditions. Quantitative analysis revealed significant overall improvement in reading comprehension scores after the integration of digital tools, with particularly strong gains among lower performing learners. The findings suggest that carefully scaffolded AI integration can enhance comprehension, learner autonomy, and confidence, offering valuable pedagogical implications for foundation programmes in similar EFL contexts.</jats:p>

doi:10.63090/ijters/3049.1614.0043.title: Enhancing Speaking Performance and Critical Thinking through Inquiry-Based Learning in an ESP Course among Foundation Learners at National University
doi:10.63090/ijters/3049.1614.0043.abstract: <jats:p>Developing effective speaking skills and critical thinking abilities is essential for foundation-level learners enrolled in English for Specific Purposes (ESP) courses in higher education. However, traditional teacher-centered instructional approaches often restrict learners’ opportunities for meaningful oral communication and higher-order thinking. This study investigates the effect of Inquiry-Based Learning (IBL) on foundation learners’ speaking performance and critical thinking in an ESP course at National University after the completion of two general foundation programs. A quasi-experimental research design was employed, involving an experimental group that received inquiry-based instruction and a control group that was taught using a conventional case-study method within a content-based science context. Data was collected through post-intervention speaking performance assessments, which measured fluency, accuracy, vocabulary use, pronunciation, and clarity of explanation. Quantitative data were analyzed using inferential statistical methods, the t-test, to compare the performance of both groups. The results revealed a statistically significant difference in speaking performance in favor of the inquiry-based group, indicating that learners exposed to IBL demonstrated superior oral proficiency and higher levels of critical engagement than those receiving traditional instruction. These findings suggest that Inquiry-Based Learning is an effective pedagogical approach for enhancing speaking performance and fostering critical thinking among foundation-level ESP learners. The study provides empirical evidence in support of integrating inquiry-based methodologies into ESP foundation programs in higher education.</jats:p>

doi:10.51178/jsr.v7i2.3808.title: Implementasi Pendekatan Deep Learning Dalam Pembelajaran Fiqih di MTS Ubudiyah Pangkalan Brandan
doi:10.51178/jsr.v7i2.3808.abstract: <jats:p>Penelitian ini dilatar belakangi oleh pentingnya peran guru Fiqih dalam menciptakan pembelajaran yang bermakna dan mendalam di era. Konsep deep learning menjadi pendekatan yang relevan dalam meningkatkan kualitas pembelajaran Fiqih karena menekankan pada pemahaman mendalam, keterlibatan aktif siswa, serta integrasi nilai-nilai spiritual dan sosial.Penelitian ini bertujuan: Bagaimana perencanaan pembelajaran Fiqih berbasis konsep deep learning oleh guru Fiqih di MTs Ubudiyah Pangkalan Brandan, bagaimana prosespelaksanaan pembelajaran Fiqih dengan menerapkan tiga pilar utama deep learning (mindful learning, meaningful learning, dan joyful learning) dalam model tindakan kelas, bagaimana evaluasi setelah diterapkannya pembelajaran berbasis deep learning. Jenis penelitian ini merupakan deskriptif kualitatif, dengan metode pengumpulan data yang dilakukan melalui wawancara, observasi, dan dokumentasi. Teknik analisis data melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan kesimpulan atau verifikasi data. Pengujian keabsahan data penelitian ini menggunakan teknik triangulasi sumber, triangulasi teknik, dan triangulasi waktu. Hasil penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa: Perencanaan pembelajaran Fiqih berbasis konsep deep learning oleh guru dimulai dengen menyususn modul ajar mencakup pertanyaan pemantik, tujuan pembelajarandan alokasi waktu. Proses pelaksanaan pembelajaran Fiqih menerapkan tiga pilar deep learning dalam tindakan kelas mencakup: mengaitkan (mindful learning), mengalami (joyful & meanful learning) dan membuat makna (meanful learning & mindful learning). Evaluasi setelah diterapkannya pembelajaran berbasis deep learning memberikan umpan balik kontribusi positif terhadap efektivitas pembelajaran Fiqih di MTs Ubudiyah Pangkalan Brandan.</jats:p>

doi:10.38035/sijet.v4i2.421.title: Improving Fifth-Grade Elementary Students' Learning Outcomes through the Implementation of Local-Wisdom-Based Audiovisual Digital Comics
doi:10.38035/sijet.v4i2.421.abstract: <jats:p>: Elementary students often have difficulty identifying intrinsic elements, reconstructing narrative structure, and drawing conclusions from long printed texts. This study aimed to improve fifth-grade students' learning outcomes through a locally grounded audiovisual digital comic. The study was packaged as a classroom action research manuscript using iterative planning, action, observation, and reflection. The action records involved 23 students in class VA at SDN Kebon Baru 07, Jakarta, during November 2025. Cycle I was a limited action with four heterogeneous students, while Cycle II expanded the revised action to 19 other students. Data were collected through learning-outcome tests, observations, and response questionnaires, then analyzed descriptively using mastery percentages and normalized gain. The mean score increased from 61 to 79 in Cycle I, with 75% mastery and a normalized gain of 0.56. In Cycle II, the mean score increased from 54 to 85, with 89.47% mastery and a normalized gain of 0.71. Overall, 21 of 23 students reached the minimum mastery criterion. The novelty lies in integrating a Minangkabau folktale, animated comic panels, narration, dialogue, sound effects, and structured reading tasks within an iterative elementary classroom action.</jats:p>
