doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0012.title: Divergent Failure Modes of Two Intrusion Detection Benchmarks Under A Common Audit
doi:10.63090/eijdsml/3139.7344.0012.abstract: <jats:p>Two public corpora carry much of the empirical load in machine learning research on intrusion detection for wireless sensor networks and for industrial internet of things deployments. Accuracy on both is routinely reported near the ceiling. We audit both with one procedure, holding features, models, metrics and seeds fixed, and they fail in different ways. On Edge-IIoTset the binary task is settled before any model is fitted. Four string valued fields record how the capture was serialised rather than how the traffic behaved, because the absent value was written as one token on benign rows and a different token on attack rows, and a depth one decision stump on any of them reaches 1.0000 where the majority baseline is 0.8417. All seven learners in the bank reach that ceiling. Removing the four fields separates them again. On WSN-DS the same audit returns almost nothing, and that is the second result. Discarding 8,873 duplicate records moves the bank average equal error rate by 0.0000, and a node disjoint split that shares no sensor with training moves it by 0.0005, against a spread of 0.0158 across the models themselves. A third check finds what neither corpus level audit does. With one attack family withheld from training, detection of the withheld behaviour runs from 0.007 to 0.886. These checks are cheap, and which of them bites is not predictable in advance.</jats:p>

doi:10.38035/sijet.v4i2.459.title: The Use of Digital and Non-Digital Learning Resources to Improve Students’ Literacy in History Class
doi:10.38035/sijet.v4i2.459.abstract: <jats:p>The development of digital technology has expanded the availability of learning resources in history education. However, the increasing availability of digital information does not automatically improve students’ historical literacy because students still need the ability to evaluate sources, understand historical contexts, and interpret evidence critically. This study aims to examine the utilization of digital and non-digital learning resources in history education and analyze their potential contribution to improving students’ historical literacy. This study employed a literature review method by examining relevant scholarly publications concerning digital history, historical learning resources, historical thinking, historical literacy, museums, historical sources, and technology-supported history learning. The selected literature was analyzed thematically based on the role of digital resources, the role of non-digital resources, the development of historical literacy and historical thinking, the integration of different learning resources, and the challenges of their implementation. The review indicates that digital resources can provide broad access to historical information through digital archives, educational videos, digital maps, virtual museums, digital storytelling, and online historical sources. Meanwhile, non-digital resources such as textbooks, historical documents, photographs, artifacts, museums, and historical sites provide authentic and contextual experiences with historical evidence. The findings suggest that integrating digital and non-digital learning resources can create a more comprehensive history learning experience by encouraging students to access, compare, evaluate, and interpret historical sources. The effective implementation of these resources requires teacher guidance, source evaluation skills, adequate learning facilities, and learning activities that emphasize historical inquiry and critical thinking.</jats:p>
doi:10.38035/sijet.v4i2.459.venue: Siber International Journal of Education Technology (SIJET)

doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1529.c6171.title: Rüzgar Türbini Aktif Güç Üretiminin Makine Öğrenmesi ve Derin Öğrenme Yöntemleriyle Tahmini
doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1529.c6171.abstract: <jats:p>Rüzgâr enerjisinin elektrik arzındaki payının büyümesiyle birlikte, üretimin kısa ve orta vadeli tahminlerinin doğru yapılması ihtiyacı ortaya çıkmaktadır. Bu bölümde, Türkiye'nin Marmara Bölgesi'nde faaliyet gösteren bir rüzgâr türbinine ait, bir yıllık (2018), 10 dakikalık gerçek SCADA ölçümlerinin (n=50.530) analizi, aktif gücü 1, 6 ve 24 saat sonrası için tahmin eden beş yöntemle (Naive Bayes, Random Forest, XGBoost, Uzun-Kısa Vadeli Bellek ağı ve Transformer) gerçekleştirilmektedir. Ölçekleme ve yüzdelik tabanlı rüzgâr eşikleri, sızıntıyı önlemek amacıyla yalnızca eğitim istatistiklerinden türetilmiştir. Bulgular, 1 saatlik ufukta hiçbir modelin Süreklilik (persistence) taban çizgisini istatistiksel olarak anlamlı biçimde geçemediğini (Diebold-Mariano p=0,44) göstermekte, buna karşılık 24 saatlik ufukta XGBoost'un persistence'a göre istatistiksel olarak anlamlı bir iyileşme sağladığını (p<0,001) ortaya koymaktadır; ancak açıklanan varyans pratikte sınırlı kalmaktadır (R²≈0,00). Nitekim 6 ve özellikle 24 saatlik ufuklarda hiçbir yöntem klasik anlamda gerçek bir tahmin becerisi sunmamaktadır. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analizi, tahminlerin kısa ufuklarda ağırlıklı olarak en son gözlemlenen güç değerine, uzun ufuklarda ise esasen iklimsel bir temel çizgi işlevi gören mevsimsel (yılın günü) örüntülere dayandığını doğrulamaktadır. Bulgular, dışsal sayısal hava tahmini girdisi olmaksızın, yalnızca geçmiş SCADA kayıtlarına dayanan istatistiksel ve öğrenme temelli yöntemlerin doğal bir öngörülebilirlik ufku sınırıyla karşı karşıya olduğunu göstermektedir. Makine öğrenmesi bu sınırı ortadan kaldırmaktan çok, sınırın kendisini nicel olarak görünür kılmaktadır.</jats:p>

doi:10.70917/fce-2025-005.title: Model Prediction of Land Surface Temperature from Satellite Data with Machine Learning
doi:10.70917/fce-2025-005.abstract:
<jats:p>BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Urbanization leads to increased building construction, forming Urban Heat Island (UHI). UHI causes heat accumulation in urban areas, making it difficult to ventilate the area. This study aims to analyze Land Surface Temperatures (LST) using Remote Sensing (RS) data to predict UHI development in urban localities in Chiang Mai, Thailand. The study aims to compare the performance of different machine learning (ML) algorithms in predicting LST and assess their potential for future use in mitigating UHI consequences in urban areas.
METHODS: RS data from Landsat 8 and Sentinel-2 satellites were used to analyze LST from 2016 to 2022. Five different ML algorithms were employed in this study: Random Forest (RF), AdaBoost Regressor (ABR), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Linear Regression (LR), and Gradient Boosting (GB). The performance of these algorithms was evaluated using statistical variables.
FINDINGS: The study found that the RF model had the highest precision in predicting LST, with the lowest Mean Absolute Error (MAEvalues among the models. However, all models had relatively low R-squared (R2)values, indicating room for developing the accuracy of the predictions.
CONCLUSION: The study demonstrates the feasibility of using RS data and ML algorithms to predict LST and comprehend UHI development in urban localities. The study also emphasizes the importance of using ML techniques to address UHI consequences in urban areas and can apply these data to urban planning to promote sustainable urban development. Further investigation is necessary to improve the accuracy of the models and determine effective strategies to mitigate UHI effects in urban areas.
 </jats:p>

doi:10.57235/sakola.v3i2.9300.title: Bullying di Lingkungan Kampus: Tantangan Dalam Mewujudkan Kehidupan Akademik yang Aman
doi:10.57235/sakola.v3i2.9300.abstract: <jats:p>Perundungan di lingkungan kampus masih kerap dipandang sebagai persoalan sepele atau bagian dari tradisi senioritas, padahal praktik ini mengancam rasa aman dan kualitas kehidupan akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis bentuk dan pola perundungan di lingkungan kampus serta keterkaitannya dengan pengalaman pada jenjang pendidikan sebelumnya, sekaligus mengidentifikasi tantangan perguruan tinggi dalam mencegah dan menanganinya. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode tinjauan pustaka terhadap 15 artikel terindeks yang terbit pada rentang 2021–2026. Seleksi literatur mengacu pada alur PRISMA 2020, sedangkan analisis data menggunakan kerangka SALSA dan sintesis tematik. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa perundungan di kampus terjadi secara luas di berbagai negara, didominasi bentuk verbal, relasional, dan digital, serta berakar pada relasi kuasa yang timpang dan praktik normalisasi. Riwayat kekerasan relasional pada masa sekolah terbukti meningkatkan risiko menjadi korban di perguruan tinggi. Tantangan utama yang dihadapi kampus meliputi budaya hierarkis, rendahnya visibilitas kebijakan, ketakutan korban untuk melapor, luasnya dampak psikologis, dan penegakan sanksi yang belum adil. Pembahasan menegaskan bahwa perundungan di kampus merupakan persoalan budaya institusi. Oleh karena itu, kehidupan akademik yang aman memerlukan evaluasi tradisi kampus, sistem pelaporan yang melindungi korban, layanan konseling, sanksi yang adil, serta pembangunan iklim psychological safety.</jats:p>
doi:10.57235/sakola.v3i2.9300.venue: SAKOLA: Journal of Sains Cooperative Learning and Law

doi:10.9734/jsrr/2026/v32i114635.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Supply Chain Management: Applications, Evidence, Implementation Constraints, and Future Directions
doi:10.9734/jsrr/2026/v32i114635.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly investigated as decision-support technologies for supply chain management (SCM), yet their value depends on the nature of the decision, data availability, organisational capability and the methods used to evaluate outcomes. This critical narrative review examines applications across demand forecasting, inventory planning, sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, risk management and sustainability. It brings together relevant peer-reviewed reviews, conceptual contributions and empirical studies, and distinguishes evidence from operational deployments from results reported in literature syntheses or simulations. The literature supports the practical relevance of data-driven prediction, pattern detection and decision augmentation, but it does not establish uniform improvements in cost, forecast accuracy, resilience or environmental performance across settings. Reviewed research also identifies integration costs, fragmented data, process misalignment, model drift, limited transparency and governance concerns as barriers to realising benefits. Recent work on generative AI broadens possible applications to document-intensive processes, synthetic scenarios and interactive decision support, while indicating that field-based validation remains limited. A process-oriented framework is proposed in which analytics inform planning, procurement, manufacturing, distribution and inventory decisions under continuous human oversight. The review argues that useful evaluations should compare AI-supported decisions against relevant operational baselines, account for service levels and cost trade-offs, and document transferability across sectors and resource settings. Future research should prioritise longitudinal field studies, cross-organisational coordination, responsible deployment and context-sensitive applications in emerging economies.</jats:p>
doi:10.9734/jsrr/2026/v32i114635.venue: Journal of Scientific Research and Reports

doi:10.29303/goescienceed.v7i4.3469.title: Pengaruh Pendekatan Saintifik melalui Model Problem Based Learning Berbantuan Lembar Kerja Peserta Didik terhadap Keterampilan Proses Sains Siswa Kelas X di Sekolah Rakyat Menengah Atas 38 Lombok Timur
doi:10.29303/goescienceed.v7i4.3469.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to determine the effect of the scientific approach through the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model assisted by Student Worksheets (LKPD) on the science process skills of tenth-grade students at Sekolah Rakyat Menengah Atas 38 East Lombok in ecosystem learning. This study employed a quasi-experimental method using a Nonequivalent Control Group Design. The sample consisted of an experimental class and a control class, each comprising 25 students. Data were collected using a science process skills test and analyzed through normality, homogeneity, linearity, and ANCOVA tests. The results showed that the scientific approach through the PBL model assisted by Student Worksheets had a significant effect on students' science process skills after controlling for their initial abilities. Therefore, this learning model is effective in improving students' science process skills in ecosystem learning.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-76143-2.title: Molecule-aware machine learning for predicting absorption and emission of benzothiadiazole derivatives
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-76143-2.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Predicting the absorption and emission wavelengths of 2,1,3-benzothiadiazole (BTD) derivatives across diverse solvents from molecular structure alone remains challenging, and conventional random-split validation can obscure whether models truly extrapolate to new chemical structures or merely interpolate solvent effects for known ones. By enforcing a molecule-aware train–test split, in which all solvent measurements of any given chemical structure are held out together, we show that champion-model
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$R^2$$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    falls by approximately 27–29 percentage points relative to random splitting, revealing that high random-split accuracy primarily reflects reliable prediction of solvent-induced spectral shifts rather than generalisation to unseen BTD structures. Within this framework, replacing binary with count-based Morgan fingerprints raises single-split
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$R^2$$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    from 0.747 to 0.941 for absorption and from 0.797 to 0.916 for emission, an improvement rooted in the ability of count fingerprints to encode the recurrence frequency of donor substructures, a key determinant of intramolecular charge-transfer character. A systematically optimised deep neural network reaches
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$R^2 = 0.954$$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    for absorption on its best of twenty random initialisations (mean
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:tex-math>$$0.83 \pm 0.12$$</jats:tex-math>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    ), the highest value reported for this dataset, yet the molecule-aware benchmark confirms that this performance does not translate to structure-level extrapolation. Comparative evaluation of graph neural networks, multi-task learning, extended descriptor sets, and ensemble methods confirms that none outperforms the count-fingerprint approach at this dataset size. Feature-importance analysis identifies tertiary amine substitution as the dominant structural driver and solvent polarity as the strongest single feature for emission (ranked first or second in all four model/encoding combinations examined, versus 8th–13th for absorption), an asymmetry consistent with the stronger solvatochromism of relaxed charge-transfer states. These results offer practical guidance for computational screening: the models are well suited to solvent selection for known dyes, whereas the design of genuinely new structures demands expanded structural diversity in the training set.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.25258/ijddt.16.88s.57.title: Noise-Resilient Attention-Guided Deep Learning Framework for Network Intrusion Detection
doi:10.25258/ijddt.16.88s.57.abstract: <jats:p>The rising complexity of the state of the art network infrastructures and the swift advancement of cyber-attacks have rendered the correct and sound detection of intrusion to be a vital security need. Conventional intrusion detection solutions tend to collapse with noisy, high-dimensional network traffic, temporally changing traffic and encourage superior Deep Learning (DL)-based options. The main goal of this work is to improve the intrusion detection reliability by resolving the issue of noise sensitivity, over-representation of redundant features and inadequate temporal modelling. This is accomplished by introducing a noise-resilient attentionguided DL architecture which are Adaptive Noise-Resilient Data Preprocessing (ANR-DP), Hybrid Recursive Attention-Based Feature Selection (HRAFS), and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based temporal classifier. ANR-DP acts dynamically on traffic noise and maintains the characteristics of the attacks, but HRAFS is expected to select stable and security-critical features through recursive elimination and attentiondriven relevance learning. The optimized features are fed through an LSTM network in order to detect sequential and long-term intrusion patterns. Experimental analysis of the CICIDS2017 dataset provides a better performance with Proposed ANR-DP having low Missing Value Ratio of 1.2, High Outlier Reduction Rate of 91.5, HRAFS achieves a Feature Reduction Ratio of 68.7% and 9.1% accuracy improvement. The LSTM classifier also has an accuracy of 98.6%, and a low false positive rate of 3.1%. These findings establish that the proposed framework is very effective in enhancing robustness, precision, and dependability, it can be applicable in the environment of network intrusion detection.</jats:p>

doi:10.1080/14786419.2026.2736641.title: Tissue-specific antibacterial and anti-biofilm activities of Penthorum chinense Pursh: integration of metabolomics and Random Forest machine learning
doi:10.1080/14786419.2026.2736641.abstract: Penthorum chinense Pursh is a traditional medicinal and edible plant rich in flavonoids and complex polyphenols. Evaluating its aqueous extracts against foodborne pathogens via biomass assay, microplate spread tests and scanning electron microscopy revealed distinct tissue-specific efficacies: leaf and stem extracts exhibited strong bactericidal effects (16–128 mg/mL), notably against Bacillus cereus, whereas flower extracts demonstrated potent biofilm inhibition (IC50 < 1 mg/mL). Broad-coverage UPLC–ESI–Q–TOF–MS metabolite profiling annotated 93 compounds, and integration with Random Forest nested cross-validation prioritised candidate constituents associated with the measured activities. While confirming established antimicrobials (gallic acid, pinocembrin, pinostrobin, (-)-epicatechin gallate, afzelechin, corilagin, and hydrolysable derivatives of quercetin, kaempferol, and liquiritin) as major active constituents, our ML model first revealed several unreported bioactive compounds. Specifically, turmeronol A, vanillic acid glucoside, lotaustralin, and 2’,6’-dihydroxydihydrochalcone-4’-O-(3′’-O-galloyl)-β-D-glucopyranoside act as crucial bactericidal agents, while Gemin D, lamiophlomiol C, 4’-hydroxyflavanone, and pinocembrin-7-O-[4,6-HHDP]-glucoside primarily contribute to anti-biofilm efficacy. Finally, their multi-target mechanisms were preliminarily explored.

doi:10.1007/s44217-026-02335-7.title: Scenario based assessment of sustainable education management under lockdowns, fuel conservation policies, and learning disruptions in Pakistan
doi:10.1007/s44217-026-02335-7.abstract: Sustainable educational management has emerged as a critical policy focus for maintaining educational continuity in times of crisis, while also optimizing resource efficiency and institutional resilience. In Pakistan, the fuel-saving strategies enacted during lockdowns have posed considerable difficulties for educational administration by interrupting instructional and learning processes. In light of this context, this research offers a scenario-based evaluation to investigate the impact of fuel conservation regulations on educational interruptions and to determine sustainable management techniques that enable continuous educational provision during emergencies. Based on relevant research, policy records, global crisis cases, and Pakistan’s educational structure, four possible outcomes include sudden disruption, persisting disparity, systemic instability, and adaptive resilience. The scenario analysis shows that digital and blended learning can help maintain continuity during brief interruptions. However, disparities in connectivity, devices, socioeconomic resources, and geographically diverse educational infrastructure may worsen inequalities. Disruptions may cause disengagement, learning deficits, dropout rates, and long-term effects on human capital, but timely institutional changes can improve educational resilience. The study shows that educational continuity depends on the duration, intensity, and government and institutional responses to interruptions. The study emphasizes the need for policymakers to prioritize affordable digital access, targeted help for at-risk learners, adaptive delivery modalities, and coherent crisis-management techniques. The study proposes a policy-focused scenario paradigm that links fuel-saving methods to sustainable educational governance and resilience in a developing country.

doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1520.c6139.title: Çevresel Performans Endeksi (EPI) Temelinde Ülkelerin Sınıflandırılması: Kümeleme ve Makine Öğrenmesi Yaklaşımı
doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1520.c6139.abstract: <jats:p>Çevresel sürdürülebilirlik, ekonomik, kurumsal ve enerji göstergeleriyle birlikte değerlendirilmesi gereken çok boyutlu bir kavramdır. Bu çalışmanın amacı, ülkelerin Çevresel Performans Endeksi (EPI) temelinde benzerliklerini belirlemek ve elde edilen küme yapısının makine öğrenmesi algoritmaları tarafından ne ölçüde tahmin edilebildiğini incelemektir. Araştırmada 144 ülkeye ait EPI, yolsuzluğun kontrolü, hükümet etkinliği, düzenleyici kalite, kişi başına gelir, eğitim düzeyi, yenilenebilir enerji tüketimi, enerji yoğunluğu ve sanayi katma değeri göstergeleri kullanılmıştır. İlk aşamada K-Means kümeleme analizi uygulanmış ve Silhouette katsayısı yardımıyla ülkelerin üç temel küme altında toplandığı belirlenmiştir. Elde edilen kümeler yüksek performanslı, orta performanslı ve düşük performanslı ülke gruplarını temsil etmektedir. İkinci aşamada küme üyelikleri çeşitli makine öğrenmesi algoritmaları kullanılarak tahmin edilmiştir. Sonuçlar, oluşturulan kümelerin yüksek doğrulukla tahmin edilebildiğini göstermektedir. En başarılı performans Destek Vektör Makineleri algoritması tarafından elde edilmiş olup doğruluk oranı %97,9’a ulaşmıştır. Bulgular, çevresel performansın ekonomik gelişmişlik, yönetişim kalitesi ve enerji göstergeleriyle yakından ilişkili olduğunu ortaya koyarken, veri madenciliği ve makine öğrenmesi yöntemlerinin ülkelerin çevresel performans profillerinin belirlenmesinde etkili araçlar sunduğunu göstermektedir.</jats:p>

doi:10.2478/cee-2027-0026.title: Cross-database validation and calibrated uncertainty for machine learning models of the shear capacity of FRP-strengthened RC beams
doi:10.2478/cee-2027-0026.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Machine learning models for the shear contribution of externally bonded fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) to reinforced concrete beams are validated almost exclusively on a random hold-out split of a single self-compiled database. Because such databases are assembled from a few dozen experimental programmes, each contributing several near-identical specimens, a random split leaves siblings of nearly every test specimen in the training set. This study provides a cross-database assessment of that practice. Two independently compiled databases (442 and 455 specimens) were harmonised into a provenance-traced dataset of 828 records from 167 programmes spanning 1992–2024, and six learners were evaluated under five regimes of increasing severity. For gradient boosting the coefficient of determination fell from 0.67 and 0.69 under random splitting to 0.39 and 0.22 under study-grouped validation, and to 0.21 under cross-database transfer. A control in which the same physical specimens were scored under each compilation in turn changed little (0.35 versus 0.37), showing that clustering by programme, not curation disagreement, is responsible. A hierarchical errors-invariables model attributes 38% of the residual variance to programme identity and delivers calibrated predictive intervals (91.8% coverage at a nominal 90%), which span a factor of about twelve. Design provisions remain less accurate than the fitted models, but the reported margin roughly halves under honest validation. A reporting protocol is proposed, requiring publication of the specimen-to-study mapping, validation grouped on it, disclosure of out-of-range evaluation cases, and reporting of interval coverage and a characteristic value.</jats:p>

doi:10.22541/essoar.15010630/v1.title: A Simple Climatology Benchmark Outperforms Machine-Learning Lightning Parameterizations
doi:10.22541/essoar.15010630/v1.abstract: <jats:p>Machine-learning approaches to predicting lightning have achieved remarkable evaluation scores, far exceeding traditional parameterizations. However, high performance, even on unseen years, does not necessarily demonstrate robust physical relationships between predictors and lightning that hold under climate change. Here, we investigate how similarity between training and testing data affects lightning model evaluation. We introduce a simple benchmark predicting the training-data mean lightning density for each grid-cell and day of year, which reproduces 92% of the variance in daily grid-cell LIS/OTD observations and outperforms machine-learning models and traditional parameterizations. This high apparent skill is largely attributable to the strong spatiotemporal smoothing of LIS/OTD. We further show that previously reported model skill in reproducing inter-annual variability results from inconsistent observational coverage and disappears under a common spatiotemporal domain. Our results suggest that common lightning-model evaluations can overstate projection skill and highlight the need to test models under conditions differing from the training distribution.</jats:p>

doi:10.64325/gv38x446.title: El aprendizaje basado en problemas como estrategia para desarrollar competencias militares
doi:10.64325/gv38x446.abstract: <jats:p>The complexity of contemporary operational environments—characterized by volatility, uncertainty, hybrid threats, and multi-domain operations—demands a profound transformation in Professional Military Education (PME) systems. This scientific article analyzes Problem-Based Learning (PBL) as a pedagogical and didactic strategy for developing higher-order military competencies, including critical thinking, adaptive leadership, decision-making under pressure, ethical-normative reasoning, and strategic planning. Using a qualitative, analytical-synthetic documentary review methodology, indexed scientific literature on the constructivist foundations of PBL and its empirical application in military academies and war colleges is examined. Findings reveal that, in contrast to traditional instructional models that often result in shallow strategic thinking, the systematic implementation of PBL—particularly when integrating ill-structured real-world problems through the 3C3R framework and tactical simulation exercises—strengthens abductive reasoning, causal literacy, and the transfer of theoretical knowledge to critical operational situations. Institutional tensions related to military hierarchical culture, the risk of restricting cadet or officer autonomy in overly directed hybrid models, and the need to train instructors as metacognitive facilitators are also discussed. It is concluded that PBL serves as an essential bridge between procedural training and higher military education.</jats:p>

doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1520.title: Karar Biliminde Nicel Yöntemler: Çok Kriterli, Optimizasyon Odaklı ve Makine Öğrenmesi Temelli Güncel Yaklaşımlar
doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1520.abstract: <jats:p>Bu kitap, karmaşık karar problemlerinin çözümlenmesinde kullanılan çok kriterli karar verme, optimizasyon ve makine öğrenmesi yaklaşımlarını yöntemsel açıklamalar ve farklı alanlardan uygulamalarla bir araya getirmektedir. On iki bölümden oluşan eser, kriter ağırlıklandırma, alternatiflerin sıralanması, kaynak kullanım etkinliğinin ölçülmesi, kümeleme, tahmin ve model sonuçlarının açıklanması gibi karar biliminin temel konularını ele almaktadır. Çok kriterli karar verme eksenindeki bölümlerde MEREC, LOPCOW, SAW, TODIM, Gri İlişkisel Analiz, AHP, TOPSIS, EDAS ve SPOTIS yöntemleri ile entropi ağırlıklandırması farklı değerlendirme problemleri kapsamında incelenmektedir. Optimizasyon odaklı yaklaşım, OECD sağlık sistemlerinin kaynak kullanım etkinliğini karşılaştıran CCR ve BCC veri zarflama analizi modelleriyle temsil edilmektedir. Makine öğrenmesi temelli bölümler ise ekonomik özgürlükler ve çevresel performans bakımından ülkelerin sınıflandırılmasını, bilgi yönetimi araçları ile iş tatmini arasındaki ilişkinin modellenmesini ve açıklanabilir yapay zekâ destekli dijital performans değerlendirmesini kapsamaktadır. Tarımsal destekler ile üretim arasındaki ilişki, panel veriye dayalı regresyon modelleriyle ele alınarak kitabın nicel analiz kapsamını genişletmektedir. E-ticaret, sağlık, mesleki varış profilleri, havacılıkta kalite güvencesi, çağdaş sanatta sürdürülebilirlik, tarımsal üretim, ekonomik özgürlükler ve dijital dönüşüm alanlarındaki çalışmalar, yöntem seçimi ile uygulama bağlamı arasındaki ilişkiyi görünür kılmaktadır. Kitap; yöntemlerin kuramsal dayanaklarını, hesaplama süreçlerini ve bulguların yorumlanmasını birlikte değerlendirmek isteyen araştırmacılar, lisansüstü öğrenciler, karar analistleri ve politika yapıcılar için bir başvuru kaynağı olarak hazırlanmıştır.</jats:p>

doi:10.46632/jitl/5/4/1.title: Evaluating Educational Policy and Administration: A Weighted Scoring Method Analysis of Performance Dimensions
doi:10.46632/jitl/5/4/1.abstract: <jats:p>This study evaluates education policy and management using the Weighted Scoring Method (WSM) across five domains: education leadership, management, administration, planning, and public education policy. Four equally weighted dimensions—policy effectiveness, equity, collaboration, and student allocation—were considered. The findings indicate that education planning ranked first with a priority score of 0.72991, demonstrating excellent collaboration and equity performance. Education management secured second place (0.70486), reflecting balanced performance across the dimensions. Education leadership ranked third (0.56527), achieving the highest equity score but requiring improved collaboration. Public education policy placed fourth (0.55337), demonstrating strong policy effectiveness but weaker student allocation. Educational administration ranked last (0.40102), highlighting the need for comprehensive improvements. The normalized data and weighted decision matrix identified the relative strengths and weaknesses of each domain. the study emphasizes strengthening collaboration, promoting equitable resource distribution, and integrating policy effectiveness with efficient student allocation to improve educational governance and management.</jats:p>

doi:10.3221/igf-esis.79.06.title: Front-resolved mode-II–III nominal driving-force evolution and group-validated machine-learning prediction for high-speed railway wheel-tread cracks
doi:10.3221/igf-esis.79.06.abstract: <jats:p>Closed wheel-tread cracks can remain compression-dominated during rolling contact while sustaining substantial in-plane and out-of-plane shear. A sequential ABAQUS–FRANC3D–Python framework resolves this response over ten crack-geometry updates. A closure-aware nominal driving force combines event-paired differences in the mode-II and mode-III stress-intensity factors. Four arc-length descriptors summarise its front distribution: mean, peak, peak coordinate and coefficient of variation. Controlled comparisons evaluate initial crack size and orientation, axle load, speed and wheel–rail friction. Thirty Latin-hypercube finite-element conditions provide 4,272 front points for condition-grouped machine-learning validation. ExtraTrees achieves a case-macro cross-validation RMSE of 16.9587 MPa·mm1/2. Four held-out numerical conditions, comprising 579 front points, give a pointwise RMSE of 8.5794 MPa·mm1/2. Front coordinate and initial orientation have the largest mean absolute SHAP contributions. The predicted terminal profiles quantify differences in driving-force magnitude and localisation across conditions within the sampled domain.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-72340-1.title: Dynamic weighted federated contrastive learning for robust medical image classification under heterogeneous data
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-72340-1.abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, AI-driven medical image classification has attracted considerable attention in recent years. However, increasingly stringent data privacy regulations have significantly restricted data sharing among medical institutions, making it difficult for traditional centralized learning frameworks to effectively exploit distributed medical data resources. As a privacy-preserving distributed machine learning paradigm, federated learning enables multiple institutions to collaboratively train models without directly exchanging raw data. Nevertheless, federated learning still faces several critical challenges in practical applications, including heterogeneous data distributions and model bias caused by non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a dynamic weighted learning method based on federated contrastive learning. Different from approaches that focus solely on local representation optimization or employ fixed aggregation weights, the proposed framework couples supervised contrastive local training with loss-feedback-based multi-factor client weighting, thereby jointly controlling local representation drift and server-side model aggregation. Specifically, contrastive learning is integrated into the federated learning framework by jointly leveraging local and global model representations for supervised contrastive optimization. This strategy effectively mitigates the distribution discrepancy among different clients and gradually aligns local models with the global model as communication rounds progress. Furthermore, during global aggregation, a loss-feedback rule is introduced to accept the candidate global model parameters and aggregation weights only when the candidate loss-feedback value decreases. In addition, a multi-factor weighted aggregation mechanism is introduced to comprehensively evaluate client contributions based on multiple factors, thereby assigning larger aggregation weights to local models that are more beneficial to global model optimization. Experiments were conducted on an osteoporosis knee X-ray dataset and a COVID–Pneumonia–Normal chest X-ray dataset under IID and different Non-IID settings. Under severe Non-IID conditions, the proposed method achieved accuracies of 92.12% and 96.27%, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 98.31% and 97.68%, and F1 scores of 90.92% and 93.22% on the two datasets, respectively. Comparisons with representative federated learning methods and the static-weighting ablation setting demonstrate that the proposed method maintains competitive classification performance and stable training behavior under heterogeneous client distributions.

doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1520.c6137.title: Türkiye’de Tarımsal Destekler ve Üretim İlişkisi
doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1520.c6137.abstract: <jats:p>Küresel iklim değişikliği, jeopolitik belirsizlikler ve tarımsal girdi maliyetlerindeki artış, gıda arz güvenliğini ve tarımsal üretimin sürdürülebilirliğini ciddi biçimde tehdit etmektedir. Tarımsal destek politikaları hem üretim istikrarının sağlanması hem de kırsal gelirlerin korunması açısından kritik bir politika aracı olarak öne çıkmaktadır. Bu çalışma, Türkiye’de uygulanan tarımsal desteklerin bitkisel ve hayvansal üretim üzerindeki etkilerini ampirik olarak incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır. Analizde, Tarım ve Orman Bakanlığı Çiftçi Kayıt Sistemi’ne (ÇKS) kayıtlı işletmelere ait 2019–2023 dönemini kapsayan il ve ilçe düzeyinde panel veriler kullanılmıştır. Bitkisel üretimde mazot ve gübre desteği ile fark ödemeleri; hayvancılıkta ise buzağı ve çiğ süt destekleri temel politika değişkenleri olarak ele alınmıştır. Üretim ve verimlilik üzerindeki etkiler, ürün, bölge ve yıl sabit etkilerini içeren çoklu regresyon modelleri aracılığıyla tahmin edilmiştir. Modellerde ayrıca iklim koşulları ve yapısal özellikler kontrol edilmiştir. Elde edilen bulgular, bitkisel üretimde mazot ve gübre desteği ile fark ödemelerinin üretim miktarı ve verimlilik üzerinde istatistiksel olarak anlamlı ve pozitif etkilere sahip olduğunu göstermektedir. Bununla birlikte, desteklerin üretim hacmi üzerindeki etkisinin verimlilik artışına kıyasla daha güçlü olduğu tespit edilmiştir. Hayvancılık desteklerinde ise buzağı ve çiğ süt desteklerinin hayvan varlığını artırıcı yönde etkili olduğu, ancak verimlilik üzerindeki etkilerin daha sınırlı kaldığı görülmektedir. Ayrıca çalışma, tarımsal desteklerin üretim kapasitesini artırmada etkili olduğunu ortaya koymakla birlikte, uzun vadede verimlilik odaklı, hedefli ve yapısal dönüşümü destekleyen politika tasarımlarının önemine işaret etmektedir.</jats:p>

                      <jats:bold>Purpose:</jats:bold>
                    </jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The goal of this study was to enhance the fairness and clinical applicability of deep learning models for classifying Alzheimer’s disease from structural MRI scans. To achieve this, we addressed two key challenges: age-related bias and unreliable probability estimates. Specifically, we investigated in-processing debiasing strategies to achieve age-invariant predictions while preserving diagnostic accuracy. We also systematically evaluated post hoc calibration methods to improve the reliability, interpretability, and clinical usefulness of predicted probabilities across diverse patient populations.</jats:p>

                    <jats:p>Structural MRI data from three independent cohorts (ADNI, AIBL, and DELCODE) were preprocessed using a standardized pipeline. Age-related bias was addressed using two in-processing strategies, adversarial training (CF-Net) and GLM-based feature residualization (PMDN), implemented in a shared 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) framework. Additionally, post hoc calibration was performed using four regression methods: logistic, probit, isotonic, and Bayesian binning. doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75917-y.title: Multi-timescale voltage optimization and control for distribution networks based on regional priority evaluation and deep reinforcement learning
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75917-y.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>With the increasing penetration of distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation, energy storage systems, and other flexible resources in distribution networks, conventional voltage regulation methods struggle to address both overvoltage and undervoltage violations and to coordinate heterogeneous devices operating at different timescales. Existing region-based multi-agent control methods typically treat partitioned regions as homogeneous decision-making units and lack an explicit mechanism to characterize spatiotemporal variations in regional regulation capability and available flexibility. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a multi-timescale voltage optimization and control method for distribution networks based on regional priority evaluation and deep reinforcement learning. First, a coordinated voltage regulation architecture spanning long and short timescales is established. At the long timescale, a double deep Q-network (DDQN) is employed to centrally schedule discrete voltage regulation devices from a system-wide perspective. At the short timescale, a comprehensive regional voltage regulation evaluation index is introduced to quantify the regulation capability and potential of each region and thereby determine its regulation priority. A priority-aware state feature encoding (PASFE) module equipped with a learnable gating mechanism then adaptively fuses regional physical information with coordination information broadcast by the upper-level controller. The resulting priority-aware representations are incorporated into the regional actor and centralized critic networks, enabling the multi-agent algorithm to perform fine-grained regulation of individual continuously adjustable devices. Case studies on the IEEE 33-bus and 141-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method effectively eliminates bus-voltage violations and outperforms the benchmark strategies in mitigating voltage deviations and reducing network losses, thereby confirming the effectiveness of regional-priority guidance in enhancing coordinated multi-timescale voltage regulation.</jats:p>

doi:10.9734/ajrcos/2026/v19i10925.title: Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity and Digital Learning Resilience in Higher Education: An Integrative Review and Capacity-Sensitive Framework for Resource-Constrained Universities
doi:10.9734/ajrcos/2026/v19i10925.abstract:
<jats:p>Purpose: Artificial intelligence (AI) is now embedded in teaching, assessment and administration in higher education, simultaneously widening educational opportunity and institutional cyber exposure. This review examines how AI-related and conventional cyber threats affect the continuity of digital learning, how AI can both amplify and mitigate those threats, and which integrated responses are feasible for resource-constrained universities, with Nigeria as the illustrative context.
Design/Methodology/Approach: A narrative integrative review following established integrative-review guidance synthesised 60 sources published mainly between 2019 and 2026, comprising peer-reviewed studies, technical standards, policy and legal instruments, and institutional or industry reports. Sources were organised by threat mechanism, institutional vulnerability, educational consequence, response and implementation constraint, and each was classified by the type of inference it can support.
Findings: Seven overlapping threat clusters were identified: AI-enhanced social engineering and identity abuse; ransomware and extortion; privacy leakage and surveillance; platform and supply-chain compromise; manipulation of AI-enabled learning systems; synthetic media and assessment-integrity attacks; and human, governance and infrastructure weaknesses. Experimental evidence shows that large language models lower the cost of persuasive phishing, while AI-text detectors and automated proctoring raise reliability and fairness concerns. AI-assisted defence offers measurable triage benefits but introduces false alarms, concept drift, privacy exposure and automation bias.
Originality/Value: The proposed AI-Cybersecurity-Digital Learning Resilience (AIC-DLR) Framework adapts NIST CSF 2.0 functions to the educational mission, overlays NIST AI risk-management guidance, and treats usable, equitable recovery of teaching and assessment, rather than system restoration alone, as the protected outcome. A tiered roadmap and a set of operationally defined indicators translate the framework into testable practice.
Practical Implications: Priorities for low-capacity institutions are accountable ownership, phishing-resistant identity for privileged users, tested and isolated backups, proportionate data practices, governed AI use and pre-authorised alternative learning channels. The framework is conceptual and unvalidated; comparative implementation studies are required to establish its effect on recovery time and equitable access.</jats:p>

doi:10.12688/f1000research.191826.1.title: Learning-strategy profiles and academic achievement in high-school students: a latent profile analysis based on the ACRA model
doi:10.12688/f1000research.191826.1.abstract: <ns3:p>Background Strategic learning is especially relevant in high school, a stage marked by increasing academic demands and a presupposed but still-developing cognitive autonomy. Research on learning strategies has relied mainly on variable-centered analyses; this study adds a person-centered analysis whose core is the identification of strategic profiles through latent profile analysis Methods Participants were 154 Ecuadorian students (55.8% female) from the three high-school grades, selected through stratified probability sampling. The ACRA Learning Strategies Scales were administered and grade-point average was collected. A latent profile analysis compared one- to six-class solutions; registered sex and grade level were entered as control variables to assess the independence and robustness of the solution. Results Three profiles ordered by strategic-repertoire intensity were identified: low (18.2%), moderate (47.4%), and comprehensive (34.4%), differing in level rather than shape, with Retrieval and Support as the most discriminating dimensions. Profile membership was independent of registered sex and grade level, a central finding supporting the robustness of the classification. The comprehensive profile outperformed the low profile, and this difference held when accounting for the control variables. Conclusions With the caution required by a cross-sectional design, findings support a positive relationship between the breadth of the strategic repertoire and academic achievement and point toward universal, curriculum-embedded strategy instruction.</ns3:p>

doi:10.1002/app.71656.title: Zn/Al‐ <scp> NO <sub>3</sub> </scp> Layered Double Hydroxide as Alternative Activator for Nitrile Rubber Vulcanization: Effect of the Accelerator‐to‐Sulfur Ratio on Curing Kinetics and Network Properties
authors: Marcus Vinícius Alves Sampaio de Souza
doi:10.1002/app.71656.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Reducing zinc content in rubber formulations remains an important challenge due to environmental concerns associated with the use of zinc oxide (ZnO) as part of vulcanization systems. Zinc‐containing layered double hydroxides (Zn/Al‐LDHs) offer an alternative approach to incorporating zinc into lamellar structure and have been investigated as both vulcanization activators and fillers. However, the curing behavior of unmodified Zn/Al‐NO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    LDH in conventional nitrile rubber (NBR) remains insufficiently understood. In this study, Zn/Al‐NO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    LDH was evaluated as an alternative low‐zinc vulcanization activator for nitrile rubber (NBR) as a replacement for the ZnO/stearic acid system. Conventional (A/S = 0.6) and efficient (A/S = 3.0) sulfur‐curing systems were compared. In the conventional system, the LDH decreased the apparent Ea from 90.81 to 70.95 kJ.mol
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    and reduced the pre‐exponential factor by approximately two orders of magnitude. Tensile strength remained comparable, whereas tear strength decreased by approximately 14%. Thermogravimetric analysis showed a slight increase in the onset degradation temperature for the LDH‐containing formulations. Based on nominal compositions, replacing the ZnO/stearic acid activation system with Zn/Al‐NO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    LDH corresponded to an estimated 71% reduction in zinc loading. Environmental benefits cannot be inferred from this reduction because zinc release, bioavailability, and ecotoxicological effects were not evaluated.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74871-z.title: A multi task deep learning framework for automated health condition prediction from retinal fundus images using hybrid attention and explainable AI
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-74871-z.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Although retinal fundus imaging is a non-invasive tool to assess systemic and fundus pathology, current deep learning algorithms are mostly single-task, lack clinical interpretability and are unable to handle acquisition variation between different domains. These constraints limit their clinical utility: when a patient comes to the clinic for fundus screening, they could also be diabetic, have glaucoma, AMD, and increased cardiovascular risk, with each disease having retinal vascular biomarkers that require a patient to be tested for in the clinic, which must be managed within a framework of common, interpretable, and generalizable models rather than a pipeline of independent models. To solve these problems, we suggest a multi-task deep learning network that simultaneously classifies DR severity (five-class), glaucoma likelihood (binary), AMD stage (four-class) and cardiovascular risk (binary) from a single retinal fundus image using a single forward pass. It adopts an EfficientNet-B4 convolutional backbone pretrained on the ImageNet dataset, a six-layer multi-head self-attention Transformer encoder (d_model = 512, h = 8), a novel dual-branch spatial-channel attention module that builds on, but significantly expands, the CBAM module, and four task-specific output heads that are optimized using the homoscedastic uncertainty-weighted multi-task loss following the formulation of Kendall et al. Per-task anatomical explanations are produced by back propagating the CNN backbone via Grad-CAM in the anatomical space. The proposed model was evaluated on EyePACS, APTOS 2019, Messidor-2 and RIM-ONE v3 and achieved an accuracy of 94.7%, AUC = 0.978, sensitivity = 93.2% and specificity = 95.8% while being statistically better than all single task models (DeLong test,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     < 0.01, Bonferroni corrected). Under the reported experimental setting, the zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation achieves AUC ≥ 0.951, which is promising for its performance across datasets. Grad-CAM saliency maps are anatomically similar to established clinical grading criteria for each disease. The four task-specific heads share a single architecture and produce four outputs in one forward pass, but no individual patient in the training corpora had verified ground-truth labels for all four conditions simultaneously; the model is trained on partially labelled, multi-source data via a masked multi-task loss, and the cardiovascular output is an AVR-derived image-based surrogate rather than a validated clinical cardiovascular diagnosis. This proposed framework could be considered for an additional potential step toward the future when it comes to multi-disease fundus screening with an interpretable single-model solution, if it is assessed and approved at an independent multi-centre level and by regulatory bodies.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1520.c6135.title: A Comparative Analysis of Quality Assurance Systems in the Aviation Sector: A Quantitative Study on ISO 9001, AS9100, and EASA Part-145
doi:10.58830/ozgur.pub1520.c6135.abstract: <jats:p>Quality assurance is of significant importance in the aviation sector due to high safety requirements and critical operational processes. Quality assurance systems are organizational and systematic structures established to ensure that all aviation activities are conducted in compliance with national and international standards as well as legal regulations. Given the high safety demands of aviation operations, these systems require not only the inspection of product or service outputs but also the execution of all processes, including design, production, maintenance, and operations, within a structured framework that allows for planning, traceability, and auditing. This study presents a comparative analysis of ISO 9001, AS9100, and EASA Part-145, which are widely used quality assurance standards in the industry. These systems were evaluated based on aviation-specific criteria, including their contribution to safety, compliance with laws and regulations, audit and traceability structures, applicability and operational compatibility, the maturity of documentation and record-keeping systems, implementation and operating costs, and requirements for personnel training and competence. The purpose of this study is to present a systematic approach to help companies in the aviation industry select or develop a quality assurance model suited to their scale and operational needs by identifying the strengths and weaknesses of various quality management systems. The SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) method was employed for qualitative analysis, while the quantitative assessment was supported by multi-criteria decision-making methods, specifically AHP (Analytic Hierarchy Process) and TOPSIS (Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution). Additionally, a sensitivity analysis was conducted to assess the robustness of the findings. In the TOPSIS analysis, EASA Part-145 was identified as the alternative closest to the ideal solution, ranking above AS9100 and ISO 9001. However, the study's findings indicated that, rather than substituting one system for another, the most rational approach would be to select the system based on the organization's size and activities.</jats:p>

doi:10.1177/27527646261496291.title: Shared “Scores”: Building Community Through Digital Game-Based Learning in Music Education
doi:10.1177/27527646261496291.abstract: <jats:p>Digital games are increasingly present in young people’s musical lives, yet their use in music classrooms can easily become individualized through scores, rankings, badges, and separate devices. In this column, I examine how digital game-based learning can support community-building in music education when teachers move beyond competition as the primary design principle. Drawing on research on digital game-based learning and music games, I offer examples and strategies, including composing for video-game scenes, structured improvisation games, multiplayer music participation, and students’ existing engagement with virtual music worlds. The goal is not to gamify every lesson, but to use play and game design to build musical community through shared participation, culturally responsive practice, and creative meaning-making.</jats:p>

doi:10.51878/teacher.v6i4.15632.abstract:
<jats:p>This study was motivated by the low learning outcomes of students in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS), particularly on environmental issues, due to teacher-centered instruction. It aimed to describe the implementation of the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model and the improvement in learning outcomes among Grade V students at UPTD SD Negeri 078131 Nikootanodao. This study employed a Classroom Action Research (CAR) design based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model, conducted in two cycles. The participants were 16 students. Data were collected through learning outcome tests, observations of teacher and student activities, and documentation. Data were analyzed qualitatively and quantitatively by calculating mean scores and classical learning mastery percentages. The findings showed that teacher activity increased from 59.62% in Cycle I to 83.66% in Cycle II, while student activity increased from 54.53% to 82.66%. The mean learning outcome score increased from 53.12 at baseline to 63.06 in Cycle I and 84.56 in Cycle II. Classical learning mastery also improved from 31.25% at baseline to 56.25% in Cycle I and 87.5% in Cycle II. Therefore, implementing PBL improved the learning process and student learning outcomes on environmental issues.
ABSTRAK
Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh rendahnya hasil belajar peserta didik pada mata pelajaran IPAS materi permasalahan lingkungan akibat pembelajaran yang masih berpusat pada guru. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan penerapan model Problem Based Learning (PBL) dan peningkatan hasil belajar peserta didik kelas V UPTD SD Negeri 078131 Nikootanodao. Penelitian menggunakan metode Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) dengan model Kemmis dan McTaggart yang dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 16 peserta didik. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes hasil belajar, observasi aktivitas guru dan peserta didik, serta dokumentasi. Data dianalisis secara kualitatif dan kuantitatif melalui perhitungan rata-rata nilai dan persentase ketuntasan klasikal. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa aktivitas guru meningkat dari 59,62% pada siklus I menjadi 83,66% pada siklus II, sedangkan aktivitas peserta didik meningkat dari 54,53% menjadi 82,66%. Rata-rata hasil belajar meningkat dari 53,12 pada kondisi awal menjadi 63,06 pada siklus I dan 84,56 pada siklus II. Ketuntasan klasikal juga meningkat dari 31,25% pada kondisi awal menjadi 56,25% pada siklus I dan 87,5% pada siklus II. Dengan demikian, penerapan PBL dapat memperbaiki proses pembelajaran dan meningkatkan hasil belajar peserta didik pada materi permasalahan lingkungan.</jats:p>

doi:10.1177/10538259261499652.title: Translating Service-Learning Standards Into Practice: A Multiple-Case Study of Undergraduate Courses
doi:10.1177/10538259261499652.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Service-learning is widely used in higher education, yet less is known about how principles of high-quality service-learning are interpreted and operationalized across undergraduate courses.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This qualitative multiple-case study examined how undergraduate instructors interpreted and operationalized principles associated with high-quality service-learning using the Standards for Quality Practice as an analytic framework.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Method</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, open-ended surveys, and course materials from 11 instructors representing 13 undergraduate service-learning courses across multiple disciplines and institutions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>lthough only one instructor reported prior familiarity with the Standards, instructors generally described practices aligned with the framework's dimensions. Instructors shared similar goals but interpreted and operationalized principles in varied, integrated, and context-dependent ways. Reflection and curricular integration reflected relatively consistent understandings, whereas meaningful service, student voice, diversity, partnerships, and other dimensions were enacted through multiple approaches. Course structure, institutional context, community partnerships, and logistical constraints further shaped implementation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Understanding service-learning quality requires examining how recommended dimensions are interpreted and enacted within particular contexts. This perspective has implications for faculty development, institutional support, and future research.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.71085/sss.05.04.628.title: The relationship between cognitive styles and learning strategies of secondary school students in Lahore, Pakistan
doi:10.71085/sss.05.04.628.abstract: <jats:p>Cognitive styles and learning strategies are widely assumed to be closely linked, and this assumption underpins advice that teachers should match instruction to students' styles. This study examined whether such a link exists among secondary school students in Pakistan. A descriptive correlational survey design was used. Data were collected from 152 students in public and private secondary schools in District Lahore, selected through simple random sampling (250 questionnaires distributed; 60.8% usable return). Students completed a 15-item paired-statement Cognitive Style Questionnaire and a 40-item adapted version of the Learning Style Survey covering ten strategy dimensions. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and standard multiple regression. Students reported frequent use of all ten strategy dimensions (M = 3.54 to 3.92 on a 0–4 scale). However, the overall correlation between cognitive style and learning strategies was negligible and non-significant (r = .025, p = .763). Only two dimensions showed weak significant correlations with cognitive style: use of physical senses (r = −.166, p = .041) and dealing with multiple inputs (r = .177, p = .029). Together, the ten dimensions explained 13% of the variance in cognitive style (R² = .13, adjusted R² = .07, F(10, 141) = 2.09, p = .029). The findings suggest that, for these learners, strategy use is largely independent of cognitive style. Strategy instruction may therefore benefit all students, regardless of style.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/978-3-032-40121-2_11.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Verification of safety requirements in hybrid systems is crucial, yet system-specific analyses are often costly or infeasible. Formal modeling enables mathematically precise representations and supports rigorous techniques such as flowpipe analysis. This work focuses on Stochastic Hybrid Models (SHM) and presents a simulator that combines
                    <jats:italic>symbolic</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>subsymbolic</jats:italic>
                    artificial intelligence. On the symbolic side, nondeterministic choices are resolved through precise computations based on precomputed state-space representations; additionally, reachability analysis enables the simulation to exclude unreachable regions in a correct-by-construction manner. On the subsymbolic side, Q-learning is used to resolve nondeterminism. We introduce suitable discretization and partitioning techniques that enable SHM models to be represented as Discrete Event Systems and analyzed through discrete event simulation. The simulator is integrated into RealySt, and provides configurable learning parameters, discretization settings, and currently supports two scheduler classes. Evaluation of the water tank benchmark and comparison with existing approaches validate our approach and show that Q-learning effectively resolves continuous nondeterminism. By integrating constraints on the energy consumption of the pumps within the water tank model, we are able to illustrate the benefit of
                    <jats:italic>guidance</jats:italic>
                    when maximizing a property with a relatively low probability of occurrence.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.65655/ocp.m29.c102.title: Designing and Quality-Assuring Online, Blended, and Flexible Higher Education
doi:10.65655/ocp.m29.c102.abstract: Digitally mediated higher education is often judged through the existence of a learning-management system, the volume of uploaded content or the proportion of teaching conducted remotely. None establishes that a programme offers academically equivalent, accessible and sustainable opportunities for learning. Building upon an integrated account of educational purpose, institutional capability and curriculum coherence, this chapter develops a context-sensitive approach to designing and quality-assuring online, blended and flexible provision. A critical, purposive documentary synthesis brings established digital-learning scholarship into dialogue with Rwanda’s Higher Education Council guidelines, continental quality principles and international accessibility and course-design benchmarks. Four theoretical perspectives, Community of Inquiry, transactional distance, self-regulated learning and constructive alignment, explain complementary design problems without being treated as predictive laws. The analysis examines delivery-mode selection, learning pathways, synchronous and asynchronous participation, learning-platform architecture, multimedia and open resources, practical learning, interaction, low-bandwidth provision, faculty development, assessment, monitoring and accreditation readiness. Its distinctive contribution is an evidence-traceable model connecting educational design decisions with demonstrated technical functioning, staff and learner capability, assessment validity and continuing improvement. Six complementary practical instruments and a worked hypothetical programme review illustrate how proposed quality criteria can be translated into verifiable questions and corrective decisions. Official requirements, professional benchmarks and author-developed recommendations remain explicitly distinguished. The proposed instruments have not been regulator-approved or independently validated; their value lies in transparent, adaptable professional reasoning rather than a claim of universal effectiveness.

doi:10.1177/23733799261495092.title: Using Photovoice to Examine Student Learning in Graduate Health Administration: A Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) Study
doi:10.1177/23733799261495092.abstract: <jats:p>This pilot study explores the use of photovoice as an experiential learning (EL) tool in graduate health administration education, focusing on concepts related to the Social Determinants of Health (SDOH). Photovoice, a methodology rooted in participatory action research (PAR), is recognized as an active learning approach that promotes deeper insights and shifts in understanding. The project engaged 51 graduate students across 3 in-person health administration courses in a 6-week assignment involving original photography and a descriptive narrative (up to 250 words) to reflect on observed SDOH in their communities. Data were collected via the graded student assignments and a subsequent open-ended reflection survey. Employing a Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) approach, the systematic analysis of the qualitative data revealed four major themes: (1). Recognizing Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) and Societal Impact; (2). Connecting Personal Experience to Professional Identity; (3). Building Systems Thinking and Applied Insight; and (4). Reimagining Learning through Experiential Reflection. These findings demonstrate how integrating participatory and experiential pedagogies cultivates purposeful reflection, applied problem-solving, and professional competencies crucial for future health promotion leaders. The study fulfills the goal of SoTL scholarship by disseminating findings to refine course design and enhance student understanding of complex health inequities.</jats:p>

doi:10.9734/jesbs/2026/v39i51530.title: Students’ Perceptions and Importance of Teacher Emotional Support in Online English Learning: Examining the Gap Between Importance and Actual Perception
doi:10.9734/jesbs/2026/v39i51530.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: Teacher emotional support is relevant to students’ emotional experiences in online English learning, but the alignment between the importance students attribute to such support and the support they report perceiving remains insufficiently examined.
Aims: To investigate university students’ perceptions of teacher emotional support in online English learning by examining two dimensions: perceived importance and actual perception.
Study Design: A quantitative research design was adopted.
Place and Duration of Study: Data were collected at a Chinese university over approximately one week.
Methodology: A total of 397 Chinese university students participated in the questionnaire survey. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and paired-samples t-tests in SPSS 28 to examine students’ perceived importance and actual perception of teacher emotional support in online English learning.
Results: Students generally regarded teacher emotional support as highly important, whereas their reported perception of teacher emotional support was comparatively lower. A significant difference was found between the two dimensions.
Conclusion: The findings suggest that a noticeable gap exists between students’ perceived importance of teacher emotional support and their actual perceptions of such support in online English learning contexts. This study provides empirical evidence for understanding teacher emotional support in online English learning and highlights the need for teachers to strengthen emotional support practices to better meet students’ emotional needs in digital learning.</jats:p>

doi:10.48175/ijarsct-38925.title: An Explainable Uncertainty-Weighted Multi-Task Learning Framework for Joint Crop Recommendation and NPK Prediction with Probabilistic Crop Conditioning
authors: Aakash Verma and Vineet Kumar Avasthi
doi:10.48175/ijarsct-38925.abstract: <jats:p>Crop selection and fertilizer planning are of generally based on farmer experience, even though suitable crops and nutrient needs depend on soil and environmental conditions that vary between fields. In many existing systems, crop recommendation and nutrient prediction are handled by separate models, and few explain  how reliable a given prediction is. This study proposes a multi-task learning model that predicts the recommended crop and the nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (NPK) requirement from seven pre crop inputs: soil type, season, soil pH, temperature, water requirement, relative humidity, and water source. A shared network feeds a crop classification head and an NPK regression head. The NPK head receives the full predicted crop probability vector instead of the true crop label, and the two task losses are balanced using learned uncertainty parameters. Monte Carlo Dropout estimates the uncertainty of each prediction, and SHAP shows which inputs drove it. On a dataset of 57,000 observations covering 57 crops, the model reached an accuracy of 0.9496 and a macro F1-score of 0.9463 for crop classification, below Random Forest (0.9627) and XGBoost (0.9618). The mean NPK R² was 0.8537, compared with 0.8518 for XGBoost and 0.8501 for a standalone DNN. The calibration error was 0.0072, and results were stable across five random seeds. SHAP showed that soil type, season, and relative humidity contributed most to both tasks. The trained model was built into a recommendation system that returns a crop, NPK values with uncertainty intervals, and an explanation.</jats:p>
