Extensive experiments across diverse search settings, including rare-species discovery and target-aligned molecule generation tasks, demonstrate BSIT's superior search efficiency over the baselines.

arxiv:2610.24161.title: TorchTPU - A Hybrid Eager/Compiled Architecture for Native PyTorch Execution on TPU
arxiv:2610.24161.abstract: TorchTPU is an open-source collaboration between Google and Meta that introduces a native and principled PyTorch backend for Google TPUs. It enables seamless out-of-the-box model execution and TPU migration while delivering industry-competitive inference and training performance through eager execution optimizations, torch.compile integration, and native hardware acceleration.

arxiv:2610.24157.title: CoDA: A Human-LM Collaborative Codebook Development Assistant for Domain-Specific Text Annotation
arxiv:2610.24157.abstract: We present CoDA, an open-source human-LM collaborative codebook development assistant that helps domain experts develop annotation guidelines for annotating new variables in unstructured text with language models. Existing language model annotation systems primarily focus on downstream classification performance, while assuming the availability of high-quality annotation guidelines, or codebooks. In practice, developing these codebooks is time-consuming and challenging, particularly for concepts that require expert knowledge. CoDA addresses this gap by collaborating with domain experts to iteratively develop codebooks through targeted review of incorrect language model predictions and incorporating expert feedback into the evolving codebook. We demonstrate CoDA on two real-world case studies: extracting health indicators from homelessness case management notes and classifying sentiment of wildlife trafficking posts on social media. Across both domains, CoDA produces codebooks that achieve downstream classification performance comparable to expert codebooks while reducing codebook development time from several weeks to two hours and requiring 5X fewer manually annotated examples. Applying CoDA to generate annotations at scale, we identified 2,410 case notes that contained health discussions or referrals and 10,196 social media posts expressing negative sentiment that may warrant investigation for potential wildlife trafficking. By accelerating codebook development, CoDA helps practitioners use language models to extract domain-specific insights from unstructured text at scale.

arxiv:2610.24126.title: Data-Driven Resource Aggregation for Scalable Digital Twin and Simulation Model Generation
arxiv:2610.24126.abstract: As industrial digitization accelerates, the use of digital twins has become widespread. However, modern manufacturing systems are highly dynamic and frequently reconfigured, making manual model development and updates increasingly difficult. Recent research on automated simulation model generation shows that historical data such as event logs can yield simulation models automatically. However, modeling every resource at full granularity leads to unnecessary complexity and computational cost. We propose a method for automatically selecting and aggregating resources to simplify simulation modeling. Our method uses ideas from inverse reinforcement learning to learn behavioral value representations of resources from production event logs. This process identifies and aggregates resources with similar functional contributions. Experiments on manufacturing systems, using throughput and system time as performance measures, demonstrate that value-based resource aggregation performs well when the goal is to substantially reduce complexity while preserving performance accuracy.

arxiv:2610.24124.title: On the Selectivity of Generative Models in Structure-Based Drug Design
arxiv:2610.24124.abstract: Designing small-molecule drugs that selectively bind to a target protein while avoiding unintended interactions with other proteins is essential for reducing side effects that contribute substantially to clinical attrition. Although structure-based drug design (SBDD) has advanced rapidly with deep learning, most generative models still optimize binding to a single target and disregard selectivity due to limited training data and unknown off-target interactions. Motivated by this gap, we introduce SELECTBENCH, a comprehensive benchmark assessing the selectivity of generative SBDD models. SELECTBENCH provides three curated evaluation tasks reflecting different real-world drug discovery scenarios: literature-based case studies, safety screening panels used in pharmaceutical development, and large-scale structure-based evaluation sets. We further introduce a suite of metrics to quantify selectivity and conduct a systematic evaluation of nine representative SBDD models, including methods explicitly trained for selectivity and widely-used inference-time guidance techniques. Our results show that even selectivity-trained models achieve only modest off-target discrimination and inference-time guidance provides limited gains, underscoring the need for method improvement. SELECTBENCH provides both a characterization of where current generative SBDD stands on selectivity and an open, extensible platform to accelerate progress. The benchmark is available at https://github.com/lovetaro/selectbench.

arxiv:2610.24113.title: Graph-Regularized Synthetic Control for Stable Counterfactual Estimation under Donor Redundancy
arxiv:2610.24113.abstract: Synthetic control methods estimate counterfactual outcomes by weighting untreated donor units to match a treated unit before treatment. In recent applications, however, the donor pool can be large, highly correlated, and short in pre-treatment history, yielding many near-equivalent solutions with unstable and difficult-to-interpret donor weights. We propose Graph-Regularized Synthetic Control (Graph-SC), a convex estimator that augments the classical pre-treatment matching objective with a graph Laplacian penalty. The graph encodes similarity among donor trajectories, encouraging coherent weights over structurally related donors while preserving the transparency of synthetic controls. We provide theoretical results characterizing the bias-variance tradeoff induced by graph regularization and establish efficient convergence guarantees with an accelerated proximal gradient method. Across a controlled simulation under donor redundancy, the California Proposition 99 benchmark, and observational counterfactual analyses on the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, Graph-SC improves weight stability, reduces sensitivity to redundant donor pools, and maintains competitive pre- and post-treatment accuracy relative to classical and regularized synthetic control baselines. Our results suggest that graph regularization is most valuable not as a universal accuracy booster, but as a principled mechanism for selecting stable and interpretable counterfactuals from near-equivalent synthetic controls with comparable pre-treatment fit.

arxiv:2610.24093.title: Does AI-Assisted Development Homogenize Software? An Empirical Study of Code Similarity, Quality, and Evolution
arxiv:2610.24093.abstract: AI-assisted software development is evolving from interactive LLM assistance toward agentic systems that autonomously perform software engineering tasks, yet the effects of this shift remain insufficiently understood. We present an empirical study of 50 long-lived Java and Python open-source projects across three eras: pre-LLM, potentially LLM-assisted, and detected agentic development. Using snapshots from Software Heritage, we examine code similarity, software quality, and software evolution. Similarity is measured semantically through embedding-based cosine similarity and syntactically through CodeBLEU*. Quality is assessed with SonarQube metrics covering maintainability, complexity, reliability, and security. Evolution is characterized by annualized growth rates of LOC, functions, classes, files, and statements, and by commit activity in the three months preceding each snapshot. Results show no consistent evidence of increased similarity as semantic and syntactic similarity decreased significantly in Java for both the LLM and agentic eras relative to the pre-LLM era, while Python showed no significant differences. Software quality remained largely stable, although the agentic era showed significantly lower code-smell and SQALE index densities. Structural growth was generally lower in the agentic era, particularly for files, whereas development activity increased moderately in Java, especially in commits and added lines. These findings challenge the assumption that LLM- and agent-assisted development necessarily homogenizes code, degrades quality, or accelerates growth.

arxiv:2610.23935.title: Factorization-Guided Training and Inference for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding
arxiv:2610.23935.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference through parallel verification of tokens proposed by a drafter. Diffusion drafters further parallelize proposal generation, but greater proposal capacity or higher mean accepted tokens (MAT) need not yield higher throughput. Because verification accepts only a consecutive prefix, early rejections can render later correct predictions ineffective, limiting MAT gains, while even higher MAT may not improve throughput if per-round latency increases. We introduce DScout, which uses two complementary factorizations to guide diffusion drafter training and inference for higher throughput. For training, DScout factorizes position-wise loss into inclusion, weighting, and prediction loss. This guides the design and combination of mixed-horizon training, intra-block unmasking, and acceptance-weighted loss to align supervision with prefix acceptance and improve MAT. For inference, DScout factorizes throughput as the ratio of MAT to per-round latency, guiding target-conditioning depth, drafter depth, and inference block size selection to identify a high-throughput configuration for each workload. Across six benchmarks, DScout achieves $3.84\times$ and $4.14\times$ mean speedups over autoregressive decoding on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, respectively, improving mean speedup over the state-of-the-art baseline by 9.1% and 7.1%. Across models and concurrency settings, our inference configuration policy provides up to 9.75% additional mean speedup over DScout's fixed configuration.

arxiv:2610.10118.title: EdgeRock: Strong Reasoning at Constant Memory
arxiv:2610.10118.abstract: We present EdgeRock, a family of multimodal models that deliver strong reasoning at constant memory. Most models keep reasoning history in a key-value (KV) cache that grows with every token, consuming accelerator memory, limiting concurrent requests, and competing with perception and control on edge devices. With fixed history, memory is allocated once and never runs out, however long the model reasons. Constant memory alone is not new: bounded-state models (recurrent, state-space, and sliding-window) already achieve it, but often at the cost of reasoning, because they cannot keep the distant details that later reasoning needs. We therefore introduce Rock Memory Anchors (RMA): the model learns what is worth remembering and stores it as KV records in a fixed-size bank, directly readable however far back the source lies. EdgeRock-4B, our first open-source release, supports text and image reasoning and reaches 82.9% mean pass@1 on AIME 2024-2026, while the bounded-state models we evaluate reach at most 18.8%, even at 14B scale. This result is on par with leading compact models whose memory grows with reasoning. Compared with its source model, EdgeRock-4B uses up to 99.1% less KV cache and delivers up to 6.42$\times$ higher end-to-end batch throughput.

arxiv:2610.23928.title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
arxiv:2610.23928.abstract: Native NVFP4 promises to accelerate reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models (LLMs), but achieving stable learning across separate training and sampling engines remains challenging. We show that matching model weights and numerical formats is insufficient to ensure consistent policy evaluation, highlighting the importance of cross-engine numerical execution. We introduce miniTE, a lightweight framework that combines execution diagnostics, cross-engine numerical alignment, and efficient native W4A4 (4-bit weights and activations) GEMM computation for LLM RL. It improves numerical execution consistency without modifying the RL objective, while reducing implementation overhead to realize the benefits of native low-bit computation. Long-horizon RL experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B demonstrate stable training and benchmark performance close to BF16, outperforming naive Transformer Engine (TE) NVFP4 in evaluation quality. On single NVIDIA B300 GPU node, the optimized learner reaches 33,540 tokens/s, yielding 1.39x and 1.47x the throughput of BF16 and TE NVFP4, respectively, for complete learner updates. We released the framework, kernels, diagnostics, and training configurations to make native low-bit RL easier.

arxiv:2610.23915.title: Your Self-Supervised Projection Head Captures Object Co-Occurrence Statistics
arxiv:2610.23915.abstract: Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) has achieved impressive success in learning semantic visual representations, yet the underlying principles driving this success remain underexplored. In this work, we hypothesize that common SSL pretext tasks implicitly model object co-occurrence statistics, a fundamental cue for visual learning. To test this, we curate three datasets of segmented objects from existing vision benchmarks using a state-of-the-art segmentation model. Through experiments across many SSL models, we reveal a hierarchical encoding of semantic information: while the visual backbone captures object categories, the projection head specializes in encoding co-occurrences between object categories. As a result, the projection head outperforms the backbone in aligning with human judgments of inter-category similarity. Furthermore, by controlling co-occurrence patterns during pre-training, we demonstrate that encoding object co-occurrences can significantly accelerate the emergence of category-level representations. Our findings uncover a previously hidden learning principle in SSL and suggest a path toward designing more effective pretext tasks by explicitly leveraging object co-occurrence structure.

arxiv:2610.25285.title: A discrete-continuous-time stochastic framework for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder-related symptom modeling and pharmacological intervention via methylphenidate
arxiv:2610.25285.abstract: This paper presents an original mathematical and computational framework for modeling the efficacy of methylphenidate as an optimal control policy acting on the nonlinear dynamics of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder. Neural processes in ADHD are conceptualized as stochastic processes with trajectories that inherently converge towards stable, yet dysfunctional patterns associated with clinical symptoms. The pharmacological intervention is mathematically formalized as an external control signal that reassesses the system's drift and redirects these trajectories towards neurotypical regimes. To bridge these theoretical stochastic models with empirical clinical data, latent representations are inferred using a novel deterministic hybrid deep learning architecture, combining a one-dimensional convolutional neural network and a Vision Transformer, trained on preprocessed functional magnetic resonance imaging data.

arxiv:2610.25019.title: LLM Agents as Suppliers of Physical System Models: Calibration and Acceptance in Modelica
arxiv:2610.25019.abstract: To procure a model of a device, a client hands a supplier a description, sometimes with recorded data or a target response, and accepts the model against this handover. We let LLM coding agents act as the supplier on handovers with data, building Modelica models from library components for four simulated systems and a real switching magnet, and ask what acceptance certifies. Several agents reach the noise floor, but a handover admits a set of models: the description leaves parts of the structure open, and the data narrow it only to the agreed accuracy. We therefore accept by membership in this set, not by matching one reference, and add layers above behaviour: a physical invariant exposes an energy-creating model at the noise floor. Interpretability becomes a property of the delivered model, tested on a variant, read where none exists and shaped through the handover. Most failures are fits delivered with a systematic residual on their own fitting data, where the handover left open how close is close enough. In a follow-up, stating a threshold makes the agents compare against it, and more deliveries pass. The argument applies wherever a handover underspecifies a model meant to be read, not only run.

arxiv:2610.25634.title: Clean Forcing: Drift-Resistant Autoregressive Video Diffusion with a Frozen Base
arxiv:2610.25634.abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models generate streaming video of arbitrary length by conditioning each new chunk of frames on those already generated. However, they suffer from exposure bias, where a model trained on clean context must continue from its own imperfect outputs, and errors compound until quality collapses within seconds (drift). Existing methods either require cluster-scale base retraining, apply training-free inference corrections with inconsistent results, or train frozen-base correctors for sampling and cache errors. We instead find that drift is largely deterministic and therefore learnable, as holding the noisy state fixed while varying only the history reveals a counterfactual velocity gap that is ~95% systematic across noise seeds. Based on this observation, we introduce Clean Forcing, which trains a 5.9M-parameter LoRA corrector on the frozen base model to regress this gap, with a closed-loop stage that adds DAgger-style aggregation and a drift-contraction objective to expose the corrector to its own rollouts. Because the clean histories can be the base model's own single-shot generations, training needs no real videos, and the merged corrector adds no inference cost. In 50 s text-to-video generation, Clean Forcing reduces Δ-drift from +11.3 to +1.65 without real video and to -0.16 with 40 real clips, improving on the best published result of +3.57 with over 150x less data. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Clean Forcing outperforms prior methods in aesthetic quality and data efficiency with reduced drift for long-horizon video generation.

arxiv:2610.22384.title: Automated end-station at the soft X-ray beamline featuring robotic air-to-ultrahigh-vacuum sample transfer, scanning probe spectroscopy, and machine learning analysis
arxiv:2610.22384.abstract: Driven by the growing integration of artificial intelligence and robotics in experimental science, we redefine the execution of user experiments at synchrotron soft X-ray beamlines by developing a highly automated end-station that can be operated without on-site staff. Installed at beamline BL08U of NanoTerasu, the system comprises four chamber units and two robots that automatically transfer samples from ambient air to an ultrahigh vacuum measurement stage for spectroscopic evaluations, before returning them to their original locations post-measurement. Soft X-ray absorption spectra are automatically acquired once programmed by scanning the micro-focused beam over the designated sample area, followed by automated evaluation using machine learning techniques such as principal-component analysis, multidimensional scaling, t-distributed stochastic neighbour embedding, and uniform manifold approximation and projection. The high-throughput data are systematically accumulated in the database for remote user examination. This unstaffed end-station provides efficient beamtime for users and allows beamline scientists/technicians to pursue more human and creative endeavors.

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch002.title: The Transformative Role of STEAM and Makerspace
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch002.abstract: <jats:p>STEAM education and makerspaces are among the most influential approaches in contemporary educational practice, emphasizing learning by doing, creativity, collaboration, and innovation. Although these approaches are often associated with recent educational reforms and technological developments, their underlying pedagogical principles can also be identified in historical educational models. Türkiye offers a unique example in this regard through two educational initiatives: the Village Institutes and DENEYAP. This chapter examines the Village Institutes and DENEYAP through the conceptual lenses of the Maker Movement and the STEAM approach. By comparing these historical and contemporary initiatives, the chapter argues that the philosophy of learning through making and doing has deep roots in the Turkish educational context. The analysis highlights both the continuities and transformations between these two models and discusses their implications for future educational practices in Türkiye.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-7734-6.ch002.title: Artificial Intelligence in Marketing From Predictive Analytics to Generative Creativity
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-7734-6.ch002.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the foundations of modern marketing, shifting from data-driven decision-making toward an era of intelligent creativity that fuses predictive analytics with generative innovation. This chapter conceptually examines how the integration of predictive and generative AI—through the Integrated Predictive–Generative Framework (IPGF)—redefines marketing intelligence by merging analytical precision with creative synthesis. Through theoretical analysis and case-based interpretation, the chapter explores predictive AI in forecasting consumer behavior and generative AI in producing personalized, emotionally resonant content. It also identifies ethical, psychological, and social implications associated with AI-driven creativity, emphasizing transparency, fairness, and human oversight as essential principles for sustainable, human-centered marketing ecosystems.</jats:p>

doi:10.32672/perisai.v5i3.4661.title: <b>PENGARUH MEDIA PEMBELAJARAN <i>CANVA AUDIO VISUAL LEARNING</i> (CAVIL) TERHADAP HASIL BELAJAR SISWA</b><b></b>
doi:10.32672/perisai.v5i3.4661.abstract: <jats:p>Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh Media Pembelajaran Canva Audio Visual Learning (CAVIL) terhadap hasil belajar siswa kelas V SD Negeri 25 Banda Aceh. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain eksperimen semu (quasi experiment) yang melibatkan dua kelompok, yaitu kelompok kontrol dan kelompok eksperimen. Teknik pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui pre-test dan post-test hasil belajar pada materi Bagaimana Kita Hidup dan Bertumbuh. Data dianalisis menggunakan uji non parametris Mann-Whitney untuk mengetahui perbedaan hasil belajar antara kedua kelompok. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rata-rata nilai pre-test kelompok kontrol sebesar  dan kelompok eksperimen sebesar  yang menunjukkan bahwa kemampuan awal siswa relatif setara. Setelah diberikan perlakuan, rata-rata nilai post-test kelompok kontrol meningkat menjadi , sedangkan kelompok eksperimen meningkat menjadi . Hasil uji Mann-Whitney pada data post-test menunjukkan nilai signifikansi sebesar , sehingga terdapat perbedaan yang signifikan antara kedua kelompok. Berdasarkan hasil tersebut dapat disimpulkan bahwa Media Pembelajaran Canva Audio Visual Learning (CAVIL) berpengaruh secara signifikan terhadap peningkatan hasil belajar siswa kelas V SD Negeri 25 Banda Aceh. Penggunaan media berbasis audio visual terbukti lebih efektif dalam meningkatkan pemahaman siswa dibandingkan pembelajaran konvensional.</jats:p>
doi:10.32672/perisai.v5i3.4661.venue: PERISAI: Jurnal Pendidikan dan Riset Ilmu Sains

doi:10.69760/aghel.026004015.title: Learning and Belonging in Les Demeurées: A Semiotic Reading of Educational Authority and Intellectual Emancipation
doi:10.69760/aghel.026004015.abstract: <jats:p>Jeanne Benameur’s Les Demeurées presents learning as a conflict over what knowledge does to relationships. This article examines how the novella constructs that conflict through recurrent semantic features, competing narrative programmes, and changes in the modalities of learning. A close reading of the French text combines Greimassian narrative semiotics with Rastierian interpretive semantics; Rancière’s account of intellectual emancipation provides a subsequent philosophical perspective. The analysis identifies a discrepancy between Luce’s retention of school discourse and her refusal to display or appropriate it under conditions associated with separation from her mother. Recurrent figures of enclosure, thresholds, naming, and material inscription change function as educational authority shifts. Embroidery reconnects retained lessons with bodily attention and an emerging wish to address the teacher. Yet this transformation neither vindicates withdrawal from schooling nor establishes the mother as an ideal educator. The teacher’s earlier instruction remains active, domestic attachment remains ambivalent, and the ending combines intellectual initiative with bereavement and continued institutional exclusion. The article argues that the novella represents educational emancipation as a reorganisation of the relations within which knowledge can become one’s own. Its distinctive contribution lies in tracing how semantic recurrences acquire different values across the narrative, allowing learning and belonging to become provisionally compatible without resolving the social conditions that initially opposed them.</jats:p>

doi:10.3130/aijt.32.1510.title: DEVELOPMENT OF A BOARD GAME AS A LEARNING TOOL TO PROMOTE HOUSEHOLD ACTIONS TOWARD NET-ZERO CARBON EMISSIONS
doi:10.3130/aijt.32.1510.abstract: Addressing climate change requires increased individual awareness and behavioral change. This study aims to encourage lifestyle transformation by illustrating how everyday behaviors influence CO2 emissions and future outcomes. To this end, a board game was developed to help players learn about the potential CO2 reduction effects of their daily choices. Through gameplay, participants recognize the impacts of various CO2-reducing actions and the significance of their cumulative effects. A workshop involving approximately 170 elementary and junior high school students confirmed behavioral changes among participants, demonstrating the effectiveness of the game.
doi:10.3130/aijt.32.1510.venue: AIJ Journal of Technology and Design

doi:10.20965/jrm.2026.p1402.title: Goal-Conditioned Self-Supervised Learning from Play Aimed at Human–Robot Collaboration
doi:10.20965/jrm.2026.p1402.abstract: <jats:p>Robots capable of accurately understanding situations based on environmental information and collaborating effectively with humans in a variety of tasks are in high demand. Deep-learning-based approaches can be effective for realizing such collaborative robots; however, collecting data and achieving high generalization performance are challenges. To address this issue, we utilize “play data” collected by teleoperating a robot when performing collaborative tasks with a human partner. This study proposes a play-supervised latent goal for human–robot collaboration (play-HRC) framework that learns from unlabeled play data for human–robot collaborative scenarios without explicit goal observation. Unlike play-supervised latent motor plan that generates actions conditioned on an externally specified goal observation, play-HRC must infer a latent goal from an initial state. At the beginning of the task execution, play-HRC infers an achievable goal from its initial state. During execution, it generates actions and predicts future environmental states while adaptively optimizing the latent goal by minimizing prediction errors. To evaluate the performance of play-HRC, we conducted tests in a real-world environment using a task in which a robot and human collaboratively manipulate objects. The results highlighted the ability of the framework to infer achievable goals, generate actions, and dynamically adjust goals in response to human behavior.</jats:p>

doi:10.55640/ijdsml-06-02-12.title: Continual Skill Adaptation for AI Agents Under Changing Tools and Policies: Selective Retention, Repair, and Retirement
doi:10.55640/ijdsml-06-02-12.abstract:
<jats:p>AI agents increasingly maintain reusable skill libraries that encode procedures, tool interactions, and policy-dependent behavior. These libraries operate in environments where software dependencies evolve and governing policies are revised. Maintaining a skill therefore requires distinguishing behavior that must be retained, behavior that requires repair, and behavior that must be retired. Conventional regression-based adaptation is poorly suited to this setting when historical tests themselves encode superseded requirements.
We introduce SkillShift, a benchmark comprising 60 reusable skills, 236 behavioral components, and 27 distinct real, dated change events (28 family-level transitions) across Python libraries, runtime environments, and published security policies, with executable validation, version-pinned environments, and a chronological evaluation protocol. We also introduce SkillLedger, which associates skill components with version-indexed evidence and selectively quarantines tests whose governing requirements have changed.
Conventional regression gating never retired prohibited behavior while historical tests remained authoritative. SkillLedger addresses this limitation and improves repair after policy changes by 22.0 percentage points over a refreshed regression-gate baseline. However, the refreshed gate matches SkillLedger on retirement after policy changes and retains far more valid behavior (99.5% versus 82.9%). Most of SkillLedger’s accidental losses come from withholding working skills whose historical tests, often invoking removed APIs, kept failing. Further experiments expose limitations in conditional policy interpretation, structured-output parsing, and task-time retirement instructions.
These findings establish a broader limitation of continual agent adaptation: the evidence used to validate a skill may become obsolete independently of the skill’s intended behavior. Reliable skill maintenance therefore requires evaluating the continuing validity of both behavioral requirements and their supporting tests.</jats:p>
doi:10.55640/ijdsml-06-02-12.venue: International journal of data science and machine learning

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1952539.title: Physics-inspired feature engineering and explainable machine learning for tensile strength prediction of CNT–Si₃N₄ reinforced FWTPET joints
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1952539.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The prediction of the tensile strength of carbon nanotube (CNT)–silicon nitride (Si₃N₄) reinforced friction welding of tube-to-tube plate using an external tool (FWTPET) joints is crucial for improving joint performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A physics-inspired machine learning framework was developed using 25 experimentally derived observations to investigate the relationships between welding parameters, engineered process descriptors, and tensile strength. Physically motivated descriptors were constructed to represent thermal input, reinforcement interaction, material flow, and dispersion effects. Hyperparameter optimization was performed for multiple regression models to improve predictive performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The XGBoost model showed the best performance, with an MAE of 5.70, an RMSE of 7.74, and an R² of 0.9772. SHAP analysis identified CNT content and the dispersion-related descriptor as the most influential predictors. Ablation analysis showed that the combination of the original experimental process variables provided greater predictability than the engineered variables alone or their combination, while the physics-inspired process variables provided further physically interpretable representations of the welding process.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results indicate that small-data machine learning, domain-based feature engineering, and explainable analysis are potential techniques for predicting the tensile strength of FWTPET joints.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.21009/jrpmj.v8i2.70668.title: Pengembangan Media Pembelajaran Berbasis Website dengan Pendekatan Contextual Teaching and Learning pada Materi Bilangan Bulat Kelas VII SMP
doi:10.21009/jrpmj.v8i2.70668.abstract: <jats:p>Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan dan menilai kelayakan media pembelajaran berbasis website dengan pendekatan Contextual Teaching and Learning (CTL) pada materi bilangan bulat kelas VII SMP. Penelitian pengembangan menggunakan model 4D (define, design, develop, disseminate). Penilaian meliputi validasi ahli materi dan bahasa (93,75%), ahli media (91,56%), respons guru dan peserta didik pada uji coba skala kecil (93,89% dan 90,33%), serta skala besar (96,67% dan 96,17%). Rata-rata sederhana dari keenam persentase tersebut adalah 93,73%; angka ini merupakan ringkasan deskriptif lintas sumber, bukan satu indeks validitas. Peserta uji coba adalah siswa kelas VIII yang telah mempelajari bilangan bulat di kelas VII sehingga hasilnya menggambarkan tanggapan pengguna retrospektif. Produk memperoleh penilaian kelayakan yang tinggi menurut para penilai dan responden. Penelitian ini tidak mengukur efektivitas media terhadap hasil belajar atau retensi konsep.</jats:p>

doi:10.15294/jese.v5i1.25274.title: Pre-service Teachers’ Perceptions of the New Pedagogical Deep Learning (NPDL)
doi:10.15294/jese.v5i1.25274.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to investigate the perceptions of pre-service Science Education teachers regarding New Pedagogical Deep Learning (NPDL) in Indonesia. Employing a descriptive survey design, the research was conducted in Central Java Province and involved a sample of 88 pre-service Science Education teachers. Data collection was performed using a questionnaire consisting of 10 items, distributed through Google Forms, complemented by follow-up interviews. Quantitative data analysis with a descriptive approach was utilized to analyze the collected data. The study yielded three primary findings. First, Science Education pre-service teachers possess a basic understanding of the Deep Learning concept, although 16% of them exhibit misconceptions by equating Deep Learning solely with artificial intelligence (AI). Second, these pre-service teachers demonstrate interest in implementing Deep Learning in the classroom; however, they require further training to deepen their understanding of what Deep Learning entails and how to effectively apply it in science education at the school level. Third, pre-service teachers are ready to implement Deep Learning and require strong ecosystem support. They express a keen interest in applying Deep Learning in the classroom.</jats:p>
doi:10.15294/jese.v5i1.25274.venue: Journal of Environmental and Science Education

doi:10.54254/2754-1169/2026.ld37780.title: Forecasting Corporate Credit Risk with Machine and Deep Learning: A Forward-Looking Early-Warning Framework for U.S. Listed Firms
doi:10.54254/2754-1169/2026.ld37780.abstract: <jats:p>Accurate assessment of corporate credit risk matters for investors, lenders and regulators, but traditional accounting-ratio models often miss the changing and non-linear pattern of financial distress. This study examines whether machine learning and deep learning models can produce more accurate and stable credit risk scores for large U.S. listed firms. The analysis uses quarterly financial statements of 1,133 S&P 1500 constituent companies from 2010 to 2025 (72,960 firm-quarter observations), and risk labels are constructed from an adapted Altman Z'-Score. Sixteen financial variables are converted into economically interpretable ratios to mitigate multicollinearity and make the models more stable. Four models are compared: XGBoost, LSTM, BiLSTM and CNN-LSTM, with hyperparameters tuned through grid search. The pattern is clear. XGBoost records the strongest in-sample performance (R² = 0.8904, RMSE = 0.1533), but its performance drops noticeably out of sample. LSTM, in contrast, produces the best test-set results (R² = 0.8073, RMSE = 0.2105). The trained models are then used to forecast credit risk for the next three quarters (2026Q1-Q3). These results emphasize the importance of capturing temporal dynamics in credit risk assessment and provide a practical early-warning framework for investors and risk managers.</jats:p>
doi:10.54254/2754-1169/2026.ld37780.venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

doi:10.30872/jlpf.v7i2.6336.title: Analysis of Junior High School Students' Misconceptions Regarding the Concept of Force and Motion in Science Learning
doi:10.30872/jlpf.v7i2.6336.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to analyze junior high school students’ misconceptions about the concepts of force and motion in science learning. A quantitative approach was employed using a Four-Tier Diagnostic Test as the research instrument. The participants consisted of 20 eighth- and ninth-grade students of SMPN Socah, Bangkalan. Data were collected using a diagnostic test that assessed students’ conceptual understanding, reasoning, and confidence levels. The results indicated that students experienced misconceptions in several force and motion concepts, particularly regarding the relationship between force and motion and the interpretation of position–time graphs. The percentage of students categorized as having misconceptions was 62.5%, which falls into the high category. Meanwhile, 27% of students were categorized as not understanding the concepts, representing the moderate category, and only 10.5% demonstrated conceptual understanding, representing the low category. Factors contributing to these misconceptions included insufficient prior knowledge, less effective instructional methods, limited learning media, and difficulties in interpreting graphical representations. These findings highlight the need for more interactive learning strategies and the use of appropriate instructional media to improve students’ conceptual understanding and reduce misconceptions in force and motion topics.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch003.title: Reimagining STEAM Education
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch003.abstract: <jats:p>The growing demand for creativity, innovation, and problem-solving in the 21st century calls for rethinking conventional STEAM education. Maker-inspired learning environments offer hands-on engagement, design thinking, interdisciplinary integration, and learner agency. This chapter examines how such pedagogies can shift STEAM education from content transmission to creative knowledge production, drawing on constructivist and constructionist theories. It highlights design principles, classroom and makerspace practices, and strategies that foster creativity, collaboration, critical thinking, and inclusivity, especially in resource-constrained contexts, with implications for curriculum, teacher development, and policy.</jats:p>

doi:10.1075/aila.00069.kes.title: Generative artificial intelligence and foreign language learning
doi:10.1075/aila.00069.kes.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Prior studies exploring teachers’ perceptions of generative artificial
          intelligence (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini have signaled tensions
          between instructors’ perceptions of GenAI’s usefulness and their beliefs regarding its
          ethicality. The current study furthers this line of inquiry, examining issues of ethics
          and utility by focusing specifically on teachers of languages other than English. Using a
          sequential mixed-methods design, this study employed a survey to understand language
          instructors’ (
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                     = 101) perceptions of the ethicality of GenAI tool use in
          higher education, along with their perceptions of the usefulness of GenAI for supporting
          second language (L2) learning. Semi-structured interviews were then conducted with six
          teachers to further understand participants’ survey responses, with some teachers sharing
          additional artifacts (e.g., course policies regarding GenAI). The findings suggest that
          most teachers (92.1%) believe GenAI tools are ethical if used for specific purposes. There
          also appears to be a connection between teachers’ ethical beliefs and their perceptions of
          GenAI’s utility, in terms of whether GenAI is used by students as a scaffold/support
          mechanism versus being used to produce content. The implications of this study provide a
          roadmap for developing discipline-specific guidelines that preserve L2 learning integrity
          while leveraging GenAI’s utility.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.3130/aijt.32.1481.title: PROTOTYPING OF LEARNING MATERIALS FOR BUILDING CONSTRUCTION METHODS USING 3D MODELING
doi:10.3130/aijt.32.1481.abstract: Understanding building construction methods requires grasping the three-dimensional relationships among building parts. As 3D modeling has become a common technology, learning materials that allow learners to actively create and edit 3D models are expected to improve learning outcomes compared with traditional lectures using drawings. However, modeling with 3D-CAD and BIM can be difficult for beginners, and complex operations may distract from the learning purpose. This study prototypes learning materials for building construction methods that are easy for beginners to use and evaluates their effectiveness through a questionnaire survey.

doi:10.54254/2755-2721/2026.37807.title: Deep Operator Learning for Interface Evolution and Uncertainty Quantification in Complex Multiphase Flow
doi:10.54254/2755-2721/2026.37807.abstract: <jats:p>Predicting moving interfaces in multiphase flow remains computationally demanding because topological changes, high curvature, and thin ligaments require fine spatial and temporal resolution. This study develops a Fourier-DeepONet surrogate that maps initial phase geometry, nondimensional flow parameters, and space-time coordinates to future volume-fraction fields while producing calibrated uncertainty. High-fidelity trajectories are generated with the adaptive volume-of-fluid solver in Basilisk for Rayleigh-Taylor instability and droplet deformation. The architecture combines convolutional branch encoding, Fourier coordinate features, global spectral mixing, physics-aware constraints, and a Normal-Inverse-Gamma evidential head. On the held-out benchmark, the model reaches an interface Dice score of 0.954 ± 0.006, an intersection-over-union score of 0.913 ± 0.009, and a volume-fraction MAE of 0.0187 ± 0.0014. Relative mass error remains 0.73 ± 0.12% over 50 frames, while uncertainty-error correlation reaches 0.812 ± 0.021 after calibration. Under unseen parameter combinations, Dice decreases by only 0.026 ± 0.007. These results support physics-constrained operator learning as a fast and reliability-aware approach to multiphase interface prediction.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1927310.title: How project-based learning improves EFL speaking in Chinese higher vocational colleges: a serial mediation study
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1927310.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    English-speaking competence remains a persistent challenge for Chinese EFL learners, and project-based learning has been advocated as a remedy, though existing evidence yields mixed effects and rarely specifies the psychological mechanisms or sub-skill profiles driving the variation. This explanatory sequential mixed-methods quasi-experimental study examined a 12-week project-based learning intervention with a 6-week delayed posttest in Chinese higher vocational college students (
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                     = 179; PBL
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 93, CTL
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 86), testing autonomous motivation and collaborative engagement as serial mediators of English-speaking competence. Speaking was rated on a four-dimensional rubric covering fluency, accuracy, complexity, and pragmatic-interactional competence, with inter-rater intraclass coefficients of 0.76 to 0.87; serial mediation was estimated using PROCESS Model 6, and inductive thematic analysis of post-intervention interviews probed the operating mechanisms within project groups. Composite speaking showed a large condition advantage at the immediate posttest (
                    <jats:italic>d</jats:italic>
                     = 1.07), concentrated on fluency (
                    <jats:italic>d</jats:italic>
                     = 0.82) and pragmatic-interactional competence (
                    <jats:italic>d</jats:italic>
                     = 0.68), modest on complexity (
                    <jats:italic>d</jats:italic>
                     = 0.48), and not statistically detectable on accuracy. Retention 6 weeks later was differential, with motivation and engagement retaining 88 and 78% of their immediate gains while composite speaking competence retained 93%. The serial indirect path through engagement was significant whereas the motivation-only path was not, indicating that engagement carries the effect and motivation reaches speaking only through engagement. Qualitative themes located the active mechanism in group accountability while revealing compressing dynamics including free-riding, conversational dominance, and L1 slippage under time pressure. These findings imply that the active ingredient of project-based learning is the psychological condition it creates for learners rather than the task choreography, and that instructional design should center on supporting learners’ needs for autonomy, competence and relatedness, and specifically on the group accountability structures through which motivation becomes speaking.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.5256/f1000research.211348.r528593.title: Peer Review Report For: Calcyon: Design and Validation of an AI-Based Chatbot Framework Integrating Computational Thinking and Self-Regulated Learning in University Calculus Learning [version 2; peer review: 2 approved, 1 approved with reservations]
doi:10.5256/f1000research.211348.r528593.abstract: Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into mathematics education has advanced rapidly; however, systematic AI-based chatbot frameworks that integrate computational thinking (CT) and self-regulated learning (SRL) scaffolding within university calculus remain limited. This study developed and formatively evaluated Calcyon, an AI-based chatbot framework designed to integrate CT processes and SRL scaffolding within university differential calculus learning. Methods A Design and Development Research (DDR) approach guided by the ADDIE model was employed, focusing on the design, development, and formative evaluation stages. Expert evaluation (n = 3) was conducted across five design dimensions using Aiken’s V to examine content and design validity. A formative student pilot study (n = 11) was conducted to evaluate prototype readability and feasibility across six dimensions. Results Expert evaluation indicated strong expert-rated design and content validity across content, instructional, technical, linguistic, and media design dimensions (Aiken’s V = 0.92). Most items met the predefined criterion, while several revisions were incorporated based on expert feedback. The student pilot indicated good readability and feasibility of the prototype. Conclusions Calcyon provides an empirically evaluated AI-based chatbot framework that integrates AI-mediated interaction, CT-oriented scaffolding, and multidimensional SRL design principles within university calculus learning. The findings provide evidence of framework quality and feasibility; however, they do not establish the effectiveness of Calcyon in improving CT, SRL, or calculus learning outcomes. Further empirical studies are required to examine its instructional effectiveness.

doi:10.3389/fcvm.2026.1893875.title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based model for predicting amputation risk in patients with lower extremity arterial disease and diabetes
doi:10.3389/fcvm.2026.1893875.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Patients with lower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) complicated by diabetes face substantial amputation risk. Pre-amputation death acts as a critical competing event that distorts risk estimation. Validated personalized prediction tools for this population remain scarce and hinder precise clinical interventions. This study aimed to develop and validate two complementary interpretable models for 12-month amputation risk in patients with LEAD and diabetes to support clinical decision-making.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 1,919 patients with LEAD and diabetes from four Chinese hospitals (January 2018-September 2024), with follow-up ending in September 2025. The primary outcome was 12-month amputation (major or minor). Prior to model construction, candidate predictors were screened via LASSO regression, random forest classifier and Boruta algorithm. Ten machine learning algorithms were then trained and evaluated by discrimination and calibration metrics. SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) was applied for interpretability. A Fine-Gray competing risk regression model was built using the same screened predictor set.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Patients were split into training (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 967), internal validation (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 414), and external validation (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 538) cohorts. The 12-month amputation rate was 14.0%. Median follow-up was 12 months; mean age was 72.7 ± 9.5 years and 65.7% were male. The optimal GraBoost model achieved internal validation AUC = 0.860 and external validation AUC = 0.828, incorporating 14 clinical predictors, including: Rutherford classification, financial burden, age, Barthel Index, diabetic foot, statin, fibrinogen (FIB), neutrophil (NEUT), residence, prealbumin (PALB), C-reactive protein (CRP), activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), body mass index (BMI) classification and wound. SHAP revealed higher grade Rutherford classification, lower Barthel Index, younger age, wounds, diabetic foot, and elevated FIB, APTT, CRP, NEUT correlated with higher amputation risk. Urban residence, normal BMI classification, lower financial burden, statin use and higher PALB were protective. Shared predictors showed consistent directional effects across GraBoost and Fine-Gray models. A dual-model web-based calculator was constructed for risk assessment.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We developed and validated complementary interpretable GraBoost machine learning and Fine-Gray competing risk models for 12-month amputation risk. The dual-model web calculator may help clinicians identify high-risk patients and guide clinical management.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch012.title: AI-Supported Maker-Inspired Learning Environments for STEAM-Oriented Language Education
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch012.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter introduces the Artificial Intelligence–Maker Experiential Learning (AI-MEL) framework for integrating AI-supported maker pedagogy into STEAM-oriented language education. Grounded in constructionist and experiential learning theories, the framework conceptualizes AI as a digital maker tool that supports creative knowledge construction, collaboration, and interdisciplinary learning. The chapter synthesizes maker pedagogy, gamified flipped learning, and AI-mediated instruction to illustrate the affordances of digitally mediated STEAM environments. Findings from a quasi-experimental study on AI-mediated gamified flipped learning in mobile-assisted language learning are reinterpreted through a maker pedagogy lens, demonstrating gains in learner motivation, vocabulary development, and self-directed learning. The AI-MEL framework foregrounds learner agency, experiential knowledge construction, interdisciplinary integration, and adaptive technological mediation, offering implications for instructional design and teacher professional development in STEAM education.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch012.venue: Transforming STEAM Education With Maker-Inspired Learning Environments

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8069-8.ch003.title: The Algorithmic Sublime
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8069-8.ch003.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores the algorithmic sublime the sense of power, and uncertainty evoked by advanced AI, machine learning, and generative models. It explores how modern AI systems achieve unprecedented capabilities, from high-performance decision-making to creative generation across art, language, and multimodal domains. The chapter analyzes the deep architectural, computational, and interpretability challenges that make these systems both transformative and opaque. It also investigates the societal, ethical, and philosophical implications of AI's growing influence on human cognition, culture, and governance. By synthesizing technical foundations with broader conceptual reflections, the survey highlights the dual nature of AI as a tool of innovation and a source of profound complexity, emphasizing the need for responsible development and human-centered oversight.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8069-8.ch003.venue: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

doi:10.31539/0xqj7n77.title: Implementasi Model Project-Based Learning dalam Pembelajaran Aktivitas Permainan Bola Voli Terhadap Hasil Belajar
doi:10.31539/0xqj7n77.abstract:
<jats:p>This study aims to determine the implementation of the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model in improving students’ learning outcomes in volleyball learning activities among seventh-grade students of SMP Negeri 01 Malangbong. This research was motivated by the low learning outcomes of students in volleyball learning activities, particularly in mastering basic movement skills of underhand passing and overhead passing. This study employed a Classroom Action Research (CAR) method consisting of four stages: planning, action implementation, observation, and reflection. The subjects of this study were 34 students of class VII-G at SMP Negeri 01 Malangbong. The research instruments consisted of observation sheets and learning outcome tests of volleyball skills. The research was conducted in two cycles through several learning actions using the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model.The results showed that the implementation of the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model provided positive changes in the volleyball learning process. Students showed increased involvement in learning activities, improved teamwork abilities, and development of basic movement skills in underhand passing and overhead passing. The improvement in learning outcomes occurred after learning improvements were implemented in Cycle II, with 7 students achieving the Minimum Mastery Criteria (KKM), representing 20.59%. These findings indicate that the implementation of the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model can support the improvement of the learning process and provide improvements in learning outcomes for some students in volleyball learning activities. However, the improvement had not yet reached classical mastery; therefore, more intensive practice and longer learning time are required.
Keywords: Volleyball, Learning Outcomes, Physical Education, Classroom Action Research, Project-Based Learning</jats:p>

doi:10.57092/ijetz.v5i3.853.title: Smartphone Use, Learning, and Student Well-Being in Higher Education: Evidence from Bangladesh
doi:10.57092/ijetz.v5i3.853.abstract: <jats:p>This study examined smartphone use and its implications for teaching, learning, and academic engagement among 353 university students aged 18–25 years in Rangpur, Bangladesh. A cross-sectional mixed-methods design combined a 29-item questionnaire (Cronbach’s α = .837) with interviews involving 10 students and 10 faculty and administrative staff members. Multiple linear regression identified communication dependency (β = .163, p = .002) and perceived academic impact (β = .141, p = .009) as significant predictors of smartphone-use frequency, explaining 10.0% of its variance. Findings indicated that extensive social media use coexisted with academic distraction, sleep disturbances, compulsive checking, and perceived isolation. Interviews also revealed the absence of institutional smartphone-use policies. These findings highlight smartphones’ dual role as learning resources and potential sources of academic disruption, underscoring the need for institutional guidelines and educational strategies that promote responsible use and support effective teaching, learning, and student well-being in higher education across diverse learning environments.</jats:p>
doi:10.57092/ijetz.v5i3.853.venue: International Journal of Education and Teaching Zone

doi:10.32672/perisai.v5i3.4672.title: <b><i>SELF-REGULATED LEARNING</i></b><b> DAN <i>GROWTH MINDSET</i> SEBAGAI PREDIKTOR KOMUNIKASI MATEMATIS SISWA SMP NEGERI 7 TANJUNGPINANG</b><b></b>
doi:10.32672/perisai.v5i3.4672.abstract: <jats:p>Kemampuan komunikasi matematis merupakan kompetensi penting dalam pembelajaran matematika, namun observasi awal di SMP Negeri 7 Tanjungpinang menunjukkan masih terdapat kesulitan dalam merepresentasikan dan menjelaskan gagasan matematis secara tepat. Kondisi ini mengindikasikan perlunya mengkaji faktor internal yang mendukung perkembangan kemampuan tersebut, khususnya self-regulated learning dan growth mindset. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis self-regulated learning dan growth mindset sebagai prediktor kemampuan komunikasi matematis siswa SMP Negeri 7 Tanjungpinang. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain korelasional prediktif. Populasi penelitian berjumlah 420 siswa kelas VII dengan sampel 100 siswa. Data dikumpulkan melalui angket self-regulated learning, angket growth mindset, dan tes kemampuan komunikasi matematis, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear berganda. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kedua prediktor secara simultan signifikan dalam memprediksi kemampuan komunikasi matematis, dengan nilai F sebesar 42,186 dan signifikansi 0,001 serta koefisien determinasi sebesar 0,465. Secara parsial, self-regulated learning merupakan prediktor signifikan dengan nilai t sebesar 5,214 dan signifikansi 0,001, sedangkan growth mindset juga merupakan prediktor signifikan dengan nilai t sebesar 3,687 dan signifikansi 0,001. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa penguatan regulasi belajar dan pola pikir berkembang berperan penting dalam mendukung kemampuan komunikasi matematis siswa.</jats:p>
doi:10.32672/perisai.v5i3.4672.venue: PERISAI: Jurnal Pendidikan dan Riset Ilmu Sains

doi:10.3744/snak.2026.63.5.343.title: Comparison of Machine Learning Models Based on Different Ship Hull Form Representations for Hydrodynamic Performance Prediction
doi:10.3744/snak.2026.63.5.343.abstract: Accurate prediction of ship hydrodynamic performance is essential for hull form optimization during the early design stage. This study investigates two approaches for incorporating ship hull geometry into machine learning-based surrogate models using offset data. The first approach represents hull geometry as an RGB image and applies a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D CNN), while the second directly utilizes offset curves with a one-dimensional CNN and a temporal convolutional network (1D CNN + TCN) to capture longitudinal hull form variations. Models for predicting the residual resistance coefficient, effective wake fraction, and thrust deduction factor were trained using approximately 440 model test dataset from the Korea Research Institute of Ships and Ocean Engineering (KRISO). Their performance was compared with a baseline multilayer perceptron (MLP) model using only principal ship dimensions. The results demonstrate that incorporating hull geometry significantly improves prediction accuracy over the MLP model. Although the average prediction performance of the 2D CNN and 1D CNN + TCN models was similar, the 1D CNN + TCN model achieved higher hull form sensitivity in propulsion performance prediction. These results indicate that offset-based hull representation provides an effective input for machine learning surrogate models and that TCN-based architectures are advantageous for capturing longitudinal hull form variations.
doi:10.3744/snak.2026.63.5.343.venue: Journal of the Society of Naval Architects of Korea

doi:10.54963/ti.v10i4.103058.title: Deep Learning-Powered Spatial Transcriptomics Analysis to Predict Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Response from Pre-Treatment Digital Pathology Slides
doi:10.54963/ti.v10i4.103058.abstract: <jats:p>Response to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is governed in part by the spatial organization of the tumour microenvironment, yet most deep learning models applied to digital pathology treat tissue regions independently and therefore do not represent the neighbourhood interactions that shape immune activation. This study develops and retrospectively evaluates a Neighborhood-aware Masked Graph Spiking Neural Network (NAMG-SNN) that classifies ICI responders and non-responders from pre-treatment haematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images. Whole-slide images are stain-normalized, tiled and encoded into patch-level embeddings that combine statistical, textural, morphological and deep semantic descriptors. A spatial graph is then constructed over the retained patches and pruned by an adaptive similarity mask that suppresses weak or artefactual neighbourhood edges. The masked graph is propagated through a leaky integrate-and-fire spiking network whose accumulated firing rates form a spatial transcriptomic representation, which is finally classified into responder and non-responder categories. The model was evaluated on an integrated cohort assembled from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), the Panoptic segmentation of nUclei and tissue in Melanoma pathology Challenge (PUMA challenge) and the Phoenix virtual spatial transcriptomics resource, using patient-level splitting. On the integrated test data the framework reached 97.31% accuracy, 96.94% precision, 97.82% recall, 97.38% F1-score and 98.87% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.947 and Cohen’s kappa of 0.946, exceeding convolutional, transformer and graph baselines trained under identical conditions. Transcriptomic reconstruction reached a Pearson correlation of 0.962, mean absolute error of 0.051, root mean square error of 0.081 and structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.966. Ablation confirmed that neighbourhood-aware graph construction, adaptive masking and spike-based learning each contributed to performance. These results are retrospective and computational.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1924557.title: How L2 selves shape attitudes toward AI-assisted language learning: the mediating roles of intrinsic and extrinsic motivation in cross-cultural Asian contexts
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1924557.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study investigates the relationship between the L2 motivational self-system and attitudes toward AI-enhanced second language (L2) learning, and tests whether intrinsic and extrinsic motivation mediate these relationships among students learning Chinese or English as a foreign language in Thailand, Macau, and Mainland China.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Questionnaire data were collected from 361 participants. Correlational analysis, hierarchical regression, and a bootstrapping approach were used to test mediational relations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Both the ought-to L2 self and the ideal L2 self were significantly associated with attitudes toward AI-enhanced L2 learning, with the ideal L2 self showing the stronger association. In the overall sample, and in the Thai and Mainland Chinese samples analyzed separately, intrinsic and extrinsic motivation statistically fully mediated the association between the ought-to L2 self and attitudes toward AI-enhanced L2 learning. In the Macau sample, extrinsic motivation was more involved than intrinsic motivation in transmitting this effect. For the ideal L2 self, intrinsic and extrinsic motivation only partially mediated the relationship with attitudes toward AI-enhanced L2 learning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Positive attitudes toward AI-enhanced L2 learning are not formed merely through future self-representations; they are also linked to learners’ intrinsic and extrinsic motivation. By examining the interaction between the L2 motivational self-system and intrinsic and extrinsic motivation across different regions, this study extends L2 motivation research to the area of AI-enhanced language learning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1186/s40562-026-00504-y.title: Explore the ideology of deep learning in ENSO forecasts
doi:10.1186/s40562-026-00504-y.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) exerts profound influence on global climate variability, yet its prediction remains a grand challenge. Recent advances in deep learning have significantly improved forecasting skill, but the opacity of these models hampers scientific trust and operational deployment. Here, we introduce a mathematically grounded interpretability framework based on bounded variation function. By rescuing the “dead” neurons from the saturation zone of the activation function, we enhance the model’s expressive capacity. Our analysis reveals that ENSO predictability emerges dominantly from the tropical Pacific, with contributions from the Indian and Atlantic Oceans, consistent with physical understanding. Controlled experiments affirm the robustness of our method and its alignment with established predictors. Notably, we probe the persistent Spring Predictability Barrier (SPB), finding that despite expanded sensitivity during spring, predictive performance declines–likely due to suboptimal variable selection. These results suggest that incorporating additional ocean–atmosphere variables may help transcend SPB limitations and advance long-range ENSO prediction.</jats:p>

doi:10.54254/2753-7048/2026.38014.title: The Consistency Between Vertical Gestures and Emotional Valence has an Impact on the Vocabulary Learning of Dutch in Chinese Native Speakers
doi:10.54254/2753-7048/2026.38014.abstract: <jats:p>Research on embodied cognition indicates that spatially congruent actions help in the acquisition of vocabulary knowledge, but it is unknown whether it is enough to use just a minimal pointing gesture to make one activate metaphorical mapping between vertical space and emotion valence. In the present study, we offer an experiment that aims to investigate the effect of gesture–valence congruency on the learning of Dutch vocabulary words for native Chinese speakers. Participants will have to learn sixteen new Dutch nouns that are associated with positive or negative valence Chinese words. They will be divided into three groups based on the congruency of the pointing gesture used (metaphorically congruent, metaphorically incongruent, or control condition). The measure of success will be recognition accuracy of the learned words. It is hypothesized that there will be maximum recognition accuracy in the congruent group, medium accuracy in the control group, and minimum accuracy in the incongruent group. Thus, the proposed study is the continuation of previous works in the field of embodied metaphors.</jats:p>
doi:10.54254/2753-7048/2026.38014.venue: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media

doi:10.20965/jrm.2026.p1413.title: Target Following for a Snake-Like Robot Using Rolling Locomotion via Deep Reinforcement Learning
doi:10.20965/jrm.2026.p1413.abstract: <jats:p>The turning motion of snake-like robots based on center of gravity shift has superior energy efficiency compared to the undulatory locomotion that simultaneously drives many joints, but precise guidance control has been difficult due to its nonlinear dynamic characteristics. 	In this paper, we propose a control method using deep reinforcement learning 	for following target points in all directions in the turning motion using center of gravity shift and ground reaction forces. 	The target direction is defined as a normalized vector in the body coordinate system. 	This allows us to present target direction information to the agent that is independent of changes in self-orientation, and we show that it can acquire a policy for accurate following in all directions. 	The results of motion analysis confirmed that the learned policy not only skillfully utilizes the ground reaction forces at the time of contact to make dynamic trajectory corrections, but also achieves target following by flexibly switching the turning strategy according to the target direction.</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/dta-02-2026-0223.title: Smart questioning, answering, and clarifying to support adaptive learning
doi:10.1108/dta-02-2026-0223.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly integrated into higher education; however, many AI-based systems function primarily as reactive answer generators rather than adaptive instructional supports. This study develops and evaluates smart questioning, answering, and clarifying (SmartQAC), a pedagogically grounded AI-supported learning system that operationalizes structured dialogic scaffolding through questioning, answering, and clarification mechanisms to support adaptive learning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>SmartQAC integrates retrieval-augmented generation, prompt-routing strategies, and structured dialogic interactions to promote metacognitive engagement and conceptual development. A quasi-experimental study involving 52 undergraduate students was conducted within a database course as an illustrative domain application. Mixed-method analyses were performed using pre-test and post-test assessments, interaction logs, questionnaires, and interviews to examine learning achievement, learning behaviors, and learner perceptions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Results indicate that students using SmartQAC achieved significantly higher learning achievement than those in the control group. Interaction behaviors within the SmartQAC environment were positively associated with students' learning achievement. Furthermore, participants reported positive perceptions regarding instructional usefulness, autonomy support, engagement, and pedagogical value.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study demonstrates how dialogic instructional principles can be operationalized within a retrieval-augmented large language model system to support adaptive learning. The findings provide empirical evidence for the effectiveness of integrating questioning, answering, and clarification mechanisms into AI-supported learning environments and offer practical design implications for future adaptive educational systems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11417231/v1.title: Beyond AUROC: External Validation, Calibration, and Explainability of Machine Learning Models for 30-Day Hospital Readmission Using Electronic Health Records—A Rapid Systematic Review
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11417231/v1.abstract: Studies evaluating machine learning (ML) algorithms predicting 30-day hospital readmission using EHRs have relied on AUROC as a sole criterion. The AUROC score provides no insight into whether an ML model transfers to new hospitals or periods, whether the probabilities provided are calibrated, or whether the explanation offered can be trusted. This study was conducted as a rapid systematic review using streamlined methods informed by Cochrane rapid review guidance and reported according to the applicable PRISMA 2020 reporting items. It examined the extent to which EHR-based machine learning studies predicting 30-day hospital readmission reported external or temporal validation, calibration, explainability, clinical utility, and subgroup fairness. PubMed and Europe PMC databases were searched for studies conducted between January 2020 and October 2026, resulting in the screening of 1,644 records in two phases and inclusion of 156 studies coded based on their abstracts. Out of 62 studies providing an AUROC score for readmission as the only outcome, the median highest AUROC score was 0.76 (interquartile range 0.69--0.85). Only 19 studies (12.2\%) included external (10) or temporal (10; one both) validation, and AUROC decreased in four of five studies that evaluated both settings. Calibration was mentioned in 24 abstracts (15.4\%) but only one study used a metric specific to calibration; decision curve analysis appeared in 6 (3.8\%) and fairness analysis in 7 (4.5\%), and 112 studies (71.8\%) did not report any of these four evaluations. Sixty abstracts (38.5\%) reported explainability, mainly via SHAP, but no one evaluated the explanations. From 2020-2023 to 2024-2026, SHAP usage increased from 5.8\% to 29.9\% ($p<0.001$), while external or temporal validation remained unchanged at 11.6\% and 12.6\% ($p=1.0$). The rate of adoption of post-hoc explanation has been much higher than the rate of adopting these evaluations for deciding about the safety of a model. We propose a minimal ``beyond AUROC'' evaluation set for readmission prediction models.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11417231/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
