doi:10.54254/2755-2721/2026.ld38058.title: Applications of Educational Data Mining in Identifying Learning Difficulties among Novice Programmers
doi:10.54254/2755-2721/2026.ld38058.abstract: <jats:p>This narrative review examines how educational data mining (EDM) can inform instructional decisions about learning difficulties among novice programmers. This paper draws on a focused set of publications, including empirical and application-oriented studies. The analysis focuses on target alignment, timing, and granularity. Submission histories and compiler feedback can reveal learning processes that are not reflected in final grades. Repeated attempts may indicate either progress or ongoing difficulties. Grouping learners and sequence analysis help identify behavioral patterns. Supervised prediction is used to estimate outcomes, while cognitive diagnosis assesses knowledge mastery. Early records may help prioritize students for review. Concept-focused support requires more detailed evidence and checks against actual assignments. Differences in targets, observation windows, and validation designs limit comparisons across studies. Results based on complete learning histories do not establish early prediction capability. Model explanations also do not establish intervention effects. The proposed framework remains empirically unvalidated. Evaluation should address measurement quality, generalizability, predictive error, privacy, and fairness. The effects of subsequent instructional support on learning require separate assessment.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fbuil.2026.1947550.title: New hybrid models integrating the aquila optimizer with machine learning algorithms to predict the strength of geosynthetic-reinforced subgrade soil
doi:10.3389/fbuil.2026.1947550.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Accurately predicting the California Bearing Ratio (CBR) of geosynthetic-reinforced subgrades is critical for pavement design but remains challenging due to the complex, nonlinear soil-reinforcement interaction. This study develops a novel hybrid modeling framework that integrates the Aquila Optimization Algorithm (AOA) with machine learning models such as Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Ridge Regression, and XGBoost to enhance the prediction of soaked CBR values. A comprehensive database of 90 tests, encompassing key soil properties and reinforcement parameters, was used for model development. The AOA significantly boosted the predictive performance of all base models. The proposed AOA-XGBoost hybrid model demonstrated superior accuracy, achieving a convincing coefficient of determination (R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.980), a low mean squared error (MSE = 1.78), and a minimal mean absolute error (MAE = 5.075) on the testing dataset. This performance notably surpassed the plain XGBoost model (R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.954, MSE = 1.99, MAE = 11.82), corresponding to a 2.8% gain in R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    , a 10.6% reduction in MSE, and a 57.1% reduction in MAE. Similarly, the AOA-ANN model (R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.945, MSE = 2.87, MAE = 13.87) showed a clear improvement over the plain ANN (R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.929, MSE = 3.06, MAE = 18.09), reflecting a 1.8% gain in R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    , a 6.2% reduction in MSE, and a 23.3% reduction in MAE. Five-fold cross-validation, reported as mean ± standard deviation, confirmed the robustness and generalization capability of this ranking. AOA-XGBoost produced the best cross-validated results: R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.8819 ± 0.0765, RMSE = 6.4218 ± 3.1846, MAE = 3.5217 ± 1.4826, MAPE = 19.6842 ± 4.7315%, and A20 = 0.6427 ± 0.1186. Sensitivity analysis revealed that reinforcement characteristics, particularly the number of layers (29.4% contribution) and tensile strength (21.8%), are the most dominant factors influencing CBR values. Hence, the results conclusively demonstrate that the AOA-assisted hybrid framework, particularly AOA-XGBoost, provides a robust and highly accurate tool for forecasting reinforced subgrade strength, supporting process innovation in pavement design through data‐driven assessment, with substantial potential to reduce reliance on time-consuming laboratory tests and improve pavement design efficiency.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.54254/2755-2721/2026.37777.title: High Dimensional Factor Discovery for Cross Sectional Equity Returns via Sparse Deep Learning
doi:10.54254/2755-2721/2026.37777.abstract: <jats:p>The expansion of high-dimensional firm characteristics has made cross-sectional equity return prediction more difficult because redundant variables, accumulated noise, and nonlinear exposures often appear at the same time. Traditional multifactor models provide strong economic interpretation, but their predefined factor sets are limited. They cannot fully use the complex information contained in public financial data, trading data, and market-state variables. The study focuses on U.S. common stocks listed on major exchanges from 2010 to 2024. It integrates Stooq market trading data, SEC EDGAR financial disclosure data, and Kenneth French factor data to construct a monthly cross-sectional feature matrix. A sparse deep learning model is then used to identify stable return-related factors. The model combines a feature gating layer, nonlinear hidden layers, and a bottleneck factor layer to achieve variable selection and latent factor learning. It is compared with the Fama-French five-factor regression, LASSO, random forest, and standard neural network through rolling out-of-sample tests. The illustrative experimental results show that the sparse deep model achieves an out-of-sample R² of 0.72 percent, a Spearman IC of 0.031, and a long-short portfolio Sharpe ratio of 0.91. After transaction costs, the Sharpe ratio remains 0.73. The results indicate that the sparse structure can reduce high-dimensional noise and improve the stability and economic interpretability of factor discovery. This framework provides an executable path for explainable machine learning asset pricing in fintech applications.</jats:p>

doi:10.32672/perisai.v5i3.4608.title: <b>PENGEMBANGAN OJS BERBAISIS DEEP LEARNING, KODING KECERDASAN ARTIFISIAL DAN STEM SEBAGAI EKOSISTEM INOVASI PENGUATAN SOFT SKILLS LULUSAN SMA</b>
doi:10.32672/perisai.v5i3.4608.abstract: <jats:p>Transformasi digital menuntut lulusan SMA menguasai soft skills, literasi digital, dan pemanfaatan kecerdasan artifisial (AI). Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan Open Journal System (OJS) berbasis Deep Learning, koding, AI, dan STEM sebagai ekosistem penguatan soft skills. Metode Research and Development dengan model ADDIE dan pendekatan embedded mixed methods diterapkan kepada 26 siswa kelas XII SMAN 2 Sandai. Data dikumpulkan melalui validasi ahli, skala soft skills sebelum dan sesudah implementasi, observasi, wawancara, serta dokumentasi. Skala mengukur berpikir kritis, komunikasi, kolaborasi, kreativitas, literasi digital, dan tanggung jawab akademik. Data dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif, paired sample t-test, N-Gain, dan analisis kualitatif. Produk memperoleh kelayakan 89,2% (sangat layak). Rerata soft skills meningkat dari 59,50 menjadi 86,69 dengan N-Gain 0,671 (sedang) dan perbedaan signifikan (p < 0,001). Implementasi juga menghasilkan 26 artikel melalui siklus submission–review–revision–publication. OJS terbukti mendukung penguatan soft skills dan budaya riset siswa.</jats:p>
doi:10.32672/perisai.v5i3.4608.venue: PERISAI: Jurnal Pendidikan dan Riset Ilmu Sains

doi:10.1108/qrj-05-2025-0163.title: Learning together, growing together: teacher educators' engagement in a virtual professional learning
doi:10.1108/qrj-05-2025-0163.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study explores how Indonesian teacher educators engage in virtual professional learning through a WhatsApp-based virtual professional learning community (VPLC), focusing on processes of “learning together” and “growing together.”</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using an interpretive qualitative case study design, data were collected primarily through semi-structured interviews exploring participants' experiences of engagement within a WhatsApp-based VPLC. Guided by a multidimensional engagement framework (behavioral, cognitive, collaborative, social, and emotional), the analysis shows how peer feedback, resource sharing, structured dialogue, and reflective inquiry support instructional adaptation and professional confidence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Findings underscore the importance of emotional support, trust, and distributed leadership in sustaining engagement. Despite challenges such as workload pressures and uneven digital literacy, mobile-based professional communities offer meaningful, context-sensitive spaces for collaborative and ongoing professional growth.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes to the literature in three ways. First, it shifts attention from school teachers to teacher educators, a group that remains underrepresented in VPLC research. Second, it examines a self-organized WhatsApp-based professional learning community operating outside formal institutional professional development structures. Third, it demonstrates how multidimensional engagement (behavioral, cognitive, emotional, collaborative, and social) supports professional learning within a resource-constrained and geographically dispersed Indonesian context.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.20965/jrm.2026.p1383.title: Deep Learning-Based Morphological Analysis for Identifying Culture Status and Contractile Motion in Skeletal Muscle Tissues
doi:10.20965/jrm.2026.p1383.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    This study investigates a deep learning-based framework that uses static microscopic images to identify culture status and contractile motion in cultured skeletal muscle tissues. Noninvasive functional evaluation is important for advancements in tissue engineering and biohybrid robotics. However, acquiring large-scale labeled datasets is often difficult owing to the time-consuming nature of functional measurements. To explore the feasibility of image-based evaluation under the data constraints, we implemented a structured image processing and validation pipeline. First, tissue regions were isolated using U
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    -Net, achieving a Dice coefficient of 0.984 to reduce background interference. Second, an ensemble learning strategy was examined via a culture-day identification task using 528 images. A soft-voting ensemble of convolutional neural networks achieved a Macro F1-score of 0.817, indicating that morphological features associated with culture progression could be effectively captured. Additionally, self-supervised pre-training via SimSiam was tested to extract domain-specific representations from unlabeled images. For contractile motion identification, the ImageNet-pre-trained EfficientNetV2-S paired with a random forest classifier attained an accuracy and F1-score of 75.0% and 0.800, respectively. These results suggest that functional properties of cultured tissues can be partially inferred from static morphological characteristics. While the limited size of the dataset and low identification confidence pose challenges, this study provides a baseline methodology for noninvasive, image-based cellular sensing in engineered biological systems.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.1108/jrit-05-2026-0158.title: When creativity meets artificial intelligence: a sequential path to smart learning and academic performance
doi:10.1108/jrit-05-2026-0158.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study examines how the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and students' creative thinking (CT) contribute to smart learning (SL) and academic performance (AP) in higher education. It further examines whether AI use and SL mediate the relationship between CT and AP in a sequential manner.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A quantitative approach was adopted, and data were collected from 227 university students in Bangladesh. Structural equation modelling with SmartPLS was used to evaluate the proposed relationships.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results show that both AI usage and CT are positively and significantly related to SL and AP. Beyond these direct associations, the data also point to a meaningful serial mediation pathway: students with stronger CT tend to report greater AI usage, which is in turn associated with higher SL engagement, and this heightened engagement is associated with better AP.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study uniquely links CT, AI use, SL and AP in Bangladeshi higher education. It shows how CT affects academic achievement through sequential paths of AI usage and SL, clarifying how student talents convert into outcomes in digital learning environments. The findings suggest that institutions should promote CT and use AI-based learning tools to improve student performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
doi:10.1108/jrit-05-2026-0158.venue: Journal of Research in Innovative Teaching & Learning

doi:10.30872/jlpf.v7i2.6194.title: Socio-Scientific Issues (SSI) Approach to Physics Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
doi:10.30872/jlpf.v7i2.6194.abstract: <jats:p>Physics learning in the 21st century requires instructional approaches that develop students’ conceptual understanding while fostering their ability to analyze and make informed decisions regarding complex real-world issues. The Socio-Scientific Issues (SSI) approach has emerged as a promising strategy for connecting physics concepts with social and environmental contexts. This study aims to systematically examine the application of the Socio-Scientific Issues (SSI) approach in physics learning during the period 2015–2025. Specifically, this study identifies topic trends, learning models, the implementation of the SSI approach, and its impact on the physics learning process. The method used is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. Data were collected from the ScienceDirect and Google Scholar databases using the keywords "Learning Outcomes", "Physics Learning", and "Socio-Scientific Issues". A total of 22 articles met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final synthesis. The results indicate that climate change is the most frequently addressed topic in implementing the SSI approach in physics learning, with junior high school being the dominant educational level represented in the reviewed studies. Furthermore, the SSI approach has proven effective in improving students' scientific argumentation skills and strengthening their understanding of physics concepts in real-life contexts. These findings suggest that integrating socio-scientific issues into physics learning provides a meaningful and contextual strategy for enhancing science education.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch013.title: Origami and Physical Computing for STEAM Education, Sustainability, and Animal Welfare
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch013.abstract: <jats:p>The growing presence of digital technologies in children's and young people's lives highlights the need for educational experiences that integrate technology in critical, creative and pedagogically meaningful ways. This chapter presents a conceptual pedagogical design based on two maker-inspired STEAM activities in which participants construct tangible virtual animals using origami, reused paper and physical computing. Drawing on Arduino and BBC micro, the proposed activities simulate animal states and care needs through variables, sensors, buttons, actuators and visual or auditory feedback. The chapter analyses how the integration of physical computing, artistic expression, sustainability and animal welfare education may support computational thinking, ethical reflection and hands-on learning. Since the activities have not yet been implemented, the chapter does not report empirical outcomes; rather, it offers a conceptual framework, activity design and evaluation considerations for future use in non-formal education, formal schooling and teacher education.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch013.venue: Transforming STEAM Education With Maker-Inspired Learning Environments

doi:10.15849/ijasca.129.title: Trustworthy Phishing URL Detection Using Machine Learning: Performance Analysis and Future Directions
doi:10.15849/ijasca.129.abstract: <jats:p>Over the years, Uniform Resource Locator (URL) Phishing has been a threat to online security because their scams exploit trust in a misleading URL to trick unsuspecting users into disclosing their username or passwords and other personal information. Not only that, but it is also crucial to identify these malicious URLs and ensure online platforms and users are protected. The ISCXURL2016 data was utilized for the purpose of analyzing the performance of different Machine Learning (ML) models in differentiating phishing and legitimate URLs in this paper. A wide range of classifiers were explored including the classic classifiers as well as more advanced ensemble classifiers. The results of the experiments indicate that ensemble-based boosting models can be more beneficial for URL phishing detection. HistGradientBoost achieved the highest accuracy of 98.47%, followed closely by LightGBM and XGBoost that both outperformed the accuracy of 98%. The other classifiers, RandomForest and ExtraTrees, also performed well with accuracy above 97% and traditional classifiers such as Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA) showed the poorest performance with an accuracy of 67.75%. The results show that the boosting-based ensembles provide a suitable negation of the complex and non-linear structure of phishing URLs. Along with empirical evaluation, it offers a Properties & Positioning viewpoint as well as the importance of the ML-based phishing detection in the broader context of cybersecurity issues. Moreover, it discusses the future directions, with Federated Learning (FL) in the context of decentralized and privacy-preserving collaboration and Large Language Models (LLM) in the context of semantic reasoning and flexibility. These insights together will provide the building blocks for more intelligent, adaptive and trustworthy phishing organizations.</jats:p>
doi:10.15849/ijasca.129.venue: International Journal of Advances in Soft Computing and its Applications

doi:10.1108/jbim-01-2026-0103.title: Learning-oriented climates and sales capability development in B2B markets: how coworker support mediates the path from climate to salesperson competence
doi:10.1108/jbim-01-2026-0103.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine how learning-oriented organizational climates and perceived support structures relate to salesperson development in complex business-to-business (B2B) sales contexts, distinguishing between satisfaction with development and perceived competence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Survey data were collected from USA-based sales professionals. The study used confirmatory factor analysis and partial least squares structural equation modeling to test relationships among learning-oriented climate cues, perceived training, supervisory and coworker support, and two developmental outcomes. Internal work constraints were tested as a moderator of the coworker support–competence relationship.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Learning-oriented climates were positively associated with perceived support and with satisfaction with development; tolerance for mistakes was also positively associated with perceived competence, whereas openness to new ideas was not. Coworker support was the support source most consistently and significantly related to perceived competence in the full sample. In the context-specific B2B analysis, coworker support emerged as the only significant predictor of perceived competence. All three support sources were positively related to satisfaction with development, whereas perceived competence was driven specifically by coworker support. Internal work constraints significantly moderated the coworker support–competence relationship, but opposite to a substitution account: coworker support mattered more when constraints were low.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings demonstrate that salesperson development is shaped by an integrated system of climate cues and social support rather than sharply differentiated pathways. Coworker-based learning emerges as a particularly salient component of competence formation in complex selling environments.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Managers should view capability development as embedded in social learning systems supported by learning-oriented climates and multiple support sources, rather than relying solely on formal development structures.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study offers a theoretically grounded account of how learning-oriented climates and multisource social support jointly shape evaluative and capability-based development in B2B sales contexts, while highlighting the particular salience of coworker-based learning for competence formation in complex B2B selling.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.51878/academia.v6i4.12543.title: PENGEMBANGAN MEDIA PEMBELAJARAN GAME-BASED LEARNING BERBASIS KEARIFAN LOKAL UNTUK MENINGKATKAN PEMAHAMAN NILAI BUDAYA PADA SISWA SD
doi:10.51878/academia.v6i4.12543.abstract: <jats:p>This research is based on the low understanding of local cultural values in elementary school students due to learning that is still dominated by lecture methods and less use of interactive media. This condition causes students to be less actively involved in the learning process, so cultural values have not been optimally internalized. This research aims to develop a local wisdom-based game-based learning medium in the form of Room Challenges Heritage (WANGTARA) to increase the understanding of cultural values in elementary school students. The research method used is Research and Development (R&D) with an ADDIE model that includes the Analysis, Design, Development, and Implementation stages. The research was conducted at SDN SKIP Sukabumi City in the last semester of the 2026/2027 school year with research subjects consisting of material experts, media experts, V-grade teachers, and 19 V-grade students. Data collection techniques use observations, interviews, documentation, and angkets, while research instruments include expert validation sheets, practitioner angkets, student response angkets, and pre-test and post-test tests. Research results show that WANGTARA media was successfully developed through Genially's platform by combining elements of escape room games and local cultural heritage materials. Media implementation shows a positive response from students because it is able to create interactive, challenging, and fun learning. It also encourages students' active involvement in collaborative activities and critical thinking, and helps them understand local cultural values more meaningfully. Thus, WANGTARA learning media has the potential to be an innovative alternative in learning cultural values in elementary schools.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75043-9.title: A hybrid data-centric machine learning for lost circulation prediction using imbalanced drilling and geological datasets
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75043-9.abstract: Lost circulation remains one of the most critical operational challenges in drilling engineering, yet predictive modeling in real-field conditions is often constrained by severely imbalanced and limited datasets. While previous studies have primarily relied on single imbalance-handling techniques or large datasets, this study introduces a sequential, hybrid data-centric machine learning framework specifically designed for small, multiclass, and highly skewed drilling datasets. A dataset of 258 operational records from the Buzergan oil field in southern Iraq, including drilling parameters, mud properties, and geological indicators, were used to predict lost circulation severity. Unlike conventional approaches, this work systematically integrates synthetic sampling techniques, ensemble learning (bagging and stacking), and cost-sensitive class-weight optimization within a staged workflow, where each enhancement step builds upon the previous one. Importantly, class weights were computed from the original imbalanced distribution and transferred to synthetically augmented datasets, preserving the true imbalance structure while improving minority-class sensitivity. Hyperparameter tuning was conducted using Optuna with Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE), and model evaluation emphasized the Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) to ensure robust assessment under multiclass imbalance. The results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid framework significantly outperforms standalone oversampling or ensemble strategies. The CatBoost model combined with the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) and optimized custom class weights achieved the highest classification performance (Accuracy: 0.8846; Weighted F1: 0.8651; MCC: 0.8236; weighted Area Under the Curve, AUC-W: 0.9154), while a stacking ensemble exhibited superior ranking capability (AUC-W: 0.934). The primary novelty of this study lies in (1) treating class weight as a tunable hyperparameter rather than a fixed correction factor, (2) sequentially combining synthetic data generation with imbalance-aware weighting, and (3) validating the framework under strict stratified cross-validation and clean hold-out testing to prevent data leakage. This structured hybrid methodology offers a template applicable to other small-sample, imbalanced classification problems in drilling; validating the trained models themselves on other fields remains future work.

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-7431-4.ch008.title: Deep Learning for Intelligent Waste Management and Real-Time Organic and Recyclable Waste Classification for Smart Cities
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-7431-4.ch008.abstract: <jats:p>Growing waste production and rapid urbanization pose serious logistical and environmental challenges. Reducing the burden on landfills and promoting the circular economy rely on effective separation of recyclable and organic waste. In this chapter, a deep learning based real-time classification framework that uses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with transfer learning and is optimised for Internet of Things deployment is presented for differentiating between recyclable and organic waste. The system shows promise for integration into smart bins and urban recycling infrastructure with an accuracy of approximately 93%. In addition to technical design, the chapter discusses deployment concerns, ethical concerns, application contexts, and new developments like federated learning and sustainable AI. This work helps bridge the gap between environmental sustainability and AI research and is in line with the goals of smart cities.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-7431-4.ch008.venue: E-Waste and the Circular Economy in Technology

doi:10.51582/interconf.19-20.10.2026.007.title: The role of project-based learning in developing English language
doi:10.51582/interconf.19-20.10.2026.007.abstract: <jats:p>The meaning of words can also limit their potential for combination. Many researchers highlight the close interrelationship between a word's semantics and its syntactic function. Therefore, in our view, it is more appropriate to approach the issue of valency by considering not only the grammatical characteristics of words but also their semantic properties.Based on the description of word relationships provided by A.A. Ufimtseva and V.G. Admoni, the combinatory potential of various parts of speech has been investigated by examining the completeness or incompleteness of their lexical content, while also taking into account the concepts of sentence constituents and syntactic relations. These authors were the first to propose analyzing the relationship between dominant and dependent sentence constituents. The grammatical potential of words was studied in conjunction with their lexical semantics. Thus, the characteristics of word combinability were determined to be directly dependent on their lexical meanings. In the research works of I.S. Gorelik, E. Ioffik, V.L. Zavgorodnyaya, D.N. Ufimtseva, and others, valency is examined from precisely this perspective. It should be noted that the study of valency characteristics— not only of verbs but also of other parts of speech—is of particular interest to researchers. Some researchers interpret valency more broadly by taking into account both its potential and its possibilities for realization—in other words, by considering factors of both language and speech.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75507-y.title: Hierarchical reinforcement learning with model predictive elevator control for risk-sensitive multi-robot transport scheduling in hospitals
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-75507-y.abstract: Hospitals increasingly deploy autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) to move specimens and medicines between wards and laboratories. These fleets must meet clinical deadlines that differ across request classes, which couples two decisions: which request each robot serves, and the order of its stops. Intra-hospital transport is formulated here as a multi-objective Markov game and solved with hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning for transport (HMART). A shared graph-attention encoder feeds a sequential assignment decoder and a route-improvement decoder, a conditional value-at-risk constraint bounds the tail of class-weighted tardiness, and a model predictive control layer coordinates the capacitated elevators. Two instantiations are evaluated: HMART-H, whose decoders are engineered, and HMART-RL, whose assignment decoder is a trained attention network. In a discrete-event simulator of a four-floor hospital with three elevators, at heavy load with twelve robots over twenty paired seeds, HMART-H lowers mean total weighted tardiness from 2359 ± 214 to 29 ± 6 against the strongest dispatching rule, mean work-in-process from 80.1 ± 6.4 to 14.3 ± 1.9, and the ninety-fifth percentile tardiness tail by more than an order of magnitude, while raising the STAT on-time rate from 0.925 ± 0.011 to 0.969 ± 0.007; all differences are significant under Holm-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. HMART-RL reaches 40 ± 8 and transfers across fleet sizes and building configurations without retraining. These gains are obtained in simulation and require confirmation in a live building.

doi:10.21009/jrpmj.v8i2.71090.title: Perbedaan Pemahaman Matematis dan Perilaku Belajar pada Pembelajaran Contextual Teaching and Learning: Studi Kuasi-Eksperimen Materi Persamaan Linear Satu Variabel di MTs
doi:10.21009/jrpmj.v8i2.71090.abstract: <jats:p>Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk mengetahui dan menganalisis pengaruh model pembelajaran contextual teaching learning (CTL) pada motivasi dan kemampuan pemahaman matematis siswa. Penelitian ini mengambil desain spesifik Nonequivalent Control Group Design. Sampel dari penelitian ini adalah siswa MTs Ma’arif 2 Muntilan Kelas 7 yang berjumlah 61 orang yang terbagi menjadi kelas 7A sebanyak 31 orang sebagai kelompok kontrol dan kelas 7B sebanyak 30 orang sebagai kelompok eksperimen. Analisis data dilakukan melalui metode statistik deskriptif dan uji N-gain. Pengambilan data kualitatif dilakukan dengan metode observasi dan wawancara. Hasil penelitian ini menunjukan model pembelajaran CTL memiliki pengaruh signifikan pada kelompok eksperimen yang mendapatkan peningkatan rata-rata dari hasil awal pretest 61,00 menjadi 81,33 pada posttest dan N-gain sebesar 0,52. Observasi dan wawancara juga memperlihatkan pengaruh signifikan model pembelajaran CTL pada motivasi siswa.</jats:p>

doi:10.47852/bonviewjcce62029582.title: Beyond Complexity: Evaluating Simple vs. Complex Deep Learning Architectures for Urban Density Mapping
doi:10.47852/bonviewjcce62029582.abstract:
<jats:p>The spatial distribution of population density and land use is a fundamental metric for targeting spatial planning policies under the Sustainable Development Goals. This study presents a comparative evaluation of deep learning architectures for urban density estimation, with an emphasis on spatial generalization. The study was conducted in Jakarta and its surrounding cities (Jabodetabek), a highly heterogeneous region that provides a rigorous setting for evaluating model generalization. Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and European Space Agency WorldCover 2020 data were acquired through Google Earth Engine, together with the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index and the Normalized Difference Built-up Index to explicitly represent vegetation and built-up characteristics. Quantitative evaluation showed that all deep learning models performed well, with R² exceeding 0.94 in all experiments. The U-Net architecture achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with the lowest mean squared error (MSE = 0.0006954). Notably, the lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) proved to be a highly competitive alternative (MSE = 0.0006998), requiring approximately four times fewer parameters and delivering roughly twice the inference speed of the deeper U-Net and ResNet models. In contrast, complex models such as EfficientNet and ResNet showed diminishing returns in accuracy relative to their design complexity, while classical machine learning baselines (Random Forest and XGBoost) failed to capture spatial configurations robustly. These findings demonstrate that increasing network depth does not necessarily improve performance in spatial fractional regression. Therefore, model selection should balance predictive accuracy against computational and environmental costs.

doi:10.30872/jlpf.v7i2.6564.title: Differences Comparative Analysis of Students' Mathematical Thinking Skills and Learning Outcomes between Matrix Inverse and Substitution-Elimination Methods in Dynamic Electricity
doi:10.30872/jlpf.v7i2.6564.abstract: <jats:p>Dynamic electricity is a physics topic that students often find challenging, especially in solving two-loop circuit problems that require mathematical reasoning. This study examined the differences in students’ mathematical thinking skills and learning outcomes between the matrix inverse method and the substitution-elimination method in senior high school dynamic electricity learning. A quasi-experimental design, specifically the Posttest-Only Control Group Design, was employed within a quantitative research approach. The experimental class comprised 31 students taught using the matrix inverse method, while the control class consisted of 33 students taught using the substitution-elimination method. Data were collected through a five-item essay test based on reasoning, generalization, critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication indicators. Data analysis was conducted using the Mann–Whitney test and independent samples t-test. The results indicated significant differences in mathematical thinking ability (sig. 0.016 < 0.05) and learning outcomes (sig. 0.005 < 0.05). The experimental class achieved higher mean scores in mathematical thinking ability (66.90) and learning outcomes (68.42) compared to the control class (58.82 and 56.42). The findings demonstrate the potential of the matrix inverse method to enhance students’ mathematical thinking skills and learning outcomes when learning dynamic electricity.</jats:p>

doi:10.5194/egusphere-2026-4477.title: A dropsonde-based machine-learning framework for estimating marine atmospheric boundary layer height around the Korean Peninsula
doi:10.5194/egusphere-2026-4477.abstract: <jats:p>Abstract. This study presents an observation-based machine-learning framework for estimating marine atmospheric boundary layer (MABL) height around the Korean Peninsula using aircraft dropsondes collected during 2020–2024. Of 1193 profiles, 1179 were collocated with ERA5 and 666 had well-defined MABL tops assigned through expert interpretation of thermodynamic and moisture profiles; 642 complete cases were used for machine learning. Dropsonde observations and ERA5 sea surface temperature were combined to estimate air–sea heat fluxes using a COARE 3.0-based formulation. Selected profile-based diagnostics and ERA5 planetary boundary layer height (PBLH) were evaluated against the expert-interpreted reference. Five machine-learning algorithms were trained using all thermodynamic regimes together and evaluated by five-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by observation date. For the same 642 profiles, the machine-learning models reduced mean absolute error by 38.3–41.0 % relative to ERA5 PBLH. Random Forest, XGBoost, and a deep neural network yielded mean absolute errors of 155.5–155.9 m; the neural network had the lowest root-mean-square error (209.5 m) and the highest correlation (0.815). Random Forest permutation importance identified near-surface relative humidity and relative humidity at 925 hPa as the leading predictors. Moisture-related variables remained important across three thermodynamic regimes defined using 850 hPa temperature and lower-tropospheric stability. The proposed framework thus reproduced the expert-interpreted MABL height reference more closely than ERA5 PBLH for well-defined cases. The expert heights are physically informed references, not independent direct measurements of turbulent boundary layer depth.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch007.title: Institutional Conditions for Sustainable STEAM Innovation
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch007.abstract: <jats:p>Sustainable innovation in science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics (STEAM) education requires more than curricular integration or technological enhancement; it fundamentally depends on the institutional ecosystems that shape teaching and learning processes. This chapter examines how maker-inspired learning environments such as makerspaces, fabrication laboratories (fablabs), and design studios can transform STEAM education when supported by collaborative school cultures, professional learning systems, and strong institutional networks. Drawing on ecological systems theory, teacher professional identity frameworks, and organizational learning theory, the chapter proposes an Institutional STEAM Ecosystem Model integrating leadership, teacher professional development, curriculum co-design, sustainable infrastructure, and community partnerships. Through conceptual analysis and illustrative cases from primary and secondary education, the chapter argues that sustainable STEAM transformation emerges from systemic alignment rather than isolated innovation initiatives</jats:p>

doi:10.1088/0256-307x/43/11/110602.title: Experiment-compatible measurement-feedback quantum state preparation with reinforcement learning
doi:10.1088/0256-307x/43/11/110602.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ground-state preparation is a critical task in quantum simulation and quantum computing, as it enables the study of correlated phases and the generation of entangled resource states. While measurement–feedback control has emerged as a promising route to state preparation, existing schemes either rely on handcrafted, task-specific policies or are designed using full quantum-state information that is unavailable in real experiments and becomes impractical for large many-body systems. Here we develop an adaptive measurement–feedback protocol based on reinforcement learning under partial observability. The controller uses only the history of experimentally accessible measurement outcomes to choose both the measurement operator and the feedback action in real time. To make training compatible with experiments, we introduce a stochastic terminal reward built from one-shot measurements of randomly sampled Hamiltonian components, avoiding unphysical full-state reconstruction while remaining an unbiased estimator of the target energy. We demonstrate the method by preparing ground states of the Bose–Hubbard model and by generating GHZ states, establishing a scalable and hardware-compatible route to quantum state preparation.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1975752.title: Machine learning models integrating 2D and 3D intratumoral heterogeneity features from multi-sequence MRI: accurate prediction of perineural invasion in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1975752.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Perineural invasion (PNI) occurs in the majority of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cases and is strongly associated with local recurrence, neuropathic pain, and poor survival, yet no reliable method exists for its preoperative identification. Here, we developed and externally validated a multi-sequence MRI-based intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) scoring framework integrated with machine learning for the non-invasive prediction of PNI in PDAC.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using preoperative T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted, and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI from 205 surgically resected patients across four medical centers (100 training, 43 internal test, and 28 and 34 external validation patients), we extracted two-dimensional and three-dimensional ITH features via K-means clustering-based subregion partitioning and incorporated independent clinical predictors tumor location and clinical T-stage to construct combined predictive models. Eleven machine learning algorithms were systematically evaluated.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The combined clinical-ITH model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.907 in the internal test set and AUCs of 0.860 and 0.869 in the two external validation cohorts. Corresponding AUCs were 0.881, 0.860, and 0.850 for the ITH model and 0.758, 0.342, and 0.700 for the clinical logistic regression model.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>SHAP analysis ranked three T2WI-derived features as the largest contributors to the combined model output, feature effects varied in direction and were not uniformly monotonic. These findings demonstrate that multi-sequence MRI-based ITH quantification provides an interpretable approach to preoperative PNI assessment with consistent discrimination across the two external surgical cohorts, offering a potential tool to guide surgical planning and adjuvant therapy selection in pancreatic cancer.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1007/s10207-026-01349-4.title: A unified drift-adaptive and robust residual autoencoder with attention and few-shot learning for zero-day intrusion detection
doi:10.1007/s10207-026-01349-4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Autoencoder-based unsupervised intrusion detection systems (IDS) offer a promising approach for identifying zero-day attacks without requiring labeled malicious data. However, residual autoencoder (RAE) frameworks remain limited by static decision thresholds, susceptibility to concept drift (CD), limited adversarial robustness, and restricted adaptability to emerging attack patterns. To address these limitations, we propose the Attention-Boosted Streaming Residual Autoencoder (ASRAE), a unified framework that integrates attention-enhanced representation learning, online CD detection with adaptive thresholding, benign-only adversarial training, post-identification few-shot meta-learning, and explainability through integrated gradients (IG). Experiments on UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2017, and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 show that ASRAE outperforms the evaluated unsupervised baselines, achieving ROC-AUC values of 0.952, 0.940, and 0.931, respectively. Under the controlled simulated concept-drift setting, ASRAE maintains a ROC-AUC above 0.91, while adversarial evaluation using Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) and Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) demonstrates improved robustness to feature-space perturbations. The few-shot adaptation stage further enables adaptation to held-out attack families using only a small number of labeled samples while largely preserving benign reconstruction performance. ASRAE requires an average inference time of 9.2 ms per sample in the evaluated experimental environment. Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of ASRAE across the benchmark, simulated-drift, adversarial, and few-shot adaptation settings.</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s12909-026-10641-9.title: The hospital as a third classroom: a qualitative descriptive-interpretive study of situated learning and the hidden curriculum among medical interns
doi:10.1186/s12909-026-10641-9.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Much medical training occurs through everyday clinical work, where informal teaching and the hidden curriculum shape learning and professional identity. Social pedagogy offers a relational and ethical lens for these processes. We explored interns’ experiences of the hospital as a third classroom: a workplace learning environment alongside university teaching and the formal internship programme.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted a qualitative descriptive-interpretive study in an urban private hospital in Ecuador. Twenty-one rotating medical interns from the 2024–2025 cohort completed an anonymous online questionnaire with 10 open-ended questions in July 2025. Responses were examined through complete reading, open inductive coding, identification of meaning units, thematic grouping and a double-entry matrix. Social pedagogy informed interpretation. Reported institutional expectations provided documentary context, rather than a separately reported documentary analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Three related themes were identified. The hospital functioned as a situated learning community through bedside participation, corridor microteaching, night-shift learning, role modelling and patient and family education. The hidden curriculum and ethical climate influenced whether interns could ask questions, acknowledge uncertainty and develop respectful professional identities. Accessible tutors, interprofessional rounds and humanising practices bridged formal intentions and everyday learning, whereas workload, rigid hierarchy, inconsistent feedback and service-level variation restricted educational opportunities. Together, the themes describe learning opportunities, the relationships governing participation and the organisational conditions supporting or constraining them.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this cohort, social pedagogy helped interpret the relational, participatory and ethical dimensions of workplace learning. Protecting brief teaching moments, responding respectfully to uncertainty and reflecting interprofessionally on hidden messages are potential implications for clinical teachers; their feasibility and effects require evaluation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch006.title: Integrating Biomimicry Into STEAM Education Through Maker-Inspired Design Practices for Pre-Service Teachers
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch006.abstract: <jats:p>Biomimicry is increasingly recognized as a promising approach for connecting scientific inquiry, engineering design, and sustainability. At the same time, STEAM education seeks meaningful ways to integrate the Arts alongside science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. This chapter proposes the Bio-Maker model, a framework for integrating biomimicry into STEAM education within pre-service teacher preparation. Drawing on literature from biomimicry, STEAM education, maker-inspired design, and teacher education, the chapter argues that biomimicry design challenges provide a valuable context for interdisciplinary learning because observation, visual representation, and iterative design are embedded within the biomimicry process. To illustrate its application, the chapter presents a four-week course component with activities, assessment tools, learning outcomes, and sample activity sheets. The chapter concludes with implications for teacher education and future research.</jats:p>

doi:10.51178/jetl.v8i3.3768.title: Pengaruh Prokrastinasi Akademik dan Self Regulated Learning terhadap Hasil Belajar siswa
doi:10.51178/jetl.v8i3.3768.abstract: <jats:p>Hasil pembelajaran adalah salah satu tanda keberhasilan dalam proses belajar yang dipengaruhi oleh sejumlah faktor, baik yang berasal dari diri siswa maupun dari lingkungan mereka. Prokrastinasi dalam bidang akademik dan pembelajaran yang teratur menjadi aspek penting yang terkait dengan bagaimana siswa mengelola waktu, mengontrol perilaku belajar, serta menyelesaikan tugas akademiknya. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menyelidiki dampak prokrastinasi akademik dan pembelajaran teratur terhadap hasil belajar siswa pada pelajaran Ekonomi di SMA Negeri 1 Basa Ampek Balai Tapan, baik secara terpisah maupun bersamaan. Metode penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan jenis asosiatif. Populasi yang terlibat adalah seluruh siswa di SMA Negeri 1 Basa Ampek Balai Tapan yang belajar mata pelajaran Ekonomi berjumlah 586 siswa. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui kuesioner dan dokumentasi, sedangkan untuk analisis data digunakan analisis regresi linier berganda dengan bantuan aplikasi SPSS. Temuan penelitian menunjukkan bahwa prokrastinasi akademik memberikan pengaruh negatif dan signifikan terhadap hasil belajar, dengan thitung sebesar -2,043 dan nilai signifikansi 0,042 < 0,05. Pembelajaran yang teratur memberikan pengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap hasil belajar, dengan thitung sebesar 2,706 dan nilai signifikansi 0,007 < 0,05. Secara bersamaan, prokrastinasi akademik dan pembelajaran teratur memiliki pengaruh yang signifikan terhadap hasil belajar, dengan nilai F sebesar 3,702 dan signifikansi 0,026 < 0,05. Nilai R Square sebesar 0,031 menunjukkan bahwa kedua variabel tersebut dapat menjelaskan variasi hasil belajar sebesar 3,1%, sementara 96,9% lainnya dipengaruhi oleh faktor lain di luar model penelitian ini.</jats:p>
doi:10.51178/jetl.v8i3.3768.venue: Journal Of Education And Teaching Learning (JETL)

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11399301/v1.title: An Optimization-Driven Feature Selection and Deep Learning Framework for Accurate Credit Card Fraud Detection
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11399301/v1.abstract: The rapid growth of digital financial services has increased the volume and complexity of credit card transactions, creating significant challenges for financial institutions seeking to identify fraudulent activities accurately and efficiently. Traditional fraud detection approaches often struggle with extreme class imbalance, high-dimensional transaction data, evolving fraudulent behaviors, and the need for real-time decision-making. This paper proposes an optimization-driven feature selection and deep learning framework for accurate credit card fraud detection. The framework integrates feature selection, hyperparameter optimization, class-imbalance management, and deep neural network classification into a unified detection pipeline. An optimization mechanism identifies informative transaction features while reducing redundant variables and computational overhead. The selected features are subsequently processed by a deep learning classifier trained to distinguish legitimate transactions from fraudulent activities. To improve practical reliability, the framework incorporates cost-sensitive learning, precision-recall-based evaluation, probability calibration, and threshold optimization. The widely used European credit card transaction dataset is discussed as a potential benchmark for empirical evaluation. The proposed framework is expected to provide a systematic approach to improving fraud detection performance, although its actual effectiveness must be established through controlled experiments. The paper contributes a reproducible methodological foundation for developing efficient, adaptive, and scalable fraud detection systems in modern financial environments.

doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010691/v1.title: Grassmannian Density Learning for Physically Consistent Kohn–Sham Electronic Structure Prediction
doi:10.26434/chemrxiv.15010691/v1.abstract: <jats:p>Deep-learning electronic-structure models show great potential to accelerate first-principles calculations, with broad implications for materials science, biology and drug discovery. Yet no consensus has emerged on which physical quantity should be modeled to represent electronic states. As two fundamental quantities that arise naturally in Kohn–Sham density functional theory, the Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian and electronic density have attracted the most attention. Hamiltonian prediction, however, devotes substantial modeling capacity to degrees of freedom that do not affect the occupied electronic subspace, whereas direct regression of density matrices or real-space densities removes this redundancy but cannot ensure that the prediction represents a physically admissible electronic state. Motivated by the fact that electronic states themselves reside on a constrained manifold, we observe that predicting coordinates directly on this manifold can simultaneously eliminate redundant degrees of freedom and preserve physical admissibility. Here we introduce GeoK, a framework that predicts compact occupied–virtual orbital-rotation generators as coordinates on the manifold of electronic states, thereby ensuring each prediction corresponds to a valid electronic state of the target molecular system. We further develop a neural-network architecture tailored to this geometric prediction task. Across in-distribution and out-of-distribution benchmarks, as well as downstream applications, GeoK consistently improves electronic-state prediction over the evaluated Hamiltonian and unconstrained densityregression baselines, while supporting robust deployment in downstream first-principles workflows. These results establish orbital-rotation generator prediction as a principled and reliable paradigm for intrinsic electronic-state modeling, opening a route towards more accurate and transferable deep-learning electronic-structure models.</jats:p>

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8069-8.ch002.title: Creativity Meets Emerging Technology
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8069-8.ch002.abstract: <jats:p>Emerging technologies are reshaping creativity in design, education, and professional practice. Rather than acting as neutral tools, technologies such as artificial intelligence, extended reality, and digital fabrication increasingly function as active collaborators in creative processes. This chapter reframes creativity as a relational, system-based capability emerging from human–technology interaction. It examines implications for creative practice, education, and ethics, emphasising that there must be responsible, reflective, and sustainable approaches to technology-enabled creativity.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8069-8.ch002.venue: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch004.title: From Makerspaces to Mindsets
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-9953-9.ch004.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores the essential role of teachers in transforming STEAM education through maker-inspired learning environments. It highlights that successful implementation depends on well-prepared educators who can facilitate open-ended inquiry and navigate the “productive struggle” inherent in design-based learning. Drawing on a qualitative study of 23 educators, the author examines diverse professional pathways and emphasizes the need for a shift in teacher identity from a source of knowledge to a facilitator of exploration. Key recommendations include strengthening preservice preparation, providing sustained, differentiated professional development, and prioritizing professional networks to reduce isolation and foster a sustainable STEAM ecosystem.</jats:p>

doi:10.32672/perisai.v5i3.4627.abstract: <jats:p>Penelitian ini berangkat dari permasalahan rendahnya keterampilan proses sains (KPS) peserta didik di MAS Persis Pajagalan yang berkaitan dengan belum optimalnya penyajian aktivitas ilmiah dalam bahan ajar pada materi gelombang bunyi. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis kelayakan bahan ajar berbasis model Learning Cycle 7E, keterlaksanaan pembelajaran, serta peningkatan KPS peserta didik kelas XI B setelah menggunakan bahan ajar tersebut. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan mixed methods dengan metode Research and Development (R&D) yang mengadaptasi model ADDIE dan desain one group pretest-posttest. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 25 peserta didik. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui lembar validasi ahli, lembar observasi keterlaksanaan pembelajaran, dan tes KPS berupa pretest dan posttest. Analisis data meliputi Indeks Validitas Gregory, persentase keterlaksanaan pembelajaran, N-Gain, serta Paired Sample T-test. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa bahan ajar memperoleh nilai Indeks Validitas Gregory sebesar 1,00 dari validasi ahli materi dan media sehingga termasuk kategori sangat tinggi. Keterlaksanaan pembelajaran juga berada pada kategori sangat baik, dengan persentase aktivitas guru sebesar 95,15% dan aktivitas peserta didik sebesar 89,22%. Efektivitas bahan ajar ditunjukkan melalui peningkatan rata-rata skor KPS dari 46 pada pretest menjadi 82 pada posttest, dengan nilai N-Gain sebesar 0,67 yang berada pada kategori sedang. Hasil Paired Sample T-test menunjukkan nilai Sig. (2-tailed) < 0,05, sehingga terdapat perbedaan yang signifikan antara skor pretest dan posttest. Dengan demikian, bahan ajar berbasis model Learning Cycle 7E berbantuan Flipbook memenuhi kriteria kelayakan dan dapat digunakan dalam pembelajaran untuk mendukung peningkatan keterampilan proses sains peserta didik pada materi gelombang bunyi.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fnbeh.2026.1981387.title: Editorial: Sleep and cognition: the role of sleep patterns and deprivation in memory and learning
doi:10.3389/fnbeh.2026.1981387.abstract: This Special Research Topic was conceptualized to bridge the gap between basic neurophysiological mechanisms of sleep and their real-world cognitive implications across the lifespan. While the essential roles of slow-wave sleep (SWS) microstructures-such as slow oscillations and sleep spindles-and REM sleep in memory consolidation are well established, how these neural processes interact with daily lifestyle stressors, shift work, cultural demands, and aging remains incompletely understood. The primary objective of this Research Topic was to bring together multi-level evidence-spanning high-density EEG, event-related potentials, wearable in-home monitoring, and large-scale epidemiological cohorts-to elucidate how sleep patterns, deprivation, and night-to-night variability shape cognitive integrity in diverse populations.Sleep significantly contributes to memory consolidation and cognitive performance. In particular, oscillatory events occurring during slow-wave sleep (SWS), such as slow oscillations (SOs) and sleep spindles, are crucial for reorganizing and transferring new information acquired during wakefulness, from the hippocampus to the neocortex, while rapid eye movement (REM) sleep plays a vital role in emotional memory processing (Wilson and McNaughto, 1994;Marshall and Born, 2007;Diekelman and Born, 2010). Therefore, it is not surprising that sleep deprivation has negative consequences on memory consolidation (Crowley et al., 2024). Moreover, once sleep architecture changes across lifespan, with progressive difficulty in sleep maintenance and percentage of SWS decreasing with age (Ohayon et al., 2024), it is essential to study the influence of sleep in cognition in different age groups. The articles compiled in this Research Topic investigate these neurophysiological underpinnings, examine the impacts of acute and chronic sleep deprivation, and elucidate how sleep quality and night-to-night variability affect cognitive function across diverse populations, from young students to older adults.Exploring the microstructural mechanisms of sleep, Keeble et al. present a mini-review detailing how the precise temporal coordination between SOs, sleep spindles, and hippocampal ripples during SWS facilitates memory transfer and synaptic plasticity. They discuss how SWS disruptions-driven by aging, neurological disorders, and pharmacotherapy-lead to memory impairments, and highlight the potential of emerging neuromodulation techniques (e.g., closed-loop acoustic stimulation) to restore sleep microstructure and enhance cognitive health.Taking a behavioral approach to sleep-dependent memory triage, Kurdziel et al. investigate how intentional top-down goals interact with emotional salience during overnight sleep, since it is known that executive control processes can suppress certain memories to be recalled (Anderson and Green, 2001). They applied a task with remember vs. forget instructions of neutral and negative words in sleep or wake condition, and demonstrated that percentage of SWS and delta power were negatively associated with total recall, while sleep spindle correlated with negative remember-cued words. Besides, REM theta power was associated with negative foils intrusions. The study shows that top-down instruction overrides emotional salience when the cues are competing and sleep events associated with selective memory consolidation.The critical role of sleep quality in the cognitive outcomes of younger cohorts is further highlighted in two student-focused studies. Xu et al. demonstrate a high prevalence of insomnia (54.1%) and poor sleep quality (58.9%) among college students in Guangzhou. They show that short sleep duration exacerbates sleep disturbances, which directly correlate with declines in attention, language, and visual-perceptual learning, placing students at risk of long-term cognitive decline. This vulnerability is modulated by sociocultural contexts, as demonstrated by Ampofo et al. in a cross-cultural study comparing university students in Tokyo and London. They find that Tokyo students suffer from significantly poorer sleep quality, had shorter sleep duration and lower sleep efficiency compared to their London peers, and that cultural factors-such as intense academic pressure and societal norms prioritizing productivity over rest in Japan-significantly moderate the relationship between sleep quality and memory, making the detrimental impact of poor sleep on verbal learning more pronounced in Tokyo. This study suggests that interventions to improve sleep quality and cognitive functioning in university students need to consider cultural and lifestyle differences.When sleep is severely disrupted or altogether absent, the cognitive consequences are immediate. Ren et al. investigate the impacts of 24-hour total sleep deprivation (TSD) on healthy adults, combining subjective reaction times (using the auditory Oddball paradigm) with objective auditory P300 eventrelated potentials (ERPs). They show that acute sleep loss significantly extends P300 latency, indicating delayed auditory cognitive processing and reduced attentional alertness. Interestingly, they compare individuals with and without a chronic history of night-shift work (>24 months). While acute sleep loss dramatically impairs reaction times in the non-shift group, chronic night-shift workers show persistent baseline alterations in cognitive metrics, suggesting that chronic sleep disruptions induce cumulative, unrestored neurobiological damage.Addressing the challenge of capturing naturalistic sleep-cognition relationships, Brooks et al. present a multi-night, in-home wearable EEG study in healthy older adults. They showed that even with participants putting the EEG device themselves, ∼71% of the recorded data was usable. Over approximately 10 nights, they demonstrate substantial night-to-night variability in both macro-and microarchitectural sleep metrics (e.g., WASO, SO, and spindle density). Interestingly, despite clear nightly fluctuations, they find that next-day executive functions (inhibition and cognitive flexibility) remain resilient to daily sleep variations.As the global population ages, understanding the relationship between sleep patterns and cognitive decline becomes paramount. In a large-scale, nine-year longitudinal study of 9,970 older Chinese adults, Qian et al. explore the links between sleep patterns and cognitive frailty. Older Chinese adults with poor sleep quality and short sleep duration (< 6 hours) had 67% and 48% higher risk of cognitive weakness, respectively, while no and excessive napping, increased the risk of cognitive debilitation by 23% and 69% respectively. This and Brooks' study underscores the feasibility of using portable devices to conduct ecologically valid sleep research, while providing crucial statistical parameters (variance components and effect sizes) to guide the design of future longitudinal studies in different populations.Together, the contributions to this Research Topic span the full spectrum of sleep and cognitive science. They transition from laboratory-based microstructural investigations and acute deprivation experiments to naturalistic, multi-night home monitoring and large-scale demographic epidemiological cohorts. By integrating these multi-level methodologies, this Research Topic moves the field forward beyond traditional single-night paradigms toward ecologically valid and lifespan-oriented sleep science.Nevertheless, key open questions remain: What neural compensatory mechanisms allow certain cognitive functions to remain resilient despite night-to-night sleep fluctuations, and how can microarchitectural sleep biomarkers be leveraged for the early detection of cognitive frailty? Collectively, these studies reinforce the profound, multi-dimensional impact of sleep on brain health, and highlight the urgent need for more research in age and culturally diverse populations, and in pharmacological or behavioral approaches to prevent or mitigate the cognitive impacts of sleep deprivation. Those interventions should be culturally tailored, occupational, and age-specific to preserve cognitive integrity across the lifespan.

doi:10.54254/2755-2721/2026.ast37792.title: Molecular Toxicity Prediction and Machine Learning
doi:10.54254/2755-2721/2026.ast37792.abstract: <jats:p>With the rapid growth in the number of chemicals, conventional in vivo and in vitro toxicity tests face challenges including high cost, long experimental cycles, and ethical concerns, creating an urgent need for efficient computational toxicology approaches. This review systematically summarizes the application of machine learning to molecular toxicity prediction, with particular emphasis on two core components: algorithm selection and descriptor construction. At the algorithmic level, the principles and applicable scenarios of conventional machine-learning models, including random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and k-nearest neighbors (KNN), as well as deep-learning methods, are introduced in detail, together with the classification framework of supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised learning. At the descriptor level, in view of the dependence of conventional computational descriptors on accurate molecular structures, the advantages and recent applications of mass spectrometry (MS) data as a new type of descriptor are highlighted. These applications include molecular-structure recognition (CANOPUS and SIFTER), quantitative compound analysis (an internal-standard replacement strategy based on natural organic matter background peaks and virtual molecular projection CNNs for nanoparticles), and spectrum prediction. Current studies indicate that combining mass-spectrometric descriptors with machine learning can reduce dependence on structural databases and enable rapid classification and quantitative prediction of unknown compounds, showing considerable potential for environmental monitoring and toxicity screening. Nevertheless, current models remain strongly data-dependent and are limited by insufficient interpretability and restricted applicability domains. Future work should therefore focus on expanding datasets, improving model interpretability, and strengthening cross-domain generalization.</jats:p>

doi:10.54365/adyumbd.1984661.title: Climatic Drivers of Water Availability in the Atatürk Dam Basin: An Explainable Machine-Learning (XGBoost–SHAP) Framework Using ERA5-Land (1950–2025)
doi:10.54365/adyumbd.1984661.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Water availability in the Atatürk Dam basin, the largest reservoir of the Southeastern Anatolia Project (GAP) and a snow-fed Euphrates headwater, is sensitive to warming, yet its climatic drivers have not been ranked. Existing studies use trend tests, process models, or black-box machine learning. This study attributes and forecasts total runoff (a water-availability proxy) from basin-mean monthly ERA5-Land data (1950–2025), using XGBoost against linear and random-forest baselines under leakage-free cross-validation and exact TreeSHAP. The model reproduced the reanalysis runoff (R² ≈ 0.97, NSE ≈ 0.96), and SHAP ranked three-month accumulated snowmelt, deep-layer soil moisture, and water-year cumulative precipitation as the dominant drivers, with nonlinear thresholds; permutation and water-balance tests confirmed it is leakage-free. Antecedent snow-depth memory weakened over time while the snowmelt share was preserved, consistent with significant warming, snow decline, and rising evaporative demand (Mann–Kendall, Sen's slope); annual runoff showed no trend. From antecedent state, runoff was forecast about three months ahead (one-month R² ≈ 0.89). The framework can inform climate-resilient GAP reservoir operation; as it is reanalysis-based and unvalidated against gauges, future work should add gauge validation and gridded, scenario-based settings.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10774377/v1.title: Explainable graph reinforcement learning for resilience assessment and self-healing decision-making in distribution networks
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10774377/v1.abstract: The rapid integration of distributed generation and the growing frequency of extreme weather events are stressing the security of distribution-network supply , and fault self-healing must now reconcile three competing demands: decision quality, real-time performance, and explainability. Mathematical programming yields near-optimal solutions but is too slow for online use, whereas existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods decide within milliseconds but remain opaque, which limits operator trust. We present an explainable graph reinforcement learning method for resilience assessment and self-healing decision-making in distribution networks. The network is first modelled as a graph and a graph attention network (GAT) extracts topology-aware state representations; the GAT is then embedded as the shared backbone of a soft actor–critic (SAC) agent, whose maximum-entropy objective improves exploration in complex fault scenarios. A dual-track explainability mechanism combines intrinsic multi-head attention heatmaps with post-hoc SHAP attributions, providing evidence of both where the agent attends and why it decides, and a resilience index is embedded directly in the reward so that maximizing resilience becomes the training objective. Joint MATLAB–Python simulations on the IEEE 33-bus and 123-bus systems show that the method achieves decision quality within 3% of the mixed-integer linear programming optimum, reaches millisecond-level online decision times (roughly three orders of magnitude faster than conventional optimization), and produces interpretable attention maps and SHAP rankings.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10774377/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8069-8.ch011.title: Aesthetic Pedagogies and Epistemic Justice-by-Design for Embodied and Interface-Rich Learning
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8069-8.ch011.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter reconceptualises Aesthetic Pedagogy as a core infrastructure of creative technology education. It advances Epistemic Justice-by-Design and Multimodal Axiology as integrative constructs for analysing how typography, chromatics, motion, sound, haptics, avatars, dashboards, AI interfaces, and XR environments shape cognition, affect, embodiment, cultural recognition, learner agency, and participatory knowledge production. Drawing across Cognitive Load Theory, Embodied Cognition, Critical Pedagogy, Human-Computer Interaction, Design Justice, Sensory Justice, Data Justice, and Postdigital Sustainability, the chapter develops a justice-oriented framework for interface-rich and multisensory learning ecologies. It argues that creative technology must be governed through accessibility, explainability, ecological restraint, linguistic plurality, and aesthetic stewardship.</jats:p>
doi:10.4018/979-8-3373-8069-8.ch011.venue: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1882283.title: Characteristics and perceived pathways of students' informal learning experiences in highly flexible public spaces of higher education: a mixed-method study based on four universities in Zhejiang Province
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1882283.abstract: <jats:p>Against the backdrop of the paradigm shift toward a learning-centered model in higher education, flexible public spaces (FPS) in higher education institutions have emerged as critical campus venues supporting students' informal learning (IL). Existing studies have focused mostly on formal instructional contexts and objective spatial attributes, while operational quantitative assessment tools for Chinese university public spaces and integrated measurement of students' subjective learning experiences remain scarce. Employing an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design with a cross-sectional approach, this study examines the characteristics, internal associations, and subjective perceived pathways of students' IL in highly flexible FPS, based on 296 valid questionnaires and seven semi-structured interviews from four universities in Zhejiang Province. The study focuses on descriptive exploration and only examines statistical associations between variables; no causal inferences are drawn. Results show that students' overall IL experiences in highly flexible FPS are at a moderately high level, with significant positive correlations among learning satisfaction, self-efficacy and learning engagement. Qualitative analysis identifies three subjective perceptual pathways: atmospheric catalysis, autonomy enhancement, and social triggering, as well as an inherent tension between spatial openness and learning focus. These findings provide empirical references for the functional optimization of campus public spaces.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1888127.title: Gamified flipped learning and the affective domain of language learning: a qualitative case study of online English classes
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1888127.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Gamification and flipped learning have each been linked to enhanced learner engagement, but qualitative accounts of their combined, semester-long use in online language classrooms remain scarce, particularly in Indian higher education, and the affective domain is rarely examined as a central construct in its own right rather than as a by-product of achievement studies. This exploratory qualitative case study addresses this gap by examining how undergraduate students perceived the influence of gamified flipped online English instruction on the affective domain of their language learning at a university in Chennai, India, during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methodologically, an intact Foundation English cohort (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 28) received pre-class materials (videos, audio recordings, and presentation slides) and played daily in-class digital games designed on the Kahoot and LearningApps platforms over one semester; 10 students volunteered for end-of-semester, semi-structured, one-on-one interviews, and transcripts were analysed in NVivo 14 using a codebook approach to thematic analysis, proceeding through initial coding, theme development, and theme review and refinement, supported by a structured codebook and co-author consensus review of the coding. Ten themes emerged under the parent construct of the affective domain: motivation and the engaging nature of the games were the most pervasive. Participants also reported gains in self-confidence, a sense of social presence, and a preference for collaborative play, and they described boredom during uninterrupted gameplay and inconsistent use of the pre-class materials, which led them to prefer in-class conceptual explanation before playing.
