doi:10.3389/frsip.2026.1901600.title: Deep learning–based pavement crack classification and road condition assessment for intelligent transportation infrastructure
doi:10.3389/frsip.2026.1901600.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Efficient maintenance of road infrastructure is essential for ensuring traffic safety, preserving pavement serviceability, and supporting the long-term sustainability of transportation networks. However, conventional pavement inspection mainly relies on manual visual assessment, which is time-consuming, costly, and subjective. This study proposes a deep learning–based framework for automated pavement crack classification and road condition assessment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The proposed framework uses real-world pavement images collected through the Multifunctional Pavement Assessment System (SMAC). Transfer learning was applied using ResNet50 and EfficientNet-B0 architectures to classify six pavement surface categories. Data augmentation and weighted cross-entropy loss were employed to improve robustness and address class imbalance. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix analysis. A Road Condition Index (RCI) was then formulated from the classification results to support maintenance prioritization.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>EfficientNet-B0 achieved an overall classification accuracy of 89.8%, outperforming ResNet50 (73.3%). It obtained F1-scores of 0.92 for alligator and longitudinal cracks, 0.93 for transverse cracks, and 1.00 for non-cracked pavement surfaces. The proposed RCI successfully differentiated pavement degradation levels and supported maintenance prioritization.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The proposed framework provides an intelligent, interpretable, and practical solution for pavement crack classification, road condition assessment, and maintenance-oriented decision support. These results demonstrate the potential of deep learning for scalable pavement monitoring and more efficient infrastructure management within intelligent transportation systems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.2118/236954-ms.title: Machine Learning-Based Assessment of Stress-Dependent Fracture Conductivity for Improved Gas Recovery in the Marcellus Shale
doi:10.2118/236954-ms.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Fracture conductivity is not a static completion property. As reservoir pressure declines and effective closure stress increases, the proppant pack may rearrange, deform, crush, or embed into the fracture surfaces, progressively reducing the hydraulic fracture’s flow capacity. The phenomenon is particularly important in the Marcellus Shale, where stress-dependent conductivity affects both fracture performance and the reliability of long-term gas-recovery forecasts.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>This study develops a machine-learning surrogate model to predict fracture conductivity as a function of closure stress, proppant type, proppant concentration, and mesh size. A structured dataset containing 3,000 cases was generated with Predict-K. The two categorical inputs were one-hot encoded, resulting in 13 numerical inputs to the artificial neural network (ANN) while preserving the four-variable engineering representation of the problem. Feedforward networks trained with Levenberg-Marquardt and Bayesian Regularization algorithms were initially compared at a common 75-neuron architecture. Bayesian Regularization substantially improved predictive performance, reducing the testing root mean square error (RMSE) from 54.66 to 19.22 md-ft. Subsequent architecture optimization identified a 50-neuron network as the most robust configuration. The final model reproduced the Predict-K conductivity surface with a testing RMSE of 13.40 md-ft and near-perfect correlation between predicted and target values. Evaluation on an independent subset containing only 100M white-sand yielded RMSE of 7.33 md-ft.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Given the exceptionally high predictive accuracy, the modeling was subjected to a series of validation and diagnostic tests, including partition-overlap checks, duplicate screening, target-leakage analysis, stress-level holdout experiments, target shuffling, conventional-regression benchmarking, and fully random data partitions. The results indicated that ANN has successfully learned the underlying nonlinear conductivity relationships embedded in Predict K dataset. The developed ANN should therefore be regarded as a computationally efficient surrogate for the Predict-K conductivity surface within the range of conditions represented in the training data. The model can rapidly generate stress-dependent conductivity relationships for integration into reservoir simulation workflows; however, independent laboratory measurements and field-scale validation remain necessary before operational deployment. The ANN was validated as a surrogate of the Predict-K response surface rather than as an independent predictor of physical conductivity behavior.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/s10462-026-11723-2.title: Leveraging machine learning in balancing inventories and analyzing market trends: a comprehensive systematic review
doi:10.1007/s10462-026-11723-2.abstract: Rapid market changes, shorter product life cycles, and supply-chain disruptions have increased the complexity of inventory management and demand forecasting. This review examines how machine learning techniques and trend analysis improve forecasting accuracy, reduce uncertainty, and support intelligent inventory decision-making. From an initial pool of 116,377 studies, 78 papers were systematically selected for detailed analysis. The review covers supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement learning, deep learning, hybrid forecasting approaches, and emerging quantum machine learning techniques. Models such as Random Forest, XGBoost, LSTM, and Temporal Convolutional Networks are widely used for demand forecasting and inventory optimization, while reinforcement-learning methods support adaptive inventory control. The study also highlights recent advances in explainable AI, resilience-aware optimization, and sustainability-focused inventory systems, while discussing challenges related to data sparsity, explainability, and governance.

doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.6c01588.title: MARS: Machine-Learned Force Field Framework for Automated Conformational Sampling, Vibrational Spectroscopy, and Microsolvation
doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.6c01588.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We present MARS, an open-source Python package for automated conformational ensemble generation, infrared spectrum prediction, and explicit microsolvation of molecular systems. Built on JAX for GPU acceleration and automatic differentiation, MARS is carried out with machine-learned force fields (MLFFs), including SO3LR and MACE, with a four-phase conformational sampling workflow combining metadynamics, multitemperature molecular dynamics, and genetic algorithms. The package provides automated vibrational mode classification using Wilson B-matrix projections and functional group identification via graph-based pattern matching. We benchmark MARS on chemically diverse systems, including alkanes, halogenated aromatics, amino acids, peptides, drug-like molecules, phosphamides, host–guest complexes, and microsolvated biomolecular models. Semiempirical quantum-chemical methods have until now provided the practical state of the art for automated conformational sampling. Our benchmarks show that modern MLFFs can improve upon this paradigm by combining greater accuracy for high-level relative conformer energies with lower computational cost and more favorable scaling with molecular size. IR benchmarks against experimental gas-phase spectra additionally show performance comparable to quantum-chemical methods, with chemically interpretable mode assignments. Applications to alanine peptides, proline/β-cyclodextrin inclusion complexes, alanine dipeptide, and 2-methoxycyclohexanone further demonstrate that MARS captures conformational reorganization, noncovalent binding motifs, solvent-induced stability shifts, and spectroscopic signatures. These results establish MARS as a transferable and accessible platform for ensemble-based molecular modeling with machine-learned potentials. MARS is freely available at github.com/tcpunilu/mars.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1958096.title: A systematic review of DoS and DDoS attack detection in cloud environments: evolutionary trends and the emerging role of meta-learning for cross-domain adaptability
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1958096.abstract: <jats:p>Denial of Service (DoS) and Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks continue to be one of the most persistent and rapidly evolving threats to current network infrastructures as they are becoming more sophisticated and increasingly disrupting the availability, reliability and security of cloud-based systems, Software-Defined Networks (SDNs), Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems and next generation communication environments. This paper provides a systematic review of the literature on DoS and DDoS attack detection and mitigation, covering the various stages of evolutions in the field from early statistical and anomaly-based methods to adaptive machine learning and deep learning, as well as domain specific detection methods. The review, which is based on a thorough examination of 120 papers (114 primary studies and 6 supplementary studies), provides a synthesis of the latest advances in network and application-layer detection, protocol-specific detection frameworks, cloud-based intrusion detection systems, SDN-enabled programmable detection, IoT/Fog/Edge architectures, ensemble and hybrid models, transfer learning, and blockchain-based security mechanisms. A systematic review of benchmark datasets, feature engineering techniques and comparative performance shows that current deep learning systems attain almost perfect classification rates in experimental environments, but fundamental limitations in their generalizability, computational efficiency, preservation of privacy and explainability remain a constraint for their deployment in real-world environments. Importantly, this is a lot of work, but less than 6 % of the reviewed studies (seven out of 120) use meta-learning, transfer learning or few-shot approaches explicitly, which reflects the ongoing lack of capability in the field of adaptive generalization and a deficiency in addressing zero-day attacks and domain shift in dynamic cloud environments. We propose the emerging paradigm of meta-learning as the most promising one for next-generation cloud-based intrusion detection, which can be adapted to new domains with very few labeled examples — directly overcoming the three key limitations of existing approaches, namely the zero-day detection gap, domain shift limitations and label scarcity. This review offers a structured basis for researchers and practitioners designing explainable, privacy-preserving and computationally efficient detection systems and highlights the critical need for moving along the path of designing cloud-based intrusion detection systems based on meta-learning.</jats:p>

doi:10.12688/f1000research.191070.2.title: Design and expert validation of the OEPR learning model for sea turtle conservation educational tourism in Pacitan, Indonesia
doi:10.12688/f1000research.191070.2.abstract: <ns3:p>Background Sea turtle conservation sites can function as authentic learning environments, but educational visits frequently remain informal, knowledge-centred, and disconnected from sustained participation. This study developed and established the initial content validity of an experiential learning model for conservation-based educational tourism at Taman Beach, Pacitan, Indonesia. Methods An educational research-and-development study combined a preliminary needs assessment, document and literature analysis, field observation, stakeholder interviews, model design, and expert validation. Qualitative evidence was organised into six design needs. The resulting Orientation–Exploration–Practice–Reflection (OEPR) model was reviewed independently by experts in education, environmental education, and sea turtle conservation using five-point instruments covering syntax, social system, reaction principles, support system, model effects, model handbook, and facilitator guide. Scores were summarised as percentages, while written comments were analysed thematically and converted into revision decisions. Results The needs assessment identified fragmented visit sequences, mainly lecture-based interpretation, limited media, weak community coordination, no structured learner assessment, and no systematic follow-up. Eleven years of monitoring records contained 14,441 eggs and 11,892 hatchlings; annual hatching proportions varied substantially, reinforcing the need to connect education with authentic monitoring data. Expert validity was 98.33% for education, 96.94% for environmental education, and 98.24% for conservation. Reviewers retained the four-stage syntax but strengthened sense of place, inquiry, social–ecological analysis, authentic practice, standard operating procedures, safety, scaffolding, reflection, and action planning. Conclusions OEPR offers a coherent, place-based structure for transforming a conservation visit into an experiential and reflective learning cycle. The evidence supports content validity and readiness for feasibility and pilot testing, but not yet effectiveness. Subsequent studies should evaluate implementation fidelity, learner outcomes, and ecological safeguards with larger participant samples.</ns3:p>

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.470.title: Learning Community as a Dominant Predictor of Teacher Performance: The Role of Principal Transformational Leadership and Academic Supervision
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.470.abstract: <jats:p>Educational management transformation requires improving teacher performance through effective school leadership, professional collaboration, and continuous academic supervision. However, learning quality in public junior high schools in Bumiayu District, Brebes Regency, remains uneven despite the implementation of academic supervision and learning communities. This study examines the effects of transformational school leadership, learning communities, and academic supervision on teacher performance and identifies the most dominant factor. A quantitative approach with an associative ex post facto design was employed. The sample consisted of 132 teachers from public junior high schools in Bumiayu District, selected through saturated sampling. Data were collected using a validated and reliable Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed through prerequisite tests, simple and multiple regression, t-tests, and an F-test. The results show that transformational leadership significantly affects teacher performance, contributing 20.3%, while academic supervision contributes 27.3%. Learning communities have the strongest effect, with a correlation coefficient of 0.851 and a coefficient of determination of 72.4%, remaining significant in the multiple regression model. Simultaneously, the three variables significantly affect teacher performance, explaining 72.5% of its variance. These findings highlight learning communities as a strategic priority for improving teacher performance</jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.470.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.1108/978-1-83742-229-620261013.title: Insights into a Successful Online Course on Effective Pedagogies for Distributed Teaching and Learning
doi:10.1108/978-1-83742-229-620261013.abstract: <jats:p>In the Caribbean region, the need for capacity building among education stakeholders became more prominent when a series of natural disasters during the COVID-19 pandemic resulted in visible gaps in education delivery across the Caribbean. In strengthening capacity and providing opportunities for an equitable education, an online course that catered to 554 teachers in nine countries across the region was designed and implemented. This chapter explores, through a reflective leadership framework, the success of the course on ‘Effective Pedagogy in Distributed Teaching and Learning’. The decision-making processes, adjustments by facilitators, lessons learned during course development and evaluation of the course's success were carefully examined. Key themes are highlighted and discussed along with practice-based evidence from the course design, development and delivery phases. These themes were derived from reflective notes of team members, interviews, meeting transcripts, discussions and participant reflections and assignments recorded during the project. Themes were grouped into categories based on the course design and implementation processes. These included instructional and content design, technical support, tutors and participant perspectives. Themes identified were leadership, team selection, support systems, content selection, user interface design, learner support responsiveness and quality, time management, evaluation and feedback, usefulness and application of the knowledge learned in the course. Through examination of these themes, and positioning within an effective leadership and reflection framework, a model of successful online professional development is suggested. This model can inform the planning and execution of future online courses and professional development programmes within the Caribbean and similar contexts.</jats:p>
doi:10.1108/978-1-83742-229-620261013.venue: Enhancing Inclusive Practices, Teacher Development and Institutional Capacities in the Caribbean

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.443.title: The Effect of the Brainstorming Method on Creative Thinking Skills in Science and Social Studies Learning for Grade VI Students at SDN 1 Weru Lor
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.443.abstract:
<jats:p>Creative thingking skills constitute one of the essential 21-st-century competencies that need to be developed from elementary school, yet science and social studies (IPAS) instruction in the field is stilldominated by lecture method, which positons students as passive listeners. This study aims to analyze the effect of the brainstorming method on student creative thingking skill in IPAS learning for sixth-grade elementary school students. The study employed a quantitative approach with quasi-experimental design in the form of a nonequivalent control group design. The research subjects consisted of 63 sixth-grade students at SDN 1 Weru Lor, divided into a control class of 31 students receiving conventional instruction with the brainstorming method. Data were collected through an essay-based creative thingking skills test constructed from Torrance’s four indicators, namely fluenc, flexibility, originality, and elaboration, administered as a pretest and posttest, supported by teacher and student observation sheets assessing the implementation od the brainstorming method. Data analysis include descriptive statistics, the Shapiro-Wilk normality test , the Levene homogeneity test, the Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test, N-Gain analysis, Normality of N-Gain and Mann-Whitney U test. The result showed that mean pretest-posttest score of the control class increased from 59.45 to n65.68, while the experimental class increased from 63.75 to 83.09. The mean N-Gain of the control class was 16.43 % (low category), while that of the experimental class was 58.72 % (moderate category) The Mann-Whitney U test on N-Gain yielded a significancevalue of 0.000 <0.05. Thus there was significant difference in the improvement of creative thingking skills between students who received instruction using the brainstorming method and those who received conventional instruction. The brainstorming method was proven to be a viable alternative teaching method for improving students creative thingking skills in IPAS learning at elementary school level. 




 </jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.443.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.461.title: <b>The Effect of Implementing Clickable Hotspots Animated Learning Media on the Learning Outcomes of Fourth-Grade Elementary Students</b>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.461.abstract:
<jats:p>This study was motivated by students' learning outcomes that were not yet optimal and the use of learning media that tended to be conventional and less interactive. This study aimed to determine students' learning outcomes before and after the implementation of Clickable Hotspots animation learning media and to determine the effect of implementing the media on students' learning outcomes in IPAS on the material Forces Around Us. This study used a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental method and a Two Group Pretest–Posttest Design. The sample consisted of 50 students, with 25 students of class IV A as the experimental group and 25 students of class IV B as the control group. The sampling technique used was saturated sampling. Data were collected through pretest and posttest questions and student learning activity observation sheets. Data analysis used descriptive statistics, normality test, homogeneity test, Independent Samples t-Test, and N-Gain analysis. The results showed that the mean pretest score of the experimental group was 61.20, while the control group was 59.20. After the treatment, the mean posttest score of the experimental group increased to 77.80, while the control group increased to 74.20. The Independent Samples t-Test obtained a Sig. (2-tailed) value of 0.192 > 0.05, so H₀ was accepted and H₁ was rejected. The N-Gain analysis showed a mean score of 0.400 for the experimental group and 0.375 for the control group, both categorized as moderate. Therefore, the implementation of Clickable Hotspots animation learning media showed a descriptive increase in learning outcomes, but did not have a statistically significant effect on the learning outcomes of fourth-grade elementary school students.
 




 </jats:p>

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1946849.title: GraphLane: a spatio-temporal graph learning framework for lane localization
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1946849.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Lane localization is an important component of advanced driver assistance systems and autonomous driving, where accurate estimation of lane geometry is essential for safe vehicle navigation. Nevertheless, the current lane detection algorithms may face difficulties in complex driving situations due to poor visual feature extraction, unstable temporal prediction, and inadequate modeling of structural relations between lanes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In order to overcome these issues, this paper introduces the unified spatio-temporal graph learning approach that integrates spatial feature extraction, temporal context aggregation, uncertainty-driven graph formation, graph attention reasoning, and geometric optimization. The proposed GraphLane framework dynamically learns graph connections between lane keypoints while incorporating uncertainty estimation to suppress unreliable feature interactions and temporal consistency to improve structural stability across consecutive frames. A geometry-aware optimization strategy is further introduced to encourage smooth and physically consistent lane predictions. The framework was evaluated on the CULane test set using the proposed row-anchor-based lane-existence and localization evaluation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Experimental results show that the proposed GraphLane framework achieves a lane-existence precision of 0.9769, recall of 0.8990, F1-score of 0.9363, and an average localization error of 19.28 pixels. Qualitative analysis shows that the framework produces smooth and consistent lane predictions under occlusions, shadows, dense traffic, and nighttime conditions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Other analyses on learned graphs, computational complexity, and ablation studies also show that incorporating temporal context, adaptive graph reasoning, and geometrically informed optimizations is effective for lane localization.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1097/cu9.0000000000000380.title: From data to decisions: Machine learning applications in kidney transplantation management
doi:10.1097/cu9.0000000000000380.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Kidney transplantation (KT) is a complex clinical process requiring accurate risk stratification, timely decision-making, and individualized management across all stages of care. Traditional clinical scores and center-specific algorithms often fail to capture the multidimensional interactions among donor, recipient, and procedural factors. In this context, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as promising tools to support precision medicine in KT.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials and Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted a narrative review of the literature published between 2010 and 2024, focusing on AI and ML applications in KT. Studies addressing pretransplant evaluation, surgical assistance, posttransplant outcomes, and immunosuppressive therapy optimization were included and qualitatively synthesized.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Artificial intelligence and ML models have demonstrated improved performance compared with conventional approaches across multiple stages of KT. In the pretransplant setting, ML-based models outperform traditional risk scores in donor–recipient matching and graft survival prediction, with the potential to reduce organ discard. Deep learning techniques applied to preimplantation biopsies enhance histopathologic assessment and reproducibility. Intraoperatively, AI-driven imaging and surgical data science tools support anatomic visualization and decision-making. Posttransplant, ML models enable earlier detection of acute rejection, prediction of delayed graft function, and noninvasive assessment using laboratory, imaging, and molecular data. Furthermore, AI-based pharmacokinetic models facilitate personalized immunosuppressive dosing, improving time within therapeutic ranges and reducing toxicity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Artificial intelligence represents a powerful adjunct to clinical expertise in KT, offering data-driven decision support across the transplant continuum. However, most available models remain retrospective and lack prospective multicenter validation, limiting immediate clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter studies and responsible implementation strategies are essential to translate AI-driven tools into routine clinical practice and improve transplant outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.61435/ijred.2026.61916.title: Enhance EV station charge and discharge based on deep learning forecasting method incorporating renewable energy sources and multi-objective optimization algorithm
doi:10.61435/ijred.2026.61916.abstract: <jats:p>As electric vehicle charging station operations become more common, proper coordination of energy management is necessary to avoid high operational costs and carbon emissions caused by electric vehicle charging requirements, intermittent renewable sources, and fluctuating electricity rates. In this research, a forecast-based optimization methodology is created with the objective of optimizing the charge-discharge management of a renewable-powered electric vehicle charging station system involving photovoltaic generation, wind generation, fuel cells, electric vehicles, and stationary batteries. First, a recurrent neural network is used to predict relevant time series data, such as photovoltaic energy, wind energy, electric vehicle load demand, fuel cell energy production, and electric vehicle energy consumption. These forecasted data are then applied to a bi-objective energy management optimization problem, which is solved using NSGA-II. The objective is to minimize operating cost and  emissions while considering power balance, grid energy exchange, and other operational constraints associated with the fuel cell, battery storage system, and electric vehicles. In this study, two scenarios are examined using one month of hourly data; Scenario 1 does not use stationary batteries, whereas Scenario 2 uses them. The forecasting results show robust predictions, with one-hour-ahead  values ranging from 0.9162 to 0.9708. The optimization results show that Scenario 2 provides better energy shifting and peak-period support through battery charging and discharging management. Compared with Scenario 1, the operating cost is reduced from $171,833.86 to $160,388.44, and  emissions are decreased from 13,485.48 kg to 12,892.23 kg, leading to 6.7% and 4.4% reductions, respectively.</jats:p>
doi:10.61435/ijred.2026.61916.venue: International Journal of Renewable Energy Development

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.451.title: Implementation of Technical Standard Operating Procedures in Teaching Factory for Developing Vocational High School Students’ Work Readiness in Accordance with Industry Standards
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.451.abstract: <jats:p>The gap between vocational high school (SMK) graduates' competencies and industry demands remains a structural challenge in Indonesian vocational education. This study aims to describe the effectiveness of implementing Technical Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) within the Teaching Factory (TEFA) program at SMK Canda Bhirawa Pare in developing students' work readiness in accordance with industry standards. A mixed method approach with a Sequential Explanatory design was employed, involving 40 respondents comprising TEFA students, supervising teachers, and alumni. Data were collected through questionnaires and semi-structured interviews. The findings indicate that the implementation of TEFA technical SOPs is highly effective with both primary variables classified under the highly effective category in fostering work discipline, responsibility, procedural compliance, and the internalization of industrial work culture among students. Convergent quantitative and qualitative data confirm that technical SOPs function not merely as operational guidelines, but as a systematic instructional instrument for developing students' professional character. This study concludes that the integration of industry-standard SOPs into TEFA programs substantially bridges the competency gap between SMK graduates and industry expectations, with practical implications for the sustainable development of Teaching Factory programs in vocational education.</jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.451.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11439866/v1.title: Physics-guided auxiliary multi-task learning for temperature-dependent thermoelectric 𝑧𝑇 curve prediction
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11439866/v1.abstract: Temperature-dependent thermoelectric performance is central to materials screening because the magnitude and position of the 𝑧𝑇(𝑇) maximum determine the useful operating window. We develop a 𝑧𝑇-prioritized, physics-guided auxiliary multi-task framework that predicts thermoelectric property curves from composition and temperature. The framework combines Magpie descriptors, Fourier temperature encoding, joint prediction of the Seebeck coefficient 𝑆, electrical conductivity 𝜎, thermal conductivity 𝜅, power factor 𝑃𝐹, and figure of merit 𝑧𝑇, high-𝑧𝑇 reweighting, staged optimization, dynamic physical regularization, and curve smoothing. The curated dataset contains 4222 observations from 755 formula-defined materials and 270 elemental systems over 275–1275 K. The ten-seed ensemble gives training-set 𝑅2 = 0.9563 for 𝑃𝐹 and 𝑅2 = 0.9405for𝑧𝑇;material-grouped out-of-fold evaluation gives 𝑅2 = 0.8927 for 𝑃𝐹 and 𝑅2 = 0.8765 for 𝑧𝑇, with 𝑧𝑇 MAE = 0.0764 and RMSE = 0.1166. The model reproduces temperature-dependent responses across the measured ranges of representative materials. External validation on four literature-derived materials and 24 points gives 𝑅2 = 0.9755, MAE = 0.0128, and RMSE = 0.0198. The resulting composition-based workflow supports candidate ranking and operating-window selection through coupled property prediction and soft physical supervision.

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.512.title: Examining the Effects of Digital Service and Customer Experience on Hotel Guest Satisfaction: A Quantitative Study at Whiz Prime Hotel Padang
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.512.abstract: <jats:p>This research is grounded in the importance of digital services and customer experience in enhancing hotel guest satisfaction. This study aims to determine the influence of digital services and customer experience on guest satisfaction at Whiz Prime Hotel Padang. This research used a quantitative approach with a causal associative method. The sample consisted of 150 respondents selected using purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics 27. The results showed that Digital Service had a positive and significant effect on Guest Stay Satisfaction, with a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05. Customer Experience also had a positive and significant effect on Guest Stay Satisfaction, with a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05. Simultaneously, Digital Service and Customer Experience had a positive and significant effect on Guest Stay Satisfaction. Based on the Standardized Beta value, Digital Service had a more dominant effect than Customer Experience. These findings indicate that improving the quality of digital services and providing positive guest experiences can support higher guest satisfaction during their stay.</jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.512.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.523.title: Blended Learning-Based Pancasila Education: Spaces for Practice and Reflection
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.523.abstract: <jats:p>Civic and Pancasila Education tends to emphasize value understanding as a primary learning outcome, while the connection between reflection and value practice in blended learning remains insufficiently explained. This study analyzes students’ reported experiences, reflection, meaning-making, and practice of Pancasila values in blended learning. The study employed reflexive thematic analysis of 871 response units from 67 students at Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia, comprising 47 Elementary School Teacher Education students and 20 Accounting Education students, based on 13 open-ended narrative questions. The analysis identified five categories: learning experiences and self-regulation; social interaction and value practice; value understanding, reflection, and application; contexts and challenges of value practice; and implications for learning design. The findings indicate differentiated pedagogical functions between online and face-to-face spaces. Online spaces primarily supported reflection and self-regulation, whereas face-to-face spaces provided contexts for value practice through interaction, deliberation, and collaboration. Tensions between Pancasila values and social realities also formed part of the experiences that prompted further reflection and meaning-making. These findings are synthesized to explain the relationship between reflective and practical spaces within students’ blended learning experiences.</jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.523.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.1108/sup-02-2025-0005.title: Supporting novice teachers for deeper learning through a school–university partnership
doi:10.1108/sup-02-2025-0005.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study was conducted to examine how a school and a university partnered to support a cohort of beginner teachers who graduated from the same teacher education program and taught in the same school. Deeper learning principles served as a framework for understanding their experiences during the two-year induction support program.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This qualitative study collected and analyzed data from five novice teachers over a two-year period. The data included interviews and transcriptions from new teacher support sessions. Data were analyzed by the author and a team of doctoral students. The new teacher sessions were based on Babinski and Rogers' (2002) model of teacher support.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results showed that the new teacher support program helped novice teachers feel more confident and prepared using deeper learning principles. The teachers reported increased collaboration, practical problem-solving skills and stronger professional relationships because of participating in the program.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This article examines a school–university partnership that supported novice teachers through a cohort-based induction model grounded in deeper learning principles. The limitations and implications of this study are also discussed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1962940.title: The influencing factors of postoperative sleep disturbance in elderly patients undergoing transurethral prostate surgery and the construction and validation of a machine learning prediction model
doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1962940.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Postoperative sleep disturbance (POSD) is a common complication in elderly patients undergoing transurethral prostate surgery, which impairs recovery and increases disease burden. To date, prediction models for POSD in this population, particularly those based on machine learning techniques, remain scarce.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To investigate the incidence and influencing factors of POSD in elderly patients undergoing transurethral prostate surgery, and to construct prediction models based on conventional logistic regression and seven machine learning algorithms.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A total of 563 elderly patients who underwent elective transurethral prostate surgery at our hospital between March 2024 and December 2025 were prospectively enrolled and randomly divided into a training set (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 338) and a validation set (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 225) at a ratio of 6:4. LASSO regression (with lambda.1se) was used to screen predictive variables, and multivariate logistic regression to identify independent risk factors. Logistic regression, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), naive Bayes, decision tree, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbors, and artificial neural network models were constructed. Model performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was employed for interpretability analysis of the optimal model.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The incidence of POSD was 62.2%. Independent risk factors included preoperative anxiety (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-Anxiety [HADS-A] score), nocturia frequency (≥3 times/night), elevated systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), preoperative noise score, and moderate-to-severe cough-related pain (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.05). The random forest model demonstrated the best overall performance, with an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.89–0.96) in the training set and 0.964 (95% CI: 0.93–0.99) in the validation set, and exhibited superior calibration and clinical utility compared with the other models. SHAP analysis revealed that the HADS-A score contributed the most to the predictions.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Preoperative anxiety, increased nocturia frequency (≥3 times/night), elevated SII, high noise score, and moderate-to-severe cough-related pain are independent risk factors for POSD in elderly patients undergoing transurethral prostate surgery. The random forest prediction model exhibits optimal performance and can be used for early clinical risk identification and individualized intervention.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Clinical trial registration</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2600124377.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/fsurg.2026.1987508.title: Machine learning model with post-hoc SHAP interpretation based on perioperative clinical and imaging parameters for prediction of 1-year radiographic recurrence after hallux valgus surgery
doi:10.3389/fsurg.2026.1987508.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Radiographic recurrence after hallux valgus surgery is an important issue affecting long-term imaging outcomes. Previous studies have suggested that preoperative deformity, postoperative residual HVA/IMA, and sesamoid reduction are associated with recurrence, but nonlinear relationships may exist among multiple parameters. The aim of this study was to establish and temporally validate a machine learning prediction model based on conventional perioperative clinical and imaging parameters and to provide
                      <jats:italic>post-hoc</jats:italic>
                      model interpretation using SHAP.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      597 patients undergoing hallux valgus surgery in the Department of Trauma, First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University from 2021 to 2025 were retrospectively enrolled. Radiographic recurrence was defined as HVA &gt;20° on the fixed 12-month postoperative weight-bearing anteroposterior radiograph. Patients operated from 2021 to 2023 formed the development cohort (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                      =389), and patients operated from 2024 to 2025 formed the independent temporal-validation cohort (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                      =208). Eighteen candidate predictors were screened in the development cohort using collinearity assessment, LASSO, RFE, and permutation importance. A unified eight-feature set was then locked and used for comparison of LR, RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, and SVM using 5-fold outer/3-fold inner nested cross-validation conditional on the fixed feature set. Models were evaluated using ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Brier score, calibration, and DCA, with
                      <jats:italic>post-hoc</jats:italic>
                      SHAP-based interpretation of the final SVM.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 109 patients met the 1-year radiographic recurrence criterion (18.3%). Eight variables were retained: age, preoperative HVA, preoperative IMA, preoperative DMAA, 6-week postoperative HVA, 6-week postoperative IMA, 6-week postoperative DMAA, and 6-week postoperative sesamoid grade. The development-cohort ROC-AUCs of LR and SVM were 0.908 and 0.906, respectively, with corresponding PR-AUCs of 0.766 and 0.757. SVM was retained as the final model on the basis of its lower Brier score and overall performance profile, without claiming statistical superiority over LR. In the temporal-validation cohort, SVM ROC-AUC was 0.944 (95% CI 0.908–0.973), PR-AUC 0.805, Brier score 0.071, sensitivity 0.892, and specificity 0.842. SHAP showed the largest model contributions for 6-week IMA, HVA, and sesamoid grade.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The SVM model with
                      <jats:italic>post-hoc</jats:italic>
                      SHAP-based interpretation showed promising performance for prediction of fixed 1-year radiographic recurrence using routine clinical and perioperative imaging parameters. Residual IMA, HVA, and sesamoid grade at 6 weeks were leading predictive signals within the model rather than causal determinants of recurrence. The model may support early risk stratification and enhanced follow-up, but multicenter external validation, reproducibility assessment, and prospective impact studies remain necessary before clinical implementation.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.231.title: STRENGTHENING DIGITAL CITIZENSHIP COMPETENCIES OF PPKn MASTER STUDENTS AS PROSPECTIVE UMKM ENTREPRENEURS: A LEGAL-NORMATIVE REVIEW AND ACTUALIZATION OF PANCASILA ECONOMICS
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.231.abstract:
<jats:p>Digital transformation has reshaped citizenship, higher education, and MSME entrepreneurship in Indonesia. In this context, Master’s students of Pancasila and Civic Education should no longer be positioned merely as prospective educators or academics, but also as digital citizens with the potential to become actors of people-centered entrepreneurship grounded in Pancasila values. The state has established a regulatory framework for the facilitation, protection, and empowerment of MSMEs, including the strengthening of the digital ecosystem; however, digital literacy, digital ethics, legal awareness, and social justice orientation remain substantive challenges (Government of the Republic of Indonesia, 2021; Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs of the Republic of Indonesia, n.d.; “Transformasi Digital UMKM Indonesia,” n.d.).
This study aims to analyze a model for strengthening the digital citizenship competence of Master’s students in Pancasila and Civic Education as prospective MSME entrepreneurs through a juridical-normative approach and the perspective of Pancasila economics. The study employs qualitative library research with juridical-normative, philosophical, and conceptual approaches. Data were collected through document studies of legislation, recent academic publications, institutional reports, and relevant scholarly articles, and were analyzed using content analysis and thematic interactive analysis.
The findings show that strengthening digital citizenship competence among Master’s students in Pancasila and Civic Education should be constructed through four integrated dimensions: digital-regulatory literacy, digital ethical-participatory capacity, digital social entrepreneurship capacity, and a Pancasila-based economic justice orientation. From the normative perspective, the national legal framework has opened legal and institutional space for MSME digitalization, yet it has not been fully translated into postgraduate civic education designs that prepare students as sovereign, responsible, and justice-oriented actors in the digital economy. This study offers a novelty by reconstructing digital citizenship competence not merely as the ability to use digital media safely and ethically, but as a form of civic-economic competence that connects digital rights, constitutional responsibilities, business legal compliance, and the praxis of people-centered economy in digital spaces (“Strengthening Citizenship Skills,” n.d.; “Strategi Penerapan Ekonomi Pancasila,” n.d.; “Implementasi Pancasila dalam Kebijakan Ekonomi,” n.d.; Government of the Republic of Indonesia, 2021; Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs of the Republic of Indonesia, n.d.).
The study concludes that Master’s students in Pancasila and Civic Education occupy a strategic position as agents of civic entrepreneurship reform who can bridge civic education, economic law, and national MSME empowerment. The implications point to the need for curriculum reformulation, stronger campus policies, and the development of a Pancasila-based digital civic entrepreneurship learning ecosystem.</jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.231.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.1108/gkmc-06-2025-0480.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning for meta data management in libraries: a computational analysis
doi:10.1108/gkmc-06-2025-0480.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study explores the growth, trends and patterns of scholarly research by using bibliometric and computational methods. This study aims to identify prolific authors, influential journals, collaborative networks and emerging themes. This paper offers insights into how Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are transforming metadata practices to enhance information organisation, retrieval and interoperability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A structured three-phase methodology was adopted. At first, appropriate keywords were identified, and the required data was extracted from the Scopus database (2010–2024) using a Boolean search string. Of 3,624 records, 3,424 articles were found relevant after removal of irrelevant articles manually. Software such as Biblioshiny and VOSviewer were used to analyse the trends in publication, citation patterns, co-occurrence of keywords and the collaborative patterns. Social Network Analysis was applied to map the co-authorship patterns, collaboration at institutional and country levels.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results of this study indicate steady growth in AI and ML research in library metadata, though citation impact has declined since 2018. Kanwal Ameen is the most productive author, and the USA is the most productive country. Dominance by a few journals and authors aligns with Bradford’s and Lotka’s Laws. The collaboration pattern remains limited among authors and countries. Thematic evolution shows a shift from traditional metadata access to intelligent technologies like AI, ML and IoT. Regional collaborations are stronger than author-level links, and recent trends align with broader digital transformation</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first known study to comprehensively examine AI and ML applications in library metadata management through computational bibliometric analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1108/dlo-06-2026-0308.title: The hidden learning cost of generative AI: the THINK framework for preserving critical thinking in AI-enabled workplaces
doi:10.1108/dlo-06-2026-0308.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This paper examines how regular use of generative AI enhances productivity, but somehow, in contrast, reduces the opportunities for employees to utilize critical thinking skills and translate their hands-on experience into organizational learning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper is a problem-based conceptual synthesis linking AI literacy, organizational learning, human-AI collaboration, evidence from knowledge workers, and knowledge collapse theory. On the other hand, human-AI augmentation and disengagement are considered opposing risks from which five workplace safeguards are derived.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper shows that the issue is not the use of GenAI, but organizations that reward flawless automation output while ignoring verification, human reasoning, and visible employee learning. The paper introduces the THINK framework interlinking organizational practices: Transparency, Human judgment, Intellectual engagement, Navigation of evidence and Knowledge construction.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The THINK framework conceptual synthesis is selective and not empirically tested. Future research should validate the application effect across different sectors, industries and levels of GenAI adoption.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The THINK framework can be integrated into employee training, performance management discussions, decision-making and AI governance systems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper transposes the traditional argument about GenAI-mediated cognition into a simple, auditable framework that managers can apply on the job as coaches, learning professionals, and AI governance teams.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11136078/v1.title: Physics-Residual Learning with Few-Shot Calibration for Cross-Geological UCS Prediction: A Model-Agnostic Framework
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11136078/v1.abstract: Forecasting Uniaxial Compressive Strength (UCS) across geologically varied landscapes poses difficulties, since data-centric models developed on localized datasets often falter when applied to unfamiliar geological areas. This research assesses the cross-geological applicability of UCS predictions via a Leave-One-Country-Out methodology across six nations and 397 rock specimens, contrasting solely data-driven models with a physics-based residual technique among four foundational modules. Zero-shot outcomes indicate a significant compromise: Direct ML attained a slightly reduced initial RMSE (58.5 MPa) compared to Physics-Residual (60.2 MPa), however this benefit concealed significant instability, since single-sample calibration unexpectedly heightened error. Physics anchoring converted extrapolation inaccuracies into systematic, interpretable biases grounded on physical principles. We provide a Calibratability Index (CI) that measures the proportion of the domain gap bridged using five calibration samples; Physics-Residual attained a CI of 0.511 compared to 0.364 for Direct ML. Diversity-oriented active sampling using non-invasive Vp and density assessments decreased RMSE to 37.7 MPa at k = 3 and 36.8 MPa at k = 5, indicating a 17% enhancement compared to random sampling. The Wilcoxon tests validated significance (p < 10⁻⁸) with moderate effect sizes (Cohen's d = − 0.53 to − 0.58). Geological Bias Correction multipliers varied from 0.36 in Turkey to 5.60 in South Africa, indicating that cross-domain error is organized and geologically significant. Feature engineering yielded no enhancement compared to the original predictors, affirming the notion of parsimony for datasets with few samples. The methodology is independent of models and facilitates a decrease of over 90% in destructive testing needs, creating an effective process for dependable UCS forecasting in new geological contexts.

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.471.title: <b>Application of Maqashid Al-Syariah in Dispute Resolution of Sharia Mortgage Default at BSI KCP Makassar Veteran</b>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.471.abstract: <jats:p>Sharia Home Ownership Credit (KPR) financing plays a role in meeting the community's housing needs, but its implementation has the potential to cause default disputes when customers are unable to meet their installment obligations. Dispute resolution is not only oriented towards receivables recovery, because housing is a basic need for family sustainability. This study aims to analyze the factors causing defaults, dispute resolution mechanisms, and the application of Maqashid al-Syariah in resolving sharia mortgage defaults at BSI KCP Makassar Veteran. The research uses a qualitative field design with a sociolegal approach. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and documentation, then analyzed interactively through data condensation, data presentation, and conclusion drawn. The results of the study showed that defaults were mainly influenced by irregular income, business decline, termination of employment, illness, urgent needs, family problems, and uncooperative behavior of customers. Settlement is carried out in stages through persuasive communication, deliberation, restructuring in the form of rescheduling, reconditioning, and restructuring, formal warnings, and the sale of collateral, auction, or legal channels as the last option. These practices reflect the application of hifz al-din, hifz al-nafs, hifz al-aql, hifz al-nasl, and hifz al-mal. The research concludes that the BSI KCP Makassar Veteran mechanism leads to a balance between contract certainty, bank asset protection, customer protection, and family benefits. Its effectiveness requires verification of ability to pay, documentation, two-way communication, and proportional decisions in each case in a transparent, fair, and sustainable manner</jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.471.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.58602/itsecs.v4i4.416.title: Klasterisasi Kabupaten/Kota di Provinsi Jawa Barat Berdasarkan Profil Indikator Kesehatan dan Sosial-Demografi Menggunakan Machine Learning
doi:10.58602/itsecs.v4i4.416.abstract: <jats:p>Disparities in regional health status remain a major challenge for data-driven public health planning in Indonesia. This study aims to develop a machine learning-based clustering approach to group 27 regencies/cities in West Java Province according to the similarity of their health and socio-demographic indicator profiles using open government data. The research follows the CRISP-DM framework, from business understanding to deployment. Five of nine indicators were converted into population-based and live-birth-based rates to remove the confounding effect of regional size differences, then selected using variance thresholding and Spearman correlation, resulting in eight final features. Five clustering algorithms were compared: K-Means, K-Medoids (PAM), DBSCAN, Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering, and Fuzzy C-Means (FCM), with the optimal number of clusters determined through the Elbow Method and Silhouette Analysis. The results indicate k=6 as the optimal number of clusters, with K-Means, K-Medoids, and Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering producing identical and best cluster quality (Silhouette Index 0.289; Davies-Bouldin Index 0.978; Calinski-Harabasz Index 9.52), outperforming Fuzzy C-Means (0.184), while DBSCAN failed to form meaningful clusters due to the relatively homogeneous density distribution of the data. Cluster profiles revealed significant disparities, particularly in doctor ratio, proper sanitation, and access to proper water sources: the Bekasi-Depok cluster showed the most favorable profile, while the small-city cluster (Sukabumi, Tasikmalaya, Banjar, Cirebon) showed the highest infant and maternal mortality rates despite relatively adequate health infrastructure. This study provides a methodological contribution as a foundation for developing an open-data-based regional health and socio-demographic indicator mapping system to support more targeted regional health policy.</jats:p>

doi:10.15294/upej.v15i2.31899.title: Physical Analysis of a Fishing Rod and Development of an Elasticity E-Module as a Supplement for Mechanics Learning
doi:10.15294/upej.v15i2.31899.abstract: <jats:p>Mechanics instruction at the university level, particularly for students in the Physics and Physics Education study programs, is often hindered by the abstract nature of the content, complex formulas, and unengaging modes of delivery. A preliminary study showed that 83.3% of students found mechanics difficult to understand, partly because of the limited variety of learning media. One interesting topic in mechanics is the dynamics of elastic bodies, including fishing rods. These dynamics involve numerous physical concepts and complex mathematical equations, so an enrichment module is needed to facilitate students’ understanding. This study aimed to develop an elasticity e-module as a supplement for mechanics learning, focusing on the analysis of the curvature of a fishing rod (an elastic rod) and a comparison of the acceleration multiplication factor between elastic and non-elastic rods subjected to a force impulse. This study used a Research and Development (R&D) approach with the 4D development model (Define, Design, Develop, Disseminate). The physical analysis was conducted theoretically and experimentally on tapered elastic rods. In the curvature experiment, the load was varied, whereas in the acceleration experiment, the acceleration response was observed using the accelerometer sensor of a smartphone. The developed e-module was validated by subject-matter and media experts and tested with students as users. The validation results showed that the e-module was categorized as “very feasible” in both content and media aspects. Meanwhile, students’ responses fell into the “very good” category for material presentation (90.53%), language (91.58%), visual display (88.84%), usefulness (91.89%), technical aspects (91.75%), and evaluation (90.53%). Therefore, the elasticity e-module is feasible for use as a supplement in Mechanics courses. </jats:p>

doi:10.33687/ijef.003.04.00169.title: Operational Readiness for AI Driven Learning: Examining the Inter-play of Self-Assessed Competence, Usage Patterns and Trust
doi:10.33687/ijef.003.04.00169.abstract: <jats:p>Since the release of generative AI systems in autumn 2022, AI use in academic contexts has gained relevance worldwide. Developing AI-related competencies has emerged as an educational task within the field of learning technologies aimed at enhancing learning outcomes. Against this background, the DigiTaKS*-project investigates how usage patterns, trust in AI, and self-assessed AI compe-tencies are interrelated and how these factors influence students’ operational readiness to integrate AI-driven applications into their learning processes. We frame this presented approach as an idea that can be adapted to different regions and educational systems. This contribution presents findings from a questionnaire study conducted among bachelor’s students in Humanities and Social Sciences at a German university (N = 70). Results indicate that usage, trust, and self-assessed AI competence are closely intertwined and significantly predict opera-tional readiness to integrate AI into academic learning processes. These findings highlight the need for structured educational approaches that systematically foster these interrelated dimensions. In response, the Open Educational Resource (OER) “ComDigiS*” was developed within the project DigiTaKS* to systematically promote reflective, competence-oriented, and equitable AI integration in academic contexts. It conceptualizes AI as a form of machine intelligence and supports in-teracting with AI across different cognitive levels from understanding and apply-ing to critically reflecting thereby fostering a holistic set of AI-use competencies for students. However, the paper presents student AI practices based on ques-tionnaire results and the Open Educational Resource ComDigiS* for promoting (AI) competence development.  Grounded in a European setting, the study pro-poses an approach intended for context-sensitive adaptation across diverse edu-cational systems. While the study is grounded in a European higher-education context, it explicitly acknowledges the situatedness of its concepts. This opens a perspective on how the proposed heuristic can be adapted to diverse educational settings across regions, such as educational contexts across the African conti-nent.</jats:p>

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.407.title: <b>Teacher Performance in Relation to School Culture and Principal Leadership Style</b><b><sup></sup></b>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.407.abstract:
<jats:p>This study aims to evaluate the influence of school organizational culture and principal leadership style on teacher performance at SD Negeri 2 Rawalaut, both partially and simultaneously. Quantitative methods were used in this study, which were designed as a correlational survey. This study is a population study (total sampling) because all teachers at SD Negeri 2 Rawalaut, totaling 35 people. The tool used was a questionnaire with a five-choice Likert scale, which was tested for validity and reliability. Multiple linear regression analysis was used with the help of Jamovi version 2.7.24, which was preceded by prerequisite tests for normality, linearity, heteroscedasticity, and multicollinearity. The results of the study show that: (1) The principal's leadership style has a positive and significant impact on teacher performance, with a calculated t value greater than t table (3.45 greater than 2.034) and a significance of 0.002 less than 0.05; (2) School organizational culture has a positive and significant impact on teacher performance, with a calculated t value greater than t table (2.85 greater than 2.034) and a significance of 0.007 less than 0.05; and (3) Principal leadership style. Other variables outside this study influence 62.8% of the total, with a calculated F value greater than F table (9.48 greater than 3.285) and a contribution (R2) of 37.2%. These results indicate that improving school culture and improving the quality of principal leadership are two successful methods for improving teacher performance.




 </jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.407.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.446.title: <b>The Effect of Wordwall-Assisted STAD Cooperative Learning Model to Improve Students' Problem-Solving Ability in Two-Variable Linear Equation Systems for Grade VIII Students at SMP St. Yoseph Medan</b>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.446.abstract:
<jats:p>This study aims to determine the effect of the Student Teams Achievement Division (STAD) cooperative learning model assisted by Wordwall on the mathematical problem-solving abilities of eighth-grade students of St. Yoseph Catholic Private Junior High School Medan in the 2025/2026 Academic Year and the improvement of students' mathematical problem-solving abilities after the model is implemented. This study uses a quantitative approach with the Pre-Experimental Design method using the One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. The research sample consisted of 36 students. Data analysis used normality tests, Paired Sample t-Test, and N-Gain. The results showed that the average pretest score of 50.806 increased to 80.167 in the posttest. The results of the hypothesis test obtained tₕᵢₜᵤₙg = 53.303 and tₜₐᵦₑₗ = 2.030, so that H₀ was rejected and Hₐ was accepted. The N-Gain test results obtained an average of 0.611, categorized as moderate. Thus, it can be concluded that the Student Teams Achievement Division (STAD) cooperative learning model assisted by Wordwall has a significant effect and is able to improve students' mathematical problem-solving abilities.




 </jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.446.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.485.title: Improving Students' Science Learning Outcomes Through the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) Model Assisted by Canva and Quizizz Media in Fifth-Grade at SDN 3 Tabongo
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.485.abstract: <jats:p>Masalah dalam penelitian ini adalah rendahnya hasil belajar murid pada mata pelajaran IPA kelas V di SDN 3 Tabongo. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk meningkatkan hasil belajar murid melalui penerapan model Problem Based Learning (PBL) berbantuan media Canva dan Quizizz pada mata pelajaran IPA materi Cahaya dan Sifat-Sifat Cahaya. Jenis penelitian ini adalah Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) yang dilaksanakan dalam dua siklus. Teknik pengumpulan data yang digunakan meliputi observasi, wawancara, tes, dan dokumentasi. Berdasarkan hasil observasi awal diketahui bahwa hasil belajar murid masih rendah. Pada pelaksanaan tindakan Siklus I, murid yang mencapai ketuntasan belajar sebanyak 2 orang (10%), sedangkan 18 orang (90%) belum mencapai ketuntasan sesuai KKTP. Hasil tersebut belum memenuhi indikator keberhasilan yang telah ditetapkan sehingga penelitian dilanjutkan ke Siklus II. Setelah dilakukan perbaikan pembelajaran melalui penerapan model Problem Based Learning (PBL) berbantuan media Canva dan Quizizz, hasil belajar murid mengalami peningkatan yang signifikan. Pada Siklus II, jumlah murid yang mencapai ketuntasan belajar meningkat menjadi 18 orang (90%), sedangkan 2 orang (10%) belum mencapai ketuntasan. Dengan demikian, indikator keberhasilan penelitian telah tercapai, yaitu minimal 90% murid memperoleh nilai sesuai KKTP (≥75). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penerapan model Problem Based Learning (PBL) berbantuan media Canva dan Quizizz efektif dalam meningkatkan hasil belajar murid pada materi Cahaya dan Sifat-Sifat Cahaya.</jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.485.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.24256/iqro.v9i3.12421.title: ChatGPT as a Supporting Medium for Islamic Religious Education: Strengthening Students’ Learning Experience and Academic Integrity
doi:10.24256/iqro.v9i3.12421.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly ChatGPT, offers opportunities to enhance learning while raising concerns about academic integrity. This study examines the role of ChatGPT in Islamic Religious Education (IRE) and formulates strategies to preserve students’ academic integrity. Using a qualitative library research approach, it analyzes scientific articles, books, policy documents, and other credible sources on generative AI, IRE, learning autonomy, and academic integrity through content analysis and thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that ChatGPT can improve access to learning resources, support independent learning, clarify complex concepts, and provide preliminary feedback. However, excessive reliance may encourage plagiarism, weaken critical thinking, reduce originality, and produce inaccurate information. Six complementary strategies are proposed: institutional policies, academic guidelines, cultivation of academic honesty, higher-order thinking tasks (C4–C6), authentic performance-based assessment, and contextual and problem-based learning. These strategies position ChatGPT as a supporting tool rather than a substitute for students’ intellectual processes, and its outputs must be critically verified against credible scholarly sources. The study concludes that the educational value of ChatGPT in IRE depends on sound pedagogical design and a strong ethical framework. Because the framework is a conceptual synthesis of the literature, it has not been empirically validated and should be tested in future research.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11444038/v1.title: STEP-VERIFIER: Learning to Verify Intermediate Agent Behavior with Process Reward Models
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11444038/v1.abstract: Large language model agents complete tasks through long sequences of tool calls, yet most training signals only indicate whether the entire attempt succeeded. We explore whether a separate verifier can learn to judge the quality of individual actions before an episode finishes. Our system, STEP-VERIFIER, scores each environment-observation and action pair instead of whole trajectories. It is trained on automatically synthesized comparisons distilled from a success-labeled corpus of logged interactions: Monte-Carlo return differences between states sharing a common prefix yield pairwise supervision, and a Bradley-Terry ranking head converts these pairs into calibrated per-action scores. While the policy is being learned, the verifier filters low-quality interaction logs before each update and provides dense intermediate feedback that is annealed toward zero as training progresses, so the final policy never relies on the verifier at deployment. Using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct backbones, STEP-VERIFIER outperforms training from final scores alone across GAIA, ToolBench, and AgentBoard, and its per-action scores align substantially better with human judgments than trajectory-level scoring baselines.
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11444038/v1.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1949960.title: IFI-ML: a novel framework combining Fuzzy Inference and Machine Learning for Parkinson's disease classification
doi:10.3389/frai.2026.1949960.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Early detection of Parkinson's Disease (PD) remains challenging due to vocal signal complexity and severe data imbalance, which necessitates that machine learning (ML) models deliver higher classification accuracy. This study aims to break the systematic, inverse trade-off between sensitivity and specificity in voice-based PD classification. We present the Intelligent Fuzzy Inference and Machine Learning (IFI-ML) framework, an uncertainty-aware architecture utilizing entropy-based partitioning, hybrid classifiers, and a Sugeno Type-2 Fuzzy Inference System (FIS). While traditional frameworks apply global resampling techniques such as the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) or Random Over-Sampling (ROS) across entire datasets, the proposed IFI-ML framework utilizes information gain-driven clustering to segment samples into sensitive (uncertain boundary) and non-sensitive partitions. The framework optimizes conventional ML classifiers on the stable, non-sensitive clusters, while routing critical boundary samples to the Type-2 FIS to handle local class overlap without distorting the overall data distribution. We evaluated our framework on two public, imbalanced datasets from the University of California, Irvine (UCI) Machine Learning repository: Parkinson's voice Dataset 1 (
                    <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    ) and Dataset 2 (
                    <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ). The proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 97% on
                    <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    and 92.17% on
                    <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    , while simultaneously raising specificity to 94-95% on
                    <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    and 75-88% on
                    <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    . The Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) improves to 0.93 and 0.77, respectively. Furthermore, IFI-ML reduces false-positive and false-negative rates to 3-7% on
                    <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>1</jats:sub>
                    across all classifiers, and limits false-positive rates to 11-12% for the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) model on
                    <jats:italic>D</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    . Under a rigorous 10-fold cross-validation (10 CV) scheme, the framework consistently outperforms 15 baseline machine learning models. These benchmark results show the clinical reliability and robustness of the proposed approach, establishing a state-of-the-art benchmark for non-invasive vocal biomarkers.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11443654/v1.title: Acoustic Machine Learning for Multi-Species Identification in the Pantanal Wetlands
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11443654/v1.abstract: Biodiversity monitoring in remote ecosystems, such as Brazil’s Pantanal wetlands, is often constrained by logistical barriers, seasonal fluctuations, and the vast scale of data acquisition. While Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM) offers a scalable alternative through continuous multi-species soundscape recording, high environmental noise and sparse labeled data remain significant hurdles for automated identification. This study proposes a robust machine learning framework for multi-label acoustic recognition. By extracting high-dimensional features—including Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) and spectral centroids—from short audio segments, we developed an ensemble learning pipeline utilizing a Random Forest classifier. Our approach integrates both primary and secondary labels to account for background vocalizations, enhancing model resilience in complex acoustic environments. Evaluated on the BirdCLEF+ 2026 dataset using macro-averaged ROC-AUC, our results validate the synergy between advanced feature engineering and ensemble methods. This framework provides a scalable foundation for monitoring understudied taxa and informs conservation strategies in one of the world’s most vulnerable ecological frontiers.
