doi:10.65215/ltspreprints.2026.10.20.000.title: Weakly Supervised Multiple Instance Learning for Benign–Malignant Classification of Parotid Gland Tumors on Whole-Slide Images
doi:10.65215/ltspreprints.2026.10.20.000.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: Accurate differentiation between benign and malignant parotid gland tumors (PGTs) is important for diagnosis and treatment planning. Although histopathologic examination of hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides remains the diagnostic reference standard, whole-slide image (WSI) assessment is labor-intensive and may be challenging in histologically heterogeneous lesions. Weakly supervised multiple instance learning (MIL) enables WSI-level classification using case-level diagnostic labels without requiring region-level annotation.
Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 101 patients with PGTs, including 58 benign and 43 malignant cases, represented by 189 digitized WSIs. Patient-level stratified five-fold cross-validation was performed to ensure that all WSIs from an individual patient were assigned exclusively to one fold. Following automated tissue detection and quality-controlled patch extraction, 256 × 256-pixel patches were encoded using either ResNet-50 or the pathology-pretrained CTransPath backbone. Three MIL strategies—CLAM-SB, attention-based MIL (ABMIL), and mean pooling—were evaluated. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and area under the precision–recall curve.
Results: CTransPath + CLAM‑SB yielded the highest mean AUC among the evaluated configurations (0.83), with an accuracy of 0.81 sensitivity of 0.82, specificity of 0.80, and F1‑score of 0.80. Under the CLAM‑SB framework, CTransPath showed a higher mean AUC than ResNet‑50 (0.83 vs. 0.81). Using CTransPath features, CLAM‑SB achieved higher mean AUC than ABMIL (0.80) and mean pooling (0.77). However, pairwise differences between models did not reach statistical significance. The optimized CLAM‑SB configuration with a bag loss weight of 0.3 further increased the mean AUC to 0.86.
Conclusions: Weakly supervised MIL enabled benign–malignant classification of PGTs from routine H&E WSIs without region-level annotation. In this retrospective single-center cohort, CTransPath combined with CLAM-SB showed the most favorable overall performance, with a consistent trend toward better discrimination across models. Given the limited sample size, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and warrant validation in larger, multicenter cohorts with external validation to confirm their generalizability and clinical utility.</jats:p>
doi:10.65215/ltspreprints.2026.10.20.000.venue: Shenzhen Medical Academy of Research and Translation

doi:10.58602/itsecs.v4i4.401.title: Evaluasi Kinerja MobileNetV2 Berbasis Transfer Learning untuk Klasifikasi Multikelas Penyakit Stroberi
doi:10.58602/itsecs.v4i4.401.abstract: <jats:p>Identifikasi penyakit stroberi secara akurat diperlukan untuk mendukung pengendalian penyakit dan mempertahankan produktivitas tanaman. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi kinerja MobileNetV2 berbasis transfer learning dalam klasifikasi multikelas penyakit stroberi serta menganalisis pengaruh fine-tuning terhadap performa model. Dataset publik yang digunakan terdiri atas 2.053 citra yang terbagi ke dalam tujuh kelas, yaitu Angular Leaf Spot, Anthracnose Fruit Rot, Blossom Blight, Gray Mold, Leaf Spot, Powdery Mildew Fruit, dan Powdery Mildew Leaf. Dataset dibagi menggunakan stratified sampling dengan rasio sekitar 80:10:10 menjadi 1.642 citra pelatihan, 205 citra validasi, dan 206 citra pengujian. Seluruh citra diubah ukurannya menjadi 224 × 224 piksel dan diproses menggunakan fungsi preprocess_input MobileNetV2, sedangkan augmentasi hanya diterapkan pada data pelatihan. Dua skenario transfer learning dibandingkan, yaitu feature extraction dengan backbone dibekukan dan fine-tuning dengan backbone diaktifkan kembali menggunakan learning rate yang lebih rendah. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa feature extraction memperoleh akurasi 95,63% dengan macro F1-score 0,87, sedangkan fine-tuning meningkatkan akurasi menjadi 98,06% dan macro F1-score menjadi 0,96. Peningkatan kinerja terutama terlihat pada kelas minoritas Anthracnose Fruit Rot dan Powdery Mildew Fruit. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa fine-tuning mampu meningkatkan kemampuan MobileNetV2 dalam menyesuaikan representasi fitur pralatih terhadap karakteristik visual penyakit stroberi. Meskipun demikian, jumlah sampel yang terbatas pada beberapa kelas menunjukkan perlunya validasi lebih lanjut menggunakan dataset yang lebih besar, seimbang, dan berasal dari kondisi lapangan.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10031328/v1.title: Adaptive Noise in Human Game Play: An Information-Theoretic Signature that Separates Learning Models on Matching-Pennies Data
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10031328/v1.abstract: Reinforcement learning is a standard model of how humans play repeated games, yet it predicts that exploration anneals away and play becomes deterministic. Human subjects do not behave this way. We characterize human play in the Selten and Chmura (2008) 2 ×2 matching-pennies experiments with four information-theoretic signatures of the action trajectory, computed on period-by-period data from all 108 independent subject groups. Two signatures dominate. Humans maintain a high, roughly stationary policy entropy across the whole 200-period session (mean entropy rate 0.64 bits), and they show strong transfer entropy from the opponent's last action to their own next action (0.06 bits; 55% of the 864 individual subjects exceed a 100-shue surrogate null at the 5% level). Matched Q-learning reproduces neither: it anneals to near-deterministic play (entropy rate 0.06) and carries essentially no opponent-responsiveness (transfer entropy 0.002; 7% of agents exceed the null, barely above the false-positive rate). No temperature setting closes both gaps at once, because Q-learning trades stochasticity against responsiveness while humans achieve both. Running four further standard learning models through the identical protocol, only self-tuning EWA enters the human region of the (entropy rate, transfer entropy) plane. This recovers, from a model- free trajectory measure, the model-selection result of Chmura, Goerg and Selten (2012), who found self-tuning EWA best predicts individual round-by-round choices. The transfer- entropy signature is consistent with this: among standard learners, only self-tuning EWA is simultaneously stochastic and opponent-responsive, as humans are. We are explicit that this is an architectural correlation rather than a demonstrated cause. JEL Classication: C72, C73, C92, D83

doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1951634.title: BDNF-related biomarkers and cognitive impairment in chronic kidney disease: associations and machine learning-based discrimination analysis
doi:10.3389/fmed.2026.1951634.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Cognitive impairment is a common complication among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, biomarkers associated with cognitive impairment in this population remain insufficiently characterized. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) may be involved in neurobiological processes related to cognitive function, but its association with cognitive impairment among patients with CKD remains unclear.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this cross-sectional study, 240 patients with CKD underwent cognitive assessment and serum BDNF measurement during the same clinical evaluation. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine the associations of BDNF and the BDNF/eGFR ratio with prevalent cognitive impairment. Restricted cubic spline analyses were performed to assess potential dose–response relationships, and subgroup analyses were conducted to explore potential effect modification. Additionally, nine machine learning algorithms were applied to evaluate the discrimination ability of BDNF-related indicators for distinguishing participants with and without cognitive impairment. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret the contribution of variables in the best-performing model.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Higher levels of BDNF and BDNF/eGFR ratio were significantly associated with lower odds of prevalent cognitive impairment after multivariable adjustment (BDNF: OR = 0.72, 95% CI: 0.63–0.82; BDNF/eGFR ratio: OR = 0.62, 95% CI: 0.45–0.82). Quartile analyses showed consistent inverse associations, and restricted cubic spline analyses indicated linear relationships. Significant effect modification was observed by sex for both markers and by stroke history for the BDNF/eGFR ratio. Among the evaluated machine learning approaches, the random forest model demonstrated the highest discrimination performance, with AUCs of 0.803 for BDNF and 0.844 for BDNF/eGFR ratio. SHAP analysis indicated that BDNF-related markers contributed substantially to the classification of cognitive impairment status.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>BDNF and BDNF/eGFR ratio were inversely associated with prevalent cognitive impairment in patients with CKD. These findings suggest that BDNF-related markers may be associated with cognitive impairment status and provide potential biological insights into CKD-related cognitive dysfunction. Further longitudinal studies are required to determine whether these biomarkers can contribute to future risk assessment or clinical decision-making.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1978846.title: AI self-efficacy and satisfaction with studies among Peruvian university students: the indirect role of language learning strategies
doi:10.3389/feduc.2026.1978846.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education is transforming how students access learning resources, regulate their learning, and engage in academic activities. However, the mechanisms through which perceived competence in using these technologies relates to students' academic experiences remain insufficiently understood, particularly in the context of language learning. This study aimed to examine whether language learning strategies statistically accounted for an indirect association between AI self-efficacy and satisfaction with studies among Peruvian university students.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A cross-sectional study was conducted with 254 university students. AI self-efficacy, language learning strategies, and satisfaction with studies were assessed, and their relationships were examined using structural equation modeling (SEM).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The model showed acceptable robust fit (CFI = .954; TLI = .943; RMSEA = .067; SRMR = .055). AI self-efficacy was positively associated with language learning strategies (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = .431,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &lt; .001), which, in turn, were positively associated with satisfaction with studies (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = .523,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &lt; .001). The direct association between AI self-efficacy and satisfaction with studies was not statistically significant (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = .068,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = .421), whereas the indirect association through language learning strategies was statistically significant (
                      <jats:italic>β</jats:italic>
                       = .225,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      &lt; .001). The model explained 30.9% of the variance in satisfaction with studies.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings indicate a statistical indirect association consistent with the hypothesized model, but the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causality. The results highlight the potential relevance of integrating AI-related competencies with strategic and self-regulated learning in higher education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26oct570.title: CyberSentinel-DB: A Machine Learning-Based Framework for Detecting and Preventing Emerging Cyber Threats in Digital Banking
doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26oct570.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of digital banking services has increased the convenience of online financial transactions. However, it has also exposed banking systems to emerging cyber threats such as phishing, ransomware, Distributed Denialof-Service (DDoS) attacks, account takeover, and suspicious transaction activities. Traditional rule-based security systems may struggle to identify previously unseen attacks and adapt to changing threat patterns. This study proposes CyberSentinel-DB, a machine learning-based framework for detecting and preventing emerging cyber threats in digital banking. The proposed framework combines supervised machine learning techniques for classifying known cyber threats with unsupervised learning techniques for identifying unusual activities and potential unknown attacks. Transactional patterns, login behavior, IP addresses, transaction frequency, and session-related features can be analyzed to identify suspicious activities. The framework also considers real-time threat monitoring, automated alerts, and preventive actions to improve banking security. Model performance can be evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, false-positive rate, and detection latency. The proposed framework aims to support adaptive, scalable, and privacy-aware cyber threat detection in digital banking environments.</jats:p>
doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26oct570.venue: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.430.title: <b>Analysis of Robotic Surgery Services on Burnout with Wellbeing and Job Satisfaction as Mediating Variables Among Operating Room Nurses: A Case Study at Siloam Hospitals Lippo Village</b>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.430.abstract:
<jats:p>Objective: Burnout among operating room nurses is a serious issue that affects healthcare service quality and hospital workforce turnover. This study aims to examine the effect of robotic surgery services on the Burnout of operating room nurses, with Wellbeing and Job Satisfaction as mediating variables. Methods: This study employed a quantitative approach with an explanatory, cross-sectional research design. The sample consisted of all 35 operating room nurses at Siloam Hospitals Lippo Village, selected through total sampling. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling – Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 4.0 software. Results: The results show that robotic surgery services have a positive and significant effect on Wellbeing (coefficient 0.660; t = 5.429) and Job Satisfaction (coefficient 0.734; t = 8.737), and a negative and significant effect on Burnout (coefficient -0.635; t = 5.621). Wellbeing was also found to have a negative and significant effect on Burnout (coefficient -1.650; t= 9.482) and to mediate the relationship between robotic surgery services and Burnout. Conversely, Job Satisfaction was found to have a positive effect on Burnout, thus failing to function as a mediator as initially hypothesized, likely due to multicollinearity between Job Satisfaction and Wellbeing. Discussion: These findings indicate that the implementation of robotic surgery services can serve as a hospital management strategy to enhance the psychological Wellbeing and Job Satisfaction of operating room nurses while reducing the risk of Burnout, primarily through strengthening Wellbeing as the main mediating pathway.




 </jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.430.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.429.title: The Effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Teachers' Digital Archiving on Microsoft 365 via OneDrive and SharePoint Cloud Storage Platforms at SMPN 01 Tilamuta
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.429.abstract: <jats:p>Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi efektivitas penggunaan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dalam pengarsipan digital guru melalui ekosistem Microsoft 365, khususnya pada platform OneDrive dan SharePoint di SMPN 01 Tilamuta. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode deskriptif evaluatif. Data diperoleh melalui observasi, wawancara, serta survei terhadap 15 guru yang mengikuti sosialisasi dan pelatihan Microsoft 365. Analisis dilakukan terhadap empat dimensi utama, yaitu Microsoft 365, Microsoft Copilot, SharePoint, dan OneDrive. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan Microsoft 365 memperoleh skor rata-rata keseluruhan sebesar 73,29 dengan kategori baik. Dimensi Microsoft 365 memperoleh skor tertinggi sebesar 78,17, diikuti OneDrive sebesar 74,05 dan Microsoft Copilot sebesar 71,43, sedangkan SharePoint memperoleh skor 69,52 dengan kategori cukup. Temuan juga menunjukkan bahwa pemanfaatan AI melalui Microsoft Copilot mampu meningkatkan efisiensi kerja guru, di mana 53% responden merasakan penghematan waktu lebih dari 50% dan 94% responden melaporkan adanya peningkatan kualitas hasil pekerjaan. Meskipun demikian, masih ditemukan beberapa kendala, seperti keterbatasan pemahaman pengguna, kebutuhan pelatihan lanjutan, serta kekhawatiran terkait privasi dan keamanan data. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa integrasi AI dalam Microsoft 365 melalui OneDrive dan SharePoint efektif mendukung pengarsipan digital guru, meningkatkan efisiensi kerja, serta mempermudah pengelolaan dan temu balik dokumen. Namun, optimalisasi penggunaan SharePoint dan peningkatan kompetensi pengguna terhadap fitur AI masih diperlukan untuk memperoleh manfaat yang lebih maksimal.</jats:p>
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.429.venue: Journal of Education and Teaching Learning

doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.469.title: Implementation of Project-Based Learning Model with a Demonstration Approach on the Operational Competence of Mastercam X5 Turning for 11 TPM 5 Students at SMK Canda Bhirawa Pare
doi:10.59211/mjpjetl.v4i2.469.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to describe the implementation of the Project Based Learning (PjBL) model with a demonstration approach, measure improvements in students’ practical performance competence, and explore students’ learning experiences in Mastercam X5 Turning learning at a vocational high school. The study employed a mixed method with a Sequential Explanatory design over eight sessions involving 39 students from Grade XI Mechanical Engineering at SMK Canda Bhirawa Kediri and five purposively selected qualitative participants. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, validity and reliability tests, Shapiro-Wilk, Wilcoxon, and N-Gain, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically. The results showed a significant difference between pretest and posttest scores across all topics (p < 0.001), with N-Gain in the moderate category (0.4379–0.5302). Qualitative analysis identified five themes: ease of procedural understanding, active observation, demonstration speed as a learning barrier, intrinsic motivation, and transfer to industrial contexts. Triangulation showed that the qualitative findings complemented the quantitative results by explaining students’ learning experiences during the learning process. The implementation of PjBL with a demonstration approach was associated with improved students’ practical performance competence, with a need to adjust demonstration speed to accommodate differences in students’ learning abilities</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/prt-05-2026-0084.title: Preparation and performance prediction of PES/TiO2 ultrafiltration membranes using machine learning
doi:10.1108/prt-05-2026-0084.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this study, polyethersulfone (PES) and titanium dioxide (TiO2) were used as membrane materials and PVP-K30 was used as a pore-forming agent. PES/TiO2 ultrafiltration membranes were prepared using the nonsolvent-induced phase separation (NIPS) method to investigate the effects of PES concentration, TiO2 concentration, temperature and PVP-K30 content on membrane performance. The purpose of this study is to use machine learning to conduct an in-depth analysis of the relationship between membrane fabrication process conditions and membrane performance, thereby providing a data-driven basis for ultrafiltration membrane design and process optimization.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study first completed the preparation of PES/TiO2 ultrafiltration membranes, measured and conducted a basic analysis of their performance. Given the complex relationship between membrane preparation conditions and performance, traditional methods struggle to fully reveal their underlying patterns. Based on this, this study introduced machine learning (ML) analysis methods and constructed three machine learning models, including gradient boosted decision tree (GBDT), random forest and extreme random tree. The authors conducted an in-depth investigation into the relationship between preparation conditions (including PES concentration, TiO2 concentration, PVP-K30 content and temperature) and membrane performance (membrane flux and rejection rate). In addition, the authors used the shapley additive explanation (SHAP) method to provide a global interpretation of the ML models and evaluate interaction effects.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The R2 values for these three machine learning models were all greater than 0.75 on both the training and test sets, indicating that the models are highly reliable. Among them, the GBDT model performed the best. The study found that, for membrane flux, temperature and TiO2 generally had a positive effect, while PES and PVP-K30 generally had a negative effect. For rejection rate, temperature and TiO2 generally had a negative effect, while PES and PVP-K30 generally had a positive effect. Furthermore, the study found that the optimal concentration range for PES is 18 wt%–18.2 wt% and the optimal concentration range for TiO2 is 0.8 wt%–1 wt%.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is the first to combine the preparation of PES/TiO2 ultrafiltration membranes with interpretable machine learning (ML), constructing three machine learning models. This approach provides a new perspective on traditional research into ultrafiltration membrane preparation and performance. Furthermore, this method was used to analyze the direction of the effects of PES/ TiO2 ultrafiltration membrane preparation conditions on membrane performance, identifying the optimal concentration ranges for PES (18.0 wt%–18.2 wt%) and TiO2 (0.8 wt%–1.0 wt%), thereby providing a data-driven reference for optimizing membrane formulations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.54855/callej.2627211.title: Investigating AI-Mediated Informal Digital Learning of English Practices among Indonesian Undergraduates
doi:10.54855/callej.2627211.abstract: <jats:p>AI’s unprecedented advancement has impacted various fields, including foreign language learning. This research aimed to investigate EFL students’ engagement with AI for their informal English Learning and their perceptions regarding AI’s practicality and challenges. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, this study carried out an online survey involving 82 students in the quantitative phase. It was followed by semi-structured interviews in the qualitative phase. Descriptive statistics and thematic analysis were employed to discover the patterns of AI’s acceptance, students’ voices on AI’s usability, AI practicality, reasons for using AI, and analytical considerations. The quantitative phase indicates that the percentage of AI use is high (97.6%), but its usage frequency remains moderate. Students approved AI’s usefulness for developing their vocabulary, assisting their writing, and regulating their own learning. Students also voiced concerns about accuracy and critical thinking loss (M=4.11) and overreliance. Semi-structured interviews with four students provided more profound insights that AI use was formed by accessibility and platform familiarity. Supporting the quantitative phase findings, students claimed AI was an easy, emotionally supportive, and helpful learning aid, but faced challenges in creating effective prompts and avoiding dependency. This study implies that students’ AI literacy advancement is mandatory to encourage more efficient, analytical, and independent AI-mediated informal language learning.</jats:p>

arxiv:2610.29094.title: Oscillation modes, Decoherence, Beam Transfer Functions, and Instabilities for a Beam Subjected to Space-Charge Forces
arxiv:2610.29094.abstract: Based on the oscillation modes of a bunch subject to the space-charge force, we discuss the decoherence of the dipole oscillation, the beam transfer function, and the beam instability. The longitudinal phase space is discretized into \(n_l\times n_J\) grids in the azimuthal and radial directions, respectively. The transverse dipole moment in the longitudinal phase space is represented by a vector of length \(n_l n_J\), and the transformation given by the Vlasov equation is represented by a matrix transformation of size \(n_l n_J\times n_l n_J\). Solving the eigenvalue problem of this matrix gives the \(n_l n_J\) eigen-oscillation modes of the bunch. Using the resulting eigenvectors within a standard linear-algebraic treatment, we analyze these three phenomena. The analysis was performed for the Rapid Cycling Synchrotron (RCS) of the China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) using \(n_l=41\) and \(n_J=40\), and it visualizes the features related to the continuous distribution of the tune, Landau damping, and isolated modes separated from the continuous tune region.

arxiv:2610.29475.title: Density-Level Backward Error for Low-NFE Generative Flows
arxiv:2610.29475.abstract: Low-NFE generative ODE sampling is constrained not only by solver order, but also by how a fixed budget of network evaluations is distributed along the flow. We develop a density-level backward-error framework that identifies the component of a solver's modified-equation defect that changes the evolving marginal, while excluding solenoidal trajectory distortion that is invisible in Wasserstein tangent geometry. The resulting residual induces a solver-order-aware compute-allocation rule and, through gauge freedom, an objective for selecting numerically favorable velocity representatives of the same density path. This separates our approach from schedule search driven by trajectory or endpoint surrogates and from higher-order solver design. Exact Gaussian and mixture models establish the mechanism, including cases where curvature-based allocation fails and continuum-optimal transport is not discretization-optimal. On a pretrained CIFAR-10 EDM probability-flow ODE, density-aware allocation consistently improves fixed-update Euler sampling in the low-NFE regime. Matched-seed convergence to a dense Euler reference confirms that the method accelerates approximation of the same high-NFE flow rather than changing the asymptotic sampler.

arxiv:2610.29331.title: From Prompts to Posteriors: Can LLM Agents Perform Bayesian Inference in Context?
arxiv:2610.29331.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied across the scientific discovery pipeline, from synthesizing literature to generating hypotheses to informing experimental design. A unifying principle behind these tasks is the need to continuously update beliefs as evidence accumulates, for which Bayesian inference provides a natural framework. However, existing work assumes that LLMs cannot carry out principled Bayesian belief updating in context, instead relying on simplifications and heuristics. To challenge this assumption, we present a principled evaluation of Bayesian reasoning capabilities in LLMs, analyzing both the model's internal consistency as well as its ability to recover an externally determined posterior. Specifically, we build an evaluation framework spanning qualitative epistemological examples to probe probabilistic coherence, quantitative benchmarks of Bayesian inference capabilities, and analyses of the impact of non-Bayesian updates on downstream task performance. Across different scenarios, we find that LLMs generally violate Bayes' rule when updating their beliefs in context. However, when equipped with modern reasoning abilities and code execution capabilities, their performance drastically improves, enabling even the close approximation of analytically intractable posteriors. Our evaluation shows that current LLMs with access to appropriate tools could already be used to make complex belief updates in scientific discovery, enabling rapid acceleration of the efficiency and scale of AI-powered scientific discovery.

arxiv:2610.29295.title: Latent space configuration for neural network finetuning, fast ranking, and embedding dimensionality reduction
arxiv:2610.29295.abstract: Finding K most similar elements for a query in a large gallery of neural network (NN) embeddings is essential in various areas of computer science and industrial applications of artificial intelligence. This paper proposes search algorithms for structured latent spaces (LS) of NNs which allow to speed up top K item retrieval owing to O(1) complexity small candidate gallery subset search. ArcFace-pretrained IResNet50 models are finetuned using Latent Space Configuration (LSC) methodology to obtain new distribution of embeddings with desired geometric properties. Applying the proposed algorithms to embeddings obtained from finetuned models leads to several times speed-up over baseline exhaustive search. Specifically, we report up to 3 times speed-up on GPU and 40% speed-up on CPU compared to the baseline method GPU speed. These results are obtained for the original and reduced numbers of LS dimensions. The results show that LS dimensionality reduction allows to further accelerate the search and even improve rank-N metrics.

arxiv:2610.29261.title: Group Distributionally Robust Optimization over Decentralized Networks
arxiv:2610.29261.abstract: We study group distributionally robust optimization (GDRO) over decentralized networks, where workers collaborate to learn robust models by minimizing the maximum local risk. Existing methods optimize only dual-regularized surrogates and establish guarantees for a globally averaged model that is not available to workers. In this paper, we directly optimize the original GDRO objective and establish guarantees for local models in semi-decentralized (SemiDec) and fully decentralized (Dec) settings. A key difficulty is that applying the primal-dual decomposition from centralized GDRO yields worker-dependent losses whose evaluation requires unavailable cross-worker information. To address this challenge, we develop a novel error decomposition that recasts decentralized GDRO as (i) a decentralized online convex optimization (D-OCO) problem and a prediction-with-expert-advice problem in SemiDec, and as (ii) two coupled D-OCO problems in Dec, with discrepancy terms capturing inconsistencies among local decisions. By isolating consensus errors in analysis, we develop modular frameworks that support different consensus routines. We then establish the \emph{first} per-worker convergence guarantees for optimizing the original GDRO objective over decentralized networks. Instantiations with accelerated gossip and Choco-gossip achieve an $O(\sqrt{(\log m)/T})$ convergence rate over $T$ update rounds, while experiments demonstrate improved worst-worker performance over baselines.

arxiv:2610.29013.title: Target Regeneration Shrinks the Gains of Draft-Training Objectives in Speculative Decoding
arxiv:2610.29013.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language models by verifying drafted tokens in parallel. New draft-training objectives are usually credited with the acceptance they add over cross-entropy on externally written responses, yet many pipelines let the target rewrite them. We ask how much of that gain survives. With a vision-language target and a block drafter, we train three objectives on four versions of one corpus: cross-entropy on corpus tokens, token-level distillation from the target, and distillation gated to positions that would survive verification. Distillation and the gate add large gains on external responses, but after greedy regeneration, distillation adds a smaller gain and the gate little or none. The shrinkage persists across data orders, position weights, verifiers, decoding temperatures and, for distillation, initializations and learning rates. Most of it remains at matched supervised length and at each objective's best measured training length. A second vision corpus shows the shrinkage, as does a text-only replication, for distillation also with an autoregressive drafter. Objective gains should therefore be measured against a target-regenerated baseline and across training lengths. Our code is available at https://github.com/js-lee-AI/TargetRegeneration.

arxiv:2610.28909.title: DiffResearch: Accelerating Deep Research with Diffusion Language Models
arxiv:2610.28909.abstract: Deep research systems iteratively plan, gather evidence, synthesize, and revise, making end-to-end latency a key bottleneck for interactive use. Almost all production systems are built on autoregressive (AR) language models and inherit left-to-right decoding in planning and long-form writing. We present DiffResearch, an open multi-agent deep research framework that places a diffusion language model (dLLM) at the core of every stage, and measure how a diffusion backbone changes latency and report quality. Holding the agentic scaffold, retrieval code, prompts, and evaluation fixed, we swap the backbone between an open diffusion model and a comparable AR model. Across 100 Deep Research Bench tasks, the diffusion backbone is roughly 6 times faster end-to-end, driven by order-of-magnitude reductions in planning and writing. We further introduce dFast, a decomposition mode that reads intermediate denoising states and extracts subqueries before generation finishes, providing a 1.99 times median speedup for decomposition in isolation with no loss of report quality. On the benchmark's RACE rubric, dFast obtains the best overall score among the three configurations. Finally, in a public system-level leaderboard snapshot, an instance built on a stronger diffusion model ranks above several commercial systems. We release DiffResearch under an Apache-2.0 license.

arxiv:2610.28907.title: JaxMARL-BC: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Macroeconomic Modelling, in Seconds
arxiv:2610.28907.abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) offers a principled way of populating simulated economies with many heterogeneous decision makers. Its adoption, pioneered in finance, has nonetheless been slow in macroeconomics because of two main limitations: the lack of a shared frame of reference connecting MARL systems to dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) models the profession already trusts, and the very long training times. The first limitation was recently addressed by the Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Business Cycle (MARL-BC), which places deep RL households in a real business cycle economy and reduces to classic DSGE models in specific limits. Here we address the second limitation. We present JaxMARL-BC, a JAX-accelerated simulator that trains MARL-BC economies in seconds (between 75x and 724x faster than the reference implementation), and scales to 200,000 independent learning households. We verify its correctness against the known DSGE limits, characterise its scaling through a simple cost law, and demonstrate its value by a proof-of-concept calibration of an extended model with heterogeneous returns on capital, in a two-hour experiment that would previously have taken over a month. We release JaxMARL-BC as open source.

arxiv:2610.28759.title: GPU-Accelerated Construction of the Gabriel Graph: Parallelization Strategies and Applications to Large-Margin Classification and Graph-Based Clustering
arxiv:2610.28759.abstract: The Gabriel graph is a proximity graph widely used in computational geometry and geometric machine learning, underlying large-margin classifiers and, as we show in this work, density-aware clustering methods. Its construction, however, has cubic time complexity $O(N^3)$ in the naive formulation, which severely limits its use on datasets beyond a few thousand samples. This paper presents a set of GPU parallelization strategies, implemented in CUDA, that make Gabriel graph construction practical at scale. We introduce (i) an implicit closed-form mapping from a linear thread index to the corresponding vertex pair $(i,j)$, which removes the need for an explicit $O(N^2)$ adjacency structure and lets every thread locate its pair in constant time and constant memory; (ii) a two-pass, bitmask-based, atomically-compacted edge-list construction that produces a dense edge array proportional only to the number of edges actually found; and (iii) a thread-coarsening strategy in which each thread evaluates several candidate pairs, trading launch and scheduling overhead against load balance. We evaluate these strategies on the acceleration of a Gabriel-graph-based large-margin classifier (NN-clas) and on a novel Gabriel-graph clustering algorithm that identifies connected components on a residual graph and performs GPU-parallel Union-Find with hierarchical edge-based merging. On 14 public benchmark datasets, the GPU implementation reduces Gabriel graph construction time by two to nearly four orders of magnitude relative to a sequential CPU baseline (up to 8484x), without loss of classification accuracy, and the proposed clustering method is statistically competitive with DBSCAN on the topological validity index Dunn while eliminating the need for an explicit density radius parameter.

arxiv:2610.28703.title: Scalable Stress-Constrained Topology Optimization: A Super-resolution and Simultaneous Approach Based on Machine Learning
arxiv:2610.28703.abstract: Large-scale topology optimization (TO) remains computationally demanding, especially for stress-constrained problems. To address this challenge, we propose the simultaneous neural topology optimization (SNTO) framework where we represent state, adjoint, and design variables with custom neural networks (NNs) whose parameters are jointly optimized within a single optimization loop that leverages continuous adjoint analysis and automatic differentiation. This optimization minimizes a multi-component loss function that combines the design objective, an aggregation of the local stress constraints, and the potential energy functionals. Our NNs have a unique architecture that accelerates convergence while enabling the networks to capture sharp gradients and boundaries which are critical to stress-constrained TO. To achieve scalability to millions of degrees of freedom (DoF), we develop a hardware-aware training scheme in which the design domain is partitioned into subdomains that are distributed across multiple GPUs. To control peak GPU memory usage, we further slice each subdomain into smaller regions whose loss gradients are evaluated sequentially and accumulated to update the NN parameters. Unlike domain decomposition approaches, our partitioning naturally ensures field continuity across the subdomains and does not require the introduction of additional terms into the loss function. For validation, we first evaluate the proposed framework on various 2D stress-constrained benchmarks and compare our results to a conventional finite element-based approach, showing that SNTO produces super-resolution designs with sharper boundaries, smaller gray areas, and lower volume fractions. We then consider large-scale 3D problems with up to eight million collocation points and distribute the training over up to eight GPUs.

arxiv:2610.28699.title: Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey
arxiv:2610.28699.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables adaptive and autonomous decision-making in embedded, edge, and heterogeneous computing systems. Field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) and integrated circuits (ICs) offer low latency, energy efficiency, and architectural flexibility for RL deployment, while introducing challenges in resource constraints, implementation complexity, and hardware-algorithm co-design. This review surveys more than 100 studies on RL implementations across FPGA and IC platforms, emphasizing architectures, implementation strategies, performance evaluation, and applications. The literature is organized by RL family, including model-based Markov decision processes, classical value-based methods, deep RL, actor-critic, policy-gradient, and multi-agent approaches. We further classify studies by abstraction level, hardware realization strategy, and application domain, examining how RL algorithms map onto reconfigurable and fixed hardware. Unlike surveys restricted to particular algorithms or platforms, this work provides a unified analysis of FPGA and IC implementations, covering acceleration, reconfigurable architectures, energy-aware control, and system-level optimization. Comparative assessments consider resource utilization, latency, throughput, power consumption, and reported performance gains. Finally, we identify recurring architectural patterns, practical limitations, open challenges, and research directions for efficient RL-driven hardware systems. The survey offers a consolidated reference for researchers developing and evaluating RL solutions on specialized hardware.

arxiv:2610.29439.title: How Far Can Foundation Models Be Distilled for Efficient Jet Tagging?
arxiv:2610.29439.abstract: Jet tagging is one of the most important applications of machine learning at the Large Hadron Collider. Recent models build in more physics knowledge or rely on large-scale pretraining, but the experiments place strict limits on their inference cost. Knowledge distillation can transfer their performance to small students that are cheap to run. We ask which properties of a teacher help the student, how small a student can get and how close it can come to the state of the art. On a jet tagging benchmark, we distil six teachers that differ in architecture, symmetry and pretraining, including two foundation models, into five small students. Every teacher improves every student, and the gain depends mainly on the strength of the teacher. We then shrink our two strongest distilled students, Transformer and L-GATr-slim, in width and in depth. With 20 thousand parameters, a distilled L-GATr-slim outperforms every published jet tagger trained from scratch at a fraction of the inference cost of every teacher. Even with two thousand parameters, it matches ParT, a model with a thousand times as many parameters. We also study what the students learn from their teachers. Our benchmark of inference cost shows that students of the same size can differ by almost an order of magnitude in speed. We release the code and the weights of all trained models.

arxiv:2610.28747.title: A Reverse-Gold Theorem: Positive-Data Identification by Substrate-Bounded Contrastive Learners
arxiv:2610.28747.abstract: Gold's theorem shows that no learner can identify an arbitrary language in a superfinite class from positive presentations alone. We prove a positive result of a different shape. Fix an innate \emph{recursive contrast operator} $R$ mapping any string to a finite set of structurally bounded perturbations of it, and a discriminative scorer of bounded capacity trained by InfoNCE-style contrastive estimation \citep{vandenoord2018,macollins2018} on self-generated perturbations. Under a faithfulness condition relating operator, scorer, and target, the trained scorer achieves \emph{PAC conditional identification} from positive data alone: with high probability it ranks all but an $\varepsilon$-fraction of positives above every out-of-language perturbation in their own orbit, with sample complexity polynomial in the capacity, the orbit size, the score bound, and $1/\varepsilon$. The negatives are constructed by the learner, not supplied by an oracle, and no global normalizing constant over strings is ever computed. The misranking bound follows from the geometry of the contrastive loss---per-example loss floors plus a definite loss increment under misranking---yielding an $\varepsilon^{-2}$ rate, together with an explicit approximation gap that quantifies the cost of in-language (``colliding'') perturbations and vanishes for orbit-pure operators. The ranking guarantee lifts to a global membership classifier under a margin condition, and the same operator composed with the learned scorer is a normalization-free Metropolis--Hastings generator. We instantiate the hypotheses for substitutable context-free languages \citep{clarkeyraud2007} and the subregular classes \citep{heinz2010,hayashikamigaito2025}, and state an open conjecture locating the construction in the mildly context-sensitive hierarchy.

arxiv:2610.28693.title: Interaction-Gated Time-Frequency Learning for Parameter-Efficient PPG-Based Heart Rate Estimation
arxiv:2610.28693.abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) enables low-cost and non-invasive heart rate (HR) monitoring but remains sensitive to waveform distortion, physiological variability, and measurement interference. Temporal waveform characteristics and frequency-domain periodicity provide complementary information for HR estimation; however, effectively exploring and integrating these representations within a compact model remains challenging. This paper proposes TF-IG, a parameter-efficient interaction-gated time-frequency learning framework for PPG-based HR estimation. TF-IG employs a dual-branch architecture in which a temporal branch captures pulse morphology via dilated depthwise-separable convolutions, while a frequency branch extracts cardiac periodicity information from bounded log-spectrogram representations. To combine the two domains, we introduce an interaction-gated fusion module that explicitly models feature agreement and discrepancy, while also learning feature-wise weights to balance temporal and spectral information. A parameter-shared regression head further maps the temporal, spectral, and fused representations into the final HR prediction space. Experiments on the benchmark BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset using a subject-exclusive training, validation, and test protocol show that TF-IG achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.227 BPM, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.060 BPM, a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.9934, and 92.28 percent of estimates within 3 BPM, while remaining parameter-efficient with only 84.6K parameters. Ablation results further demonstrate the complementary contributions of the temporal and frequency branches, interaction-gated fusion, and shared regression head. These results indicate that explicitly modeling cross-domain interactions provides an effective accuracy-complexity trade-off for lightweight PPG-based HR estimation.

arxiv:2610.29398.title: Region-Aware Multi-View Inspection Using Deep Learning and Domain-Informed Decision Fusion
arxiv:2610.29398.abstract: Automated optical inspection of precision components with tiny surface defects remains challenging when different regions of the same component exhibit different defect characteristics and, therefore, different acceptance criteria. This paper presents a region-aware, dual-model inspection framework that combines instance segmentation of localized seat-region defects with image-level classification of global shaft-region anomalies. Rather than treating these two model detections as sufficient evidence for component rejection, a deterministic decision fusion layer that formalizes industrial Standard Operating Procedures is applied to the model outputs to make the final component level decision. A PLC-synchronized imaging system acquires 18 seat and 18 shaft images over a full 360-degree rotation to provide multi-view circumferential coverage. The framework was evaluated on 380 automotive fuel injector needles, covering representative operational defect types, using identical model predictions in all configurations. Direct model-output aggregation via simple union logic (where any single-view detection flags a rejection) identified all 104 non-conforming components but produced a component level false rejection rate of 57.6%. Inclusion of a complete decision layer maintained the observed non-conforming (NOK) recall of 100% while reducing the false rejection rate to 10.9%, corresponding to an 81.1% reduction in false-positive component decisions. The results demonstrate that formalized manufacturing acceptance criteria can complement sensitive visual models by translating frame-level detections into practical and traceable component-level decisions.

arxiv:2610.29630.title: Space weather dependence of decameter-scale ionospheric irregularities spatial distribution
arxiv:2610.29630.abstract:
This paper describes an approach to constructing nowcast and forecast predictive models for the occurrence of high-latitude decameter ionospheric irregularities based on SuperDARN and SECIRA radar data and space weather parameters. The method relies on self-learning pattern recognition in the dynamics of space weather parameters, that influence the irregularities formation. The proposed approach is a data-driven, multiscale method in which the spatial distribution of irregularities is approximated using a neural network of an original architecture, inspired by graph neural networks.
  The model was trained and tested using data from 11 radars during the period 2010-2025 (SuperDARN: CVW, ICE, ICW, INV, PGR, PYK, RKN, SAS, STO; SECIRA: EKB, MAGW). It is shown that the model achieves optimal performance when using geomagnetic coordinates MLT,MLAT. The optimal set of parameters for the best nowcast and forecast over studied set of parameters is a combination of geomagnetic and solar disturbance indices ($a_{p}$, $K_{p}$, $AE$, F10.7) from ground-based observations, and satellite-measured solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field parameters ($P_{sw}$, $E_{sw}$, $\widetilde{B_{z}}$, $T_{sw}$). Hourly mean values for all the parameters were used in the analysis. The results indicate that acceptable forecast quality is achieved with a lead time of up to 7-9 hours, with the highest quality reached for nowcast (zero lead time). It is shown that the parameters $\widetilde{B_{z}}$ and F10.7 are significant for nowcasting only and can be neglected for other lead times. It is shown that $AE$ and $T_{sw}$ are significant for mid-term forecast (\textgreater 2hours ahead) and can be neglected for short-term predictions.
  Statistical relationships between the maximum latitude of the equatorial boundary of the irregularities and space weather parameters are also discussed.

arxiv:2610.29111.title: SU(2)-Equivariant Spinor Message Passing for Molecular Magnetism
arxiv:2610.29111.abstract: Predicting molecular magnetism often requires electronic-structure calculations with spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which are costly to repeat across many molecules. The underlying electronic states can transform as spinors, yet equivariant surrogates typically use only integer-rank features. Inspired by the spinor nature of these electronic states, we develop eSpinor, an SU(2)-equivariant graph neural network that propagates spinor features. We initialize spinor features from eigenvectors of an approximate SOC Hamiltonian and use gauge-covariant message passing with a gauge-invariant readout to make predictions independent of the arbitrary eigenbasis choice. On cobalt single-molecule magnet candidates, eSpinor improves zero-field-splitting predictions relative to NequIP, including for unseen ligands. For a dysprosium magnetic resonance imaging probe, eSpinor improves real electron-spin correlations over a Hamiltonian-informed baseline despite similar static crystal-field errors and fewer parameters, while accurately predicting low-field nuclear relaxation in water and after transfer to methanol without retraining. Overall, these results demonstrate that SU(2)-equivariant spinor message passing is a useful inductive bias for molecular magnetism. We also find that similar static tensor errors can yield different dynamical errors, motivating model selection based on accuracy for the intended physical observables.

arxiv:2610.29604.title: Local and Global Recursive Ridge Regression for Online Residual Correction of Frozen Multivariate Forecasters under Label Delay
arxiv:2610.29604.abstract: A frozen multi-horizon forecaster can be corrected online from its own residuals. However, under label delay the target of a block arrives only after the whole horizon has passed, and the corrector's retained state grows with the number of channels. Aiming to combine a small retained state with a large error reduction, we propose DRiC (DCT Ridge Corrector), which fits a ridge regression of the leading discrete cosine transform (DCT) coefficients of the next residual block on those of the frozen forecast and of the latest input block, with sufficient statistics updated recursively. Its local variant, DRiC-L, keeps one such regression per channel; its global variant, DRiC-G, pools all channels into one regression, whose statistics do not depend on the channel count. A guard tracks a running scale of the frozen forecast's residual for each channel; it skips updates on blocks far outside that scale and clips the issued correction. We evaluate on seven datasets (four ETT series, Weather with its missing-value codes filled, Electricity, and Traffic) with DLinear, PatchTST, and iTransformer backbones, against 10 naive, gradient-trained, and closed-form methods. DRiC-L with eight DCT coefficients (DRiC-L8) reduces the mean squared error (MSE) by 14.55% on average over 126 conditions, against 12.98% for ELF, the most accurate comparator, while retaining 15-17 times less state, although ELF is more accurate on Traffic. DRiC-G retains 14.6 kB on the 321-channel Electricity data and 18.9 kB on the 862-channel Traffic data and is the most accurate method at or below its state on both. However, 5 to 7 of the 10 comparators, all with at least 10 times its state, are more accurate there. On the unfilled Weather file, DRiC-L8 without the guard has on average 8.0 times the frozen forecast's MSE, whereas with the guard it reduces the MSE by 7.94%. Code: https://github.com/keiotakmin/dric.

hash:e9eed26c6bcc.title: Автоматизированное машинное обучение для нейтронной спектрометрии
hash:e9eed26c6bcc.abstract: Radiation monitoring outside accelerator shielding is performed using the Bonner multi-sphere spectrometer, which detects neutrons across a wide energy range. Since neutron spectra cannot be directly measured, computational unfolding methods are required. In this study, neutron spectrum deconvolution models were developed using the LightAutoML and FEDOT automated machine learning frameworks, optimizing hyperparameters and ensemble combinations of multiple algorithms. For training and validation a synthetic spectra were generated as weighted combinations of thermal, epithermal, fast and high-energy component. The models were evaluated on a test set of 375 real spectra, with uncertainty assessed via Monte Carlo simulations incorporating random input errors. Reconstruction quality was measured using Spearman and Pearson correlation, cosine similarity, cross-entropy, Wasserstein distance, Kullback–Leibler divergence, maximum mean discrepancy and $R^2$.
hash:e9eed26c6bcc.venue: ФИЗИКА ЭЛЕМЕНТАРНЫХ ЧАСТИЦ И АТОМНОГО ЯДРА

doi:10.62885/edusci.v4i1.1342.title: Comparative Literature Study on Independent Learning Methods, Deep Learning, and Flipped Classroom in 21st Century Education
doi:10.62885/edusci.v4i1.1342.abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The transformation of 21st-century education has accelerated the adoption of student-centered pedagogies that promote learner autonomy, higher-order thinking, active engagement, and technology-supported learning. Independent (Merdeka) Learning, Deep Learning, and Flipped Classroom have been widely discussed; however, previous studies have predominantly examined these approaches separately, leaving limited understanding of their complementary roles within an integrated pedagogical framework.
Aims: This study aims to systematically compare the conceptual foundations, implementation characteristics, and complementary functions of Independent Learning, Deep Learning, and Flipped Classroom and to develop an integrative framework for 21st-century education.
Methods: We conducted a qualitative Systematic Literature Review (SLR) following the PRISMA framework. We identified relevant literature published between 2013 and 2025 through Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, then screened it using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The selected studies were analyzed through thematic coding, comparative analysis, and synthesis to identify conceptual patterns, distinctive characteristics, and opportunities for pedagogical integration.
Results: The findings show that the three approaches share a student-centered orientation but operate at different, complementary levels. Independent Learning provides a philosophical and policy-oriented foundation emphasizing learner autonomy and curriculum flexibility; Deep Learning provides a cognitive orientation toward conceptual understanding, critical thinking, and knowledge transfer; and Flipped Classroom provides an instructional strategy that reorganizes learning activities through technology-supported pre-class preparation and active in-class engagement. Their integration therefore connects philosophical, cognitive, and instructional dimensions within a unified learning framework.
Conclusion: The study proposes an integrative pedagogical framework in which Independent Learning serves as the philosophical foundation, Deep Learning as the cognitive objective, and Flipped Classroom as the instructional strategy. This synthesis is the study's principal contribution, moving beyond fragmented examinations of individual learning approaches toward a holistic framework designed to strengthen student autonomy, meaningful learning, higher-order thinking, and active engagement in 21st-century education. Future research should empirically validate the proposed framework across diverse educational levels and learning contexts.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-73866-0.title: Positive-unlabelled learning for recorded damp and mould risk in UK housing
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-73866-0.abstract: Operational housing records identify damp-and-mould complaints and repairs, while dwellings without recorded events remain unlabelled rather than verified negatives. We formulate recorded damp-and-mould risk prioritisation as a Positive-Unlabelled (PU) learning problem using anonymised UK housing administrative data. The dataset contains 65,214 dwellings described by 291 property-level and household-level snapshot features, with 8,580 recorded positives and 56,634 unlabelled cases. We develop and evaluate a two-stage sample-selection PU framework: an out-of-fold XGBoost scorer first identifies conservative reliable negatives, and weighted Stage-2 classifiers then combine positives, reliable negatives, and weakly weighted residual unlabelled cases. The Stage-1 scorer achieved an out-of-fold development-set PU-AUC of 0.7547. The selected Stage-2 XGBoost model achieved a held-out PU-AUC of 0.7760 and average precision of 0.2981, and increased Recall@20% from 44.0% to 47.0%, retrieving 51 additional recorded positives compared with the Stage-1-only scorer. Supervised XGBoost baselines achieved similar recorded-label performance, while Stage-1 learner ablation showed that the framework supported alternative reliable-negative selectors. Grouped SHAP analysis connected the fitted scores to heating and fuel systems, household and occupancy context, assessment status, dwelling characteristics and energy performance. Targeted predictor exclusion reduced PU-AUC to 0.7648 and Recall@20% to 43.6%, quantifying dependence on selected inputs without resolving their temporal availability. These findings provide an empirical basis for PU-based recorded-risk prioritisation in housing, combining improved ranking over the initial scorer, explicit control over unlabelled training data and interpretation through housing-domain feature groups.

doi:10.3389/fnins.2026.1902749.title: Striatal and orbitofrontal grey matter volumes are associated with cognitive event related potentials during associative learning task performance in male and female children and adolescents
doi:10.3389/fnins.2026.1902749.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The individual differences in gray matter volumes and event-related potentials may underlie variability in associative learning. However, little is known about the sex differences in these structure–function relationships across development.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The current study investigates associations between local gray matter volumes and brain responses during associative learning task in children and adolescents aged 7–21 years. We hypothesized that gray matter volumes of the basal ganglia and prefrontal cortex would be associated with event-related potentials indices of associative learning, in a sex-dependent manner. Final analysis included 138 participants (68 females, 70 males). Participants completed an associative learning task with concurrent EEG event-related potentials recording. Gray matter volumes were analyzed within 5
                      <jats:italic>a priori</jats:italic>
                      regions of interest, predominantly located in the basal ganglia vicinity and prefrontal cortex.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In females, anterior N400 latency to Early-stage stimulus onsets was positively associated with gray matter volume in the left putamen/lentiform nucleus and to Late-stage stimulus onsets with gray matter volume in the subgenual anterior cingulate. Anterior P300 amplitude to Late-stage feedback presentation was positively associated with gray matter volume in the right nucleus accumbens/putamen and the right medial orbitofrontal cortex. Correlations involving the subgenual anterior cingulate and medial orbitofrontal cortex were significantly stronger in the female group relative to the male group. In males, anterior P300 amplitude to Early-stage feedback presentation was associated with gray matter volume in a left hippocampus/amygdala cluster, yet not significantly differently from females. In exploratory analysis, after accounting for total brain volumes, age was positively associated with the volumes of striatal and orbitofrontal regions in both sexes, with largely overlapping patterns.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Therefore, findings support structure–function relationships linking gray matter volumes of striatum and orbitofrontal cortex to brain activity during reinforcement learning performance. Given that associative learning is an instance of reinforcement learning, its underlying neural processes are influenced by the structural development of striatal and orbitofrontal regions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3389/fcell.2026.1868333.title: DeepOSSA: a deep learning framework for personalized survival prediction in osteosarcoma patients
doi:10.3389/fcell.2026.1868333.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Osteosarcoma, the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children and adolescents, is marked by high invasiveness and heterogeneous outcomes due to inter-patient variability in tumor biology and treatment response. Accurate prognostic modeling is crucial for personalized risk stratification and clinical decision-making.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We developed and validated DeepOSSA, a deep learning framework for individualized survival prediction in osteosarcoma, leveraging high-dimensional, sparsely encoded clinical data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Clinical data from 895 osteosarcoma patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2018 were extracted. Continuous variables were optimally discretized using X-tile, and categorical covariates were one-hot encoded. We compared DeepOSSA against seven representative models spanning classical machine learning (support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and gradient boosted decision trees (GBDT)), deep learning (multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and Transformer), and survival analysis (Cox proportional hazards (CoxPH) and DeepSurv). DeepOSSA integrates a Transformer-based representation tower for high-order sparse feature crossing with a Cox-style discrete-time survival head, enabling joint optimization of feature representation and time-to-event modeling. Performance was evaluated on a held-out test set using the area under the curve (AUC) and F1-score.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      DeepOSSA outperformed all baselines in discrimination and balanced classification, achieving an AUC of
                      <jats:inline-formula>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" id="m1">
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mn>0.8058</mml:mn>
                            <mml:mo>±</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mn>0.0081</mml:mn>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:math>
                      </jats:inline-formula>
                      and an F1-score of
                      <jats:inline-formula>
                        <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" id="m2">
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mn>0.6506</mml:mn>
                            <mml:mo>±</mml:mo>
                            <mml:mn>0.0060</mml:mn>
                          </mml:mrow>
                        </mml:math>
                      </jats:inline-formula>
                      , representing average relative improvements of 13.11% (AUC) and 8.99% (F1), respectively. Among all evaluated models, DeepOSSA achieved the highest AUC (exceeding 0.8) and demonstrated competitive performance compared with previously published, externally validated Cox nomograms for osteosarcoma. In time-dependent evaluation, its predictive advantage over CoxPH increased during long-term follow-up, where proportional hazards assumptions are most violated. Ablation studies confirmed the necessity of each architectural component, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis demonstrated that the model’s risk predictions are driven by clinically established prognostic factors. By capturing attention-based nonlinear interactions and temporal dynamics, DeepOSSA enables more precise patient stratification than traditional linear models.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>DeepOSSA is a robust and interpretable framework that bridges Transformer-based representation learning with principled survival analysis. It effectively models complex, nonlinear relationships among sparse clinical features and survival outcomes, offering strong potential for translating heterogeneous clinical data into actionable insights for precision oncology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.36985/hbkxef82.title: <b>PENERAPAN <i>ETHNO-5E LEARNING</i> BERBASIS EMPAL GENTONG CIREBON UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KREATIVITAS DAN LITERASI BUDAYA MURID MENGENAI HAKIKAT SAINS DAN METODE ILMIAH </b>
doi:10.36985/hbkxef82.abstract: <jats:p>Materi Hakikat Sains dan Metode Ilmiah di kelas VII SMP merupakan pengetahuan mengenai alam semesta yang diperoleh melalui serangkaian proses ilmiah. Namun, pembelajaran yang cenderung konseptual dan teoritis belum optimal dalam mengembangkan kreativitas dan literasi budaya murid melalui integrasi kebudayaan khas Cirebon dengan konsep IPA. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan kreativitas dan literasi budaya murid melalui penerapan model Ethno-5E Learning yang dipadukan dengan pendekatan CRT dan Ethnoscience berbasis empal gentong khas Cirebon. Penelitian ini menggunakan desain Penelitian Tindakan Kelas yang dilaksanakan dalam tiga siklus, meliputi tahap perencanaan, pelaksanaan tindakan dan observasi, serta refleksi. Subjek penelitian berjumlah 34 murid, 1 guru, dan 1 observer di kelas VII SMPN 2 Sumber. Kreativitas dan literasi budaya diukur menggunakan instrumen pre-test dan post-test yang telah divalidasi oleh dua guru IPA berpengalaman. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rata-rata kreativitas murid meningkat dari 46.91 menjadi 82.50, dengan N-gain sebesar 0.67 dan perbedaan yang signifikan (p = 0,007). Sementara itu, rata-rata literasi budaya meningkat dari 45.00 menjadi 78.23, dengan N-gain sebesar 0.60 dan perbedaan yang signifikan (p = 0.001). Dengan demikian, penerapan Ethno-5E Learning berbasis empal gentong khas Cirebon dapat meningkatkan kreativitas dan literasi budaya murid melalui pembelajaran IPA yang kontekstual dan berakar pada kearifan lokal.</jats:p>

doi:10.12928/admathedust.v13i3.31201.title: EFEKTIVITAS PENGGUNAAN GAME BASED LEARNING BERBANTU GOOGLE SLIDE TERHADAP PEMAHAMAN KONSEP MATERI HIMPUNAN
doi:10.12928/admathedust.v13i3.31201.abstract: <jats:p>Masih kurangnya pemahaman siswa terhadap konsep-konsep matematika, terutama dalam materi himpunan menuntut adanya inovasi dalam pembelajaran. Tujuan dari penelitian ini adalah untuk mengetahui efektivitas penggunaan metode Game Based Learning (GBL) berbantu Google Slide terhadap peningkatan pemahaman konsep siswa. Penelitian ini menerapkan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain pre-experimental jenis one group pretest-posttest. Subjek penelitian merupakan siswa kelas VII.6 SMP Negeri 1 Tarumajaya yang berjumlah 34 orang, yang dipilih melalui Teknik cluster random sampling. Instrumen yang digunakan berupa tes pemahaman konsep yang telah diuji validitas dan reliabilitasnya. Data analisis melalui uji prasyarat dan uji hipotesis dengan bantuan Microsoft Excel.Temuan penelitian menunjukan adanya peningkatan skor rata-rata dari pretest sebesar 37,65 menjadi 75,09 pada posttest. Uji normalitas Shapiro-Wilk menunjukan bahwa data berdistribusi normal. Selanjutnya, uji paired sample t-test menghasilkan nilai t-hitung sebesar 15,13 yang lebih besar dari t-tabel (2,03) dengan p-value < 0,005, yang mengindikasikan adanya perbedaan signifikan antara hasil pretest dan posttest. Selain itu, nilai rata-rata N-Gain sebesar 0,60 tergolong dalam kategori sedang. Temuan ini menunjukan bahwa penggunaan GBL berbasis Google Slide efektif dalam meningkatkan pemahaman konsep matematika siswa.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fnins.2026.1940267.title: Overcoming subject variability in P300 decoding based on quantification by deep learning
doi:10.3389/fnins.2026.1940267.abstract: <jats:p>Binary P300 decoding is a cornerstone of P300-based brain-computer interfaces, enabling applications such as assistive communication, neurorehabilitation, and cognitive monitoring. However, substantial subject variability in EEG patterns poses a major challenge to the development of generalized P300 decoders. To address this problem, this study proposes SQ_EMoE, a subject-variability-aware enhanced Mixture-of-Experts framework that uses the confidence produced by a deep subject-identification network as a practical proxy for trial-level subject distinctiveness. High-confidence trials are routed to subject-specific experts, whereas uncertain trials are redirected to a pooled general expert, allowing the framework to dynamically balance subject-specific specialization and cross-subject generalization. Latent subject representations are further visualized to qualitatively examine subject separability and its relationship with routing behavior. Experiments on eight random subjects from each of two public P300 datasets yielded mean ROC–AUC values of approximately 0.86 on BNCI Horizon 2020 and 0.89 on P300-LINI, outperforming pooled EEGNet and architecture-matched pooled P300MCNN baselines. Ablation experiments further demonstrated the contribution of confidence-controlled fallback to the general expert. To evaluate scalability, the framework was additionally tested on all 22 subjects of P300-LINI. With the original subject-identification network, SQ_EMoE achieved a mean ROC–AUC of 0.8518; after strengthening the subject representation and identification network, performance increased to 0.8760, exceeding the pooled P300MCNN baseline (0.8482) and slightly surpassing the oracle routing or within-subject decoding (0.8744). Leave-one-subject-out experiments further showed that the under-realized SQ_EMoE conservatively redirects most completely unseen-subject trials to the general expert when reliable subject-specific routing is unavailable. These results demonstrate that effective modeling of subject variability, together with adaptive integration of shared and subject-specific representations, provides a promising alternative to conventional one-size-fits-all EEG decoding.</jats:p>

doi:10.31233/osf.io/69js3_v1.title: Cross-clade limits of melanosome-based color prediction: a cautionary machine learning study
doi:10.31233/osf.io/69js3_v1.abstract: Reconstructing dinosaur coloration from fossilized melanosomes has revolutionized paleontology, but most predictive models are trained exclusively on modern birds. Whether these models generalize across clade boundaries to non-theropod dinosaurs remains a critical, untested question. We trained Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest (RF) classifiers on 342 modern bird melanosome measurements spanning five color categories (black, brown, gray, iridescent, and yellow) and validated them on eight theropod fossils with known coloration. QDA achieved 75% validation accuracy (6/8 correct), SVM 62.5% (5/8), and RF 12.5% (1/8) this reflects the destabilizing effect of a severely under-sampled minority class. When applied to four non-theropod specimens (Psittacosaurus and juvenile Diplodocus), all three models collapsed to predicting "yellow", with SVM and RF confidence probabilities between 0.46 and 0.70. This uniform collapse is a synthetic artifact: the yellow class contained only three original training samples, and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) inflated it to parity with the largest class (~173 samples), creating a spurious decision region that intersects the fossil morphospace. Our results demonstrate that aspect-ratio-based classifiers are not only limited within theropods but are actively misleading across clade boundaries when minority-class oversampling is applied naively. We establish a cautionary, reproducible benchmark for deep-time color reconstruction and identify minority-class oversampling as a previously unrecognized source of systematic error in paleocolor machine learning.

doi:10.1080/17449642.2026.2752589.title: Learning mathematics in distracting environments
doi:10.1080/17449642.2026.2752589.abstract: I suggest that digital distraction fosters unequal learning environments for mathematics. This is because learning mathematics is particularly vulnerable to distraction due to the high working memory load required for mathematical problem-solving. At the same time, there is socioeconomic variance in people’s executive functions, including working memory resources. Because of these reasons, I argue that digital distraction should be seen as an obstacle to learning mathematics for learners who come from vulnerable backgrounds. According to Peter Westen’s (1985) three-part analysis of opportunity in equality of opportunity, to guarantee equality of opportunity, obstacles that target already vulnerable groups should be kept to a minimum. By applying Westen’s analysis to this issue, I further argue that achieving equal opportunity for learning mathematics entails limiting digital distraction in the mathematics classroom. On this basis, I then present normative criteria for evaluating the permissibility of digital distraction in learning situations in general.
