doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11115298/v1.title: AI-Adaptive Learning Paths and Task-Difficulty Synchronization: A Longitudinal Study of Student Persistence and Engagement
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11115298/v1.abstract: This longitudinal mixed-methods quasi-experimental study examined how AI-adaptive learning paths and task-difficulty synchronization influenced student persistence and engagement among 79 undergraduate pre-service English teachers enrolled in the “Teaching People with Disabilities” course at the Faculty of Education, Beni-Suef University. The study was conducted across three academic phases from Semester 2 of 2025 to Semester 2 of 2026. Quantitative data were collected using the Student Engagement Scale for AI-Adaptive Learning, platform log data, and twice-weekly experience sampling micro-surveys. Qualitative data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 20 students selected according to high and low persistence patterns. Latent growth curve modeling showed significant growth in engagement over time, and AI-adaptive path quality significantly predicted steeper engagement growth. Cox regression indicated that students in synchronized difficulty states were less likely to disengage. Polynomial regression confirmed a curvilinear “flow” relationship, with engagement highest when tasks were optimally challenging and lower when tasks were boring or anxiety-inducing. Mediation and moderation analyses showed that engagement mediated the relationship between adaptive path quality and persistence, while perceived competence mediated the relationship between synchronization and engagement. Interview findings further revealed that difficulty synchronization functioned as an affective regulator by reducing frustration, supporting competence, and strengthening professional passion for inclusive teaching. However, low-persisters reported concerns about algorithmic rigidity, reduced autonomy, and technical friction. The findings suggest that AI-adaptive learning systems can support persistence when they combine personalized sequencing with transparent, flexible, and pedagogically grounded difficulty regulation.

doi:10.51878/learning.v6i4.15531.title: ANALISIS PERAN GURU DALAM MENANAMKAN SIKAP EMPATI KEPADA PESERTA DIDIK MELALUI PEMBELAJARAN PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA DI KELAS V SD
doi:10.51878/learning.v6i4.15531.abstract:
<jats:p>ABSTRACT 
Cultivating empathy in elementary schools requires learning practices that not only convey moral values but also provide opportunities for students to apply them in their daily interactions. This study aims to describe teachers’ efforts, school support, and the challenges encountered in cultivating empathy through Pancasila Education in Grade V at UPTD SD Negeri 077272 Lolofaoso Tabaloho. The study employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive method. The informants consisted of the school principal, the Grade V teacher, and three students selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, then analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. Data trustworthiness was examined using source and technique triangulation. The findings identified five teacher strategies: role modeling, positive behavioral habituation, collaborative learning, advice and reinforcement, and the creation of a supportive learning environment. These practices were reinforced by school culture and cooperation with parents. Students demonstrated empathetic behaviors through caring, mutual respect, willingness to help, and cooperation, although differences in individual characteristics, environmental influences, and limited instructional time remained challenges. The study concludes that empathy cultivation is implemented through the integration of teachers’ practices and support from the school environment, with students’ behaviors serving as indicators of how empathetic values are applied in everyday life.
ABSTRAK
Penanaman empati di sekolah dasar memerlukan praktik pembelajaran yang tidak hanya menyampaikan nilai moral, tetapi juga memberi ruang bagi peserta didik untuk menerapkannya dalam interaksi sehari-hari. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan upaya guru, dukungan sekolah, serta kendala dalam menanamkan sikap empati melalui pembelajaran Pendidikan Pancasila di kelas V UPTD SD Negeri 077272 Lolofaoso Tabaloho. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode deskriptif. Informan terdiri atas kepala sekolah, guru kelas V, dan tiga peserta didik yang ditentukan melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data diperoleh melalui observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan. Keabsahan data diperiksa menggunakan triangulasi sumber dan teknik. Hasil penelitian mengidentifikasi lima bentuk upaya guru, yaitu keteladanan, pembiasaan perilaku positif, pembelajaran kolaboratif, pemberian nasihat dan penguatan, serta penciptaan lingkungan belajar yang mendukung. Pelaksanaannya diperkuat oleh budaya sekolah dan kerja sama dengan orang tua. Perilaku empatik peserta didik terlihat melalui kepedulian, sikap saling menghargai, kesediaan membantu, dan kemampuan bekerja sama, meskipun perbedaan karakter, pengaruh lingkungan, serta keterbatasan waktu masih menjadi kendala. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa penanaman empati dilaksanakan melalui keterpaduan praktik guru dan dukungan lingkungan sekolah, dengan perilaku peserta didik sebagai indikasi penerapan nilai empati dalam keseharian.</jats:p>

doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26oct749.title: Learning Analytics in Indian Universities: Developing an Early Warning Framework for Student Success
doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26oct749.abstract: <jats:p>Learning Management Systems (LMS) collect behavior data that could help universities identify academic risks before they occur, such as during exams or when students withdraw from a course. While the field of learning analytics has been extensively researched worldwide, evidence on the generalization, effectiveness, and transferability of predictive models and corresponding interventions to Indian universities remains limited. This paper examines the potential of LMS-collected data to detect academic risks early, such as disengagement, poor academic results, lack of assignment submission, and dropout risk. The paper conducts a literature review and conceptual synthesis, focusing on educational data mining, behavior prediction, early warning systems, and learning analytics interventions, particularly in Indian higher education. The review concludes that assessment participation, assignment submission behavior, resource use, and online engagement can support prediction. Still, interpretation should depend on course characteristics, data quality and availability, technological capabilities, and measurement timing. Empirical studies in India show that predicting and analyzing educational engagement is possible, yet evidence on the effectiveness of early warning systems at Indian universities remains limited. We introduce an Indian Early Academic Risk Detection Framework (IEARDF) with five interrelated elements: identifying behavioral markers, contextualizing them, predicting risk, human academic intervention, and decision-making. The study distinguishes predictive performance from intervention effectiveness and emphasizes transparency in decisionmaking, privacy, and equity in student support. The proposed framework provides a basis for empirically validating these concepts.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-77014-6.title: Deep learning-based mitotic quantification for objective adjunct for grading of urothelial carcinoma: a multi-institutional validation study
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-77014-6.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Histological grading of urothelial carcinoma is subject to interobserver variability. We evaluated whether artificial intelligence (AI)-based whole-slide mitotic quantification provides an objective adjunct to histological grading. We developed and validated a deep learning-based mitotic detection framework trained on 91,183 patches with 318,893 annotations. A multi-reader crossover study was conducted in internal (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 149) and external (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 316) cohorts, where three independent pathologists graded cases in unassisted and model-assisted phases. In the combined cohort (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 465), AI-derived mitotic count showed high diagnostic accuracy for high-grade carcinoma (area under the curve [AUC] 0.91, 95% CI 0.89–0.94) at a cut-off of 17.5 mitoses per 2 mm². AI assistance significantly improved mean reader AUC from 0.90 to 0.98 in the internal cohort (
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     = 0.038). In the external cohort, the mean reader AUC increased from 0.84 to 0.95, although this difference did not reach statistical significance (
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     = 0.11). AI assistance also significantly reduced interobserver variability (Fleiss’s κ: 0.72 to 0.93 internally; 0.62 to 0.85 externally; both,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     < 0.001). AI-based mitotic quantification provides an objective and standardized adjunct to histological grading and reduces interobserver variability. This approach may improve diagnostic accuracy and support clinical decision-making, pending prospective validation.
                  </jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11169466/v1.title: From Soft to Hard Constraints in Physics-Informed Extreme Learning Machines: Analysis and Algorithms
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11169466/v1.abstract: Physics-informed extreme learning machines (PIELM) cast the numerical solution of partial differential equations (PDEs) as a single linear least-squares problem by fixing the hidden-layer weights at random, yet the standard soft-constraint formulation augments the PDE residual system with boundary equations, requiring a single coefficient vector to reconcile two competing objectives. A Gram-matrix eigenvalue analysis reveals that this competition suppresses boundary influence along directions where the PDE block dominates, and that uniform row scaling cannot reduce the resulting spectral spread. To eliminate this structural imbalance, we embed Dirichlet boundary conditions directly into the trial function via a lifting term and a boundary-vanishing distance function, so that the resulting least-squares system involves only the interior PDE residual while the one-shot closed-form structure is preserved. Boundary conditions are thereby satisfied to machine precision without entering the coefficient solve. Across seven Dirichlet benchmarks covering Helmholtz, Poisson, Kovasznay Navier--Stokes, wave, and nonlinear reaction equations on convex, non-convex, and curved domains, the hard-constrained formulation yields identically zero boundary residuals and reduces relative L² errors by up to seven orders of magnitude under identical random bases and collocation layouts, at comparable computational cost. The code and data accompanying this manuscript will be made publicly available at https://github.com/xgxgnpu/Physics-informed-vibe-coding/tree/main/HC-PIELM.

doi:10.1093/pnasnexus/pgag359.title: Machine learning detection of small Strombolian eruptions in noisy multi-temporal infrared images: Toward continuous monitoring
doi:10.1093/pnasnexus/pgag359.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We show that a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on denoised multi-temporal infrared images (single images whose red, green, and blue channels hold three consecutive frames so that change between them appears as color) can detect small Strombolian eruptions that previously fell below the detection limits of conventional automated methods. Strombolian eruptions at Mount Erebus, Antarctica, range from large eruptions that eject lava throughout the crater to small eruptions that are mostly contained within the lake. We built these images from thermal imagery of the Ray lava lake and trained a CNN to classify them into three categories: “no eruption”, “small eruption”, and “large eruption”. A training and verification dataset of more than 54,000 images was built through a three-stage process, Clean → Expanded → Denoised, starting from a curated set of eruptions. We applied confident learning (Cleanlab) with five iterations of five-fold Stratified Group K-Fold cross-validation. On the held-out test set, the denoised model achieved a macro F1 of 0.9782, Matthews Correlation Coefficient = 0.9397, and macro AUC = 0.9981. To test temporal generalization, we applied the model to all December 2015 images, recorded over 10 months after the latest training images, during which the lake’s morphology changed. The network detected 49 large and 420 small eruptions. Manual verification of all detections and 2,461 stratified-sampled “no eruption” frames confirmed per-class precision of 0.98 for “large eruption” and 0.97 for “small eruption”, with a population-weighted macro F1 of 0.93.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10680781/v1.title: Predicting high-risk HPV infection and genotype co-infection using genital tract microecological and pathogen characteristics: a machine learning study
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-10680781/v1.abstract: Background Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) is the principal cause of cervical cancer and its precursor lesions. Vaginal microecological dysbiosis and genital tract co-infections may influence HR-HPV acquisition, clearance, and persistence. However, quantitative prediction models integrating vaginal microecological indicators, genital tract pathogens, and HR-HPV genotype co-infection patterns remain limited. Methods This retrospective study included 3,403 patients who underwent concurrent HPV genotyping, vaginal microecological assessment, and genital tract pathogen testing at the gynecology outpatient clinic of Hainan Women and Children’s Medical Center between January 2022 and December 2025. Of these, 765 were HR-HPV-positive and 2,638 were HR-HPV-negative. Candidate predictors were selected using univariable analysis, multicollinearity assessment based on the variance inflation factor (VIF ≦ 4), and the Boruta algorithm. Seven machine learning models were developed, and their hyperparameters were optimized using grid search with 10-fold cross-validation within the training set. Classifier chains (C ≦ C) and ensemble classifier chains (ECC) were applied to the multi-label prediction of HR-HPV genotypes. Model predictions were interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results In multivariable logistic regression, Ureaplasma urealyticum (UU; aOR = 2.051), Chlamydia trachomatis (CT;aOR = 1.982), severe bacterial vaginosis score (aOR = 1.614), abnormal vaginal pH (aOR = 1.375), and sialidase positivity (aOR = 1.747) were independently associated with HR-HPV positivity (all P < 0.05). The random forest model achieved the best discrimination in internal validation (AUC = 0.772, sensitivity 0.735, F1 = 0.650). For the ulti-label task, eight HR-HPV genotypes with at least 30 positive cases were included; the ECC model yielded a higher Jaccard score (0.0226) than the independent-label model (0.0190). SHAP identified UU, age, CT, and cocci abundance as leading predictors, whereas a higher Lactobacillus proportion lowered predicted risk. Conclusions Vaginal microecological dysbiosis and genital tract infections were independently associated with HR-HPV positivity. The random forest model showed moderate discrimination, and ECC provided a modest improvement in multi-genotype prediction. These findings may inform risk-based screening, pending external validation.

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11005575/v1.title: A multimodal CT-based machine-learning model for differentiating pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma from conventional non-small cell lung cancer: an internally validated study
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11005575/v1.abstract: Background: Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC) is difficult to distinguish from conventional non-small cell lung cancer (c-NSCLC) before pathological diagnosis. We evaluated whether clinical–CT semantic features, radiomics and deep-learning features can support this distinction. Methods: After image quality control, 397 patients (83 PSC, 314 c-NSCLC) from three institutions were analysed. Six models (clinical-only, radiomics-only, deep-only, clinical+radiomics, clinical+deep and full fusion) were developed and evaluated with repeated nested cross-validation (five outer folds repeated 20 times, five inner folds), with preprocessing, feature selection, hyperparameter tuning, classifier selection and threshold selection confined to training folds. Discrimination, calibration and operating-point performance were estimated from patient-level out-of-fold predictions. The influence of CT acquisition heterogeneity was examined in sensitivity analyses. Results: The prespecified full fusion model achieved an AUROC of 0.890 (95% CI 0.848–0.930) and an AUPRC of 0.739 (0.643–0.823; PSC prevalence 0.209). At a training-derived high-sensitivity threshold, sensitivity and specificity were 0.855 and 0.755. The clinical+radiomics model performed similarly (AUROC 0.895, 0.851–0.934), the clinical-only model reached 0.843 (0.796–0.887), and deep features alone were not discriminative (AUROC 0.533). Intratumoral low-attenuation area (LAA) presence and LAA ratio were independently associated with PSC. Acquisition parameters alone also discriminated the groups (AUROC 0.901); after adjustment for acquisition variables, radiomics retained incremental value over clinical features (ΔAUROC 0.075, P<0.001), but residual confounding by source or protocol cannot be excluded. Conclusions: Intratumoral LAA features and CT radiomics may help flag PSC before pathology in an internally validated setting, whereas Kinetics-pretrained deep features added no value. Because acquisition heterogeneity may contribute to imaging-based performance and a negative prediction cannot exclude PSC, the model should be regarded as exploratory and requires external validation with standardized acquisition before clinical use.

doi:10.30743/jetcivil.v7i1.14507.title: MORAL AWARENESS-BASED PSYCHOSOCIAL RESILIENCE AMONG STUDENTS WITH SPECIAL NEEDS FOLLOWING FLOODS: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR LOCAL WISDOM-BASED TRAUMA-INFORMED LEARNING
doi:10.30743/jetcivil.v7i1.14507.abstract: <jats:p>This article aims to develop a conceptual framework for local wisdom–based trauma-informed learning to support psychosocial resilience recovery and strengthen moral awareness among students with special needs following floods. The study adopts a conceptual approach through a narrative literature review of trauma-informed education, play as a medium for psychosocial recovery, post-disaster recovery experiences in Indonesia, traditional games in inclusive education, and children's moral development. The analysis identifies key ideas, compares findings and limitations of previous studies, and synthesizes them contextually into a learning design responsive to students' needs. The findings comprise five core conceptual propositions, a mapping of six trauma-informed principles into activity design guidelines, and a five-phase session sequence integrating traditional games, a sense of safety, moral reflection, and academic support. The framework also incorporates ethical considerations, activity adaptations for diverse student needs, and an evaluation design addressing psychosocial indicators, participation, and moral awareness. However, available empirical evidence remains limited, particularly concerning students with special needs after floods. As no field data were collected, the proposed framework cannot yet be considered effective and requires further empirical validation.</jats:p>

doi:10.1142/s0217590826480048.title: DEEP LEARNING APPROACHES FOR HIGH-FREQUENCY CARBON FUTURES PRICE FORECASTING: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF RECURRENT, ATTENTION-BASED, CONVOLUTIONAL AND HYBRID MODELS
doi:10.1142/s0217590826480048.abstract: <jats:p>Carbon markets have expanded rapidly in recent years as part of climate change mitigation efforts. Accurate forecasting of the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU-ETS) futures prices holds significant value for companies, investors and policymakers, who rely on these forecasts for risk management and strategic planning. This study examines the forecasting performance of standalone and hybrid deep learning models for EU allowance (EUA) futures prices using high-frequency open, high, low and close (OHLC) data. The forecasting models include Transformer, Informer, Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), TCN-Transformer and TCN-BiGRU, along with benchmark models. The empirical results show that recurrent neural network-based models generally outperform alternative architectures. Among the standalone models, BiGRU and Transformer deliver the most robust forecasting performance across different frequencies and price series. Among the hybrid models, TCN-BiGRU consistently outperforms TCN-Transformer and the corresponding standalone models in most cases. The findings highlight the importance of modeling temporal dependencies in high-frequency carbon futures markets.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1906004.title: A multi-criteria evaluation of online learning platforms for student engagement and academic performance: an Analytic Hierarchy Process
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1906004.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Online learning platforms have become an important component of higher education, yet their effectiveness depends on multiple educational and technological characteristics. This study aimed to determine the relative importance of four criteria for evaluating online learning platforms from graduate students’ perspective.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We administered a structured questionnaire to 50 graduate students with prior experience in online learning environments. We evaluated Content Quality, User Interface, Accessibility, and Interactivity through pairwise comparisons based on the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). The study aggregated individual judgments, calculated priority weights, and examined the consistency of the pairwise comparisons.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Content Quality received the highest normalized weight (0.416; 41.6%), followed by User Interface (0.297; 29.7%), Interactivity (0.147; 14.7%), and Accessibility (0.140; 14.0%). The results indicate that respondents placed greater relative importance on Content Quality and User Interface when evaluating online learning platforms. The findings show that graduate students assign different levels of importance to educational content, interface usability, interaction, and access when they evaluate online learning platforms. The results provide a quantitative basis for assessing platform characteristics and may help educational institutions and platform developers design and evaluate online learning environments. Further research with larger, more diverse samples is needed to examine whether these priorities apply across institutions and educational contexts.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1038/s42003-026-11119-6.title: Predicting transcriptional burst kinetics from histone modifications with deep learning
doi:10.1038/s42003-026-11119-6.abstract: Transcription is inherently bursty, and burst frequency and burst size provide mechanistically informative phenotypes that are not uniquely determined by mean expression alone. Yet it remains difficult to quantify, at genome scale, how histone-modification landscapes encode these burst kinetics. Here we show that DeepBurst, a deep learning model, predicts gene-specific burst-frequency and burst-size regimes from histone-modification profiles around transcription start sites. DeepBurst uses self-attention to learn combinatorial, position-dependent predictive patterns, with training labels inferred from single-cell transcriptome data using mechanistic bursting models. Across three human cell lines and two label-inference procedures, DeepBurst achieves consistent performance under chromosome-based splits and shows strong cross-cell type generalization. Model interpretation shows that burst frequency benefits from broader chromatin context, whereas burst size depends more strongly on promoter-proximal signals. Model-constrained in silico perturbations further identify histone-profile changes predicted to shift bursting regimes. DeepBurst therefore enables genome-wide mapping from readily measurable histone-modification landscapes to hard-to-assay transcriptional bursting dynamics, while generating testable hypotheses for future perturbation studies.

doi:10.1038/s41746-026-03221-0.title: A hybrid framework for Turner Syndrome facial detection: integrating deep feature learning and geometric prior knowledge under data scarcity
doi:10.1038/s41746-026-03221-0.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Turner Syndrome (TS) is a chromosomal disorder characterized by growth retardation and congenital ovarian dysgenesis. Given the considerable morbidity and mortality, early diagnosis and timely intervention are crucial to improving outcomes. However, the gold standard diagnostic method, karyotype analysis, is time-consuming and requires specialized laboratory expertise. Since TS patients often present distinct facial features, AI-based facial recognition could help identify patients with characteristic appearance as a screening tool. Inspired by the value-of-information principle, we propose a hybrid framework integrating deep feature learning and geometric prior knowledge under data scarcity. We retrospectively constructed this AI facial recognition model for TS detection and validated it in a prospective cohort. The proposed framework achieved 95.41% accuracy, 96.55% sensitivity, and 95.24% specificity, substantially simplifying the diagnostic process. When training was performed only on the hard subset obtained after difficulty-based stratification into three equal groups, the sensitivity reached 100.00%, indicating that all patients were correctly identified. Grad-CAM visualization of key facial regions improved model interpretability and aligned predictions with clinical insights. Our method offers a low-cost and easily accessible approach to TS screening. By allowing for an earlier detection of TS, particularly in medical resource-limited settings, this method has the potential to facilitate timely interventions. This novel paradigm also provides insight for facial recognition-aided diagnosis in other diseases.</jats:p>

doi:10.12928/admathedust.v13i3.31174.abstract: <jats:p>Tujuan dari riset ini ialah untuk meningkatkan motivasi belajar peserta didik dengan menerapkan pendekatan problem based learning (PBL) berbantuan GeoGebra pada bahan ajar Dilatasi di kelas XI C SMA Negeri 4 Palu. Penelitian tindakan kelas (PTK) digunakan dalam riset ini, yang dikerjakan dalam dua siklus. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan observasi, dokumentasi kegiatan pembelajaran, dan angket motivasi belajar. Peserta didik menjadi lebih antusias, lebih aktif dalam diskusi, dan lebih mampu mengaitkan konsep matematika dengan situasi dunia nyata. Oleh karena itu, penerapan pendekatan PBL dengan bantuan GeoGebra bisa menjadi alternatif strategi pembelajaran yang efektif untuk menumbuhkan motivasi belajar matematika peserta didik.</jats:p>

doi:10.62189/ci.1974430.title: A unified ensemble learning framework for electric motor fault diagnosis, thermal state prediction, and remaining useful life estimation
doi:10.62189/ci.1974430.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Electric motors are critical components of modern industrial and transportation systems, making accurate fault diagnosis and predictive maintenance essential for operational reliability. This study proposes a unified machine learning framework for motor fault classification, temperature prediction, and remaining useful life (RUL) estimation using three publicly available electric motor datasets. The proposed pipeline integrates sliding-window segmentation, multi-domain feature extraction, consensus-based feature selection, and physically motivated descriptors derived from electrical and thermal measurements. Five machine learning algorithms, namely Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), XGBoost, LightGBM, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), were systematically evaluated. For fault diagnosis on the Ottawa UOEMD-VAFCVS dataset, evaluated with a file-level train–test split in which all segments of a recording are kept in the same partition, LightGBM achieved the highest performance on the held-out recordings (Accuracy = 1.0000, F1-score = 1.0000, ROC-AUC = 1.0000). Sliding-window segmentation increased the number of trainable observations from 128 to 2,432 and improved the macro F1-score from 0.569 to above 0.994 across all models. For thermal prediction on the PMSM dataset, LightGBM obtained R² values of 0.993, 0.991, 0.989, and 0.987 for rotor, stator winding, stator tooth, and stator yoke temperatures, respectively, with mean absolute errors below 1.4°C. In an exploratory experiment on the synthetically generated EVIoT dataset, which contains no genuine run-to-failure trajectories, XGBoost and LightGBM reached R² = 0.933 on a 30-step smoothed RUL target; this value largely reflects the smoothing of the target and is reported only as a demonstration of the pipeline, not as validated prognostic capability. A Friedman test over N repeated runs indicated significant differences among the five classifiers (χ² = 11.556, p = 0.021, Kendall’s W = W). Within the evaluated configurations, feature-engineered gradient-boosting models matched or exceeded the LSTM baseline at low computational cost; a systematic comparison with end-to-end deep architecture is left for future work.</jats:p>

doi:10.34680/2076-8052.2026.1(143).34-46.title: Research on the impact of the geo-distributed data processing node network model on the results of training reinforced machine learning models
doi:10.34680/2076-8052.2026.1(143).34-46.abstract: <jats:p>The diversity of reinforcement learning algorithms for optimizing computational services in geo-distributed data processing nodes creates conditions where algorithm selection becomes a non-trivial task. Existing publications compare algorithms against each other but do not consider the relationship between the communication network topology of geo-distributed data processing nodes and specific algorithms with their hyperparameters. The absence of a formalized methodology necessitates empirical hyperparameter tuning through trial and error, which increases algorithm convergence time by 3–10 times and significantly raises computational costs. Objective article – to investigate the impact of the geo-distributed data processing node network model on reinforcement learning algorithm training results and to develop a framework for analytically generating hyperparameter recommendations based on network topological characteristics. The LWMECPS Estimator network model evaluation system was developed, based on graph theory and employing a set of metrics for quantitative assessment of network topological properties: average shortest path length C(G), network diameter D(G), network density ρ(G), and average node degree k̄. Based on these metrics, the framework analytically generates hyperparameter recommendations for PPO, SAC, and TD3 algorithms. Experimental evaluation on the LWMECPS GYM test setup – a distributed four-node Kubernetes cluster – demonstrated that after two iterations of analytical formula refinement, SAC and TD3 achieved improvements in average reward of 31 and 10 units respectively, and reductions in network latency of 7 and 2 ms relative to baseline values; PPO yielded a result close to baseline. Overall, the framework improved training stability by 57% and reduced average latency by 3%. The developed approach can be used by MEC system researchers and developers for selecting and configuring reinforcement learning algorithms according to network topology class, significantly reducing computational costs compared to exhaustive hyperparameter search.</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/lfet-10-2025-0124.title: The impact of gamification on language learning: a Quasi-experimental study in higher education
doi:10.1108/lfet-10-2025-0124.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine the role of gamification, conceptualized as a reflective lesson improvement cycle in the areas of engagement, motivation and language proficiency at the higher education level.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A quasi-experimental design spanning 14 weeks was conducted with 300 undergraduate university students as part of a collaborative lesson study process consisting of a cyclical process of: plan, teach, reflect. Statistical analysis was conducted with the use of ANOVA, Cohen’s d and Kruskal–Wallis tests.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The findings showed significant improvement in all language skill areas, with a large effect size (d = 1.37) suggesting gamification made a considerable contribution to engagement and learning outcomes for the students.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Research limitations/implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study was conducted at one university, and involved a 14-week intervention. These factors may limit the generalization of findings. Although we employed appropriate statistical analyses (ANOVA, Cohen’s d, Kruskal–Wallis), more extensive longitudinal studies are necessary to confirm the meaning of sustained findings. Qualitative understanding related to teachers’ reflections could add depth to contextual understandings. Nevertheless, these findings signal a route by which reflective, gamified learning cycles can inform evidence-based approaches to instructional reform, and drive experimental research on language education and engagement-oriented pedagogical innovation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Practical implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results suggest that using gamification in a reflective lesson-study framework has a positive impact on student motivation, engagement and language proficiency. Educators can implement the plan–teach–reflect cycle to enhance lessons by addition integration of game-like components such as; levels and badges, and include feedback to improve lessons in a continual means, while higher education institutions could integrate this into professional learning programs, allowing for teachers use of gamified reflection, as a data-informed application, to improve teaching quality viewed as fostering active learning in varied contexts at higher education institutions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Social implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Gamification encourages students to experience inclusion, collaboration and empowerment through the reflective cycle of gamification experiences within higher education. The collaborative structure of gamification experiences allows for teamwork, self-reflection and accountability. Collaborative activities promote building resilience, creativity and social/environmental responsibility – core competencies for education around Industry 5.0. Gamification experiences strengthen the academic and interpersonal dimensions, making it easier for students to experience challenges as areas of growth. As a socially engaged pedagogical model, gamification promotes equity, engagement and human-centered learning, and supports global commitments to adaptive, sustainable educational reform initiatives.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study provides context-rich, practice-oriented evidence from a 14-week, multi-component gamified language intervention in higher education (n = 300). This investigation adds to predominantly short-term literature by examining longer-term implementation across layers-including sustainable engagement over practice in speaking, listening, reading and writing, and plotting out how a lesson-study cycle hones instruction iteratively. The study does not isolate individual game mechanics; it evaluates the entire instructional package in a real-life classroom environment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1007/s42452-026-09578-x.title: Optimizing distributed resource allocation using GAG-ASGRU in blockchain-enabled federated reinforcement learning systems
doi:10.1007/s42452-026-09578-x.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Resource Allocation (RA) among devices is important as cloud computing rapidly expands, requiring many devices to share their resources. Prior models use various approaches for RA but become less effective as traffic demand increases. This paper proposes Blockchain (BC)-Centric Federated Reinforcement Learning (FRL) for RA, utilizing Galois AMSGrad-ArcTan Softplus Gated Recurrent Units (GAG-ASGRU). First, mobile nodes are implemented. Then, sensed data are sent to the RA phase. Next, network attributes are extracted from data requests. The Crossover Mutation Entropy-based Artificial Gorilla Troop Optimization Algorithm (CME-AGTOA) is used for load balancing. From a dataset containing historical transmission data, features are extracted and reduced using Exponential Fisher’s Linear Discriminant Analysis (E-FLDA). The reduced features are used to train GAG-ASGRU. The trained system tests incoming data requests to identify suitable resources for allocation. If additional response time is required, the request must be authenticated and transmitted over a global network to ensure a prompt response. Authentication uses an Interpolation-centric Algorithm for Secure Hashing 512 (I-ASH512) to generate a Hashcode (HC) and ensure BC verification. Finally, RA is performed by evaluating the HC value with the BC server. The proposed system achieves 98% RA and an Energy Consumption (EC) of 1024 mJ, demonstrating its reliability and better performance compared to previous techniques.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s44401-026-00156-2.title: Discordance between actual care and recommendations by a reinforcement learning model for sepsis
doi:10.1038/s44401-026-00156-2.abstract: Fluid and vasopressor management of sepsis requires a complex set of sequential treatment decisions tailored to individual responses. We examined the frequency and implications of disagreement between reinforcement-learning (RL), using the AI Clinician as a test example, and actual clinical decisions. A novel discordance score was defined as the Euclidean distance between clinical team actions and RL-recommended treatments (range 0 to 5.66), across 25 treatment options of vasopressors and intravenous (IV) fluids. Among 30,678 ICU patients with sepsis cared for across 309,415 time-epochs, discordance was more common among epochs of patients with SOFA > 6 than those with SOFA < 6, and for intravenous fluid choices than for vasopressors. After multivariable adjustment, greater discordance was associated with 90-day mortality (adjusted odds ratio (OR) 1.11, 95%CI: 1.05,1.18) in the SOFA strata > =6 but not for SOFA < = 4 (adjusted odds ratio (OR): 1.02, 95%CI: 0.97,1.08).

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-72542-7.title: A multi-task learning approach for consumer sentiment classification and emotion detection via behavioral data
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-72542-7.abstract: Sentiment analysis captures overall opinion polarity, but it often fails to reveal the key emotions that drive consumer behavior. The recognition of both sentiment and emotions provides crucial information to uncover underlying drivers of consumers behavior and brand loyalty. These important insights enable businesses to detect emerging issues, refine products and services, and personalize consumer experiences. This study proposes a multi-task approach that performs sentiment classification and emotion detection tasks based on consumer reviews and corresponding ratings. To this end, we propose Consumer Sentiment and Emotion Modeling ( COSMO-MT ), a deep learning-based multi-task model for sentiment classification and emotion detection. It begins with an input layer followed by embedding layers that provide sentiment-specific, emotion-specific, and shared embeddings from the input text. Each embedding is processed through shared layers consisting of CNN, BiLSTM, and attention mechanisms. Moreover, several auxiliary features are incorporated into the shared layers to provide explicit linguistic information. The outputs of the shared layers are then passed to task-specific layers for sentiment classification and emotion detection. Finally, corresponding dense and output layers generate predictions for both tasks. We evaluate the efficacy of the proposed COSMO-MT model on two publicly available datasets. It significantly outperforms existing studies and baseline methods.

doi:10.1007/s10791-026-10642-8.title: Quantum-Inspired Variational Optimization of neuromorphic self-supervised heterogeneous graph transformers for multimodal Parkinson’s disease representation learning
doi:10.1007/s10791-026-10642-8.abstract: Early diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease (PD) remains challenging due to the heterogeneous nature of multimodal clinical data, limited annotated datasets, suboptimal multimodal fusion strategies, and the absence of uncertainty-aware decision-making in existing deep learning models. This paper proposes NeuroQ-MGST, a Neuromorphic Self-Supervised Multimodal Graph Transformer with Quantum-Inspired Variational Optimization, for robust and interpretable PD diagnosis. The proposed framework integrates a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) encoder to capture temporally sparse modality-specific representations, a self-supervised contrastive and masked reconstruction objective to exploit unlabeled data, and a Dynamic Heterogeneous Graph Construction (DHGC) with a Hierarchical Multimodal Graph Transformer (HMGT) to model complex cross-modal interactions among speech, gait, neuroimaging, and clinical biomarkers. To improve optimization in highly non-convex multimodal learning spaces, a Quantum-Inspired Variational Optimization (QIVO) module performs structured global representation refinement, while a Bayesian Monte Carlo Dropout layer provides calibrated predictive uncertainty for confidence-aware clinical decision support. Experimental evaluation on the PMMD 2.0 and UCI Parkinson’s Disease datasets demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework, achieving 98.7% accuracy and 98.9% AUC-ROC, outperforming recent state-of-the-art multimodal approaches. Ablation studies validate the contribution of each architectural component, and cross-cohort evaluation on an independent European dataset achieves 95.8% zero-shot accuracy, confirming strong generalization capability. The proposed NeuroQ-MGST framework provides an accurate, interpretable, and uncertainty-aware solution for next-generation AI-assisted Parkinson’s disease diagnosis.

doi:10.25170/kolita.v24i24.8591.title: PROJECT-BASED LEARNING FOR GRAMMAR DEVELOPMENT: A CASE STUDY OF POSTER CREATION ON THE 2025 SUMATRA FLOOD DISASTER
doi:10.25170/kolita.v24i24.8591.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the implementation of Project-Based Learning (PBL) as a pedagogical strategy for facilitating grammar development among first-semester vocational students in the English Business and Public Relations programs. Employing a qualitative case study design, the research explores how poster creation centered on the 2025 Sumatra flood disaster supported students’ mastery of countable and uncountable nouns, relative clauses, and reported speech. Data were collected through analysis of student-produced posters, classroom observation notes, and reflective responses. The findings indicate that embedding grammar instruction within a socially relevant and visually mediated project enhanced students’ grammatical awareness and communicative application. Students demonstrated increased syntactic complexity, improved noun categorization accuracy, and more consistent use of reporting structures. Furthermore, the contextualized theme stimulated engagement, empathy, and collaborative interaction. The study argues that grammar instruction becomes more effective when integrated into authentic, task-based experiences aligned with vocational communication needs. These findings contribute to the growing discourse on contextual grammar pedagogy and provide practical implications for vocational English instruction within student-centered curricular frameworks.contextual pedagogy, grammar instruction, Project-Based Learning, qualitative case study, vocational English.</jats:p>

doi:10.1093/oso/9780197908051.003.0002.title: An organism, not a machine
doi:10.1093/oso/9780197908051.003.0002.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter argues that if Europe is to shape its own destiny, it first needs to understand what kind of political creature it is. The EU, it suggests, is best seen as a learning community perpetually in the making, held together less by shared essence or high destiny than by the repeated work of adaptation. In that light, the Union resembles a living organism: it survives by absorbing shocks, improvising responses, and turning constraints into capabilities. Complexity underwrites this survival. Dispersed authority, overlapping institutions, and layered modes of governance make the Union harder to map, but also harder to kill. Critics often judge the EU by machine standards—coherence, speed, a single chain of command—and predict collapse when they do not see them. However, what looks like malfunction in mechanical terms can be ordinary adaptation in organism terms: a system rebalancing and improvising. This lens clarifies why Europe has always outlived its obituaries.</jats:p>

doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26oct728.title: AI-Based Smart Cow Shelter Analysis and Management System Using Internet of Things and Machine Learning
doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26oct728.abstract: <jats:p>Cow shelters need coordination between animal identification, health observations, activity tracking, environmental factors, feed and water supplies, vaccination schedules, medical records, and operational actions. Precision livestock farming has created useful tools using sensors, identification systems and artificial intelligence. Recent reviews still show problems with combining information, checking data quality, making systems work together, and supporting decisions [1] [2] [7] [10] [24]. This paper introduces a cow-shelter system that connects RFID animal tagging, different types of IoT sensors, ESP32-based data collection at the edge, Wi-Fi communication, Flask web services, MySQL databases, clear rule-based alerts, and machine learning—all within a single management process. The system links animal data with shelter-zone details and keeps track of time, data quality, management actions, and past alerts. The analysis is done in stages: simple rules give alerts, and machine learning comes later once enough labelled and checked data is available. Features used in the analysis include sensor readings, changes over time, average trends, activity summaries, environmental data, and feed and water status. A repeatable way to test the system is created, measuring sensing delay, alert timing, data transmission reliability, dashboard speed, recovery after failure, and how well predictions work. The main contribution is not in technology but in the full system design: an information-to-action process built around animal identity, multiple sensors, resource tracking, records, analysis, alerts, and human input. The paper does not give accuracy or timing results and does not claim the individual parts are new.</jats:p>

doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202662083.title: Metaheuristic physics-informed extreme-learning machine for initial orbit determination of near-Earth asteroids from too-short arcs
doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202662083.abstract:
<jats:p>Modern wide-field astronomical surveys are substantially increasing the volume of observational data and the discovery rate of near-Earth asteroids (NEAs), placing growing demands on efficient and automated initial orbit determination (IOD). The physics-informed extreme-learning machine (PIELM) is an artificial intelligence (AI)-based algorithm for IOD that reconstructs orbital trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. However, optical survey observations often span arcs that are too short to provide sufficient geometric constraints, making it difficult for the standard PIELM to determine a reliable initial orbit. New IOD methods capable of handling too-short arcs (TSAs) are therefore increasingly needed.
We develop a new AI-based method for determining the initial orbits of NEAs from TSAs. It yields reliable initial estimates for subsequent least-squares refinement.
We propose a metaheuristic PIELM method, termed MH-PIELM. An artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm explores candidate solutions defined by a single line-of-sight range, with PIELM embedded directly within the search to reconstruct the corresponding trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. The resulting PIELM loss serves as the fitness function, guiding the ABC algorithm toward promising candidate solutions.
The method was tested on the initial optical observations reported for several NEAs. The MH-PIELM solutions enabled successful least-squares refinement, whose results closely agreed with the Jet Propulsion Laboratory reference solutions. The refined orbits were then used to predict the astrometric positions on the following day. Comparisons with the corresponding observations showed a useful short-term predictive capability for follow-up observations and target recovery, demonstrating the feasibility of the MH-PIELM approach.
MH-PIELM offers a new AI-based strategy for initial orbit determination from TSAs by combining metaheuristic global search with physics-informed machine learning. It extends the applicability of the standard PIELM to challenging TSA observations.</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s12883-026-05447-7.title: Data-driven prognostic stratification in Guillain-Barré syndrome: a machine learning approach
doi:10.1186/s12883-026-05447-7.abstract: Current classifications of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) cannot adequately predict the prognosis and response to immunotherapy of patients, leading to treatment uncertainty and suboptimal outcomes. This study aimed to establish a novel, data-driven classification to identify clinically distinct GBS subtypes and improve outcome prediction. Clinical, laboratory, and electrodiagnostic data from 155 patients with GBS who underwent plasmapheresis were retrospectively analyzed. A clustering algorithm, mixture model, was applied to identify distinct patient subgroups. Subsequently, a streamlined, interpretable decision tree model was developed using the most crucial features. Three distinct clusters were identified. Cluster 1 ( n = 39) represented the most severe presentation, with a median admission GBS disability scale of 5 and the lowest rate of post-treatment independent ambulation at 30 days after symptom onset (12.8%). Cluster 2 ( n = 61) demonstrated the baseline severity (median of GBS disability scale: 3) at admission and the most favorable prognosis, with 54.1% having independent ambulation. Cluster 3 ( n = 55), characterized by prominent demyelinating features, showed a notably higher response rate to plasmapheresis (85.5% of patients improving by ≥ 1 GBS disability scale), despite presenting with intermediate severity (median of GBS disability scale: 4). The decision tree model, incorporating five common clinical and electrophysiological variables, achieved excellent classification fidelity to practically approximate the clusters (accuracy: 0.877). Machine learning identified three GBS subtypes with distinct prognoses and clinical trajectories to plasmapheresis. Derived from these findings, a simple five-variable decision tree provides a practical tool for early prognostic stratification, facilitating early prognostic outcome estimation and risk-adapted clinical monitoring.

doi:10.3389/fvets.2026.1952589.title: Deep learning for diagnostic and clinical decision support in companion animals: a systematic review of CNN- and LSTM-based approaches
doi:10.3389/fvets.2026.1952589.abstract: <jats:p>Early disease detection prior to the onset of advanced clinical signs remains a critical imperative in veterinary medicine. This systematic review provides a methodological synthesis of Convolutional Neural Networks and Long Short-Term Memory networks applied to diagnostic and clinical decision support in canine and feline patients, evaluating both algorithmic performance and clinical feasibility. Adhering to the PICO-CS framework and PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we queried Scopus and Web of Science for peer-reviewed studies published between 2021 and 2026, retrieving a final corpus of 57 primary studies. Eleven clinical domains were identified, with evidence heavily concentrated in Oncology (28.1%), Cardiology (15.8%), and Pulmonology (12.3%). CNN architectures predominated in spatial imaging modalities—including radiographs, clinical photography, ultrasonography, and microscopic imagery—whereas LSTM networks were deployed for temporal signals and sensor-derived telemetry. Binary classification tasks achieved the highest performance metrics (accuracy reaching up to 99%), whereas multi-class formulations exhibited broader variability due to dataset imbalance. Cross-study benchmarking revealed substantial heterogeneity in datasets, evaluation metrics, and validation protocols, while reliance on high-performance computational infrastructure poses a barrier to point-of-care deployment in resource-constrained clinics. We conclude that while deep learning architectures hold significant promise as clinical decision-support tools, transitioning to routine veterinary practice requires prospective external validation, representative open-access datasets, and lightweight models optimized for conventional clinical hardware.</jats:p>

doi:10.62885/edusci.v4i1.1323.title: Implementation of the PjBL-STEM Model Utilizing Algodoo for Science Learning in Improving Cognitive Learning Outcomes, Critical Thinking Skills, and Creative Thinking Skills
doi:10.62885/edusci.v4i1.1323.abstract:
<jats:p>Aims. This research aimed to determine the effect of the PjBL-STEM model using Algodoo on science learning.
Methods. This research employs a quasi-experimental design with a nonequivalent control group. The population selected was the Semester 2 Class VIII students at SMPN 1 Sumber in 2023/2024. The sample of this study comprised 25 students from classes VIII C and VIII D. Data were collected through essay tests and student response questionnaires. Data were processed using prerequisite tests, the independent-samples t-test, and the N-Gain test.
Result. The results showed an increase in average pretest and posttest scores for cognitive learning outcomes from 56 to 88 points, with an N-Gain score of 0.73, categorized as high. Meanwhile, based on critical thinking skills and creative thinking skills, each student experienced an increase in each indicator, with an average pretest score of 45.5 and 43.35 points and an average posttest score of 83.34 points and 87.75 points. Each N-Gain was 0.69 and 0.78, categorized as medium and high, respectively. Students gave a very positive response to the PjBL-STEM model using Algodoo, with an average score of 85.55%, indicating that all aspects received a very positive response.
Conclusion. The interesting aspect received the highest average score (86.82%), followed by achieving learning objectives (86.80%) and convenience (83.03%).
Implementation. These results indicate that the PjBL-STEM model, which uses Algodoo for science learning, can significantly improve students' cognitive learning outcomes, critical thinking skills, and creative thinking skills</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s12911-026-03580-4.title: Application of machine learning prediction models for in-hospital mortality in diabetic sepsis patients: a study based on the MIMIC IV database
doi:10.1186/s12911-026-03580-4.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Sepsis complicated by diabetes mellitus represents a significant clinical challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Accurate prognostication of in-hospital mortality in this complex patient population is crucial for optimizing clinical decision making, resource allocation, and patient management strategies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted a retrospective cohort study utilizing data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-IV) database. The study focused on adult ICU patients with concurrent diagnoses of sepsis and diabetes mellitus. Six machine learning algorithms were evaluated for their predictive performance: Logistic Regression (LR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), XGBoost and LightGBM. Additionally, we assessed the prognostic capability of the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score. Model discrimination was quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). To enhance model interpretability, we employed SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values to elucidate the relative importance of predictor variables.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study cohort comprised 7716 patients, with 1357 (17.6%) experiencing in-hospital mortality. Among the machine learning models evaluated, GBDT exhibited superior predictive performance achieving an AUC of 0.792 (95% CI: 0.769–0.814). This performance surpassed that of other machine learning algorithms and the conventional SOFA score. SHAP analysis provided valuable insights into the hierarchical importance of various clinical and demographic features contributing to the GBDT model’s predictions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our findings demonstrate the potential of machine learning approaches in accurately predicting in-hospital mortality among ICU patients with sepsis and diabetes mellitus. These advanced analytical techniques outperform traditional scoring systems such as SOFA. The integration of SHAP values enhances model interpretability, potentially facilitating the adoption of these predictive tools in clinical practice. Further multi-center validation studies and prospective trials are warranted to confirm the generalizability of these results and to explore the clinical impact of implementing such models in diverse healthcare settings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.25073/2588-1086/vnucsce.7456.title: 6G Semantic Intelligence for UAV Anti Jamming: A Transformer Augmented Predictive Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework
doi:10.25073/2588-1086/vnucsce.7456.abstract:
<jats:p>This paper proposes a semantic-aware predictive hybrid Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) framework for UAV anti-jamming communications under partial observability and nonstationary interference. The framework integrates Transformer-based channel-wise interference prediction, adaptive semantic-rate control, energy-aware horizontal UAV mobility, and hierarchicaldiscrete–continuous control within a unified POMDP. The semantic payload is explicitly coupledwith achievable rate, transmission duration, delivery success, and propulsion–communication energy,while predictor learning is separated from the on-policy PPO update. Evaluation over 50 independenttrials shows that, at a jammer power of 30 dBm and CSI error variance of 10-3, the proposed methodachieves a semantic accuracy of 0.751 ± 0.005, a task-success rate of 0.715 ± 0.007, and an SINRof 6.48 ± 0.28 dB, while consuming 23.58 ± 0.20 J/slot. The closest LSTM-Hybrid PPO baselineobtains 0.694±0.006, 0.642±0.006, 5.37±0.26 dB, and 25.46±0.17 J/slot, respectively. The Transformer predictor achieves an RMSE of approximately 0.039 under perfect CSI and 0.091 at a CSIerror variance of 10-2. Under an unseen jammer-policy shift, online predictor adaptation recoverssemantic accuracy to approximately 0.859, compared with 0.746 for a frozen predictor. Ablation results indicate complementary contributions from prediction, semantic-rate adaptation, mobility, andhierarchical hybrid control.Keywords: Deep Reinforcement Learning, Predictive Anti-Jamming, Semantic Communication,Transformer-Based Prediction, UAV Networks.

doi:10.61784/wjsr3021.title: TENNIS RACKET HANDLES, OVERGRIPS, AND MOTOR SKILL LEARNING: A NARRATIVE REVIEW
doi:10.61784/wjsr3021.abstract: <jats:p>Overgrips modify the geometry and surface of a tennis racket handle, but their role in skill learning is unclear. This narrative review evaluates articles published since 2016 on grip measurement, vibration, hand loading, and equipment adaptation for beginners. The review distinguishes the properties of the finished grip from hand position and the force applied during a stroke. Recent techniques measure grip pressure and estimate tendon forces, although some studies include only one or two participants. Comparisons between playing levels describe differences in grip-force timing and magnitude without establishing their causes. Vibration measurements also depend on how firmly a player holds the racket. Most publications on equipment adaptation deal with balls, racket size, and court dimensions. In the evaluated literature, direct evidence linking overgrip wrapping characteristics with motor learning remains limited. Research on the topic in Chinese university tennis courses could start with measuring the finished grip, then examine immediate use and stroke control before assessing retention and transfer. This sequence would allow manufacturing consistency and learning outcomes to be tested separately. An automated overgrip wrapping system requires a usable prototype and its direct evaluation.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fphys.2026.1922656.title: Dynamic machine learning architecture integrating time-phased predictions for acute kidney injury following extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
doi:10.3389/fphys.2026.1922656.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a frequent, severe complication of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) therapy, substantially contributing to unfavorable outcomes. No effective machine learning (ML) models exist for early, accurate detection. This study developed a two-phased prediction model using clinical data from pre-ECMO and on-ECMO stages for ECMO-induced AKI (ECMO-AKI), and further integrated two models to formulate a consensus risk-stratification strategy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This retrospective study included 344 patients undergoing ECMO from 2015 to 2026. Clinical and laboratory variables from pre-ECMO and on-ECMO stages were respectively used to develop two ECMO-AKI diagnostic models via a analytical framework incorporating 12 ML algorithms. Multiple analytical methods were utilised to evaluate pre-ECMOAKI and on-ECMOAKI models. The Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) method was used to interpret two models and to quantify and visualize the features. Latent class growth mixture model (LCGMM) was applied to investigate the association between longitudinal feature trajectories and ECMO-AKI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Pre-ECMOAKI and on-ECMOAKI models incorporated into 12 ML, yielding 66 and 91 combinations, respectively. Among these, glmBoost + gradient boosting machine (GBM) as a superior algorithm for predicting ECMO-AKI. Pre-ECMOAKI (9 features) and on-ECMOAKI (10 features) models exhibited superior discrimination performance, with area under curve (AUC) of 0.867 (95%CI: 0.819-0.911) and 0.907 (95%CI: 0.870-0.941) in derivation cohort, 0.732 (95%CI: 0.678-0.780) and 0.803 (95%CI: 0.711-0.889) in held-out validation cohort, respectively. A risk-stratification framework integrating pre-ECMOAKI and on-ECMOAKI predictions achieved a class-specific precision of 90.23% for ECMO-AKI events in the consensus high-risk group and 90.79% for non-ECMO-AKI events in the consensus low-risk populations. SHAP analysis reveals that endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX), cardiopulmonary resuscitation time (CPRT) and total bilirubin (TBI) are important feature variables in two models. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) regression, threshold effect analysis, and LCGMM indicated EASIX &gt; 4.7 (with sustained increasing trend), CRPT &gt; 24 min, and TBI &gt; 20.2 μmol/L (with continuous upward trend) were associated with an elevated ECMO-AKI risk.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Two-phased dynamic prediction models (pre-ECMOAKI and on-ECMOAKI) were constructed based on glmBoost +GBM, which act as an accurate and interpretable diagnostic tool for ECMO-AKI. Based on consistency analysis of predictions of two models, this framework allows early risk stratification and thus holds potential for individualized management.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202660440.title: Data representation matters: Optimising machine learning for X-ray source classification by leveraging spatio-spectral information
doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202660440.abstract:
<jats:p>Distinguishing between faint extended X-ray sources, such as galaxy clusters, and point-like sources, primarily active galactic nuclei (AGNs), is a fundamental yet challenging task in X-ray surveys, which are crucial to cosmological studies and astrophysical source population analyses.
This paper presents a benchmark comparison of convolutional neural network models for classifying simulated observations of AGNs and galaxy clusters, focussing on the impact of data representation and interpretability of those data. XMM-Newton
We systematically evaluated 1D, 2D, 2D+1D, and 3D CNNs trained on distinct data representations derived from simulated observations of AGNs and clusters: 1D (spectral), 2D (imaging), and 3D (event cube) data. Our experimental design leverages the physical constraints of the apparent size–redshift relation to ensure realistic source populations at fixed flux limits. We further applied 3D-GradCAM to interpret the learned features and assess the physical basis for the model's decision making to move beyond black-box classification. XMM-Newton
Our results demonstrate that increased spectral resolution enhances classifier performance using 1D data and 2D spatial information provides a strong morphological baseline, the integration of both domains yields significant diagnostic gains. We find that a 3D CNN architecture applied directly to spatio-spectral event cubes provides the most robust performance, with superior consistency across cross-validation folds. Interpretability analysis reveals that the 3D model autonomously learns to distinguish the diffuse thermal emission of the intracluster medium from the localised, non-thermal power-law signatures of AGNs.
The 3D CNN exploits multi-dimensional correlations that are lost in lower dimensional projections. While the performance gain over combined 2D and 1D baselines is marginal, the 3D approach demonstrates an inherent ability to perform an implicit background characterisation. By operating directly on total photon counts within event cubes, this method bypasses the need for manual background subtraction and modelling, offering a consistent, streamlined, end-to-end pipeline for the automated classification of X-ray sources in large-scale catalogues.</jats:p>

doi:10.36618/competitive.v21i1.4854.title: CHATBOT PANDUAN FITUR APLIKASI WAKTOO MENGGUNAKAN TF-IDF DAN SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE
doi:10.36618/competitive.v21i1.4854.abstract: <jats:p>Efisiensi layanan karyawan merupakan aspek penting dalam manajemen sumber daya manusia. Namun, keterbatasan jumlah personel sering menghambat penyampaian informasi dan panduan penggunaan aplikasi perusahaan kepada karyawan baru, khususnya mahasiswa magang. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan chatbot sebagai media pendamping dalam memberikan informasi terkait penggunaan aplikasi Waktoo HRM, meliputi presensi, manajemen tugas, dan kebijakan perusahaan. Dataset yang digunakan terdiri atas pattern, response, dan label intent yang disimpan pada database MongoDB. Sistem chatbot dibangun menggunakan Streamlit dengan pendekatan Natural Language Processing (NLP), memanfaatkan Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) sebagai metode ekstraksi fitur dan Support Vector Machine (SVM) melalui implementasi LinearSVC pada pustaka Scikit-Learn sebagai algoritma klasifikasi intent. Evaluasi model dilakukan menggunakan train-test split 80:20 serta Stratified 5-Fold Cross Validation pada data latih untuk mengukur konsistensi dan kemampuan generalisasi model. Kinerja model dievaluasi menggunakan metrik accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, dan confusion matrix. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan accuracy sebesar 84,44%, precision 85,69%, recall 84,44%, dan F1-score 84,01%. Selain itu, cross-validation menghasilkan rata-rata F1-score sebesar 0,87 dengan standar deviasi 0,02 yang menunjukkan performa model yang konsisten. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kombinasi TF-IDF dan SVM efektif dalam mengklasifikasikan intent pengguna pada chatbot Waktoo HRM.</jats:p>

doi:10.4038/p.v17i1.91.title: අධිප්‍රජානනය, සතිපට්ඨාන සූත්‍රය හා ඉගෙනුම් - ඉගැන්වීම් ක්‍රියාවලිය පිළිබඳ අධ්‍යයනයක් - A Study of Metacognition and the Satipatthana Sutta in Relation to the Teaching and Learning Process
doi:10.4038/p.v17i1.91.abstract: <jats:p>This article examines the relationship between the modern psychological concept of metacognition and the teachings found in the Satipatthana Sutta within the Buddhist tradition. Metacognition refers to awareness and regulation of one’s own thinking processes, including the ability to observe, evaluate, and guide cognitive activities. The study explores how similar ideas appear in early Buddhist teachings, particularly through the practice of mindfulness described in the Satipatthana Sutta. Using a qualitative and interpretive approach, the discussion analyses primary Buddhist texts together with relevant secondary sources. The analysis shows that the mindfulness practices explained in the Satipatthana framework encourage continuous awareness of mental states, actions, and experiences, which closely parallels the functions of metacognitive awareness described in educational psychology. The article argues that these Buddhist insights can contribute meaningfully to contemporary discussions of learning, self-regulation, and reflective thinking. By comparing these two perspectives, the study highlights the relevance of classical Buddhist teachings for understanding  and developing metacognitive skills in modern educational contexts. </jats:p>
