doi:10.3389/fbinf.2026.1949507.title: Improving cognitive impairment classification in Alzheimer’s disease using tabular diffusion augmentation and late fusion deep learning
doi:10.3389/fbinf.2026.1949507.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Alzheimer’s disease is the most common cause of dementia and is often detected after substantial neurodegeneration has occurred. Distinguishing cognitively impaired individuals from cognitively normal ones using genetic and demographic data can help characterize the genetic contributions to impairment. Deep learning can capture complex, nonlinear genetic relationships among these features, but its use in clinical genomics is limited by the small size of patient cohorts.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We evaluated whether TabDDPM-based synthetic augmentation could improve cross-sectional classification of cognitive impairment using demographic and APOE-region genotype features. From 542 ADNI participants, we created a stratified 433-participant development cohort (80%) and a 109-participant held-out cohort (20%). Eight predictive models were evaluated using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation with 10 repeats. The 346 or 347 participants in the outer training partition were divided into three internal TabDDPM subsets: 80% for generator training, 10% for hyperparameter selection, and 10% reserved for internal generator evaluation. Run-specific synthetic samples were added to the outer training partition at 3×, 5×, 7×, and 10× augmentation. The selected predictive model configuration and augmentation ratio were then evaluated on the 109-participant held-out cohort for assessment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The synthetic data showed similar demographic structure and common-variant genotype distribution to the real cohort. Synthetic augmentation improved mean AUC across nonlinear models. The best-performing model, a categorical late-fusion neural network, achieved a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.781 with 7× augmentation, compared with 0.738 using real data alone. For the 7× versus 0× comparison, the internal cross-validation analysis yielded a raw paired DeLong p-value of 0.0012 and a Holm-adjusted p-value of 0.03. This improvement was observed in the 109-participant held-out cohort: AUC increased from 0.721 to 0.769, with gains in both sensitivity (0.68–0.77) and specificity (0.58–0.66).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These results suggest that synthetic data augmentation can improve deep learning performance in data-constrained clinical genomic classification. The approach does not replace real patient data, but it can help models learn more stable patterns from cohorts with limited sample size. Because the framework uses standard tabular genomic and demographic features, it may extend to other genomic classification tasks where individual-level patient data are limited.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1007/s44163-026-02382-x.title: The personalized psychological intervention optimization system of transformer temporal modeling and deep reinforcement learning collaboration
doi:10.1007/s44163-026-02382-x.abstract: Long-term digital psychological intervention faces issues such as delayed state feedback, observation absence, and scattered individual responses. Static input is difficult to retain cross-period dependencies, and a unified strategy will also widen user differences and cause fluctuations in continuous actions. To address these problems, a personalized intervention system that combines Transformer temporal modeling and proximal policy optimization is constructed. Structured psychological state representation organizes continuous behaviors and subjective feedback into an updateable sequence. The Transformer encoder extracts long-term dependencies and local mutations, the individual embedding absorbs user response deviations, and the Kullback–Leibler (KL) constraint inhibits adjacent strategy jumps. The experiment uses StudentLife data and accompanying simulations, semi-synthetic data. The cumulative reward of the complete model reaches 634.7 ± 21.8, with a 95% confidence interval of 619.11–650.29. The rule strategy, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) immediate state model, and the configuration without individual embedding are 412.6 ± 38.4, 528.3 ± 42.7, and 561.9 ± 35.2, respectively. The differences among the three groups, after Holm correction, all reach significant levels ( p < 0.001). The complete model enters the stable range after 1620 rounds, and the variance of the reward after convergence drops to 19.4. The rate of change in emotional intensity, the improvement value of state stability, and the cumulative variance of individual rewards is 0.091, 0.052, and 28.4, respectively. The ablation results show that temporal encoding mainly affects long-term benefits and convergence stability, and individual embedding focuses on reducing the dispersion among users. The existing evidence supports strategy optimization in non-clinical environments, but does not constitute a psychological mechanism explanation, causal effect proof, or clinical effectiveness conclusion.

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11448274/v1.title: Predictive Degradation Modelling of Solar Encapsulants: A Deep Learning Approach to IEC 61215 Thermal Cycling
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11448274/v1.abstract: The operational lifespan of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems relies heavily on the thermo-mechanical stability of Ethylene-Vinyl Acetate (EVA) encapsulants. However, evaluating long-term durability using traditional accelerated physical aging protocols, such as IEC 61215 thermal cycling, is highly resource-intensive and often fails to capture complex, nonlinear degradation kinetics. To bypass these limitations, this study introduces a computational machine learning framework to forecast the structural degradation of mica nanoclay-reinforced EVA nanocomposites. A high-fidelity, physics-informed synthetic dataset (1,220 data points) was generated to model tensile strength decay and microcrack density evolution across four formulation variants (0, 1, 3, and 5 wt.% mica nanoclay) over a simulated 1,500-cycle exposure horizon (-40°C to + 85°C). A Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network and a Random Forest (RF) ensemble regressor were deployed to map these defect evolution parameters. Both architectures demonstrated exceptional predictive accuracy, with the RF achieving an R² of 0.994 and the LSTM achieving an R² of 0.993. The computational models mathematically validated that an optimal 5 wt.% filler concentration significantly delays crack coalescence, extending the 50% mechanical endurance limit. This data-driven approach fundamentally accelerates the reliability-driven design of next-generation, environmentally resilient photovoltaic modules without the need for multi-month destructive testing.

doi:10.1021/acsomega.6c07307.title: A Gradient Boosting-Based Machine Learning Model for the Prediction of the Hardness of Thermoplastic Polymers
doi:10.1021/acsomega.6c07307.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Modern experimental techniques can measure the hardness of thin films and structural features on the nanometer scale. These techniques can be applied to many types of materials, but as the hardness of the material decreases, more specialized and precise equipment is needed. For polymers, this analysis can be relatively expensive and time-consuming, so here we demonstrate a gradient-boosting-based machine-learning model that can provide a fast and reliable prediction of the hardness of thermoplastic polymers. This model is based on the XGBoost algorithm and shows reasonably good performance with an R2 value of 0.46–0.69. The features used in this study include experimental (mechanical and thermal properties) and molecular descriptors obtained using RDKit. The model is robust, with reasonable performance obtained when key experimental features are removed and/or when the selection of polymers is reduced. This suggests that this approach will be useful in “bottom-up” strategies for polymeric materials development.</jats:p>

doi:10.3390/jmse14211982.title: TGB-UNet: Dual-Scale Topographic Gating and Topography-Guided Boundary Learning for Instantaneous Waterline Extraction on Tidal Flats
doi:10.3390/jmse14211982.abstract: <jats:p>Extracting instantaneous waterlines on tidal flats is challenging because spectral confusion among turbid water, wet bare tidal flats, and residual channel water can cause misclassification and boundary displacement. This study proposes a Topography-Guided Boundary U-Net (TGB-UNet) for Hangzhou Bay using Gaofen-1 and Gaofen-6 multispectral imagery. The model incorporates slope and local relative elevation through dual-scale topographic gating and topography-guided auxiliary boundary learning. Compared with FCN-8s, vanilla U-Net, and HED-UNet, TGB-UNet achieved the best mean performance across six evaluation metrics. Its F1 and boundary F1 scores reached 98.44% and 83.52%, respectively, while the average symmetric surface distance (ASSD) was 50.13 m, a reduction of 44.41% relative to vanilla U-Net. Ablation experiments showed that direct terrain concatenation did not yield consistent gains, whereas gated fusion and topography-guided boundary learning improved waterline localization. Tidal-level-stratified comparisons showed the largest absolute reductions in ASSD and the 90th-percentile boundary distance under low-tidal-level conditions. A spatial holdout test in an adjacent coastal sector further showed that TGB-UNet retained its advantage over vanilla U-Net across all six metrics. These results indicate that incorporating static topographic priors through dual-scale gating and topography-guided auxiliary boundary learning helps improve instantaneous waterline localization at complex water–land interfaces on tidal flats.</jats:p>
doi:10.3390/jmse14211982.venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

doi:10.1007/s44197-026-00652-6.title: Anthropometry–Blood Pressure Mapping in China: Double/Debiased Machine Learning Across 38 Ethnic Groups
doi:10.1007/s44197-026-00652-6.abstract: Hypertension is among the most prevalent cardiometabolic diseases globally, and abnormalities in body weight and composition represent the most modifiable and population-effective intervention targets. Ethnic groups in China exhibit substantial differences in genetic background, dietary patterns, and lifestyle, which may contribute to ethnic heterogeneity in the associations between obesity phenotypes and blood pressure. However, cross-ethnic studies examining body composition–hypertension associations remain limited. This study aimed to quantify the associations between seven body composition indices and prevalent hypertension, and to characterize heterogeneity across 38 ethnic groups in China. Based on cross-sectional survey data from 30,035 adults across 38 ethnic groups in China collected between 2018 and 2025, we employed a double/debiased machine learning framework combined with generalized random forests (DML–GRF) to systematically evaluate the associations between seven body composition indices—body mass index, body roundness index, body fat percentage, body water percentage, visceral fat level, lean body mass, and muscle-to-fat ratio—and hypertension, as well as their ethnic heterogeneity. Body mass index, body roundness index, body fat percentage, visceral fat level, and lean body mass were positively associated with hypertension, whereas body water percentage and muscle-to-fat ratio showed inverse associations. Significant ethnic heterogeneity was observed for all seven indices ( P ≤ 0.001): the Salar and Hui showed the strongest associations across multiple indices, whereas no index reached significance in the Derung, Monba, and Gelao, where limited stratum size precludes an interpretation of no association. Based on association profiles, the 38 ethnic groups were classified into four patterns: high-sensitivity (13 groups), fat-sensitive (7 groups), muscle-protective (6 groups), and relatively tolerant (12 groups), with statistically significant differences across all indices among the four patterns. The strength of associations between body composition indices and hypertension varies substantially across Chinese ethnic groups. These findings provide an evidence base for developing ethnicity-specific hypertension prevention strategies and support a shift from universal body mass index-based screening toward precision public health approaches.
doi:10.1007/s44197-026-00652-6.venue: Journal of Epidemiology and Global Health

doi:10.1515/revneuro-2026-0186.title: Application of interpretable deep learning in brain age prediction: a comprehensive review
doi:10.1515/revneuro-2026-0186.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Brain age prediction has emerged as a promising approach for characterizing interindividual differences in brain aging. However, the increasing complexity of deep learning models has created a substantial gap between predictive performance and interpretability. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) has, therefore, become increasingly important for identifying the neuroanatomical features underlying brain age predictions. This review systematically examines interpretable deep learning approaches for brain age prediction. A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect identified 32 eligible studies, which were organized into post-hoc explanation methods and intrinsically interpretable models. We further propose a four-dimensional operational framework encompassing Algorithm Reliability, Robustness and Reproducibility, Biological Validation, and Clinical Utility. The reviewed literature indicates a transition from localized feature attribution toward generative, disentangled, attention-based, and anatomically meaningful representations. However, interpretation remains sensitive to methodological and imaging-related factors, while brain age gap (BAG) is also influenced by age dependency, calibration, reference-population composition, and site heterogeneity. Future research should emphasize standardized evaluation and prospective clinical validation to develop reliable and clinically meaningful brain age biomarkers.</jats:p>

doi:10.1038/s41598-026-76866-2.title: HGCN-GRU: temporal memory learning for hypergraph sequential recommendation
doi:10.1038/s41598-026-76866-2.abstract: Sequential recommendation systems aim to predict users’ future interactions by modeling the temporal evolution of their preferences. Hypergraph-based representations are particularly well suited to this setting because they can capture high-order, non-pairwise dependencies among multiple users and items within a unified relational structure, enabling the modeling of complex collaborative patterns beyond conventional pairwise interactions. Despite this advantage, existing hypergraph-based sequential recommenders often rely on shallow temporal propagation, such as residual gating or single-step hypergraph convolution across adjacent snapshots, which limits their ability to preserve long-range semantic dependencies across distant time periods. Moreover, when trained solely with supervised signals, these models suffer from data sparsity, as the limited interaction density in real-world scenarios provides insufficient supervisory evidence for learning discriminative representations. In this work, we propose HyperGraph Convolutional Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (HGCN-GRU), a sequential recommendation framework that addresses both limitations through two complementary contributions. First, we replace the residual gating mechanism of existing hypergraph-based models with a Gated Recurrent Unit coupled with a temporal attention module. Unlike single-step propagation, the GRU models the sequence of per-period hypergraph embeddings as a temporal process, enabling the accumulation of semantic information across distant time steps, while the attention module adaptively emphasizes the most informative historical periods. Second, we introduce a self-supervised contrastive learning objective that generates auxiliary training signals directly from the hypergraph structure via stochastic hyperedge dropout augmentation. By aligning user representations derived from two independently augmented views, the contrastive module compensates for the scarcity of supervised signals in sparse interaction settings without requiring additional annotations. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets of varying density, namely Amazon Review, MovieLens-1 M, and Yelp, demonstrate that HGCN-GRU consistently outperforms seven competitive baselines across all evaluation metrics. The proposed model consistently outperforms the strongest baseline across datasets with varying interaction densities. The improvements remain substantial across datasets, including the sparsest setting, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework under different levels of interaction sparsity. Ablation studies further confirm that the GRU-based temporal memory and the contrastive objective address complementary weaknesses of existing hypergraph recommendation frameworks.

doi:10.61401/rmaps.v4i1.745.title: A Review on Analysis of K-Means Clustering Machine Learning Algorithm based on Unsupervised Learning
doi:10.61401/rmaps.v4i1.745.abstract: <jats:p>Purpose: This study revisits the K-means clustering algorithm as a core technique of unsupervised machine learning and explains, in plain terms, how it groups unlabeled data into meaningful clusters.Methodology: The paper combines a narrative review of studies published mostly between 2021 and 2026 with a manual, step-by-step computation of K-means on a small one-dimensional dataset of nine values, using Euclidean distance and K=2. The final partition is then checked with the within-cluster sum of squares and the silhouette coefficient for K values from one to four.Results: The algorithm stabilized after three reassignment rounds and produced the clusters {2, 3, 4, 10, 11, 12} and {20, 25, 30}, with centroids of 7 and 25. The within-cluster sum of squares fell from 348.00 to 150.00, and the mean silhouette coefficient reached 0.660, although K=3 gave a higher value of 0.711.Conclusions: K-means is simple, fast, and easy to interpret, yet its output depends strongly on the chosen number of clusters and on the starting centroids.Limitations: The worked example relies on a small one-dimensional dataset and does not test high-dimensional, noisy, or streaming data.Contributions: The paper offers a transparent teaching case that links the classic procedure to current validation practice and to recent applied studies.</jats:p>
doi:10.61401/rmaps.v4i1.745.venue: Review of Multidisciplinary Academic and Practice Studies

doi:10.21067/bimasakti.v9i1.13190.title: PENERAPAN METODE EXTREME LEARNING MACHINE UNTUK MENINGKATKAN AKURASI ALGORITMA K-NEAREST NEIGHBORS DALAM KLASIFIKASI PENYAKIT KANKER PAYUDARA
doi:10.21067/bimasakti.v9i1.13190.abstract: <jats:p>Breast cancer is a major health concern that poses a significant threat to women across the globe. While early detection plays a vital role in improving survival rates, achieving high diagnostic accuracy continues to be a challenge. In this study, the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm is employed as a fundamental classification technique, which is further enhanced using the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) to boost the accuracy of breast cancer classification. The dataset utilized in this research was obtained from Kaggle, comprising 569 samples with 32 features. The research methodology involves data preprocessing, dividing the dataset into training and testing sets with different ratios, and assessing the model’s performance through a confusion matrix.The results show that integrating ELM into KNN increases the average accuracy from 70.86% to 95.44%, achieving the highest accuracy of 96.50% at a 75% training and 25% testing ratio. These findings confirm that the ELM–KNN combination produces a more accurate and efficient model for breast cancer diagnosis.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1942153.title: Multiparametric MRI-based radiomics combined with deep learning for preoperative risk stratification of endometrial carcinoma
doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1942153.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To develop and compare radiomics, deep learning, clinical, and combined models based on multiparametric MRI radiomics and 2.5D deep learning features for preoperative risk stratification of endometrial carcinoma (EC).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This retrospective study included 246 patients with pathologically confirmed EC, with preoperative clinical and imaging data collected. Clinical data, T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) were collected. Radiomics and deep learning models were constructed based on T2WI, CE-T1WI, and their combination. A combined model integrating multiparametric radiomics features, deep learning features, and clinical parameters was subsequently developed. Model performance and clinical utility were evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and the DeLong test for pairwise model comparisons. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was employed to enhance model interpretability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis identified maximum tumor diameter, MR-DMI, BMI and ER status as independent predictive factors. Comparison of radiomics, deep learning, clinical, and combined models demonstrated that the multiparametric MRI model outperformed single-sequence models based on radiomics or deep learning, while the combined model exhibited the best predictive performance in the validation set, achieving an AUC of 0.891, accuracy of 0.86, sensitivity of 0.909, specificity of 0.765, and F1-score of 0.896. DeLong test results showed that, in the training set, the combined model had higher predictive performance than all other models, and the differences were statistically significant (P &lt; 0.05). In the validation set, the combined model showed statistically significant improvements compared with the clinical model and the T2+CET1-Rad model (P&lt;0.05). Decision curve analysis indicated that the combined model provided the highest clinical net benefit.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The combination of multiparametric MRI-based radiomics and 2.5D deep learning demonstrated favorable predictive performance in stratifying risk for EC, suggesting its potential utility as a non-invasive tool and offering a promising adjunctive approach to support personalized treatment planning and prognostic evaluation for EC patients in clinical practice.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.47732/darris.v9i2.653.title: TRANSFORMING EDUCATIONAL METHODOLOGIES: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF COMPUTER-BASED LEARNING MODELS, APPLICATIONS, AND IMPLEMENTATION CHALLENGES
doi:10.47732/darris.v9i2.653.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the implementation of computer-based learning (CBL) in contemporary education, focusing on its instructional models, supporting and inhibiting factors, and available learning applications. Using a qualitative descriptive approach based on a review of primary and secondary literature, the study identifies four main CBL models: drill and practice, tutorials, simulations, and instructional games. The reviewed literature indicates that CBL may improve students’ understanding by up to 40% compared with conventional methods. Key enabling factors include access to technology and awareness among educational institutions, whereas major barriers include high costs and disparities in technological competence. The study also identifies nine widely used learning applications that can support CBL, each offering distinct features and functions.</jats:p>

doi:10.1108/cwbr-07-2026-0008.title: Entrepreneurial commitment, ambidextrous entrepreneurial learning and opportunity identification of new ventures in China: a moderated mediating effect model
doi:10.1108/cwbr-07-2026-0008.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Grounded in organizational learning theory, this study examines how entrepreneurial commitment influences opportunity identification through ambidextrous entrepreneurial learning, and assesses whether environmental munificence moderates these relationships.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Data were collected through a survey of 240 entrepreneurs in China.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Entrepreneurial commitment is positively associated with both exploratory and exploitative learning. Exploratory learning and exploitative learning play a mediating role in the relationship between entrepreneurial commitment and opportunity identification. Environmental munificence has different effects on the relationship between entrepreneurial commitment and the two learning styles. Environmental munificence positively regulates the relationship between entrepreneurial commitment and exploitative learning, and negatively regulates the relationship between entrepreneurial commitment and exploratory learning. The results further reveal that greater environmental munificence strengthens the entrepreneurial commitment–exploitative learning relationship while weakening the commitment–exploratory learning relationship.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study contributes to organizational learning theory by positioning exploratory and exploitative learning as mediating mechanisms in the relationship between entrepreneurial commitment and opportunity identification, and showing the moderating role of environmental munificence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.25170/kolita.v24i24.8578.title: SUPRIATNOKO’S FIVE-FINGERS TECHNIQUE MODEL: INNOVATION IN ENGLISH GRAMMAR LEARNING TO IMPROVE INDONESIAN STUDENTS’ COMMUNICATIVE COMPETENCE
doi:10.25170/kolita.v24i24.8578.abstract: <jats:p>Mastery of grammar, especially English tenses, is a fundamental component in developing effective communication skills among Indonesian EFL students. However, in practice, tenses remain one of the most challenging aspects for students across educational levels to comprehend and apply. Despite the wide range of instructional methods available, tense instruction in Indonesian classrooms still predominantly emphasizes formula memorization rather than functional use in real communication. Consequently, students tend to forget grammatical rules easily, struggle to apply tenses flexibly, and experience low confidence in speaking and writing. This study aims to (1) develop the Supriatnoko Five-Finger Technique Model as an innovative instructional framework for teaching English tenses, (2) examine its theoretical foundations in embodied learning and communicative language teaching, and (3) evaluate its preliminary effectiveness in improving students’ functional use of tenses in speaking and writing. The study employed a research and development (R&D) design combined with a limited pilot implementation. The development phase included conceptual design, model formulation, and instructional material preparation. The pilot implementation involved classroom application at Sekolah Terbuka Madani Depok using a quasi-experimental approach with comparative observation of students’ performance before and after the intervention. Data were collected through speaking and writing assessments, classroom observation, and student feedback questionnaires. The Supriatnoko Five-Finger Technique Model is a visual and kinesthetics’ instructional approach that maps five major English tense categories—present, past, future, perfect, and continuous—onto the five fingers of the hand. Each finger is associated with a distinct communicative question type: WH-questions, Yes/No questions, Negative tag questions, Positive tag questions, and Assumption questions. The novelty of this study lies in its integration of embodied learning, functional tense categorization, and communicative question-based interaction into a single instruction model that operationalizes grammatical tenses to support functional language use, rather than focusing on vocabulary acquisition or classroom commands. Preliminary findings indicate that 97.4% of students demonstrated measurable improvement in their speaking and writing performance compared to conventional teaching methods. Although promising, the model requires further large-scale testing and refinement across diverse secondary and language training contexts to ensure broader applicability and effectiveness.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1951607.title: The psychology behind physics teachers’ attitudes toward out-of-school learning: the roles of self-efficacy and anxiety
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1951607.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aimed to examine physics teachers’ attitudes toward out-of-school learning, self-efficacy beliefs, and anxiety in terms of various demographic variables, and to determine whether their self-efficacy and anxiety regarding out-of-school learning are significant predictors of their attitudes toward out-of-school learning.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      An explanatory sequential mixed-methods research design was employed. Quantitative data were collected from 41 physics teachers employed by the Ministry of National Education in a province of Türkiye using the Self-Efficacy Belief Scale for Organizing Educational Field Trips to Out-of-School Learning Environments, the Anxiety Scale, and the Attitude Scale, all of which were developed by experts in the field. Following the quantitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 16 teachers selected from the quantitative sample through maximum variation sampling to explore their views and experiences in greater depth. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent samples
                      <jats:italic>t</jats:italic>
                      -tests, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression analysis, whereas qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A statistically significant gender difference was found in attitudes toward out-of-school learning, with male teachers reporting higher scores than female teachers. The remaining demographic comparisons were not statistically significant; however, given the limited sensitivity associated with the small subgroup sizes, these results were considered inconclusive rather than evidence of no group differences. Self-efficacy was identified as a significant positive predictor of attitudes toward out-of-school learning, whereas anxiety was found to be a significant negative predictor. Together, self-efficacy and anxiety accounted for 39% of the variance in attitude scores in this sample (
                      <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                       = 0.39; adjusted
                      <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                       = 0.36). The qualitative findings further indicated that teachers’ anxiety was primarily associated with student safety, legal procedures, administrative responsibilities, curriculum intensity, limited resources, and a lack of practical implementation experience.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this sample, self-efficacy and anxiety were associated with attitudes toward out-of-school learning, while the demographic comparisons identified a significant gender difference in attitude scores but no other statistically significant group differences. Whether support aimed at teachers’ self-efficacy and implementation-related concerns increases the use of out-of-school learning requires further investigation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.1177/00405175261489807.title: Design of an eco-friendly curtain cotton wearable antenna assisted by machine learning for medical applications
doi:10.1177/00405175261489807.abstract: <jats:p>The design and development of an environmentally friendly curtain cotton patch antenna for high-performance wearable medical applications is presented. While textile substrates, such as jeans, jute, felt, and cotton have been widely explored, recent studies show increasing interest in integrating machine learning (ML) for antenna performance prediction, fast optimization, and intelligent material selection. With a high gain of 9.5 dBi and an operating frequency of 3.44 GHz. The return loss of the antenna is −33.144 dB, which shows decreased signal reflections and good impedance matching. Curtain cotton is a desirable choice for wearable healthcare applications since it offers a biocompatible and environmentally friendly substrate material. With a larger gain and a smaller return loss than conventional antennas, the proposed antenna performs better. Computer Simulation Technology (CST) software was used for the antenna’s design and optimization, allowing for precise modeling and behavior analysis. The proposed antenna’s design and functionality were validated by CST simulations, which showed the antenna’s performance in terms of return loss, radiation patterns, and electric and magnetic field distributions. The antenna is a perfect fit for a variety of medical and healthcare applications, owing to its performance and design.</jats:p>

doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1986129.title: When college students perceive GAI feedback as credible: the role of perceived GAI feedback credibility in promoting deep learning through cognitive engagement
doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1986129.abstract: <jats:p>Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) has rapidly developed in higher education and has raised new questions from an educational psychology perspective. Why does GAI feedback promote meaningful learning for some college students but fail to produce similar learning benefits for others? To answer this question, this study develops a theoretical framework based on Information Processing Theory, Elaboration Likelihood Model, and Constructivist Learning Theory. This study examines how perceived GAI feedback credibility influences college students’ deep learning and explores the mediating role of cognitive engagement in this relationship. This study adopts a stratified simple sampling method and collects questionnaire data from 506 undergraduate students and uses structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine the proposed model. The results show that perceived GAI feedback credibility has positive relationships with both cognitive engagement and deep learning. In addition, cognitive engagement plays a significant mediating role between perceived GAI feedback credibility and deep learning, suggesting that credible GAI feedback may support deep learning by encouraging college students to engage in cognitive processing and reflective thinking. This study extends research on learning psychology in GAI-supported learning environments by explaining how college students evaluate and process GAI feedback. The findings indicate that the influence of GAI feedback on learning does not simply result from the technology itself. Instead, college students’ judgments of feedback credibility and their following cognitive engagement play important roles in shaping deep learning processes.</jats:p>

doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26oct663.title: UPI Fraud Detection Using Machine Learning with AI-Based Risk Score and Transaction Blocking
doi:10.38124/ijisrt/26oct663.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid growth of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions has increased the need for effective methods to detect and prevent digital payment fraud. This project proposes a machine learning-based UPI fraud detection system that analyzes transaction details and identifies patterns that may indicate suspicious activity. Features such as transaction amount, time, frequency, recipient information, device details, and transaction history are used to assess each payment.The system applies machine learning to classify transactions and generate an AI-based risk score. It provides explanations for flagged transactions, such as unusually large payments, repeated transfers within a short period, or payments to unfamiliar recipients. Based on configurable risk thresholds, the system can approve low-risk transactions, send medium-risk transactions for review, and block high-risk transactions. A web-based dashboard displays transaction records, risk scores, alerts, explanations, and decision status for users and administrators.The proposed system aims to support faster fraud monitoring and provide a structured process for handling suspicious payments. Its performance depends on the quality and representativeness of the transaction data used for training and evaluation. The system is intended as a fraud prevention support tool, with final deployment and transaction blocking dependent on integration with authorized payment services</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s40001-026-05352-2.title: Integrating deep learning and handcrafted radiomics features for Helicobacter pylori infection identification on multi‑region gastroscopic images: a comparative study
doi:10.1186/s40001-026-05352-2.abstract: Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) infection is a major pathogenic factor of chronic gastritis, peptic ulcer, and gastric cancer. Early non-invasive screening is clinically important. Conventional gastroscopic diagnosis relies heavily on endoscopists’ experience with high subjectivity. This study aimed to develop a fusion model of deep learning and radiomics based on gastroscopy images for intelligent, objective, and accurate identification of H. pylori infection. A total of 6235 gastroscopic images from 151 patients at Longgang District People’s Hospital of Shenzhen were retrospectively collected. Datasets were constructed according to the gastric body, fundus, antrum, angle, and a combined four-region set. Five CNN models, including AlexNet and DenseNet121, were used with transfer learning and fivefold cross-validation. A dual-branch deep learning–radiomics fusion framework was established, and performance was evaluated by accuracy, AUC, and other metrics. ResNet50 and DenseNet121 were the best-performing single models, with ResNet50 reaching an AUC of 0.8563 in the gastric body. Integrating radiomics features improved classification performance in some regions, although the benefit was region-dependent; the DenseNet121 fusion model achieved the highest fusion AUC of 0.8184 in the gastric fundus. Despite imperfectly balanced single-region sample sizes, the combined four-region dataset achieved performance comparable to that of the best single-region subset, supporting the model’s robustness to moderate inter-region heterogeneity. In an independent external cohort of 50 patients, the gastric body and fundus remained the best-performing regions (highest AUCs: 0.7836 for single models and 0.7085 for fusion models), although overall external performance was modest and requires confirmation in larger multicentre studies. The combination of deep learning and radiomics effectively improves the diagnostic performance of H. pylori infection using gastroscopy images. The gastric body and fundus are the most valuable regions. This non-invasive and interpretable approach can provide real-time intelligent assistance for routine gastroscopy and shows promising clinical application prospects.

doi:10.4038/p.v17i1.90.title: ග්‍රාමීය පාසල්වල ජ්‍යෙෂ්ඨ ද්විතීයික සිසුන්ගේ ඉංග්‍රීසි විෂය ඉගෙනුම කෙරෙහි බලපාන ගැටලු - Issues Impacting English Language Learning among Senior Secondary Students in Rural Schools
doi:10.4038/p.v17i1.90.abstract: <jats:p>In the modern era, the world is developing a globally interconnected economy alongside political networks, making it essential for learners to develop strong communication and problem-solving skills, for which the English language has become an indispensable medium. Although English has been taught as a compulsory second language since 1943, a significant majority of the student population, particularly senior secondary students in rural schools, has failed to achieve proficiency - a situation far more prevalent in rural areas than in urban ones. This study employed a mixed-methods research approach to analytically investigate the problems affecting English language learning among these students, utilizing questionnaires and interviews as primary instruments and written sources for secondary data. The research sample, selected via simple random sampling, consisted of five principals, five teachers of Grades 10 and 11, and 80 senior secondary students from Category 02 schools within the Buttala Education Division of the Monaragala District. Quantitative data were analyzed using  tables, charts, and percentages, while qualitative data were analyzed through thematic analysis. The findings revealed that English achievement levels among these students are below 50%, with a vast majority expressing dissatisfaction with their marks. Furthermore, the study identified a critical lack of use of learning aids and a heavy reliance on the traditional lecture-discussion method. To address these issues, the research suggests that teachers emphasize the value of English to students, increase the use of instructional aids, assess performance across all four language skills, and implement feedback programs and subject-related workshops to enhance overall student achievement.</jats:p>

doi:10.1186/s12982-026-03091-7.title: Parent and stakeholder perspectives on a school-based food programme supporting diverse communities in the United Kingdom: a qualitative study
doi:10.1186/s12982-026-03091-7.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Schools are key community assets to guide health-promoting behaviours and drive culturally inclusive practices and interventions. The
                      <jats:italic>Food for Thought</jats:italic>
                      programme was delivered in two primary schools in Doncaster, South Yorkshire, incorporating monthly cooking and gardening workshops to engage parents and children over six-months. The programme aimed to support cultural sharing and parental involvement through hands-on food-growing and cooking activities.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This research aimed to understand why community members attended the programme and to explore their perspectives on how their contributions influenced school food provision, education and the learning environment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Three semi-structured focus groups were conducted with both parents and key stakeholders (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 28) who had participated in and experienced the programme. Data were recorded, transcribed verbatim and analysed thematically using deductive and inductive processes.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Six major themes were identified within two deductive coding categories. Under motivations for attendance and community contribution, participants described the opportunity for social connection alongside personal drivers rooted in their interest in food, cooking and cultural exchange. The programme’s peer-led and inclusive approach facilitated collective learning and community participation, which influenced skills, cultural sharing and future opportunities. Under food Provision, education, and the learning environment the programme positioned the school as a community hub for food and cultural exchange. This environment supported the participants’ recognition of the food learning journey described as moving ‘from seed to plate’.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Overall, this study highlights the potential of a culturally inclusive multicomponent school-based community food programme to support diverse communities by providing a valuable learning experience through growing and cooking.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

doi:10.3390/make8110344.title: Cross-Dataset Generalisation of Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Three-Class Alzheimer’s Disease Staging: A Six-Model Benchmark Including a Bidirectional State-Space Model
doi:10.3390/make8110344.abstract: <jats:p>Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common neurodegenerative disorder, and its pathology accumulates for years before symptoms appear, which places the mild cognitive impairment (MCI) stage at the centre of early detection. Machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) applied to structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) report high classification accuracy, yet these figures are usually measured within a single cohort and are rarely tested for transfer to an independent cohort, so whether they translate into clinical usefulness remains unresolved. The objective of this study is to address that gap directly. Six classifiers, three classical learners (Extra Trees, LightGBM and CatBoost) and three deep networks (ConvNeXt, CoAtNet and an introduced bidirectional Vision Mamba model, MambAD) were trained and tested on identical hippocampal slices from three publicly available datasets, namely ADNI, OASIS and a public Kaggle collection, for the three-class staging of cognitively normal (CN), MCI and AD. Every model was evaluated within cohorts and, more importantly, across cohorts, with subject-level scoring on the two clinical datasets. Within the primary ADNI cohort, the introduced model reached the highest balanced accuracy (BAC) at 0.578, although this lead was not statistically significant; across the six models, none dominated on every task, and no pairwise difference between models reached significance. BAC fell from about 0.55 within-cohort to between 0.38 and 0.45 across cohorts for every model, and the deep models transferred better on the ranking metric than the classical learners. The results show that a lightweight state-space model can match far larger pretrained backbones under matched conditions, and they confirm that single cohort accuracy overstates readiness, with cross-dataset generalisation remaining the binding constraint on clinical use.</jats:p>

doi:10.51878/learning.v6i4.15516.title: UPAYA GURU DALAM MENGIMPLEMENTASIKAN LITERASI BUDAYA DAN KEWARGAAN PADA PESERTA DIDIK KELAS RENDAH DI SEKOLAH DASAR
doi:10.51878/learning.v6i4.15516.abstract:
<jats:p>ABSTRACT
Lower-grade education requires an empirical bridge between theoretical understandings of civic norms and cultural experiences closely tied to students’ daily lives. This article captures in depth teachers’ pedagogical practices in implementing cultural and civic literacy, while mapping various supporting and inhibiting factors at UPTD SD Negeri 078493 Fadorosifulubanua. To uncover this reality, the field investigation was designed through a descriptive qualitative approach involving one school principal, three lower-grade teachers, and fifteen students as key informants, supported by initial observation data on thirty-one pupils. Information collection was carried out through the triangulation of observation techniques, in-depth interviews, and document review, which were subsequently filtered and verified through qualitative data condensation stages. Empirical findings indicate that the strengthening of such literacy is actualized through the integration of cultural values into instructional materials, daily role modeling, disciplinary habituation, and the introduction of local wisdom. Nonetheless, the implementation process still encounters obstacles regarding limited local learning media and variations in individual student characteristics. The study concludes that the effectiveness of instilling these values heavily relies on the availability of contextual learning resources and sustainable synergy between the school and families.
ABSTRAK
Pendidikan tingkat kelas rendah menuntut adanya jembatan empiris antara pemahaman teoretis mengenai norma kewargaan dan pengalaman kultural yang lekat dengan keseharian siswa. Artikel ini memotret secara mendalam praktik pedagogis guru dalam mengimplementasikan literasi budaya serta kewargaan, sekaligus memetakan beragam faktor pendukung dan penghambat di UPTD SD Negeri 078493 Fadorosifulubanua. Guna menguak realitas tersebut, penelusuran lapangan dirancang melalui pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif yang melibatkan satu kepala sekolah, tiga guru kelas rendah, dan lima belas peserta didik sebagai key informants, dengan didukung data observasi awal terhadap tiga puluh satu siswa. Pengumpulan informasi ditempuh lewat triangulasi teknik observasi, wawancara mendalam, serta bedah dokumen, yang kemudian disaring dan diverifikasi melalui tahapan kondensasi data kualitatif. Temuan empiris mengindikasikan bahwa penguatan literasi tersebut diejawantahkan lewat integrasi nilai kultural ke dalam materi ajar, keteladanan harian, pembiasaan disiplin, serta pengenalan kearifan lokal. Kendati demikian, proses implementasinya masih membentur kendala berupa keterbatasan media belajar setempat serta variasi karakteristik individu siswa. Konklusi studi menegaskan bahwa efektivitas penanaman nilai ini sangat bergantung pada ketersediaan sumber belajar yang kontekstual serta sinergi berkelanjutan antara pihak sekolah dan keluarga.</jats:p>

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11153173/v1.title: Serum uric acid-to-creatinine ratio and preeclampsia: a retrospective cross-sectional analysis with machine learning discrimination using the MIMIC-IV database
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11153173/v1.abstract: Objective Preeclampsia continues to be a primary cause of health complications and death for expectant mothers and their unborn children. Early identification of pregnant women at risk, followed by timely preventive interventions, carries clear clinical value. We examined whether the serum uric acid to creatinine ratio (UA/Cr) measured at admission is associated with preeclampsia and whether it adds discriminative value when used in machine learning (ML) models. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using the MIMIC-IV database, identifying 4,756 pregnant women with gestational age ≥ 20 weeks; 4,247 were excluded for missing data, leaving 509 for analysis (78 preeclampsia cases, 431 controls). Preeclampsia was identified by ICD-9/10 codes. UA/Cr (uric acid mg/dL ÷ creatinine mg/dL, first admission-day value) entered logistic regression as both a continuous variable and a quartile variable (Q1 as reference), with two adjustment sets: Model 1 adjusted for age, and Model 2 for age, language, and red blood cell count. Restricted cubic splines characterized nonlinearity, and subgroup analyses tested robustness. Six machine learning algorithms—random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, AdaBoost, and TabPFN—were trained on the training set (n = 355) and validated on the validation set (n = 154). Features were selected by univariate screening, variance inflation factor (VIF) diagnostics, and LASSO.Univariate analysis for screening, VIF diagnostics, and LASSO were utilized to choose features. Result UA/Cr rose with preeclampsia risk and the dose–response curve was approximately linear (nonlinearity P = 0.911): each 1-unit increment was associated with an OR of 1.184 (95% CI 1.061–1.320, P = 0.002). The highest quartile carried an OR of 2.758 versus the lowest quartile (95% CI 1.318–6.128, P = 0.009; trend P = 0.020). AUCs in the validation set ranged from 0.655 to 0.761 (LightGBM the highest), with UA/Cr ranking second in feature importance. The four top-performing models did not differ significantly from one another. Conclusion In this MIMIC-IV cohort of hospitalized pregnant women, a higher admission UA/Cr was associated with preeclampsia, and an ML model built from routine admission data achieved moderate concurrent discrimination. Because of the cross-sectional design, the analysis does not support prospective prediction. Prospective and external validation, alongside head-to-head comparison with absolute uric acid, is required before any clinical use in risk stratification.

doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11021999/v1.title: Construction and Multi-Model Performance Evaluation of an Intelligent Screening Model for Meige Syndrome Based on Machine Learning
doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11021999/v1.abstract: Objective To develop and validate an intelligent screening model for Meige syndrome (MS) based on routine clinical inquiry data, enabling quantitative differentiation among MS patients, patients with other ocular diseases, and normal individuals. Methods A total of 3,996 clinical cases were enrolled. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression was applied to rank the importance of 12 candidate variables. The predictive performance of four models—multinomial logistic regression, support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and artificial neural network (ANN)—was systematically compared with emphasis on goodness-of-fit, predictive accuracy, and probability calibration. Results Statistically significant differences across all 12 variables were observed among the three groups (all P  < 0.05). Importance ranking identified history of other craniofacial conditions, age, sleep quality, history of drinking, and history of thyroid disease as the five most important predictors. Among simplified models built on these five variables, ANN demonstrated optimal overall performance: testing set accuracy of 0.777, AUC of 0.864, and the best probability calibration stability. RF ranked second (accuracy 0.776, AUC 0.858) but exhibited systematic calibration deviation in high-probability intervals. Multinomial logistic regression and SVM showed comparatively limited efficacy. The simplified model closely approximated the full-variable model in diagnostic performance, and decision curve analysis suggested possible meaningful clinical utility. Conclusion The simplified ANN model, requiring no laboratory testing and completable within one minute, may serve as a practical auxiliary tool for early MS screening in primary healthcare settings.

doi:10.21067/bimasakti.v9i1.13207.title: ANALISIS SENTIMEN KOMENTAR NETIZEN PADA MEDIA SOSIAL INSTAGRAM TIMNAS INDONESIA MENGGUNAKAN METODE NAÏVE BAYES DAN SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE
doi:10.21067/bimasakti.v9i1.13207.abstract: <jats:p>Social media has become an integral part of modern society, providing a platform for public expression. In Indonesia, soccer is a popular sport, and the Indonesian national team is a major topic of discussion on social media, especially Instagram. This study aims to analyze the sentiment of netizen comments on the official Instagram account of the Indonesian national team (@timnasindonesia) using the Naïve Bayes and Support Vector Machine (SVM) methods. The data used consisted of 2,920 comments from 50 posts between September 28, 2023, and May 10, 2024, focusing on the U-23 and Senior National Team matches. Naïve Bayes and SVM were chosen because both are effective methods for sentiment classification. Naïve Bayes uses a probabilistic approach, while SVM seeks the best hyperplane to separate data classes. The results of the study show that both methods can be used to analyze sentiment with a good level of accuracy. Testing results on each training and testing data with different presentations will give different accuracy results. The test results from the Naive Bayes method obtained the highest accuracy value of 69% with a ratio of 70:30. Meanwhile, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) method obtained the highest accuracy of 74% at the same ratio. It can be concluded that the Support Vector Machine method obtained a higher accuracy value than the Naive Bayes method, making it more optimal for use in classifying the sentiment of netizen comments in this study.</jats:p>

doi:10.1007/s12145-026-02280-x.title: Integrating ensemble learning with empirical rock-physics equations for sonic-log reconstruction and geomechanical property estimation: a case study from the Williston basin
doi:10.1007/s12145-026-02280-x.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Accurate prediction of geomechanical properties is important for reliable hydrocarbon reservoir exploration and development, but conventional well logging and core analysis can be costly, time-consuming, and limited by incomplete sonic-log coverage. This study develops a two-stage hybrid framework that integrates ensemble machine learning with empirical rock-physics relationships to predict geomechanical properties from readily available conventional well logs. Deep resistivity (AT90), gamma ray (GR), caliper (HCAL), neutron porosity (NPHI), and bulk density (RHOZ) logs were used as input features for model training and prediction of compressional-wave transit time (DTCO) and shear-wave transit time (DTSM). Four ensemble learning algorithms—Random Forest, Light Gradient Boosting Machine, Extra Trees, and Extreme Gradient Boosting—were evaluated, and the predicted sonic responses were subsequently incorporated into established rock-physics equations to estimate Poisson’s ratio, Young’s modulus, and shear modulus. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were further employed to quantify feature contributions and interpret the relationship between model predictions and petrophysical controls. Extra Trees produced the best predictions, with coefficients of determination (R-squared) of 0.97 for both targets; root mean squared error and mean absolute error were 10 and 6.1 for DTSM and 3.7 and 2.1 for DTCO, respectively. Measured DTSM showed poor agreement with the Castagna correlation, whereas elastic properties calculated from machine-learning predictions agreed well with those derived from measured logs. The scientific contribution is an interpretable, formation-specific framework that connects conventional-log prediction of missing sonic curves to physics-based estimation of multiple elastic properties, providing a practical basis for reservoir characterization where complete sonic coverage is unavailable.</jats:p>

doi:10.55041/isjem08714.title: A Review of Machine Learning Techniques for Customer Segmentation and Personalized Marketing in E-Commerce
doi:10.55041/isjem08714.abstract:
<jats:p>Customer segmentation and personalized marketing have become central applications of machine learning within modern e-commerce architectures. While traditional segmentation models depend on static demographic categorizations and heuristic rule sets, machine learning algorithms allow platforms to uncover subtle behavioral patterns across complex customer transaction streams. This review presents a critical analysis of widely deployed approaches, including unsupervised clustering (K-Means, Hierarchical, DBSCAN), value-based models (RFM analysis), supervised predictive algorithms (Decision Trees, Random Forests), and collaborative filtering systems for product recommendation. We assess their technical tradeoffs, operational constraints, and real-world deployment viability. Furthermore, this review highlights critical open research challenges regarding model interpretability, high-dimensional data sparsity, real-time feedback processing, data privacy regulations, and the integration of segmentation engines into dynamic marketing automation pipelines.

Key Words: Machine Learning, Customer Segmentation, Personalized Marketing, E-Commerce, K-Means, RFM Analysis, Recommendation Systems, Predictive Analytics.</jats:p>

doi:10.1071/ah26108.title: From local audit to national learning: revisiting the case for a national colonoscopy clinical quality registry in Australia
doi:10.1071/ah26108.abstract: <jats:p>Colonoscopy is central to colorectal cancer prevention and early detection, yet Australia lacks a national mechanism to aggregate and benchmark colonoscopy quality data. The Colonoscopy Clinical Care Standard establishes local monitoring of key quality indicators, which can identify service-level problems, but cannot show whether variation is isolated, systemic, improving over time or concentrated in particular settings. This creates a national blind spot in one of the country’s most common cancer-prevention procedures. Current arrangements remain fragmented across health services and do not support consistent national oversight. Since colonoscopy registry development was previously deprioritised in 2016, the Australian context has changed substantially: a national clinical care standard is now in place, cross-college governance of colonoscopy recertification has matured, endoscopy reporting software has improved structured data capture and broader national clinical quality registry frameworks now support more coordinated registry development. A national colonoscopy clinical quality registry could build on existing local data collection, and support coordinated national quality assurance by enabling confidential benchmarking, identifying unwarranted variation, strengthening clinical governance, and informing accreditation, training and service improvement.</jats:p>
